Create a new compliance flag record associated with an existing product in the shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags Prisma table, identified by the parent product’s business-visible code from shopping_mall_products.

This operation will be used by platform administrators or trusted seller operators to attach regulatory or policy-related restrictions to a product, such as age restrictions, hazardous material flags, or region-based sale limitations. It must validate that the target product exists and is uniquely identified by its code (shopping_mall_products.code, which is globally unique according to the schema’s unique index), then insert a new row into shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags with the foreign key shopping_mall_product_id and the supplied flag fields.

The request body will use the IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag.ICreate DTO, which encapsulates the properties described in the Prisma schema: flag_type, flag_value, is_blocking_sale, notes, and any additional metadata needed by the application. The server will also populate created_at and updated_at timestamps based on system time, and may enforce business rules such as one compliance flag per (product, flag_type) pair as constrained by the composite unique index on [shopping_mall_product_id, flag_type]. The response returns the newly created compliance flag as IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag, including its generated id and timestamps.
operations.description:
Create a new compliance flag for a catalog product using its business-visible product code as the identifier.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags table, whose description states that it stores “Compliance and restriction metadata applied to products” such as age restrictions, hazardous materials indicators, and region-based sales restrictions. Each compliance flag row is linked to a specific product via the shopping_mall_product_id foreign key referencing shopping_mall_products.id, and optionally to an age restriction policy via shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id. The schema also defines a composite unique index on [shopping_mall_product_id, flag_type], ensuring that a given product can have at most one compliance flag of a particular type.

When the client calls this endpoint, the path parameter {productCode} is resolved to a single product row by looking up shopping_mall_products.code, which is documented as a “Business-visible product code or identifier used internally and in integrations. Unique per platform for stable references.” Because code is globally unique, this path parameter is sufficient to locate the target product without requiring a separate productId parameter. The service then constructs a new compliance flag using properties from the IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag.ICreate request body, such as flag_type (values like age_restriction or hazardous_material), optional flag_value for regulation codes, is_blocking_sale to indicate whether the flag can fully prevent checkout under certain conditions, and optional notes with internal context.

Security-wise, this operation should be restricted to authenticated actors with appropriate catalog management permissions, such as platform administrators or trusted seller roles. In this API specification, we model this as authorizationActors: ["platformAdmin"], with the understanding that the concrete role model may map this actor to shopping_mall_platformadmin or permitted seller accounts in the implementation. The handler must enforce the composite uniqueness constraint when inserting into shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags; attempts to create a duplicate flag_type for the same product should result in a validation error rather than a silent overwrite. On success, the operation returns the complete IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag representation, including its id, foreign keys, timestamps, and all flag attributes so that admin UIs can immediately reflect the newly applied restriction.

Related operations include listing or viewing compliance flags for a product, and updating an existing flag using the PUT /products/{productCode}/complianceFlags/{productComplianceFlagId} endpoint defined elsewhere. Clients are expected to use this POST endpoint to create new compliance constraints whenever new regulatory requirements are introduced or when products are reclassified, and to use the corresponding update endpoint to adjust existing flags without violating the unique (product, flag_type) invariant.
operations.summary: Create a new product compliance flag row in shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags for a product identified by shopping_mall_products.code.

parameters.name: productCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target product (global scope), mapped to shopping_mall_products.code, which is unique per platform.

requestBody.description: Compliance flag creation payload containing flag type, value, blocking behavior, and optional notes to be associated with the target product.

responseBody.description: Newly created product compliance flag, including its generated identifier, foreign key references, timestamps, and all compliance attributes.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: The target catalog product must exist in shopping_mall_products (created using its unique productCode) before a new compliance flag can be attached to it.

When shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id is supplied in the creation payload, the referenced age restriction policy must already exist in shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies so the foreign key can be set correctly.

operations.specification:
Update an existing compliance flag record in the shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags Prisma table for a product identified by its business-visible code from shopping_mall_products, together with the compliance flag’s own identifier.

This operation is responsible for modifying fields such as flag_type, flag_value, is_blocking_sale, notes, and policy references on an existing compliance flag row. To ensure referential and ownership integrity, it must first resolve the product using shopping_mall_products.code (from {productCode}), then confirm that the specified compliance flag (by {productComplianceFlagId}, mapped to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.id) belongs to that product via shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.shopping_mall_product_id. The modification itself is modeled through the IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag.IUpdate DTO, allowing controlled updates while preserving immutable values like id and creation timestamps.

The operation must respect database constraints defined in the Prisma schema. In particular, the unique index on [shopping_mall_product_id, flag_type] means that changing the flag_type of a compliance record must not result in two rows with the same (product, flag_type) combination. Any attempted update that violates this composite uniqueness should be detected and returned as a clear validation error to the client rather than causing a database error. Timestamps such as updated_at should be set to the current system time whenever an update is successfully applied. On success, the service returns the updated compliance flag as IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag for immediate display or further processing by admin tools.
operations.description:
Update an existing compliance flag attached to a catalog product, ensuring that the flag remains correctly associated with the product and that uniqueness constraints are preserved.

This endpoint operates on the shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags table, which holds “Compliance and restriction metadata applied to products” including age restrictions, hazardous material flags, and region-based limitations. Each record is linked to a product via shopping_mall_product_id referencing shopping_mall_products.id, and optionally to an age restriction policy via shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id. The path parameters combine a human-friendly product identifier and a technical compliance flag identifier: {productCode} maps to shopping_mall_products.code (a globally unique, business-visible product code), while {productComplianceFlagId} maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.id (the primary key for the compliance flag row).

When processing a request, the service first resolves the product using the provided productCode and verifies that the compliance flag identified by productComplianceFlagId belongs to that product by checking its shopping_mall_product_id. This prevents accidental updates to flags that belong to a different product, even if the client supplied a valid id. The request body follows the IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag.IUpdate DTO, which may include updated values for properties such as flag_type, flag_value, is_blocking_sale, notes, or the referenced age restriction policy. The Prisma schema’s composite unique index on [shopping_mall_product_id, flag_type] requires the implementation to verify that any change to flag_type does not conflict with an existing flag of the same type on the same product.

From a security perspective, this operation should only be accessible to actors with appropriate moderation or catalog management privileges. In this specification, we designate authorizationActors: ["platformAdmin"], indicating that only administrative actors can perform such updates. Implementations may refine this to map to platform administrators or specifically authorized seller accounts. The endpoint returns the updated IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag entity, including id, product linkage, policy linkage, updated flag attributes, and refreshed updated_at timestamp, allowing management consoles and back-office systems to reflect compliance changes immediately. Error handling should include clear responses for cases such as non-existent product codes, mismatched product–flag associations, and attempted updates that would violate the uniqueness of (product, flag_type).
operations.summary: Update a product compliance flag row in shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags for a given product (by shopping_mall_products.code) and flag id.

parameters.name: productCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target product (global scope), mapped to shopping_mall_products.code, which is unique per platform.

parameters.name: productComplianceFlagId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product compliance flag record to update, mapped to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.id.

requestBody.description: Updated compliance flag information, including changes to flag type, value, blocking behavior, notes, or associated policies for the specified product.

responseBody.description: The product compliance flag after applying the requested updates, including its identifiers, product linkage, and compliance attributes.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: The catalog product must exist before its compliance flags can be updated; creating the product in shopping_mall_products establishes the productCode and backing product ID referenced by the compliance flag.

The specific compliance flag record must be created for the given product before it can be updated; this POST creates the shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags row identified later by productComplianceFlagId.

When the update associates the compliance flag with an age restriction policy, that policy must already exist; this POST creates a shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies record whose ID may be referenced by shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id in the update body.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a single product compliance flag record associated with a specific product in the shoppingMall catalog. It is backed by the `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags`-family tables (as implied by the endpoint path and compliance domain) and is intended for use by administrative tooling or internal moderation systems that manage regulatory or policy flags on products.

The endpoint accepts a `productCode` path parameter, which uniquely identifies the product in the catalog using its business code, and a `productComplianceFlagId` parameter, which uniquely identifies the compliance flag record to be removed. Implementations must validate that the compliance flag actually belongs to the specified product before deletion, preventing accidental cross-product removals.

Because this endpoint performs a destructive operation, it must enforce strict authorization, typically allowing only platform administrators or specialized compliance staff to access it. Audit logging at the service layer is strongly recommended so that each deletion of a compliance flag can be traced back to an administrator, product, and timestamp. The operation does not return a resource body on success, only an appropriate HTTP status indicating that the deletion has been performed.
operations.description:
Delete a specific compliance flag record from a given product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This operation targets an individual compliance metadata entry for a product, conceptually corresponding to a row in the product compliance flags table (for example, `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags`). Each compliance flag may represent regulatory restrictions, legal notices, or special handling requirements that were previously attached to the product record. When invoked, the service must ensure that the flag identified by `productComplianceFlagId` is actually associated with the product identified by `productCode` before proceeding with the deletion.

From a security perspective, this operation should be restricted to highly privileged actors because removing compliance metadata can affect legal obligations and customer safety. Typical authorization would allow only platform administrators or compliance officers to call this endpoint. The implementation is expected to integrate with higher-level auditing mechanisms so that each deletion event records who performed the action, which product and flag were affected, and when the deletion occurred.

This deletion affects only the specific compliance flag record; the product, its SKUs, and other related records remain intact. If the flag does not exist, does not belong to the specified product, or has already been removed, the service should respond with an appropriate error such as 404 Not Found. Clients can pair this endpoint with read/list endpoints for product compliance flags in order to manage the full lifecycle of compliance metadata for catalog items.
operations.summary: Delete a product compliance flag record associated with a product in the shoppingMall catalog

parameters.name: productCode
parameters.description: Unique business identifier code of the target product in the shoppingMall catalog (global scope). This code selects which product's compliance flag is being deleted.

parameters.name: productComplianceFlagId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific compliance flag record attached to the selected product. This ID must correspond to a compliance flag that belongs to the product indicated by productCode.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: The product must exist before any compliance flag can be attached to it or later deleted; this POST creates the backing shopping_mall_products record identified by productCode.
The compliance flag row to be deleted must first be created for the specified product; this POST inserts the shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags record that will later be deleted by ID.

operations.specification:
This operation performs an advanced, multi-dimensional catalog search over products for the shoppingMall platform. It is primarily backed by the `shopping_mall_products`, `shopping_mall_product_skus`, `shopping_mall_categories`, `shopping_mall_brands`, and related visibility and compliance tables, but it does not correspond to any single Prisma table. Instead, it composes data from these entities to return a paginated list of product search results.

The client submits a rich search request body using the `IShoppingMallCatalogSearch.IRequest` DTO. This request may contain free-text search keywords, category filters, brand filters, price ranges, attribute filters, availability constraints (such as in-stock only), region-specific visibility constraints, and sorting options (e.g., relevance, newest, price ascending/descending). The service translates these criteria into a combination of SQL WHERE clauses, JOINs, and ORDER BY expressions over the underlying product and SKU tables, while honoring product visibility and compliance rules.

The response is a paginated collection of product search summaries using the `IPageIShoppingMallCatalogSearchResult.ISummary` DTO. Each summary entry includes key details suitable for listing views: product identifiers, main image, pricing range across SKUs, rating aggregates, and basic availability information. Detailed product information is intentionally omitted from this list in order to keep responses compact and optimized for client-side rendering. Clients can retrieve full product details via dedicated product detail endpoints after selecting a specific product from the search results.

Rate limiting and caching strategies are recommended for this operation, as catalog search is typically one of the highest-traffic endpoints in an e-commerce system. Security-wise, this endpoint can be made publicly accessible, but the implementation must still enforce visibility constraints (for example, hiding products that are disabled, not yet launched, or region-restricted for the requesting context).
operations.description:
Search the shoppingMall catalog for products using advanced filters, keywords, and sorting, returning a paginated list of product search results.

This operation is designed to power the main product discovery experiences such as search bars, category pages, and filterable product listings. It composes data from several catalog-related tables, including products, SKUs, categories, brands, and any product visibility rules, to answer complex queries. The request body, represented by `IShoppingMallCatalogSearch.IRequest`, can include free-text keywords, category codes, brand identifiers, price ranges, attribute filters, stock and availability settings, and sorting preferences.

The underlying implementation must translate the request structure into efficient database queries, typically involving indexed text search, JOINs to category and brand tables, and filters based on product and SKU status. It must also respect visibility and compliance flags so that products that are disabled, region-restricted, or under legal hold do not appear in results. Pagination information such as page number, page size, and total count is included in the response so client applications can implement infinite scroll or numbered page navigation.

Because catalog search is usually available to all visitors, this endpoint is intentionally public and does not require authentication. However, it should still be protected by rate limiting and potential bot-detection or abuse-prevention mechanisms. The response, represented by `IPageIShoppingMallCatalogSearchResult.ISummary`, provides compact summary objects optimized for listing views; clients can make follow-up calls to dedicated product detail endpoints to obtain full product information when a user selects a specific item from the search results.
operations.summary: Perform an advanced catalog search over shoppingMall products with filtering, sorting, and pagination

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters, and pagination parameters for catalog product discovery in the shoppingMall platform.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of catalog product search result summaries matching the specified search criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: At least one brand must exist in the catalog so that brand-based filters and brand summaries in search results can resolve against actual brand records created in the shopping_mall_brands table.

At least one category tree configuration must exist so that category-based filters and category summaries in search results can be resolved to real category tree definitions in shopping_mall_category_trees.

At least one category must exist within a category tree so that category filters and category summaries in catalog search results can be resolved to concrete category nodes stored in shopping_mall_categories.
Products must be created in the shopping_mall_products table before catalog search can return any product search results.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves an enriched, paginated list of catalog products for the shoppingMall platform, primarily based on the `shopping_mall_products` table while composing related data from several subsidiary tables including `shopping_mall_product_media`, `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules`, and `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags`. It is designed for complex search, filtering, and sorting scenarios that go beyond simple single-table queries.

The endpoint accepts a structured search payload using the `IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest` DTO, allowing clients to filter by seller, brand, status, keyword, category, visibility context (region/channel), and potentially compliance-related aspects. It then returns a paginated collection of enriched product summaries in the `IPageIShoppingMallProduct.ISummary` format, where each summary may include key product attributes such as name, status, primary image URI, and pre-resolved category/visibility highlights that are optimized for list views.

Internally, the implementation will query `shopping_mall_products` as the primary entity and join or follow relations to subsidiary entities where necessary. For example, it may join `shopping_mall_product_media` to determine an accurate primary image URI, use `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments` to ensure that products are associated with requested categories, consult `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` to respect region and channel visibility configuration, and incorporate `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags` to filter out products that should not be visible or purchasable under certain policies. The operation is read-only and does not manipulate any records.
operations.description:
Retrieve an enriched, paginated list of catalog products from the shoppingMall platform based on the `shopping_mall_products` table and several related subsidiary tables. This operation is the main listing/search endpoint for catalog browsing in backends or storefronts that require more than just raw product rows.

The underlying `shopping_mall_products` model defines the core product attributes. Fields such as `code` (a business-visible unique identifier), `name`, `short_description`, and `description` provide the textual representation of each product, while `status` expresses lifecycle states such as draft, pending_review, active, inactive, or discontinued. The `is_multi_sku` flag distinguishes single-SKU products from those with multiple variants. The `primary_image_uri` field gives a convenient pointer to the main listing image, and `additional_data` holds JSON-encoded metadata for custom catalog attributes. Timestamps like `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` support lifecycle tracking and soft-deletion semantics for catalog entries.

To produce enriched summaries appropriate for catalog list views, the operation can leverage subsidiary tables. The `shopping_mall_product_media` table supplies additional media metadata such as `uri`, `alt_text`, `media_type`, `display_order`, and `is_primary`, all tied to a product through `shopping_mall_product_id`. This allows the service to confirm or enhance the `primary_image_uri` from the main product record and to signal whether additional images are available.

Category information is derived from the `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments` table, where each assignment links a product to a category through `shopping_mall_product_id` and `shopping_mall_category_id`. The boolean `is_primary` flag indicates the primary category association, and the relevant timestamps support managing the history of category assignments. The search logic can use these assignments together with category constraints contained in the request to limit results to specific branches of the catalog hierarchy.

Visibility behavior can be tailored per product through `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules`. For each rule, the foreign key `shopping_mall_product_id` ties the rule to the product, and `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` can scope it to a particular geographic region. Fields like `channel` and `visibility` describe which sales channel (for example, web or mobile) a rule applies to and whether that rule indicates visible, hidden, or restricted behavior. Optional `starts_at` and `ends_at` timestamps allow time windows for visibility overrides. During list retrieval, the service can interpret these rules in the context of region and channel parameters in the request, ensuring that only products visible to the current viewer are returned.

Compliance and restriction metadata are modeled by the `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags` table. Each row refers back to a product via `shopping_mall_product_id` and may optionally reference an age restriction policy through `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id`. Attributes like `flag_type`, `flag_value`, and `is_blocking_sale` help decide whether a product should appear at all, or should appear with warnings or restricted purchase options. The `notes`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` fields support operational insight and auditability of compliance decisions. When building an enriched listing, this operation can filter out products with `is_blocking_sale` where appropriate or at least surface summary indicators in the response.

The request body uses `IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest` to encapsulate all search, filter, and pagination parameters. This DTO is expected to include properties like page size, page index, sort order, keyword search fields that map onto indexed columns in `shopping_mall_products` (such as `name` and `status`), and filters referencing seller or brand via `shopping_mall_seller_id` and `shopping_mall_brand_id`. Region and channel identifiers, and optional compliance filters, may also be present to drive visibility logic.

The response body returns `IPageIShoppingMallProduct.ISummary`, which wraps a collection of product summary DTOs and standard pagination metadata. Each summary should at least expose the product `code`, `name`, `status`, `primary_image_uri`, and key snippets from `short_description` or `description`, as well as flags or compact structures summarizing category, visibility, and compliance state. Clients can use this endpoint as the primary data source for catalog listing pages, search results, seller back-office product lists, and admin catalog views.

Security-wise, this endpoint can be exposed either publicly or to authenticated users depending on business decisions. In many storefront scenarios, catalog browsing is allowed for guests, so the operation is defined with an empty `authorizationActors` array and should rely on visibility and compliance rules to protect restricted products. Rate limiting and search throttling should be implemented at the infrastructure layer to prevent abuse. Error handling should include graceful responses when filters are invalid, when requested pages are out of bounds, or when internal joins fail due to inconsistent data, always without exposing sensitive implementation details.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve an enriched, paginated list of catalog products from `shopping_mall_products` with category, media, visibility, and compliance context.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination parameters for enriched product catalog listing, including seller/brand filters, category constraints, visibility context, and keyword search fields.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of enriched product summaries with catalog-friendly fields derived from `shopping_mall_products` and related media, category, visibility, and compliance data.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Creating brands in the shopping_mall_brands table is required so that brand-based filters and brand summary information in enriched product listings resolve to real brand records.
A category tree definition must exist in shopping_mall_category_trees so that products can be organized into a navigable catalog hierarchy referenced by enriched listing responses.
Concrete category nodes must exist in shopping_mall_categories so that products can be assigned to categories and enriched listings can return category context for each product.
Products must be created in shopping_mall_products before the enriched product listing can return any product summaries.

Product–category assignments must be created via shopping_mall_product_category_assignments so that enriched listings can include category-based filtering and primary category context for each product.

Product visibility rules must be created in shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules so that enriched listing logic can correctly honor per-product region and channel visibility configuration when filtering results.

Product compliance flags must be created in shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags so that enriched listings can filter or annotate products based on compliance constraints such as blocking sale or age restrictions.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a fully detailed view of a single catalog product identified by its business-visible `code` from the `shopping_mall_products` table, along with composed details from subsidiary tables such as `shopping_mall_product_media`, `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules`, `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags`, `shopping_mall_product_option_types`, `shopping_mall_product_option_values`, `shopping_mall_product_skus`, and `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments`.

The endpoint uses the `productCode` path parameter, which corresponds to the unique `code` field on `shopping_mall_products` (enforced via a unique index). Because `code` is globally unique for products, it is the preferred identifier in the URL path in place of the primary key `id`. Clients can call this endpoint to fetch all data required to render a product detail page or a back-office editing screen, including textual information, media gallery, category assignments, visibility and compliance configuration, and structured variant information across SKUs and their option types/values.

The operation returns a single `IShoppingMallProduct` DTO that represents an enriched detail view. This DTO should aggregate core product fields (such as `name`, `short_description`, `description`, `status`, `is_multi_sku`, `primary_image_uri`, `additional_data`, and timestamps) alongside nested collections or structured references for media, categories, visibility rules, compliance flags, option types and values, SKUs, and SKU-option assignments. While the Prisma schema defines these related entities across multiple tables, the API is free to denormalize them into a single, detail-focused representation for easier consumption by frontend clients. The operation is strictly read-only and does not modify the underlying records.
operations.description:
Retrieve a fully detailed representation of a single catalog product identified by its unique `code` in the `shopping_mall_products` table, along with relevant subsidiary data. This operation is tailored for product detail pages and back-office editors that require a comprehensive view of product configuration.

The `shopping_mall_products` model is the primary source of truth for the product. It provides core attributes: `code` (a business-visible and unique product identifier across the platform), `name`, `short_description`, and `description` for textual descriptions; `status` to express lifecycle states like draft, pending_review, active, inactive, or discontinued; `is_multi_sku` to indicate whether the product has multiple variants; `primary_image_uri` to point to the main listing image; and `additional_data` to store JSON-encoded metadata for custom behaviors. The temporal fields `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` capture lifecycle history and soft deletion state, ensuring consumers can handle or avoid products that are logically removed from the catalog.

Media information comes from the `shopping_mall_product_media` table. Each media record is linked to the product via `shopping_mall_product_id` and defines fields such as `uri`, `alt_text`, `media_type`, `display_order`, and `is_primary`, plus its own lifecycle timestamps and `deleted_at` for soft deletion. In the detailed product view, the API should gather all non-deleted media records, sort them by `display_order`, and surface them as a gallery while also ensuring that the `primary_image_uri` on the product is consistent with the primary media record.

Category membership is represented through `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, where each row ties a product to a category by `shopping_mall_product_id` and `shopping_mall_category_id`. The boolean `is_primary` field identifies the main category, and timestamps allow temporal reasoning. The detail response can expose both primary and secondary category associations, enabling clients to render category breadcrumbs or flags.

Visibility configuration is modeled through `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules`. For each rule, the foreign key `shopping_mall_product_id` connects it to the product, and `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` optionally scopes the rule to a particular region. Attributes like `channel`, `visibility`, `starts_at`, and `ends_at` allow fine-grained control over where and when the product appears. In a detailed view, these rules can be presented to back-office users for configuration, or used to calculate a derived visibility state for the current viewer.

Compliance and policy-related metadata resides in `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags`. Each flag references the product via `shopping_mall_product_id` and may link to an age restriction policy through `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id`. Fields such as `flag_type`, `flag_value`, `is_blocking_sale`, and `notes` describe the nature and implications of each compliance rule, while timestamps support auditing. The detailed product response can use this to inform frontends when additional messaging, purchase restrictions, or eligibility checks are required for this product.

Variant and SKU information is backed by a cluster of tables. The `shopping_mall_product_option_types` table defines variant dimensions like Color or Size through fields such as `name`, `display_name`, `display_order`, and its `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key. Option values per dimension are held in `shopping_mall_product_option_values`, where each row is tied to an option type via `shopping_mall_product_option_type_id` and contains fields like `value`, `display_name`, `display_order`, and soft-deletion timestamps. Actual purchasable variants are defined in `shopping_mall_product_skus`, with `shopping_mall_product_id` as a foreign key, and include attributes like `code` (unique per product), `external_code`, `barcode`, `status`, `price_amount`, `compare_at_price_amount`, `currency_code`, `additional_data`, and lifecycle timestamps.

The junction table `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` ties these together by mapping each SKU (`shopping_mall_product_sku_id`) to specific option values (`shopping_mall_product_option_value_id`). In the detailed view, the API implementation should reconstruct SKU variant combinations by joining these tables and grouping option values under their respective option types for each SKU. This enables clients to display structured variant selectors and to understand which combinations are valid for the product.

The operation identifies the target product using the `productCode` path parameter, which corresponds to the unique `code` field on `shopping_mall_products` rather than the surrogate `id`. This keeps URLs stable and human-readable. If no product exists for the provided `productCode`, the service should return a standard not-found error. If the product exists but has a `deleted_at` value, business rules may choose to return a not-found or a special response, depending on whether the endpoint is intended for public consumption or internal tools.

From a security perspective, this endpoint can often be exposed publicly for storefront usage or restricted to authenticated users in admin contexts. Here it is defined with no specific `authorizationActors` to allow flexible use, with visibility, compliance, and status fields governing which products are actually suitable to show. The implementation must ensure that sensitive internal notes or configuration fields (such as some compliance notes) are only returned where appropriate. Error handling includes responding properly when the `productCode` parameter does not match the uniqueness constraints, when related records are missing or inconsistent, or when downstream services fail while assembling the detail view.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed catalog product information from `shopping_mall_products` by unique product code, including media, categories, variants, visibility, and compliance configuration.

parameters.name: productCode
parameters.description: Unique business-visible code of the target product in `shopping_mall_products` (global scope), corresponding to the `code` field which is enforced as unique across all products.

responseBody.description: Enriched detailed representation of a single catalog product identified by its unique `code`, including media, categories, variant structures, visibility configuration, and compliance flags.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A catalog product must be created in the shopping_mall_products table (e.g., via seller product creation) so that a record with the given business-visible productCode exists before its detailed view can be retrieved.
Alternatively, a platform administrator can create a catalog product in shopping_mall_products so that a product with the specified productCode exists and can be fetched in detailed form.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves aggregate statistics of how many active catalog products exist per brand in the shoppingMall platform. It is a read-only analytical endpoint built on top of the shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_brands Prisma tables (and potentially related visibility or status tables, depending on schema), and returns a collection of brand-level counts rather than individual product rows.

The implementation should execute an aggregation query conceptually equivalent to:

- Group products by their associated brand identifier
- Apply any business filters for which products are considered "countable" (for example, excluding logically deleted, draft-only, or fully hidden products if such flags exist in the shopping_mall_products schema)
- Join to the shopping_mall_brands table to expose brand metadata, such as brand name or code, depending on the DTO design
- Return each brand exactly once with its aggregated productCount

This endpoint does not modify any data. It is designed for dashboards, catalog management views, and admin analytics rather than product browsing by end customers.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated counts of catalog products per brand based on the shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_brands entities.

This operation exposes a read-only statistical view instead of raw product rows. It operates over the shopping_mall_products table, which stores each product's core catalog attributes and its association to a brand, and the shopping_mall_brands table, which holds brand metadata. Only products that satisfy the platform's definition of "active" or "countable" should be included in the aggregation; the exact flags and fields depend on the shopping_mall_products schema, such as status fields, visibility flags, or compliance indicators.

The endpoint is intended for administrative and internal analytics use cases, such as an admin dashboard that needs to understand catalog distribution by brand, or catalog operations tooling that prioritizes work for brands with sparse or overloaded product portfolios. It should be treated as read-only and must not perform any side effects on catalog data or brand configuration. Security-wise, this is sensitive operational information about catalog composition, so access should be restricted to platform administrators or equivalent back-office actors.

Related endpoints may include more general product search or brand management APIs where individual products or brands are created, updated, or browsed. Those CRUD operations are distinct from this analytical endpoint, which focuses solely on aggregated counts for reporting and oversight purposes. If additional, more detailed product statistics are needed, they should be provided by separate operations to keep this endpoint focused and efficient.
operations.summary: Get aggregated counts of shopping_mall_products per brand from the shopping_mall_brands table.

responseBody.description: Array of brand-level product count statistics, each entry representing a single brand and its productCount.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: At least one brand should exist in the shopping_mall_brands table so that brand-level product count statistics have brand entities to aggregate over.
Sellers create catalog products associated with brands in the shopping_mall_products table; these products are required for computing per-brand product counts.
Platform administrators can also create catalog products linked to brands in shopping_mall_products; such products form the data set over which brand-level product counts are aggregated.

operations.specification:
This operation returns a summary of product counts grouped by status across the entire shoppingMall catalog. It is a read-only analytical endpoint based primarily on the shopping_mall_products table, which holds product status information (for example, draft, active, archived, or blocked), and may also factor in other catalog-related tables depending on the schema.

The implementation should execute an aggregation query that:

- Groups products by their status field(s) as defined in the shopping_mall_products schema
- Counts the number of products in each status bucket
- Optionally computes additional derived metrics if required by the DTO, such as ratios or totals

This endpoint is designed for dashboards and operational monitoring rather than browsing or editing individual products. It provides an at-a-glance view of catalog health and workflow distribution (e.g., how many products still sit in draft or require moderation).
operations.description:
Return an aggregated summary of the number of catalog products in each status category, based on the shopping_mall_products table.

The operation reads from the shopping_mall_products entity, which contains each product's current lifecycle or publication status. Typical statuses might include draft, pending review, active, suspended, or archived, depending on how the Prisma schema defines the product status field. The endpoint groups all products by these statuses and returns the counts per status bucket in a compact summary structure.

This statistical overview is intended for platform administrators and internal catalog managers who need to monitor how products are distributed across different workflow stages. For example, a spike in pending or rejected products may indicate issues in seller behavior or moderation policies, while a large number of archived items may impact search results and catalog freshness. The operation is strictly read-only and does not modify any product records or statuses.

Related operations may include more detailed product search endpoints or admin tools that list products filtered by specific status values. Those endpoints provide row-level detail, whereas this summary endpoint focuses on aggregate counts to power dashboards, KPIs, and alerting thresholds. Error handling should follow general API conventions, returning suitable error responses if the underlying aggregation fails or if authorization checks do not pass.
operations.summary: Get an aggregated status distribution summary for shopping_mall_products.

responseBody.description: Object containing product status buckets and their corresponding counts across the catalog.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: At least one product must exist in the catalog before aggregated status distribution statistics over shopping_mall_products are meaningful. Creating a product ensures there is a row in shopping_mall_products whose status can be counted by this analytical endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new guest shopping cart in the shopping_mall_guest_carts Prisma model. It is used for unauthenticated visitors (guests) who start adding items before creating an account or logging in. The operation will insert a new row into shopping_mall_guest_carts with the necessary identifying fields (such as a generated cart ID, timestamps, and any metadata defined in the schema) and initialize it in an empty state without any line items.

The business purpose is to provide a temporary, anonymous cart container that can later be associated with a guest session, converted to a customer cart when the user registers or logs in, or simply used for one-time checkout flows that the business supports. Implementation should respect any uniqueness constraints on identifiers present in shopping_mall_guest_carts and follow the model’s required fields and default values.

Clients will send the required creation payload using the IShoppingMallGuestCart.ICreate DTO, which is derived directly from the shopping_mall_guest_carts schema (excluding system-managed fields like auto-generated IDs or timestamps if those exist). The service layer will validate this data according to the Prisma model’s constraints and business rules before persisting the new guest cart and returning the created cart as an IShoppingMallGuestCart DTO.
operations.description:
Create a new guest cart record in the shopping_mall_guest_carts table for an unauthenticated visitor.

This operation is designed for the guest user flow where a visitor has not yet logged in or registered but wants to start building a cart. It inserts a new row into the shopping_mall_guest_carts Prisma model, using the fields described in that schema (such as the cart identifier, linkage to a guest user identity if present, and any configuration or region context). Required fields defined in the Prisma schema must be provided through the IShoppingMallGuestCart.ICreate request body or defaulted at the database level.

Security-wise, this endpoint is intentionally public and does not require prior authentication, so authorizationActors is set to an empty array. Implementations should still apply appropriate rate limiting and basic abuse protection because cart creation is an inexpensive, repeatable operation that could be targeted by bots. If the schema includes linkage to guest sessions, the service should ensure that the combination of session and cart obeys any uniqueness or lifecycle rules defined at the business level.

From a business-logic perspective, the created guest cart serves as the root parent entity for related records such as shopping_mall_guest_cart_items. Downstream operations like adding items, updating quantities, or converting the guest cart into a customer cart will rely on the identifier returned by this API. Any errors—such as violation of required fields or invalid foreign key references—should be surfaced as validation or conflict errors aligned with the platform’s general error-handling guidelines.

Related operations include reading an existing guest cart with GET /guestCarts/{guestCartId} and item-level operations that target the subsidiary shopping_mall_guest_cart_items table. Together, these endpoints support the complete guest shopping experience before authentication or account creation.
operations.summary: Create a new guest cart record in the shopping_mall_guest_carts table.

requestBody.description: Payload used to create a new guest cart for an unauthenticated visitor, based on the shopping_mall_guest_carts schema.

responseBody.description: The newly created guest cart, as stored in the shopping_mall_guest_carts table.

operations.name: create

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a single guest cart from the shopping_mall_guest_carts Prisma model by its unique identifier. It performs a read-only lookup of the cart row, typically using the primary key column (such as id) that corresponds to the guestCartId path parameter, and returns the cart data as an IShoppingMallGuestCart DTO.

The primary purpose is to allow clients to restore or inspect the state of a previously created guest cart—for example, when a visitor returns to the site with a stored cart identifier or when a front-end application reloads and needs to rehydrate the cart. The operation must only read from shopping_mall_guest_carts and should not modify any state. If additional projection or composition with related tables is required (such as loading line items from shopping_mall_guest_cart_items), that should be handled in the service implementation and reflected in the DTO if the design calls for it.

The endpoint expects a guestCartId path parameter, which represents the unique identifier of the guest cart record. The parameter should map to the primary key field in shopping_mall_guest_carts (commonly a UUID stored as a string). The response body uses the IShoppingMallGuestCart DTO, which aligns with the Prisma schema’s fields and any documented description comments for those columns.

Because guest carts are not sensitive user accounts and this read operation is primarily used to support anonymous shopping flows, the endpoint is configured as public with an empty authorizationActors array. Implementations should still ensure that only valid identifiers can be used and that no additional sensitive information beyond what is defined on shopping_mall_guest_carts is exposed. If the specified guestCartId does not exist, the API should return an appropriate not-found error consistent with the platform’s standard error responses.

This operation is typically used in conjunction with the POST /guestCarts creation endpoint and with item-level endpoints that operate on subsidiary tables such as shopping_mall_guest_cart_items. Client applications will call this endpoint whenever they need to re-fetch or synchronize the state of a guest cart using a known identifier.
operations.description:
Retrieve an existing guest cart from the shopping_mall_guest_carts table using its unique identifier.

This operation accepts a guestCartId path parameter, which is expected to correspond to the primary key column of the shopping_mall_guest_carts Prisma model (commonly represented as a UUID string). The service layer queries the database for the matching record and returns it as an IShoppingMallGuestCart DTO. If the underlying schema defines relationships to subsidiary entities like shopping_mall_guest_cart_items, the implementation may choose to include those related data in the response according to the DTO design.

The endpoint is public and does not require authentication, aligning with the anonymous guest cart use case. However, it must still validate that the provided guestCartId is well-formed and handle the case where no matching cart exists by returning an appropriate not-found response. No updates or side effects should occur during this read operation; it is strictly a retrieval of cart state from shopping_mall_guest_carts.

Clients typically call this API after a cart has been created via POST /guestCarts, when reloading a page, or when restoring a guest session from persisted storage. Along with item management operations on shopping_mall_guest_cart_items, this endpoint is a key part of maintaining a seamless shopping experience for unauthenticated users.
operations.summary: Get an existing guest cart from the shopping_mall_guest_carts table by its identifier.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target guest cart in the shopping_mall_guest_carts table.

responseBody.description: The guest cart corresponding to the provided guestCartId, as stored in the shopping_mall_guest_carts table.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A guest cart must be created in shopping_mall_guest_carts before it can be retrieved by its guestCartId.

operations.specification:
Update a specific guest shopping cart in the shopping_mall_guest_carts Prisma table, including its line items from shopping_mall_guest_cart_items. This operation allows the client (typically the web or mobile frontend) to replace the current state of a guest cart identified by its UUID guestCartId with a new set of items and associated cart-level properties such as currency or client metadata.

The implementation will load the target cart row from shopping_mall_guest_carts by its primary key, validate that it is still active/usable according to business rules (for example, not already converted into an order), and then reconcile the provided list of items with existing shopping_mall_guest_cart_items for that cart. Items for SKUs not present in the request will be removed; quantities for existing items will be updated; and new rows will be inserted for newly added SKUs. The cart's aggregate values (such as total quantity or cached price breakdowns, if present in the schema) will then be recalculated and persisted.

This API is designed as a full replacement (PUT) style update rather than a partial patch. The request body type IShoppingMallGuestCart.IUpdate will be aligned with the Prisma schema fields for shopping_mall_guest_carts and shopping_mall_guest_cart_items, excluding identifiers that are derived from the guestCartId path parameter. The response will return the updated cart as IShoppingMallGuestCart, including its nested items, so that the client always has a canonical view of the latest cart state.
operations.description:
Update the full state of a specific guest shopping cart identified by its UUID guestCartId.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_guest_carts table, which represents temporary carts owned by unauthenticated guest users of the shoppingMall platform. Each cart aggregates one or more line items stored in the shopping_mall_guest_cart_items table, each referencing a specific SKU and quantity. The API expects that the client sends the complete desired cart contents via the IShoppingMallGuestCart.IUpdate DTO, which mirrors the configurable fields of the cart as defined in the Prisma schema together with an items collection representing the desired line items.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is typically public in the sense that it does not require an authenticated customer or seller session, because guest carts are associated with anonymous browser sessions or device identifiers. However, the implementation must still validate that the provided guestCartId actually corresponds to a cart that belongs to the calling context (for example by matching on a cookie or other session token) to avoid exposing or modifying another visitor's cart. Rate limiting and size limits on the number of items per cart should also be enforced according to platform policy settings in tables such as shopping_mall_mall_configs or related configuration entities if present.

Internally, the service will load the shopping_mall_guest_carts row, verify that it is not already locked or converted to an order, and then perform a reconciliation against the shopping_mall_guest_cart_items rows scoped by the cart's primary key. Any existing item whose SKU is omitted from the new item list will be deleted; items whose SKU appears with a quantity of zero may also be removed according to business rules; and items present with positive quantities will be inserted or updated accordingly. After persisting these changes, any derived fields on the cart (like totals, currency, or last_updated timestamps) will be recalculated. If the cart cannot be found, the API should respond with a 404-style error, and if validation fails it should return a structured validation error as described in the general exception-handling requirements.

Clients typically call this endpoint after local cart editing operations (adding, removing, or changing quantities of items) to synchronize the browser's in-memory cart with the server-side representation. It is closely related to any "get guest cart" and "create guest cart" operations that may exist, and is usually invoked before a guest proceeds to checkout and transitions into a customer order in shopping_mall_orders. Error handling should clearly distinguish between missing carts, invalid SKUs, and inventory or policy violations so that the frontend can present meaningful feedback to the user.
operations.summary: Update an existing guest cart in shopping_mall_guest_carts including its items via full replacement.

parameters.name: guestCartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target guest cart record in shopping_mall_guest_carts whose state will be fully updated.

requestBody.description: Complete replacement payload for the guest cart state, excluding identifiers derived from the guestCartId path parameter, following the shopping_mall_guest_carts and shopping_mall_guest_cart_items schema fields.

responseBody.description: The updated guest cart record from shopping_mall_guest_carts including its reconciled line items from shopping_mall_guest_cart_items.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: The target guest cart must already exist in shopping_mall_guest_carts before its full state can be replaced using this update operation.
At least one guest cart item can be created in shopping_mall_guest_cart_items under this cart so that the update operation can reconcile incoming items against existing ones when needed.

operations.specification:
Permanently delete a specific guest shopping cart from the shopping_mall_guest_carts Prisma table, along with all of its associated line items from shopping_mall_guest_cart_items. This operation removes the server-side representation of a guest cart identified by its UUID guestCartId when it is no longer needed, such as when the visitor explicitly clears their cart or when a cart is invalidated by business logic.

The implementation will locate the shopping_mall_guest_carts row by its primary key derived from the guestCartId path parameter, ensure that the cart is eligible for deletion (for example, it has not already been converted to a customer order in shopping_mall_orders), and then delete both the cart and its dependent shopping_mall_guest_cart_items rows in a single transactional operation. No request body is necessary, and the operation does not return the deleted cart in the response body; clients rely on the success status code to confirm that the cart has been removed.

This deletion is a hard delete operation that physically removes rows from the database rather than marking them as deleted, because the Prisma schema for shopping_mall_guest_carts is assumed not to define a dedicated deletion flag column. Any cleanup of related session or tracking data outside these two tables is handled by other components of the system.
operations.description:
Delete a specific guest shopping cart and its line items from the shopping_mall_guest_carts and shopping_mall_guest_cart_items tables.

This operation focuses on the shopping_mall_guest_carts table, which represents temporary, unauthenticated guest carts in the shoppingMall platform. Each guest cart is associated with zero or more line items stored in the shopping_mall_guest_cart_items table. When a guest wishes to clear their cart, or when the system determines that a specific cart should no longer exist (for example, after a successful checkout that migrates contents into shopping_mall_orders), this endpoint can be invoked to remove the cart record and all of its dependent items.

From an access control point of view, the endpoint is considered public in the sense that it is not tied to an authenticated customer account, but the implementation must still ensure that the caller is entitled to operate on the targeted guest cart. This is generally enforced by validating that the guestCartId in the path is associated with the caller's browser or device session, often using a cookie, token, or similar correlation mechanism. The system should also check that the cart has not already been transformed into an order to avoid accidentally removing historical data required for audit or reporting.

Technically, the provider handling this operation will read the shopping_mall_guest_carts row by its primary key, verify any deletion preconditions (such as status fields defined in the Prisma schema), and then execute a transaction that deletes all related shopping_mall_guest_cart_items rows before deleting the cart itself. If the cart does not exist, a 404-style error is returned. If business rules prevent deletion (for example, due to a locked status), a suitable error with a clear explanation should be sent back. This endpoint is typically used in conjunction with guest cart retrieval and update operations and helps keep the database clean by removing stale or abandoned guest carts when appropriate.
operations.summary: Delete an existing guest cart from shopping_mall_guest_carts together with its items.

parameters.name: guestCartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the guest cart in shopping_mall_guest_carts to be deleted.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A guest cart must exist in shopping_mall_guest_carts before it can be deleted by its guestCartId.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the list of items currently contained in a specific guest cart in the shoppingMall platform. It is associated with the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` primary table, which represents anonymous or unauthenticated shoppers' carts, and the subsidiary `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table, which stores individual line items referencing specific SKUs and quantities.

The endpoint is designed as a PATCH method on `/guestCarts/{guestCartId}/items` to support potential future extensions for complex filtering or projection of cart items, while the initial implementation behaves as a straightforward list retrieval of all active items for the given guest cart. The core responsibility is to read from the guest cart and its related guest cart items, without performing any modification or side effects.

The operation does not require authentication because guest carts are typically linked to a client-side identifier (such as a cookie or local storage token) rather than a logged-in account. However, the implementation must still validate that the provided `guestCartId` corresponds to an existing, non-expired guest cart, and that the cart has not been converted into a customer cart as part of a login or checkout flow.

The response returns a structured collection of guest cart items in a paginated summary form, using the DTO type `IPageIShoppingMallGuestCartItem.ISummary`. Each summary entry is expected to include SKU identifiers, associated product information in summarized form, quantities, and pricing snapshots as modeled in the underlying Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` and any related tables. No request body is required for this basic retrieval use case, so `requestBody` is null and all inputs are conveyed via the path parameter.

Error handling must cover cases where the guest cart does not exist, is expired, or the identifier is malformed. In such cases the implementation should return appropriate HTTP error responses such as 404 for not found and 400 for invalid identifiers. Since this is a read-only operation, it must not modify any state in the underlying database tables.
operations.description:
Retrieve all items currently stored in a specific guest cart identified by its unique guestCartId on the shoppingMall platform.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` table, which defines temporary shopping carts owned by unauthenticated guest users, and the related `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table, which contains individual line items referring to SKUs, quantities, and pricing snapshots captured at the time items were added. The `guestCartId` path parameter is treated as the unique identifier of the guest cart record, matching the primary key of `shopping_mall_guest_carts` in the Prisma schema.

When invoked, the system looks up the guest cart using the provided identifier and then queries the associated guest cart items. The response is shaped into a paginated collection using the `IPageIShoppingMallGuestCartItem.ISummary` DTO, where each summary entry represents an individual line item. Summary objects typically include SKU references, basic product metadata, the quantity in the cart, and pricing information appropriate for display in a mini-cart or full cart page. The exact fields included in the summary are defined by the DTO but are ultimately backed by columns in `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` and joined product-related tables.

Because guest carts are associated with unauthenticated visitors, this endpoint does not enforce user-level authentication, and `authorizationActors` is an empty array. Nevertheless, the implementation must validate that the `guestCartId` is structurally valid and corresponds to an existing cart record that has not expired, been invalidated, or already been migrated into a persistent customer cart. If the cart is not found, the API should respond with a 404 error; if the identifier format is invalid, a 400 error is appropriate.

This endpoint is read-only and must not change any state in the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` or `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` tables. Related operations that work with the same tables include the POST `/guestCarts/{guestCartId}/items` endpoint for adding new items, and potential future endpoints for updating quantities or clearing the cart. Clients will typically call this list operation after mutating operations to refresh the cart view shown to the user.
operations.summary: Retrieve the list of shopping_mall_guest_cart_items for a specific shopping_mall_guest_carts record.

parameters.name: guestCartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target guest cart whose items should be retrieved. This value maps directly to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` table and is expected to be a string identifier such as a UUID or opaque token assigned when the guest cart was created.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of guest cart item summary objects representing the current contents of the specified guest cart.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A guest cart record must be created in shopping_mall_guest_carts so that guestCartId refers to an existing cart when listing its items.
Guest cart items must be created in shopping_mall_guest_cart_items under the specified guest cart before they can be listed.

operations.specification:
This operation adds a new item into a specific guest cart in the shoppingMall platform. It is primarily associated with the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` subsidiary table, which stores line items representing SKUs, quantities, and pricing snapshots, and secondarily with the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` primary table, which identifies the owning guest cart.

The endpoint is defined as `POST /guestCarts/{guestCartId}/items`. The `guestCartId` path parameter identifies the target guest cart record in `shopping_mall_guest_carts`. The request body uses the `IShoppingMallGuestCartItem.ICreate` DTO to carry the information required to create a new guest cart item, such as the SKU being added, the desired quantity, and any other attributes defined in the Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` (for example, initial pricing snapshots or references to promotional contexts).

On execution, the implementation must validate that the referenced guest cart exists and is eligible to receive new items (for example, it is not expired and has not been converted to a customer cart). It must also validate fields in the create DTO against the underlying Prisma schema and business rules, including SKU existence in `shopping_mall_product_skus`, inventory constraints from `shopping_mall_inventory_items`, and any relevant catalog visibility or age restriction policies. If the item already exists in the cart for the same SKU, business rules may dictate either creating a separate line or merging quantities; this behavior should be clearly specified in the service-layer logic and consistently applied.

The operation does not require authentication because guest carts are owned by unauthenticated visitors, but robust input validation and rate limiting should be applied to prevent abuse. The response returns the newly created guest cart item as a full entity representation using `IShoppingMallGuestCartItem`, allowing the client to immediately reflect the new line item in the cart UI.

Error handling must cover invalid or non-existent `guestCartId` values, invalid SKU references, violations of inventory or policy constraints, and any other inconsistencies detected during validation. Appropriate HTTP status codes such as 400 for validation errors and 404 for missing guest carts or SKUs must be returned, with structured error bodies consistent with the platform-wide error handling strategy.
operations.description:
Create a new line item within a specific guest cart identified by its unique guestCartId on the shoppingMall platform.

This operation writes to the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table, which models individual line items belonging to a guest cart, and uses the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` table to locate and validate the owning cart. The `guestCartId` path parameter points to the primary key of the guest cart row, while the request body, shaped as `IShoppingMallGuestCartItem.ICreate`, provides details such as the SKU to add, the quantity, and any other attributes defined in the Prisma schema. The DTO mirrors the structure of `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` and ensures that only allowed fields are accepted on creation.

When the endpoint is invoked, the system first resolves the guest cart by the provided identifier. If the cart is not found, has expired, or has been migrated to a customer context, the API must reject the request with an appropriate error, typically 404 for a missing cart or 409 if business rules dictate a conflict scenario. Once the cart is validated, the service checks that the requested SKU exists in `shopping_mall_product_skus`, that inventory in `shopping_mall_inventory_items` is sufficient for the desired quantity, and that any relevant visibility, age restriction, or compliance flags do not prohibit adding this item to the cart.

Upon successful validation, a new record is created in `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items`, storing references to the guest cart and SKU as well as the requested quantity and pricing snapshot fields as modeled in the schema. The created entity is then mapped to the `IShoppingMallGuestCartItem` DTO and returned to the client. This enables the frontend to update the cart representation immediately based on the authoritative state from the backend.

Because guest carts are used by unauthenticated users, this endpoint does not require authentication, and `authorizationActors` is an empty array. Nevertheless, implementations should apply rate limiting and robust validation to mitigate abuse. Related operations include PATCH `/guestCarts/{guestCartId}/items` for listing current cart contents and potential future PUT or DELETE endpoints for modifying or removing individual guest cart items.
operations.summary: Create a new shopping_mall_guest_cart_items record under a specific shopping_mall_guest_carts guest cart.

parameters.name: guestCartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target guest cart into which a new item will be inserted. This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` table and is typically a string such as a UUID or opaque token issued when the guest cart was created.

requestBody.description: Payload describing the new guest cart item to create, including the SKU identifier, quantity, and any other creation-time fields defined for `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items`. The DTO is scoped to fields that are allowed on creation and excludes server-managed columns.

responseBody.description: The newly created guest cart item entity associated with the specified guest cart, including identifiers, SKU reference, quantity, and pricing snapshot fields as modeled in the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: Guest cart must be created before a new guest cart item can be added under it, because guestCartId must reference an existing shopping_mall_guest_carts record.
Product SKU must exist in shopping_mall_product_skus before it can be referenced by sku_id when creating a guest cart item.

operations.specification:
Retrieve a single guest cart item by its identifier within a specific guest cart. This operation is associated with the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` Prisma model, which represents individual line items in a temporary shopping cart owned by an unauthenticated guest user, and the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` model, which owns these items.

The endpoint `GET /guestCarts/{guestCartId}/items/{guestCartItemId}` returns the detailed representation of one cart item, including SKU reference, quantity, and pricing snapshot fields defined on `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items`. The `guestCartId` is used to ensure the item belongs to the expected cart, preventing cross-cart access when only the item ID is known.

This is a read-only operation: it does not mutate inventory, pricing, or cart state. It is primarily used by the front-end when restoring or validating a guest cart (for example, when a guest user reloads the page or resumes a checkout flow) and needs to display individual line details. Because guest carts are tied to ephemeral identities such as browser sessions or signed cookies, authorization is handled at a higher layer, and the operation itself is exposed as a public endpoint in terms of `authorizationActors`.

The response body uses the DTO `IShoppingMallGuestCartItem`, derived from the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table, containing all fields necessary to render a cart line item in the UI, including quantity, price information snapshot, and links to the associated SKU or product for further lookup.
operations.description:
Fetch detailed information about a single item inside an unauthenticated guest user's shopping cart.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table, which stores line items for guest carts, and ensures that the requested `guestCartItemId` is associated with the specified `guestCartId`. Typical fields on this model include foreign keys to the owning guest cart and the selected SKU, numeric quantity fields, and snapshot pricing/discount fields so that the cart can present a stable view of what the user intended to purchase.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is conceptually public because guest carts are not tied to a logged-in account. Actual access control is enforced at the infrastructure layer using a guest cart token or cookie that maps to `guestCartId`. The API operation itself therefore declares an empty `authorizationActors` array and expects upstream middleware to ensure only the rightful guest session can resolve and view the corresponding cart and item.

In relation to other operations, clients will usually call this endpoint after manipulating cart contents, or when rehydrating a cart from a stored identifier, to confirm the current state of a single item. It is complementary to list-style operations on guest cart items and to write operations that add or update cart lines. The endpoint is read-only: it must not adjust inventory reservations or modify any order-related records, and it should respond with a clear error if the cart or item does not exist or the item does not belong to the given cart.
operations.summary: Get a specific guest cart item from the shopping_mall_guest_cart_items table by cart and item identifiers.
