It operates on the shopping_mall_seller_payout_items Prisma model and must respect all constraints and relationships defined there, including foreign keys to the seller payout batch, seller, and any referenced orders or order lines.

Because payout items contribute to financial balances, deletion is tightly controlled. The implementation should check the parent payout's status field(s) as described in the Prisma schema comments, ensuring that deletions are only allowed while the payout is in a draft, pending, or otherwise non-final state. When an item is erased, the system should recalculate any aggregate totals on the parent payout as needed. All such operations should be wrapped in a transaction to maintain consistency between the item table and the parent payout table.
operations.description:
Erase a single seller payout item from a seller payout batch in the shopping_mall_seller_payout_items table, subject to strict financial and audit constraints.

This operation is intended for platform administrators performing back-office corrections. Each seller payout item is a financial record that contributes to the payout total for a seller, so deleting an item is only appropriate when a clear business reason exists, such as the item being created in error or referencing a cancelled underlying transaction that should not be paid out. The Prisma schema for shopping_mall_seller_payout_items typically documents these relationships and the role of each item in settlement.

Access to this endpoint must be restricted to high-privilege actors only. The authorizationActors array therefore uses the "platformAdmin" actor role. The controller and service implementation must verify that the authenticated actor has platform administrator privileges before proceeding. Additionally, business logic must check that the parent payout identified by sellerPayoutId remains in an editable state; if it has already been paid, exported to accounting, or locked by audit policies (as documented in the schema comments), the delete attempt should be rejected with a conflict or similar error.

On successful execution, the target payout item row is completely removed from the database, and any dependent aggregates such as the payout's total amount or item count are updated in the same transaction to remain accurate. This operation complements other administrative payout management APIs such as listing payout items, retrieving details of a single item, and updating an item via the corresponding PUT endpoint on the same path.
operations.summary: Erase a seller payout item record from the shopping_mall_seller_payout_items table.

parameters.name: sellerPayoutId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the parent seller payout batch to which the target payout item currently belongs.

parameters.name: sellerPayoutItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific seller payout item within the seller payout batch that will be permanently removed.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: The seller payout batch must exist before a specific seller payout item within that batch can be deleted; creating the batch generates the sellerPayoutId used in this delete operation.

A seller payout item must first be created within the target payout batch before it can be removed; this operation creates the item and returns the sellerPayoutItemId referenced by the delete endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves aggregated payment transaction statistics grouped by payment status from the Prisma model shopping_mall_payment_transactions. It is designed to give business stakeholders and platform operators an at-a-glance view of how many payment transactions exist in each status (such as pending, authorized, captured, failed, refunded) and the corresponding monetary totals.

The endpoint does not map one-to-one to a single row in the database; instead, it computes a statistical view over many rows. It is strictly read-only and does not modify any underlying payment or order data. The resulting DTO type, IShoppingMallPaymentStatusStatistics, represents computed metrics rather than a persisted entity. The implementation will typically execute a GROUP BY over the status column in shopping_mall_payment_transactions (and possibly filter by date range or payment method based on additional query or request criteria defined in the DTO), and then project the grouped results into this DTO structure.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics of payment transactions grouped by their current status in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation is built on top of the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma model, which stores individual payment transactions associated with customer orders in the marketplace. For each status value recorded in this table (for example, pending, authorized, captured, failed, cancelled, or refunded, depending on the final schema), the implementation computes aggregate metrics such as the total number of transactions and the total monetary volume. These aggregates help business stakeholders monitor payment health, detect anomalies, and understand cash flow patterns without exposing sensitive per-transaction details.

From a security perspective, this is an informational, read-only endpoint intended primarily for internal dashboards or administrative tools. The endpoint itself only exposes aggregated values, not raw card or account information, and therefore can be safely used in reporting contexts where detailed PII is not required. Access control can be implemented so that only appropriate actors, such as platform administrators or financial operations staff, can call this endpoint, but the underlying operation remains a pure read against the payment transaction data.

The operation is conceptually related to other payment and refund reporting endpoints. For example, it can be used together with the refunds-by-reason statistics endpoint to provide a complete view of payment lifecycle performance: this endpoint focuses on how many transactions are in each status and how much money is associated with them, while the refunds endpoint focuses on why money is returned. Error handling should ensure that, if there are no payment transactions in the database or within the specified filters, the API still returns a valid response object with empty arrays or zeroed aggregates rather than an error, making it easy for clients to consume this data in dashboards.
operations.summary: Get aggregated payment statistics grouped by status from shopping_mall_payment_transactions

responseBody.description: Aggregated payment transaction statistics grouped by payment status, including counts and monetary totals per status bucket.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: At least one payment transaction should exist in shopping_mall_payment_transactions so that the statistics endpoint has data to aggregate; this operation creates such a transaction to contribute to the status-based statistics.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves aggregated refund statistics grouped by refund reason from the Prisma model shopping_mall_refund_transactions, and optionally any associated reason-code or classification models if present. It is intended to give administrators and analysts a clear picture of why refunds are being issued across the platform, helping to identify patterns such as product quality issues, shipping problems, or payment errors.

Rather than returning individual refund records, the endpoint computes a statistical view by grouping refund transactions according to their recorded reason or reason code. For each reason group, it calculates metrics such as the number of refunds and the total refunded amount. The response is represented by a computed DTO type IShoppingMallRefundReasonStatistics, which is not a direct mapping of a single table row but a structured aggregation of multiple rows (and possibly joined metadata about reasons).

The operation is read-only, has no side effects on underlying refund or order data, and is suitable for use in dashboards, reports, and analytical tooling where understanding refund drivers is critical for improving the shopping experience and reducing operational costs.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated refund statistics for the shoppingMall platform, grouped by the business reason associated with each refund transaction.

This endpoint is based primarily on the shopping_mall_refund_transactions Prisma model, which represents refund transactions that return funds to customers for all or part of an order. In many implementations, each refund transaction includes a structured reason field or a reference to a reason code table that classifies why the refund occurred, such as customer remorse, product defect, shipment delay, or payment processing error. The operation groups refund records by these reasons and computes aggregate metrics like total refund count and total refunded amount per reason.

From a security and compliance standpoint, the endpoint exposes only aggregated monetary values and high-level reason categories. It does not reveal sensitive payment instrument details or full customer identities, making it appropriate for use on internal analytics dashboards or admin reporting tools. Access control can be configured so that only appropriate actors, such as platform administrators or financial operations staff, can invoke this endpoint, but the underlying data access pattern remains a pure read of aggregated refund information.

This endpoint is complementary to the payments-by-status statistics endpoint. While payments-by-status focuses on the health and progression of payment transactions, this refunds-by-reason endpoint explains why money is being returned. Together, they provide a holistic view of payment and refund dynamics on the shoppingMall platform. Error handling should ensure that the API returns an empty or zeroed statistics structure when there are no matching refund transactions, allowing client dashboards to handle the response gracefully without special-casing nulls or missing fields.
operations.summary: Get aggregated refund statistics grouped by refund reason from shopping_mall_refund_transactions

responseBody.description: Aggregated refund statistics grouped by refund reason, including counts and monetary totals per reason bucket.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A refund transaction must exist in shopping_mall_refund_transactions before aggregated refund statistics by reason can be computed. This POST operation creates refund transaction records that are later read and grouped by reason in the refunds-by-reason statistics endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves aggregated statistics about payment chargebacks grouped by their current status using data from the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` Prisma table. It is a read-only analytics endpoint that computes counts and optionally monetary totals per chargeback status to support risk monitoring and financial reporting.

Implementation-wise, the service will query the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` model, grouping rows by the status field (for example, distinct status values stored in the schema) and computing aggregate metrics such as the number of chargebacks per status and the total disputed amount per status. The operation does not expose raw chargeback records; instead it returns a denormalized analytical DTO `IShoppingMallChargebackStatusStatistics` that contains one entry per status with its associated aggregates.

This endpoint is designed for back-office dashboards, finance, and risk teams who need a quick view of how many chargebacks exist in each state over a given time window. Filtering (such as by date range, payment method, seller, or region) can be added within the implementation and reflected in the DTO, but the core contract remains that the response is an aggregated, status-centric view, not individual chargeback rows.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics about payment chargebacks grouped by status based on data from the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` Prisma model.

This operation serves the business need of monitoring risk and financial exposure related to disputed payments. Instead of returning individual chargeback records, it returns an analytical view where each entry corresponds to a particular chargeback status and includes aggregate metrics such as how many chargebacks are currently in that status and what total disputed amount they represent. The underlying data comes from the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table, which stores information about chargebacks raised through financial institutions against completed payments.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint should not be exposed to general customers or sellers. It is primarily intended for internal platform staff such as risk analysts, finance staff, and platform administrators. For that reason, the endpoint is restricted to the `platformAdmin` actor via the `authorizationActors` field, and the implementation should ensure that only authenticated platform administrators can access the data. The aggregation itself is read-only and does not modify any underlying records.

In terms of relationships, each chargeback record in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` is typically associated with payment transactions and orders, but this operation deliberately abstracts away those details to present only status-level aggregates. Implementations may optionally allow filters to restrict the aggregation to particular time windows, payment methods, or seller segments, but those filters are modeled outside the path as query parameters or in higher-level configuration, not as path parameters. If the Prisma schema includes fields such as creation timestamps or monetary amounts, they should be used to compute the aggregates.

Related operations might include more detailed chargeback listing endpoints (for example, a PATCH /chargebacks search API) or overall payment statistics endpoints. However, this specific operation focuses only on the status distribution of chargebacks, which is a common KPI for risk and finance dashboards. Error handling should ensure that, if no chargebacks exist or filters exclude all data, the endpoint still returns a valid response with an empty list of status entries rather than an error, clearly indicating that there are currently no matching chargebacks.
operations.summary: Get aggregated statistics of payment chargebacks by status from shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks

responseBody.description: Aggregated statistics of payment chargebacks grouped by their status, including counts and monetary totals per status.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A payment chargeback record must exist in shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks before aggregated chargeback statistics by status can be computed. This POST operation creates chargeback records that are later read and grouped by status in the chargebacks-by-status statistics endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves aggregated statistics about seller payout activity over a specified time period using the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma table as its primary data source. It is a read-only analytics endpoint that summarizes how much has been paid out to sellers, how many payout batches were processed, and potentially other indicators such as average payout amount during the requested period.

Implementation-wise, the service queries `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`, applying optional filters for a requested date range and possibly for specific sellers, regions, or payout methods as defined in the request DTO `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutPeriodStatistics.IRequest`. The query will group results by a chosen time grain (for example, day, week, or month) and compute aggregates such as total payout amount, number of payout batches, and number of distinct sellers receiving payouts in each period bucket. The resulting analytical series is returned in a DTO `IPageIShoppingMallSellerPayoutPeriodStatistics` that supports pagination over time buckets or over combined filter dimensions.

This endpoint is designed for financial reporting and marketplace health monitoring. It allows platform administrators and finance teams to understand payout dynamics, track growth in seller earnings, and reconcile external accounting systems. Because it is analytical and read-only, it does not modify any records in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` or related tables, but it relies on the correctness and completeness of those records for accurate reporting.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics of seller payout activity over a specified time period using data from the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model.

This operation supports finance, accounting, and marketplace management use cases by providing a summarized view of how funds are being distributed from the platform to sellers. The underlying `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` table records payout batches that transfer funds from the platform to individual sellers. For reporting, this endpoint allows callers to specify a time window and optionally other filter criteria, then returns aggregated values such as total payout amount within that window, the number of payout batches processed, and how many sellers received payouts.

Security-wise, this endpoint exposes sensitive financial information and must be restricted to internal actors such as platform administrators. Accordingly, the `authorizationActors` field is set to `["platformAdmin"]`. Implementations should ensure that authentication and authorization checks are in place so that only properly privileged users can access the statistics. The endpoint itself is read-only and intended only for dashboard views and reporting tools.

The request body type `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutPeriodStatistics.IRequest` should capture filter parameters such as start and end timestamps, optional seller identifiers, and the desired time granularity for aggregation (for example, daily or monthly). The response type `IPageIShoppingMallSellerPayoutPeriodStatistics` represents a paginated collection where each item corresponds to a single period bucket and contains its aggregated metrics. This pattern aligns with other analytical endpoints that return time-series or period-based statistics rather than individual database rows. If no payouts exist in the requested period, the endpoint should return an empty list with pagination metadata indicating zero total items instead of treating the situation as an error.
operations.summary: Search seller payout statistics by period using shopping_mall_seller_payouts aggregates

requestBody.description: Filter and aggregation parameters, including time range and optional seller filters, for computing seller payout statistics by period.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of aggregated seller payout statistics per period bucket matching the requested filters.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Seller payout batch records must exist in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` before aggregated payout statistics can be computed over a period.

operations.specification:
This operation computes analytics for the payment funnel of the shoppingMall platform using data from multiple Prisma tables related to orders and payments. It does not correspond to a single Prisma model but instead aggregates information from shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_payment_transactions, shopping_mall_payment_authorizations, shopping_mall_payment_captures, shopping_mall_payment_status_events, shopping_mall_refund_transactions, and shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks.

The endpoint accepts a complex search and filter payload that specifies time ranges, segmentation dimensions (such as region, payment method, and device or channel if present in the schema), and optional filters on order or payment attributes. It then computes funnel stages such as orders created, payments initiated, authorizations approved, captures completed, refunds issued, and chargebacks recorded, along with conversion rates between stages. The response is a structured analytics DTO that surfaces counts, monetary totals, and conversion percentages per segment and overall for the selected period.

The analytics are read-only and do not modify any underlying data. They are designed for use in dashboards and reporting tools to help business stakeholders understand payment performance, identify bottlenecks in the payment funnel, and monitor the impact of payment configuration changes or external payment provider issues.
operations.description:
Retrieve analytical statistics describing the payment funnel behavior on the shoppingMall platform over a specified time window.

This operation reads from the shopping_mall_orders table to identify the universe of orders in scope, typically constrained by order creation or checkout completion timestamps. It then joins to the shopping_mall_payment_transactions model to locate associated payment attempts per order, as well as to shopping_mall_payment_authorizations and shopping_mall_payment_captures to determine which transactions successfully progressed through authorization and capture stages. Additional read access is performed on shopping_mall_payment_status_events to reconstruct the lifecycle of each payment, and on shopping_mall_refund_transactions and shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks to understand how much of the authorized and captured volume was later reversed.

Security considerations: this is a read-only analytics endpoint intended for internal stakeholders such as platform administrators, finance teams, and risk analysts. It should not expose sensitive per-customer details such as full PANs or personally identifiable information. Instead, the response focuses on aggregated counts, amounts, and ratios. Access should therefore typically be restricted to the platformAdmin actor, with rate limiting appropriate for dashboard refresh intervals rather than end-user browsing patterns.

The request body allows specifying reporting time ranges, segmentation dimensions (for example by region, payment method, or seller), and optional filters on order or payment attributes to narrow the scope. The backend implementation must validate that requested time windows are reasonable, that segment combinations do not generate excessive cardinality, and that callers are authorized to see the requested scope (for example, platform admins may see global data, while in some deployments a finance operator might be limited to a subset of regions).

The response summarizes, for each segment and overall, funnel stages such as orders created, payments initiated, authorizations approved, captures completed, refunds processed, and chargebacks raised. It also exposes conversion rates between stages and monetary totals for authorized, captured, refunded, and charged-back amounts. This endpoint will usually be consumed together with other analytics APIs such as seller earnings analytics to provide a complete view of financial health.
operations.summary: Compute aggregated payment funnel analytics using shoppingMall order and payment-related tables.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and segmentation criteria for computing the payment funnel analytics over a selected time range.

responseBody.description: Aggregated payment funnel analytics including counts, monetary totals, and conversion rates per segment and overall.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Customer orders must exist in `shopping_mall_orders` for the payment funnel to have an order base to analyze.
Payment transactions must exist in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` so that stages like payments initiated, authorized, and captured can be computed in the funnel analytics.
Payment authorization attempts must exist in `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` to compute authorization-related stages and conversion rates within the payment funnel.
Payment capture records must exist in `shopping_mall_payment_captures` so that captured amounts and capture-stage metrics can be calculated for the payment funnel analytics.
Refund transactions must exist in `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` so that refund counts and refunded amounts can be reflected in the payment funnel analytics.
Chargeback records must exist in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` to compute chargeback counts and amounts as a final stage in the payment funnel analytics.

operations.specification:
This operation computes seller earnings analytics for the shoppingMall platform by aggregating financial data from multiple Prisma tables related to seller payouts and underlying orders. It does not map to a single Prisma model but composes information from shopping_mall_seller_payouts, shopping_mall_seller_payout_items, shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_seller_segments, shopping_mall_order_lines, shopping_mall_refund_transactions, shopping_mall_refund_items, and shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.

The endpoint accepts a complex analytics request payload that specifies time ranges, seller selection criteria, segmentation dimensions (such as region, category, or payout cycle), and optional filters on order or payout attributes. It then calculates per-seller earnings including gross merchandise value (GMV), platform fees, net earnings, refunded amounts, chargebacks impact if applicable, and payout status across the requested period.

This is a read-only analytics endpoint designed for administrative dashboards, financial reconciliation tools, and potentially seller-facing analytics panels if the implementation chooses to share subsets of this information directly with sellers. The response uses a dedicated analytics DTO rather than directly exposing raw Prisma entities, providing aggregated numbers and trend indicators suitable for visualization.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated seller earnings analytics across a specified time range on the shoppingMall platform.

Internally, this operation queries the shopping_mall_seller_payouts model to identify payout batches within the requested period and joins to shopping_mall_seller_payout_items to break down each payout batch into per-order or per-line components. It leverages shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_seller_segments, and shopping_mall_order_lines for contextual order information and line-level amounts, and consults shopping_mall_refund_transactions alongside shopping_mall_refund_items to net out refunded portions from gross earnings. Where available, it can also surface risk or performance indicators based on shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries to help interpret the earnings figures.

Security considerations: this analytics endpoint typically exposes sensitive financial information including seller-level revenue, fees, and payout status. By default it should be restricted to the platformAdmin actor, with any seller-facing variant enforcing strict scoping so that a seller only sees their own earnings. The design here uses an administrative actor model, expecting that seller self-service analytics would be implemented via a separate, more tightly scoped endpoint if required by the product.

The request body allows clients to specify reporting windows, seller selection (individual seller, group of sellers, or all sellers), segmentation dimensions (for example by region, category, or payout cycle), and sorting options. The backend must enforce reasonable limits on requested time ranges and segment cardinality to avoid heavy queries. It should also validate that the caller is authorized to access the requested seller scope.

The response summarizes, per seller and optionally per segment, values such as gross merchandise value, platform commissions and fees, discounts, refunded amounts, net earnings, and payout statuses. It can additionally return trend indicators compared to previous periods if the implementation chooses to compute these. This endpoint will commonly be used together with payment funnel analytics to provide a complete view of platform and seller financial performance.
operations.summary: Compute aggregated seller earnings analytics from shoppingMall seller payout and order-related tables.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and segmentation criteria for computing seller earnings analytics over a selected time range.

responseBody.description: Aggregated seller earnings analytics including per-seller gross amounts, fees, refunds, and net earnings.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Seller payout batches must exist in shopping_mall_seller_payouts so that aggregated seller earnings analytics can compute metrics based on payout data for each seller.

operations.specification:
This operation provides a paginated, filterable financial report that summarizes payment transactions, refunds, chargebacks, and seller payouts to produce a settlement view for the shoppingMall platform. It primarily aggregates data from the Prisma models `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`, `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`, and `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`, without mapping directly to a single table.

The endpoint is designed for administrative and finance-team users to reconcile platform-level payment flows with external payment gateways and accounting systems. It allows callers to specify a reporting window, filter by payment method, currency, seller, and high-level status flags, and retrieve normalized settlement rows that capture gross payment amounts, fees, net amounts, refunded portions, and chargeback impacts.

Although this report reads from multiple primary and subsidiary tables, it is implemented as a read-only analytical view. No records are created, updated, or removed in any of the underlying tables by this API. Instead, it performs read queries, joins, and aggregations across the payment and payout domain entities to compose a settlement statement for the requested period and scope.
operations.description:
Generate a detailed payment settlement report across payment, refund, chargeback, and payout data for the shoppingMall platform.

This operation is read-only and composes information from several Prisma models related to payments and settlements such as `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations`, `shopping_mall_payment_captures`, `shopping_mall_payment_status_events`, `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`, `shopping_mall_refund_items`, `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`, `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`, and `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`. The purpose is to present a unified settlement-oriented view that helps finance and operations teams reconcile total collected amounts, processor fees, net revenue, refunded totals, and chargeback exposure.

The request body allows specifying a date range (for example based on transaction creation time or capture time), payment method filters, currency filters, and optionally limiting the report to a specific seller or group of sellers. It may also support high-level status filters such as including only completed captures, including or excluding pending refunds, or including only settled payouts. These filters are represented by the DTO type `IShoppingMallPaymentSettlementReport.IRequest`, which encapsulates the business rules for what constitutes "in-scope" data for a given settlement run.

The response returns a paginated list of settlement rows using the DTO type `IPageIShoppingMallPaymentSettlementReportRow`. Each row aggregates one logical settlement unit, for example per order or per payment transaction, with fields for gross amount, total discounts, platform fees, processor fees, net amount to the platform, net amount to sellers, total refunded amount, chargeback amounts, and final settled status. The exact composition logic is aligned with the financial policies defined in the payment and refund policy tables (such as `shopping_mall_refund_policies`) but those policies themselves are not directly mutated by this API.

Security-wise, this endpoint is restricted to platform-level administrative actors represented by the `platformAdmin` role, because it exposes full-funnel financial amounts, fee breakdowns, and cross-seller data that should not be visible to customers or individual sellers. The implementation is expected to apply robust pagination and potentially asynchronous processing or caching if the requested time windows are large, but the API contract itself is synchronous and returns a normal paginated response.

Related endpoints include seller-facing reporting operations such as the seller payout statement report, as well as lower-level search APIs for raw payment transactions and refunds. However, this particular operation focuses specifically on an accounting-friendly settlement view that can be exported or used as the basis for reconciliation with external ledgers.
operations.summary: Generate a paginated payment settlement report aggregating payment-related tables in shoppingMall.

requestBody.description: Filter and configuration parameters for generating the payment settlement report, including date range, payment method filters, currencies, seller scoping, and status flags.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of settlement rows summarizing payment, refund, chargeback, and payout amounts for the requested period and filters.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Payment transactions must exist in shopping_mall_payment_transactions so that the settlement report can aggregate gross amounts, fees, and statuses for reconciliation.
Refund transactions must exist in shopping_mall_refund_transactions so that the settlement report can include refunded amounts when computing net settlement values.
Payment chargeback records must exist in shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks so settlement rows can reflect chargeback impacts on net revenue and exposure.
Seller payout batches must exist in shopping_mall_seller_payouts so the settlement report can correlate what has been paid out to sellers with collected payments, refunds, and chargebacks.

operations.specification:
This operation produces a seller-centric payout statement report for the shoppingMall platform, aligning financial information from the Prisma models `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`, `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`, `shopping_mall_orders`, `shopping_mall_order_lines`, and the various payment and refund entities such as `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` and `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`.

The core purpose of the endpoint is to allow authorized actors to retrieve, for a given seller or set of sellers and time period, a structured view of payout batches, the orders and order lines included in those payouts, associated fees, refunds, and adjustments. It is an analytical, read-only reporting API that helps sellers and platform finance teams understand how the final payout amounts were computed from raw orders and payment flows.

Rather than exposing a single underlying table, the operation constructs a statement row DTO that groups payout information by payout batch, seller, and possibly by order, making it suitable for human-readable statements and export to external accounting systems.
operations.description:
Retrieve a detailed seller payout statement report that joins payout, order, and payment data to explain how seller payouts are computed over a specified period.

This operation reads from the payout and order-related Prisma models, including `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`, `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`, `shopping_mall_orders`, `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments`, and `shopping_mall_order_lines`. It may also reference payment- and refund-related models like `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`, and `shopping_mall_refund_items` to calculate net amounts after refunds and adjustments. No inserts, updates, or deletions are performed; this is strictly a read-only analytical endpoint that composes and aggregates existing transactional data.

The request payload, described by `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutStatementReport.IRequest`, allows callers to specify which seller or sellers to report on, the payout date window or order completion window, the currencies of interest, and additional filters such as payout status (scheduled, processing, completed). It can also include flags to control the granularity of the statement, for example whether to include per-order-line breakdown or only per-payout-batch summary rows.

The response, using `IPageIShoppingMallSellerPayoutStatementRow`, returns a paginated list of payout statement rows. Each row includes key data for reconciliation such as seller identity, payout batch identifier, associated order identifiers, gross order amount, platform and processor fees, commission, refunded amounts, chargebacks affecting the payout, and the final payout amount transferred to the seller. This enables both the platform and individual sellers to trace how each payout was derived from underlying sales.

From a security and authorization perspective, the endpoint is intended for use by platform administrators overseeing payouts as well as authenticated sellers viewing their own statements. The `authorizationActors` configuration therefore includes both `platformAdmin` and `seller` actors. The implementation must ensure that a seller can only view their own payout statements, while platform administrators with the `platformAdmin` role can view statements for any seller.

This operation is closely related to the higher-level payment settlement report endpoint but focuses specifically on the seller payout side of the flow. Together, these reports provide a comprehensive view of both platform-level settlements and seller-level payouts without mutating any of the underlying payment or order records.
operations.summary: Generate a paginated seller payout statement report aggregating payout and order data in shoppingMall.

requestBody.description: Filter and configuration parameters for generating seller payout statements, including seller selection, payout or order date ranges, currencies, and granularity options.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of seller payout statement rows detailing how individual payout amounts were derived from orders, refunds, and adjustments.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A seller payout batch must exist in the shopping_mall_seller_payouts table before it can be included and explained in the seller payout statement report. Creating at least one seller payout batch ensures the report has payout data to aggregate and present.

Seller payout item rows must exist in shopping_mall_seller_payout_items so that the payout statement report can break down batch-level payouts into item-level rows linked to sellers, orders, and amounts.
Customer orders must exist in shopping_mall_orders so that payout computations have underlying sales data to reference when deriving gross payable amounts per seller.
Order line items must exist in shopping_mall_order_lines to provide line-level revenue and fee bases that roll up into seller payouts and therefore into the payout statement rows.
Payment transactions must exist in shopping_mall_payment_transactions so that the payout statement report can reconcile payouts against captured customer payments.
Refund transactions must exist in shopping_mall_refund_transactions so that the report can include refund and chargeback adjustment amounts in the payout computations.

operations.specification:
This operation produces a seller-centric payout statement report for the shoppingMall platform, aligning financial information from the Prisma models `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`, `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`, `shopping_mall_orders`, `shopping_mall_order_lines`, and the various payment and refund entities such as `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` and `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`.

The core purpose of the endpoint is to allow authorized actors to retrieve, for a given seller or set of sellers and time period, a structured view of payout batches, the orders and order lines included in those payouts, associated fees, refunds, and adjustments. It is an analytical, read-only reporting API that helps sellers and platform finance teams understand how the final payout amounts were computed from raw orders and payment flows.

Rather than exposing a single underlying table, the operation constructs a statement row DTO that groups payout information by payout batch, seller, and possibly by order, making it suitable for human-readable statements and export to external accounting systems.
operations.description:
Retrieve a detailed seller payout statement report that joins payout, order, and payment data to explain how seller payouts are computed over a specified period.

This operation reads from the payout and order-related Prisma models, including `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`, `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`, `shopping_mall_orders`, `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments`, and `shopping_mall_order_lines`. It may also reference payment- and refund-related models like `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`, and `shopping_mall_refund_items` to calculate net amounts after refunds and adjustments. No inserts, updates, or deletions are performed; this is strictly a read-only analytical endpoint that composes and aggregates existing transactional data.

The request payload, described by `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutStatementReport.IRequest`, allows callers to specify which seller or sellers to report on, the payout date window or order completion window, the currencies of interest, and additional filters such as payout status (scheduled, processing, completed). It can also include flags to control the granularity of the statement, for example whether to include per-order-line breakdown or only per-payout-batch summary rows.

The response, using `IPageIShoppingMallSellerPayoutStatementRow`, returns a paginated list of payout statement rows. Each row includes key data for reconciliation such as seller identity, payout batch identifier, associated order identifiers, gross order amount, platform and processor fees, commission, refunded amounts, chargebacks affecting the payout, and the final payout amount transferred to the seller. This enables both the platform and individual sellers to trace how each payout was derived from underlying sales.

From a security and authorization perspective, the endpoint is intended for use by platform administrators overseeing payouts as well as authenticated sellers viewing their own statements. The `authorizationActors` configuration therefore includes both `platformAdmin` and `seller` actors. The implementation must ensure that a seller can only view their own payout statements, while platform administrators with the `platformAdmin` role can view statements for any seller.

This operation is closely related to the higher-level payment settlement report endpoint but focuses specifically on the seller payout side of the flow. Together, these reports provide a comprehensive view of both platform-level settlements and seller-level payouts without mutating any of the underlying payment or order records.
operations.summary: Generate a paginated seller payout statement report aggregating payout and order data in shoppingMall.

requestBody.description: Filter and configuration parameters for generating seller payout statements, including seller selection, payout or order date ranges, currencies, and granularity options.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of seller payout statement rows detailing how individual payout amounts were derived from orders, refunds, and adjustments.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Seller payout batches in shopping_mall_seller_payouts must exist so that the seller-facing payout statement can present actual payouts made or scheduled for that seller.
Seller payout item records in shopping_mall_seller_payout_items must be created so that the seller payout statement can show detailed line-level payout components (per order or segment).
Underlying customer orders in shopping_mall_orders must exist to provide the sales basis for the seller’s payouts shown in the statement.
Order lines in shopping_mall_order_lines must exist so that the payout statement can attribute gross amounts, fees, and adjustments to concrete sold items.
Payment transactions in shopping_mall_payment_transactions must exist to link seller payouts to completed customer payments in the seller-facing statement.
Refund transactions in shopping_mall_refund_transactions must exist so that the seller payout statement can accurately reflect reductions from refunds and similar adjustments.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves an aggregated payments overview for the shoppingMall platform, focusing primarily on financial data sourced from the Prisma tables related to payments and refunds: `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, `shopping_mall_payment_status_events`, and `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`. It is a read-only analytical endpoint that computes summary statistics such as total processed volume, counts by payment status, and refund ratios over a recent time window rather than returning raw transactional rows.

The implementation should execute read queries over the payment and refund tables, grouping and aggregating by relevant dimensions like status, method, and time buckets (for example, daily totals over the last N days). No mutations of the underlying tables are performed. Instead, the endpoint returns a dashboard-friendly DTO `IShoppingMallPaymentsOverview` that encapsulates these computed metrics in a structure suitable for admin dashboards.

This endpoint is intended for administrative users who need a high-level snapshot of payment health and trends, and it should respect any constraints or comments defined in the corresponding Prisma models for transaction states, allowed status values, and monetary field precision.
operations.description:
Retrieve a high-level payments overview for the shoppingMall platform, summarizing data from the payment-related Prisma tables without exposing individual transaction records.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` table, which stores core payment transaction records for customer orders, and from supporting tables like `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` that track the evolution of each transaction's state over time, and `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` that record funds returned to customers. Using these tables, the endpoint computes key performance indicators such as total processed payment volume, counts of successful versus failed transactions, current pending payments, and aggregate refund amounts for a recent analysis period.

From a security perspective, this overview is intended for platform-level administrative actors only, because it reveals sensitive financial indicators about the entire marketplace rather than data scoped to a single customer or seller. The endpoint must therefore enforce that only authenticated admins with appropriate privileges can access it. However, it should not return personally identifiable customer information or raw card details; instead, it focuses on aggregated metrics and counts computed from the payment tables.

In terms of behavior, the API allows optional query parameters or default server-side configuration to define the time window (for example, last 7 days) and possibly filter by payment method or region. Regardless of the window, the operation must handle large underlying data volumes efficiently by relying on database-level aggregations such as SUM, COUNT, and GROUP BY on the `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` and `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` tables. Any errors in accessing the database or inconsistencies in the tracked payment statuses should result in appropriate error responses, and the implementation should log such issues for later investigation.

This operation is typically used alongside more detailed administrative endpoints that drill down into individual transactions, but it is specialized for dashboard use where a concise summary DTO `IShoppingMallPaymentsOverview` is preferable to raw transaction lists. It does not depend on other API calls to be executed beforehand, although client dashboards may call it together with related overview endpoints such as the payouts overview to present a unified financial picture.
operations.summary: Get an aggregated payments overview derived from shopping_mall_payment_transactions and related tables.

responseBody.description: Aggregated payments overview metrics for the shoppingMall platform, computed from payment and refund tables.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A payment transaction must exist in shopping_mall_payment_transactions so that the payments overview can compute aggregated payment volume and transaction counts.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves an aggregated payouts overview for the shoppingMall platform, focusing on financial flows from the platform to sellers. It primarily reads from the Prisma tables `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` and `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`, and may also reference `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries` for contextual performance metrics. The endpoint is read-only and computes summary statistics such as total payout volume, counts of completed versus pending payouts, and per-period payout trends.

Implementation-wise, the operation issues analytical queries that aggregate data from the seller payout tables, using SQL constructs such as SUM, COUNT, and GROUP BY on payout dates, statuses, and possibly seller segments. The result is mapped into a dedicated DTO `IShoppingMallPayoutsOverview`, which is designed for dashboard visualization and does not directly mirror any single Prisma table structure. No modifications are made to the payout or performance tables by this endpoint.

The endpoint is intended for platform administrators who require a concise summary of how much has been paid out to sellers, what amounts remain scheduled, and how seller performance correlates to payouts over time. It must honor any constraints or comments defined in the Prisma models for payout status values, monetary precision, and linkage between payouts and underlying orders.
operations.description:
Retrieve a high-level payouts overview for the shoppingMall platform, summarizing platform-to-seller payout activity without returning individual payout records.

This operation reads from `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`, which represents payout batches that transfer funds from the platform to sellers, and from `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`, which contains the per-order or per-line components included in each payout batch. Optionally, it can also leverage `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries` to include contextual indicators such as average dispute rates or refund ratios that relate to seller performance in the same period.

From a security and authorization standpoint, the payouts overview provides sensitive financial insights into seller earnings and platform obligations. For this reason, access is restricted to administrative actors such as platform admins, and the endpoint must enforce that only authenticated `platformAdmin` users can call it. The response does not include personally identifiable seller information beyond what is necessary for aggregation; instead, it focuses on totals, counts, and trend metrics.

The behavior of the endpoint may be influenced by an implicit or configurable time window, for example summarizing payouts over the last 7, 30, or 90 days. Implementations should rely on efficient database-level aggregation functions when querying the payout tables, especially in large-scale environments where the number of payouts and payout items can be substantial. In case of underlying data access issues or inconsistent payout statuses, the API should respond with appropriate error information and ensure that such incidents are logged in audit or error log tables like `shopping_mall_error_logs` or `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` if defined.

This payouts overview endpoint is typically used together with the payments overview to give platform administrators a full financial dashboard of incoming customer payments and outgoing seller payouts. While other endpoints can be used to drill down into individual payouts and their items, this operation is optimized for dashboard consumption through the compact `IShoppingMallPayoutsOverview` DTO.
operations.summary: Get an aggregated payouts overview derived from shopping_mall_seller_payouts and related tables.

responseBody.description: Aggregated payouts overview metrics for the shoppingMall platform, computed from seller payout tables.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A seller payout batch must exist in shopping_mall_seller_payouts so that the payouts overview can aggregate payout volume and batch counts.
Seller payout item rows should exist in shopping_mall_seller_payout_items so that the payouts overview can compute component-level payout aggregates across orders and lines.

operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves a paginated list of inventory item records from the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` Prisma table. It is designed to support backoffice and internal tooling features that need to inspect current stock positions per SKU, including on-hand quantity, reserved quantity, stock status, and configuration flags such as `backorder_enabled` and `preorder_enabled`.

The endpoint uses HTTP PATCH on `/shoppingMall/inventoryItems` to allow complex search payloads to be passed in the request body. The search DTO `IShoppingMallInventoryItem.IRequest` encapsulates filterable fields like `productSkuId`, `stockStatus`, and numeric range filters for `on_hand_quantity` or `reserved_quantity`, as well as pagination and sorting parameters. The response returns a paginated collection of inventory item summaries using `IPageIShoppingMallInventoryItem.ISummary`.

From a database perspective, this operation primarily queries the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` table, optionally joining with `shopping_mall_product_skus` for SKU-related filters. Implementations should respect any soft-deletion or archival fields defined on `shopping_mall_inventory_items` (for example, by excluding logically removed records) and leverage indexes on status or timestamp fields for efficient filtering and sorting.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of inventory items from the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` table.

This operation provides a flexible search facility over per-SKU inventory state. Each record in `shopping_mall_inventory_items` represents the stock position for a single SKU from `shopping_mall_product_skus`, combining `on_hand_quantity` (units physically available) and `reserved_quantity` (units already reserved for pending orders) with configuration fields such as `low_stock_threshold`, `stock_status`, `backorder_enabled`, and `preorder_enabled`. The search payload allows clients to filter by SKU identifier, specific stock statuses such as `in_stock`, `low_stock`, `out_of_stock`, `backorder_allowed`, or `preorder_only`, and to apply numeric ranges to quantities to find, for example, items with low remaining on-hand stock.

Security-wise, this list surface typically exposes operational data that should not be visible to end customers. The operation can therefore be restricted to authenticated platform actors, but since concrete actor roles are handled at a higher layer, the `authorizationActors` field is left empty here so that authorization can be configured by downstream agents using actual actor names like `customer`, `seller`, or `platformAdmin`. Implementations should still enforce appropriate access control, for example limiting sellers to their own SKUs if this endpoint is reused for merchant tooling. Rate limiting and query complexity controls should be in place because this search endpoint can combine multiple filters and sorting options.

At the data access layer, the handler translates the incoming `IShoppingMallInventoryItem.IRequest` search criteria into Prisma queries on `shopping_mall_inventory_items`. Queries should exclude logically removed records when a soft-deletion field exists on the model and should take advantage of existing indexes on status or timestamp columns for efficient querying and sorting, especially when filtering by status or listing items ordered by recency. The response wraps results in a paginated container `IPageIShoppingMallInventoryItem.ISummary`, which exposes only the fields necessary for list views while including standard pagination metadata such as page, limit, and total counts.

This endpoint is typically used together with the detail retrieval endpoint `GET /shoppingMall/inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}`. Clients first call this PATCH endpoint to search for relevant inventory items and then call the detail endpoint for a specific `inventoryItemId` when deeper inspection or editing of a particular inventory record is required.
operations.summary: Search and list inventory items from the shopping_mall_inventory_items table with filters and pagination.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters, and pagination parameters for querying inventory items.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of inventory item summaries that match the provided search criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A product SKU must exist before its per-SKU inventory record can be created or managed; inventory items reference shopping_mall_product_skus via product_sku_id.
Inventory item records in shopping_mall_inventory_items must be created for SKUs before they can appear in search results returned by this inventory items search endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed information for a single inventory item identified by its unique `id` from the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` Prisma table. It maps to the `GET /shoppingMall/inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}` endpoint and returns a full `IShoppingMallInventoryItem` DTO representing the per-SKU inventory state, including quantities, configuration thresholds, and status flags.

The path parameter `inventoryItemId` corresponds directly to the primary key field `id` of `shopping_mall_inventory_items`, which is typically defined as a UUID. The operation performs a lookup scoped to active records and should exclude any logically removed records if the model defines a soft-deletion or archival field. If no active inventory item is found for the given identifier, the operation responds with an appropriate not-found error.

This detail retrieval is typically used by administrative tools, inventory management consoles, or automated jobs that need the complete inventory record for a given SKU. It complements the list/search endpoint on `/shoppingMall/inventoryItems` by providing full field visibility once a specific record has been selected.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full inventory item record for a specific `shopping_mall_inventory_items.id`.

This operation looks up a single inventory item by its unique identifier, provided as the `inventoryItemId` path parameter. The underlying Prisma model `shopping_mall_inventory_items` stores per-SKU inventory state fields such as `on_hand_quantity`, `reserved_quantity`, `low_stock_threshold`, and `stock_status`, along with boolean flags `backorder_enabled` and `preorder_enabled`. It also tracks lifecycle timestamps like `created_at` and `updated_at`, and may include a nullable archival or soft-deletion column depending on the final schema design.

From a security perspective, this endpoint exposes operational inventory details that are generally restricted to administrative or internal tooling contexts, not to end customers browsing the catalog. The `authorizationActors` field is left empty here so that higher-level configuration can decide which concrete actors (for example, `platformAdmin` or `seller`) are allowed, while the core specification remains agnostic. Implementations should still ensure that only appropriately privileged identities can call it and may add ownership checks so that sellers only see inventory for their own SKUs.

In the data access layer, the handler must query `shopping_mall_inventory_items` by `id` and exclude logically removed records when a soft-deletion field exists on the model. If the identifier does not match any active record, the service should return a clear 404-style not-found error. When a record is found, it is mapped to the `IShoppingMallInventoryItem` DTO, which exposes all core fields from the schema and can include related SKU information via additional queries if needed. This endpoint is commonly invoked after a client has obtained the `inventoryItemId` from the `/shoppingMall/inventoryItems` search endpoint, allowing users to inspect and potentially edit detailed inventory configuration for a specific SKU.
operations.summary: Get detailed information for a single inventory item from the shopping_mall_inventory_items table by id.

parameters.name: inventoryItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target inventory item, corresponding to shopping_mall_inventory_items.id.

responseBody.description: Complete inventory item record associated with the provided inventoryItemId.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A product SKU must be created first, as each inventory item row in shopping_mall_inventory_items is linked to a specific SKU via product_sku_id.
The specific inventory item identified by inventoryItemId must have been created in shopping_mall_inventory_items before it can be retrieved in detail.

operations.specification:
This operation creates a new inventory item record in the shopping_mall_inventory_items Prisma table. It is used to establish and initialize per-SKU inventory state for each sellable variant within the shoppingMall platform. The operation accepts structured creation data describing which SKU the inventory item belongs to, the initial on-hand quantity, safety stock thresholds, and configuration flags controlling behaviors such as backorder or preorder eligibility as defined in the underlying schema.

From an implementation perspective, the service will validate that the referenced product SKU exists in the shopping_mall_product_skus table and that there is not already an inventory record for the same SKU when the schema enforces uniqueness per SKU. Business rules such as minimum and maximum allowed initial quantities, adherence to regional inventory policies, and consistency with related backorder or preorder settings are all enforced before the record is persisted. Upon success, the fully populated IShoppingMallInventoryItem DTO representing the new inventory state is returned to the caller.

This creation endpoint is expected to be called primarily by internal tools or seller/platform admin workflows that onboard new SKUs into the catalog and need to make them stock-aware. It provides the foundational inventory state that later processes such as reservations, movements, fulfillments, and stock reporting will rely on.
operations.description:
Create a new inventory item entry for a specific SKU in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_inventory_items table, which represents per-SKU inventory state for each sellable variant. Each record typically links to a shopping_mall_product_skus entry and stores core quantitative fields such as current on-hand quantity, reserved quantity snapshot fields, and configuration flags that affect how the platform treats stock during checkout and fulfillment. The operation accepts a payload described by IShoppingMallInventoryItem.ICreate, which includes all creation-time attributes allowed by the schema, excluding any fields automatically maintained by the system such as generated identifiers or timestamps.

When a request is received, the service first authenticates the caller as an authorized actor (for example, a seller managing their own SKUs or a platform administrator managing catalog-wide inventory). It then validates that the referenced SKU exists and that the actor has permission to manage inventory for that SKU. The service also verifies numeric invariants, such as non-negative starting quantities, and cross-checks any policy-related flags against configuration entities like shopping_mall_backorder_settings and shopping_mall_preorder_settings, ensuring that the new inventory item is consistent with broader business rules.

On successful validation, the system inserts a new row into shopping_mall_inventory_items, initializing the stock state according to the request. The response returns an IShoppingMallInventoryItem representation of the created entity, which can then be used by admin dashboards, seller tools, or automated provisioning flows. Errors are returned if the SKU does not exist, if an inventory record for the SKU already exists when the schema enforces uniqueness, if the caller lacks permission, or if validation rules are violated. This endpoint is typically used in conjunction with inventory reservation, movement, and fulfillment APIs that consume and adjust the stored quantities over time.
operations.summary: Create a new inventory item in the shopping_mall_inventory_items table for a specific SKU.

requestBody.description: Payload describing the inventory item to create, including SKU reference, initial quantities, and configuration flags as allowed by the schema.

responseBody.description: The newly created inventory item representing per-SKU inventory state in the system.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: A product SKU must be created in the shopping_mall_product_skus table before an inventory item can be established for that SKU. This endpoint creates a new SKU variant under an existing product, providing the product_sku_id that inventory items reference.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing inventory item record in the shopping_mall_inventory_items Prisma table. It allows authorized actors to adjust per-SKU inventory state such as on-hand quantity, safety stock, or configuration flags that govern checkout behavior. The target record is identified by the inventoryItemId path parameter, which typically corresponds to the primary key of shopping_mall_inventory_items.

The operation consumes an IShoppingMallInventoryItem.IUpdate DTO that contains only the updatable fields defined by the schema. During implementation, the service loads the existing inventory item, validates that it is associated with a SKU that the caller is permitted to manage, and applies the requested changes. It performs consistency checks to ensure resulting quantities remain valid (e.g., non-negative counts, adherence to maximum thresholds) and that any changes to backorder or preorder flags remain aligned with configuration defined in related policy or inventory-setting tables.

Upon successful update, the service persists the changes to the shopping_mall_inventory_items table and returns the updated IShoppingMallInventoryItem DTO. This operation is critical for ongoing inventory maintenance tasks, including manual stock corrections, bulk synchronization from external warehouse management systems, and administrative overrides for special campaigns or incident recovery.
operations.description:
Update an existing inventory item entry representing per-SKU inventory state in the shoppingMall platform.

This operation interacts with the shopping_mall_inventory_items table, which stores key inventory attributes for individual SKUs. Using the inventoryItemId path parameter, the service locates the target record and then applies the modifications described by the IShoppingMallInventoryItem.IUpdate payload. Updatable fields may include quantities (for example, adjusting on-hand stock after a physical count), thresholds such as safety stock or reorder points, and configuration fields that influence whether a SKU can be sold when stock is low or zero.

Before applying updates, the service enforces authorization and validation rules. Only actors like sellers (for their own SKUs) or platform administrators may modify inventory, and the system ensures that the requested changes do not violate fundamental invariants, such as creating negative available quantities or contradicting higher-level policies from shopping_mall_backorder_settings, shopping_mall_preorder_settings, or region-specific constraints. If the referenced inventoryItemId does not exist, or if the caller is not permitted to manage it, the service returns an appropriate error.

After successful validation, the updated record is saved back to the shopping_mall_inventory_items table, and the operation returns the fresh IShoppingMallInventoryItem representation. This updated DTO can immediately be used by dashboards, reports, or external systems to reflect the current stock state. This endpoint is often used alongside order and fulfillment flows that indirectly affect inventory through reservations and movements but sometimes require direct, explicit adjustments via this API.
operations.summary: Update an existing inventory item in the shopping_mall_inventory_items table identified by inventoryItemId.

parameters.name: inventoryItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target inventory item record in the shopping_mall_inventory_items table to be updated.

requestBody.description: Payload containing updated inventory fields such as quantities, thresholds, or configuration flags for the inventory item.

responseBody.description: The updated inventory item after applying the requested changes.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: An inventory item record must exist in the shopping_mall_inventory_items table before it can be updated. This endpoint creates the inventory item and returns its id, which is then used as inventoryItemId in the update operation.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a specific inventory item record from the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` Prisma model. It is invoked with `DELETE /inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}` and uses the `inventoryItemId` path parameter as the primary key (typically a UUID string) of the target row.

Inventory items in `shopping_mall_inventory_items` represent per-SKU inventory state for sellable variants in the shoppingMall platform, including links to reservations and movements stored in related tables such as `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` and `shopping_mall_inventory_movements`. This endpoint is intended for exceptional administrative or maintenance use cases where an inventory item must be removed entirely, for example when a SKU is permanently decommissioned and its inventory tracking record should no longer exist.

Before performing the deletion, the implementation should ensure that removing this record does not violate referential integrity or critical business rules. Typical checks include verifying that there are no active reservations in `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` tied to this item and that any historical records in related tables are handled according to schema-defined relations (for example, via cascading deletes or by preventing deletion when dependent rows exist). On success the operation returns no body, indicating that the inventory item row has been removed from the database.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a specific inventory item row from the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` table by its unique identifier.

This endpoint operates on the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` Prisma model, which holds per-SKU inventory state records used across the shoppingMall platform. Each record typically relates a SKU to a particular inventory bucket or location and tracks available quantities and other stateful attributes. Because these rows are central to stock accounting and fulfillment logic, deletion is considered a privileged administrative action rather than a routine operation.

From an authorization perspective, only platform-level administrative actors should be allowed to perform this operation. The `platformAdmin` actor is used to represent such privileged users. Implementations should apply the appropriate authentication and authorization middleware to ensure that only authenticated platform administrators can invoke this endpoint; customers, sellers, and guest users must be denied access.

On invocation, the service looks up the inventory item by the `inventoryItemId` path parameter. If the item does not exist, a not-found error should be returned. If it exists, the service must enforce business rules that protect active orders and reservations. For instance, if there are currently active records in `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` referencing this item, the deletion should be rejected with a descriptive error. Likewise, any constraints implied by relations to `shopping_mall_inventory_movements`, `shopping_mall_backorder_settings`, or `shopping_mall_preorder_settings` should be respected. Only when all checks pass should the item be deleted.

This operation fits into a broader inventory management toolset that may include endpoints for creating and updating inventory items, listing them, and analyzing reservations or movements. A typical admin workflow might use a search endpoint on `/inventoryItems` to find candidates, inspect details through a GET endpoint, and finally call this DELETE endpoint to erase obsolete inventory tracking rows. After successful deletion, subsequent attempts to retrieve or list the deleted item will no longer include it in results.
operations.summary: Permanently erase an inventory item from the shopping_mall_inventory_items table by its identifier

parameters.name: inventoryItemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target inventory item record in the shopping_mall_inventory_items table, typically a UUID string representing a per-SKU inventory state row.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: An inventory item record must exist in the shopping_mall_inventory_items table before it can be permanently deleted by ID.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered, searchable, and paginated list of inventory reservations associated with a specific inventory item by querying the `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` Prisma model. It is exposed as `PATCH /inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}/reservations`, where the `inventoryItemId` path parameter scopes the search to reservations tied to a particular inventory item from `shopping_mall_inventory_items`.

The `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` table typically holds rows representing reserved quantities of inventory for workflows such as checkout, payment processing, and order fulfillment. Each reservation is associated with an inventory item, and may reference orders or order lines, reservation statuses, expiration times, and other metadata. This endpoint allows platform administrators to inspect and analyze all reservations currently or historically linked to a specific inventory item.

The request body uses the `IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.IRequest` DTO to describe complex search criteria, including filters for reservation status, creation or expiration date ranges, and identifiers of related orders or order lines, along with pagination and sorting parameters. The response structure `IPageIShoppingMallInventoryReservation.ISummary` returns a paginated collection of reservation summary projections suited for list or dashboard views, plus pagination metadata such as total count and current page.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of inventory reservations linked to a specific inventory item in the `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` table.

This endpoint is built on the `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` Prisma model, which captures reservations of inventory units tied to inventory items from `shopping_mall_inventory_items`. By specifying the `inventoryItemId` path parameter, callers restrict the query to reservations associated with a single inventory item, making it easier to understand how that item’s stock is reserved across active or historical business flows, such as checkout sessions and open orders.

The request body follows the `IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.IRequest` contract, enabling clients to pass structured filters and pagination instructions. Implementations should support common filters like reservation status (for example, active, released, expired), creation and expiration date ranges, and order or order-line identifiers, along with pagination controls such as page index, page size, and sort fields. The `PATCH` method is chosen instead of `GET` because these search criteria can be complex and nested, and encoding them in a JSON body significantly improves clarity and extensibility compared to query string parameters.

Because it exposes operational details about inventory reservations, the endpoint is restricted to privileged administrative users represented by the `platformAdmin` actor. Authentication and authorization middleware should enforce that only authenticated platform administrators can access this endpoint; customers, sellers, and guests must not be able to query reservation internals.

The response body uses the `IPageIShoppingMallInventoryReservation.ISummary` DTO, which returns a page of reservation summaries along with pagination metadata. Each summary entry should include essential fields such as the reservation identifier, reserved quantity, status, links to related orders or order lines, and key timestamps, while omitting heavy or internal-only fields that are better suited to detailed inspection endpoints. Errors should be returned if the specified `inventoryItemId` does not correspond to an existing row in `shopping_mall_inventory_items`, if filters are invalid, or if the caller lacks the required privileges.
