operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A brand must exist so that products can be associated with a valid brand before SKUs and reviews reference them.
The catalog product must be created in shopping_mall_products so that the productId in the review path refers to a real product.
The SKU variant must exist in shopping_mall_product_skus so that the skuId in the review path refers to a real SKU belonging to the product.
A review record in shopping_mall_product_reviews must be created for the given product and SKU before it can be updated with PUT.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes an existing product review associated with a specific product and SKU in the ShoppingMall platform. It operates primarily on the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` Prisma model, which stores customer-authored reviews and star ratings, and may also affect related subsidiary models such as `shopping_mall_product_review_reports`, `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses`, and `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` depending on how cascading behavior is implemented in the service layer.

The endpoint is designed for authorized platform administrators (modeled as the `platformAdmin` actor) to remove a review identified by its unique `reviewId`, while also scoping the request to a particular `productId` and `skuId`. These additional identifiers ensure that the deletion is performed in the correct product and SKU context, which is important when the same customer may have reviews across multiple products or variants.

The implementation must validate that the review exists, that it is linked to the specified product and SKU, and that the caller has sufficient permissions to perform a deletion. Business logic should also ensure that any associated aggregate rating data for the product and SKU is recalculated or updated after removal, using the `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` model or equivalent aggregation mechanism. Error handling must clearly distinguish between not-found conditions (e.g., review does not exist for this product/SKU) and authorization failures (e.g., caller is not allowed to erase the review).
operations.description:
Erase a specific product review record that belongs to a given product and SKU in the ShoppingMall catalog.

This operation targets the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` model, which represents customer-authored textual feedback and star ratings for catalog items. Each review is typically associated with a product, and optionally with a more granular SKU variant, enabling fine-grained feedback at the variant level. By requiring `productId`, `skuId`, and `reviewId` in the path, the API ensures that the deletion is scoped to the correct product and SKU context, preventing accidental removal of reviews that might share similar identifiers but belong to different catalog items.

From a security perspective, the endpoint is restricted to platform administrators responsible for catalog quality and moderation. While business rules may allow customers to update or hide their own reviews via other operations, permanent removal of a review record is usually reserved for moderation scenarios, such as handling policy violations, inappropriate content, or legal takedown requests. The authorization logic must verify that the caller has the `platformAdmin` actor role and, if applicable, that any additional moderation policies defined in the ShoppingMall configuration tables are satisfied before performing the deletion.

In relation to the database, the operation primarily deletes a row from `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. Depending on the schema and cascade configuration, related subsidiary data such as `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` (reports and abuse flags), `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` (seller replies), and entries contributing to `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` must be handled. The service implementation should either rely on database cascading rules or explicitly clean up associated records and then recalculate rating aggregates for the affected product/SKU so that average ratings and review counts remain consistent.

Related operations include listing reviews for a product or SKU, creating new reviews after an order is completed, updating existing review content, and listing or managing reports against reviews. When this erase operation is invoked, clients should expect that subsequent retrieval operations for the same reviewId will return a not-found response, and that product rating aggregates may change accordingly as the removed review is no longer counted.
operations.summary: Erase a ShoppingMall product review associated with a specific product and SKU

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product whose review is being erased. This identifier scopes the operation to the correct product in the ShoppingMall catalog so that only reviews belonging to this product are affected.

parameters.name: skuId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the SKU variant within the specified product for which the review was written. This value ensures that the targeted review is associated with the correct variant context in cases where a product has multiple SKUs.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product review record in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table that should be permanently removed.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A product review for the specified product and SKU must be created by a customer before a platform administrator can erase it using this delete operation.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered, paginated list of abuse reports and moderation flags associated with a specific product review in the ShoppingMall platform. It operates on the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` Prisma model, which represents reports and abuse flags submitted against product reviews, typically by customers, sellers, or automated systems.

The endpoint is designed to help moderation or administrative tooling inspect all reports tied to a particular review identified by `reviewId`. By using the PATCH method with a request body, the operation supports rich querying features such as pagination, sorting, filtering by report status or severity, and limiting results to certain time ranges or reporter types. This design allows admin consoles to efficiently navigate large volumes of reports for heavily flagged reviews.

The implementation must validate that the referenced review exists in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` model and that the calling actor is authorized to view moderation-related data, since reports can contain sensitive details about policy violations or user behavior. Business logic may also integrate with dispute or appeal workflows, connecting this report data with tables like `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` (which record historical moderation actions) to provide a complete moderation history. Errors should clearly differentiate between missing reviews, invalid request filters, and insufficient permissions.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of reports and abuse flags for a specific product review in the ShoppingMall platform.

This operation focuses on the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` model, which stores structured information about reports submitted against product reviews. Each report typically records who reported the review, the reason or category of the report, timestamps, and possibly internal status fields used during moderation workflows. By identifying the target review through the `reviewId` path parameter and accepting a rich search request body, the endpoint allows administrative tools to query reports using criteria such as report status, severity, reporter type, or created-at ranges.

From a security and privacy perspective, access to this endpoint is limited to platform administrators or dedicated moderation staff, represented here by the `platformAdmin` authorization actor. Reports can contain sensitive information including descriptions of policy violations, mentions of personal data, or internal classification fields. The authorization layer must therefore ensure that only properly authenticated and authorized platformAdmin users can call this operation. The request body type aligns with an `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.IRequest` style DTO that expresses pagination parameters, sorting options, and optional filters, while the response uses a paginated summary type `IPageIShoppingMallProductReviewReport.ISummary` so that list views can be rendered efficiently in admin consoles.

In relation to other parts of the system, this operation is typically used alongside endpoints that manage review moderation decisions stored in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` and those that view or modify the underlying review entity in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. When a platformAdmin investigates a problematic review, they may first call this reports index to understand the pattern and volume of reports, then proceed to apply moderation actions or communicate with involved parties through separate workflows.
operations.summary: List and search ShoppingMall product review reports for a specific review

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product review whose associated reports and abuse flags should be retrieved from the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` table.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, pagination, and sorting options for listing reports associated with the specified product review. This includes fields for page size, page index, sort order, and optional filters such as status, severity, or created-at ranges.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of summary records representing reports and abuse flags attached to the specified product review, suitable for use in admin moderation interfaces.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: An abuse report must first be created for the specified review before a platform administrator can list and search those reports.

operations.specification:
Retrieve a single product review report associated with a specific review from the shopping mall domain.

This operation targets the Prisma table `shopping_mall_product_review_reports`, which stores individual abuse or issue reports that customers, sellers, or administrators raise against entries in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. Each report captures who raised the concern, which review it targets, the reason category, free-text description, timestamps, and current handling status (for example, pending, accepted, or rejected).

The endpoint is designed for detail retrieval: given a `reviewId` and a `reportId`, it returns a fully detailed `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport` representation. It is read-only and does not alter any state in the underlying table. This is typically used in admin dashboards or internal moderation tools to inspect a specific report in depth, including its relationships to the underlying review and possibly moderation actions recorded elsewhere.

The operation assumes that `reviewId` and `reportId` are stable unique identifiers (likely UUID strings) defined as primary or unique keys in their respective Prisma models. It validates that the `reportId` belongs to the given `reviewId` to avoid cross‑review data leakage. If no such combination exists, the implementation must return a 404-style error.

The response body uses the DTO `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport`, whose fields are derived directly from the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` Prisma model (including status, reason, description, linkage to review, and audit timestamps).
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a single product review report for moderation, audit, or troubleshooting purposes.

This GET operation is scoped to a specific review in the shopping mall platform and returns exactly one report record from the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` table, which is conceptually tied to a parent record in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. The `reviewId` path parameter identifies the parent review being examined, while the `reportId` path parameter identifies the exact report entry raised against that review. The implementation must ensure that the report both exists and is associated with the given review; otherwise, a not‑found response should be returned.

From the database perspective, `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` contains fields such as the foreign key to the product review, a reporter identity reference, reason category, free‑form description, created/updated timestamps, and the current resolution or handling status. These schema details map into the `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport` DTO, which is returned as the response payload. No mutation against this table is performed by this endpoint; it is strictly read‑only.

Security‑wise, this endpoint is intended for platform administrators and possibly specialized moderation staff rather than general customers or sellers, because reports can include sensitive details and internal resolution notes. Authorization logic should therefore ensure that only actors with appropriate admin‑level roles can access this data. The operation can be used alongside list/search endpoints (such as a PATCH on `/reviews/{reviewId}/reports`) that provide paginated listings of reports; once an admin locates a report in such a listing, they would call this GET endpoint to see full details before deciding on a moderation action handled by other write endpoints.
operations.summary: Get a single shopping_mall_product_review_reports record for a given review and report identifier.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target product review whose report is being inspected. This value corresponds to the primary or unique key of a record in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table and is used to scope the report lookup to a single parent review.

parameters.name: reportId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific product review report to retrieve from the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` table. The implementation must verify that this report belongs to the review identified by `reviewId` to prevent cross‑review data leakage.

responseBody.description: Detailed representation of the requested product review report record associated with the given review, mapped from the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` Prisma table.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A product review must exist before its associated review report can be retrieved; the review creation operation generates the reviewId that scopes reports.
The specific review report must be created before it can be fetched by reviewId and reportId; this operation creates entries in shopping_mall_product_review_reports.

operations.specification:
Create a new product review report entry for a specific product review in the shopping mall platform.

This operation writes to the Prisma table `shopping_mall_product_review_reports`, which stores abuse or issue reports raised against entries in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. Each new row created by this endpoint represents a single report that associates a reporter (typically a customer or sometimes a seller) with a particular product review, along with structured and unstructured information describing the problem.

Clients supply the report payload in the request body using the DTO `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.ICreate`. That DTO is derived directly from the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` schema fields and is expected to contain properties such as a reason category (e.g., spam, offensive content, false information), optional free‑text description, and any additional metadata required by the business rules. The server side will also bind this report to the target review identified by the `reviewId` path parameter and infer the reporter identity from the authenticated session, rather than allowing clients to specify foreign keys directly.

On successful creation, the endpoint returns the fully populated `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport` instance as stored in the database, including generated identifiers, timestamps, and default status values (for example, a status like "pending" for newly created reports). Validation must ensure that the referenced review exists in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table and that business rules such as rate limiting or duplicate‑report prevention are enforced according to the platform’s policies.
operations.description:
Submit a new report against a specific product review, so that moderation or administrative staff can later review and act on it.

This POST operation is scoped to a particular product review, identified by the `reviewId` path parameter, which refers to a record in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table. The caller provides report details in the request body via the `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.ICreate` DTO. Typical fields in this DTO, derived from the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` Prisma model, include a categorical reason, optional textual explanation, and any structured fields the business requires for triage.

The implementation must verify that the referenced review exists and is eligible for reporting (for example, not already fully removed or locked), and then create a new row in the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` table linked to that review and to the authenticated reporter. System‑managed columns such as the report identifier, creation timestamp, and initial status are set by the backend, not by the client.

From a security standpoint, authenticated customers are typically the primary reporters of problematic reviews. Therefore this endpoint is restricted to the `customer` actor, while detailed role‑specific behavior is left to the business logic (for example, allowing sellers or admins to use separate tools). Anti‑abuse protections such as rate limiting and duplicate detection are recommended and should be implemented in the service layer that handles inserts into `shopping_mall_product_review_reports`. Once created, follow‑up operations such as viewing, moderating, or resolving reports are handled by other endpoints (for example, admin-only GET or PUT routes).
operations.summary: Create a new shopping_mall_product_review_reports record for a given product review.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product review that is being reported. This corresponds to a primary or unique key in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table and determines which review the new report record in `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` will be associated with.

requestBody.description: Payload describing the product review report to create, based on fields defined in the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` Prisma model (such as reason category and description). The server will additionally bind this report to the review identified by `reviewId` and to the authenticated reporter.

responseBody.description: The newly created product review report record as persisted in the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` table, including generated identifier, timestamps, and initial status.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: A customer-authored product review must exist before a report can be submitted against it; this operation creates the review record that provides the reviewId foreign key for reports.

operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing product review report in the shopping mall platform. It is associated with the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` Prisma table, which stores reports and abuse flags submitted against product reviews. The endpoint allows authorized actors (specifically platform administrators) to modify the status or handling details of a specific report identified by `reportId`, which itself is scoped to a particular product review identified by `reviewId`.

The primary purpose of this API is to let back-office tools change attributes such as the report resolution status (e.g., pending, accepted, rejected), moderator notes, and any classification fields defined in the underlying Prisma model. The exact updatable fields will be captured in the DTO `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.IUpdate`, which mirrors the Prisma schema fields that are business-updatable (excluding identifiers and immutable audit fields).

This operation must validate that both the referenced review and the report exist and that the report indeed belongs to the given review, using the foreign key relationships defined in the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` model (for example, a `product_review_id` column referencing `shopping_mall_product_reviews`). It should also enforce any domain rules such as only allowing state transitions that make sense (e.g., you cannot move from `rejected` back to `pending` if the Prisma comments describe such constraints).

The updated report record is returned as the response using the `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport` DTO, which corresponds closely to the Prisma table columns while possibly omitting internal-only fields. This ensures that moderation tools have immediate confirmation of the new state after the update is applied.
operations.description:
Update an existing product review report associated with a specific product review in the shopping mall domain.

This operation targets the the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` Prisma table, whose description states that it stores reports and abuse flags submitted against product reviews. Each report is typically linked to a `shopping_mall_product_reviews` record through a foreign key such as `product_review_id`. The path parameters `reviewId` and `reportId` should map to the unique identifiers of the corresponding `shopping_mall_product_reviews` and `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` rows. The service must verify that the report referenced by `reportId` is actually associated with the review referenced by `reviewId`, preventing cross-review tampering.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is intended for administrative and moderation tooling rather than general customers or sellers. Therefore, `authorizationActors` is set to `["platformAdmin"]` to reflect that platform administrators are responsible for handling abuse reports. The authentication and role checking will be enforced at the controller/service layer, but the operation specification must clearly indicate that normal customers cannot call this endpoint directly.

In terms of business logic, the request body of type `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.IUpdate` will include only the fields that moderators are allowed to change, such as status flags, moderator comments, category of violation, and timestamps for resolution when relevant. Fields like primary keys or immutable creation metadata from the Prisma model must not be updatable. The implementation should also perform validation according to any constraints described in the Prisma schema comments, such as restricting the set of allowed status values or requiring that a resolution note be provided when a report is closed.

Related operations include listing reports for reviews (likely a PATCH /reviews/{reviewId}/reports endpoint) and deleting reports (the DELETE /reviews/{reviewId}/reports/{reportId} operation described separately). Together, these APIs provide a complete administrative workflow for managing abuse reports on product reviews, ensuring high-quality content and compliance with marketplace policies.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a specific product review report from the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` Prisma table. It is designed for administrative and moderation use cases where a report has been resolved, deemed invalid, or otherwise no longer needs to be tracked in the system according to marketplace policies.

The endpoint uses two path parameters: `reviewId`, referencing a row in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`, and `reportId`, referencing a row in `shopping_mall_product_review_reports`. The implementation must enforce that the report identified by `reportId` is associated with the review identified by `reviewId`, typically via a foreign key field such as `product_review_id` on the report record. If there is a mismatch, the operation should fail with a suitable error to prevent accidental or malicious cross-entity deletion.

The operation does not accept a request body; all required context is provided by the path parameters and the authenticated administrator identity. On success, the report row is removed from the database, which means it will no longer appear in reporting or moderation queries. If the Prisma schema or domain rules require preserving an audit trail, that responsibility should be handled by separate audit tables like `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits`, not by this endpoint itself.

Because deleting report data can affect compliance and auditability, this operation is restricted to privileged actors such as platform administrators, reflected by the `authorizationActors` array. Implementers should ensure that appropriate authorization checks and logging are performed in the service layer when this endpoint is invoked, including capturing who deleted the report and why.
operations.description:
Delete a specific product review report associated with a given product review from the shopping mall system.

This operation operates on the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` Prisma table, which holds customer- or seller-submitted reports and abuse flags targeting product reviews stored in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. The `reviewId` parameter identifies the parent review record, while `reportId` identifies the report record to be removed. Before performing the deletion, the service should verify that the report belongs to the specified review, using the foreign key relationship defined in the Prisma schema (for example, comparing `product_review_id` to `reviewId`).

The deletion performed by this endpoint is a permanent removal of the report record from the database. Once removed, the report will no longer be available for moderation workflows or reporting, so the business logic must ensure this action is appropriate given the report's status and any retention policies described in your requirements documentation. If auditability is required, implementers should record the deletion action in a separate audit table such as `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` before or after removing the row.

Security and permissions are critical here, because the ability to delete reports can be sensitive. The `authorizationActors` is set to `["platformAdmin"]` to indicate that only platform administrators (or equivalent high-privilege roles) may call this operation. Authentication middleware and service-level authorization checks should enforce this constraint and may also log additional information such as the administrator's identity and the reason for deletion.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of moderation events associated with a specific product review. It is associated with the `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` Prisma model, which stores historical moderation actions applied to `shopping_mall_product_reviews` records. The endpoint allows a privileged platform administrator to review how a given review has been moderated over time, without providing any capability to create, modify, or remove moderation events.

The API uses the HTTP PATCH method because it accepts a potentially complex search/filter request body. The request body DTO `IShoppingMallProductReviewModerationEvent.IRequest` encapsulates filtering options such as time ranges, moderation action types, the identity of the actor who performed the moderation, free-text search over moderator notes, and pagination parameters like page index, page size, and sorting instructions. All moderation events returned are constrained to the review specified by `reviewId`, which corresponds to a primary key in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`.

From the Prisma perspective, the implementation will query the `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` table with a mandatory foreign-key condition on the given review, applying additional filters defined in the request body. Only fields that exist in that model—such as timestamps, action enum, actor references, and comment text—may be projected into the DTO. This operation is read-only and does not alter any database records, making it safe for audit and compliance use cases where a complete, immutable history of moderation is required.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filterable list of moderation events for a single product review.

This endpoint works over the `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` Prisma model, which records individual moderation actions performed against entries in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table. Each moderation event row typically stores the identifier of the target review, the moderation action type (for example approve, hide, reject, or edit), the timestamp when the action occurred, references to the platform administrator or automated system that performed the action, and optional explanatory notes or structured metadata. The endpoint groups those rows logically as a history for the review referenced by the `reviewId` path parameter.

The PATCH method is used so that complex filtering and pagination parameters can be supplied via JSON in the request body. The `IShoppingMallProductReviewModerationEvent.IRequest` DTO is expected to define properties such as date range filters, action-type filters, actor filters, and pagination controls, as well as sorting options (for example newest-first by created-at timestamp). The `reviewId` must be a UUID string that matches a record in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`; the implementation should verify that the review exists and respond with an appropriate error if it does not, or if the caller attempts to query a review they are not permitted to inspect.

Access to moderation history is sensitive, because moderator notes may contain internal reasoning, risk assessments, or references to fraud detection workflows. For this reason, the operation is restricted to the `platformAdmin` actor in `authorizationActors`. The controller layer will enforce authentication and authorization decorators so that only authenticated platform administrators can call this API. In addition, service-level logic should log access to moderation histories for audit purposes.

This list operation complements the detail endpoint `GET /reviews/{reviewId}/moderationEvents/{moderationEventId}`, which retrieves one specific moderation event with full detail. A typical workflow is that an administrator first calls this list endpoint to see the entire moderation timeline and then uses the detail endpoint to inspect a particular event in depth. Neither endpoint provides any capability to modify the underlying moderation records; changes to moderation state are handled by other administrative flows that write to `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the full details of a single moderation event attached to a specific product review. It is implemented against the `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` Prisma model, which represents individual moderation actions applied to entries in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. The path design includes both `reviewId` and `moderationEventId` so that the service can verify that a requested moderation event belongs to the expected parent review, preventing cross-review data leakage.

The operation uses the HTTP GET method and returns a single `IShoppingMallProductReviewModerationEvent` DTO. This DTO should map directly to the fields of the `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` model, including the associated review identifier, moderation action type, timestamp, references to the administrative or automated actor who performed the action, and any notes or extended metadata stored in the table. No request body is required, because the combination of `reviewId` and `moderationEventId` in the path uniquely identifies the record to retrieve.

On the database side, the implementation will perform a lookup in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` scoped by both the primary key for the moderation event and the foreign key pointing to the review identified by `reviewId`. If either the review does not exist in `shopping_mall_product_reviews` or the event is not associated with that review, the service should return a not-found style error. This strict scoping is important for correctness and security, ensuring that callers cannot infer or access moderation events outside of the intended review context.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a single moderation event for a given product review.

This endpoint reads from the `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` Prisma model, which contains historical records of moderation actions applied to rows in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table. A moderation event usually stores the review identifier, an action type describing what decision was made (such as approve, hide, or reject), the time at which the decision occurred, references to the platform administrator or automated rule engine responsible, and optional note or metadata fields. By returning a single `IShoppingMallProductReviewModerationEvent` DTO, the API exposes all of these fields in a structured form suitable for administrative UIs.

Two path parameters are required to identify the target record. The `reviewId` parameter is a UUID string that corresponds to the primary key of a product review in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. The `moderationEventId` parameter is a UUID string that identifies a row in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`. The service must ensure that the moderation event referenced by `moderationEventId` is in fact linked to the review referenced by `reviewId`; if not, it should return a 404-like error instead of leaking information about unrelated moderation events.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to platform-level administrators, represented by the `platformAdmin` actor in `authorizationActors`. Administrative and moderation tools may call this API when an operator selects a specific moderation event from the list provided by `PATCH /reviews/{reviewId}/moderationEvents` and needs to view the full rationale and data associated with that decision. The endpoint is purely read-only and does not support creating, updating, or deleting moderation events, preserving the integrity of the moderation audit trail stored in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`.

operations.name: at

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the seller's response associated with a specific product review in the shoppingMall domain. It is built on top of the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` primary table as the owning review entity and the `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` subsidiary table, which stores a single optional seller-authored response per review. The API locates the target review by its unique identifier and then fetches the linked seller response row if present.

The endpoint is intended for read-only access from clients that need to display the conversation context around a review, especially on product detail pages, order history screens, or seller dashboards. It does not modify any database state. The implementation is expected to join or follow the relation from the review to the seller response, handling the case where no response exists by returning a null/empty payload while still indicating success.

The response DTO type `IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse` represents the denormalized view of the seller response, including core fields from `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` (such as body text, created/updated timestamps, and visibility flags) and any necessary identifiers to trace back to the owning review and seller. It must strictly reflect the Prisma schema fields and must not assume non-existent auditing columns such as `deleted_at` or `created_by` unless they are actually present in the model definition.
operations.description:
Retrieve the seller-authored response for a specific product review so that clients can render the full review conversation context.

This operation reads from the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table, which stores customer-authored product reviews, and its related `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` table, which is modeled as a subsidiary entity that holds a seller's reply to that review. Typically, there is at most one seller response per review, enforced by either a one-to-one relation or a unique constraint on the foreign key column linking the response back to `shopping_mall_product_reviews`.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is designed primarily for public or broadly accessible read scenarios. The seller response is part of the visible review content that customers see alongside ratings and review text. Because visibility rules and moderation are handled at the data level (for example, using status or visibility fields defined in the Prisma schema and potentially cross-checked against `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`), the endpoint itself does not need to restrict access to authenticated actors. However, implementations should ensure that responses marked as hidden or removed according to business rules are not returned to general consumers.

In terms of database relationships, the handler will resolve the review using the `reviewId` path parameter, which maps to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` model. It then navigates to the associated record in `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` via the defined Prisma relation. If the response exists and passes any review-policy or moderation checks defined in related policy tables (such as `shopping_mall_review_policies`), the response DTO is returned. If no response exists, the API should return a 200 OK with a null body or an empty structure, allowing clients to easily detect that no seller reply has been authored yet.

Validation rules for this operation focus on verifying that the `reviewId` is well-formed (for example, a UUID string if that is how the Prisma model defines the primary key) and that the referenced review record exists and is in a state where its associated content may be displayed. Any failure to find the review should result in a not-found error, whereas absence of a seller response for a valid review is not considered an error.

This endpoint is typically used together with other review-related APIs, such as listing product reviews, retrieving a single review detail, or creating/updating the seller response. For example, a client might call a product review list API, then call this endpoint for each review to lazily fetch associated seller responses if they are not already embedded in the list response.
operations.summary: Retrieve the seller response entity for a given product review (shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses).

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target product review whose seller response should be retrieved. This maps to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` model and is typically a UUID string, uniquely identifying a single customer-authored review within the shoppingMall platform.

responseBody.description: Seller response associated with the specified product review, or null/empty when no response has been authored. The structure follows the `IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse` DTO, which corresponds to the `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` Prisma model and exposes fields such as response body content, timestamps, and identifiers referencing the owning review and seller.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A customer-authored product review must exist before a seller response can be retrieved for that review. Creating a review generates the reviewId used by this endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation creates or replaces the seller's response associated with a specific product review in the shoppingMall domain. It writes to the `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` subsidiary table, which is linked one-to-one with the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` primary table. The API uses the `reviewId` path parameter to identify the owning review row, then inserts a new seller response if none exists or overwrites the existing one according to business rules.

The request body uses the `IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse.ICreate` DTO, which represents the minimal set of fields a seller must supply when authoring a response. This typically includes the textual content of the response and optional metadata such as language or visibility hints, but it must not include the foreign key to the review itself, as that is derived from the `reviewId` path parameter. All other fields such as identifiers and system timestamps are generated by the backend according to the Prisma schema definitions.

The operation returns the resulting seller response in the `IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse` DTO form, allowing clients to immediately render the newly authored or updated response. The implementation must honor review and response policies defined in configuration tables like `shopping_mall_review_policies` and may record moderation events in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` as appropriate.
operations.description:
Create or replace a seller-authored response for a specific product review identified by `reviewId`.

This operation targets two closely related Prisma models: the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` primary table, which contains the original customer review, and the `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` subsidiary table, which holds a seller's reply. When invoked, the handler first validates that the review identified by the `reviewId` path parameter exists and is in a state that allows responses (for example, not permanently removed or blocked by moderation according to `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`). If the review is not found, a not-found error is returned.

From a security and authorization standpoint, only authenticated sellers who are authorized to act on behalf of the seller associated with the underlying order or product should be permitted to call this endpoint. Accordingly, the `authorizationActors` field is set to `["seller"]`, and the business logic must additionally verify ownership and permissions using relations defined in the Prisma schema (for example, linking reviews to orders, order lines, products, and the responsible seller account). Customers and anonymous users are not allowed to create or modify seller responses.

The request body conforms to `IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse.ICreate`, which encapsulates the seller-provided content and any optional attributes allowed at creation time. It intentionally excludes identifiers and foreign keys, since the review linkage comes from `reviewId` and other system fields are generated server-side. Input validation should ensure that the response text meets platform rules defined in `shopping_mall_review_policies`, such as maximum length, prohibited content, and formatting constraints.

If the targeted review currently has no associated seller response, the operation will create a new row in `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses`. If a response already exists, platform policy may dictate whether this call replaces the content (acting like an upsert), rejects the request with a conflict error, or updates specific fields; for this specification, the recommended behavior is to overwrite the existing response content while updating timestamps. In all successful cases, the API returns the resulting seller response as `IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse`, allowing clients to render the up-to-date reply alongside the review.

This endpoint is commonly used from seller-facing dashboards where merchants manage their engagement with customer feedback, as well as from moderation tools that may need to trigger automated or templated responses under the seller's identity. It complements read-only operations that list reviews or retrieve individual reviews and responses for display to shoppers.
operations.summary: Create or overwrite the seller response for a given product review (shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses).

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target product review for which the seller is authoring a response. This maps to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` model and is typically a UUID string.

requestBody.description: Payload containing the seller-authored response content and any allowed creation-time attributes. The DTO `IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse.ICreate` corresponds to the `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` Prisma model and must not redundantly include the review identifier, which is supplied via the `reviewId` path parameter.

responseBody.description: The newly created or updated seller response for the specified product review, represented by `IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse`, which reflects the fields of the `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` Prisma model including identifiers and server-generated timestamps.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: A customer-authored product review must exist before a seller can create or overwrite a seller response linked to that review. The review creation operation returns the reviewId required by this endpoint.

operations.specification:
Update or create a seller response for a specific product review in the shoppingMall_product_review_seller_responses table, identified indirectly via the parent review in shoppingMall_product_reviews.

This PUT operation will allow an authenticated seller, who owns the product associated with the review, to create a new response if none exists yet or update the existing response content and visibility flags. The primary Prisma table is shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses, which stores seller-authored responses tied to a product review, and it is related to shopping_mall_product_reviews and shopping_mall_products to ensure the seller has authority over the underlying product.

The request body will carry structured response content fields (e.g., body text, optional internal notes or visibility settings) in the DTO type IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse.IUpdate. The API will enforce that the path parameter reviewId refers to an existing review record and that the authenticated seller is allowed to respond. On success, it returns the full seller response resource using IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse, including timestamps and status fields defined in the Prisma schema.
operations.description:
Update or create the seller’s response associated with a specific product review on the shoppingMall platform.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses table, which stores seller-authored replies to customer reviews recorded in shopping_mall_product_reviews. Each seller response is logically attached to a single review and, through that review, to a specific product in shopping_mall_products. When the seller calls this API, the service first validates that the supplied reviewId in the path corresponds to an existing review and that the authenticated seller account owns the product referenced by that review. This ownership check ensures that sellers can only respond to reviews on their own products.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is restricted to authenticated seller actors, represented by the authorizationActors value ["seller"]. The implementation must verify the seller identity from the authentication context, compare it against the seller associated with the product in the underlying Prisma relations, and reject attempts to respond to reviews for products that the seller does not control. The operation should also respect any business rules encoded in fields or comments within the Prisma schema, such as maximum response length, whether multiple responses are allowed, and whether responses can be edited after initial publication.

In terms of business logic, the API accepts a request body defined by IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse.IUpdate, which includes the editable fields of the seller response such as the textual content and optional flags that control visibility or publication status. If a response already exists for the given review, the operation updates that record; if not, it creates a new response row linked to the review. The service must handle validation errors, such as missing content or invalid state transitions, and return appropriate error codes.

This endpoint complements other review- and rating-related operations that allow customers to create reviews and admins to moderate them. While customers and admins interact with shopping_mall_product_reviews and moderation tables, sellers use this endpoint specifically to manage their own responses, enabling transparent dialogue in the review section of the shoppingMall platform.
operations.summary: Update or create the seller response associated with a product review (shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses).

operations.name: update

A seller response record for the given reviewId must be creatable via POST before it can be updated via PUT; this POST operation establishes the initial seller response row referenced by subsequent updates.

operations.specification:
Delete the seller’s response associated with a specific product review from the shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses table, identified indirectly via the parent review in shopping_mall_product_reviews.

This DELETE operation allows an authenticated seller to remove their existing response to a review of one of their products. It operates primarily on the shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses table and uses the reviewId path parameter to locate the corresponding response record linked to the review. The service must ensure the seller owns the product associated with the review before performing the deletion.

The endpoint does not require a request body and, on successful deletion, does not need to return a response body. It simply performs a hard removal of the seller response record while leaving the original customer review in shopping_mall_product_reviews intact. Business rules from the Prisma schema, such as constraints on when responses may be removed, should be enforced in the implementation.
operations.description:
Remove the seller’s response associated with a particular product review on the shoppingMall platform.

This operation targets the shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses table, which stores seller-authored replies to reviews defined in shopping_mall_product_reviews. By supplying the reviewId in the path, the API locates the existing response tied to that review and deletes it from the database. The customer’s original review, stored in shopping_mall_product_reviews, remains unaffected; only the seller’s reply record is removed.

Security enforcement is critical: only authenticated seller actors may invoke this endpoint, as indicated by authorizationActors ["seller"]. The implementation must derive the seller identity from the authentication context, traverse the relationships from review to product and seller as defined in the Prisma schema, and verify that the calling seller is the legitimate owner of the product. If the review does not belong to a product owned by the seller, or if no response exists for the given reviewId, the operation should fail with appropriate error codes.

From a business perspective, this deletion is used when a seller wants to retract or replace their public response, for example before posting a new response via the corresponding PUT /reviews/{reviewId}/sellerResponse endpoint. The operation should respect any policy constraints defined by the platform, such as restrictions on deleting responses after moderation or within certain time windows. Related APIs include customer review creation and editing operations on shopping_mall_product_reviews and moderation endpoints that manage the visibility and compliance of both reviews and seller responses.
operations.summary: Delete the seller response associated with a product review (shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses).

A seller response must be created before it can be deleted. This POST operation creates the seller response row that will later be removed by the DELETE endpoint.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the rating aggregate data for a specific product from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates`. The underlying table stores precomputed, materialized statistics such as average rating, total review count, and possibly breakdowns by rating value for each product, and optionally for each SKU. Consequently, the operation does not require authentication and exposes an empty `authorizationActors` array. operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the rating aggregate information for a specific product from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates`. It is designed as a PATCH-based search-style retrieval scoped to a single product, allowing the client to control aspects such as whether SKU-level breakdowns should be included, or to filter by region or time window if supported by the underlying schema.

The endpoint accepts the `productId` as a required path parameter, which corresponds to the primary key or unique identifier of a record in the `shopping_mall_products` table and is used to locate related aggregate rating rows in `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates`. Any additional search or filter criteria are passed via a JSON request body typed as `IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.IRequest`.

The response returns a structured view of the rating aggregates for the target product, potentially including overall average rating, total review count, distribution of ratings, and optional per-SKU aggregations, as defined in the `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` schema. The response type is modeled as `IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate`, which exposes the full aggregate structure for the product within the shopping mall service context.
operations.description:
Retrieve rating aggregates for a specific product using its identifier while allowing optional, structured filter criteria through the request body.

This operation focuses on read-only analytic data stored in the `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` table, which is conceptually derived from individual customer reviews recorded in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table. The aggregate table typically contains fields such as total review count, sum or average of rating scores, and potentially breakdowns per SKU or per region. The Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` is expected to define the exact set of aggregate fields, indexes, and any constraints that ensure efficient lookup by product.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is safe to expose publicly because it returns only summarized rating information and no personally identifiable review content. For that reason, `authorizationType` is set to null and `authorizationActor` is also null, indicating no authentication requirement at the interface layer. Implementations may still apply rate limiting or IP-based throttling to protect against scraping and abuse.

The `productId` path parameter is mandatory and identifies which product's aggregates should be retrieved. It is typically a string identifier (often a UUID or business-specific product key) that matches the primary key in the `shopping_mall_products` table. The request body, typed as `IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.IRequest`, can encapsulate optional filters such as region codes, sales channel, time windows, or flags indicating whether SKU-level aggregates should be included, depending on what fields and query patterns the Prisma schema and business requirements support.

Error handling should include clear responses when the referenced product does not exist, when no aggregate data is available yet (for example, a product with no reviews), or when invalid filter criteria are supplied. Related operations include product review listing endpoints and product detail retrieval endpoints, which together provide both the detailed review content and the summarized aggregate metrics used in catalog and product detail UI components.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a global summary of review and rating statistics across the shopping mall platform using the Prisma table `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` as its primary data source, and optionally incorporating other analytic tables if defined. It is modeled as a GET endpoint because it does not require complex filter criteria in the request body; instead it returns a standard, platform-wide summary snapshot.

The purpose of this endpoint is to provide high-level statistics such as total number of reviews, average rating across all products, distribution of ratings, and possibly key indicators like number of products with at least one review. These summary metrics can be displayed on administrative dashboards, reporting views, or public-facing pages where aggregate marketplace health indicators are needed.

The response type `IShoppingMallReviewStatisticsSummary` is a computed DTO that does not map directly to a single Prisma table row but instead represents the result of aggregation queries over tables like `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and possibly `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. The operation is read-only and does not modify any database state.
operations.description:
Retrieve a global summary of review and rating statistics across the shopping mall platform, computed primarily from the `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` table and related review data.

This operation is designed as a lightweight, read-only GET endpoint that returns a standardized summary snapshot without requiring any request body. The underlying implementation is expected to execute aggregation queries that compute platform-wide metrics such as total review count, average rating across all products, counts of reviews per rating bucket, and potentially additional indicators such as number of products with at least one review or distribution of reviews over recent time periods.

From a security perspective, this endpoint returns only aggregated, non-personal data and can therefore be safely exposed as a public endpoint. The `authorizationType` is null and `authorizationActor` is null to reflect that the interface specification layer does not enforce authentication. Implementations may still choose to restrict this endpoint to internal dashboards or apply rate limiting depending on deployment requirements.

The response body is typed as `IShoppingMallReviewStatisticsSummary`, which is a descriptive DTO representing computed statistics rather than a direct Prisma model. Its fields might include numeric counts, averages, and arrays describing rating distributions, all derived from one or more underlying tables like `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. Error handling should be straightforward; in normal operation the endpoint should always return a valid summary, even if some metrics are zero when the platform has limited review data.

Related operations include product-level rating aggregate retrieval and detailed review listing endpoints, which together provide both the global overview and the granular insights needed for analytics and UX components.

responseBody.description: Aggregated platform-wide review and rating statistics, including counts, averages, and distributions as defined by the summary DTO.

operations.specification:
This operation computes aggregated review statistics grouped by product using data primarily from the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` Prisma table and, for performance, optionally from materialized aggregates such as `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates`. It is a read-only analytical endpoint that supports advanced filtering and pagination, returning per-product metrics such as total review count, average rating, and rating distribution.

The endpoint accepts a complex filter and pagination payload in the request body, which allows clients (admin dashboards or seller tools) to scope statistics by product identifiers, rating ranges, creation date ranges, moderation states, regions, or other catalog-related constraints that are derivable from the surrounding shopping mall schema. Internally, the implementation performs GROUP BY and aggregation queries over the underlying review data set and does not create, modify, or delete any records in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`.

Because the request body can be complex, the HTTP method is PATCH while the semantics remain strictly read-only. No path parameters are required. The response returns a paginated list of product-level statistics DTOs following the `IShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsByProduct` contract, wrapped in the generic pagination container `IPageIShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsByProduct`.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated review statistics per product, based on customer-authored reviews stored in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table.

The `shopping_mall_product_reviews` model, described as "Customer-authored product reviews and star ratings", is expected to contain fields such as rating value, textual content, references to the reviewing customer, associated product or SKU, timestamps, and moderation or visibility state. This API leverages those columns to compute summary metrics per product, such as total number of reviews, average rating, and rating histograms. Where available, it may use precomputed aggregates from `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` for efficiency, but its logical source of truth is the underlying review records.

Clients send a structured filter object in the request body, typed as `IShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsByProduct.IRequest`. Typical fields include lists of product identifiers, optional seller constraints, minimum and maximum rating thresholds, creation date ranges, and paging/sorting options. The endpoint uses these criteria to determine which reviews are included in each product’s statistics, and the response is returned as a paginated collection `IPageIShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsByProduct`, where each item summarizes statistics for a single product.

From a security perspective, this endpoint is intended for internal analytics and operational tooling. It is limited to authenticated marketplace actors, such as platform administrators and sellers, represented by `authorizationActors: ["platformAdmin", "seller"]`. The concrete authorization layer must ensure that sellers can only see statistics for products they own, while platform administrators may have global visibility. Errors should be returned when filters reference products outside the caller’s permitted scope, or when filter combinations are invalid or excessively broad for the system’s resource limits.

This operation computes aggregated review statistics grouped by seller using the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` Prisma table joined with catalog and seller ownership relationships. It is designed for performance monitoring, quality tracking, and marketplace governance by summarizing metrics such as total reviews received, average rating across a seller’s catalog, and rating distributions over a filtered set of reviews.

The endpoint accepts a rich filter and pagination payload via the request body, enabling clients (platform administrators and sellers) to scope statistics by seller identifiers, product categories, rating thresholds, time windows, moderation states, and possibly region or channel information. Internally, the implementation groups review data by seller, which is inferred through the association of each review with products or SKUs that belong to a specific seller. No review data is created, updated, or deleted by this operation; it is purely analytical.

Like the product-based statistics endpoint, this is a read-only operation implemented as HTTP PATCH to support complex request bodies. It returns a paginated list of seller-level review statistics DTOs according to the `IShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsBySeller` contract, wrapped in `IPageIShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsBySeller`. The primary underlying Prisma table is `shopping_mall_product_reviews`, and additional tables such as `shopping_mall_seller` and `shopping_mall_products` are involved for resolving seller ownership during aggregation.

This operation takes a filter payload typed as `IShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsBySeller.IRequest`, including optional seller identifiers, category filters, rating ranges, date intervals (for example, last 30 days), and moderation state constraints. Using these filters, the service aggregates review data per seller to compute metrics such as total number of reviews, average rating, and rating distribution buckets.

The response is a paginated collection `IPageIShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsBySeller`, where each entry summarizes the computed statistics for a single seller under the specified filters. This Aggregated information is used by admin dashboards for marketplace health monitoring, by seller performance views, and by risk or fraud analysis tools that may combine these statistics with other signals such as `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries`.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to authenticated actors, specifically platform administrators and sellers, declared as `authorizationActors: ["platformAdmin", "seller"]`. Platform administrators generally have full visibility across all sellers, while each seller is limited to viewing only their own statistics. These constraints must be enforced by the authorization layer. Error handling should cover invalid identifiers or filter combinations, attempts to access data outside the caller’s scope, and requests that are too broad to serve efficiently within system limits.

operations.specification:
This operation searches and retrieves a paginated list of administrator action audit records from the Prisma table `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits`. It is designed for platform administrators to review historical actions taken in the admin console, such as configuration changes, moderation actions, and management activities across the shoppingMall platform.

The endpoint follows the standard PATCH-based search pattern, accepting a rich filter and pagination request body of type `IShoppingMallAdminActionAudit.IRequest` and returning a paginated collection of summary records using `IPageIShoppingMallAdminActionAudit.ISummary`. The request DTO encapsulates filter fields such as admin identifier, action type, target resource type, time range, and result status, while the summary response focuses on the key attributes required for list views (timestamps, actor identity, action type, and high-level outcome).

This specification assumes that the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` table is a primary business entity for auditability and compliance, and that records are created automatically by the system whenever an administrator performs a significant action. As such, this operation is strictly read-only and does not expose any capability to modify, create, or delete audit log entries.
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of administrator action audit records from the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` table.

This operation allows authorized platform administrators to query historical admin actions performed within the shoppingMall platform. Typical use cases include investigating configuration changes, tracking moderation decisions on product reviews, examining dispute handling actions, and auditing changes to policies, payouts, or other administrative resources. The underlying Prisma model `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` is expected to contain fields such as the acting administrator identifier, associated session or IP information, action type or category, target resource type and identifier, timestamps, and a result or status field describing whether the action succeeded.

The request body of type `IShoppingMallAdminActionAudit.IRequest` supports advanced search and filtering. Platform admins can filter by one or more administrator accounts, by action categories (for example, configuration changes, review moderations), by the type of resource affected, by time ranges (from–to created timestamps), and by outcome status. The request DTO also defines pagination parameters (page number, page size) and sorting options such as sorting by newest actions first or by specific action attributes. These filters enable admins to quickly narrow down the audit trail to the subset of actions relevant to a particular investigation or compliance review.

The response uses the paginated summary container type `IPageIShoppingMallAdminActionAudit.ISummary`. Each summary entry includes the core audit information necessary for list and table views: the unique audit record identifier, timestamp of the action, the acting administrator identity (for example, admin account code or ID), the high-level action type, the primary target entity, and the overall result of the action. Detailed technical fields that are only needed in drill-down views are intentionally omitted from the summary to keep list responses compact and efficient. Retrieve the full details of a single fraud or risk rule definition from the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` Prisma model using its unique business code.

This GET `/fraudRuleDefinitions/{ruleCode}` operation is a read-only detail endpoint for the primary fraud rule configuration table `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`. The model is expected to enforce uniqueness on the `rule_code` column so that each `ruleCode` path parameter maps to exactly one record. Using `rule_code` instead of a surrogate ID results in stable, human-meaningful URLs suitable for admin tooling and audit references.

The response DTO `IShoppingMallFraudRuleDefinition` exposes all relevant columns from `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`, such as `rule_code`, rule name, detailed description, rule category, severity, activation flags, evaluation scope, configuration payload (for thresholds, conditions, or scoring), and lifecycle timestamps like `created_at` and `updated_at`. The operation performs a single lookup in the Prisma model and maps the result into this DTO without modifying the underlying data.
operations.description:
Get the detailed configuration of a single fraud rule definition identified by its `rule_code` in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` Prisma table.

This GET operation on `/fraudRuleDefinitions/{ruleCode}` is bound to the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` model, which stores all fraud and risk rule definitions for the shoppingMall platform. The `{ruleCode}` segment corresponds to the `rule_code` column in that table and is treated as a globally unique business identifier. This design allows administrators and risk analysts to refer to rules using stable codes that appear in dashboards, configuration exports, and incident tickets.

When invoked, the implementation queries `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` for the row whose `rule_code` equals the supplied `ruleCode`. If found, the record is converted to the `IShoppingMallFraudRuleDefinition` DTO, which mirrors the model fields: identification attributes (`rule_code`, name), rich description, categorical attributes such as rule `category` and `severity`, execution flags like `is_active`, and any configuration or parameter fields that drive the behavior of the fraud engine. Timestamps like `created_at` and `updated_at` are also included to support audit and change-tracking use cases.

Access to this endpoint is limited to platform administrators represented by the `platformAdmin` actor, since the configuration of fraud rules is sensitive and must not be exposed to customers, sellers, or guest users. A typical workflow begins with an administrator calling the list/search endpoint `PATCH /fraudRuleDefinitions` to find candidate rules, then calling this detail endpoint with a selected `ruleCode` to inspect full configuration before optionally editing via separate write APIs.

If no record exists in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` for the provided `ruleCode`, the server should return a 404 Not Found response using the platform’s standardized error structure. Inactive rules are still returned, with their activation status reflected in the DTO, so that administrators can inspect and potentially re-enable them. The operation remains strictly read-only with no side effects on the underlying Prisma model.

Create a new fraud rule definition in the shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions Prisma table. This operation allows platform administrators or risk engineers to register a new fraud and risk rule that will later be evaluated against orders, payments, accounts, or other events.

The rule will be identified by a unique business-level `ruleCode` column in the shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions model (string, globally unique). Other core columns typically include a human-readable name, severity level, category, description, activation flag, and a serialized condition or expression definition that the fraud engine uses to evaluate whether a rule is triggered.

This API accepts a DTO of type `IShoppingMallFraudRuleDefinition.ICreate`, which mirrors the Prisma columns except for system-managed fields like primary key and timestamps. The implementation must validate uniqueness of `ruleCode`, ensure that required business fields are present, and reject invalid condition payloads according to the fraud engine’s expected structure.
operations.description:
Create a new fraud rule definition record in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` table so that the platform’s fraud detection engine can evaluate it for future transactions.

This operation works against the Prisma model `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`, whose purpose is to store configurable fraud and risk rules evaluated against orders, payments, accounts, or other events. Each row represents a single rule identified by a unique `ruleCode` that is stable across deployments and environments, a human-friendly rule name and description, a category or domain (for example, payment, account, logistics), a severity level used by downstream decisioning logic, and a structured or serialized condition definition that the rule engine executes. There is also typically a boolean flag such as `isEnabled` to decide whether the rule is currently active.

From a security perspective, only privileged backoffice actors such as platform administrators or a dedicated risk operations team should be able to create new fraud rules. As a result, this endpoint should be protected and exposed only to the `platformAdmin` actor (or equivalently named backoffice account type). The implementation must enforce strict input validation, ensuring that the condition structure is syntactically valid for the configured fraud engine and that any referenced fields (such as order value, customer age, device fingerprint score, etc.) are part of the engine’s allowed field set. Error responses should clearly indicate invalid fields or malformed expressions rather than leaking internal engine details.

This operation is closely related to the update endpoint `PUT /fraudRuleDefinitions/{ruleCode}`, which modifies existing rule definitions. Typical workflows in the admin UI will first list rules (via a separate search endpoint on this table), use this POST endpoint to create a new rule, then later use the PUT endpoint to adjust thresholds or enable/disable a rule. Attempts to create a rule with an already existing `ruleCode` must result in a conflict error and no database insertion. On success, the response returns the full `IShoppingMallFraudRuleDefinition` representation, allowing the client to immediately render the rule details in the admin console.
