It is backed by the `shopping_mall_access_logs` Prisma model and reflects the result of applying search filters, time range constraints, and sorting options defined in `IShoppingMallAccessLog.IRequest`.

Admin consoles, security monitoring tools, and performance dashboards typically bind directly to this structure: `pagination` is used to drive paging controls, while `data` provides the current page of access log summaries for visualization, export, or drill-down into more detailed log views.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata describing the current slice of error log results.

Includes the current page index, page size, total number of error log entries that matched the filters, and the computed total number of pages. This information is derived from querying the `shopping_mall_error_logs` table using the criteria in `IShoppingMallErrorLog.IRequest`.

data.description:
Array of error log summary DTOs for the current page.

Each element is an `IShoppingMallErrorLog.ISummary` instance representing a single error or exception event recorded in the `shopping_mall_error_logs` Prisma model. Summaries typically surface fields such as occurrence time, severity, error code or category, short message, and correlation identifiers so that operators can quickly identify and prioritize issues without loading full stack traces or large diagnostic payloads.

IPageIShoppingMallErrorLog.ISummary.description:
Paginated collection of application error log summary entries for the shoppingMall platform.

This container wraps a page of `IShoppingMallErrorLog.ISummary` records along with pagination information and is returned by the `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/errorLogs` index operation. It represents the filtered, sorted, and paginated view of rows stored in the `shopping_mall_error_logs` Prisma table based on the search criteria supplied in `IShoppingMallErrorLog.IRequest`.

Administrative consoles, observability dashboards, and incident investigation tools use this structure to browse and triage error logs over time. The `pagination` object feeds paging controls and total count indicators, while the `data` array provides the individual error summaries that can be clicked or expanded to access more detailed error information via dedicated detail endpoints.

pagination.description:
Pagination state for the current slice of integration event log summaries.

This object follows the shared `IPage.IPagination` contract and carries information such as the current page index, page size, total number of log records that matched the filter criteria, and the total number of pages. Monitoring dashboards and admin tools use this information to render navigation controls and to understand how large the result set is when browsing integration logs from the `shopping_mall_integration_event_logs` table.

data.description:
Collection of integration event log summary records for the current page.

Each element is an `IShoppingMallIntegrationEventLog.ISummary` instance that represents a single row from the `shopping_mall_integration_event_logs` Prisma model, projected into a lightweight form optimized for list and dashboard views. These summaries surface key fields such as identifiers, provider type and name, event type, direction, status, latency, HTTP status code, and timestamps so that platform administrators can quickly scan integration behavior without loading full detail payloads for every record.

IPageIShoppingMallIntegrationEventLog.IS.description:
Paginated collection of integration event log summaries for administrative observability.

This schema wraps a list of `IShoppingMallIntegrationEventLog.ISummary` records together with `IPage.IPagination` metadata to support efficient paging over large volumes of integration log data stored in the `shopping_mall_integration_event_logs` table. It is used as the response body for the `PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/integrationEventLogs` endpoint, which allows platformAdmin actors to search, filter, and page through historical interactions with external providers and infrastructure services without retrieving all records at once.

pagination.description:
Pagination information describing the current window of performance incident summaries.

This object conforms to the shared `IPage.IPagination` structure and includes fields such as current page number, page size, total incident count matching the filters, and total number of pages. It is used by admin-facing monitoring UIs to drive navigation over potentially large time-series datasets of performance incidents aggregated from logging tables.

data.description:
Array of performance incident summary records for the current page.

Each element is an `IShoppingMallLoggingPerformanceIncident.ISummary` object that represents a single detected performance incident, typically aggregated from log-oriented Prisma models such as `shopping_mall_error_logs`, `shopping_mall_access_logs`, and `shopping_mall_integration_event_logs`. These summaries expose key diagnostics such as detection time, severity, category, affected service or endpoint, and metric values, enabling platform administrators to review and triage incidents directly from reporting dashboards.

IPageIShoppingMallLoggingPerformanceInci.description:
Paginated list of performance incident summaries derived from ShoppingMall logging data.

This schema is the response envelope for the `PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/reports/logging/performanceIncidents` endpoint. It combines paging metadata (`IPage.IPagination`) with a list of `IShoppingMallLoggingPerformanceIncident.ISummary` records so that platform administrators can efficiently browse and analyze performance-related incidents, such as slow responses, timeouts, and error spikes, without loading the full underlying log streams at once.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the integration failure incident report.

This object follows the `IPage.IPagination` schema and exposes the current page index, page-size limit, total record count, and total number of pages. It allows administrative UIs and reporting tools to navigate large volumes of integration failure logs in a controlled way, avoiding unbounded scans against logging storage while still providing full visibility over time.

data.description:
List of integration failure incident summaries for the current page.

Each element is an `IShoppingMallLoggingIntegrationFailure.ISummary` DTO that represents a single failed or degraded interaction with an external system, aggregated from log sources such as `shopping_mall_integration_event_logs` and `shopping_mall_error_logs`. This collection is ordered and filtered according to the search criteria provided in `IShoppingMallLoggingIntegrationFailure.IRequest`, and is intended for use in administrative dashboards, SLA tracking views, and incident investigation workflows.

IPageIShoppingMallLoggingIntegrationFail.description:
Paginated collection of integration failure incident summaries in the ShoppingMall platform.

This wrapper combines page-level navigation information with a list of `IShoppingMallLoggingIntegrationFailure.ISummary` records returned by the `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/reports/logging/integrationFailures` reporting endpoint. Platform administrators use this structure to browse, slice, and analyze failed external integrations—such as payment gateways, shipping carriers, and notification providers—while keeping responses bounded and efficient for both clients and the underlying logging and analytics infrastructure.

IShoppingMallCustomerAuth.IJoin.description:
Request body schema for a customer self-registration (join) operation on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used when a new customer signs up themselves and should include both identity credentials and session context fields so that the platform can create authentication credentials, the customer profile, and an initial session/audit trail. The server will create related records in shopping_mall_customer, shopping_mall_auth_credentials, and shopping_mall_auth_credentials_of_customers, plus optional auth log and security event rows.

email.description:
Customer email address used both as the login identifier and the primary email in shopping_mall_customer.
Must be unique among customers and among auth credentials with actor_type = "customer".

password.description:
Plain-text password chosen by the customer.
The backend hashes this value and stores it in shopping_mall_auth_credentials.password_hash.
Clients must never send pre-hashed passwords.

name.description:
Display name of the customer stored in shopping_mall_customer.name.
Shown in customer-facing UIs and communications.

oneOf.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security analytics.
Optional: if omitted or null, the server may infer IP from the HTTP request.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security analytics.
Optional: when null, the server may infer the IP from the transport context.

href.description:
Full URL of the page where the registration request was initiated.
Used to populate shopping_mall_customer_sessions.href for audit and security analysis.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL of the page that led to the registration request.
Stored in shopping_mall_customer_sessions.referrer for auditability and fraud analysis.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IAuthorized.description:
Response body schema returned when a customer is successfully authorized on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents an authorization envelope that combines the current identity snapshot of the authenticated customer with issued JWT tokens. The identity portion is primarily sourced from the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model (fields such as `id`, `email`, `name`, `status`, `is_verified`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`), while sensitive lifecycle fields like `deleted_at` remain internal to the backend and are not exposed.

The root-level scalar fields (`id`, `email`, `name`, `status`, `isVerified`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`) provide a canonical view of the customer at the moment the tokens are issued. The nested `customer` summary property exposes a compact projection suitable for UI consumption, list displays, and embedding into other DTOs. Together with the `token` object, this structure enables clients to treat the user as logged in immediately after join, login, email verification, password reset completion, or password change operations.

The DTO is intentionally read-only from the client perspective. Any changes to the underlying `shopping_mall_customer` record (such as status transitions, name updates, or verification state changes) will be reflected only in newly issued authorization envelopes created by subsequent authentication or refresh flows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated customer.

This value maps directly to the primary key `id` of the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model and remains stable for the lifetime of the account.

email.description:
Primary email address of the customer used for login-related communication, order notifications, and marketing messages where allowed by policy.

This corresponds to the `email` column of `shopping_mall_customer` and will typically match the login email stored in `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` for actor_type = "customer". The value must never expose any password or credential secrets.

name.description:
Display name or full legal name of the customer as stored in `shopping_mall_customer.name`.

This value is used in administrative and customer-facing UIs wherever a human-readable name is required. How it is composed (first name / last name / nickname) is determined by business and localization rules, but within this DTO it always reflects the current persisted value at the time of authorization.

phone.description:
Primary contact phone number for the customer when available.

This field is not a direct column of the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model and may be populated from extended profile data or left undefined if no phone number has been captured. Implementations should treat this as an optional convenience attribute for downstream communication and UI display rather than a required identity key.

status.description:
High-level lifecycle or access status of the customer account.

This maps to the `status` column of the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model and is used, together with risk and credential information, to determine whether the account is allowed to authenticate or perform actions. Typical values include states such as `active`, `suspended`, `blocked`, or `closed`, but the exact vocabulary is defined by the business domain.

isVerified.description:
Flag indicating whether the customer’s primary email address has been verified.

This property reflects the `is_verified` column of the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model and is updated by flows such as email verification completion, certain administrative actions, or migration scripts. Downstream business logic may use this flag to gate access to specific features or to decide whether additional verification steps are required.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the customer account record was first created in the system.

This value corresponds to the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_customer` and typically represents the moment of successful registration or backoffice account creation. It is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the customer account record was last updated.

This value maps to the `updated_at` column of `shopping_mall_customer` and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable fields such as `name`, `status`, or `is_verified` change. It allows clients to detect staleness or to display "last updated" information in administrative interfaces.

customer.description:
Summary projection of the authenticated customer profile intended for UI and list views.

This nested object is built primarily from the `shopping_mall_customer` record but intentionally omits sensitive fields such as email, full status details, and verification history. It provides a compact representation that can be embedded into other resources or cached on the client side without exposing internal-only attributes.

IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a customer account that exposes only the minimal fields needed for identification in UI components, lists, and lightweight references.

This DTO is a read-only projection primarily sourced from the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model but may be augmented with additional profile data such as avatar configuration. It deliberately omits sensitive or internal-only fields like `email`, `status`, `is_verified`, and `deleted_at` to support data minimization and privacy by design. When more detailed customer information is required, callers should use the full `IShoppingMallCustomer` DTO or the authorization envelope rather than this summary view.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer account.

This value maps directly to the `id` primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model and is the stable reference used across orders, reviews, and other related entities.

display_name.description:
Display name or nickname representing the customer in user interfaces.

This value is typically derived from the underlying `shopping_mall_customer.name` column or from related profile configuration, and may be anonymized, masked, or localized depending on business rules. It is intended purely for display and should not be used as a primary key or for secure identification.

avatar_url.description:
Optional URL of the customer avatar image used for compact identification in lists and activity feeds.

The value is a fully qualified URI pointing to a pre-uploaded image stored in an external object storage or media service. No binary data or base64-encoded content is ever included in this field; consumers must treat it strictly as a URL reference and fetch the image through the appropriate media delivery pipeline.

IShoppingMallCustomerAuth.ILogin.description:
Login credentials and session context for an existing shopping mall customer.

Used when a customer signs into the shopping mall platform using email and password. Also carries connection metadata needed to create an authentication session record such as IP, current URL, referrer URL, and User-Agent information for security analytics and audit logs.

email.description:
Customer email address used as the login identifier.

Must match the email stored in shopping_mall_auth_credentials for actor_type "customer" so that the backend can look up the correct credentials row and associated customer account.

password.description:
Plain text password provided by the customer for authentication.

The backend hashes this value using the configured password hashing algorithm and compares the result against the stored password_hash in shopping_mall_auth_credentials. The raw password value is never persisted.

oneOf.description:
Optional client IP address for session and security tracking.

When provided, this should be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 string and will be recorded into shopping_mall_customer_sessions, shopping_mall_auth_logs, and shopping_mall_security_events for traceability.

Explicit null value indicating that the client did not supply an IP address.

In this case, the server derives the IP from the underlying connection context when creating session and security event records.

ip.description:
Optional client IP address for session tracking and security analytics.

If omitted or set to null, the server derives the effective client IP from the HTTP connection metadata and still persists it into session and security logging tables.

href.description:
Absolute URL of the page where the login was initiated.

Captured and persisted into shopping_mall_customer_sessions and possibly shopping_mall_security_events so that operators can understand the navigation context in which the login occurred.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL from which the customer navigated to the login page.

Stored in session and security event records for analytics, fraud detection, and understanding customer navigation flows leading up to authentication.

userAgent.description:
Optional HTTP User-Agent string supplied by the client during the login request.

When present, this value is written into shopping_mall_auth_logs and shopping_mall_security_events (for example as user_agent) to describe the device, browser, and runtime environment used during the authentication attempt. If omitted, the backend may derive the User-Agent directly from the HTTP request headers instead of this field.

IShoppingMallCustomerAuth.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token payload used to renew an authenticated customer session.

The client sends a previously issued refresh token so that the backend can validate it, check underlying credential and customer state, and issue new JWT tokens for the customer. Optional client context such as the User-Agent string can also be provided for richer logging and security analytics on refresh events.

refreshToken.description:
Refresh token previously issued to the authenticated customer.

The backend validates this token according to platform rules (signature verification, expiry checks, rotation policies) and uses its claims to resolve the underlying shopping_mall_auth_credentials and shopping_mall_customer records before issuing new JWT access and refresh tokens.

userAgent.description:
Optional HTTP User-Agent string describing the client environment at the time of the refresh request.

When provided, this value can be recorded into shopping_mall_auth_logs and shopping_mall_security_events for TOKEN_REFRESH events, helping security and analytics teams understand which devices and runtimes are performing token refresh operations. If omitted, the backend may use the User-Agent from the HTTP request headers instead of this field.

IShoppingMallCustomerAuth.IVerifyEmail.description:
Request payload for verifying a customer’s email address using an opaque verification token that was previously issued and stored in shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens.

The client submits only the token that was delivered out of band (typically via email). The backend uses this token to locate the corresponding verification record, validate expiry and consumption state, and then mark the associated customer’s email as verified while updating related authentication records. No actor IDs or session identifiers are included here; those are derived server-side from the token and authentication context.

token.description:
Opaque email verification token previously issued to the customer and stored in shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens.token.

This value is treated as a secure random string with no client-visible structure. It is used by the backend to look up the verification record, confirm that it has not expired or been consumed, and resolve the associated auth credentials and customer identity.

IShoppingMallCustomerAuth.IRequestPasswo.description:
Request payload for initiating a customer password reset workflow.

The client provides the customer’s login email address, and the backend creates a corresponding password reset token in shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens when an eligible credentials record exists. The endpoint always returns a generic acknowledgement regardless of whether the email is registered, preventing account enumeration. No authentication context or actor IDs are supplied in this DTO.

email.description:
Customer login email address used to locate the corresponding shopping_mall_auth_credentials row with actor_type = "customer".

The backend uses this email to determine whether a password reset token can be issued. The response is intentionally generic so callers cannot infer whether an account exists for this email.

IShoppingMallCustomerAuth.IRequestPasswo.description:
Generic acknowledgement response returned after a customer password reset request has been processed.

This DTO intentionally does not reveal whether the email belongs to an existing account. It only indicates that the request has been accepted and, optionally, includes simple hints about follow-up actions such as checking the inbox. It must never expose any security‑sensitive details or account existence information.

oneOf.description:
High‑level status of the password reset request handling.

Must always be a generic, non‑revealing value that does not indicate whether the email address is registered. Typical values are "accepted" or "processed" to indicate that the request has been handled by the system.

High‑level status of the password reset request handling.

Must always be a generic, non‑revealing value that does not indicate whether the email address is registered. Typical values are "accepted" or "processed" to indicate that the request has been handled by the system.

status.description:
High‑level status of the password reset request handling.

Must always be a generic, non‑revealing value that does not indicate whether the email address is registered. Typical values are "accepted" or "processed" to indicate that the request has been handled by the system.

message.description:
Human‑readable message describing that the password reset request has been accepted and that, if an account exists, the platform may send further instructions via email.

This message must be phrased in a way that does not confirm whether the email is associated with any account.

IShoppingMallCustomerAuth.IResetPassword.description:
Password reset completion payload for customer accounts.

This DTO is used when the customer completes a password reset flow using a previously issued reset token. It carries the opaque reset token value and the new password the customer wishes to set.

The server validates the token against shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens (including expiry and consumed status), resolves the owning shopping_mall_auth_credentials row, verifies that actor_type="customer" and that the credentials are in a modifiable state, and then updates the stored password hash.

The DTO must never include any credential or actor identifiers such as auth_credentials_id, customer_id, or email; those are resolved on the server side from the token and database relations. The password field contains the plain text password which will be securely hashed on the backend before being stored in the password_hash column.

token.description:
Opaque password reset token previously issued and stored in shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.token.

This value is treated as an unguessable secret and is used by the server to look up and validate the corresponding password reset record. It must not be guessable or derivable from public information.

password.description:
New plain text password that the customer wishes to set.

The server hashes this value and stores it into shopping_mall_auth_credentials.password_hash. Clients must not send pre‑hashed passwords. Server‑side validation should enforce password strength rules such as minimum length and complexity, but those rules are not encoded directly in this schema.

IShoppingMallCustomerAuth.IChangePasswor.description:
Request body payload for an authenticated customer password change operation.

This DTO is used when a logged-in shopping mall customer wants to update their password by providing the current password and a new desired password. The backend validates the current password against the stored hash and, if valid, replaces it with a hash of the new password and records appropriate authentication and security events.

currentPassword.description:
Current password of the authenticated customer. This value is provided in plain text by the client solely for verification against the stored password hash.

The backend hashes this value and compares it with the password_hash stored in shopping_mall_auth_credentials for the customer actor. It is never stored directly.

newPassword.description:
New password the customer wants to set for their account. Provided in plain text by the client.

The backend hashes this value and persists the hash into shopping_mall_auth_credentials.password_hash for the corresponding customer credentials row. The plaintext value must not be stored.

IShoppingMallSellerJoin.IRequest.description:
Request body payload for registering a new seller account on the shopping mall platform.

This DTO collects login credential information and basic seller profile data required to create both a credentials record in shopping_mall_auth_credentials (with actor_type="seller") and a seller profile record in shopping_mall_seller. The operation may also trigger email verification workflows and audit logging, but these behaviors are handled by the backend and are not exposed as fields in this request.

email.description:
Login email address for the seller account.

This value is stored in shopping_mall_auth_credentials.email for actor_type="seller" and typically also used as the primary contact email in shopping_mall_seller. It must be unique for seller credentials according to the (actor_type, email) uniqueness constraint.

password.description:
Plain text password to be used for the seller account.

The backend hashes this value and stores only the derived password_hash in shopping_mall_auth_credentials. The plaintext password must never be persisted.

storeName.description:
Display name of the seller's store.

This value is persisted in shopping_mall_seller.store_name and is often subject to uniqueness constraints or business validation to avoid duplicates and impersonation of existing brands.

contactPhone.description:
Primary contact phone number for the seller.

Used for operational contact and support. The exact format is validated according to platform policy, but typically follows international phone number standards.

IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized seller session information returned after successful join, login, or refresh operations.

Represents the authenticated seller context for the shopping mall platform, including the seller's unique identifier, core identity attributes, a normalized seller summary object, and issued JWT token information. This structure is used by clients to persist authentication state and attach tokens to subsequent API calls on behalf of the seller actor.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated seller actor.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the seller entity in the shopping_mall_seller table and is used as the stable subject identifier (sub) in authorization logic and resource ownership checks.

email.description:
Primary email address registered for the seller account.

This field is typically unique across all sellers and is used for login, notifications, and compliance-related communication.

store_name.description:
Public storefront name of the seller.

This value is typically unique within the platform so that buyers can clearly identify merchants. It may be subject to validation rules to avoid impersonation or policy violations.

oneOf.description:
Contact phone number for the seller’s store or business.

Used by support staff or buyers (when exposed) to reach the merchant. Format may follow E.164 or a region-specific pattern depending on platform configuration.
Null when no contact phone has been registered or when the seller has explicitly removed the stored phone number.

contact_phone.description:
Contact phone number field for the seller account, represented as an optional string.

When present, it carries a formatted phone number that may follow E.164 or another platform-defined standard. When null, it indicates that no phone number is currently registered for the seller.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the seller account.

Typical values include states such as `pending`, `active`, `suspended`, or `terminated`, as defined by business rules. This field determines whether the seller can operate on the platform and may be updated by either the seller (for limited transitions) or platform administrators.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the seller account was first created in the system.

This is a system-managed, read-only field that reflects the initial onboarding time for the merchant.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the seller record.

Automatically maintained by the system whenever mutable fields of the seller are changed.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when the seller account was logically deleted or closed, if applicable.

When this field is non-null, business logic may treat the seller as archived, closed, or otherwise inactive depending on platform policy.
Null when the seller account has never been logically deleted or closed and is still considered active within historical records.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion timestamp for the seller account.

When this field is a non-null ISO 8601 date-time string, the seller is considered closed, archived, or otherwise inactive according to platform policy. When null, the seller is treated as not having been logically deleted.

seller.description:
Normalized summary representation of the authenticated seller account.

This object follows the standard `.ISummary` pattern used across the platform for BELONGS-TO relations, allowing other DTOs to embed seller identity consistently while avoiding circular references. It provides the canonical set of summary fields for the seller, while the top-level scalar fields in this DTO act as denormalized conveniences for legacy consumers.

IShoppingMallSellerLogin.IRequest.description:
Seller login request payload for authenticating an existing seller account.

Carries the seller's login email and password for verification against shopping_mall_auth_credentials with actor_type "seller". This DTO is used by the /auth/seller/login endpoint and includes session context fields required for audit logging and security analysis.

email.description:
Seller's login email address used as the unique credential identifier for actor_type "seller".

Must match the email stored in shopping_mall_auth_credentials for the seller actor.

password.description:
Plain text password corresponding to the seller's login email.

The backend validates this value by hashing it and comparing it against the stored password_hash in shopping_mall_auth_credentials. Clients MUST NOT send pre-hashed passwords.

oneOf.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security analysis.

May be provided when the client has reliable knowledge of the originating IP (for example, in SSR or trusted proxy scenarios). When omitted or null, the backend derives the IP from the HTTP request context.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security analysis.

May be provided when the client has reliable knowledge of the originating IP (for example, in SSR or trusted proxy scenarios). When omitted or null, the backend derives the IP from the HTTP request context.

href.description:
Full URL of the page from which the login request was initiated.

Used for session context, security auditing, and behavioral analytics. Clients should send the canonical browser location at the time of login.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the previous page or context that led to the login action.

Used for security monitoring and funnel analysis. May be an empty path-like URL when the login was initiated directly.

IShoppingMallSellerRefresh.IRequest.description:
Request payload for refreshing a seller's JWT tokens using an existing refresh token.

This DTO is used by the seller token refresh endpoint to submit the refresh token that should be validated and exchanged for a new access/refresh token pair. It carries only the token and optional context metadata, and never includes any seller identifiers or credential IDs, which are resolved internally from the token itself.

refreshToken.description:
Existing seller refresh token issued by the platform.

This value is treated as an opaque string by the client. The backend validates it against the token store, resolves the corresponding credentials and seller identity, and checks expiry and revocation state.

IShoppingMallSellerEmailVerificationIssu.description:
Request payload for issuing a new email verification token for a seller.

This DTO is used when a seller requests that a verification email be (re)sent to confirm ownership of their email address. The operation is invoked by an authenticated seller, so seller identity comes from the authentication context and MUST NOT be supplied in the body.

The payload carries only minimal email and context information needed to drive verification and messaging behavior.

email.description:
Seller email address that should be verified.

This must match the email stored in the seller's authentication credentials, and is used to determine which credentials record in shopping_mall_auth_credentials requires a new verification token.

IShoppingMallSellerEmailVerificationIssu.description:
Response DTO returned after initiating an email verification process for a seller account.

Indicates that an email verification token has been issued and dispatched via email for the seller's credentials. Does not include the raw verification token value for security reasons. Clients use this response only to confirm that the flow has started and to inform the seller to check their inbox.

success.description: Indicates whether the email verification issuance request was accepted and processed successfully. When false, the client should treat the request as failed and may present an appropriate error message based on HTTP status and error body.

message.description: Human-readable message summarizing the outcome of the verification issuance request, such as "Verification email has been sent". Intended primarily for display in client UIs and logs.

IShoppingMallSellerEmailVerificationComp.description:
Request DTO used to complete seller email verification by consuming a previously issued verification token.

The client submits the opaque verification token string that was delivered to the seller via email. The backend validates that the token exists, has not expired, and has not already been consumed, then marks it as consumed and applies any credential status changes defined by platform policy.

token.description: Opaque email verification token string that uniquely identifies a row in shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens. Typically carried in a verification link sent to the seller's email address and treated as an unguessable secret value.

IShoppingMallSellerEmailVerificationComp.description:
Response payload returned after attempting to complete a seller email verification flow.

When `success` is true, the supplied verification token has been validated and consumed, and the seller's email address is now treated as verified in the authentication system. Internal token and credential state changes remain hidden from the client and are reflected only in server-side entities such as shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens, shopping_mall_auth_credentials, shopping_mall_auth_logs, and shopping_mall_security_events.

When `success` is false, the verification flow has not been completed, typically because the token was invalid, expired, or already consumed. The response still avoids exposing sensitive internal details and instead provides a safe, human-readable `message` that the client can surface to the seller. Clients use `requiresAdditionalAction` together with `success` to determine whether the seller can proceed into the application or must complete further steps or re-trigger the verification process.

success.description:
Indicates whether the seller email verification token was successfully processed and the seller's email address is now considered verified.

A value of `true` means the token was valid, unexpired, unused, and has been consumed, and any associated credential state (for example, status fields on shopping_mall_auth_credentials) has been updated according to platform policy. A value of `false` means the verification could not be completed (for example, due to an invalid, expired, or replayed token), and the seller remains in a non-verified state from the platform's perspective.

message.description:
Human-readable message summarizing the result of the verification flow, suitable for display in UI confirmation or error screens.

On success, this typically conveys that the email has been verified and may optionally hint at the next step (for example, returning to login or dashboard). On failure, it describes the high-level reason the verification did not complete (such as an invalid or expired link) without exposing sensitive implementation details. The message text may be localized at the presentation layer using this value as a key or template hint depending on client design.

requiresAdditionalAction.description:
Flag indicating whether the seller must perform additional actions after this verification attempt before gaining full access to the platform.

When `requiresAdditionalAction` is `false` and `success` is `true`, the seller can typically proceed directly to using the application with a fully verified email. When `requiresAdditionalAction` is `true`, the seller may need to complete follow-up steps such as providing additional profile information, awaiting manual review, or re-initiating the verification flow if the token was invalid or expired. Client applications should use this flag, together with `success`, to decide whether to route the seller to a simple confirmation screen, a more detailed onboarding or support flow, or back to the area where a fresh verification can be requested.

IShoppingMallSellerPasswordResetRequest..description:
Request payload to initiate a password reset flow for a seller.

The client provides the seller's login email address so that the backend can locate the corresponding authentication credentials, create a password reset token, and send a reset link via out-of-band channels such as email. The API always responds with a generic acknowledgment so that account existence cannot be inferred from this call.

email.description: Email address of the seller account for which a password reset should be initiated. The backend uses this to locate the associated credentials record while ensuring that the response does not reveal whether the account exists.

IShoppingMallSellerPasswordResetRequest..description:
Response DTO for initiating a seller password reset request.

This schema represents the public-facing acknowledgment returned after a seller submits a password reset request. It intentionally does not reveal whether a matching seller account or credentials record exists in the system, thereby preventing attackers from probing for valid email addresses.

The response indicates only that the reset process has been accepted for processing (if possible) and that, when appropriate, a password reset email or out-of-band notification will be sent. Internal details about shopping_mall_auth_credentials or shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens are never exposed through this DTO.

success.description:
Indicates whether the password reset request was accepted for processing.

This flag is typically true when the request payload is syntactically valid and the system has performed all necessary checks and side effects (such as logging security events), regardless of whether a matching seller account actually exists. It may be false only in cases where the request itself is invalid or the operation cannot be performed due to system-level errors.

message.description:
Human-readable message describing the outcome of the password reset request initiation.

This message should be phrased in a generic way that does not reveal whether a seller account exists for the provided identifier. For example, it may say that if an account is associated with the provided email, a reset link will be sent. The message is intended for display in client applications and may be localized at the presentation layer.

IShoppingMallSellerPasswordResetComplete.description:
Request DTO for completing a seller password reset using a previously issued reset token.

Clients call this operation when a seller follows a password reset link or otherwise obtains a valid password reset token. The request supplies the opaque token string along with the seller's new password. The backend validates and consumes the token stored in shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens and updates the corresponding credentials record in shopping_mall_auth_credentials with a new password hash.

The DTO carries only user-supplied data. It does not include any actor identifiers or credential record IDs; those are resolved on the server side based on the token. Additional session or context fields (such as ip, href, referrer) are not required here because this operation does not establish a new authenticated session; it only updates existing credentials.

token.description:
Opaque password reset token string issued earlier during the reset request flow.

This value corresponds to the token column in shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens and is used to look up and validate the reset token row. The token must be treated as a secret value and is typically delivered to the seller via email or other out-of-band channel. It should be unguessable and validated against expiration and consumption rules.

password.description:
New password that the seller wishes to set for their account.

The backend will hash this value and store the result in the password_hash (or equivalent) field of the relevant row in shopping_mall_auth_credentials. Clients must never pre-hash this value. Server-side validation should enforce strength requirements such as minimum length and complexity, but those rules are applied in service logic rather than encoded directly in this schema.

IShoppingMallSellerPasswordResetComplete.description:
Response schema for completing a seller password reset using a password reset token.

Indicates whether the password reset operation succeeded after validating and consuming a token from shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens and updating the corresponding credentials in shopping_mall_auth_credentials. It does not expose any sensitive credential information and is intentionally minimal for security reasons.

success.description:
Indicates whether the seller password reset and token consumption completed successfully.

true when the provided token was valid, not expired, not previously consumed, and the associated credentials record in shopping_mall_auth_credentials was successfully updated with a new password_hash. false when validation failed or the operation could not be completed.

IShoppingMallSellerPasswordChange.IReque.description:
Request schema for an authenticated seller to change their password.

The seller must provide their current password and the desired new password. The backend validates the current password against the stored password_hash in shopping_mall_auth_credentials for the authenticated seller and, on success, updates the password_hash to reflect the new password.

This DTO never includes any actor identifiers such as seller_id or auth credential IDs; those are derived from the authenticated context on the server.

currentPassword.description:
The seller's current password in plain text.

Used to re-authenticate the seller by validating against the existing password_hash in shopping_mall_auth_credentials associated with the authenticated seller account.

newPassword.description:
The seller's desired new password in plain text.

The backend applies platform password policy validation and, if accepted, hashes this value and stores it in the password_hash field of shopping_mall_auth_credentials for the authenticated seller.

IShoppingMallSellerPasswordChange.IRespo.description:
Response schema indicating the result of an authenticated seller password change attempt.

This DTO is returned by POST /auth/seller/password/change after validating the current password against shopping_mall_auth_credentials and, on success, updating the password hash and writing audit logs. It never exposes any password or password_hash data and only communicates high‑level outcome and optional error context.

success.description: Flag indicating whether the seller password change operation completed successfully.

message.description: Human‑readable message summarizing the outcome of the password change attempt. Useful for display in UI notifications.

errorCode.description: Optional machine‑readable error code when success is false. Can be used by clients to handle specific failure reasons such as INVALID_CURRENT_PASSWORD or WEAK_NEW_PASSWORD.

IShoppingMallPlatformAdminJoin.IRequest.description:
Request payload for registering a new platform administrator and creating initial authentication credentials.

This DTO is used by POST /auth/platformAdmin/join to insert rows into shopping_mall_platformadmin and shopping_mall_auth_credentials (scoped with actor_type = "platformAdmin"), bind them via shopping_mall_auth_credentials_of_platformadmins, and open an initial shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions record.

It contains administrator profile fields plus the plain‑text password to be hashed and stored in shopping_mall_auth_credentials.password_hash. It also carries session context fields (ip, href, referrer) so that the initial admin session can be recorded in shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions and related security/audit logs.

email.description: Platform administrator email address. Must be unique for actor_type = "platformAdmin" across shopping_mall_platformadmin and shopping_mall_auth_credentials. Used both as login identifier and primary contact email.

name.description: Display name of the platform administrator as stored in shopping_mall_platformadmin.name.

password.description: Plain‑text password chosen by the new platform administrator. The backend hashes this value and stores it as password_hash in shopping_mall_auth_credentials. Must satisfy the platform's password strength policy.

oneOf.description: Optional client IP address for the joining admin session. When provided, it is stored in shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions.ip and may be copied into shopping_mall_auth_logs and shopping_mall_security_events.

ip.description: Optional client IP address for the joining admin session. When provided, it is stored in shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions.ip and may be copied into shopping_mall_auth_logs and shopping_mall_security_events.

href.description: Current page URL at the time of registration. Stored in shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions.href to capture session establishment context and may also be referenced by auth/security logs.

referrer.description: Referrer URL from which the admin registration flow was initiated. Stored in shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions.referrer for auditability and risk analysis.

IShoppingMallPlatformAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized platform administrator session representation including identity lifecycle information and issued JWT tokens for authenticated access to the shopping mall admin APIs.

This DTO combines the core profile of the platform administrator (identifier, email, display name, lifecycle status, and derived activity flag) with the authorization token pair that was issued after successful join, login, or refresh flows.

Downstream administrative tools and dashboards can use the identity fields to display who is operating the backend and can rely on the `status` and `isActive` fields to understand whether the account is fully enabled, temporarily restricted, or subject to additional operational controls at the time the session was established.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated platform administrator.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` record that represents the administrator identity. It is stable over the full lifecycle of the administrator account and is used as the anchor for sessions, credentials, and audit records.

email.description:
Primary email address of the platform administrator account.

The email value is used as the unique login identifier within the `platformAdmin` actor scope in `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` and as the main address for administrative communication such as alerts, notifications, and operational messages.

displayName.description:
Human-readable display name for the platform administrator.

This value is typically derived from the `name` column on `shopping_mall_platformadmin` and is shown in admin consoles, dashboards, and audit logs to make it easier for humans to recognize which administrator performed a given action.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the platform administrator account at the time this authorized session was created.

Typical values reflect business-level account states such as `active`, `suspended`, `locked`, or `compromised`, and are derived from the underlying admin identity and credential status columns that are checked during join, login, and refresh flows.

Client applications and admin dashboards can use this field to display nuanced account state and to implement status-specific behaviors, while the simpler `isActive` flag indicates whether this status currently allows normal sign-in and operation.

isActive.description:
Boolean indicator that the platform administrator account is currently allowed to sign in and perform administrative operations.

This flag is derived from the underlying `status` of the administrator identity and associated credentials (and any applicable risk controls). When `true`, the account is considered operational for standard admin duties; when `false`, the account may be locked, suspended, or otherwise restricted even though it still exists for audit and historical reference.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp representing when the platform administrator account was created in the system.

The value is an ISO 8601 date-time string reflecting the `created_at` field of the underlying `shopping_mall_platformadmin` record and is useful for audit trails, lifecycle analytics, and admin onboarding reporting.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp representing when the platform administrator account was last updated.

The value is an ISO 8601 date-time string mapped from the `updated_at` field of `shopping_mall_platformadmin`, capturing the most recent change to identity attributes such as name, status, or contact information.

IShoppingMallPlatformAdminLogin.IRequest.description:
Login credentials and session context for a platform administrator attempting to sign in.

Includes the administrator's email and password along with connection metadata required to create a platformadmin session record, such as client IP address and page URLs.

email.description: Platform administrator email address used as the unique login identifier within the platformAdmin actor scope.

password.description: Plain-text password submitted by the platform administrator for authentication. The backend hashes and compares this against the stored password hash.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for the login attempt, used for security analytics and audit logging.

ip.description: Client IP address for the login attempt, used for security analytics and audit logging. When omitted or null, the server may infer the IP from the incoming request.

href.description: Full URL of the page from which the login request originated. Used to populate the admin session context and auth logs.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the previous page that led to the login action. Used for session context and security auditing.

IShoppingMallPlatformAdminRefresh.IReque.description:
Request payload for refreshing JWT tokens for a platform administrator using an existing valid refresh token.

This DTO carries the refresh token issued during a prior successful login or join operation, plus optional client context fields used for logging and risk analysis. The backend uses the token to locate the associated `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` record with `actor_type = "platformAdmin"`, verify eligibility for refresh, and then issue new JWT tokens.

Unlike login and join DTOs, this refresh payload does not create a new credential; it only validates the existing refresh token and records audit data in `shopping_mall_auth_logs` and related security tables.

refreshToken.description:
Refresh token previously issued to the platform administrator.

The backend validates this token against its server-side token store to ensure it has not expired or been revoked, then uses its subject information to locate the corresponding `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` record for a `platformAdmin` actor.

oneOf.description:
Optional client IP address associated with this refresh request.

If provided, it should be a textual IPv4 or IPv6 address and is recorded in `shopping_mall_auth_logs` and security telemetry. When omitted, the server derives the IP from the incoming HTTP request context.

ip.description:
Optional client IP address associated with this refresh request.

If provided, it should be a textual IPv4 or IPv6 address and is recorded in `shopping_mall_auth_logs` and security telemetry. When omitted, the server derives the IP from the incoming HTTP request context.

oneOf.description:
Optional user agent string describing the client software that is performing the refresh.

Typical values are HTTP User-Agent headers identifying the browser or native client. The implementation may persist this value into `shopping_mall_auth_logs` or `shopping_mall_security_events` for anomaly detection and device analytics.

userAgent.description:
Optional user agent string describing the client software that is performing the refresh.

Typical values are HTTP User-Agent headers identifying the browser or native client. The implementation may persist this value into `shopping_mall_auth_logs` or `shopping_mall_security_events` for anomaly detection and device analytics.

oneOf.description:
Optional correlation or trace identifier propagated from the client.

This identifier can be used to join refresh activity to other application logs and distributed traces, improving observability around administrator authentication flows.

correlationId.description:
Optional correlation or trace identifier propagated from the client.

This identifier can be used to join refresh activity to other application logs and distributed traces, improving observability around administrator authentication flows.

IShoppingMallGuestUserJoin.IRequest.description:
Request payload for registering a new guestUser identity on the shopping mall platform.

This DTO carries benign context about an unauthenticated visitor, such as a temporary identifier, client IP, user agent, and an optional guest cart token to associate an existing anonymous cart with the new guest identity. It does not contain passwords, emails, or other credential material; guest users are authenticated purely by tokens issued after this join.

The backend uses this payload to create a new row in `shopping_mall_guestuser`, optionally link a `shopping_mall_guest_carts` record when a matching `guest_token` is supplied, and write audit entries into `shopping_mall_auth_logs` and `shopping_mall_security_events`.

temporaryIdentifier.description:
Opaque client-side identifier used to correlate pre-registration behavior with the new guestUser.

This is typically derived from cookies or local storage and may be used in `shopping_mall_security_events.actor_identifier` or analytics systems. The value should be treated as an opaque string without semantic meaning to the server.

oneOf.description:
Optional token that identifies an existing anonymous guest cart to be associated with the new guestUser.

When provided, the backend looks up a `shopping_mall_guest_carts` row by its unique `guest_token` and, if found, links it to the created `shopping_mall_guestuser` via `shopping_mall_guest_carts.shopping_mall_guestuser_id`. If not provided or not found, no cart association is performed.

guestCartToken.description:
Optional token that identifies an existing anonymous guest cart to be associated with the new guestUser.

When provided, the backend looks up a `shopping_mall_guest_carts` row by its unique `guest_token` and, if found, links it to the created `shopping_mall_guestuser` via `shopping_mall_guest_carts.shopping_mall_guestuser_id`. If not provided or not found, no cart association is performed.

oneOf.description:
Optional client IP address associated with the guest registration request.

If supplied, it should contain a textual IPv4 or IPv6 address and is recorded to `shopping_mall_auth_logs` and `shopping_mall_security_events` for security analytics and funnel tracking.

ip.description:
Optional client IP address associated with the guest registration request.

If supplied, it should contain a textual IPv4 or IPv6 address and is recorded to `shopping_mall_auth_logs` and `shopping_mall_security_events` for security analytics and funnel tracking.

oneOf.description:
Optional user agent string of the client performing the guest registration.

Typical values mirror HTTP User-Agent headers and are persisted into authentication and security logs for device analytics and anomaly detection.

userAgent.description:
Optional user agent string of the client performing the guest registration.

Typical values mirror HTTP User-Agent headers and are persisted into authentication and security logs for device analytics and anomaly detection.

href.description:
Current page URL at the time of guest registration.

This field captures the connection context for the new guest session, allowing later analysis of which landing pages drive guest conversions. It is stored alongside session and audit records.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page) that led the visitor to the registration action.

This field is used for attribution and funnel analytics and is typically derived from the browser's document.referrer value or equivalent client-side context.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized guest user session envelope returned after guest registration or token refresh.

Represents the authenticated guestUser actor on the shopping mall platform along with issued JWT tokens required for subsequent API calls. This payload is produced by the guest join and guest refresh authentication flows and never exposes sensitive credential material because guest users do not have password-based accounts.

Internal soft-delete lifecycle fields are intentionally excluded to avoid leaking archival state. Only the minimal guest identity and token information required by clients is exposed.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user in the shopping_mall_guestuser table.

This ID is used as the stable subject identifier for the guestUser actor across issued tokens and logging tables.

temporary_identifier.description:
Opaque identifier used to correlate pre-registration or pre-authentication activity for this guest, such as values derived from cookies or client-side storage.

Although the originating client context may treat this value as optional before registration, once a guest user record is created in shopping_mall_guestuser this field is always populated and therefore is required in authorization payloads. API consumers can safely rely on its presence for correlation, funnel analysis, and security event linkage.

user_agent.description:
Captured HTTP user agent string or similar client descriptor associated with the guest user at the time of persistence.

This value is useful for analytics, device-specific debugging, and aligning client-visible behavior with authentication logs in shopping_mall_auth_logs and shopping_mall_security_events.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this guest user record was first created in the system, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

Clients can use this for informational displays or to understand how long a particular guest identity has existed, but it should not be treated as an authorization control in itself.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the most recent update to this guest user record, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

This value allows clients and administrative tools to reason about the freshness of guest metadata without exposing internal soft-delete or archival state.

IShoppingMallGuestUserRefresh.IRequest.description:
Request payload for refreshing a guestUser authorization session.

Carries the refresh token previously issued to the guestUser along with optional telemetry fields used for authentication logging and security analytics. The backend validates the token, checks the associated shopping_mall_guestuser record, and issues a new IShoppingMallGuestUser.IAuthorized envelope on success.

refreshToken.description:
Refresh token associated with an existing guestUser session.

This token is used to request a new access token without re-registering the guest identity.

oneOf.description:
Client IP address for this refresh request.

Used only for logging and security analytics. When omitted, the server may derive the IP from the transport layer.

Explicitly indicates that the client does not provide an IP value for this refresh request.

In this case, the server may still infer the network origin from the transport layer for logging and risk analysis.

ip.description:
Client IP address for this refresh request or null when not explicitly provided.

Used for observability and risk analysis in shopping_mall_auth_logs and shopping_mall_security_events. When not supplied or set to null, the backend may still rely on connection-level information for IP derivation.

oneOf.description:
User-Agent header string describing the client software and device making the refresh request.

When provided, it is captured into authentication and security logs to support device fingerprinting, anomaly detection, and troubleshooting of client-specific issues.

Explicitly indicates that the client does not provide a user agent string for this refresh request.

In this case, the backend may use a default value or omit user agent enrichment in logging and risk analysis.

userAgent.description:
Optional user agent string of the client performing the guest token refresh.

This field may be omitted or set to null when the client cannot or does not wish to send a user agent value. When present as a non-empty string, it is persisted into authentication and security logs for device analytics and anomaly detection, complementing the IP address telemetry.

IShoppingMallConfig.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request schema for retrieving paginated ShoppingMall configuration entries.

Used by platform administrators to search, filter, and paginate over configuration records stored in the `shopping_mall_configs` table. This DTO is sent in the request body of the PATCH `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/configs` endpoint.

It supports generic pagination and sorting controls as well as configuration-specific filters such as key prefix, category, and activation flags.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve for the configuration list.

Must be a positive integer starting from 1. If omitted, the backend should apply its own default (typically page 1).

limit.description:
Maximum number of configuration entries to return per page.

Must be a positive integer. The backend may enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to configuration keys, names, or descriptions.

Admin tools can use this field to implement keyword-based search over configuration metadata.

keyPrefix.description:
Optional configuration key prefix filter.

When provided, restricts results to configuration entries whose key starts with the given prefix. Useful for grouping related configurations (for example, `payment.`, `shipping.`, `review.`).

category.description:
Optional configuration category or group filter.

Represents a logical grouping of configuration entries such as `payment`, `shipping`, `risk`, or `catalog`. The exact set of categories is defined by business conventions and may be enforced by validation logic in the service layer.

isActive.description:
Optional active status filter for configuration entries.

When true, returns only active or currently applied configurations. When false, returns disabled or inactive configurations. When null or omitted, no filter is applied based on active status.

orderBy.description:
Field name used to sort configuration entries in the result set.

Common values include `key`, `updatedAt`, or `createdAt`, depending on the actual Prisma model fields. The service should validate the field name to prevent invalid or unsafe sorting expressions.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering configuration entries.

`asc` sorts in ascending order, while `desc` sorts in descending order. Defaults are determined by the backend when not explicitly provided.

Sort direction to apply when ordering configuration entries.

`asc` sorts in ascending order, while `desc` sorts in descending order. Defaults are determined by the backend when not explicitly provided.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering configuration entries.

`asc` sorts in ascending order, while `desc` sorts in descending order. Defaults are determined by the backend when not explicitly provided.

IShoppingMallConfig.description:
Represents a single global configuration entry for the shoppingMall platform.

Each row models a low-level key/value style configuration item grouped by a logical namespace, such as "checkout", "payment", or "reviews". These configuration entries are used across multiple subsystems to control feature toggles, numeric thresholds, and string parameters that influence runtime behavior.

Records in this table are primarily managed by platform administrators and are expected to change infrequently under controlled processes. Soft deletion is supported through the deleted_at field so that historical configuration state can be preserved for audit and troubleshooting purposes.

id.description:
Primary key for the configuration entry.

This UUID uniquely identifies a single configuration row in the shopping_mall_configs table. It is generated by the system and is used as the stable reference when updating or querying a specific configuration.

API clients receive this value in read responses and use it as the configId path parameter for update operations.

namespace.description:
Logical namespace that groups related configuration keys.

Typical examples include values like "checkout", "payment", "reviews", or other domain-oriented segments. Namespaces allow administrators and services to organize configuration entries by functional area.

Combined with the key field, the namespace helps avoid collisions and supports efficient lookups for all active configuration values within a particular domain.

key.description:
Unique configuration key within a namespace.

The key expresses the specific configuration item, such as "max_cart_items", "payment_timeout_seconds", or "review_moderation_threshold". Each key must be unique within its namespace according to the unique index on (namespace, key).

Service code typically uses the combination of namespace and key to retrieve the correct configuration value at runtime.

value.description:
Configuration value stored as text.

The raw configuration data is persisted as a string so that a single column can represent booleans, numbers, JSON, or other structured types. The consuming subsystem is responsible for parsing and interpreting the value according to its own expectations.

Administrators should follow documentation for each key to ensure values use the correct format and semantic meaning so that downstream services can safely consume them.

description.description:
Human-readable explanation of the configuration entry.

This optional text explains what the configuration key controls, which subsystems depend on it, and any important operational or business constraints. It is primarily intended for platform administrators working with configuration consoles or audit tools.

When null, the configuration still functions technically, but administrators have less context, so providing a clear description is strongly recommended.

active.description:
Indicates whether this configuration row is currently active.

When true, the configuration entry is considered part of the effective runtime configuration set and can be used by consuming services. When false, the row is retained for audit or rollback purposes but should be ignored by configuration loaders.

Typical administrative flows toggle this flag instead of deleting records outright, allowing safe rollback to previous configurations if needed.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration row was created.

This value is set by the system at insert time and reflects when the configuration entry first became available in the database. It is useful for audit, historical analysis, and understanding when certain behavior changes were introduced.

Clients should treat this field as read-only metadata and never attempt to modify it through write APIs.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration row was last updated.

Every time an administrator or internal process modifies mutable fields on the configuration, this timestamp is refreshed. It provides a clear indicator of the most recent change and can be compared with created_at to understand the configuration lifecycle.

Like created_at, this field is managed exclusively by the system and is not writable through public APIs.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the configuration row.

When null, the configuration entry is considered logically present, subject to the active flag and other business rules. When set to a date-time value, the row is treated as soft-deleted and should not be used by runtime configuration lookups.

Soft deletion allows the platform to preserve historical configuration entries for audit, debugging, and retrospective analysis without exposing them as active settings.

IShoppingMallConfig.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new global configuration entry in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO covers all writable business fields of the shopping_mall_configs model that are necessary to define a configuration item at creation time. It intentionally excludes system-managed columns such as id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at, which are populated automatically by the backend.

Administrative tools and platform operators use this shape when defining new configuration entries that control feature toggles, numeric thresholds, and other global behaviors.

namespace.description:
Logical namespace that groups related configuration keys for this new entry.

Namespaces such as "checkout", "payment", or "reviews" allow the platform to organize configuration records by functional area. The combination of namespace and key must be unique, so clients should choose namespaces that clearly segment different configuration domains.

This value is required on creation and cannot be omitted; it determines where this configuration conceptually belongs.

key.description:
Configuration key that must be unique within the given namespace.

The key expresses the specific setting being configured, for example "max_cart_items", "payment_timeout_seconds", or "review_moderation_threshold". Together with namespace, it is protected by a unique constraint in the database.

Administrative clients should use clear, stable identifiers here because other systems and documentation will reference this key over time.

value.description:
Configuration value stored as text for the new entry.

The value is persisted as a string regardless of the logical type (boolean, number, JSON, etc.). Consuming subsystems interpret and validate the value according to the semantics associated with the namespace and key.

Callers should ensure that the value uses a format expected by downstream services, such as "true"/"false" for booleans, numeric strings for thresholds, or serialized JSON for complex structures.

description.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of the new configuration entry.

This text should describe what behavior the configuration controls, which subsystems read it, and any constraints or recommended ranges for the value. Providing a clear description improves the maintainability of the configuration catalog.

If omitted or set to null, the configuration still functions, but administrators will have less context when inspecting configuration lists in management tools.

active.description:
Initial active state of the configuration entry.

When true, the configuration becomes part of the effective runtime configuration set as soon as it is created. When false, the row is stored but should not be considered during configuration resolution until it is explicitly activated.

This flag allows administrators to predefine configuration entries and only activate them when the platform is ready for the change.

IShoppingMallConfig.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing global configuration entry in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents the subset of shopping_mall_configs fields that are allowed to change after a configuration has been created. It is used together with a path parameter that supplies the immutable config identifier. All properties are optional so that clients can send partial updates.

Update operations typically adjust the value, description, or active flag while preserving the configuration identity and audit history. System-managed fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are not writable through this DTO and are maintained by the backend automatically.

namespace.description:
Optional new namespace for the configuration entry.

Changing the namespace moves the configuration record into a different logical group. Implementations may restrict namespace changes based on business rules or operational safety, but when allowed, this field lets administrators reorganize configuration domains.

If omitted, the existing namespace value is left unchanged.

key.description:
Optional new configuration key within the entry’s namespace.

When provided, this updates the identifier part of the configuration while still preserving the same primary id. Because the (namespace, key) pair is unique, callers must ensure the new key does not conflict with an existing configuration in the same namespace.

If not supplied, the configuration retains its current key.

value.description:
Updated configuration value stored as text.

Administrators use this field to change the effective setting, for example adjusting numeric thresholds, toggling boolean flags, or modifying JSON structures. The new value must still conform to the expectations of consuming subsystems.

If this property is omitted, the existing value remains unchanged.

description.description:
Updated human-readable explanation for the configuration entry.
