IShoppingMallPolicySetting.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request DTO for querying shopping mall policy setting profiles from the shopping_mall_policy_settings table.

This type is used by administrative and backoffice tools to submit complex search criteria when browsing policy setting profiles. It supports filtering by category, active status, effective period windows, keyword search over name and description, and standard pagination and sorting options.

The request body is consumed by the PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/policySettings endpoint and is translated into database queries over fields such as code, name, category, active, effective_from, effective_to, created_at, and updated_at, using indexes defined on these columns.

page.description: Page number for paginated search results. Starts from 1. Used together with pageSize to control the slice of results returned.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of items to return per page. Must be a positive integer and is typically capped to prevent excessive result sizes.

categories.description:
Optional list of policy categories to include in the result set. Typical values include "cancellation", "refund", "review", and "age_restriction".

When provided, only policy setting profiles whose category is one of the specified values will be returned.

active.description:
Optional filter on the active flag of the policy setting profile. When true, only currently active profiles are included. When false, only inactive or disabled profiles are included.

If omitted, both active and inactive profiles may be returned depending on other filters.

effectiveFromGte.description:
Lower bound for the effective_from timestamp filter.

When provided, only profiles whose effective_from is greater than or equal to this value are included. The timestamp must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

effectiveFromLte.description:
Upper bound for the effective_from timestamp filter.

When provided, only profiles whose effective_from is less than or equal to this value are included. The timestamp must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

effectiveToGte.description:
Lower bound for the effective_to timestamp filter.

When provided, only profiles whose effective_to is greater than or equal to this value are included. The timestamp must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

effectiveToLte.description:
Upper bound for the effective_to timestamp filter.

When provided, only profiles whose effective_to is less than or equal to this value are included. The timestamp must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit offset.

keyword.description:
Free-text search term applied to human-friendly fields such as name and description.

The backend may normalize this value and apply it to full-text or ILIKE-style searches over the corresponding columns.

IShoppingMallPolicySetting.description:
Full DTO representing a single shopping mall policy setting profile stored in the shopping_mall_policy_settings table.

Policy setting profiles represent high-level configuration groups that control platform behavior for domains such as cancellation, refund, review, and age restriction. Each profile is identified by a globally unique business code and includes human-friendly metadata, category classification, a serialized configuration payload, lifecycle flags, and audit timestamps.

This type is used as the detailed response body for operations that retrieve or mutate individual policy setting profiles, such as GET /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/policySettings/{policySettingCode}, POST /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/policySettings, and PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/policySettings/{policySettingCode}.

id.description:
System-generated unique identifier of the policy setting profile.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_policy_settings table and is used internally by the backend for joins, indexing, and low-level persistence concerns.

code.description:
Business identifier code of the policy setting profile.

This string is unique across all rows in shopping_mall_policy_settings and is enforced by a unique index. Other domain-specific policy tables reference this profile using this code as a stable identifier, for example: "default_cancellation_profile" or "holiday_refund_profile".

name.description:
Human-friendly name of the policy setting profile.

This value is presented in administrative user interfaces so that operators can quickly recognize the purpose of the profile, such as "Default Cancellation Policy" or "Strict Review Moderation".

description.description:
Optional human-readable description explaining the intended business purpose, scope, and behavior of this policy setting profile.

Administrative tools typically display this text to help operators understand when and how to apply or modify the configuration profile. When the underlying column is null, this property is returned as null, and clients may choose to hide or gracefully omit it from detailed views.

category.description:
Logical category of the policy setting profile.

Common examples include domain categories such as "cancellation", "refund", "review", and "age_restriction". The platform may define additional categories for other policy domains, and downstream services interpret this category to decide which engine or enforcement rules apply.

config_payload.description:
Serialized configuration payload containing structured parameters for the policy engine.

Typically this field stores a JSON document encoded as text, which downstream services parse to enforce the detailed behavior of the policy, such as cancellation windows, refund thresholds, review moderation limits, or age restriction rules. When null, the profile does not carry additional structured parameters and relies solely on its category and basic flags.

active.description:
Flag indicating whether this policy setting profile is currently active.

Only active profiles are normally considered by runtime policy evaluation. Inactive profiles may represent archived, deprecated, or draft configurations that are kept for audit and rollback purposes but should not influence live behavior.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp indicating when this policy setting profile becomes effective in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

When present, the profile is considered applicable on or after this moment, assuming it is also marked active. When the underlying value is null, the profile is effectively unconstrained on the start side and may be considered effective immediately when active.

effective_to.description:
Timestamp indicating when this policy setting profile stops being effective in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

When present, the profile is considered applicable up to and including this moment while active. When the underlying value is null, the profile is unconstrained on the end side and may remain effective indefinitely until updated or deactivated.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the policy setting profile was created, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

This audit field is managed automatically by the persistence layer and allows administrators and auditors to understand when the configuration was first introduced into the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the policy setting profile was last updated, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

This audit field is also managed automatically by the persistence layer and is useful for understanding when configuration changes took effect and for diagnosing behavior changes over time.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the policy setting profile, represented as an ISO 8601 date-time value in UTC when present.

When this field is non-null, the profile is treated as logically deleted and should no longer be used for new policy references, although it may still appear in historical views and audit reports. A null value means the profile is considered active from a lifecycle perspective, subject to its `active` flag and effective period constraints.

IShoppingMallPolicySetting.ICreate.description:
DTO schema for creating a new shopping mall policy setting profile.

This request body is used by platform administrators to define a new configuration profile in the shopping_mall_policy_settings table. It captures the core business attributes such as the globally unique business code, human-readable name, and logical category, along with optional descriptive text, configuration payload, and effective period flags that control when and how the profile is applied.

code.description:
Globally unique business identifier code for this policy setting profile.

This value maps to shopping_mall_policy_settings.code and is used as a stable reference by other domain-specific policy tables. It must be unique across all policy setting profiles and is often used in URLs or configuration references instead of the internal numeric or UUID primary key.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the policy setting profile.

This name is displayed in administrative UIs and should clearly describe the intent of the profile, such as "Default Cancellation Policy" or "Strict Review Moderation".

category.description:
Logical category of the policy setting profile.

Typical examples include "cancellation", "refund", "review", or "age_restriction" and are used to group profiles by their business domain. The backend enforces which categories are allowed and how they are interpreted.

description.description:
Optional long-form explanation of the policy setting profile and its intended business use.

When provided, this text helps administrators understand when and how this configuration should be applied. When null, no descriptive text is stored for this profile.

config_payload.description:
Optional serialized configuration payload for the policy setting profile.

This field usually contains a JSON string with structured parameters interpreted by downstream subsystems, such as cancellation windows, refund thresholds, review limits, or age restriction rules. When null, the profile relies only on its basic flags and category without additional structured parameters.

active.description:
Flag indicating whether this policy setting profile is active.

When true, and when the effective period conditions are satisfied, the profile may be used by domain-specific policy tables. When false, the profile is considered inactive even if its effective window would otherwise permit use. When null, the system may apply default activation behavior defined by business rules.

effective_from.description:
Start of the effective period for this policy setting profile in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

When set to a timestamp, the profile is considered applicable on or after this moment, assuming it is also marked active. When null, the profile has no explicit start constraint and may be effective immediately when active.

effective_to.description:
End of the effective period for this policy setting profile in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

When set to a timestamp, the profile is considered applicable up to and including this moment, assuming it is also marked active. When null, the profile has no explicit end constraint and remains potentially effective indefinitely while active. Business logic ensures that effective_to does not precede effective_from when both are provided.

IShoppingMallPolicySetting.IUpdate.description:
DTO schema for updating an existing shopping mall policy setting profile.

This request body is used by platform administrators to modify mutable attributes of a configuration profile in the shopping_mall_policy_settings table. The target profile is identified by its business code in the request path, and all fields in this DTO are optional so that clients can perform partial updates while the backend maintains system-managed timestamps and identifiers.

name.description:
Updated human-readable name for the policy setting profile.

When provided, this value replaces the previous name shown in administrative UIs.

description.description:
Updated detailed explanation of the policy setting profile.

When provided as a non-null string, this value replaces the previous description to clarify the profile’s intended business use. When explicitly set to null, any existing description is cleared.

category.description:
Updated logical category of the policy setting profile.

Administrators may use this field to move a profile between categories such as "cancellation", "refund", "review", or "age_restriction". Business rules may restrict which transitions are allowed or require additional validation.

config_payload.description:
Updated serialized configuration payload for the policy setting profile.

Typically a JSON string containing structured parameters that downstream enforcement logic interprets. When set to a non-null string, it replaces the previous payload. When explicitly set to null, any previously stored payload is cleared so the profile no longer carries structured parameters.

active.description:
Updated active state flag for the policy setting profile.

When set to true, and when the effective period conditions are satisfied, the profile may participate in enforcement. When set to false, the profile becomes inactive even if its effective window would otherwise permit use.

effective_from.description:
Updated start of the effective period for this policy setting profile in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

When set to a timestamp, the profile becomes applicable on or after this moment while active. When set to null, any previously configured effective-from constraint is removed so that the policy can be considered effective immediately when active. Business logic ensures this value remains logically consistent with effective_to when both are set.

effective_to.description:
Updated end of the effective period for this policy setting profile in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

When set to a timestamp, the profile is considered applicable up to and including this moment while active. When set to null, any previously configured effective-to constraint is removed so that the policy can remain effective indefinitely while active. Business logic validates that effective_to does not precede effective_from when both are provided.

IShoppingMallCancellationPolicy.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request payload for querying cancellation policy records from the shopping_mall_cancellation_policies table.

This DTO is used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/cancellationPolicies endpoint to express flexible filters, full-text search terms, sorting options, and pagination parameters when listing cancellation policies for review and management. It does not map directly to a single Prisma model row and therefore does not declare x-autobe-prisma-schema.

Clients combine these fields to locate policies by business code, name, active flag, effective date ranges, region- and policy-setting associations, and free-text matches in human-readable fields. The server translates these filters into SQL/Prisma conditions and returns a paginated IPageIShoppingMallCancellationPolicy.ISummary response.

codes.description:
Optional list of exact business codes to match against the `code` column.

When provided, only policies whose `code` value is contained in this array should be returned. This is useful for bulk lookups by known identifiers.

name.description:
Optional human-readable name filter.

Implementations typically apply this as a case-insensitive partial match condition against the `name` column so that administrators can search by fragments of the policy name.

active.description:
Optional active flag filter.

When true, only currently active policies should be returned. When false, only inactive policies are returned. When null or omitted, both active and inactive policies may be included according to other criteria.

effectiveFromFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the `effective_from` column.

When provided, only policies whose `effective_from` is greater than or equal to this timestamp (or null when treated as always-effective) should be considered.

effectiveFromTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the `effective_from` column.

When provided, only policies whose `effective_from` is less than or equal to this timestamp should be considered.

effectiveToFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the `effective_to` column.

When provided, only policies whose `effective_to` is greater than or equal to this timestamp (or null when treated as open-ended) should be considered.

effectiveToTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the `effective_to` column.

When provided, only policies whose `effective_to` is less than or equal to this timestamp (or null when treated as open-ended) should be considered.

region_setting_ids.description:
Optional list of region configuration identifiers (`shopping_mall_region_settings.id`) to filter by.

When provided, only cancellation policies whose `region_setting_id` is included in this array (or meets equivalent region-scoping logic) should be returned.

policy_setting_ids.description:
Optional list of policy-setting profile identifiers (`shopping_mall_policy_settings.id`) to filter by.

When provided, only cancellation policies whose `policy_setting_id` is included in this array should be considered.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied to human-readable columns such as `name` and `description`.

Implementations commonly use this value to perform LIKE / ILIKE matches or full-text search over the `name` and `description` fields to support keyword-based discovery.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination.

When omitted, implementations typically default to page 1. Combined with `limit` to select a slice of the result set.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

Implementations should enforce an upper bound to protect performance (for example, 100 or 200 records maximum).

orderBy.description:
Field name to use for sorting results.

Common values include `code`, `name`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. The implementation should validate allowed values to prevent unsafe dynamic ordering.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied with `orderBy`.

Use `asc` for ascending order.

Sort direction applied with `orderBy`.

Use `desc` for descending order.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied with `orderBy`.

Use `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order.

IShoppingMallCancellationPolicy.description:
Full representation of a cancellation policy record stored in the `shopping_mall_cancellation_policies` table.

This DTO is returned from administrative APIs that create or update cancellation policies and from detail retrieval endpoints. It exposes the business identifier, descriptive metadata, behavioral flags, timing rules, activation state, system-managed fields, and high-level contextual associations to region and policy setting profiles.

The `code` field is a globally unique business code used to address the policy in API paths and configuration references. Server-managed fields include the primary key `id`, the creation and update timestamps, and an optional `deleted_at` timestamp used for soft deletion. Optional associations link the policy to region and policy setting configuration entities when present, replacing raw foreign key identifiers for a more expressive, object-based representation.

id.description:
System-generated unique identifier (UUID) for the cancellation policy record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_cancellation_policies` table and is generated by the database or ORM when the policy is created.

code.description:
Globally unique business identifier code for this cancellation policy.

Used as a stable external identifier in API paths (such as `cancellationPolicyCode`), configuration UIs, logs, and foreign key references. Enforced as unique in the underlying Prisma model.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the cancellation policy.

Displayed in administrative interfaces so operators can quickly understand and select the appropriate policy.

description.description:
Optional long-form description of the cancellation policy.

Used to explain the business rules, applicability, and any special conditions associated with this policy. May be null when no descriptive text has been provided.

allow_cancellation_before_shipment.description:
Indicates whether customers are allowed to cancel orders before shipment according to this policy.

When true, orders that have not yet been shipped may be eligible for cancellation subject to timing and status rules. When false, cancellation generally occurs only through post-shipment flows such as returns or may be blocked entirely.

allow_partial_cancellation.description:
Indicates whether partial cancellation of orders is allowed under this policy.

When true, customers can cancel specific lines or quantities while leaving the rest of the order unchanged. When false, cancellations must target the entire order.

max_hours_after_payment.description:
Maximum number of hours after payment during which cancellation is allowed, if defined.

Represents a time window counted from the payment completion timestamp. When null, there may be no fixed hour limit, and other rules determine the eligibility of cancellation requests.

config_payload.description:
Serialized configuration payload containing complex or advanced cancellation rules.

Typically contains JSON or another machine-readable format that encodes detailed conditions and behaviors beyond the basic flags. Interpreted only by backend systems and usually opaque to clients.

effective_from.description:
Start timestamp from which this policy is considered effective for new applicable orders, if defined.

Orders created at or after this time can be governed by this policy when other selection criteria match. Null indicates the policy may be effective immediately or according to other platform rules.

effective_to.description:
End timestamp after which this policy should no longer be applied to new orders, if defined.

Orders created after this time should not be governed by this policy. Historical orders may still reference the policy for auditing and reporting.

active.description:
Indicates whether this cancellation policy is currently active.

Active policies are eligible to be selected in configuration UIs and applied to new orders. Inactive policies remain stored for historical and auditing purposes but should not be used for new configurations.

region_setting.description:
Optional region configuration associated with this cancellation policy.

When present, this summary object describes the `shopping_mall_region_settings` entry that scopes where the policy applies (for example, a specific country, region, or market). When null, the policy may be considered globally applicable or associated via other mechanisms.

policy_setting.description:
Optional policy setting profile associated with this cancellation policy.

When present, this summary object represents the `shopping_mall_policy_settings` entry that groups this policy into a broader configuration profile. When null, the policy may stand alone or be linked through other configuration constructs.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this cancellation policy record was created.

Set automatically by the system when the row is inserted into the `shopping_mall_cancellation_policies` table and not directly modifiable by clients.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this cancellation policy record was last updated.

Automatically refreshed by the system whenever a mutable field of the policy is changed via an update operation.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this cancellation policy record was soft-deleted, if applicable.

When null, the policy is considered not deleted from a data perspective, though it may still be inactive according to the `active` flag.

IShoppingMallCancellationPolicy.ICreate.description:
Creation payload for defining a new cancellation policy in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by high-privilege platform administrators or configuration owners to create a new cancellation policy row in the `shopping_mall_cancellation_policies` table. It captures the business identifier, human-readable metadata, behavioral flags, optional timing rules, and optional associations to region and policy setting configuration profiles.

The `code` field is a globally unique business code enforced by a unique index in the underlying Prisma model and is used to address policies via API paths and foreign key references. Optional fields such as `region_code` and `policy_setting_code` allow the new policy to be linked atomically to an existing region setting and policy setting by their business codes instead of raw UUID identifiers.

All server-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are excluded from this creation DTO. Associations expressed via codes are resolved by the backend to the corresponding Prisma foreign keys.

code.description:
Globally unique business identifier code for this cancellation policy.

This value is enforced as unique in the `shopping_mall_cancellation_policies` table and is used as the path parameter (`cancellationPolicyCode`) in administrative APIs. It should be stable over time and suitable for use in logs, configuration UIs, and cross-entity references.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the cancellation policy.

Displayed in administrative UIs so configuration owners and operators can easily differentiate between multiple policies (for example, "Default Global Cancellation Policy" or "Holiday Promotion Cancellation Rules").

description.description:
Optional long-form description of the cancellation policy.

This field is used to document the business intent, constraints, and any special notes about when and how the policy should be applied. It is typically shown in admin configuration screens for reference.

allow_cancellation_before_shipment.description:
Flag indicating whether customers are allowed to cancel orders before shipment.

When `true`, orders that have not yet reached a shipped or fulfilled state may be eligible for cancellation according to additional timing and status rules. When `false`, cancellations may only be allowed after shipment (for example, via return flows) or may be blocked entirely.

allow_partial_cancellation.description:
Flag indicating whether partial cancellation of orders is allowed under this policy.

When `true`, customers may cancel one or more lines or quantities within an order while leaving the remaining items intact. When `false`, cancellation requests must target the full order.

max_hours_after_payment.description:
Optional maximum number of hours after payment during which cancellation is allowed.

When set, this value defines a time window counted from the payment completion timestamp within which customers can submit cancellation requests that fall under this policy. When null, the platform may apply other rules or allow cancellation without a fixed hour limit.

config_payload.description:
Optional serialized configuration payload for complex or advanced cancellation rules.

Typically contains a JSON-encoded structure or other machine-readable configuration that allows the business to express conditions beyond the simple flags exposed as top-level fields. The exact structure is interpreted by backend logic and is opaque to clients.

effective_from.description:
Optional start timestamp from which this policy becomes effective for new applicable orders.

When provided, new orders created at or after this timestamp can be governed by this policy if other selection criteria match. When omitted or null, the policy is considered effective immediately upon creation.

effective_to.description:
Optional end timestamp after which this policy should no longer be applied to new orders.

When provided, new orders created after this timestamp should not be governed by this policy. Historical orders may still reference the policy for auditing purposes.

active.description:
Flag indicating whether this cancellation policy is currently active for selection and application.

Inactive policies remain in the database for historical reference but should not be applied to new orders or configuration assignments.

region_code.description:
Optional business code of the region setting to associate with this cancellation policy.

When provided, this code must match the unique business code of an existing region configuration in `shopping_mall_region_settings`. The backend resolves this code to the corresponding foreign key so that the policy is scoped to that region. When null or omitted, the policy may be treated as globally applicable or associated via other mechanisms.

policy_setting_code.description:
Optional business code of the policy setting profile to associate with this cancellation policy.

When provided, this code must match the unique business code of an existing policy setting in `shopping_mall_policy_settings`. The backend resolves this code to the corresponding foreign key so that the policy becomes part of that configuration profile. When null or omitted, the policy stands alone or is linked through other configuration constructs.

IShoppingMallCancellationPolicy.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for modifying an existing cancellation policy in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by platform administrators or configuration owners to adjust the mutable properties of an existing cancellation policy in the `shopping_mall_cancellation_policies` table. The target record is identified externally via its globally unique business `code` path parameter (`cancellationPolicyCode`), so no identity fields are present in this structure.

All fields in this DTO are optional, enabling partial updates; any omitted field is left unchanged. Immutable system-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, and `deleted_at`, as well as the `code` business identifier, cannot be modified via this DTO. The service updates `updated_at` automatically when changes are applied.

Administrators can use this DTO to rename the policy, adjust descriptive text, toggle flags such as `allow_cancellation_before_shipment` and `allow_partial_cancellation`, tune timing rules, change activation status, or update associations to region and policy setting profiles using their business codes instead of raw UUID identifiers.

name.description:
New human-readable name for the cancellation policy.

If provided, this value replaces the current name in the `shopping_mall_cancellation_policies` record and will be shown in administrative UIs.

description.description:
New long-form description for the cancellation policy.

Used to update the explanatory text shown in configuration tools. When explicitly set to null, previously stored descriptive text may be cleared depending on business rules.

allow_cancellation_before_shipment.description:
Updated flag controlling whether customers are allowed to cancel orders before shipment under this policy.

When provided, this value replaces the existing `allow_cancellation_before_shipment` setting.

allow_partial_cancellation.description:
Updated flag indicating whether partial cancellation of orders is allowed under this policy.

When provided, this value replaces the existing `allow_partial_cancellation` setting.

max_hours_after_payment.description:
Updated maximum number of hours after payment during which cancellation is allowed.

When provided with a non-null value, the time window for eligible cancellations is replaced. When explicitly set to null, the platform may interpret this as removing the fixed hour limit and falling back to other rules.

config_payload.description:
Updated serialized configuration payload for complex or advanced cancellation rules.

When provided, this value replaces the existing payload. When explicitly set to null, the existing payload may be cleared so that only simple top-level flags apply.

effective_from.description:
Updated start timestamp from which this policy becomes effective for new applicable orders.

When provided, this replaces the existing `effective_from`. When explicitly set to null, the policy may be considered effective immediately without a fixed start boundary.

effective_to.description:
Updated end timestamp after which this policy should no longer be applied to new orders.

When provided, this replaces the existing `effective_to`. When explicitly set to null, the policy may become open-ended until changed again.

active.description:
Updated activation flag for this cancellation policy.

When provided, this value replaces the current `active` status, controlling whether the policy can be selected for new configurations or applied to new orders.

region_code.description:
Optional business code of the region setting to associate with this cancellation policy.

When provided, this code is resolved by the backend to the corresponding `shopping_mall_region_settings` entry and replaces any existing region association. When explicitly set to null, the current region association is cleared so that the policy is no longer scoped to a specific region.

policy_setting_code.description:
Optional business code of the policy setting profile to associate with this cancellation policy.

When provided, this code is resolved by the backend to the corresponding `shopping_mall_policy_settings` entry and replaces any existing policy setting association. When explicitly set to null, the current association is cleared so that the policy is no longer grouped under a specific policy setting profile.

IShoppingMallRefundPolicy.IRequest.description:
Search filter, pagination, and sorting request DTO for querying refund policy configurations stored in the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` table.

This type is used by administrative search endpoints (for example, PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/refundPolicies) to express rich filter criteria over refund policy definitions, such as matching specific policy codes or names, restricting by active status or effective date ranges, and specifying pagination and ordering options. It does not map directly to a single Prisma model row but instead represents query parameters for listing operations.

page.description: 1-based page index to retrieve. Used together with `limit` to paginate over refund policy records. When omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of refund policy records to return in a single page. The backend should enforce an upper bound to protect performance (for example, 100 or 200 records per page).

search.description: Free-text search keyword applied to one or more text fields such as policy code, name, or description. The exact matching behavior (prefix, substring, or full-text search) is implementation-specific.

codes.description: Optional list of refund policy business codes to include in the result set. Each value should match the `code` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`.

name.description: Optional exact or partial match filter for the human-readable name of the refund policy. The implementation may perform case-insensitive matching or apply other text search rules.

isActive.description: Filter flag indicating whether to return only currently active (`true`) or inactive (`false`) refund policy records. When omitted, both active and inactive policies may be returned depending on the implementation.

effectiveFromGte.description: Lower bound (inclusive) for the start of the policy's effective period, used to find policies that become effective on or after the given timestamp.

effectiveFromLte.description: Upper bound (inclusive) for the start of the policy's effective period, used to constrain results to policies whose effective-from dates are not later than the given timestamp.

effectiveUntilGte.description: Lower bound (inclusive) for the end of the policy's effective period, used to search for policies that remain effective at or beyond the given timestamp.

effectiveUntilLte.description: Upper bound (inclusive) for the end of the policy's effective period, used to find policies that expire on or before the given timestamp.
