IShoppingMallRefundPolicy.description:
Detailed refund policy configuration DTO representing a single configuration object that controls how refunds are processed for orders and payments in the shoppingMall platform.

This type is directly backed by the Prisma model `shopping_mall_refund_policies`, which stores canonical policy definitions. The DTO exposes core scalar columns such as `code`, `name`, refund behavior flags, numeric thresholds, lifecycle timestamps, and a serialized configuration payload.

In addition to the direct column mappings, the DTO also projects a small number of convenience and relationship fields such as `maxRefundRate`, `regionCode`, and `policySettingCode`. These help API consumers understand how the policy is scoped and interpreted without needing to work with raw foreign keys or parse the configuration payload themselves.

This DTO is intended for administrative configuration and monitoring views. It is not used for per-transaction state, which is represented by separate payment and refund transaction entities that reference these policies by code or identifier.

id.description:
Internal unique identifier of the refund policy record.

This value corresponds to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` table and uniquely identifies the policy across the platform. It is primarily used internally and in deep links or debugging tools rather than as the main stable business reference.

code.description:
Business-level unique code of the refund policy.

This maps directly to the non-nullable, unique `code` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`. Administrative APIs and other configuration entities use this value in paths and references, for example `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/refundPolicies/{refundPolicyCode}`. The code is expected to be stable over the lifetime of the policy so that historical records remain interpretable.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the refund policy.

This corresponds to the `name` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` table. It is shown in administrative user interfaces, logs, and reports, allowing operators to quickly recognize the purpose of the policy without inspecting its internal configuration.

description.description:
Optional long-form description of the refund policy and its intended use.

This field reflects the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`. It can document eligibility conditions, product or category scopes, approval workflows, and any caveats that are important for finance, support, or compliance teams when interpreting the policy.

isActive.description:
Indicates whether this refund policy is active for new business flows.

This boolean is a projection of the non-nullable `active` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` Prisma model. When `true`, and when the effective period allows it, the policy may be selected by refund-processing logic for new transactions. When `false`, the policy is considered retired for new usage, although historical transactions may continue to reference it for audit and reporting purposes.

allowFullRefund.description:
Flag indicating whether full (100%) refunds are allowed under this policy.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `allow_full_refund` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`. When `true`, the rules governed by this policy permit refunding up to the full eligible amount for qualifying orders or line items. When `false`, the policy must be combined with other limits such as percentages or fixed thresholds to constrain refund amounts.

allowPartialRefund.description:
Flag indicating whether partial refunds are allowed under this policy.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `allow_partial_refund` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`. When `true`, refunds can target a subset of order lines or a partial monetary amount. When `false`, the policy enforces all-or-nothing refund behavior within its scope, so partial refunds are not permitted.

maxDaysAfterDelivery.description:
Maximum number of days after delivery within which a customer can request a refund or return under this policy.

This property corresponds to the nullable `max_days_after_delivery` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` table. When present, it specifies a simple day-based window anchored at the delivery event, beyond which refund or return requests are no longer eligible under this policy. A `null` value indicates that the eligibility window is governed solely by other configuration values or rules contained in the configuration payload.

requireAdminApprovalOverAmount.description:
Monetary amount threshold above which an administrator or other privileged actor must approve the refund.

This field maps directly to the nullable `require_admin_approval_over_amount` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`. When non-null, any refund whose gross amount is greater than or equal to this value should be routed through a manual approval workflow before funds are released. When null, no specific amount-based approval threshold is enforced by this field, although other policy logic may still require approval.

configurationPayload.description:
Serialized configuration payload containing advanced or custom refund rule definitions.

This property is a projection of the nullable `config_payload` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` Prisma model. It typically contains JSON text that encodes additional conditions such as product- or category-level exclusions, per-channel variations, or tiered refund behavior that cannot be conveniently expressed as simple scalar columns.

The exact schema of this payload is defined by the refund-processing subsystem and is validated there. API consumers should treat it as an opaque configuration blob unless they explicitly implement the same interpretation logic.

maxRefundRate.description:
Derived maximum refundable rate expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1 of the eligible amount.

Unlike `maxDaysAfterDelivery` and `requireAdminApprovalOverAmount`, this property does not correspond to a single dedicated column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`. Instead, it is a convenience projection that may be computed from the configuration payload or other policy parameters to summarize the most permissive refund percentage the policy allows.

For example, a value of `1.0` indicates that up to 100% of the eligible amount can be refunded, whereas `0.5` would indicate that refunds are capped at 50%. When not applicable or not explicitly defined by the policy, this property may be omitted from responses.

effectiveFrom.description:
Timestamp from which this refund policy becomes effective for new operations.

This is a direct projection of the nullable `effective_from` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string. Refunds for events occurring before this timestamp should not apply this policy, while events on or after this timestamp may apply it if the policy is active and other conditions are met.

effectiveUntil.description:
Timestamp after which this refund policy is no longer effective for new refund operations.

This value reflects the nullable `effective_to` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string. Refunds initiated after this moment should not use this policy, although existing historical records may continue to reference it for audit. A null value indicates that the policy does not have a fixed end date and remains effective until deactivated or replaced.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this refund policy record was created in the system.

This property is a projection of the non-nullable `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`, formatted as an ISO 8601 date-time string (typically in UTC). It is used for audit trails, chronological sorting, and correlating configuration changes with observed operational behavior over time.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this refund policy record was last updated.

This value maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`, stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string. Each successful modification of the policy, including changes to scalar fields or the configuration payload, should update this timestamp and allow administrators to detect recent configuration changes.

deletedAt.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the refund policy, if it has been retired from active use.

This property corresponds to the nullable `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_refund_policies`. When non-null, the policy is considered logically deleted or archived and should not be applied to new refund operations. Historical references are preserved so that audits and reports can reconstruct the configuration that was in force at the time of a past transaction.

regionCode.description:
Optional business-level region code indicating the market or geographic area where this refund policy applies.

This field is a high-level projection derived from the nullable foreign key `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` that links to a `shopping_mall_region_settings` record. When present, it typically mirrors the `code` field from the associated `IShoppingMallRegionSetting.ISummary` object, signaling that the policy is scoped to that region. When absent, the policy may be considered global or scoped by other configuration rules.

policySettingCode.description:
Optional business-level code of a shared policy setting profile associated with this refund policy.

This value is projected from the foreign key `shopping_mall_policy_setting_id`, which links to a `shopping_mall_policy_settings` record. When present, it typically matches the `code` of an `IShoppingMallPolicySetting.ISummary` and indicates that foundational configuration parameters are inherited or shared from that profile. When absent, the policy is self-contained and does not depend on a separate policy setting profile.

IShoppingMallRefundPolicy.ICreate.description:
Creation DTO for registering a new refund policy definition in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO captures business-facing configuration input required to define how refunds are handled for a class of orders or items, including a stable business code, human-friendly name, descriptive text, refund eligibility windows expressed as `refundWindowDays`, maximum refundable rate expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1 (`maxRefundRate`), approval behavior, lifecycle flags, and optional scoping references.

It deliberately excludes system-managed identifiers, timestamps, and authentication context. The authenticated platform administrator performing the operation is derived from the authorization layer and is never specified explicitly in this request body. The fields in this DTO are designed to map directly onto the main refund policy representation `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy`, so that names and semantics are consistent across create, read, and update flows.

code.description:
Business-level unique code for the refund policy.

This value is used as the primary external identifier when referencing the policy in administrative tools and APIs. It must be unique across all refund policies to avoid ambiguity, and once created it should remain stable over the lifetime of the policy.

name.description:
Human-friendly name of the refund policy.

Displayed in administrative UIs, logs, and reports so that operators can easily recognize the purpose of the policy without needing to inspect its detailed configuration.

description.description:
Optional long-form description of the refund policy.

This may document business intent, eligibility criteria, and any edge cases or exceptions that operators should be aware of when applying or modifying the policy.

allowFullRefund.description:
Flag indicating whether full (100%) refunds are allowed under this policy.

When `true`, the policy permits refunding the entire eligible amount for qualifying transactions, subject to other rule constraints. When `false`, refunds must be constrained by other limits such as `maxRefundRate` or stricter business rules.

allowPartialRefund.description:
Flag indicating whether partial refunds are allowed under this policy.

When `true`, the policy supports refunding portions of the original amount or specific line items. When `false`, the policy enforces all-or-nothing refund behavior within its scope.

refundWindowDays.description:
Maximum number of days after a defined business anchor event during which a refund can be requested.

The anchor event (for example, order completion, shipment, or delivery) is determined by the platform’s business rules or the attached configuration payload. A value of `0` may restrict eligibility to same-day refunds, while larger values increase the allowable window.

maxRefundRate.description:
Maximum refundable rate of the original payment amount, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

For example, `1.0` indicates that the full eligible amount may be refunded, while `0.5` restricts refunds to at most half of the eligible amount. This field maps directly to the `maxRefundRate` property on `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy`. Implementations should validate that the value falls within a sensible numeric range of 0 to 1 inclusive.

requireManualApprovalOverAmount.description:
Monetary threshold above which manual approval is required for a refund request.

When present, refund requests whose amount meets or exceeds this value must be explicitly approved by an authorized operator such as a seller or platform administrator. The currency and precision follow the platform’s standard money representation. This threshold works together with the `requiresManualApproval` behavior exposed on `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy`, allowing implementations to derive coarse-grained flags from more detailed configuration.

configurationPayload.description:
Optional serialized configuration payload encoded as JSON text.

This field is intended for advanced rule definitions that are not directly modeled as separate scalar fields, such as per-category overrides, complex eligibility conditions, or integration-specific flags. The backend is responsible for validating and interpreting its structure and will expose the same content via the `configurationPayload` field on `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy` when reading the policy back.

isActive.description:
Flag indicating whether the refund policy is currently active for new business flows.

When `true`, the policy may be considered by refund-processing logic once its effective period has started. When `false`, the policy should not be applied to new refund operations, though historical records may continue to reference it for audit and reporting purposes. This field maps directly to the `isActive` property on `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy`.

effectiveFrom.description:
Optional timestamp from which this refund policy becomes effective, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When provided, the policy should only apply to events occurring at or after this moment. When `null`, the policy is considered effective immediately upon creation, subject to its `isActive` flag. The value is ultimately surfaced via the `effectiveFrom` property on `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy` when the policy is read.

effectiveUntil.description:
Optional timestamp after which this refund policy ceases to be effective for new operations, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When provided, events occurring strictly after this moment should not apply this policy. When `null`, the policy remains effective until it is explicitly deactivated or superseded by other configuration. The corresponding field on the main entity is `effectiveUntil`, which always reflects the persisted value or a normalized default.

regionCode.description:
Optional business-level region code that scopes where this refund policy is applicable.

When set to a non-null value, only orders or customers associated with the matching region context should consider this policy during refund calculations. When `null`, the policy may be treated as globally applicable or subject to higher-level region-routing rules. In responses, `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy.regionCode` will expose the persisted value or a normalized representation based on how nulls are handled by the implementation.

policySettingCode.description:
Optional business-level code referencing a shared policy setting profile.

This allows multiple refund policies to reuse centralized configuration blocks, such as approval workflows or escalation matrices, without duplicating those details in each policy. Supplying `null` can be used to clear an existing association. In the main entity, the corresponding field `policySettingCode` will expose the stored value that results from this configuration.

IShoppingMallRefundPolicy.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing refund policy definition in the shoppingMall platform.

All properties are optional to support partial updates, and only the provided fields are applied. The target policy is identified externally, for example by its business `code` in the URL path, not by any field in this object.

The fields in this DTO mirror the configurable aspects of `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy` as closely as possible, using the same names and semantics (`refundWindowDays`, `maxRefundRate`, `configurationPayload`, `isActive`, `effectiveFrom`, `effectiveUntil`, `regionCode`, `policySettingCode`) so that consumers can reason about updates and reads using a consistent vocabulary.

name.description:
Updated human-friendly name of the refund policy.

If provided, replaces the current display name used in administrative interfaces and reports. When omitted, the existing name remains unchanged.

description.description:
Updated long-form description of the refund policy.

If provided, replaces the existing descriptive text used to document the policy’s purpose and detailed rules. When omitted, the current description is preserved.

allowFullRefund.description:
Updated flag specifying whether full (100%) refunds are allowed under this policy.

If provided, overrides the existing configuration and may immediately change how new refund requests are evaluated for eligible transactions. When omitted, the previous flag value is retained.

allowPartialRefund.description:
Updated flag specifying whether partial refunds are allowed under this policy.

If provided, overrides the existing configuration and may immediately affect whether partial refund amounts are permitted under this policy. When omitted, the existing behavior is preserved.

refundWindowDays.description:
Updated maximum number of days after the anchor event during which a refund can be requested.

If provided, replaces the existing refund window and should be validated for consistency with other policy settings. A value of `0` can be used to restrict eligibility to same-day refunds, while larger values extend the allowable window.

maxRefundRate.description:
Updated maximum refundable rate of the original payment amount, expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1.

If provided, replaces the existing limit used when calculating allowable refund amounts under this policy. This field maps directly to `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy.maxRefundRate`, and implementations should validate that values fall within the inclusive 0–1 range.

requireManualApprovalOverAmount.description:
Updated monetary threshold at or above which manual approval is required for refund requests.

If provided, overrides the existing threshold and may change which refund requests require explicit operator approval. The threshold interacts with coarse-grained behavior represented by the `requiresManualApproval` field on the main entity, and implementations may derive that boolean from the presence and value of this threshold and other configuration.

configurationPayload.description:
Updated advanced configuration payload encoded as JSON text.

If provided, replaces the existing configuration blob stored with the refund policy. The backend is responsible for validating that the JSON structure conforms to expected schemas and for exposing the same content via `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy.configurationPayload` when the policy is retrieved.

isActive.description:
Updated active flag for this refund policy.

When set to `false`, the policy should no longer be applied to new refund operations, though historical data may continue to reference it. When set to `true`, and combined with appropriate effective period configuration, the policy becomes eligible for use. If omitted, the existing active flag is not changed.

effectiveFrom.description:
Updated timestamp from which this refund policy becomes effective, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Providing a non-null value changes when the policy should start applying to new events. Providing `null` may clear a previously set start boundary so that effectiveness is controlled solely by other attributes. When omitted, the existing `effectiveFrom` value is retained.

effectiveUntil.description:
Updated timestamp after which this refund policy should no longer apply to new events, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Providing a non-null value sets or changes the end of the effective period. Providing `null` may clear a previously configured end boundary, allowing the policy to remain effective indefinitely (subject to `isActive`). When omitted, the current `effectiveUntil` value remains unchanged.

regionCode.description:
Updated business-level region code defining where this refund policy applies.

If provided with a non-null value, overrides the existing region association, constraining the policy to that region. Providing `null` can be used to clear a previously set region so that the policy becomes global or subject to higher-level routing. When omitted, the existing region configuration is preserved.

policySettingCode.description:
Updated business-level code referencing a shared policy setting profile.

If provided with a non-null value, replaces the existing link to a reusable configuration profile. Providing `null` detaches the policy from any shared profile so that it stands alone. When omitted, the current association remains unchanged.

IShoppingMallReviewPolicy.IRequest.description:
Filter, search, sort, and pagination criteria for listing review policies from the shopping_mall_review_policies table for administrative management.

This DTO encapsulates all query parameters used by platform administrators to search and paginate review policy definitions, including full-text search over policy name and description, filtering by activation status, effective period, region/profile scoping, and numeric threshold windows. It is tightly aligned with the underlying `shopping_mall_review_policies` Prisma model while remaining purely read-only and side-effect free.

search.description:
Full-text search keyword applied to the review policy `name` and `description` fields.

The backend may leverage GIN or other text indexes on the `name` and `description` columns of `shopping_mall_review_policies` to implement efficient search behavior, typically using ILIKE or full-text expressions based on this value. When omitted or empty, no full-text search constraint is applied.

code.description:
Optional exact or prefix match filter for the business code of the review policy.

This value is matched against the non-nullable `code` column of the `shopping_mall_review_policies` table, which is enforced by a unique index. Depending on implementation, it may be treated as an exact match (for example `default_review`) or as a prefix for partial matching such as `strict_`, but callers should not rely on a specific matching strategy without consulting API documentation.

active.description:
Tri-state filter flag indicating whether to return only active or only inactive policies.

When set to `true`, only rows where the non-nullable `active` column of `shopping_mall_review_policies` is true are returned. When set to `false`, only inactive policies are returned. When omitted or set explicitly to null, no filter is applied to the `active` column, and policies of any activation state may be included in the result set.

region_setting_id.description:
Optional filter by the UUID primary key of the associated region setting from the `shopping_mall_region_settings` table.

When provided, this value must equal the `id` column of a `shopping_mall_region_settings` record, and only review policies whose foreign key `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` matches this UUID are returned. This filter complements the `region_setting` relation exposed in read models, allowing admins to scope results to a specific market or geographic area.

policy_setting_id.description:
Optional filter by the UUID primary key of the associated policy configuration profile from the `shopping_mall_policy_settings` table.

When supplied, this value should match the `id` column of a `shopping_mall_policy_settings` row, and only review policies whose `shopping_mall_policy_setting_id` foreign key equals this UUID are included. It is useful for retrieving all review policies bound to a given shared policy setting profile that may also be referenced by other policy types.

effective_from_gte.description:
Lower bound for the `effective_from` field of review policies, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When present, only policies whose `effective_from` column is greater than or equal to this value (or policies whose `effective_from` is null and are treated as effective from the beginning of time, depending on business rules) are included. This allows administrators to focus on policies that became active after a certain point in time.

effective_to_lte.description:
Upper bound for the `effective_to` field of review policies, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

If provided, the query is restricted to policies whose `effective_to` column is less than or equal to the supplied value, or to policies whose `effective_to` is null and are interpreted as open-ended according to service logic. This is typically used to locate policies that are expiring within, or that expired before, a particular time window.

max_days_after_delivery_for_review_min.description:
Optional lower bound filter for the `max_days_after_delivery_for_review` configuration column on `shopping_mall_review_policies`.

When this integer is set, only policies whose `max_days_after_delivery_for_review` value is greater than or equal to the provided number of days are returned. Combined with `max_days_after_delivery_for_review_max`, it allows clients to query for policies whose review window length falls within a specific numeric range. Service implementations should validate that the minimum does not exceed the maximum when both are present.

max_days_after_delivery_for_review_max.description:
Optional upper bound filter for the `max_days_after_delivery_for_review` configuration column on `shopping_mall_review_policies`.

When provided, this filter restricts results to policies whose `max_days_after_delivery_for_review` value is less than or equal to the supplied integer. Used together with the corresponding `min` filter, it defines a closed numeric interval for allowed review window sizes in days.

allow_edit_within_days_min.description:
Optional lower bound filter for the `allow_edit_within_days` configuration column.

Setting this value causes the query to return only policies where the `allow_edit_within_days` field is greater than or equal to the given integer, thereby selecting policies that provide at least this many days of edit allowance after review creation. It is often used with `allow_edit_within_days_max` to define an acceptable edit-window range.

allow_edit_within_days_max.description:
Optional upper bound filter for the `allow_edit_within_days` configuration column.

When specified, only policies whose `allow_edit_within_days` value is less than or equal to this integer are included in the result set. This is useful when searching for policies that differ by how strict or permissive their edit windows are, particularly when combined with the related `min` filter.

auto_hide_report_threshold_min.description:
Optional lower bound filter for the `auto_hide_report_threshold` configuration column.

Supplying this field restricts results to policies that require at least the given number of distinct abuse reports before automatic hiding is triggered. It enables administrators to find policies with relatively conservative or aggressive automatic moderation thresholds, especially when paired with the corresponding maximum filter.

auto_hide_report_threshold_max.description:
Optional upper bound filter for the `auto_hide_report_threshold` configuration column.

When this value is present, the query returns only policies whose `auto_hide_report_threshold` is less than or equal to the specified number of reports. In conjunction with the `min` filter, it defines a numerical band for automatic hiding behavior based on abuse report volume.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination when returning a list of review policies.

If omitted, the backend typically defaults this value to 1, representing the first page of results. Values less than 1 do not satisfy the schema requirements and should be rejected or normalized by the service according to its error-handling policy.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page when paginating review policies.

Clients may propose any positive integer, but the backend implementation is expected to enforce a sensible upper bound (for example 100 or 500) to preserve performance and protect the system from excessively large result sets. When this property is not provided, a default page size defined by the service is applied.

order_by.description:
Field name used to sort the result set of review policies.

Typical allowed values include `code`, `name`, `effective_from`, or `created_at`, each mapping to the corresponding column in `shopping_mall_review_policies`. The backend must validate and whitelist acceptable columns to avoid invalid or unsafe sort expressions; unsupported values should result in a validation error or be ignored according to API conventions.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction for the result set, indicating whether records should be ordered in ascending or descending order by the `order_by` field.

When set to `"asc"`, rows are ordered in ascending order based on the chosen column. When set to `"desc"`, rows are ordered in descending order. If omitted, the service may apply a default direction, often descending by `created_at` or `updated_at` to show the most recent policies first.

IShoppingMallReviewPolicy.description:
Detailed review and rating policy definition entity mapped from the `shopping_mall_review_policies` Prisma model.

This DTO represents the full set of fields describing how product reviews and ratings behave for the shoppingMall platform, including eligibility windows, edit allowances, automatic hiding thresholds, and optional configuration payload. Policies may optionally be scoped to regions and configuration profiles and support activation flags, effective period constraints, and soft deletion semantics for historical analysis and auditing.

id.description:
UUID primary key of the review policy record.

This non-nullable field corresponds to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_review_policies` table and is generated by the system. It uniquely identifies a review policy row for internal joins, auditing, and low-level API operations, even when business-facing APIs prefer to use the `code` field for addressing.

code.description:
Business-facing unique code that identifies the review policy, such as `default_review` or `strict_moderation`.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `code` column of the `shopping_mall_review_policies` Prisma model, which is protected by a unique index to guarantee global uniqueness. It is commonly used in admin URLs, configuration references, and integrations that need a stable, human-readable identifier for a policy.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the review policy shown in administrative tools and configuration screens.

The value originates from the non-nullable `name` column of `shopping_mall_review_policies` and should provide a concise and descriptive label for the policy. Administrators rely on this name in lists, dropdowns, and dashboards when selecting or comparing different review policies.

description.description:
Optional, longer-form description that documents the intent and behavior of this review policy.

This field corresponds to the nullable `description` column in the `shopping_mall_review_policies` table. When present, it can describe eligibility rules, moderation strategies, timing constraints, and any special considerations. When null, the policy is documented primarily by its `name`, `code`, and scalar configuration values.

max_days_after_delivery_for_review.description:
Maximum number of days after an order is marked as delivered during which a customer is allowed to submit a review.

This property is backed by the nullable `max_days_after_delivery_for_review` integer column on `shopping_mall_review_policies`. A positive integer defines a hard upper bound on the review window; when null, the policy may defer to other configuration (for example, to values in `config_payload`) or indicate that no explicit limit is imposed by this field alone.

allow_edit_within_days.description:
Number of days after review creation during which a customer may edit their review under this policy.

The value comes from the nullable `allow_edit_within_days` column in the Prisma model. When it is a positive integer, it defines how long an edit window remains open after the original submission. When null, editing may be disabled entirely or governed by separate rules encoded in `config_payload` or other service-level configuration.

auto_hide_report_threshold.description:
Number of distinct abuse reports required before a review is automatically hidden pending moderation.

This property reflects the nullable `auto_hide_report_threshold` integer column in `shopping_mall_review_policies`. When set, reaching or exceeding this threshold causes the platform to automatically hide the review from public display and flag it for moderator attention. When null, automatic hiding based solely on report count is disabled and reviews remain visible until handled through other moderation flows.

config_payload.description:
Serialized configuration payload that contains additional, potentially complex rules for review handling, typically represented as JSON text.

This field is mapped from the nullable `config_payload` column on `shopping_mall_review_policies`. The payload may encode advanced policy attributes such as prohibited content categories, rating scale configuration, language-specific constraints, or experiment toggles. The DTO treats the payload as opaque text, leaving interpretation to domain-specific logic within the service layer.

active.description:
Indicates whether this review policy is currently active and should be applied to new review-related operations.

The value is backed by the non-nullable `active` boolean column in `shopping_mall_review_policies`. Inactive policies may remain in the database for historical reference or future reactivation, but application services should typically exclude them from runtime policy selection unless explicitly requested by administrative tooling.

effective_from.description:
Optional timestamp from which this policy becomes effective for new review operations, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This property corresponds to the nullable `effective_from` column of the Prisma model. When set, only events occurring at or after this moment should consider the policy active (assuming `active` is also true). When null, the policy is treated as effective immediately once it is created and marked active, subject to higher-level business rules.

effective_to.description:
Optional timestamp after which this policy ceases to apply to new operations, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

The value maps to the nullable `effective_to` column on `shopping_mall_review_policies`. When populated, it marks the end of the policy's effective period for new reviews, although historical reviews may still reference the policy for audit purposes. When null, the policy has no predefined expiration and remains in effect until deactivated or otherwise superseded.

region_setting.description:
Optional association to the region configuration that scopes this review policy to a particular market or geographic area.

This property represents the relation defined by the nullable `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` foreign key, which links to a row in the `shopping_mall_region_settings` table. When non-null, it exposes a lightweight `IShoppingMallRegionSetting.ISummary` object so that admin tools can display regional context in lists and detail views without issuing a separate region detail query.

policy_setting.description:
Optional association to a shared policy configuration profile that this review policy is bound to.

It corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_policy_setting_id` foreign key and points to a record in the `shopping_mall_policy_settings` table. When populated, the embedded `IShoppingMallPolicySetting.ISummary` gives administrators a concise view of the overarching configuration profile that supplies additional parameters for this review policy and possibly other policy types such as cancellation or refund policies.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this review policy record was created, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This non-nullable field is mapped from the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_review_policies`, typically maintained automatically by the database or ORM. It is useful for auditing changes, sorting lists by creation time, and understanding how long a particular policy has been in use.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this review policy record was last updated, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

The value is taken from the non-nullable `updated_at` column in the Prisma model and is refreshed on each successful modification. It allows administrators and support staff to quickly identify recently changed policies that may require review, testing, or communication to stakeholders.

deleted_at.description:
Optional timestamp used for soft deletion, indicating that the policy has been retired from active use while remaining available for historical reference.

This property maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column on `shopping_mall_review_policies`. When non-null, most queries for active or usable policies should treat the record as logically deleted, even though it remains persisted for audit trails, analytics, and reconstruction of past decision contexts related to reviews and moderation actions.

IShoppingMallReviewPolicy.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new review and rating policy in the shopping_mall_review_policies table.

Used by platform administrator tools to define how product reviews behave, including eligibility windows, edit rules, auto-hiding thresholds, and optional scoping to regions or shared policy settings. Client supplies only business-configurable fields; identity and lifecycle timestamps are managed by the backend.

code.description:
Business-meaningful unique identifier for the review policy.

Examples include values like "default_review" or "strict_moderation". This maps directly to the `code` column in the `shopping_mall_review_policies` table, which has a unique index. Must be non-empty and globally unique across all review policies.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the review policy for admin UIs.

Displayed in administrative tools when selecting or managing policies. Must be a non-empty string.

description.description:
Optional free-form description of the review policy.

Typically documents eligibility requirements, moderation strategies, and time windows for reviews. When omitted or null, no additional description is stored.

max_days_after_delivery_for_review.description:
Maximum number of days after an order reaches delivered status during which a customer may submit a review.

When set to an integer value, review creation is allowed only within this many days after delivery. When null, the policy may fall back to other configuration or effectively apply no explicit limit from this field.

allow_edit_within_days.description:
Number of days after review creation during which the customer is allowed to edit their review.

When set, edits are permitted only within this many days from initial creation. When null, the policy either disallows editing or defers to other configuration, depending on business rules.

auto_hide_report_threshold.description:
Number of distinct abuse reports required before a review is automatically hidden pending moderation.

When set to a positive integer, hitting or exceeding this threshold triggers automatic hiding of the review. When null, automatic hiding based on report counts is disabled, and all reports require manual moderation.

config_payload.description:
Serialized configuration payload for additional policy rules.

Typically contains JSON text encoding detailed constraints, such as prohibited content categories, rating scale configuration, or other advanced settings. When null, only the scalar columns define the policy behavior.

active.description:
Indicates whether this review policy is currently active.

Active policies are considered by review subsystems when evaluating review creation, editing, and moderation behavior. Inactive policies may be retained for historical reference but should not affect new operations.

effective_from.description:
Optional start timestamp from which this policy becomes effective for new review-related operations.

When provided, the policy should be treated as applicable only at or after this instant. When null, the policy is considered effective immediately upon activation or creation, subject to other business rules.

effective_to.description:
Optional end timestamp after which this policy should no longer be applied to new review-related operations.

When provided, the policy is treated as expired after this instant, though it may still be referenced for historical data. When null, the policy has no predefined expiration.

shopping_mall_region_setting_id.description:
Optional foreign key referencing a region configuration in `shopping_mall_region_settings`.

When set, the policy is scoped to the referenced region or market. When null, the policy is treated as globally applicable or independent of region-level configuration.

shopping_mall_policy_setting_id.description:
Optional foreign key referencing a shared policy configuration profile in `shopping_mall_policy_settings`.

When set, the review policy is linked to a broader configuration group that may also be referenced by other policy types. When null, the policy operates solely based on its own scalar fields and config payload.

IShoppingMallReviewPolicy.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing review and rating policy in the shopping_mall_review_policies table.

Used by platform administrator tools to modify behavior of an already defined review policy, identified externally by its `code`. All fields are optional and represent partial updates; ownership, primary key, and creation timestamps are immutable and managed by the backend.

name.description:
Updated human-readable name of the review policy for admin UIs.

When provided as a non-null string, replaces the existing name. When explicitly set to null, business logic may either clear or reject null names depending on schema constraints; typically, null should be treated as "do not change" in update handlers.

description.description:
Updated free-form description of the review policy.

When provided, replaces the existing description. When explicitly set to null, any existing description is cleared. When omitted, the description remains unchanged.

max_days_after_delivery_for_review.description:
New maximum number of days after delivery during which customers may submit reviews.

When provided as an integer, updates the configured window. When explicitly null, the numeric limit is cleared so that either no explicit limit applies or other configuration determines the behavior. When omitted, the field remains unchanged.

allow_edit_within_days.description:
New number of days after review creation during which editing is allowed.

When provided as an integer, updates the permitted edit window. When explicitly null, any existing edit window configuration is cleared. When omitted, the current value is preserved.

auto_hide_report_threshold.description:
New threshold for automatically hiding reviews based on abuse reports.

When set to an integer, defines how many distinct abuse reports are required before automatic hiding occurs. When explicitly null, the automatic hiding behavior based on report count is disabled. When omitted, the existing threshold is left unchanged.

config_payload.description:
Updated serialized configuration payload for the policy.

Typically JSON text encoding advanced rules. When provided as a string, replaces the existing payload. When explicitly null, clears any previously stored configuration payload. When omitted, the payload remains unchanged.

active.description:
Updated active flag indicating whether the policy should currently be applied.

When provided, toggles the active status of the policy. When explicitly null, business logic may treat it as a request to clear explicit activation or may reject null depending on constraints; commonly, null is interpreted as "no change" and should be avoided unless explicitly supported by the update handler.

effective_from.description:
Updated start timestamp from which the policy becomes effective.

When provided with a date-time string, sets or adjusts the policy’s activation window start. When explicitly null, clears any previously configured start bound. When omitted, the existing value is not changed.

effective_to.description:
Updated end timestamp after which the policy no longer applies to new operations.

When provided, sets or adjusts the policy’s expiration time. When explicitly null, removes any existing end bound. When omitted, the current value is preserved.

shopping_mall_region_setting_id.description:
Updated foreign key referencing a region configuration in `shopping_mall_region_settings`.

When provided with a string, changes or sets the region scope of the policy. When explicitly null, clears any existing region scoping so that the policy is no longer tied to a specific region. When omitted, the region association remains unchanged.

shopping_mall_policy_setting_id.description:
Updated foreign key referencing a shared policy configuration profile in `shopping_mall_policy_settings`.

When provided with a string, links the policy to a different or new policy-setting profile. When explicitly null, clears the association so the policy no longer relies on an external profile. When omitted, the current association is preserved.

IShoppingMallAgeRestrictionPolicy.IReque.description:
Request DTO for querying age restriction policies in the shopping mall platform.

This schema encapsulates search filters, sorting options, and pagination parameters used by platform administrators to retrieve a list of age restriction policy configurations from the shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies table. It supports filtering by business code, name, active state, minimum age range, and effective period, as well as scoping by related catalog or region configuration and standard list controls such as page and limit.

The request is used as the body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/ageRestrictionPolicies endpoint, enabling complex JSON-based search criteria beyond simple query-string parameters. All fields are optional so that callers can combine filters flexibly. The backend translates this DTO into Prisma queries with appropriate WHERE, ORDER BY, and pagination clauses.

page.description: 1-based page index to retrieve when listing age restriction policies. If omitted, the backend SHOULD default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return in a single page of results. The backend SHOULD enforce a sensible upper bound to protect performance.

search.description: Free-text search term applied to human-readable fields such as name or description of the age restriction policies. Intended for quick keyword search in admin tooling.

code.description: Exact or prefix match filter for the business code of the age restriction policy (e.g. "adult_only", "teen_restricted"). This maps conceptually to the code column of shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies.

name.description: Filter for the human-readable name of the age restriction policy. Implementations may treat this as a contains or prefix match depending on search strategy.

isActive.description: If provided, filters policies based on whether they are currently marked active. When true, only active policies should be included. When false, only inactive or retired policies should be returned.

minimumAgeFrom.description: Lower bound (inclusive) for the minimum_age_years field used to filter age restriction policies. When provided together with minimumAgeTo, defines a numeric range.

minimumAgeTo.description: Upper bound (inclusive) for the minimum_age_years field used to filter age restriction policies. When provided together with minimumAgeFrom, defines a numeric range.

requireVerifiedAge.description: Optional filter indicating whether to restrict results to policies that require customers to have a verified age status (true) or those that do not (false).

effectiveFromGte.description: Lower bound (inclusive) filter for the effective_from timestamp of policies. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

effectiveFromLte.description: Upper bound (inclusive) filter for the effective_from timestamp of policies. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

effectiveToGte.description: Lower bound (inclusive) filter for the effective_to timestamp of policies. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

effectiveToLte.description: Upper bound (inclusive) filter for the effective_to timestamp of policies. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

regionSettingCode.description: Optional filter to restrict policies that are associated with a particular region configuration, expressed as the business code of a shopping_mall_region_settings entry when such association exists.

policySettingCode.description: Optional filter to restrict policies linked to a higher-level policy settings profile, expressed as the business code of a shopping_mall_policy_settings record when such association exists.

IShoppingMallAgeRestrictionPolicy.description:
Main response DTO representing an age restriction policy record in the shoppingMall platform.

This type mirrors the shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies Prisma model for read operations and is returned from creation and update endpoints. It exposes public, non-sensitive fields that describe how age-based eligibility is enforced across catalog, checkout, and review flows.

System-managed identifiers and timestamps are included so that admin tools and other services can reason about record identity and lifecycle, while sensitive authentication or internal-only fields are excluded.

id.description:
System-generated unique identifier of the age restriction policy record.

This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies table and is used internally for joins and references.

code.description:
Business identifier for the age restriction policy.

This value, such as "adult_only" or "teen_restricted", is globally unique across all non-deleted policies and is used as the human-readable code in URLs and admin tools.

name.description:
Human-friendly display name for the age restriction policy.

Shown in admin dashboards, configuration listings, and policy detail screens.

oneOf.description:
Long-form description explaining the intent, legal context, and usage guidance of the age restriction policy.

Helps administrators, compliance teams, and auditors understand how and why the policy is applied.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text for the policy.

When null, no additional human-readable description has been provided.

minimum_age_years.description:
Minimum required age in years for customers to access products and categories governed by this policy.

Enforcement logic compares customer age or verified date of birth against this value during visibility, purchase, or review checks.

require_verified_age.description:
Indicates whether customers must have a verified age status on their account to satisfy this policy.

When true, the system must confirm verified identity or equivalent before granting access to governed items.

oneOf.description:
Serialized configuration payload, typically JSON text, that represents complex or region-specific rule sets associated with this policy.

This can encode advanced eligibility conditions that the enforcement engine evaluates at runtime.

config_payload.description:
Optional serialized configuration payload for advanced rule sets.

When null, the policy is enforced solely through standard fields such as minimum_age_years and require_verified_age.

active.description:
Flag indicating whether this age restriction policy is currently active.

Inactive policies remain stored for historical reference but should not be applied to new operations.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp from which this policy becomes effective for new operations.

Stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with explicit offset.

effective_from.description:
Start of the effective period for this policy.

When null, the policy is considered effective immediately from creation.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp after which this policy should no longer be applied to new operations.

Stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with explicit offset.

effective_to.description:
End of the effective period for this policy.

When null, the policy remains in effect until explicitly deactivated or updated.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this age restriction policy record was first created.

Recorded as an ISO 8601 date-time string and used for auditing and historical analysis.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this age restriction policy record was last updated.

Recorded as an ISO 8601 date-time string and updated automatically whenever mutable fields change.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when this age restriction policy record was soft-deleted or logically retired.

Recorded as an ISO 8601 date-time string when the policy is no longer considered active in the system.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete marker for the age restriction policy.

When null, the policy is considered present in the active dataset; when non-null, it is treated as logically deleted or retired.

oneOf.description:
Summary view of the region configuration associated with this age restriction policy.

When present, this indicates that the policy is scoped to a specific regionSetting record in shopping_mall_region_settings, and enforcement should consider that regional context.

Indicates that this age restriction policy is not bound to a specific region setting.

Global or cross-region policies typically have a null regionSetting so they can be applied wherever appropriate.

regionSetting.description:
Associated region configuration summary for this age restriction policy.

This association reflects the nullable foreign key shopping_mall_region_setting_id and provides contextual region information without exposing the raw foreign key identifier.

oneOf.description:
Summary view of the higher-level policy setting profile associated with this age restriction policy.

When present, this links the policy to a shopping_mall_policy_settings record that may define shared configuration parameters across multiple policy types.

Indicates that this age restriction policy does not use a shared higher-level policy setting profile.

Standalone policies with self-contained configuration typically leave this association null.

policySetting.description:
Associated policy setting profile summary for this age restriction policy.

This association reflects the nullable foreign key shopping_mall_policy_setting_id and surfaces shared configuration context without exposing the raw foreign key identifier.

IShoppingMallAgeRestrictionPolicy.ICreat.description:
Request DTO for creating a new age restriction policy in the shoppingMall platform.

This structure captures business-level fields that define how age and eligibility restrictions are applied to products and categories, including business code, display name, minimum required age, flags controlling whether verified age is required, optional serialized configuration payload, effective period, and optional associations to region and policy setting records.

It intentionally excludes system-managed fields such as id and timestamps, which are generated by the backend, and any actor identity fields, which are inferred from the authenticated platform admin context.

code.description:
Business identifier for the age restriction policy.

This value is used as a stable, human-readable code such as "adult_only" or "teen_restricted" and must be unique across all non-deleted policies in the shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies table.

name.description:
Human-friendly display name for the age restriction policy.

This is shown in admin and policy management tools so that platform administrators can easily identify the policy in lists and detail views.

description.description:
Optional long-form description explaining the intent, legal context, and usage guidance of the age restriction policy.

Admins can use this field to document compliance rationales, links to internal policies, and notes about how and where the policy should be applied.

minimum_age_years.description:
Minimum required age in years for customers to access products and categories governed by this policy.

Must be a non-negative integer and should fall within a reasonable age range as required by business and legal constraints.

require_verified_age.description:
Flag indicating whether customers must have a verified age status on their account to satisfy this policy.

When true, enforcement logic will require evidence such as verified ID checks; when false, eligibility can be determined from self-reported or inferred age alone.

config_payload.description:
Optional serialized configuration payload, typically JSON text, that defines complex or region-specific rule sets for the policy.

This can include additional conditions based on regions, risk scores, or multi-step verification flows that the enforcement engine interprets at runtime.

active.description:
Indicates whether the age restriction policy is currently active.

Inactive policies are stored for reference and historical purposes but should not be applied to new catalog, checkout, or review operations.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp from which this policy becomes effective for new operations.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with explicit offset.

effective_from.description:
Start of the period during which this policy is considered effective.

When null, the policy is effective immediately upon creation.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp after which this policy should no longer be applied to new operations.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with explicit offset.

effective_to.description:
End of the period during which this policy is considered effective.

When null, the policy remains in effect indefinitely until explicitly deactivated or updated.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the region setting record to associate with this age restriction policy.

When provided, this must reference an existing row in shopping_mall_region_settings and scopes the policy to that regional configuration. Leave null to create a global or cross-region policy.

region_setting_id.description:
Optional foreign key identifier linking this age restriction policy to a region setting.

This corresponds to the nullable shopping_mall_region_setting_id column in the underlying Prisma model and allows the policy to be scoped to a specific region when needed.

oneOf.description:
Identifier of the policy setting profile to associate with this age restriction policy.

When provided, this must reference an existing row in shopping_mall_policy_settings and allows shared configuration parameters to be reused across multiple policy records.

policy_setting_id.description:
Optional foreign key identifier linking this age restriction policy to a higher-level policy setting profile.

This corresponds to the nullable shopping_mall_policy_setting_id column in the underlying Prisma model and allows the policy to participate in shared configuration profiles when appropriate.

IShoppingMallAgeRestrictionPolicy.IUpdat.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing age restriction policy in the shoppingMall platform.

This structure allows platform administrators to modify mutable business fields of a policy identified by its unique business code in the URL path. All properties are optional to support partial updates, and system-managed fields such as id and timestamps are intentionally excluded.

Ownership and identity information are not present, as authorization is derived from the authenticated platform admin context.

name.description:
Updated human-friendly display name for the age restriction policy.

If provided, this replaces the existing name shown in admin and policy management tools.

description.description:
Updated long-form description for the age restriction policy.

Can be used to record new compliance notes, documentation links, or clarifications about how the policy should be applied.

minimum_age_years.description:
Updated minimum required age in years for customers to access products and categories governed by this policy.

Must remain a non-negative integer and adhere to business and legal constraints.

require_verified_age.description:
Updated flag indicating whether customers must have a verified age status on their account to satisfy this policy.

Changing this value alters whether enforcement logic requires strong age verification evidence.

config_payload.description:
Updated serialized configuration payload, typically JSON text, that defines complex or region-specific rule sets.

If provided, this replaces the existing configuration used by the enforcement engine at runtime.

active.description:
Updated active state of the age restriction policy.

When set to false, the policy is considered inactive and should not be applied to new operations, though existing historical references remain valid.

oneOf.description:
New timestamp from which this policy becomes effective for new operations.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with explicit offset.

effective_from.description:
Updated start of the period during which this policy is considered effective.

Setting this to null makes the policy effective immediately, overriding any previously scheduled start.

oneOf.description:
New timestamp after which this policy should no longer be applied to new operations.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with explicit offset.

effective_to.description:
Updated end of the period during which this policy is considered effective.

Setting this to null removes any previously configured end date so the policy remains in effect until further changes.

oneOf.description:
Updated identifier of the region setting record to associate with this age restriction policy.

When provided, this must reference an existing row in shopping_mall_region_settings and will change or establish the regional scope of the policy.

region_setting_id.description:
Optional updated foreign key identifier linking this age restriction policy to a region setting.

Set to null to clear any existing regional association and make the policy global or cross-region; omit the field to leave the current association unchanged.

oneOf.description:
Updated identifier of the policy setting profile to associate with this age restriction policy.

When provided, this must reference an existing row in shopping_mall_policy_settings and will change or establish the shared configuration profile for the policy.

policy_setting_id.description:
Optional updated foreign key identifier linking this age restriction policy to a higher-level policy setting profile.

Set to null to remove any existing profile association; omit the field to keep the current association as-is.

IShoppingMallRegionSetting.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying region configuration entries in the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO is consumed by the `PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/regionSettings` endpoint and follows the same logical semantics as the platform’s standard pagination request (`IPage.IRequest`): it carries the current page index (`page`) and the page size (`limit`) together with optional filter and sort criteria. Unlike the generic `IPage.IRequest` schema, the fields are inlined here to keep the request type self-contained for region settings.

All parameters are read-only filters and controls; the operation is strictly read-only and does not modify any state in the underlying `shopping_mall_region_settings` Prisma model. When omitted, the server is expected to apply sensible defaults for pagination and sorting, and to interpret null or absent filters as "no restriction" for that dimension.

page.description:
1-based index of the page of region settings to retrieve, representing the **current page number**.

This plays the same role as the `current` field in the generic pagination schema (`IPage.IPagination.current`). It must be a positive integer. When omitted, the server should default to the first page (typically `1`) and use `limit` (or its default) to compute the offset into the `shopping_mall_region_settings` result set.

limit.description:
Maximum number of region setting summaries to return in a single page.

This field has the same semantics as `limit` in `IPage.IPagination`: it defines the page size. It must be a positive integer within server-defined bounds (for example, a minimum of 1 and a maximum such as 100). When omitted, the implementation should fall back to a safe default page size, and this value is used together with `page` to compute pagination.

search.description:
Free-text search keyword applied to region configuration fields such as `code` or `name`.

Implementations may apply this term to one or more columns in the `shopping_mall_region_settings` table (for example, `code`, `name`, or localized labels) using `LIKE`, full-text search, or other text-search mechanisms depending on database capabilities.

regionCodes.description:
Optional list of region business codes to filter by.

Each value in this array must correspond to the `code` column in the `shopping_mall_region_settings` Prisma model. When provided, only regions whose `code` is included in this collection should be returned.

active.description:
Filter flag indicating whether to restrict results to active or inactive regions.

When set to `true`, only regions with `active = true` in `shopping_mall_region_settings` should be returned. When set to `false`, only regions with `active = false` should be returned. When omitted, both active and inactive regions may be included according to business rules or default filters.

isoCountryCode.description:
Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to filter regions by.

This filter maps directly to the `iso_country_code` column in the `shopping_mall_region_settings` Prisma model. Typical values include two-letter uppercase strings such as `"US"`, `"KR"`, or `"JP"`. When provided, results should be limited to regions whose `iso_country_code` matches the given value.

currencyCode.description:
Optional ISO 4217 currency code to filter regions by.

This filter maps directly to the `currency_code` column of `shopping_mall_region_settings`. Examples include `"USD"`, `"KRW"`, or `"EUR"`. When specified, only regions whose `currency_code` matches the provided value should be returned.

timezone.description:
Optional IANA timezone identifier used to filter regions.

This filter corresponds to the `timezone` column in `shopping_mall_region_settings`. Typical values include strings such as `"Asia/Seoul"` or `"America/New_York"`. When provided, the result set should be restricted to regions configured with that representative timezone.

orderBy.description:
Optional field name to sort region setting summaries by.

Clients should supply values that the server recognizes as sortable fields, typically aligned with the entity’s column names or well-known aliases such as `"code"`, `"name"`, or `"created_at"`. Implementations should validate the supplied value against an allowed whitelist and fall back to a default ordering when it is missing or invalid.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction for the ordered result set.

Accepts values like `"asc"` for ascending or `"desc"` for descending order. When omitted, implementations should default to ascending order or to a service-defined default. The allowed values and behavior should mirror the sort-direction conventions used across other search endpoints in the platform.

IShoppingMallRegionSetting.description:
Detailed region configuration entity for the ShoppingMall platform backed by the shopping_mall_region_settings Prisma model.

Represents a single region configuration entry that groups markets or geographic areas such as individual countries (for example, "US", "KR") or business-defined segments (for example, "EU_MARKET"). Each record stores a unique business code along with human-readable labels and optional metadata used by other subsystems such as payment, fulfillment, and policy engines.

This DTO is used by administrative and internal tooling to inspect the full configuration for a region. It exposes only non-sensitive, business-facing fields from the underlying Prisma model, including timestamps used for audit and operational visibility.

id.description:
System-generated UUID primary key of the region configuration entry.

This value is assigned by the database when the record is created and never changes afterward. It is not used as the primary identifier in external APIs, which instead rely on the unique business code.

code.description:
Unique business identifier code for the region.

Typically corresponds to values such as ISO country codes ("US", "KR") or platform-defined region identifiers like "EU_MARKET". The Prisma model enforces a uniqueness constraint on this field, and API paths such as `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/regionSettings/{regionCode}` use it as the external key.

name.description:
Human-readable name or label for the region.

Examples include "United States", "Korea", or "European Union". This value is intended for display in administrative UIs and logs.

iso_country_code.description:
Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code associated with the region.

When present, it should be a two-letter uppercase string such as "US" or "KR" that maps the logical region to a canonical country code. When null, the region may represent a composite market or a non-country-specific grouping.

currency_code.description:
Optional ISO 4217 currency code configured as the default for this region.

Common examples include "USD" for US dollars, "KRW" for Korean won, or "EUR" for euros. When null, downstream systems must determine currency through other configuration sources.

timezone.description:
Optional representative IANA timezone identifier for the region.

This is used for time-based calculations such as cancellation windows or business-day computations. Examples include "Asia/Seoul" or "America/New_York". When null, timezone-dependent logic must rely on alternative configuration.

active.description:
Indicates whether the region is currently active in the ShoppingMall platform.

When true, the region may participate in catalog visibility, ordering, and other workflows. When false, the region is considered inactive and may be excluded from user-facing operations while remaining available for historical and audit purposes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the region configuration entry was first created.

Stored in UTC and represented in ISO 8601 date-time format. This field is managed by the backend and is read-only to API clients.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this region configuration entry.

Stored in UTC and represented in ISO 8601 date-time format. Automatically updated by the backend whenever mutable fields are changed.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-deletion timestamp marking when the region was logically retired.

When null, the region is considered not deleted. When set to a date-time value, the region is treated as retired for most business flows but preserved for audit and historical referencing.

IShoppingMallRegionSetting.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new shopping mall region configuration entry in the shopping_mall_region_settings table.

This DTO is used by platform administrators or configuration tools to define a new logical region identified by a unique business code and a human-readable name. Optional metadata such as ISO country code, currency code, and timezone can be supplied to influence downstream policy behavior. Server-managed fields like id and timestamps are excluded from this schema.

code.description:
Unique business identifier code of the region.

Typically uses ISO country codes like "US" or "KR" or platform-defined identifiers such as "EU_MARKET". Must be unique across all region settings and is used as the primary external identifier in APIs and configurations.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the region.

Examples include "United States", "Korea", or "European Union". Used in admin UIs and logs to clearly describe the region represented by this configuration entry.

iso_country_code.description:
Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code mapped to this region.

When provided, this code can be used by external systems and reporting tools that expect standard country identifiers. May be null when the region covers multiple countries or is a custom market segment.

currency_code.description:
Optional default ISO 4217 currency code associated with this region.

Examples include "USD", "KRW", or "EUR". When set, it can be used as a default currency for pricing, payment, and reporting within this region. May be null when the region does not enforce a single default currency.

timezone.description:
Optional representative timezone identifier for the region, such as an IANA timezone string.

Common examples are "America/New_York" or "Asia/Seoul". This value is used by time-based policies (such as cancellation or refund windows) that need a canonical timezone for calculations. May be null when the region does not require a single canonical timezone.

active.description:
Flag indicating whether this region configuration is currently active.

Active regions can be referenced by policies and may be exposed in administrative user interfaces. Inactive regions are effectively disabled for new business operations but may still exist for historical reference.

IShoppingMallRegionSetting.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing shopping mall region configuration entry in the shopping_mall_region_settings table.

This DTO is used by platform administrators or configuration tools to modify attributes of a region identified by its unique business code in the request path. Only mutable business fields are exposed; server-managed fields such as id and timestamps are excluded and maintained by the backend.

name.description:
Updated human-readable name of the region.

If provided, replaces the existing name shown in administrative tools and logs for this region.

iso_country_code.description:
Updated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code associated with this region.

Set to a non-null string to change the mapped country code, or explicitly set to null to clear the mapping when the region represents multiple countries or a custom market segment.

currency_code.description:
Updated default ISO 4217 currency code for this region.

Set to a non-null string such as "USD", "KRW", or "EUR" to change the default currency, or explicitly set to null to remove the default currency association.

timezone.description:
Updated representative timezone identifier for this region, typically an IANA timezone string.

Set to a non-null string such as "America/New_York" or "Asia/Seoul" to change the canonical timezone used in time-based policy calculations, or explicitly set to null to remove the assigned timezone.

active.description:
Updated activation flag for the region configuration.

Set to true to mark the region as active for new business operations or false to disable it while keeping the record for historical and policy reference.

IShoppingMallShippingZoneSetting.IReques.description:
Search and filter payload for querying shopping mall shipping zone configuration entries.

Used by platform administrators to request a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of records from the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings table via the PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/shippingZoneSettings endpoint. This DTO expresses complex search criteria in a structured JSON body instead of query parameters.

page.description: Page number to retrieve for the paginated result set. Starts from 1. Used together with pageSize to control pagination when listing shipping zone settings.

pageSize.description:
Number of records to include per page in the paginated result set. Used together with page to control pagination when listing shipping zone settings.

Service implementations may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

search.description:
Free-text search keyword applied to human-readable fields such as shipping zone name or description.

Useful for admin operators quickly locating zones by partial name or description fragments.

code.description: Exact business code of a shipping zone to filter by. Maps to the `code` column on the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings Prisma model (for example, "DOMESTIC", "EU_ZONE", or "GLOBAL").

name.description:
Filter for shipping zones whose human-readable name matches or partially matches the provided value.

Typically applied with case-insensitive match semantics by the service implementation.

active.description:
Optional filter indicating whether to restrict results to zones based on their activation status.

When true, only active zones are returned. When false, only inactive or retired zones are returned. When omitted, both active and inactive zones may be included, depending on service rules.

regionCode.description:
Optional filter to include only zones that are associated with a particular region code.

Typically corresponds to a business code or identifier on the related shopping_mall_region_settings entity.

oneOf.description:
Field name to sort results by when returning paginated shipping zone settings.

Common values include "code", "name", or timestamp fields such as "created_at" or "updated_at". The service must validate and whitelist allowed sort fields.
