IShoppingMallShippingZoneSetting.description:
Read model for a shipping zone configuration record stored in the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings table.

This DTO represents the complete persisted state of a shipping zone as used by logistics, fulfillment, and pricing subsystems. It exposes the unique business code along with display metadata, activation state, and an association to a primary region configuration through a lightweight summary object.

Sensitive or authentication-related fields are not present on this entity. It is safe to return in administrative configuration APIs that are restricted to platform administrator actors.

id.description:
System-generated UUID primary key for the shipping zone configuration record.

This identifier is unique across all shipping zones and is used internally by the database and service layer.

code.description:
Business-meaningful unique code for the shipping zone.

This is the primary business identifier used in logistics, rate configuration, and API paths such as `shippingZoneCode`. The value is constrained by a unique index in the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings table and cannot collide with other zones.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the shipping zone used in admin tools and configuration screens.

Examples include `Domestic Shipping`, `EU Zone`, or `Global Shipping`.

oneOf.description:
Optional descriptive text explaining which regions or countries are covered by this shipping zone and how it participates in shipping rate calculations.

This variant is used when a human-readable explanation has been provided for internal operators.

Indicates that no descriptive documentation has been stored for this shipping zone.

Admin tools may render this as an empty or placeholder description.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text explaining which regions or countries are covered by this shipping zone and how it participates in shipping rate calculations.

May be null when no additional documentation has been provided for this zone.

primaryRegion.description:
Lightweight summary of the primary region configuration associated with this shipping zone.

This association is backed by the `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` foreign key in the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings Prisma model and provides region context (such as region code and name) without exposing low-level database identifiers directly in the shipping zone DTO.

active.description:
Flag indicating whether this shipping zone is active and available for use.

When true, the zone can be used by fulfillment and pricing logic to determine applicable shipping methods and rates. When false, the zone is considered disabled or retired and should not be used for new calculations, though historical data may still reference it.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this shipping zone configuration record was created.

Set automatically by the backend at insertion time and never modified afterward, this value is useful for auditing and understanding configuration history.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this shipping zone configuration record was last updated.

Automatically refreshed by the backend whenever mutable fields on the record are changed, enabling operators to track recent configuration activity.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when this shipping zone was soft-deleted or retired from active use.

Implementations may use this field to hide retired zones from normal listings while preserving them for historical and referential integrity purposes.

Indicates that this shipping zone has not been soft-deleted or retired.

Active zones typically have a null deleted_at value and may still be used for new logistics and pricing configurations.

deleted_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when this shipping zone was soft-deleted or retired from active use.

When null, the zone is considered not deleted. When non-null, the zone may be treated as retired or inactive by business logic, depending on platform rules.

IShoppingMallShippingZoneSetting.ICreate.description:
DTO schema for creating a new shipping zone configuration record in the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings table.

This request body is used by platform administrators or configuration services to define a new logistics shipping zone that groups geographic regions for shipping methods, rates, and constraints. It captures the business code identifier and core configuration fields required at creation time.

Actor identity (platform administrator) is derived from authentication context and is never included here. System-managed fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are also excluded from this DTO and are populated by the backend.

code.description:
Business-meaningful unique code for the shipping zone.

This value maps to the `code` field of the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings model and is constrained by a unique index. Examples are values like `DOMESTIC`, `EU_ZONE`, or `GLOBAL`. The implementation must ensure that this code does not collide with any existing shipping zone code, including retired zones if business rules forbid reuse.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the shipping zone used in admin tools and configuration screens.

This is typically a localized or descriptive label such as `Domestic Shipping`, `European Union Zone`, or `Global Shipping` that is suitable for display to operators managing logistics configuration.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text explaining which regions or countries are covered by this shipping zone and how it participates in shipping rate calculations.

This text is meant for internal documentation in admin tools so that operators can understand the intent and scope of the zone.

active.description:
Flag indicating whether this shipping zone is active and available for use.

This property maps directly to the `active` field of the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings Prisma model. When true, the zone can be used by fulfillment and pricing logic to determine applicable shipping methods and rates. When false, the zone is considered disabled or retired and should not be used for new calculations, though historical data may still reference it.

shopping_mall_region_setting_id.description:
Optional foreign key identifier referencing a primary region configuration entry in the shopping_mall_region_settings table.

When provided, this ties the shipping zone to a primary region definition that may represent a market, country group, or other geographic scope used by the platform. The referenced region configuration must exist for the value to be valid.

IShoppingMallShippingZoneSetting.IUpdate.description:
DTO schema for updating an existing shipping zone configuration record in the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings table.

This request body is used by platform administrators or internal tools to change properties of a shipping zone, such as its display name, description, activation state, or associated primary region setting. The target zone is identified exclusively by its business code path parameter (shippingZoneCode), not by any identifier field inside this DTO.

Creation metadata (id, created_at, created_by) and ownership remain immutable and are not exposed here. System-managed fields like updated_at are automatically refreshed by the backend implementation.

name.description:
Optional new human-readable name of the shipping zone.

When provided, this updates the display label used in admin tools and configuration screens for the zone.

description.description:
Optional new descriptive text describing coverage and usage of the shipping zone.

If set to a non-empty string, it replaces the existing description. If set explicitly to null, it clears any existing description depending on backend semantics.

active.description:
Optional updated activation flag indicating whether this shipping zone is active.

This property maps directly to the `active` field of the shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings Prisma model. When set, this toggles whether the zone is available for use by fulfillment and pricing logic. If omitted, the current activation state is preserved.

shopping_mall_region_setting_id.description:
Optional updated foreign key identifier referencing a primary region configuration entry in the shopping_mall_region_settings table.

When provided, this changes which primary region configuration is associated with the shipping zone. The referenced region must exist for the update to be valid. If set to null, any existing association may be cleared depending on business rules.

IShoppingMallCategoryTree.IRequest.description:
Request body schema for searching and paginating category tree definitions in the shoppingMall catalog.

Encapsulates filter criteria, full-text search parameters, and pagination/sorting options when querying the `shopping_mall_category_trees` Prisma model. Used by platform admin tools to retrieve a list of category tree summaries for configuration and management tasks.

search.description:
Free-text search keyword applied to category tree business code, name, or description.

Backends typically apply this to a combination of fields such as `code`, `name`, and `description` in the `shopping_mall_category_trees` table using LIKE or full-text search mechanisms.

codes.description:
Optional list of specific category tree business codes to include in the result set.

When provided, the query should only return trees whose `code` matches one of the given entries.

defaultLocales.description:
Optional list of default locale values to filter category trees by.

Each value should correspond to the `default_locale` column (for example, `"en-US"`, `"ko-KR"`) in `shopping_mall_category_trees`.

active.description:
Filter by active flag state.

- `true`: Only active category trees
- `false`: Only inactive category trees
- `null`: Do not filter by active flag (include both active and inactive)

Corresponds to the `active` column in `shopping_mall_category_trees` if present.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the category tree creation timestamp filter.

Only trees with `created_at` greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value will be returned when provided.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the category tree creation timestamp filter.

Only trees with `created_at` less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value will be returned when provided.

updatedFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the last update timestamp filter.

Only trees with `updated_at` greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value will be returned when provided.

updatedTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the last update timestamp filter.

Only trees with `updated_at` less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value will be returned when provided.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

Must be a positive integer where 1 represents the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page.

Backends should enforce an upper bound to avoid excessive result sizes.

orderBy.description:
Field name used for sorting the result set of category trees.

Typical values may include `"code"`, `"name"`, `"default_locale"`, `"created_at"`, or `"updated_at"`, depending on what columns exist in `shopping_mall_category_trees`.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction for the ordered result set.

Expected values are `"asc"` for ascending or `"desc"` for descending ordering, applied to the column indicated by `orderBy`.

IShoppingMallCategoryTree.description:
Detailed representation of a category tree configuration in the shoppingMall catalog.

Maps to a row in the `shopping_mall_category_trees` Prisma model and is used primarily in administrative APIs for platform operators. Contains the tree's stable business code, human-readable metadata, locale and activation information, and lifecycle timestamps.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the category tree record.

Typically corresponds to the primary key column (often a UUID string) of the `shopping_mall_category_trees` table.

code.description:
Globally unique business identifier for the category tree.

Used as a stable external reference in admin tools, integration code, and API paths such as `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/categoryTrees/{categoryTreeCode}`. Corresponds to the `code` column in `shopping_mall_category_trees` and is usually protected by a unique constraint.

name.description:
Human-readable display name for the category tree.

Shown in administrative user interfaces to help operators identify and select a tree (for example, `"Main Catalog"`, `"EU Regional Tree"`).

description.description:
Long-form descriptive text explaining the purpose, scope, and usage of this category tree.

Optional field that may be null when no description has been provided.

defaultLocale.description:
Default locale code associated with this category tree.

Represents the base language/region for category labels (for example, `"en-US"`, `"ko-KR"`) and typically maps to a `default_locale` column in `shopping_mall_category_trees`.

active.description:
Indicates whether this category tree is currently active and available for use in the catalog.

When `true`, the tree may be used for navigation and product classification depending on business rules. When `false`, the tree is typically considered inactive or archived.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp representing when the category tree record was first created.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string and typically mapped from the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_category_trees`.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp representing the most recent update to the category tree record.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string and typically mapped from the `updated_at` column of `shopping_mall_category_trees`.

IShoppingMallCategoryTree.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new category tree configuration in the shoppingMall catalog domain.

This DTO maps directly to the Prisma model `shopping_mall_category_trees` via `x-autobe-prisma-schema` and therefore only exposes fields that correspond to real columns in that model. System-managed fields such as the primary key identifier and lifecycle timestamps are excluded from the request body and are populated by the backend.

The `code` field acts as a globally unique business identifier for the tree, while `name` and `description` provide human-readable metadata for administrative users. Optional configuration fields such as `active` and `defaultLocale` allow a platform administrator to control activation state and default language behavior when organizing products in the catalog.

code.description:
Globally unique business identifier code for this category tree.

This value is used as an external reference in admin tools, integrations, and URL parameters (for example, as `{categoryTreeCode}`). It must be unique across all rows in `shopping_mall_category_trees` and is expected to remain stable for the lifetime of the tree so that other entities can safely reference it.

name.description:
Primary human-readable display name of the category tree.

This value is shown in administrative UIs and configuration screens and represents the main label for this tree configuration, such as "Main Catalog" or "EU Regional Tree".

description.description:
Optional descriptive text explaining the purpose, scope, or internal documentation for this category tree.

This field is intended for admins and internal stakeholders rather than end customers and typically mirrors the nullable `description` column in the `shopping_mall_category_trees` model.

active.description:
Indicates whether this category tree is currently active and eligible to be used for catalog navigation and product classification.

When `true`, the tree may be used for storefront navigation according to business rules. When `false`, the tree can be retained for configuration or historical purposes but omitted from active catalog routing. This property maps directly to the non-nullable `active` column in `shopping_mall_category_trees`.

defaultLocale.description:
Optional default locale identifier associated with this category tree.

Typical values follow BCP 47 language tags such as `"en-US"` or `"ko-KR"`. This property corresponds to the nullable `default_locale` column in `shopping_mall_category_trees` and is used by admin tools and storefronts to determine language settings for category labels and metadata when a more specific locale is not provided.

IShoppingMallCategoryTree.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing category tree configuration in the shoppingMall catalog domain.

This DTO maps directly to the Prisma model `shopping_mall_category_trees` via `x-autobe-prisma-schema` and therefore only includes fields that correspond to real, mutable columns in that model. Immutable identifiers such as the primary key and the business `code` are not exposed in this structure; the target tree is identified by the `{categoryTreeCode}` path parameter.

All properties are optional so that administrators can submit partial updates to specific configuration attributes, such as the display name, description, activation flag, or default locale, without being required to resend the full current state.

name.description:
Updated human-readable display name of the category tree.

If provided, this value replaces the existing `name` stored in `shopping_mall_category_trees` and will be reflected in administrative UIs and configuration screens.

description.description:
Updated descriptive text describing the purpose or internal documentation of this category tree.

If omitted, the current `description` value in the `shopping_mall_category_trees` record remains unchanged.

active.description:
Optional flag used to activate or deactivate this category tree.

When supplied, the value updates the `active` column in `shopping_mall_category_trees`. Setting it to `true` marks the tree as available for use in catalog navigation, while `false` can be used to hide or retire the tree without deleting it.

defaultLocale.description:
Updated default locale identifier used by this category tree.

If provided, this value overwrites the existing `default_locale` column in `shopping_mall_category_trees`. Typical values are language/region tags such as `"en-US"` or `"ko-KR"` and are used to determine fallback language behavior for category labels and metadata.

IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for shopping mall catalog categories.

This object encapsulates pagination, sorting, and rich filter criteria used when searching categories in the `shopping_mall_categories` table. It is used by PATCH-based search endpoints for both tree-scoped category listing and global category search, where complex criteria no longer fit comfortably into query-string parameters.

Implementations are expected to apply sensible defaults for pagination and sorting, to validate filter combinations against business rules and the underlying Prisma models (`shopping_mall_category_trees` and `shopping_mall_categories`), and to return clear validation errors when callers provide unsupported or inconsistent criteria.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated category search results.

When omitted, the backend should default this value to `1`. Values less than `1` are considered invalid and should fail validation or be normalized according to platform-wide pagination rules. Together with `limit`, this field determines which slice of the total result set is returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of category records to return in a single page of results.

If not specified, the backend should apply a reasonable default page size and enforce an upper bound (for example, 100 or 200) to protect the system from excessively large responses. Callers can tune this value to balance response size and number of round-trips needed to process a large catalog.

sortKey.description:
Logical sort key that determines how categories are ordered in the result set.

Typical values include business fields such as `name`, `displayOrder`, or tree-specific ordering columns. The exact set of supported values is defined by the implementation and may be documented separately; the backend must validate the incoming `sortKey` and return a clear error if an unsupported key is provided.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction applied to the selected `sortKey`.

Common values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the backend should apply a consistent default per `sortKey` (often ascending). Implementations should normalize and validate this field to avoid silent misinterpretation of unrecognized values.

keyword.description:
Free-text search keyword used to match categories by name, code, or other indexed text fields.

Backends typically implement this filter using case-insensitive matching or full-text search over columns such as `name`, `code`, and potentially `description`. It can be combined with structural filters like `treeCode` and `parentCategoryCode` to narrow the search while still supporting keyword-based discovery.

treeCode.description:
Optional filter that restricts the search to categories belonging to a single category tree.

The value must match the `code` column of a record in the `shopping_mall_category_trees` Prisma model. When provided, only categories whose foreign key points to that tree are eligible for inclusion in the results. When omitted, the search may span categories across all trees, subject to other filters and the caller’s authorization context.

parentCategoryCode.description:
Optional filter restricting results to categories whose parent category code matches the given value within the same tree.

This is a business-level projection of the `parent_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_categories` table. When combined with `treeCode`, it allows callers to list only the immediate children of a particular category or to isolate a specific subtree without retrieving the entire tree hierarchy.

minDepth.description:
Optional lower bound for the depth of categories in the hierarchy.

The `depth` semantics mirror those of the `depth` property in `IShoppingMallCategory`. Using `minDepth` allows callers to exclude nodes above a certain level—for example, to focus on leaf-level categories or deep subtrees without including higher-level structural nodes.

maxDepth.description:
Optional upper bound for the depth of categories in the hierarchy.

As with `minDepth`, this field uses the same definition of `depth` as `IShoppingMallCategory`. Providing `maxDepth` enables callers to restrict results to top-level or mid-level categories, which is useful for building navigation menus or high-level overviews without traversing every node in the tree.

isActive.description:
Optional tri-state filter that restricts categories based on their active status.

When set to `true`, only categories with the underlying `active` column equal to `true` are returned. When set to `false`, only inactive categories are included. When set to `null` or omitted, no filtering on the `active` flag is performed and both active and inactive categories may appear in the results, subject to other constraints and default visibility rules.

IShoppingMallCategory.description:
Detailed DTO for a single shopping mall catalog category.

Represents a category node stored in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma table, scoped to a parent category tree defined in `shopping_mall_category_trees`. This object is returned by category detail endpoints and by creation/update operations, and it is designed for administrative UIs and catalog-management tooling that need full visibility into the category’s structure and lifecycle.

In addition to business identifiers (`treeCode`, `code`, `slug`) and human-readable fields (`name`, `description`), the DTO exposes structural information such as `depth`, `parentCategoryCode`, and `isLeaf`, along with audit timestamps (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `deletedAt`) that reflect how the record evolves over time in the database.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the category node.

This value corresponds directly to the primary key `id` column of the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. It is generated when the category row is created and remains stable throughout the record’s lifetime.

Internal services and cross-entity references should rely on this field when a durable, opaque identifier is required, instead of depending solely on business codes or slugs that might change as the catalog is refactored.

treeCode.description:
Business identifier code of the category tree that owns this category.

In the database, the category row stores a foreign key `shopping_mall_category_tree_id` pointing to a record in `shopping_mall_category_trees`. The `treeCode` field projects that association by exposing the referenced tree’s `code` column.

Together, `treeCode` and `code` form a composite business key that uniquely identifies the category within the global catalog and is suitable for use in URLs, imports, and configuration files.

code.description:
Business identifier code of the category within its parent category tree.

This value is stored in the non-nullable `code` column of `shopping_mall_categories` and is unique within a single tree. It is commonly used in API path parameters and admin tools to reference categories in a human-readable way.

When combined with `treeCode`, this field aligns with composite uniqueness constraints such as `@@unique([shopping_mall_category_tree_id, code])` configured in the Prisma model.

slug.description:
URL-friendly slug used when constructing SEO-optimized category URLs.

The slug is backed by the non-nullable `slug` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` table. Within a given tree, slugs are expected to be unique, allowing the frontend to construct stable, readable category paths without exposing internal identifiers.

Even though the slug may change when category names change, clients should treat it as a stable, server-controlled identifier and avoid deriving or guessing slugs on their own.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the category.

This value is taken from the non-nullable `name` column of the `shopping_mall_categories` table and appears in navigation menus, breadcrumb trails, filters, and various administrative screens.

The platform’s validation rules should ensure that the name is meaningful and not empty, while localization and translation concerns are handled by higher-level mechanisms outside this DTO.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text that explains the scope or purpose of the category.

This property corresponds to the nullable `description` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. Many categories, especially structural ones, may omit this field entirely, while marketing-oriented or landing-page categories may include longer descriptive copy.

Clients must handle the possibility that this field is null or absent and avoid assuming that all categories have rich descriptions when rendering catalog pages.

depth.description:
Depth level of the category within its tree hierarchy.

This value is conceptually derived from the chain of parent relationships (for example, via repeated `parent_id` hops) rather than stored in a dedicated column. Root categories typically have the smallest depth (such as 0 or 1, depending on implementation), and each successive generation of children increments the depth by one.

User interfaces can use `depth` to render indented tree views or to filter categories to a specific hierarchy level without recomputing the structure client-side.

parentCategoryCode.description:
Business code of the parent category within the same category tree, or null if this category is a root node.

In the database, the category may hold a `parent_id` foreign key referencing another row in `shopping_mall_categories`. This DTO exposes the relationship by providing the parent’s `code` instead of the raw UUID and assumes that the parent’s `treeCode` matches this category’s `treeCode`.

A null value indicates that the category sits at the top level of the tree and has no parent category.

displayOrder.description:
Ordering index controlling the position of this category among its siblings under the same parent.

This field maps to the non-nullable `display_order` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. Categories with lower `displayOrder` values typically appear earlier in navigation menus and lists, while higher values appear later.

Administrative UIs may expose this as a simple numeric field or as a drag-and-drop sort handle; the backend stores the resulting order in this property.

isLeaf.description:
Flag indicating whether this category is treated as a leaf node in the hierarchy.

This value is backed by the non-nullable `is_leaf` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` table. While the database does not necessarily forbid creating children under a leaf-marked category, the flag acts as a structural hint for user interfaces and business logic.

For example, product-assignment flows may restrict or prioritize categories where `isLeaf` is true, and navigation components may suppress expand/collapse affordances for such nodes to keep the UI clean.

isActive.description:
Indicates whether the category is currently active and should be considered in catalog navigation, search, and product assignment.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable `active` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. When `true`, the category is visible and usable in normal storefront flows. When `false`, the category is logically disabled and may be hidden from customers while remaining accessible in administrative tools and historical references.

Platform administrators can use this flag to temporarily hide categories or deprecate segments of the taxonomy without physically deleting the underlying records.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this category record was created.

The value is taken from the non-nullable `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model and is typically set automatically by the database or ORM at insert time.

Clients can use `createdAt` for audit trails, reporting, and synchronization logic. It is considered read-only from the perspective of API consumers and should not be provided in create or update request bodies.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this category record was last updated.

This field mirrors the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_categories` and is refreshed automatically whenever the row is modified. It allows clients to detect changes over time and to implement cache invalidation or optimistic concurrency controls if needed.

Like `createdAt`, this property is managed by the system and is not intended to be edited directly through client-facing APIs.

deletedAt.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the category record, if it has been logically removed.

The value corresponds to the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. When `deletedAt` is non-null, the category is considered retired from active use, even though the database row remains available for audit trails, historical queries, and administrative review.

Standard catalog and navigation endpoints should typically exclude categories with a non-null `deletedAt`, unless they are specifically designed to expose archived data to administrators or reporting tools.

IShoppingMallCategory.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new category node within a specific category tree in the shoppingMall catalog.

This DTO captures business-level fields that are explicitly provided by the client when inserting a record into the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. The target category tree is determined by the `categoryTreeCode` path parameter in the endpoint and therefore is NOT included as a field in this schema; the server resolves `categoryTreeCode` to the non-nullable `shopping_mall_category_tree_id` foreign key.

Non-nullable Prisma columns that are not exposed as request fields, such as `slug`, `is_leaf`, and timestamp columns (for example, `created_at` and `updated_at`), are derived and populated by the server. In particular, the `slug` column is typically generated from the provided `name` or `code`, and `is_leaf` is inferred from catalog-building rules and whether the category is intended to have children. This means clients are only responsible for supplying `code`, `name`, `active` (via `isActive`), and any optional presentation or hierarchy hints, while the service ensures Prisma-level completeness and integrity.

The combination of the resolved category tree and the category's own `code` is expected to be unique, matching a composite uniqueness constraint such as `@@unique([shopping_mall_category_tree_id, code])` in the database schema. The server validates this uniqueness and enforces parent-child relationships using the internally stored identifiers.

code.description:
Business identifier code of the category, unique within a given category tree.

This value maps directly to the non-nullable `code` column on the `shopping_mall_categories` table. In combination with the resolved `shopping_mall_category_tree_id` (derived from the `categoryTreeCode` path parameter), it forms a composite unique key such as `@@unique([shopping_mall_category_tree_id, code])`, ensuring that no two categories in the same tree share the same business code.

Clients should choose stable, human-readable codes that are suitable for use in integrations and administrative tools; the server will reject duplicates within the same tree.

name.description:
Human-friendly display name of the category as shown in storefront navigation and admin UIs.

This value maps to the non-nullable `name` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. It is also commonly used as the source for generating the internal `slug` value (stored in the non-nullable `slug` column), which the server derives automatically for URL-friendly usage.

Choose names that are meaningful to customers and administrators; changing names later can affect how categories are perceived in navigation and search, but does not affect the underlying `code`.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text explaining the purpose, contents, or placement of the category in the catalog hierarchy.

This field maps to the nullable `description` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` table. When omitted or left empty, the category will not have additional descriptive text at the data layer, and UIs may fall back to showing only the category `name`.

Use this field to provide richer information for SEO, accessibility, or administrative context, such as describing the types of products contained in the category or any special rules that apply.

displayOrder.description:
Optional numeric ordering index used to sort sibling categories within the same parent when rendering menus or navigation structures.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable `display_order` column on the `shopping_mall_categories` model. When provided, it determines the relative ordering of this category among its siblings under the same parent: lower values typically appear first in navigation.

If this property is omitted in the request, the server assigns a default `display_order` value (for example, appending the new category after existing siblings) so that the underlying non-nullable column is always populated even when the client does not specify an explicit sort order.

isActive.description:
Flag indicating whether this category is currently active and should be visible for catalog navigation and product assignment.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `active` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. When set to `true`, the category is considered eligible to appear in storefront navigation and to be used for new product assignments. When set to `false`, the category is logically present in the hierarchy but may be hidden from end-user experiences while remaining visible to administrators and in historical records.

Deactivating a category does not delete it or modify related products; it only affects visibility and business logic that checks the `active` flag.

parentCategoryCode.description:
Optional business identifier code of the parent category within the same category tree.

This field represents the human-friendly counterpart of the nullable `parent_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_categories` table. When provided, the server looks up another category in the same tree by its `code`, verifies that it belongs to the resolved `shopping_mall_category_tree_id`, and then stores that category's primary key in the `parent_id` column.

If this property is omitted, the new category is treated as a root node in the tree (that is, `parent_id` remains null). Server-side validation ensures that specified parent codes are valid and belong to the same tree, and it prevents illegal hierarchies such as cycles.

IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing category node within a specific category tree in the shoppingMall catalog.

This DTO represents mutable attributes of a record in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. The record being updated is identified externally by the `categoryTreeCode` and `categoryCode` path parameters in the API, which the server resolves to the underlying `shopping_mall_category_tree_id` and primary key of the row. As a result, identifying fields such as the category tree code, category code, and internal identifiers are not included in this schema.

Server-managed columns such as `slug`, `is_leaf`, and timestamp fields (for example, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`) are not directly mutable via this DTO. The backend is responsible for maintaining those values consistently, either by recomputing them from other state or by applying internal business rules. All properties in this schema are optional to support partial updates: omitted properties leave the corresponding database columns unchanged.

name.description:
Updated display name of the category as shown in storefront navigation and admin UIs.

When provided, this value overwrites the existing `name` column on the `shopping_mall_categories` row. The server may also use the updated name to recompute a derived `slug` depending on configuration, but the slug itself remains an internal field and is not set directly through this DTO.

If this property is omitted, the current category name is preserved.

description.description:
Updated descriptive text for the category.

This property maps to the nullable `description` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` table. Supplying a new value replaces any existing description. Some implementations may treat an empty string as a request to clear the description, while others may require a separate explicit operation; callers should follow project-level conventions.

If omitted, the existing description remains unchanged.

displayOrder.description:
Updated ordering index used to sort this category among siblings in the same parent.

This field maps to the non-nullable `display_order` column on the `shopping_mall_categories` model. Providing a new value allows administrators to reorder how categories appear in navigation or management UIs relative to other categories under the same parent.

If this property is omitted, the current `display_order` value is left unchanged, so the category retains its existing position in sibling lists.

isActive.description:
Updated active/visibility flag for the category.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `active` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. Setting it to `true` reactivates a previously deactivated category, allowing it to be shown in storefront navigation and used for new product assignments; setting it to `false` hides the category from customer-facing contexts while keeping the record and its relationships intact.

If omitted, the existing `active` flag value is preserved.

parentCategoryCode.description:
Updated parent category code within the same category tree.

When supplied, this value is used to resolve a new parent category in the same `shopping_mall_category_trees` context by its `code`. The server then updates the `parent_id` foreign key on the `shopping_mall_categories` record to point to the resolved parent. This enables re-parenting operations such as moving a category under a different branch of the tree.

If this property is omitted, the current parent relationship is preserved. If your business rules support explicitly promoting a category to the root level, the implementation may allow a separate workflow or a special sentinel value to clear `parent_id`; such behavior should be documented at the API level and enforced with integrity checks that avoid cycles or invalid hierarchies.

IShoppingMallPolicyOverview.description:
Consolidated overview of high-level policy configurations for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO aggregates summary information from multiple policy-related Prisma models, including shopping_mall_policy_settings, shopping_mall_cancellation_policies, shopping_mall_refund_policies, shopping_mall_review_policies, and shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies. It is optimized for administrative dashboards so platform operators can see which policy groups exist and which concrete policies are currently active without querying each table individually.

The overview groups policies by functional area and exposes lightweight summary objects that identify the policy, describe its purpose at a high level, and indicate whether it is active or in effect. It is strictly read-only and does not represent a single persisted row in the database; instead it is a denormalized, computed projection for read models.

policySettings.description:
Collection of high-level policy configuration groups defined in shopping_mall_policy_settings.

Each entry summarizes a configuration profile or policy bundle, including identifiers, human-readable names, and activation flags. These settings typically act as parent groups for more granular cancellation, refund, review, and age restriction rules.

cancellationPolicies.description:
Summary list of cancellation policy definitions derived from shopping_mall_cancellation_policies.

Each item identifies a cancellation rule (for example by code or name) and indicates whether it is active, what its general purpose is, and, where applicable, a simple description of the cancellation window or scope. The list may be empty when no cancellation policies are configured.

refundPolicies.description:
Summary list of refund policy definitions derived from shopping_mall_refund_policies.

Entries describe the main refund rules configured on the platform, such as eligibility requirements or refund behavior types, and whether they are currently enabled. The array may be empty if no refund policies exist.

reviewPolicies.description:
Summary list of review and rating policy definitions derived from shopping_mall_review_policies.

Each element describes how customer reviews and ratings are governed, such as moderation behavior, eligibility to review, or rating constraints, and whether the policy is active. The array may be empty if no review policies are configured.

ageRestrictionPolicies.description:
Summary list of age and eligibility restriction policies derived from shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies.

Each entry describes an age restriction rule, including its identifier, short description of the restriction, and activation state. The array may be empty when no age restriction policies are defined.

IShoppingMallPolicySetting.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a shopping mall policy setting, optimized for list displays and embedding into other entities.

This summary DTO represents the same configuration profile as `IShoppingMallPolicySetting` but exposes only the key identification and classification fields required for overview screens. Heavy or detail-only fields such as `config_payload`, `effective_from`, and `effective_to` are intentionally omitted.

Field names for shared concepts (category, active, creation/update timestamps) are kept consistent with the underlying Prisma model `shopping_mall_policy_settings` and the full detail DTO to simplify mapping and reasoning across variants.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the policy setting record.

This value corresponds directly to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_policy_settings` table and is used internally for persistence, joins, and low-level indexing.

code.description:
Stable, human-readable business code that uniquely identifies this policy setting profile within the platform.

This field maps to the `code` column in `shopping_mall_policy_settings` and is enforced as globally unique via a dedicated unique index. Other domain-specific policy tables and configuration consumers reference policy settings by this code rather than the internal `id`.

name.description:
Short, human-readable name of the policy setting profile.

Administrative and backoffice UIs use this value as the primary title when listing configuration profiles, for example "Default Cancellation Policy" or "Holiday Refund Profile".

description.description:
Brief description of what this policy setting controls or influences within the shopping mall platform.

This typically summarizes the intended business use or scenario for the profile, helping operators distinguish similar configurations when browsing or searching. When the underlying `description` column is null, this property may be returned as an empty string or omitted, depending on implementation conventions.

category.description:
Logical category of the policy setting profile, such as "cancellation", "refund", "review", or "age_restriction".

This property maps to the `category` column in the `shopping_mall_policy_settings` table and is used to group and filter profiles by business domain in list and overview views.

active.description:
Indicates whether this policy setting profile is currently active.

This property mirrors the `active` column in `shopping_mall_policy_settings`. Only active profiles are normally considered by runtime policy evaluation workflows; inactive profiles are kept primarily for audit, history, or future reactivation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this policy setting record was created, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

This corresponds to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_policy_settings` and is useful for sorting and understanding the lifecycle of configuration profiles in administrative dashboards.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this policy setting record was last updated, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

This corresponds to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_policy_settings` and allows operators to quickly identify recently changed configurations in overview screens.

IShoppingMallCancellationPolicy.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of an order cancellation policy within the shopping mall platform.

Intended for use in lists, references from other entities, and quick overviews where the full rule set is not required. Includes key behavioral flags and association context so that administrators and services can understand how the policy behaves without loading the full detail DTO.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cancellation policy record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_cancellation_policies` table and uniquely distinguishes this policy from all others in the system.

code.description:
Stable business code that uniquely identifies this cancellation policy and is safe to expose to clients and integrations.

The code is enforced as unique at the database level and is the primary way other configuration records and APIs refer to this policy in a human‑readable manner.

name.description:
Short, human‑readable name of the cancellation policy suitable for display in customer and admin interfaces.

This name should clearly convey the intent or scope of the policy, such as whether it is the default policy or tailored for a specific region or product segment.

description.description:
Brief explanation of when and how this cancellation policy applies.

The text should summarize the main rules, such as allowed time windows, eligible order statuses, and who may initiate cancellations, without needing to expose the full configuration payload.

isDefault.description:
Indicates whether this policy is considered the default cancellation policy in the current business context.

When true, the policy may be automatically applied to orders or regions where no more specific policy override has been configured.

isActive.description:
Flag indicating whether this cancellation policy is currently active and eligible to be applied to new orders.

Inactive policies remain in the system for historical reference and audit purposes but should not be attached to newly created orders or flows.

maxHoursAfterPayment.description:
Maximum number of hours after successful payment during which cancellations are generally accepted under this policy.

A null value indicates that the policy does not rely on a simple hour‑based cut‑off and instead uses status‑based rules or configuration payload logic.

allowCancellationBeforeShipment.description:
Indicates whether customers are allowed to cancel orders up to the moment before shipment according to this policy.

When true, the policy explicitly permits cancellations in the pre‑shipment phase, subject to any additional constraints defined in the detailed configuration.

allowPartialCancellation.description:
Indicates whether partial cancellation of individual order lines is allowed under this policy.

When true, customers or operators may cancel specific items or quantities rather than being forced to cancel the entire order.

regionSetting.description:
Optional region configuration context that this cancellation policy is scoped to.

When present, it references a `shopping_mall_region_settings` record via a lightweight summary object, indicating that the policy only applies within that specific region. When absent, the policy is considered global or multi‑region depending on other configuration.

policySetting.description:
Optional policy setting profile that provides shared configuration parameters for this cancellation policy.

This association points to a `shopping_mall_policy_settings` summary, allowing multiple policies to share a common configuration foundation while differing in code, region, or activation windows.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation policy was created.

Stored in the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_cancellation_policies` table and expressed in ISO 8601 format for interoperability across services.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation policy was last modified.

This value reflects the most recent update to any of the policy’s persisted fields and is sourced from the `updated_at` column of the underlying Prisma model.

IShoppingMallRefundPolicy.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a refund policy configured in the shopping mall platform.

Provides lightweight information suitable for list views and references, such as policy identification, display name, key behavioral flags, and association context, without exposing the full configuration payload. Used when showing which refund policy applies to orders, payment methods, or regions.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund policy.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` table and uniquely distinguishes this policy from all others in the system.

code.description:
Business‑facing unique code of the refund policy used to reference this policy from other configurations and APIs.

Typically a short, stable identifier such as `DEFAULT_REFUND` or `DIGITAL_GOODS_NONREFUNDABLE`, enforced as unique at the database level.

name.description:
Human‑readable name of the refund policy shown in back‑office tools and, where appropriate, in user‑facing descriptions.

The name should clearly communicate the overall behavior or scope of the policy, for example whether it is restrictive or generous.

description.description:
Short description summarizing the main rules of this refund policy.

The text should highlight the eligibility window, whether full or partial refunds are allowed, typical fee handling, and any major exceptions, without needing to fetch the full detailed configuration.

isActive.description:
Indicates whether this refund policy is currently active and can be applied to new orders.

Inactive policies may remain attached to historical transactions for audit and reporting but should not be used for new refunds.

maxDaysAfterDelivery.description:
Maximum number of days after delivery within which a customer can request a refund or return under this policy.

A null value indicates that the policy does not rely solely on a simple day‑based window and instead uses other conditions or configuration rules to determine eligibility.

allowFullRefund.description:
Indicates whether full refunds are allowed in business scenarios governed by this policy.

When false, the policy may only permit partial refunds, vouchers, or store credit, depending on additional configuration.

allowPartialRefund.description:
Indicates whether partial refunds—either by selected order lines or partial monetary amounts—are permitted under this policy.

When false, eligible refunds must be processed as full refunds for the applicable scope (order, segment, or item set).

requireAdminApprovalOverAmount.description:
Optional monetary threshold above which administrator approval is required for refunds.

When present, any refund whose gross amount exceeds this value should be routed through an admin review or approval workflow. A null value means no specific amount threshold is enforced by this policy field.

regionSetting.description:
Optional region configuration context that this refund policy is scoped to.

When provided, it references a `shopping_mall_region_settings` record as a `.ISummary` object and signals that the policy is intended for that particular market or geography. When absent, the policy may be global or controlled by other scoping rules.

policySetting.description:
Optional policy setting profile that provides shared configuration parameters for this refund policy.

This association references a `shopping_mall_policy_settings` summary, allowing multiple refund policies to share foundational settings such as default behavior or compliance presets while differing in activation, region, or fine‑grained rules.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this refund policy was created in the system, in ISO 8601 format.

This value is stored in the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` table and is used for auditing and timeline reconstruction.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this refund policy was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

This value is stored in the `updated_at` column of the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` table and changes whenever any persisted attribute of the policy is modified.

IShoppingMallReviewPolicy.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a review and rating policy configured in the shopping mall platform.

Provides lightweight information suitable for listing policies, selecting applicable rules for products or categories, and displaying high-level constraints in admin tools. This summary aligns with the underlying shopping_mall_review_policies model and its associations, while avoiding heavy or opaque configuration payloads.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the review policy.

This is the same UUID primary key used in the detailed policy DTO and the backing shopping_mall_review_policies table.

code.description:
Business-facing unique code of the review policy, used to reference this policy from other configurations and APIs.

Examples include values such as "default_review" or "strict_moderation". This code is the primary human-readable identifier in URLs and configuration UIs.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the review policy shown to administrators and support staff in list and selection views.

Typical values briefly describe the policy’s purpose, such as "Default review rules" or "Strict moderation for high-risk categories".

description.description:
Optional short text summary of the core review rules, such as who can post reviews, allowed rating ranges, and basic moderation aspects.

In list views this is usually truncated or rendered as a brief tooltip to help administrators differentiate similar policies.

active.description:
Indicates whether this review policy is currently active and can be associated with products, categories, or regions for new review operations.

Inactive policies typically appear in lists only when explicitly requested for historical or audit purposes.

max_days_after_delivery_for_review.description:
Maximum number of days after delivery during which customers may submit reviews under this policy.

When set, administrators can quickly gauge how long review windows remain open when scanning policy lists. When null, no explicit limit is expressed by this field in the summary.

allow_edit_within_days.description:
Number of days after review creation during which customers may edit their reviews under this policy.

List views may display this value so that operators can easily compare edit windows across different policies without opening full detail views.

auto_hide_report_threshold.description:
Number of distinct abuse reports required before reviews are automatically hidden pending moderation.

A null value indicates that automatic hiding based on report count is disabled for this policy, which is important context when administrators compare moderation aggressiveness across policies.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which this policy becomes effective for review operations, if defined.

In list views this can be used to distinguish policies that are scheduled to start in the future or that only recently took effect.

effective_to.description:
Timestamp after which this policy ceases to apply to new operations, if defined.

When populated, administrators can quickly see whether a policy is near expiry or has an explicitly defined end date.

region_setting.description:
Summary of the region configuration to which this policy is scoped, when applicable.

This allows list views to show at a glance which market or geographic area the policy applies to, without loading the full region configuration record separately.

policy_setting.description:
Summary of the policy configuration profile associated with this review policy, when one is configured.

This provides quick insight into which shared policy profile is in effect without requiring a separate lookup for each row in the list.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this review policy was created in the system, in ISO 8601 format.

Useful for sorting and for quickly assessing how long a policy has been in use.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this review policy was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

Allows operators to identify recently modified policies that may require review or validation.

IShoppingMallAgeRestrictionPolicy.ISumma.description:
Summary view of an age restriction policy configured in the shopping mall platform.

Provides concise information about rules that control which customers may access age‑restricted or otherwise sensitive products, based on customer age, verification status, region, and shared policy profiles. This summary is optimized for list views, references from other entities, and administrative overviews rather than full policy editing.

The DTO aligns with the underlying `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies` Prisma model and exposes key identifiers, core eligibility constraints, activation status, effective period, and optional association context such as region configuration and linked policy setting profiles.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the age restriction policy.

This value corresponds to the `id` primary key in the `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies` table and is generated by the system. It does not change over the lifetime of the policy.

code.description:
Business-facing unique code of the age restriction policy.

Administrators, other configuration entities, and external integrations use this code to reference the policy. Typical examples include values such as `"adult_only"`, `"AGE_18_PLUS"`, or `"teen_restricted"`.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the age restriction policy.

This value is shown in administration UIs, logs, and reports so operators can quickly recognize the purpose of the policy without needing to inspect low-level configuration details.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text explaining the intent and scope of the age restriction policy.

This may summarize which categories or product types are governed, relevant legal or compliance considerations, and any special business rules. When `null`, no additional free-text explanation has been recorded for this policy.

minimumAge.description:
Minimum customer age in years required to access products or content governed by this policy.

This field reflects the `minimum_age_years` column in the `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies` table. When a non-negative integer is present, customers must meet or exceed this age threshold. When `null`, age may not be the primary eligibility criterion and other rules captured in configuration payloads or external services determine access.

require_verified_age.description:
Indicates whether customers must have a verified age status on their account for this policy to be satisfied.

This mirrors the non-nullable `require_verified_age` column in the `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies` Prisma model. When `true`, the platform must rely on age verification mechanisms (such as identity checks or trusted attestations) before treating the customer as eligible, even if their stated age meets `minimumAge`.

active.description:
Flag indicating whether this age restriction policy is currently active for new operations.

Active policies are considered during catalog visibility, checkout, and review flows when determining whether a customer may access restricted items. Inactive policies are ignored for new decisions but remain available for audit and historical references.

effective_from.description:
Timestamp from which this age restriction policy becomes effective for new evaluations, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When populated, any age‑restricted operations occurring before this moment should not use this policy. When `null`, the policy is treated as effective from its creation time or from a higher-level configuration context.

effective_to.description:
Timestamp after which this age restriction policy is no longer effective for new operations, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When populated, new age‑restriction decisions occurring strictly after this timestamp should not apply this policy. When `null`, the policy has no predefined end date and remains effective until it is deactivated or replaced by other configuration changes.

regionSetting.description:
Optional region configuration associated with this age restriction policy.

When non-null, this summary points to the `shopping_mall_region_settings` entry that scopes where the policy applies, such as a single country, a group of countries, or a custom market segment. When `null`, the policy may be considered global or scoped by other mechanisms rather than a concrete region record.

policySetting.description:
Optional higher-level policy setting profile linked to this age restriction policy.

When present, this value references a row in `shopping_mall_policy_settings` that provides shared configuration parameters or grouping for related policies (for example, a common "age_restriction" profile). When `null`, the policy operates independently without an associated shared profile.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this age restriction policy record was created, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value mirrors the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies` table and is useful for sorting, auditing, and understanding how long the policy has been in effect.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this age restriction policy record was last updated, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies` table. Administrators can use it to identify recently modified policies that may require review or validation.

IShoppingMallPolicyUsageStatistics.description:
Aggregated usage statistics for shoppingMall policy configurations across orders, refunds, reviews, and age-restricted interactions.

This DTO is a computed, read-only view that combines data from policy configuration tables (such as shopping_mall_cancellation_policies, shopping_mall_refund_policies, shopping_mall_review_policies, and shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies) with transactional and event tables including shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests, shopping_mall_order_return_requests, shopping_mall_product_reviews, and shopping_mall_product_review_reports.

It is optimized for platform administrator analytics dashboards, enabling admins to understand how often each policy is used, how it affects customer behavior, and whether certain rules might require tuning. The DTO groups metrics by policy type and by individual policy code, and may also expose overall summary totals for quick at-a-glance analysis.

cancellationPolicyStatistics.description:
Per-policy usage metrics for cancellation policies configured in shopping_mall_cancellation_policies.

Each entry aggregates counts of cancellation-related activity (such as number of cancellation requests or cancelled orders) that are attributed to a specific cancellation policy.

refundPolicyStatistics.description:
Per-policy usage metrics for refund policies defined in shopping_mall_refund_policies.

Each element summarizes how often a given refund policy has been applied in refund transactions over the chosen analysis window.

reviewPolicyStatistics.description:
Per-policy usage metrics for review policies defined in shopping_mall_review_policies.

Metrics typically cover counts of reviews created, moderated, or reported while a given review policy was active.

ageRestrictionPolicyStatistics.description:
Per-policy usage metrics for age restriction policies defined in shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies.

Each entry aggregates how often a specific age restriction policy blocked, warned, or otherwise affected potential purchases or interactions.

overall.description:
High-level aggregate statistics summarizing policy-related activity across all policies and policy types.

This section provides at-a-glance totals and ratios that help administrators quickly gauge the overall impact of their policy configuration.

IShoppingMallCancellationPolicyUsageStat.description:
Aggregated usage metrics for a single cancellation policy in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO ties a specific cancellation policy (identified by code) to counts of how frequently it has been applied in cancellation-related operations over a particular analysis window. It is designed for use inside IShoppingMallPolicyUsageStatistics and in admin-facing analytics views.

policyCode.description:
Code of the cancellation policy to which these statistics apply.

This should match the code used in IShoppingMallCancellationPolicy.ISummary and the corresponding row in shopping_mall_cancellation_policies.

cancellationRequestCount.description:
Total number of cancellation requests that were evaluated under this cancellation policy in the analysis period.

This count typically corresponds to records in shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests that reference orders governed by this policy.

cancelledOrderCount.description:
Number of orders that were successfully cancelled under this policy during the analysis period.

This is usually a subset of cancellationRequestCount, representing cancellation requests that resulted in an order status change to a cancelled state.

IShoppingMallRefundPolicyUsageStatistics.description:
Aggregated usage metrics for a single refund policy in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents an analytics projection rather than a direct row mapping. Each instance summarizes how one configured refund policy in `shopping_mall_refund_policies` has actually been exercised over a specific reporting window by aggregating related rows from `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`.

Typical usage is inside higher-level policy analytics responses (such as overall policy usage summaries or admin dashboards) where multiple refund policies are compared side by side. All numeric metrics in this structure are non-negative; a row with all zeros generally indicates a policy that is configured but has not been involved in any refund activity within the selected time range and filter criteria.

policyCode.description:
Business code of the refund policy to which these statistics apply.

This value corresponds to the policy identifier used by `IShoppingMallRefundPolicy.ISummary` and the business key column in the `shopping_mall_refund_policies` table. Client applications typically use this code to join this analytics row back to full policy configuration metadata and to present a stable identifier in reports and dashboards.

refundTransactionCount.description:
Total number of refund transactions associated with this refund policy within the selected reporting window.

This non-negative integer is derived from rows in `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` that are linked to the referenced refund policy, after applying any additional filters such as region, channel, or date range. The count usually includes both full and partial refunds that were evaluated under this policy during the analysis period.

refundedAmountTotal.description:
Total monetary amount refunded under this policy during the analysis window, expressed in a consistent reporting currency.

This value is computed as an aggregate (for example, a SUM over a Decimal or numeric column) from `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` rows associated with the referenced refund policy. It is always non-negative and may reflect currency conversion and rounding rules defined by the platform; for example, the implementation may convert per-transaction currency into a base currency before aggregation and apply standard rounding to the final result.

IShoppingMallReviewPolicyUsageStatistics.description:
Aggregated usage metrics for a single review policy in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO captures how one configured review and rating policy from `shopping_mall_review_policies` has been exercised over a particular reporting window. It aggregates activity across product reviews, moderation events, and abuse reports by reading from tables such as `shopping_mall_product_reviews`, `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`, and `shopping_mall_product_review_reports`.

The structure is commonly embedded in administrative analytics APIs and dashboards that compare review policies, identify heavily moderated or frequently reported content, and support policy tuning and compliance analysis. All counters are non-negative; policies that show only zero values are typically configured but have not yet accumulated review activity within the analyzed time range.

policyCode.description:
Business code of the review policy to which these statistics apply.

This value matches the policy code used by `IShoppingMallReviewPolicy.ISummary` and the corresponding business key column in the `shopping_mall_review_policies` table. It allows client code and reporting tools to join the analytics row to the full policy definition for display and further analysis.

reviewCreationCount.description:
Number of product reviews that were created while this review policy configuration was in effect during the reporting window.

This non-negative integer is typically derived from `shopping_mall_product_reviews` rows whose creation timestamps fall inside the selected analysis period and that are governed by the referenced review policy. Exact counting semantics (for example, whether soft-deleted drafts are included) follow the business rules implemented in the analytics query or view layer.

reviewModerationActionCount.description:
Number of moderation actions performed under this review policy during the reporting window.

This non-negative integer aggregates events from `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` that are associated with reviews governed by the referenced policy. Typical actions include hiding or unpublishing a review, editing review content or metadata, reinstating previously hidden reviews, and permanently deleting abusive or non-compliant reviews. Each recorded moderation event contributes one to this count.

reviewReportCount.description:
Number of abuse or issue reports submitted against reviews while this review policy was in effect during the reporting window.

This non-negative integer is usually computed from `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` rows that target reviews governed by the referenced policy and whose report timestamps fall inside the selected analysis period. Multiple reports against the same review are counted individually, providing visibility into repeated reporting activity for specific pieces of content or product areas.

IShoppingMallAgeRestrictionPolicyUsageSt.description:
Aggregated usage metrics for a single age restriction policy in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is a computed analytics projection rather than a direct Prisma model representation. All metric values are calculated over a specific analysis or reporting window that is defined by the surrounding API request (for example a date range, region filters, or actor segments) and are not persisted as-is in a dedicated table.

The statistics in this DTO are tied to a single policy identified by its business code, which corresponds to an entry in the `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies` table and is typically surfaced via `IShoppingMallAgeRestrictionPolicy.ISummary`. It is primarily used inside higher-level policy usage statistics responses to help administrators monitor how age restriction configuration influences customer interactions and access control.

policyCode.description:
Business code of the age restriction policy to which these statistics apply.

This value should match the `policyCode` (or equivalent code field) used in `IShoppingMallAgeRestrictionPolicy.ISummary` and the corresponding row in the `shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies` Prisma model, allowing consumers to join analytics results back to the underlying policy definition.

It uniquely identifies the policy within the analysis window so that dashboards and reports can attribute blocked attempts and warnings to the correct configuration entry.

blockedAttemptCount.description:
Number of purchase or access attempts that were blocked due to this age restriction policy during the analysis period.

This counter is an aggregated metric derived from order flows, catalog visibility checks, or other access-control logic that evaluates the age restriction rules. Each increment represents a user interaction that was fully prevented because the actor did not meet the required age or eligibility criteria.

Implementations should ensure that the counting logic uses a single, well-defined analysis window (for example daily, weekly, or custom date range) that is consistent with the filters used by the analytics endpoint returning this DTO.

warningShownCount.description:
Number of times a warning or informational message related to this age restriction policy was shown to users during the analysis period.

Unlike `blockedAttemptCount`, these events typically correspond to interactions where the user was allowed to proceed, but the platform chose to surface guidance, disclaimers, or advisory messages due to the policy configuration.

This metric enables administrators to distinguish between hard blocks and softer, informational interventions and to tune their policies accordingly over the same analysis window used for the other metrics.

IShoppingMallPolicyUsageOverallStatistic.description:
High-level, cross-policy aggregate metrics summarizing policy-related activity on the shoppingMall platform over a defined analysis window.

This DTO is a computed analytics snapshot that aggregates usage across multiple policy types, including cancellation, refund, review, and age restriction policies. It does not map directly to any single Prisma table; instead, its values are derived from operational data stored in entities such as `shopping_mall_orders`, `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests`, `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`, `shopping_mall_product_reviews`, and related policy configuration tables.

The overall statistics are typically used for top-level dashboard tiles and quick health checks, enabling administrators and business stakeholders to understand at a glance how frequently policy-driven flows are being triggered and how much financial impact is associated with cancellations and refunds during the requested reporting period.

totalCancellationRequestCount.description:
Total number of cancellation requests across all policies and orders during the analysis period.

This value is usually computed as the sum of all individual cancellation request records (for example from `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests`) that match the filters of the analytics query. It typically aligns with the sum of `cancellationRequestCount` fields found in per-policy usage DTOs such as `IShoppingMallCancellationPolicyUsageStatistics`.

It provides a coarse indicator of how often customers, sellers, or administrators initiate the cancellation flow within the selected reporting window.

totalCancelledOrderCount.description:
Total number of orders that ended in a cancelled state during the analysis period across all applicable cancellation policies.

This aggregate is derived from the `shopping_mall_orders` table (and possibly related status event tables) by counting orders whose terminal status indicates cancellation and whose timestamps fall within the same analysis window as the rest of the metrics.

It is useful for understanding overall cancellation impact, independent of actor or specific policy, and for monitoring long-term trends in order completion versus cancellation.

totalRefundTransactionCount.description:
Total number of refund transactions processed across all refund policies during the analysis period.

This metric is typically computed by counting refund transaction records (for example, entries in `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`) that satisfy the analytics query filters. It usually corresponds to the sum of `refundTransactionCount` in per-policy usage DTOs such as `IShoppingMallRefundPolicyUsageStatistics`.
