A high value can indicate heavy after-sales activity or potential issues with product quality, fulfillment accuracy, or payment processing.

totalRefundedAmount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded across all refund policies during the analysis window, expressed in the reporting currency used by the analytics endpoint.

The value is calculated by aggregating the monetary amounts of completed refund transactions (for example from `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` and `shopping_mall_refund_items`) that match the applied filters and fall within the same analysis period as the other metrics.

Consumers should treat this as a financial KPI that reflects the cost of cancellations, returns, and other after-sales adjustments during the reporting window, and may use it alongside revenue and payout analytics for profitability analysis.

totalReviewCreationCount.description:
Total number of product reviews created across all review policies during the analysis period.

This aggregate is derived from review records (such as rows in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`) that were created within the specified reporting window and that are governed by the configured review policies.

It helps administrators and product teams understand engagement levels in the review system and, when combined with moderation and rating aggregates, provides insight into customer satisfaction and content generation trends.

totalReviewModerationActionCount.description:
Total number of moderation actions taken on reviews across all review policies in the analysis window.

Typical sources for this metric are records in moderation event tables such as `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`, filtered by the same date range and criteria as the rest of the statistics. Each action can represent a hide, approve, escalate, or similar moderation decision.

This metric is important for understanding operational load on moderation teams, the effectiveness of automated filters, and overall content risk within the selected timeframe.

totalAgeRestrictionBlockedAttemptCount.description:
Total number of purchase or access attempts that were blocked by any age restriction policy during the analysis period.

This value is usually computed by summing the `blockedAttemptCount` metrics across all per-policy age restriction usage entries returned by DTOs such as `IShoppingMallAgeRestrictionPolicyUsageStatistics` that match the same analysis window.

It gives a platform-wide view of how often age restriction policies are actively preventing interactions, which can be used to validate compliance coverage and assess the impact of policy changes at a macro level.

IShoppingMallCategoryUsageStatistics.description:
Aggregated category usage statistics for the shoppingMall catalog.

Represents analytical, read-only metrics about how often each product category is used across products and orders. This DTO does not map directly to a single Prisma model; instead, it aggregates data from multiple catalog and order-related tables such as categories, products, category assignments, orders, and order lines.

categories.description:
Per-category usage metrics for all relevant catalog categories.

Each entry summarizes how many products belong to the category, how often items from that category appear in orders, and other derived analytics useful for administrative dashboards.

total_products.description:
Total number of active products considered across all categories.

This is an aggregate count that helps contextualize per-category product counts when analyzing catalog coverage and distribution.

total_order_lines.description:
Total number of order lines considered across all categories.

Represents the total volume of line items in orders included in this aggregation window, allowing comparison with per-category order line counts.

total_distinct_customers.description:
Total number of distinct customers included in the analysis window.

Useful for understanding how broadly customers interact with the catalog when compared to per-category distinct customer counts.

IShoppingMallCategoryUsageStatistics.ICa.description:
Per-category usage metrics within the shoppingMall catalog.

Represents aggregated analytics for a single catalog category, including how many products are assigned to it and how frequently items from that category appear in orders.

category_id.description:
Unique identifier of the catalog category for which usage statistics are calculated.

Typically corresponds to the primary key of a row in the `shopping_mall_categories` table.

category_name.description:
Human-readable name of the category.

Included to allow admin dashboards to render meaningful labels without needing a separate category lookup.

product_count.description:
Number of active products assigned to this category at the time of aggregation.

Used to understand catalog coverage and density for this category.

order_line_count.description:
Total number of order lines that reference SKUs belonging to this category.

Helps measure how frequently items in this category are purchased.

distinct_customer_count.description:
Number of distinct customers who have placed at least one order containing items from this category during the aggregation window.

Useful for understanding the breadth of customer engagement for the category.

order_line_share_ratio.description:
Proportion of order lines belonging to this category relative to the total order lines in the aggregation window.

Expressed as a floating-point value between 0 and 1, where 0 means no usage and 1 means all order lines belong to this category.

product_share_ratio.description:
Proportion of products assigned to this category relative to the total products considered in the aggregation.

Expressed as a floating-point value between 0 and 1, where 0 means no products and 1 means all products are in this category.

IShoppingMallPolicySearch.IRequest.description:
Advanced search filters, pagination, and sorting options for querying policy-related configuration records in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by platform administrators to search across multiple policy tables, including mall-wide policy settings, cancellation policies, refund policies, review policies, and age restriction policies. It allows combining multiple optional filters with pagination and sorting parameters in a single structured request body.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated search results.

Defaults to 1 when omitted. Used together with `limit` to control which slice of the full result set is returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page.

Defaults to a sensible platform-wide value when omitted (for example 20 or 50). Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessive result sizes.

policy_types.description:
Optional list of policy type codes to restrict the search to one or more policy categories.

Typical values may include codes representing mall policy settings, cancellation policies, refund policies, review policies, and age restriction policies. When omitted or empty, all policy types are eligible.

items.description:
Policy type code indicating which underlying policy table a record belongs to.

The concrete set of allowed codes is determined by platform configuration and may include values such as `mallPolicy`, `cancellation`, `refund`, `review`, or `ageRestriction`.

statuses.description:
Optional list of status codes used to filter policies by their lifecycle state.

Common examples include active, draft, deprecated, or archived statuses. When omitted, policies of all statuses are considered.

items.description:
Policy lifecycle status code.

Allowed values are determined by platform configuration and may represent states such as `active`, `draft`, or `archived`.

effective_from.description:
Lower bound of the effective date range filter.

When provided, only policies whose effective date is on or after this timestamp are included in the search results. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

effective_to.description:
Upper bound of the effective date range filter.

When provided, only policies whose effective date is on or before this timestamp are included in the search results. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

region_codes.description:
Optional list of region or market codes used to filter policies by their applicability.

For example, this may correspond to country codes, regional groupings, or internal market identifiers managed by the platform.

items.description:
Region or market code that identifies the geographic or market scope where a policy applies.

Typical examples include ISO country codes such as `US`, `KR`, or `DE`, or tenant-specific region identifiers.

search.description:
Free-text search term used to match against policy names, titles, or descriptive content.

Supports case-insensitive partial matching and may be implemented using full-text search capabilities depending on the underlying database.

sort_by.description:
Field name used to sort the aggregated policy search results.

Typical options include fields such as `updatedAt`, `effectiveFrom`, or `priority`. If omitted, a default sort order (for example, by last updated time descending) is applied.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for the search results.

Uses `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the platform applies its default direction, commonly `desc`.

Sort direction for the search results.

Uses `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the platform applies its default direction, commonly `desc`.

sort_direction.description:
Sort direction for the search results.

Uses `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the platform applies its default direction, commonly `desc`.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying guest user identities along with pagination and sorting options.

This DTO is used by platform administrators or internal tools to search records in the `shopping_mall_guestuser` table. It allows specifying time ranges, identifier-based filters, soft-delete state, and basic free-text search, while also controlling paging and ordering of the result set.

All filters are optional so that callers can combine them flexibly depending on the analysis or operational task they need to perform.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve when paginating through guest user records.

This value controls which slice of the overall result set is returned. When omitted, implementations may default to the first page (page 1) or apply a platform-specific default behavior.

limit.description:
Maximum number of guest user records to return in a single page.

Backends typically enforce an upper bound (for example, 100 or 200) to protect system performance. When omitted, a sensible platform-wide default page size is applied.

search.description:
Free-form search text that may be applied to identifier-like fields associated with a guest user record.

Typical implementations apply this term to fields such as the guest's `id` or `temporary_identifier`, using case-insensitive or partial matching where supported by the underlying database or search engine.

created_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the guest user creation timestamp range filter.

Only guest records whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are included in the result set. This is useful when analyzing guests created within a specific time window.

created_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the guest user creation timestamp range filter.

Only guest records whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are included in the result set. Combined with `created_from`, this allows administrators to constrain searches to a closed time interval.

temporary_identifier.description:
Filter by the opaque temporary identifier used to correlate guest activity before registration.

This value maps directly to the `temporary_identifier` column on the `shopping_mall_guestuser` Prisma model. It is typically derived from cookies or device identifiers and allows administrators to find all guest records associated with a particular tracking key when investigating behavior or debugging conversion funnels.

user_agent.description:
Filter by the captured user agent string or a normalized descriptor of the guest's primary device.

This field corresponds to the `user_agent` column on the `shopping_mall_guestuser` Prisma model. It is useful for analyzing guests by device type or troubleshooting issues that appear to be limited to specific browsers or platforms.

deleted_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the soft-delete timestamp range filter for guest users.

When provided, only records whose `deleted_at` value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are considered matches. This is typically used when analyzing when guest identities were logically removed from active use while retaining them for historical reporting.

deleted_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the soft-delete timestamp range filter for guest users.

When provided, only records whose `deleted_at` value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are considered matches. Combined with `deleted_from`, this allows administrators to focus on guests that were soft-deleted within a particular time window.

is_deleted.description:
Soft-delete state filter controlling whether active or logically removed guest records are returned.

When set to `true`, only guest users with a non-null `deleted_at` value (soft-deleted records) are included. When set to `false`, only guests with a null `deleted_at` value (currently active records) are returned. When omitted, no filter on the deletion state is applied and both active and soft-deleted guests may be returned depending on other criteria.

order_by.description:
Field name used for sorting the guest user result set.

Typical values include `created_at` or `deleted_at`, corresponding directly to columns on the `shopping_mall_guestuser` table. The exact set of allowed sort fields is determined by implementation and indexing strategy and should be documented at the API level for consumers.

oneOf.description:
Ascending sort direction.

When used together with `order_by`, results are ordered from smallest to largest value for the chosen field (for example, oldest to newest when sorting by `created_at`).

Descending sort direction.

When used together with `order_by`, results are ordered from largest to smallest value for the chosen field (for example, newest to oldest when sorting by `created_at`).

order_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering the guest user results.

If omitted, the platform applies its default sort direction, which is commonly `desc` for time-based fields such as `created_at`.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.description:
Detailed guest user identity record persisted by the shopping mall backend.

A guest user represents an unauthenticated visitor for whom the platform decided to create a durable identity row in the `shopping_mall_guestuser` table. This is typically done to support conversion funnel analytics, long-lived guest carts, consent tracking, or other pre-registration behaviors. The DTO mirrors the columns of the Prisma model and is primarily exposed in platform-admin and internal tooling APIs.

The entity contains a stable primary key `id` and various attributes describing the guest context, such as an opaque temporary identifier, user agent string, and standard audit timestamps. Sensitive tracking implementation details should not be added beyond what is explicitly present in the Prisma schema. This DTO is read-only for external consumers; modifications are performed through dedicated create and update DTOs and operations.

id.description:
Primary key of the guest user row in `shopping_mall_guestuser`.

This value is a server-generated UUID that uniquely identifies a single guest identity record and remains stable for the lifetime of the row. It is used as the primary join key when linking guest users to carts, analytics events, or eventual customer conversions.

temporary_identifier.description:
Opaque identifier associated with the guest user, typically derived from cookies, device IDs, or other tracking mechanisms.

This value is used to correlate anonymous activity prior to registration and may be absent for some historical or partially tracked records because the underlying column is nullable. When present, it should be treated as an implementation-specific token and not exposed directly to end users.

user_agent.description:
Captured HTTP user agent string or similar client descriptor associated with the guest user at the time of the first tracked interaction.

This field is nullable in the underlying `shopping_mall_guestuser` table, so it may be missing when the platform did not capture or chose not to persist the user agent. When available, it is useful for analytics, device segmentation, and debugging client-specific issues.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this guest user record was first created in the system.

The value is stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_guestuser` and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). It is always present for persisted rows and is set by the backend when the record is inserted.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the most recent update to this guest user record.

The value is stored in the `updated_at` column of `shopping_mall_guestuser` and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). It is always present and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable fields on the record are changed.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this guest user record was logically deleted, if soft deletion is used.

When the record is considered active, this column is null. When set, it records the moment the guest identity was soft-deleted for purposes such as privacy cleanup or deactivation while preserving historical analytics context.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new guest user identity in the shopping mall backend.

This DTO is used by trusted backend services (typically under platform admin context) to persist a previously anonymous visitor as a guest user in the `shopping_mall_guestuser` table. It captures minimal identity and tracking information provided by upstream systems, while the backend is responsible for generating primary keys and managing system timestamps.

It intentionally excludes all system-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`, which are populated by the server at insertion time. It also excludes any authentication credential fields because guest users are unauthenticated visitors and do not log in with passwords or tokens.

temporary_identifier.description:
Opaque, stable identifier for the guest user, typically derived from cookies, device identifiers, or other tracking mechanisms.

This value is used by backend services to correlate an otherwise anonymous visitor across multiple requests and sessions. It should be treated as an implementation-specific token and not exposed directly to end users.

user_agent.description:
Raw User-Agent header string captured from the guest's HTTP request.

This provides basic device and browser context for analytics, fraud detection, or debugging. Because User-Agent strings can be long and varied, implementations may choose to truncate or normalize the value before persisting it.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing guest user identity record in the shopping mall backend.

This DTO allows privileged backend services or administrative tools to modify mutable attributes of a guest user in the `shopping_mall_guestuser` table. It is used in conjunction with a path parameter (guestUserId) that identifies the target record by its primary key.

Only fields that are conceptually mutable after creation are included here. System-managed fields such as primary keys and timestamps, as well as any ownership or authentication fields, are intentionally excluded. All properties are optional so that callers can perform partial updates without needing to resend the full state.

temporary_identifier.description:
New opaque, stable identifier for the guest user, typically derived from cookies, device identifiers, or other tracking mechanisms.

Backoffice or risk systems may update this value if they decide to rotate tracking identifiers or reconcile multiple anonymous identities into a single guest record.

user_agent.description:
Updated User-Agent header string associated with the guest user.

This may be updated if the platform chooses to refresh the stored device or browser context based on more recent interactions.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp for the guest user record in the `shopping_mall_guestuser` table.

When this value is a date-time string, the guest record is considered logically deleted for most business flows while still being retained for analytics, auditing, or historical analysis. Setting this field to a non-null value typically happens when an administrator or internal system decides to retire a guest identity without physically removing the database row.

When this value is null, the guest user is treated as active or never soft-deleted. Administrative tools may explicitly set this field back to null to "undelete" a previously soft-deleted guest record, provided such behavior is allowed by business rules and audit policies.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for listing shopping mall customer accounts for platform administrators.

This DTO is used as the request body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/customers endpoint. It allows complex, JSON-based search criteria over the shopping_mall_customer table, including pagination, sorting, and common filter fields such as name, email, and creation date ranges.

It must never contain authentication credentials or actor-identifying fields coming from JWT (such as platform admin IDs). It only represents query parameters for searching customers.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated customer search results.

If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default such as 1. Combined with `limit`, this controls which slice of the matching customers is returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of customer summary records to return per page.

If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

search.description:
Free-text search keyword applied to customer-facing attributes.

Typically matches against fields such as customer name, email address, or phone number using a case-insensitive LIKE or full-text search depending on implementation.

email.description:
Exact-match filter for the customer's primary email address.

When provided, only customers whose email exactly matches this value should be returned.

name.description:
Filter for the customer's display name or full name.

Implementations commonly apply case-insensitive partial matching so that operators can search by a fragment of the name.

phone.description:
Filter for the customer's primary phone number.

The format is implementation-specific but should follow the normalization rules used in the shopping_mall_customer-related data (for example, E.164 strings or a standardized national format).

registeredFrom.description:
Inclusive start of the customer registration timestamp range filter.

Only customers whose registration or creation timestamp is greater than or equal to this value should be returned. The value must be provided in ISO 8601 date-time format, typically in UTC.

registeredTo.description:
Inclusive end of the customer registration timestamp range filter.

Only customers whose registration or creation timestamp is less than or equal to this value should be returned. The value must be provided in ISO 8601 date-time format, typically in UTC.

status.description:
High-level status filter for customer accounts.

The exact allowed values depend on the `status` column of the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model (for example, `active`, `suspended`, `closed`, or `pendingVerification`). Implementations should validate that unsupported values are rejected with a clear error response and may normalize case or map aliases according to business rules.

is_verified.description:
Filter indicating whether the customer’s email address has been verified according to the `is_verified` column of the `shopping_mall_customer` table.

When set to `true`, the search should return only customers whose accounts have successfully passed the email verification flow and are marked as verified in the underlying data. This is commonly used by administrators when they need to restrict results to fully verified customers before performing sensitive operations.

When set to `false`, the search should return customers whose email verification has not been completed or has failed, allowing support or risk teams to identify accounts that may require outreach or additional checks. When the property is omitted, the search should not filter by verification status at all, returning both verified and unverified customers subject to other filters.

orderBy.description:
Field name used to sort the customer list.

Typical values include `created_at`, `name`, or `email`, but the exact whitelist is determined by the implementation and should correspond to safe, indexed fields in the `shopping_mall_customer` model. If omitted, a sensible default such as `created_at` should be applied, usually in descending order to show the most recently registered customers first.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field.

`asc` sorts in ascending order, for example from oldest to newest when used with `created_at`, or alphabetically A→Z when used with `name` or `email`.

Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field.

`desc` sorts in descending order, for example from newest to oldest when used with `created_at`, or alphabetically Z→A when used with `name` or `email`. Many administrative UIs default to `desc` on `created_at` to surface recent accounts first.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field.

`asc` sorts in ascending order, `desc` in descending order. If omitted, implementations usually default to `desc` for recency-based sorts such as ordering by `created_at`, but may choose other sensible defaults depending on the configured `orderBy` field.

IShoppingMallCustomer.description:
Detailed representation of a single shopping mall customer account as stored in the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma table.

This DTO is used as the response body for administrative detail and update operations such as `GET /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/customers/{customerId}` and `PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/customers/{customerId}`. It exposes customer-facing profile and contact attributes, plus high-level status indicators, while deliberately excluding authentication credentials and other security-sensitive data that live in separate tables (for example, `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` and `*_sessions`).

The type is safe to return to platform administrators and internal tools but must still respect privacy and data-protection requirements; for example, it does not include password hashes, tokens, or other secrets. All identity of the acting admin comes from JWT/session context and never from this DTO.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer record in the `shopping_mall_customer` table.

This value is the primary key used throughout the system to link orders, carts, reviews, and other customer-owned entities back to the owning customer account.

email.description:
Primary email address of the customer used for login-related communication, order notifications, and marketing messages where allowed by policy.

This value must never expose underlying password or credential information and is distinct from authentication secrets stored in other tables such as `shopping_mall_auth_credentials`.

name.description:
Display name or full name of the customer as shown in administrative and customer-facing UIs.

The exact composition (first name / last name) depends on business rules and locale, but this field represents the human-readable name associated with the account.

status.description:
High-level lifecycle or access status of the customer account.

Typical examples include values such as `active`, `blocked`, `suspended`, or `pendingVerification`, but the concrete enumeration is governed by business rules and the `shopping_mall_customer.status` column. Authorization and risk logic may gate customer actions based on this value.

isVerified.description:
Indicates whether the customer’s email address (and associated identity) has been successfully verified according to the platform’s verification flows.

This flag is mapped from the non-nullable `is_verified` column in the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model and is used in combination with `status` and risk flags to decide which operations are permitted for the account.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the customer account was first created in the system.

This value corresponds to the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model and typically reflects the moment of successful registration or backoffice creation.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the customer record was last updated.

Any change to mutable fields such as name, contact information, verification state, or lifecycle status should update this value in line with the automatic timestamp behavior defined on the `shopping_mall_customer` table.

deletedAt.description:
Soft delete timestamp for the customer account, mapped from the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model.

When this value is set, the customer account is considered logically closed and should normally be excluded from active customer lists, login flows, and new business activity, while still being retained for legal, compliance, and audit purposes. Administrative tools may surface this field to allow operators to understand whether a record has been soft-deleted and when that event occurred.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating an existing shopping mall customer record based on the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model.

This DTO is used by administrative tools or backoffice systems to modify mutable profile and lifecycle attributes of a customer account while preserving system-managed identity and authentication-related data. Only fields explicitly included in the payload are candidates for update; fields left undefined in the request body must remain unchanged in the underlying database record.

Ownership, primary keys, and authentication fields (such as credential references and session information) are intentionally excluded and must be managed through dedicated authentication and credential models.

email.description:
New primary email address for the customer.

If provided, the service should validate that the email is unique where required by business rules and that changing it does not violate any verification or risk constraints. When omitted, the existing email value is preserved.

name.description:
New display name or full name for the customer.

This value replaces the existing `name` field when supplied. When omitted, the existing name stored in `shopping_mall_customer.name` is left unchanged.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle or access status for the customer account.

Administrative tooling can use this field to move a customer between states such as `active`, `blocked`, or `suspended` according to business policies. When omitted, the current status value is preserved.

isVerified.description:
Updated verification flag for the customer account.

When supplied, this value overwrites the `is_verified` column in the `shopping_mall_customer` table, allowing administrative flows to mark an account as verified or unverified. When omitted, the existing verification state remains unchanged.

IShoppingMallSeller.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for retrieving a paginated list of seller accounts from the `shopping_mall_seller` Prisma model.

This type encapsulates search filters, pagination, and sorting options for querying sellers in operational tools and dashboards. It does not map directly to a single Prisma row but to query parameters applied when listing sellers.

page.description:
1‑based page index for paginated seller search results.

Clients set this to control which slice of the overall matching seller set is returned. When omitted, implementations should default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of seller records to return in a single page.

This controls page size for list responses. Implementations may enforce an upper bound to protect performance even when a larger value is requested.

oneOf.description:
Name of the seller column used to sort the result set.

Supported values are limited to sortable fields on the `shopping_mall_seller` table: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `email`, `store_name`, or `status`. When omitted, implementations may apply a sensible default such as `created_at` descending.

Name of the seller column used to sort the result set.

Supported values are limited to sortable fields on the `shopping_mall_seller` table: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `email`, `store_name`, or `status`. When omitted, implementations may apply a sensible default such as `created_at` descending.

Name of the seller column used to sort the result set.

Supported values are limited to sortable fields on the `shopping_mall_seller` table: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `email`, `store_name`, or `status`. When omitted, implementations may apply a sensible default such as `created_at` descending.

Supported values are limited to sortable fields on the `shopping_mall_seller` table: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `email`, `store_name`, or `status`. When omitted, implementations may apply a sensible default such as `created_at` descending.

Name of the seller column used to sort the result set.

Supported values are limited to sortable fields on the `shopping_mall_seller` table: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `email`, `store_name`, or `status`. When omitted, implementations may apply a sensible default such as `created_at` descending.

sort_field.description:
Name of the seller column used to sort the result set.

Supported values are limited to sortable fields on the `shopping_mall_seller` table: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `email`, `store_name`, or `status`. When omitted, implementations may apply a sensible default such as `created_at` descending.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering seller search results.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. When omitted, implementations typically default to `desc` for time‑based fields.

Sort direction to apply when ordering seller search results.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. When omitted, implementations typically default to `desc` for time‑based fields.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering seller search results.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. When omitted, implementations typically default to `desc` for time‑based fields.

status.description:
Optional lifecycle status filter for sellers.

When provided, only sellers whose `status` column matches this value are returned. Typical values include `pending`, `active`, `suspended`, or `terminated` according to platform policy.

email.description:
Optional email filter for narrowing the seller list.

Implementations may treat this as an exact match, a prefix match, or a substring search over the `email` column of `shopping_mall_seller`, depending on business requirements.

store_name.description:
Optional store name filter for narrowing the seller list.

This value is used to filter by the `store_name` column on `shopping_mall_seller`, typically via exact, prefix, or substring matching for search experiences.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the seller creation timestamp range filter.

When set, only sellers with `created_at` greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date‑time are included in the results.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the seller creation timestamp range filter.

When set, only sellers with `created_at` less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date‑time are included in the results.

updated_from.description:
Lower bound of the last‑updated timestamp range filter.

When set, only sellers whose `updated_at` is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date‑time are returned.

updated_to.description:
Upper bound of the last‑updated timestamp range filter.

When set, only sellers whose `updated_at` is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date‑time are returned.

include_deleted.description:
Flag indicating whether logically deleted seller accounts should be included in the result set.

When true, sellers with a non‑null `deleted_at` value are eligible to be returned. When false or omitted, implementations typically exclude logically deleted sellers by default.

IShoppingMallSeller.description:
Detailed representation of a marketplace seller account in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO exposes all relevant, non-sensitive fields from the `shopping_mall_seller` Prisma model needed for administrative and operational UIs. It includes identity, contact information, lifecycle status, and timestamp metadata so that clients can inspect a seller’s profile and track its history.

The structure is designed for read operations such as GET `/shoppingMall/sellers/{sellerId}` and is also returned as the result of update operations that modify seller data. System-managed fields like identifiers and timestamps are read-only from the client perspective.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller account in the `shopping_mall_seller` table.

This value is generated by the system and is used as the primary key for all seller-related operations, including drill-down from search, audits, and payout flows.

email.description:
Primary email address registered for the seller account.

This field is typically unique across all sellers and is used for login, notifications, and compliance-related communication.

store_name.description:
Public storefront name of the seller.

This value is typically unique within the platform so that buyers can clearly identify merchants. It may be subject to validation rules to avoid impersonation or policy violations.

oneOf.description:
Contact phone number for the seller’s store or business.

Used by support staff or buyers (when exposed) to reach the merchant. Format may follow E.164 or a region-specific pattern depending on platform configuration.
Null when no contact phone has been registered or when the seller has explicitly removed the stored phone number.

contact_phone.description:
Contact phone number field for the seller account, represented as an optional string.

When present, it carries a formatted phone number that may follow E.164 or another platform-defined standard. When null, it indicates that no phone number is currently registered for the seller.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the seller account.

Typical values include states such as `pending`, `active`, `suspended`, or `terminated`, as defined by business rules. This field determines whether the seller can operate on the platform and may be updated by either the seller (for limited transitions) or platform administrators.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the seller account was first created in the system.

This is a system-managed, read-only field that reflects the initial onboarding time for the merchant.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the seller record.

Automatically maintained by the system whenever mutable fields of the seller are changed.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when the seller account was logically deleted or closed, if applicable.

When this field is non-null, business logic may treat the seller as archived, closed, or otherwise inactive depending on platform policy.
Null when the seller account has never been logically deleted or closed and is still considered active within historical records.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion timestamp for the seller account.

When this field is a non-null ISO 8601 date-time string, the seller is considered closed, archived, or otherwise inactive according to platform policy. When null, the seller is treated as not having been logically deleted.

IShoppingMallSeller.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for modifying a seller account in the `shopping_mall_seller` Prisma model.

This DTO is used by both seller self-service and platform administrator endpoints to change mutable seller attributes such as storefront name, contact information, or lifecycle status. All properties are optional to support partial updates, and only fields that actually exist and are updatable in the `shopping_mall_seller` table are included.

System-managed fields like the primary key and timestamps are intentionally excluded, and ownership-related identifiers cannot be changed through this structure.

email.description:
Updated email address for the seller account.

Changing this field may require additional verification or business checks, and should respect uniqueness constraints at the database level.

store_name.description:
Updated public storefront name for the seller.

Subject to uniqueness and policy validation to avoid conflicts with existing sellers or prohibited terms.

oneOf.description:
Updated contact phone number for the seller’s store or business.

Clients may provide a new number string that satisfies the platform’s expected phone format.
Explicit null to clear the previously stored contact phone number for the seller account, if business rules allow removal.

contact_phone.description:
Optional contact phone update field for the seller account.

When set to a non-null string, it replaces the existing stored phone number. When explicitly set to null, it clears the stored phone number if business rules permit such removal.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle status of the seller account.

Used primarily in administrative contexts to activate, suspend, or terminate seller accounts according to platform policies.

IShoppingMallPlatformAdmin.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating platform administrator accounts in the shoppingMall platform.

Encapsulates filter, sort, and pagination criteria for querying the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model and its related role-assignment entities. This structure is used by the administrative search endpoint to locate platform admins by common attributes such as name, email, status, and creation time windows while remaining read-only.

page.description: Page number for pagination when listing platform administrator accounts. The first page is typically 1. Must be a positive integer.

limit.description: Maximum number of platform administrator records to return per page. Must be a positive integer and may be capped by server-side limits to protect performance.

search.description: Free-text search keyword applied to name, email, or other searchable fields of platform administrator accounts. Typically used for partial match queries.

status.description: Optional filter for platform administrator status, such as active or disabled, according to the status semantics defined on the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` model.

roleCode.description: Optional filter for platform administrator role, represented as a role code or identifier that maps to role definitions in `shopping_mall_admin_roles` and assignments in `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`.

createdFrom.description: Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the administrator account creation timestamp. Filters platform admins created on or after this time.

createdTo.description: Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the administrator account creation timestamp. Filters platform admins created on or before this time.

orderBy.description: Field name used to sort the platform administrator list. Typical values include createdAt, updatedAt, or displayName. The server validates and restricts to a safe subset of sortable fields.

orderDirection.description: Sort direction for the ordered list of platform administrator accounts. Common values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order.

IShoppingMallPlatformAdmin.description:
Detailed DTO representing a platform administrator account in the shoppingMall platform.

Maps to a single row in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model and exposes non-sensitive profile information suitable for internal admin consoles. Includes identifiers, contact fields, lifecycle and access status flags, and lifecycle timestamps while intentionally excluding credential secrets or low-level security metadata stored in other models such as `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` or `shopping_mall_security_events`.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the platform administrator account as defined by the primary key of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` table.

This value is generated and managed by the backend (typically as a UUID) and is used as the stable reference key when retrieving or updating a platform administrator record via API operations.

email.description:
Primary email address of the platform administrator account.

This value maps directly to the `email` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model and is used for login identification, notifications, and administrative communication. It is expected to be unique among platform administrators according to the underlying unique index and must always contain a syntactically valid email address.

displayName.description:
Human-readable display name for the platform administrator, mapped from the `name` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` table.

This value is shown in admin consoles, audit logs, and other operator-facing UIs to identify the admin user in a friendly way. It can represent a full name or an internal handle depending on platform conventions, and may be updated over time without affecting the underlying identifier.

status.description:
Lifecycle and access status of the platform administrator account, mapped from the non-nullable `status` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model.

Typical values reflect business-level states such as `active`, `suspended`, or `closed`, and this field is critical for restricting or enabling sensitive administrative operations. Business rules may constrain valid transitions between statuses, and downstream services should always consult this flag before allowing an admin to perform high-impact actions.

isActive.description:
Flag indicating whether the platform administrator account is currently active and allowed to sign in and perform administrative operations.

This field provides a normalized, boolean-friendly view of the administrator's accessibility state for consumers that prefer not to interpret detailed status strings. It should be derived consistently from the underlying `status` value and any soft-deletion semantics represented by `deletedAt` so that UIs and services can quickly determine if the admin can operate the system.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp representing when the platform administrator account was created in the system, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model and is typically set automatically on insert. It is used for audit trails, compliance reporting, and for ordering or filtering administrator accounts by creation time.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp representing when the platform administrator account was last updated, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable fields on the administrator record change. It is useful for detecting stale data, troubleshooting recent modifications, and supporting optimistic concurrency strategies.

deletedAt.description:
Soft delete timestamp indicating when the platform administrator account was logically removed from active use, if applicable.

This field maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model. When `deletedAt` is non-null, the account should be treated as logically deleted while preserving historical references in audit logs and configuration change histories. Consumers should avoid treating such accounts as fully active even if other status flags might suggest otherwise.

IShoppingMallPlatformAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating an existing platform administrator account in the shopping mall platform.

This schema contains only mutable profile and administrative metadata fields that can be changed after the administrator account has been created. Immutable identifiers such as the primary key, creation timestamps, and ownership or low-level audit fields are intentionally excluded and are managed exclusively by the backend.

It is used as the request body for `PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/platformAdmins/{platformAdminId}`. The target administrator is identified exclusively by the `platformAdminId` path parameter, so this DTO must not contain any id fields or duplicates of that path parameter. All properties are optional to support partial updates; callers provide only the fields they intend to modify.

email.description:
New primary email address for the platform administrator account, if it is being changed.

This field maps to the `email` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model and must remain unique among platform administrators according to the underlying unique index. When supplied, the value must be a syntactically valid email address and should conform to any additional business rules around allowed domains or security policies.

displayName.description:
Updated human-readable display name for the platform administrator, corresponding to the `name` column in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` table.

This field is used in admin consoles, audit logs, and other internal UIs to label the administrator. It can be changed without impacting the underlying identifier and is typically subject to reasonable length and character constraints enforced at the validation layer.

status.description:
Updated lifecycle or access status of the platform administrator account, mapped from the `status` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model.

Common values include business-defined states such as `active`, `suspended`, or `closed`. Platform-specific business rules may restrict which actors can change this field and which transitions between status values are allowed. Updating this field directly can enable or restrict access to sensitive administrative operations, so it should be used carefully within privileged workflows.

deletedAt.description:
Updated soft delete timestamp for the platform administrator account, mapped from the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model.

When set to a non-null value, the account should be considered logically deleted while still retaining historical references for auditing and reporting. Clearing this field (setting it back to null) can be used to restore an account from a soft-deleted state, subject to business and governance rules. This property is typically managed only by highly privileged administrative workflows.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for listing customer authentication sessions associated with a specific customer account.

This DTO is used as the request body of `PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/customers/{customerId}/sessions`. It provides optional filters over the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table as well as pagination and sorting controls for administrative exploration of a customer's login history.

The `customerId` itself is always supplied via the URL path and is never duplicated inside this DTO. All properties are optional so that platform administrators can either retrieve a simple paginated list or apply more restrictive filters when investigating suspicious activity or answering support questions such as when and from where a customer logged in.

page.description:
1-based page index for the result set.

When omitted, the implementation may default to the first page. This value is applied together with `limit` to compute the offset when querying `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` for the specified customer.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page.

This value controls the `LIMIT` clause when querying `shopping_mall_customer_sessions`. Implementations typically enforce an upper bound (for example 50–200) to protect the system from excessively large pages requested during administrative analysis.

oneOf.description:
Sort key applied to the session result set.

- `created_at`: order sessions by their creation time, usually used to see the most recent logins first.
- `expired_at`: order sessions by their expiry time when focusing on when sessions ended or were terminated.

If omitted, the implementation commonly defaults to `created_at` in descending order.

Sort key applied to the session result set.

- `created_at`: order sessions by their creation time, usually used to see the most recent logins first.
- `expired_at`: order sessions by their expiry time when focusing on when sessions ended or were terminated.

If omitted, the implementation commonly defaults to `created_at` in descending order.

sortBy.description:
Sort key applied to the session result set.

- `created_at`: order sessions by their creation time, usually used to see the most recent logins first.
- `expired_at`: order sessions by their expiry time when focusing on when sessions ended or were terminated.

If omitted, the implementation commonly defaults to `created_at` in descending order.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied together with `sortBy`.

- `asc`: ascending order (oldest sessions first when sorting by `created_at`).
- `desc`: descending order (newest sessions first when sorting by `created_at`).

If not provided, backends typically default to `desc` to surface the most recent sessions at the top of the list.

Sort direction applied together with `sortBy`.

- `asc`: ascending order (oldest sessions first when sorting by `created_at`).
- `desc`: descending order (newest sessions first when sorting by `created_at`).

If not provided, backends typically default to `desc` to surface the most recent sessions at the top of the list.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied together with `sortBy`.

- `asc`: ascending order (oldest sessions first when sorting by `created_at`).
- `desc`: descending order (newest sessions first when sorting by `created_at`).

If not provided, backends typically default to `desc` to surface the most recent sessions at the top of the list.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the session creation timestamp window, mapped to `shopping_mall_customer_sessions.created_at`.

Only sessions whose `created_at` is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value (in UTC) should be included. Use this to focus on more recent login activity or a specific investigation time window.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the session creation timestamp window, mapped to `shopping_mall_customer_sessions.created_at`.

Only sessions whose `created_at` is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value (in UTC) should be included. Combined with `created_from`, this produces a closed time range for login activity analysis.

expired_from.description:
Lower bound of the session expiry timestamp window, mapped to `shopping_mall_customer_sessions.expired_at`.

When provided, only sessions whose `expired_at` is greater than or equal to this value are returned. Sessions without an `expired_at` value (still active) are typically excluded from this filter unless combined with additional logic at the service layer.

expired_to.description:
Upper bound of the session expiry timestamp window, mapped to `shopping_mall_customer_sessions.expired_at`.

When provided, only sessions whose `expired_at` is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are returned. This is particularly useful when reviewing historical sessions that have already ended.

is_active.description:
Filter sessions by their active or expired state as derived from `expired_at`.

- When `true`, restrict results to sessions that are still considered active according to business rules (for example, `expired_at` is null or lies in the future).
- When `false`, restrict results to sessions that have already expired or been explicitly terminated.

If omitted, both active and expired sessions may be returned depending on other filters.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by the captured IP address value stored in `shopping_mall_customer_sessions.ip`.

Implementations may treat this as an exact match or a prefix match depending on requirements (for example, to find all sessions originating from a specific subnet). This field is primarily used during security investigations to trace sessions from specific network locations.

href_contains.description:
Substring filter applied to the `href` field of `shopping_mall_customer_sessions`.

Use this field to find sessions that were initiated from a particular page or application route (for example, a specific login entrypoint or campaign landing page) by matching a fragment of the stored URL or path.

referrer_contains.description:
Substring filter applied to the `referrer` field of `shopping_mall_customer_sessions`.

This allows administrators to locate sessions that originated from a specific referring site or marketing campaign by searching for a partial match within the recorded referrer URL.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.description:
Detailed customer authentication session information for a specific shopping_mall_customer_sessions record.

Represents a single login session created for a customer actor on the shoppingMall platform. Used only for administrative and security-operations visibility, not by end customers directly. Contains captured connection metadata and lifecycle timestamps for the session.

id.description: Unique identifier of the customer session, mapped to shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer who owns this session, mapped to shopping_mall_customer.id.

This field is stored in the database but is typically used only for scoping and joins in administrative tooling. It is read-only in this DTO.

oneOf.description: Captured IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) at the time the session was established.

ip.description:
Captured IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) at the time the session was established.

May be null if the IP address was not captured or is no longer stored for privacy reasons.

href.description:
Full URL of the page from which the login attempt that created this session originated.

Typically corresponds to the browser location.href at the time of authentication.

referrer.description:
Referring URL recorded when the session was created, usually the previous page or marketing entry point.

May be an empty string or a generic landing page URL depending on client behavior.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was established, mapped to shopping_mall_customer_sessions.created_at.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the session was explicitly expired or reached its natural end-of-life.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was explicitly expired or reached its natural end-of-life.

Null indicates that the session is still considered active according to backend rules or that expiry has not been recorded.

status.description:
Derived status of the session, such as "active" or "expired".

This is a computed field at the DTO layer based on created_at, expired_at, and any underlying status flags. Exact value set is implementation-defined.

oneOf.description: Total duration of the session in seconds, computed from created_at until expired_at or the current time.

duration_seconds.description:
Total duration of the session in seconds.

Computed from created_at until expired_at or the time of inspection. May be null if duration cannot be calculated.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.IRequest.description:
Search, filtering, and pagination criteria for listing seller authentication sessions associated with a specific seller.

Used as the request body for the administrative endpoint that lists records from shopping_mall_seller_sessions for a given sellerId. Supports basic pagination, simple time-range filtering, and optional status-based filtering suitable for security and operational investigations.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated results.

If omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return per page.

If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default page size. Upper bound is typically enforced to protect system performance.

oneOf.description:
Field name used to sort the session list.

Supported values are:
- "created_at": Sort by the time the session was established
- "expired_at": Sort by the time the session was expired or closed

Field name used to sort the session list.

Supported values are:
- "created_at": Sort by the time the session was established
- "expired_at": Sort by the time the session was expired or closed

orderBy.description:
Field name used to sort the session list.

Supported values are:
- "created_at": Sort by the time the session was established
- "expired_at": Sort by the time the session was expired or closed

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for the ordered field.

"asc" for ascending order, "desc" for descending order.

Sort direction for the ordered field.

"asc" for ascending order, "desc" for descending order.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction for the ordered field.

"asc" for ascending order, "desc" for descending order.

oneOf.description: Start of the creation time window for sessions to include in the result set.

created_from.description:
Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the creation timestamp filter.

Only sessions with created_at greater than or equal to this value are returned when specified.

oneOf.description: End of the creation time window for sessions to include in the result set.

created_to.description:
Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the creation timestamp filter.

Only sessions with created_at less than or equal to this value are returned when specified.

oneOf.description: Desired status of sessions to include, such as "active" or "expired".

status.description:
Optional status filter for sessions, such as "active" or "expired".

Exact values are implementation-defined and derived from underlying session lifecycle fields.

oneOf.description: Prefix or partial IP string to match against stored session IP addresses.

ip_like.description:
Optional IP prefix or partial string used to filter sessions by captured IP address.

Supports simple pattern-style filtering as defined by the backend implementation.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.description:
Detailed representation of a single authentication session record for a seller within the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO maps directly to a row in the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` Prisma model and is used only in read-only administrative and security-operations contexts. It exposes the session identifier, the owning seller account, and core connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) alongside temporal fields so that platform administrators can accurately inspect when and from where a given seller session was established.

Because this type is tied to the Prisma schema via `x-autobe-prisma-schema`, every property corresponds to a concrete column in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions`. No computed or synthetic fields are included, ensuring that security analysis and audit tooling always operate on consistent, database-backed attributes.

id.description:
Primary key of the seller session.

This value uniquely identifies a single authentication session record in the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` table and is used as the main handle when fetching or correlating session data from administrative tools.

seller.description:
Seller account that owns this authentication session.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key and provides a summary view of the seller identity, enabling administrators to understand which merchant is associated with the session without performing additional lookups.

ip.description:
IP address observed when the seller session was established.

This IP is captured at the time of login and represents the remote address of the client initiating the session. It is used for security investigations, anomaly detection, and regional access analysis.

href.description:
Entry URL that initiated the seller login session.

This value records the full URL (including path and query string if applicable) where the authentication flow was triggered, helping to reconstruct user navigation paths and diagnose issues related to specific entry points.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL at the time the seller session was created.

The referrer indicates the previous page or external site that led to the login flow, enabling administrators to understand cross-origin access patterns and campaign-driven traffic for security and analytics purposes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the seller session was created.

This value marks the moment the authentication process successfully completed and the session record was persisted. It is used as the primary time anchor for analyzing session lifecycles and login activity patterns.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the seller session expired or was explicitly terminated.

Once the session is no longer valid—either due to reaching its natural lifetime or explicit invalidation—this timestamp is populated. Security and operational tooling use this value to determine when the session ended in historical investigations.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the seller session expired or was explicitly terminated, or null while the session is still active.

Security and operational tooling use this value to determine whether a session should be considered live or historical when reconstructing authentication flows.

IShoppingMallPlatformadminSession.IReque.description:
Search and pagination criteria for listing authentication sessions belonging to a specific platform administrator.

This DTO does not map directly to a database table. Instead, it encapsulates the query parameters that can be applied when retrieving `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` records scoped by the `platformAdminId` path parameter. It is used exclusively as the request body of the list/search endpoint and is never persisted.

The structure of this request follows the same pagination conventions used throughout the platform (as defined conceptually by `IPage.IPagination`), and adds filters relevant to admin session auditing such as activity time windows, active-only flags, and IP or user agent substring matching.

page.description:
1-based index of the page to retrieve.

Works together with `pageSize` to paginate through the platform administrator's session records following the same semantics as `IPage.IPagination.current`. A value of 1 returns the first page of results.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single page.

This value corresponds conceptually to `IPage.IPagination.limit`. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets and to maintain predictable performance for security audit queries.

sortBy.description:
Field name used to sort session records in the result set.

Common values include `created_at` to order sessions by creation time or `last_activity_at` to order by most recently active sessions. The exact list of supported fields is implementation-specific but should be documented for administrative users.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering session records.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, implementations should apply a sensible default, such as newest sessions first.

active_only.description:
If true, restrict the result set to sessions that are currently considered active.

When this flag is set, the server should filter out sessions that are already expired or revoked according to the same logic used to compute `is_active`, `is_expired`, and `is_revoked` on the session DTO.

from_created_at.description:
Optional lower bound for session creation time.

When provided, only sessions with `created_at` greater than or equal to this timestamp are included in the results. The value must be an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string.

to_created_at.description:
Optional upper bound for session creation time.

When provided, only sessions with `created_at` less than or equal to this timestamp are included in the results. The value must be an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string.

from_last_activity_at.description:
Optional lower bound for the last activity timestamp of sessions.

When provided, only sessions whose `last_activity_at` is greater than or equal to this timestamp are returned, enabling administrators to focus on sessions that have been active within a specific window.

to_last_activity_at.description:
Optional upper bound for the last activity timestamp of sessions.

When provided, only sessions whose `last_activity_at` is less than or equal to this timestamp are returned, allowing administrators to filter out sessions that have been idle for too long.

ip_contains.description:
Optional substring filter applied to the stored IP address.

When set, the server should restrict results to sessions where the `ip` (or its normalized alias `ip_address`) contains the provided substring. This is useful for narrowing the result set to a specific network range or suspicious IP pattern.

user_agent_contains.description:
Optional substring filter applied to the user agent field.

When set, only sessions whose `user_agent` value contains the given substring are returned. This allows administrators to search for sessions originating from specific browsers, devices, or integration clients during security audits.

IShoppingMallPlatformadminSession.description:
Detailed representation of a single platform administrator authentication session within the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is the primary detail view for `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` records. It exposes both the **minimal set of fields stored in the session table** and several **derived or enriched properties** that are computed at read time for security analysis and administration.

Persisted columns from the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` Prisma model include:
- `id`: primary key for the session row.
- `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` (projected here as `platform_admin_id`): foreign key to the owning administrator account.
- `ip`: raw IP address string captured at session creation.
- `href`: entry URL that initiated the admin login session.
- `referrer`: referrer URL at the time of admin login creation.
- `created_at`: timestamp when the session record was created.
- `expired_at`: nullable timestamp indicating when the session was marked as expired.

Additional properties such as `platformAdmin`, `last_activity_at`, `expires_at`, `device`, `location`, and the boolean flags `is_active`, `is_expired`, and `is_revoked` are **derived values**. They are computed from related authentication logs, current time, and other security context rather than being stored as separate columns in the session table.

Clients can rely on all non-nullable persisted columns and core derived status flags always being present, while nullable timestamps and enrichment fields may be omitted or set to null when the underlying data is not available.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the platform administrator session.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` table and is generated when a new admin session record is created. It is used as the stable handle for referencing this session in audit logs, security tools, and administrative dashboards.

platform_admin_id.description:
Identifier of the platform administrator who owns this session.

This property is the DTO projection of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` table. It points to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` model and is used to link this session back to its administrator account.

platformAdmin.description:
Summary information about the platform administrator who owns this session.

This is a **derived projection** of the `platform_admin_id` foreign key, resolved to `IShoppingMallPlatformAdmin.ISummary`. It provides key identity fields (such as id, name, and email) needed for audit and monitoring UIs without requiring a separate lookup by the client.

ip.description:
Raw IP address captured when the session was established.

This field directly reflects the `ip` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` table. It stores the textual representation of the remote IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) observed at the time of login and is retained for security forensics and anomaly detection.

ip_address.description:
Normalized IP address representation for client consumption.

This is a convenience alias derived from the stored `ip` column. Implementations may normalize or mask the IP address for display, but the underlying value is sourced from `ip`. It is provided to make it obvious in the API that this field contains network address information for the session.

href.description:
Entry URL that initiated the admin login session.

This property maps directly to the `href` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` table. It records the full URL that the administrator was visiting when the login flow began and helps security teams understand the context in which a session was established.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL at the time of admin login creation.

This property maps directly to the `referrer` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` table. It usually reflects the `Referer` header supplied by the browser and provides additional context about where the administrator navigated from when starting the login flow.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the session record was created.

This value is persisted in the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` table, typically set to the moment when the administrator successfully authenticates and a new session entry is written. It is stored in UTC using ISO 8601 date-time format.

oneOf.description:
Non-null expiration timestamp persisted in the `expired_at` column.

When this variant is used, the value records the exact moment when the session was marked as expired in the database layer, expressed as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string.

Indicates that no explicit expiration timestamp has been persisted for this session.

When this variant is selected, the session's effective expiration is determined dynamically by business rules such as idle timeouts or token lifetimes rather than by a stored `expired_at` value.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin session was marked as expired, if any.

This property directly reflects the nullable `expired_at` column in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` table. When non-null, it records the moment when the session was considered no longer valid due to timeout or administrative action. When null, the session has not been explicitly expired in the persistence layer and its status is determined by other factors.

expires_at.description:
Normalized expiration timestamp for the session, when available.

This is a **derived convenience alias** for `expired_at` that may apply additional business rules or normalization. Implementations may omit this property or leave it unset when `expired_at` is null or when the effective expiration is determined dynamically (for example, based on rolling idle timeouts). When present, it follows ISO 8601 UTC date-time format.

last_activity_at.description:
Timestamp of the last recorded activity associated with this session, if tracked.

Unlike `created_at` and `expired_at`, this value is typically **derived from authentication or access logs** rather than stored as a separate column in the session table. It is updated when the session token is used for an authenticated request so that administrators can identify idle or abandoned sessions during security reviews.

oneOf.description:
Non-null timestamp representing the moment when the session was explicitly revoked.

This value is usually sourced from security event records or the authentication subsystem rather than from the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` table itself and is expressed in ISO 8601 UTC date-time format.

Indicates that no explicit revocation timestamp is recorded for this session.

When this variant is chosen, the session has not been directly revoked and may still be considered active or merely expired according to other rules.

revoked_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this session was explicitly revoked, if ever.

This is a **derived property** that is populated from the surrounding authentication subsystem or security events, not from a column in `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions`. When non-null, it indicates that the session was actively terminated by an administrator, by automated security rules, or as part of credential rotation. A null value indicates that no explicit revocation timestamp is recorded.

user_agent.description:
User agent string associated with the client that created or last used this session, when available.

This property is typically sourced from authentication logs or access logs rather than the session table itself. It may include browser, operating system, and device details that help security analysts fingerprint the environment associated with this session.

oneOf.description:
Human-readable description or fingerprint of the device associated with this session.

This value may be derived from user agent parsing, device fingerprinting services, or explicit client metadata supplied by the admin's browser or application.

Indicates that no device fingerprint or description is available for this session.

In many deployments, device information is not captured or cannot be reliably determined, so this field may legitimately be null.

device.description:
Optional human-readable description or fingerprint of the device associated with this session.
