This enrichment value may be derived from user agent parsing, device fingerprinting services, or explicit client metadata. It is not guaranteed to be present for all sessions and should be treated as auxiliary context when analysing suspicious activity.

oneOf.description:
Approximate geolocation string for this session, such as a city, region, or country code.

Implementations typically derive this value from the session's IP address using GeoIP or similar services and may include coarse-grained geographic descriptors only.

Indicates that no geolocation enrichment is available for this session.

When null, the platform either does not perform IP geolocation or could not determine a meaningful location for the provided IP address.

location.description:
Optional approximate geolocation associated with the session.

Implementations typically derive this value from the session's IP address using GeoIP or similar services. It is usually expressed as a combination of city, region, or country code. This field is not persisted in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` table and may be omitted when no enrichment is available.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether the session is currently considered active.

This is a **computed status flag** that combines information from `expired_at`, `revoked_at`, and the current time. When true, the session is still considered valid for authenticated operations (subject to token validation). When false, the session is no longer usable, either because it has expired, been revoked, or otherwise invalidated by the authentication subsystem.

is_expired.description:
Flag indicating whether the session has passed its effective expiration time.

This value is derived from `expired_at` (and possibly additional policy such as idle timeout rules). It is true when the session is considered expired according to business rules, even if no explicit revocation has occurred. It is false when the session is still within its allowed lifetime.

is_revoked.description:
Flag indicating whether the session has been explicitly revoked.

This status flag is computed from security events and the authentication subsystem rather than directly from the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` row. When true, the session has been deliberately terminated by an administrator or automated rule and must not be accepted for further authentication, regardless of expiration time.

IShoppingMallAuthCredentials.IRequest.description:
Search filters, pagination, and sorting options for querying authentication credential records from the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` table.

This DTO is used as the request body for search operations over platform authentication credentials. It allows internal tools and administrative UIs to filter credentials by actor type, login identifier, status flags, risk flags, and creation time ranges, as well as to specify pagination and sort ordering.

It is purely a query descriptor and does not map directly to a single Prisma model for persistence, so it intentionally omits `x-autobe-prisma-schema`. The underlying implementation translates these filters into WHERE and ORDER BY clauses on `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` and its related tables.

actor_type.description:
Optional filter by the actor type associated with these credentials.

Valid values correspond to the major actor types on the platform and typically include `customer`, `seller`, and `platformAdmin`. When omitted, credentials for all actor types may be included in the search results.

login_identifier.description:
Optional filter for an exact or partial match on the primary login identifier.

This is usually an email address or username stored in the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` table. Implementations may choose to apply case-insensitive matching or substring search depending on requirements.

status.description:
Optional high-level status filter for credentials.

Common values include `active`, `locked`, `disabled`, or `requiresPasswordReset`. When provided, search results should be limited to credentials whose stored flags map to the specified status.

has_risk_flags.description:
Optional filter indicating whether the credential has any associated risk or fraud flags.

When `true`, only credentials with `shopping_mall_risk_flags` records should be returned. When `false`, only credentials without such flags should be included. When `null` or omitted, risk flags are not considered in filtering.

created_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the credential creation timestamp.

When provided, only credentials created at or after this timestamp should be included in the results.

created_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the credential creation timestamp.

When provided, only credentials created at or before this timestamp should be included in the results.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

Pagination is typically 1-based. When omitted or null, implementations should default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page.

Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessive result sizes. When omitted or null, a sensible default limit should be applied.

cursor.description:
Opaque pagination cursor token used for cursor-based pagination strategies.

If provided, it should take precedence over `page` for pagination. When omitted or null, offset-based pagination using `page` and `limit` may be used instead.

order_by.description:
Field name used for sorting the search results.

Typical sortable fields include `created_at`, `updated_at`, or `login_identifier`. Implementations should validate the provided field name against a whitelist of allowed sort keys to prevent misuse.

order_direction.description:
Direction in which to sort the search results.

Common values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. When omitted or null, a sensible default such as `desc` on `created_at` should be applied.

IShoppingMallAuthCredentials.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of shopping mall authentication credentials for an actor.

Provides non-sensitive, high-level information about an authentication credential record for customers, sellers, or platform administrators. This summary is designed for use in admin dashboards, security overviews, and risk assessments without exposing any password hashes, salts, or secret tokens.

In addition to scalar credential metadata, this summary includes a polymorphic association to the owning actor entity and high-level risk flags, so that a single list call can show who the credential belongs to and whether it is currently considered risky, without requiring additional follow-up queries.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authentication credential record.

This is the primary key for the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` row and is used when referencing this credential in security tooling, audits, and administrative APIs.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor this credential belongs to within the shopping mall platform.

Typical values align with the underlying Prisma schema and include `customer`, `seller`, and `platformadmin`. This field is primarily useful for quickly segmenting credentials by actor category in list views and analytics. For richer actor context, use the `actor` association property of this summary.

email.description:
Login email address associated with this credential, when email-based authentication is used.

This value is safe to expose in administrative contexts but MUST NOT be accompanied by any password hashes, salts, or secret tokens. It is usually the primary username for human actors and is used for search and identification.

status.description:
Current lifecycle and access status of the authentication credentials.

This field mirrors the non-nullable `status` column on the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` Prisma model and encodes high-level states such as `active`, `locked`, `disabled`, or `requiresPasswordReset`.

Administrative dashboards, security tools, and support consoles use this value to quickly understand whether a credential can currently be used for login, whether it is temporarily locked due to risk or policy decisions, or whether a user is required to reset their password before further access is granted.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the credential record was initially created.

This value is sourced from the non-nullable `created_at` column on the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` Prisma model and is expressed as an ISO 8601 UTC datetime string.

It is commonly used in audit trails, security reviews, and administrative reporting to understand how long a credential has existed, to identify very new or very old credentials, and to support investigations into account lifecycle events.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update applied to this credential record.

This value reflects the non-nullable `updated_at` column on the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` Prisma model and is expressed as an ISO 8601 UTC datetime string.

Typical updates that change this field include password rotations, status transitions (such as locking or unlocking credentials), or other administrative modifications. Security and operations teams use this value to identify credentials that have changed recently when investigating incidents or validating that policy-driven changes have been applied.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login using this credential.

Stored as an ISO 8601 UTC datetime string when available. This value is useful for security analytics, account monitoring, and customer support investigations to understand recent authentication activity on this credential.

If the credential has never been used to successfully authenticate, this property may be omitted or set to null depending on implementation details in the response mapper.

actor.description:
Polymorphic association to the concrete actor entity that owns this credential.

Depending on `actor_type`, this association exposes a summary view of the corresponding actor record (customer, seller, or platform administrator) using their respective `.ISummary` types. This allows admin tools and security dashboards to show who a credential belongs to without additional queries.

The association strictly uses `.ISummary` projections to avoid circular reference issues and to keep the credential summary lightweight for list responses.

hasActiveRiskFlags.description:
Indicates whether there are any active risk or fraud flags attached to this credential.

This boolean is derived from related records in `shopping_mall_risk_flags` and gives a quick, high-level signal as to whether the credential is currently considered risky or under scrutiny by the risk engine.

Tools that surface credential lists can use this value to highlight or prioritize records that require additional review, without loading full risk flag details for every row.

riskFlagCount.description:
Aggregate count of risk or fraud flags associated with this credential.

This scalar count is derived from `shopping_mall_risk_flags` and provides a bounded aggregate view of risk without embedding full flag records. It is particularly useful for sorting and filtering in administrative interfaces that need to prioritize credentials with multiple issues.

If not computed by the underlying query for performance reasons, this property may be omitted from the response.

IShoppingMallPlatformAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a platform administrator account for internal dashboards, logs, and audit trails.

This summary DTO focuses on non-sensitive identity and lifecycle fields that are safe to expose in admin-facing UIs and system records. It is mapped directly to the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model for core columns such as identifier, email, status, and audit timestamps, and it may also include a derived primary role key when available.

The structure is designed to give operators a quick understanding of who the administrator is, how to contact them, and whether the account is currently active or has been modified recently, without ever including authentication credentials or secrets.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the platform administrator account.

This value maps directly to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model and is used to join with related entities such as admin sessions, role assignments, and audit records.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the platform administrator used in audit logs, dashboards, and admin consoles.

The value corresponds to the `name` column in `shopping_mall_platformadmin` and is typically the display name or full name that should be shown wherever the administrator is referenced in operator tools.

email.description:
Work email address of the platform administrator used for notifications and contact.

This field maps to the `email` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` table. It must never expose any password or credential-related information and is safe to show in internal admin tools for communication and identification purposes.

status.description:
Lifecycle and access status of the administrator account.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `status` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` Prisma model. Typical values describe whether the account is active, suspended, or closed, and downstream authorization logic uses this field to determine whether the administrator is allowed to perform sensitive operations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrator account record was created.

This value corresponds to the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` table and is returned as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. It is useful in dashboards and audit tooling to understand when the administrator first joined the platform.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the administrator account record was last updated.

This value maps to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_platformadmin` and captures the most recent change to the admin profile or status. It allows operators to quickly see how recently the account was modified when reviewing admin lists or investigating incidents.

role_key.description:
Stable key of the primary admin role currently associated with this platform administrator, such as `super_admin`, `moderator`, or other configured role identifiers.

This value is not a direct column on the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` table. Instead, it is derived from the administrator's role assignments in `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments` and the role definitions in `shopping_mall_admin_roles`. It represents the main role used by authorization logic to determine the capabilities available to this administrator, and it may be absent when no primary role is assigned.

IShoppingMallAuthCredentials.description:
Detailed authentication credential DTO for the shoppingMall platform.

This type represents a single row from the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` Prisma model combined with a small set of derived convenience fields and related risk information. It is designed for administrative inspection, security analysis, and compliance auditing, and therefore focuses on safe, non-secret metadata only.

The DTO exposes the credential identifier, actor type, login email, status, audit timestamps, and optional last login time. In addition, it provides derived boolean flags such as `isActive`, `isLocked`, and `requiresPasswordReset` that normalize the underlying `status` column into easy-to-consume indicators, as well as a derived `actorId` and a collection of associated risk flags from `shopping_mall_risk_flags`.

Sensitive data such as password hashes, salts, raw tokens, or secret material from authentication flows is **never** included in this DTO and must remain confined to secure credential storage and dedicated authentication services.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authentication credential record.

This field maps directly to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` Prisma model and is used to correlate security events, risk flags, and audit logs back to this specific credential.

actorType.description:
Type of actor that owns this credential, such as `customer`, `seller`, or `platformAdmin`.

This property is a high-level representation of the `actor_type` column in the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` table. Downstream code should treat it as an enumeration over the supported actor types in the platform and use it to decide which actor table and subtype record to join when resolving the owning identity.

actorId.description:
Identifier of the actor entity (for example a customer, seller, or platform administrator) that owns this credential.

This value is not stored directly in the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` table. Instead, it is derived by following the appropriate subtype relation such as `shopping_mall_auth_credentials_of_customers`, `shopping_mall_auth_credentials_of_sellers`, or `shopping_mall_auth_credentials_of_platformadmins` and reading the primary key of the corresponding actor record. It may be omitted in rare edge cases where the subtype link cannot be resolved.

loginIdentifier.description:
Primary login identifier for this credential, represented as an email address used during authentication.

In this deployment, the login identifier maps directly to the `email` column of the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` Prisma model and is validated as an email address. It is the value that users enter when signing in and is also used for notifications related to this credential, such as password reset or security alerts.

status.description:
Current credential status describing whether and how this credential may be used for authentication.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `status` column on the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` table. Typical values include business states such as `active`, `locked`, or `compromised`, and may also include additional platform-specific statuses that drive authentication policy decisions. Derived flags such as `isActive`, `isLocked`, and `requiresPasswordReset` are computed from this value for convenience.

isActive.description:
Indicates whether this credential is currently considered active and generally allowed to be used for successful authentication.

This boolean is a normalized view of the underlying `status` column in `shopping_mall_auth_credentials`. It evaluates to `true` when `status` represents a healthy state (for example `active`) and to `false` when the credential is locked, disabled, compromised, or otherwise prevented from normal use.

isLocked.description:
Indicates whether this credential is locked due to repeated failed attempts, suspected fraud, administrative action, or other policy conditions.

This value is derived from the `status` field of the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` record according to platform-specific rules. When `true`, authentication attempts using this credential should be rejected until an unlock workflow has been completed or an administrator clears the lock.

requiresPasswordReset.description:
Flag indicating that the owning actor must reset their password before this credential can be used for normal authentication.

This convenience flag is computed from the `status` column in `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` and any associated security events. When `true`, the platform should prompt the actor to complete a password reset flow before granting full access, for example after a suspected compromise or an administrative requirement for credential rotation.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this authentication credential record was created.

This property maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` table and is returned as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. It is commonly used in security reviews and audits to understand how long the credential has existed.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this authentication credential record was last updated.

The value corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` and tracks the most recent change to the credential, such as a password update, status transition, or reassignment to a different actor.

lastLoginAt.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login performed using this credential, if any.

This field maps to the nullable `last_login_at` column of the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials` model and is returned as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC when present. It helps administrators and security tools assess recent activity and detect dormant or potentially compromised credentials.

items.description: Summary view of a risk or fraud-related flag attached to this credential.

riskFlags.description:
Collection of risk and fraud-related flags associated with this credential.

Each entry in this array is a summary representation of a record from the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` table that references this credential. Active flags indicate current concerns that should influence authorization and operational decisions, while historical flags provide context for risk analysis, monitoring, and incident investigations.

IShoppingMallRiskFlag.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for risk flags attached to a specific authentication credential.

This request type encapsulates pagination, sorting, and high-level filter criteria that the backend translates into queries on the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` Prisma model. It is designed for platform administrators and risk services that need to inspect many flags for a single credential without manually constructing low-level database filters.

page.description:
1-based index of the page to retrieve when paginating risk flag records.

If omitted, the implementation should default to the first page. This value is used together with `limit` to compute the offset when querying the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` table.

limit.description:
Maximum number of risk flag records to include in a single page of results.

Service implementations may enforce an upper bound to protect performance. This value controls the page size when querying `shopping_mall_risk_flags` for list views and dashboards.

orderBy.description:
Field name used for sorting risk flag records, such as `created_at` or a logical severity field.

Backends typically map this value to one of the indexed columns on `shopping_mall_risk_flags`, for example `created_at` for chronological ordering or `risk_level` for severity-based ordering. Invalid field names should be rejected or normalized according to service policy.

oneOf.description:
Sort in ascending order based on the chosen `orderBy` field.

For example, when combined with `orderBy = created_at`, older risk flags appear first in the result set.

Sort in descending order based on the chosen `orderBy` field.

For example, when combined with `orderBy = created_at`, the newest risk flags appear first in the result set.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering risk flag records.

The direction is evaluated in combination with `orderBy` to determine the final ordering in the query against `shopping_mall_risk_flags`.

types.description:
Optional list of logical risk flag types or codes to include in the result set.

Implementations typically map these values to one or more internal classifications associated with each row in `shopping_mall_risk_flags`, such as specific rule identifiers or subcategories derived from `reason_category`. When empty or omitted, flags of all types are considered.

statuses.description:
Optional list of status values used to filter risk flags, for example values that map to active versus cleared states.

Backends usually interpret these status strings in terms of the `active` and `cleared_at` columns on `shopping_mall_risk_flags` (for example, treating a flag as "active" when `active = true` and `cleared_at` is null, or as "cleared" when `active = false` and `cleared_at` is set). The exact status vocabulary is defined by business rules.

minSeverity.description:
Optional minimum severity threshold.

This value is often interpreted as the lowest numeric level that should be included when the implementation maps the `risk_level` string column to an ordinal scale. For example, a backend might map `low = 1`, `medium = 2`, `high = 3`, `critical = 4` and then filter out flags whose derived severity is below this threshold.

maxSeverity.description:
Optional maximum severity threshold.

Similar to `minSeverity`, this value is applied after mapping `risk_level` to an ordinal scale, limiting the result set to flags whose derived severity is less than or equal to the threshold. When both `minSeverity` and `maxSeverity` are provided, the backend returns flags whose severity lies within the inclusive range.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for the risk flag creation timestamp.

Only flags with `created_at` greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are returned. This allows administrators to focus on recent incidents or a specific investigation window.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound for the risk flag creation timestamp.

Only flags with `created_at` less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are returned. When used together with `createdFrom`, this defines a closed time window for querying `shopping_mall_risk_flags`.

IShoppingMallRiskFlag.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a risk or fraud-related flag attached to an actor's authentication credentials in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is a lightweight projection of the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` Prisma model and is optimized for use in paginated admin and risk dashboards where many flags must be scanned quickly. It exposes only non-sensitive business attributes that are useful for assessing overall risk posture and deciding which flags require deeper investigation.

The summary is typically embedded inside higher-level list responses such as `IPageIShoppingMallRiskFlag.ISummary`. For full detail, including any additional internal metadata not surfaced here, the platform can offer dedicated detail endpoints that return the corresponding full `IShoppingMallRiskFlag` representation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the risk flag record.

This value corresponds directly to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` table. It is used in follow-up detail or mutation operations, for example when clearing or escalating a specific risk flag associated with an authentication credential.

shopping_mall_auth_credentials_id.description:
Identifier of the authentication credential record this risk flag is attached to.

The value is the foreign key to `shopping_mall_auth_credentials.id` and ties the risk flag to a specific set of login credentials or actor identity. Admin tools and risk engines commonly use this field when joining risk flags to accounts, sessions, and security event histories.

risk_level.description:
Risk severity level assigned to this flag, such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`.

This string is derived from the `risk_level` column of the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` Prisma model and is used by risk engines and administrative UIs to prioritize workqueues and to highlight the most severe issues first. Implementations may enforce a controlled vocabulary through business logic even though the underlying column is a string.

reason_category.description:
Categorized reason for this risk flag, for example `suspected_fraud`, `abuse_reports`, `chargeback_history`, or `account_compromise`.

The value comes from the `reason_category` column of the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` table and groups similar incidents so that dashboards and analysts can filter and aggregate by cause. Downstream tools should rely on these categories rather than free-form text when building analytics or automated workflows.

active.description:
Indicates whether this risk flag is currently active and should affect authorization decisions.

When `true`, the flag must be considered by access-control and risk evaluation logic, potentially restricting operations or triggering additional checks. When `false`, the record is retained for historical and analytical purposes but should not constrain new operations for the associated credential.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes describing the context or evidence behind the risk assessment for internal risk and support teams.

This text is mapped from the nullable `notes` column of the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` Prisma model. It may contain analyst comments, links to external case systems, or investigation outcomes. Frontend applications should treat this information as internal-only and avoid exposing it directly to end users.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the risk flag was created.

The value comes from the non-nullable `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` table and is returned as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. It allows auditors and analysts to understand when the risk was first detected and to correlate the event with other security or transactional activity.

cleared_at.description:
Timestamp when the risk flag was cleared, downgraded, or otherwise deactivated, if ever.

This value is mapped from the nullable `cleared_at` column in `shopping_mall_risk_flags`. When present, it indicates that the underlying risk condition has been addressed or no longer applies. When absent or undefined in this DTO, the flag is considered still active, and the `active` property should typically be `true`.

IShoppingMallRiskFlag.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new risk or fraud-related flag record associated with a specific authentication credential in the shopping mall platform. This request body is used by privileged platform administrators or automated risk engines to record a new risk evaluation outcome (for example suspicious login pattern or multiple failed payments) for a given credentials record identified by the authCredentialsId path parameter.

Only business-writable fields from the shopping_mall_risk_flags model are exposed here. Identity and system-managed fields such as the primary key, foreign key to shopping_mall_auth_credentials, and timestamp fields are set by the backend and therefore not included in this create schema.

code.description:
Machine-readable risk flag code that uniquely identifies the type of risk or fraud scenario being recorded for this credentials record.

Typical examples include values like "suspicious_login_pattern", "multiple_failed_payments", "high_chargeback_ratio", or other codes used by the platform’s fraud and risk engines. This value is used by downstream authorization and monitoring logic to group and interpret risk flags.

reasonCategory.description:
Higher-level reason category that classifies the risk flag for reporting and moderation workflows.

Examples include categories such as "suspected_fraud", "abuse_reports", "chargeback_history", or "account_compromise". The exact allowed values should follow the enums or business taxonomies defined next to the shopping_mall_risk_flags Prisma model.

riskLevel.description:
Severity level of this risk flag, expressing how critical the underlying risk assessment is for the associated credentials.

Typical values follow a small ordered set such as "low", "medium", "high", or "critical". Implementations should use the risk_level enum or constraints declared on the shopping_mall_risk_flags Prisma model to validate incoming values.

message.description:
Human-readable descriptive message explaining the reason for the risk flag and any relevant context for administrators or security operators.

This is intended for display in admin consoles and security tooling, and may include short summaries like "Multiple failed payment attempts from new device" or "Chargeback ratio exceeded platform threshold".

active.description:
Indicates whether this risk flag is currently active and should influence authorization decisions and risk evaluations.

Newly created flags are typically active by default. When later cleared through an update operation, active may be set to false while a clearedAt timestamp is recorded in the underlying Prisma model.

expiresAt.description:
Optional expiration timestamp for this risk flag in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When provided, the risk management subsystem may automatically treat the flag as expired after this moment, even if active remains true at database level. When omitted or null, the flag is treated as open-ended until explicitly cleared or updated.

notes.description:
Optional additional internal notes or comments used by administrators or automated systems to store extra diagnostic information about this risk flag.

These notes are not intended for end users and may contain operational details, ticket references, or links to external investigation systems.

IShoppingMallRiskFlag.description:
Full representation of a risk or fraud-related flag record stored in the shopping_mall_risk_flags table.

A risk flag is attached to a specific authentication credentials record and captures a discrete risk evaluation outcome, such as suspicious login behavior, repeated payment failures, or excessive chargebacks. These flags are used by authorization and risk engines to adjust what actions an actor can perform in the platform.

This DTO exposes all non-sensitive fields required by administrative consoles and security tooling to understand the lifecycle and status of a risk flag, including severity, categorization, activation state, internal notes, timestamps, and a summarized view of the owning credentials. It intentionally omits direct credential authentication secrets while still providing both a foreign key reference and an associated credentials summary object.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the risk flag record in the shopping_mall_risk_flags table.

This value is generated by the backend and is used as the primary key for retrieving and updating this risk flag.

authCredentialsId.description:
Identifier of the authentication credentials record in shopping_mall_auth_credentials to which this risk flag is attached.

This is a foreign key reference, typically aligning with the shopping_mall_risk_flags.shopping_mall_auth_credentials_id column. It allows admin tools to correlate risk flags with their owning credentials without exposing credential secrets.

credentials.description:
Summarized view of the authentication credentials record that owns this risk flag.

This association provides essential contextual information—such as actor type, identifier, and status—without exposing sensitive credential secrets, enabling admin consoles and risk tooling to render a complete view of the flag and its owner in a single read operation.

code.description:
Machine-readable risk flag code that uniquely identifies the type of risk or fraud scenario being recorded for this credentials record.

Examples include values such as "suspicious_login_pattern", "multiple_failed_payments", or "high_chargeback_ratio". Used by downstream logic to group, filter, and evaluate risk flags across actors.

reasonCategory.description:
Higher-level reason category classifying this risk flag for reporting and moderation workflows.

Typical values include categories such as "suspected_fraud", "abuse_reports", "chargeback_history", or "account_compromise". The exact allowed values are determined by the enums or business taxonomy associated with the shopping_mall_risk_flags Prisma model.

riskLevel.description:
Severity level of this risk flag, expressing how critical the underlying risk assessment is.

Common values follow a small ordered set such as "low", "medium", "high", or "critical" and should correspond to the risk_level enum or similar constraint defined on the Prisma model.

message.description:
Human-readable descriptive message explaining the reason for the risk flag and any relevant context for administrators or security operators.

Displayed in admin consoles and internal tooling to assist in incident review and fraud investigation.

active.description:
Indicates whether this risk flag is currently active and influences authorization decisions and risk scoring.

When true, the flag is considered to represent a current risk condition. When false, the flag has typically been cleared or superseded but is retained for historical and audit purposes.

expiresAt.description:
Optional expiration timestamp for this risk flag in ISO 8601 date-time format.

If set, risk evaluation logic may treat the flag as expired after this instant, independent of the active field. If null, the flag persists until explicitly updated or cleared.

notes.description:
Optional internal notes or comments storing extra diagnostic information about this risk flag.

These notes are intended for administrators and automated systems, not for end-user display, and may contain investigation references or operational details.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this risk flag record was created in the system, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value is system-managed by the database or application layer and is useful for auditing when the risk evaluation was recorded.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating the last time this risk flag record was updated, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This field is automatically maintained by the persistence layer whenever mutable attributes of the risk flag are changed, such as status, notes, or risk level.

clearedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this risk flag was cleared or resolved, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This field is typically set when active transitions from true to false and may be null for flags that are still active or have never been explicitly cleared.

IShoppingMallRiskFlag.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing risk flag record in the shopping_mall_risk_flags table for a specific authentication credential.

This type allows platform administrators to modify mutable attributes such as riskLevel, reasonCategory, activation state, notes, and optionally clearedAt. Immutable fields like id, shopping_mall_auth_credentials_id, and created_at are intentionally excluded so they cannot be manipulated via the API.

Used as the request body for the PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/authCredentials/{authCredentialsId}/riskFlags/{riskFlagId} endpoint.

riskLevel.description:
Risk severity level associated with this flag.

Common values include low, medium, high, and critical. Implementations may enforce this via an enum in the underlying Prisma schema or application layer. Represents how strongly this flag should influence fraud and abuse decisions.

reasonCategory.description:
High-level classification for why this risk flag exists.

Typical categories include suspected_fraud, abuse_reports, chargeback_history, and account_compromise. Used by risk engines and administrators to understand and filter risk flag types.

active.description:
Indicates whether this risk flag is currently active and should influence authorization and risk decisions.

When changed from true to false, the implementation usually sets clearedAt to the current timestamp if not provided in the update payload. Reactivating a flag (setting from false to true) may clear or leave clearedAt null depending on business policy.

notes.description:
Optional internal notes with additional context about this risk flag, such as investigation details, evidence, or remediation steps.

This field is intended for internal administrator and security operator use and is never exposed to end users.

clearedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this risk flag was cleared or resolved.

When the active field transitions from true to false, implementations typically set this to the current time if it is not explicitly specified. When a flag is reactivated, business rules may clear this value back to null.

IShoppingMallEmailVerificationToken.IReq.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying email verification tokens belonging to a specific authentication credential.

This type is used as the request body for the PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/authCredentials/{authCredentialsId}/emailVerificationTokens endpoint, enabling platform administrators to filter tokens by status, email address, and time windows while also controlling pagination and sorting.

It does not map directly to a single Prisma model table because it represents query parameters rather than a persisted entity.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

Defaults to 1 when omitted. Combined with pageSize to determine the offset into the email verification token result set.

pageSize.description:
Number of email verification token records to return per page.

Implementations should enforce an upper bound (for example 100 or 200) to prevent excessively large result sets that could harm performance.

status.description:
Optional filter for token status.

Typical statuses include pending, verified, and expired. Used by administrators to quickly locate tokens in a particular lifecycle state.

email.description:
Optional filter for the email address associated with the token.

Implementations may support exact match, prefix match, or substring search depending on business requirements. Used to narrow results to verification tokens for a specific email.

issuedFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the token issuance time range filter.

Only tokens with issuedAt greater than or equal to this value should be included in the results.

issuedTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the token issuance time range filter.

Only tokens with issuedAt less than or equal to this value should be included in the results.

expiresBefore.description:
Upper bound filter for token expiration.

Only email verification tokens whose expiration timestamp is earlier than or equal to this value should be included.

expiresAfter.description:
Lower bound filter for token expiration.

Only email verification tokens whose expiration timestamp is later than or equal to this value should be included.

sortBy.description:
Field name to sort results by.

Common options include issuedAt and expiresAt. Implementations should validate this field against an allowed set of sortable columns to avoid unsafe dynamic ordering.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction for the result set.

Expected values are asc for ascending or desc for descending. When omitted, implementations commonly default to desc to show newest tokens first.

IShoppingMallPasswordResetToken.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying password reset token records associated with a specific authentication credentials entry in the `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens` table.

This DTO is used exclusively by platform administrators to perform complex, read-only searches over password reset token history for a single credentials record identified by the `authCredentialsId` path parameter. All filters are optional and are applied in addition to the mandatory foreign-key scope on `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.shopping_mall_auth_credentials_id`.

The fields in this request are intentionally aligned with concrete Prisma columns on `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens`, such as `token`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, and `consumed_at`, so that backend implementations can build straightforward, type-safe queries without inventing synthetic status fields or derived columns.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated results.

If omitted, the implementation should treat this as page 1. This value is used together with `limit` to determine the slice of matching password reset token records to return.

limit.description:
Maximum number of password reset token records to return in a single page.

Backends may enforce an upper bound to protect performance and should clamp or reject excessively large values according to platform-wide pagination policy.

token.description:
Optional filter for the opaque password reset token string stored in `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.token`.

This filter is primarily intended for security operations and support tooling where a specific token value (for example, copied from a log or external system) needs to be looked up precisely. Implementations may perform exact or implementation-defined matching, but MUST NOT expose or log token values inappropriately when processing this field.

createdAtFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound for the token creation timestamp filter mapped to `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.created_at`.

Only token records whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be included in the result set.

createdAtTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound for the token creation timestamp filter mapped to `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.created_at`.

Only token records whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be included in the result set.

expiresAtFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound for password reset token expiration time filtering mapped to `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.expires_at`.

Only tokens whose `expires_at` value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be returned.

expiresAtTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound for password reset token expiration time filtering mapped to `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.expires_at`.

Only tokens whose `expires_at` value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be returned.

consumed.description:
Optional flag indicating whether to limit results based on whether the token has been consumed, as derived from `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.consumed_at`.

When `true`, only tokens whose `consumed_at` column is non-null should be returned. When `false`, only tokens with `consumed_at` = null (i.e. not yet consumed) should be returned. When omitted, both consumed and unconsumed tokens are included unless further restricted by other filters.

consumedAtFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound for filtering tokens based on the moment they were consumed, mapped to `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.consumed_at`.

Only tokens whose `consumed_at` value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be returned. Records with `consumed_at` = null are not affected by this filter.

consumedAtTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound for filtering tokens based on the moment they were consumed, mapped to `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens.consumed_at`.

Only tokens whose `consumed_at` value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be returned. Records with `consumed_at` = null are not affected by this filter.

sortBy.description:
Field name to use for sorting the password reset tokens within the scoped credentials entry.

Typical supported values should correspond to concrete columns on `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens`, such as `created_at`, `expires_at`, or `consumed_at`. Backends should validate or normalize this value and fall back to a safe default if an unsupported column name is provided.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering password reset tokens by the field specified in `sortBy` in ascending order.

For example, when `sortBy` is `created_at`, this returns the oldest tokens first.

Sort direction to apply when ordering password reset tokens by the field specified in `sortBy` in descending order.

For example, when `sortBy` is `created_at`, this returns the most recently created tokens first.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering password reset tokens by the field specified in `sortBy`.

Allowed values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the backend should apply its default sort direction, typically descending by `created_at`.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying administrator role definitions from the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table.

This DTO powers administrative management consoles and back-office tooling that need to list and inspect platform administrator roles. It supports pagination, sorting, and filtering by fields that correspond directly to Prisma columns such as `code`, `name`, `description_text`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`.

All fields are optional filters. The request is strictly read-only and is typically used via a PATCH-as-search endpoint that returns a paginated list of `IShoppingMallAdminRole.ISummary` records for platform administrators with appropriate privileges.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated admin role results.

If omitted, the implementation should treat this as page 1. This value is combined with `limit` to compute the slice of matching role definitions that will be returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of administrator role records to return in a single page.

Backends may enforce a maximum value to protect performance and should clamp or reject excessively large limits according to platform-wide pagination policy.

code.description:
Optional filter for the unique role code or slug stored in `shopping_mall_admin_roles.code`.

When provided, the backend should restrict results to roles whose `code` matches this value according to the platform's matching rules (commonly an exact, case-insensitive match).

name.description:
Optional substring filter applied to the human-readable role name stored in `shopping_mall_admin_roles.name`.

When provided, only roles whose `name` contains this text (according to the implementation's collation and search configuration) should be returned.

includeDeleted.description:
Controls whether soft-deleted role definitions, identified by a non-null `shopping_mall_admin_roles.deleted_at` column, are included in the result set.

When `false` or omitted, only roles with `deleted_at` = null (i.e. active and assignable definitions) should be returned. When `true`, rows with non-null `deleted_at` may also be included to support audit and historical views of the role catalog.

createdAtFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound for role creation time filtering mapped to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.created_at`.

Only roles whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be included in the results.

createdAtTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound for role creation time filtering mapped to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.created_at`.

Only roles whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be included in the results.

updatedAtFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound for last-update time filtering mapped to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.updated_at`.

Only roles whose `updated_at` value is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be included, which is useful for finding recently changed role definitions.

updatedAtTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound for last-update time filtering mapped to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.updated_at`.

Only roles whose `updated_at` value is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 UTC timestamp should be included in the results.

sortBy.description:
Field name to use for sorting administrator roles within the result set.

Typical supported values should correspond to concrete columns on `shopping_mall_admin_roles`, such as `code`, `name`, `created_at`, or `updated_at`. Backends should validate or normalize this value and fall back to a safe default if an unsupported column name is provided.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction to apply to the field specified in `sortBy` in ascending order.

For example, when `sortBy` is `created_at`, this returns the earliest-created roles first.

Sort direction to apply to the field specified in `sortBy` in descending order.

For example, when `sortBy` is `created_at`, this returns the most recently created roles first.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply to the field specified in `sortBy`.

Allowed values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the backend should apply its default sort direction, commonly ascending by `code` or descending by `created_at` depending on UI needs.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.description:
Full representation of a platform administrator role in the shopping mall system.

This schema models records from the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma table, which defines the available role types that can be assigned to platform administrator accounts. Each role has a stable UUID primary key `id`, a globally unique machine-friendly `code` (such as `SUPER_ADMIN` or `SUPPORT_AGENT`), a human-readable `name`, optional descriptive text, and lifecycle timestamps for auditing.

Instances of this type are returned from role management APIs such as the PUT `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/adminRoles/{adminRoleCode}` operation after updates. Clients use this representation to render role configuration screens and to understand the current definition and lifecycle state of each role.

id.description:
UUID primary key of the admin role record, corresponding to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.id`.

This is an internal identifier generated by the database and used as the primary key in relations such as `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`. It is returned in responses for traceability but is not used as the primary business identifier in URLs.

code.description:
Globally unique machine-friendly code for the admin role, mapped to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.code`.

This value acts as the stable business identifier for the role and is used in API paths (for example, `{adminRoleCode}` in `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/adminRoles/{adminRoleCode}`). Typical examples include `SUPER_ADMIN`, `SUPPORT_AGENT`, or `RISK_ANALYST`. Once created, this code should remain stable to avoid breaking existing integrations.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the admin role mapped to the `name` column of the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` model.

This field is shown in admin dashboards and configuration screens to describe the role in a friendly way (for example, `Super Administrator` or `Customer Support Agent`). It can be updated using the `IShoppingMallAdminRole.IUpdate` DTO.

description_text.description:
Optional long-form description of the admin role, mapped to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.description_text`.

This text can document the responsibilities, permissions, and intended usage of the role for administrators. When `null`, it indicates that no descriptive text has been set.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this admin role record was first created, mapped to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.created_at`.

Stored in ISO 8601 date-time format with timezone information. It is managed exclusively by the backend and is useful for audit trails and historical analysis.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this admin role record, mapped to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.updated_at`.

This value is refreshed automatically whenever mutable fields such as `name` or `description_text` are modified.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-deletion timestamp for this role, mapped to `shopping_mall_admin_roles.deleted_at`.

When `null`, the role is considered active and may be used for assignments. When set to a date-time value, the role is considered logically deleted or deactivated and should no longer be assignable, although historical role assignments may still reference it for audit purposes.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.ICreate.description:
Request body DTO for creating a new platform administrator role in the shopping mall backend.

Carries the business-facing attributes required to insert a new row into the shopping_mall_admin_roles table, excluding system-generated fields such as id and timestamps. The backend enforces uniqueness of the code field and initializes created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at automatically.

code.description: Machine-friendly unique business code for the new admin role. Used as a stable identifier in URLs and configuration references (for example SUPER_ADMIN or SUPPORT_AGENT). Must be unique within shopping_mall_admin_roles.

name.description: Human-readable display name for the new admin role, shown in admin configuration UIs.

oneOf.description:
Non-null descriptive text provided at creation time to explain the responsibilities, scope, and intended usage of the new admin role. This text is visible to platform operators configuring admin permissions.

This branch applies when callers send a concrete description string.
Null branch indicating that no description text is provided when creating the admin role. When this variant is used, the role will be stored without additional descriptive metadata.

description_text.description:
Optional descriptive text for the new admin role, stored as a nullable string.

When non-null, this value documents the responsibilities, scope, and intended usage of the role so that platform operators and auditors understand what the role represents.
When null, the role is created without additional descriptive metadata beyond its code and name.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating an existing platform administrator role in the shopping mall system.

This schema represents the mutable fields of the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma model that platform administrators are allowed to change via the role update API. It is used as the request body for the PUT `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/adminRoles/{adminRoleCode}` endpoint, where `adminRoleCode` in the path identifies which role to update.

The DTO intentionally excludes system-managed fields such as the primary key `id`, the business identifier `code`, and lifecycle timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`). These values are controlled by the backend and must never be supplied by clients. Only human-readable attributes like the display `name` and descriptive text are exposed for modification. The backend will validate and then apply changes to the underlying Prisma model, refreshing `updated_at` automatically.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the admin role that appears in management UIs and configuration screens.

This field maps to the `name` column of the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma model. It should be concise but descriptive enough for platform operators to understand the purpose of the role (for example, `Super Administrator`, `Support Agent`, or `Risk Analyst`). Implementations may enforce non-empty values and length constraints (such as 1–100 characters) during validation.

description_text.description:
Optional long-form description for the admin role that explains its responsibilities, scope, and typical usage.

This field corresponds to the nullable `description_text` column on the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma model. When provided, it can be used in admin consoles or documentation to help platform owners understand when and how the role should be assigned. It may be set to `null` to explicitly clear any existing description.

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.IReques.description:
Search, filter, and pagination criteria for listing admin role assignments belonging to a specific platform administrator.

This DTO is used as the request body for the PATCH `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/platformAdmins/{platformAdminId}/roleAssignments` endpoint. It controls which rows from the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments` Prisma table are returned and how they are ordered. The path parameter `platformAdminId` identifies the administrator whose assignments are being inspected.

The schema supports typical list concerns such as paging, sorting, and filtering by activity status or associated role identifiers. It does not contain any actor identity fields, and it is read-only with respect to the underlying data; write operations that create or revoke assignments use separate DTOs and endpoints.

page.description:
1-based index of the page to retrieve when listing role assignments.

If omitted, the backend should default this to 1. Combined with `limit`, this parameter defines which slice of the assignment list is returned to the caller.

limit.description:
Maximum number of role assignment records to return per page.

Typical valid ranges might be between 1 and 100. If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default such as 20 to prevent unbounded result sets.

active_only.description:
Flag indicating whether the query should return only currently active role assignments.

When set to `true`, the backend should return only rows where `revoked_at` is null, representing active assignments. When `false` or omitted, both active and historical (revoked) assignments may be included according to other filters.

role_codes.description:
Optional list of admin role codes used to filter assignments by role.

Each entry should match the `code` field of a record in `shopping_mall_admin_roles` (for example, `SUPER_ADMIN` or `SUPPORT_AGENT`). When provided, only assignments that reference roles whose codes are in this list should be included in the results.

assigned_from.description:
Start of the date-time range filter applied to the `assigned_at` column.

When specified, only assignments with `assigned_at` greater than or equal to this value are included. A `null` value explicitly clears this lower bound.

assigned_to.description:
End of the date-time range filter applied to the `assigned_at` column.

When specified, only assignments with `assigned_at` less than or equal to this value are returned. A `null` value explicitly clears this upper bound.

revoked_from.description:
Start of the date-time range filter applied to the `revoked_at` column.

Useful when querying historical assignment revocations. When specified, only assignments with `revoked_at` greater than or equal to this value are included. A `null` value explicitly clears this lower bound filter.

revoked_to.description:
End of the date-time range filter applied to the `revoked_at` column.

When set, only assignments with `revoked_at` less than or equal to this date-time are included. A `null` value explicitly clears this upper bound filter.

order_by.description:
Field name used for sorting the result set of role assignments.

Typical allowed values include `assigned_at` and `revoked_at`, possibly extended by the implementation to support additional indexed columns. Implementations should validate supplied values against a whitelist to avoid unsafe dynamic ordering.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the `order_by` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. If omitted, the backend should default to a sensible value such as `desc` (most recent assignments first).

Sort direction applied to the `order_by` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. If omitted, the backend should default to a sensible value such as `desc` (most recent assignments first).

order_direction.description:
Sort direction applied to the `order_by` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. If omitted, the backend should default to a sensible value such as `desc` (most recent assignments first).

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new admin role assignment that links a platform administrator to a specific administrative role.

This DTO is used by platform administrators to grant a new role to another platform administrator (or themselves) in the shopping mall back-office. The server derives the owning platform admin from the path parameter `platformAdminId`, so the body only needs to specify the role being assigned and any optional metadata permitted by the assignment model.

shopping_mall_admin_role_id.description:
Identifier of the admin role to assign to the target platform administrator.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.shopping_mall_admin_role_id` and must correspond to an existing record in `shopping_mall_admin_roles`. The combination of the path-derived `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` and this role id must be unique, otherwise the server will reject the request with a conflict or validation error.

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for admin role assignments in the shopping mall platform.

This type represents the subset of fields on the shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments Prisma model that are allowed to change after the assignment has been created. It is used by administrative workflows when adjusting the lifecycle of an assignment, such as shifting the effective period of a role without changing the owning administrator or the underlying role definition.

System-managed identifiers and immutable relations, including the primary key id and foreign keys to shopping_mall_platformadmin and shopping_mall_admin_roles, are intentionally excluded from this DTO so that ownership and identity of the assignment cannot be altered through update APIs. Only temporal lifecycle fields are expected to be updated through this structure in normal business flows.

assigned_at.description:
Optional new effective start time for the admin role assignment.

This field maps directly to the assigned_at column in shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments. When supplied, it allows operators to correct or adjust when a role assignment is considered to have begun, for example when backdating an assignment after manual approval steps. When omitted, the existing assigned_at value remains unchanged.

oneOf.description:
New revocation time for the admin role assignment.

This value corresponds to the revoked_at column on shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments and marks when the role assignment should be treated as no longer active. Setting this to a non-null timestamp transitions the assignment into an ended state from the specified moment onward.

Explicitly clear the revocation time of the admin role assignment.

When revoked_at is set to null, the corresponding column on shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments is reset so that the assignment is treated as open-ended again. This is used when reactivating an assignment that was previously marked as revoked or expired.

revoked_at.description:
Revocation timestamp control for the admin role assignment.

This property wraps the revoked_at column of the shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments table and allows either setting a concrete end-of-validity timestamp or explicitly clearing it back to null. Using a non-null ISO 8601 timestamp ends the assignment as of that moment, while using null reopens the assignment so it is considered active again until a new revocation time is stored.

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.description:
Detailed representation of an admin role assignment that links a platform administrator to a specific administrative role.

This DTO mirrors a row in the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments` table and is returned by read, create, and update operations dealing with platform admin role assignments. It exposes identifiers, associated administrator and role summaries, and lifecycle timestamps for auditing and governance.

The owning platform administrator context is derived from the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` record and the corresponding API path parameters, while the assigned role is resolved from `shopping_mall_admin_roles`. The assignment can be marked as revoked via the `revoked_at` timestamp while still remaining in the system for historical traceability.

id.description:
Primary key of the admin role assignment record in `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments`.

This identifier is generated by the system when the assignment is created and is used to address the assignment in subsequent read and update operations.

platform_admin.description:
Summary of the platform administrator who owns this role assignment.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` foreign key pointing to `shopping_mall_platformadmin`. It provides enough information to identify and display the administrator in administrative UIs without exposing the raw foreign key column.

admin_role.description:
Summary of the administrative role granted to the platform administrator.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments.shopping_mall_admin_role_id` foreign key pointing to `shopping_mall_admin_roles`. It provides the role code and display information needed to understand the granted permissions without exposing low-level foreign key values.

assigned_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this role assignment became effective.

This value is typically set to the current server time when the assignment is created and is used for audit and governance reporting.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when this role assignment was revoked.

When non-null, the assignment is considered inactive from this moment onward but retained for historical purposes.

Null when the role assignment is currently active.

A null value indicates that no revocation time has been recorded yet and the assignment continues to be treated as effective.

revoked_at.description:
Nullable revocation timestamp for the role assignment.

If null, the assignment is currently active. If set to a specific date-time, the assignment is treated as revoked from that instant while remaining in the database for historical and audit purposes.

IShoppingMallSecurityEvent.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering DTO for querying security events in the shopping mall platform.

This request shape is used by multiple PATCH endpoints that read from the shopping_mall_security_events Prisma model. It allows callers to express structured filters over security event attributes, including event type, actor information, time ranges, and metadata, together with pagination and sorting controls.

The DTO is purely read-oriented and does not create, modify, or delete any rows. It is designed for administrative monitoring dashboards and per-actor security views such as those for customers, sellers, and platform administrators.

page.description:
Page index for paginated security event queries.

This value represents the 1-based page number to retrieve from the result set. When omitted, implementations typically default to the first page so that the newest security events are shown first in dashboards.

limit.description:
Maximum number of security event records to return in a single page.

This value controls page size for pagination when querying shopping_mall_security_events. Implementations may enforce an upper bound, such as 50 or 100, to keep queries performant even when the table contains large volumes of historical events.

id.description:
Optional filter restricting results to a single security event identified by its primary key in `shopping_mall_security_events`.

This value maps directly to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_security_events` Prisma model. When provided, it allows administrative tools and dashboards to narrow down search results to a specific event when performing drill-down investigations or when cross-linking from other log tables that reference a security event by its identifier.

auth_credentials_id.description:
Optional filter targeting all security events associated with a specific authentication credentials record.

This value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_auth_credentials_id` foreign key column on the `shopping_mall_security_events` table. When supplied, the query should restrict results to events that are directly linked to the given credentials row, enabling focused security and risk analysis for a single account across different time windows and event categories.

event_type.description:
Optional filter restricting results to security events with a specific event_type value.

The event_type column on shopping_mall_security_events stores machine-friendly event categories such as LOGIN_SUCCESS, LOGIN_FAILURE, PASSWORD_RESET_REQUEST, or TOKEN_REVOKED. Providing a value here narrows the query to events of one particular category, simplifying targeted investigations.

actor_type.description:
Optional filter restricting results to security events where actor_type matches the given value.

In the shopping_mall_security_events model, actor_type distinguishes kinds of actors such as customer, seller, platformAdmin, or guestUser. Using this filter helps focus on events for a single actor segment when building specialized views for each role.

actor_identifier.description:
Optional filter matching the actor_identifier column on shopping_mall_security_events.

This field is typically used when security events cannot be linked directly to shopping_mall_auth_credentials but still carry a non-sensitive identifier such as an email address or masked login string. It is useful for tracing anomalous activity tied to a particular identifier even before credential linkage is fully resolved.

ip.description:
Optional filter applied to the ip column on shopping_mall_security_events.

When supplied, this restricts results to security events observed from a particular IP address or IP address pattern. It supports basic threat hunting workflows, for example focusing on failed logins originating from a suspicious source.

user_agent.description:
Optional filter applied to the user_agent column on shopping_mall_security_events.

This filter can be used to focus on events generated from particular device classes, browser families, or normalized user agent signatures, helping analysts spot unusual client characteristics during investigations.

metadata.description:
Optional free-text or structured filter applied to the metadata column of shopping_mall_security_events.

The metadata field typically contains JSON-encoded or structured text with additional event context, such as risk rule identifiers, geoip information, or error codes. This filter can be used for simple substring searches or more advanced query strategies depending on the implementation.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the created_at time window to include in the search.

When this value is provided, only security events whose created_at column is greater than or equal to the specified timestamp are returned. It is commonly used to restrict queries to recent events, such as the last 24 hours or last 7 days.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the created_at time window to include in the search.

When this value is provided, only security events whose created_at column is less than or equal to the specified timestamp are returned. Combined with created_from, it allows building precise time range filters, for example for incident-specific forensics.

IShoppingMallSecurityEvent.description:
Security-related event row stored in the `shopping_mall_security_events` Prisma model, associated with identities, credentials, and sessions in the shoppingMall platform for monitoring, forensics, and risk analysis.

For the `GET /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/securityEvents/{securityEventId}` operation, this DTO represents a **single, immutable log record** from the `shopping_mall_security_events` table. Each property corresponds either to a concrete column on that model (for example, identifiers, timestamps, actor and session references, event type, severity, and network attributes) or to a well-defined JSON metadata column that persists structured diagnostic information. The API must not introduce arbitrary synthetic or computed fields that are not backed by the underlying schema.

This type is intended exclusively for privileged administrative and security-operations use cases, such as SOC analysts and incident responders, and is returned only from admin-only, read-only endpoints. It must never be exposed to regular customers, sellers, or guests, and it must not be used as a request body schema in any write or search operation.

id.description:
Opaque unique identifier of the security event record.

This value uniquely identifies the security event row within the `shopping_mall_security_events` table and is typically generated when the event is recorded. It is used as the primary key for retrieval operations and correlation across security tooling.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when the underlying security-relevant activity actually occurred.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time value in UTC. This may differ from the time when the event was persisted if the event passed through queues, buffers, or asynchronous pipelines before being written to the `shopping_mall_security_events` table.

recorded_at.description:
Timestamp when this security event was recorded into the persistent security events log store.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time value in UTC. This value is used to reason about ingestion latency and to order events based on when the platform stored them in the `shopping_mall_security_events` model.

event_type.description:
Machine-readable event type or category describing what kind of security event this record represents.

Typical examples include identifiers such as `login_failed`, `login_succeeded`, `password_reset_requested`, `credential_locked`, `suspicious_ip_activity`, or codes produced by fraud and risk engines. The exact allowed values are controlled by security and risk policies and are persisted in the corresponding column of the `shopping_mall_security_events` table.

severity.description:
Severity level of the security event as defined by the platform’s risk or security subsystem.

Common examples include `info`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. The precise semantics of each level are governed by internal security policies and are stored with the event so that downstream tooling and dashboards can drive triage, alerting, and reporting based on this value.

actor_type.description:
Logical type of the primary actor associated with this event, if any.

Examples may include `customer`, `seller`, `platformAdmin`, `guest`, or `system`, indicating whether the event is tied to a human end user, a marketplace participant, an internal administrator, or automated processes. This value is derived from and persisted with the event record to help security operators quickly understand which identity domain is affected.

actor_id.description:
Identifier of the primary actor associated with this event, when applicable.

This typically corresponds to the primary key of an actor entity (such as a customer, seller, or platform administrator) in the core domain tables. For purely system-generated events this field may be null, absent, or hold a reserved identifier that is still stored with the security event for internal correlation purposes.

session_id.description:
Identifier of the authentication session associated with this event, when relevant.

This value usually matches the identifier of a record in one of the session tables used for customers, sellers, or platform administrators. It enables operators to correlate multiple security events back to a single authenticated session context and is stored alongside the event in the `shopping_mall_security_events` model when available.

ip_address.description:
IP address observed for the request or connection that triggered this security event.

Represented as a textual string that may contain either IPv4 or IPv6 notation. This value is persisted as part of the event and can be used by security and risk tooling for geolocation, anomaly detection, rate limiting, correlation with external threat intelligence, and investigation workflows.

user_agent.description:
