Raw user-agent string reported by the client at the time of the event, if available.

This field helps security analysts understand the device, browser, or automation context involved in the event and is stored with the event so investigations can distinguish between legitimate traffic patterns and scripted probes or bots.

metadata.description:
Arbitrary structured metadata associated with this security event.

This field is backed by one or more JSON-capable columns on the `shopping_mall_security_events` model and can contain additional diagnostic or correlation information such as rule identifiers, geo-information, correlation IDs, risk scores, or policy evaluation details. The exact keys and value structures are implementation specific and may evolve without changing the top-level DTO, but all metadata returned here must originate from persisted event metadata rather than transient, non-stored computations.

IShoppingMallCustomerCredential.description:
Administrative view of the authentication credential state associated with a specific customer account on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents an aggregated projection that combines the linkage between a customer and their credential record with selected attributes from the core credentials model, risk configuration, and authentication history. It is intentionally designed as a read-only view for platform administrators and security operators rather than a direct mirror of any single underlying database table.

The structure purposely omits sensitive material such as password hashes, raw auth tokens, cryptographic secrets, and low-level implementation details. Only high-level, administratively safe indicators—such as login identifier, credential type, lockout status, MFA enrollment, and risk flags—are exposed. All changes to credentials must occur through dedicated authentication and account-management workflows, not through this DTO.

customer_id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer account to which this credential view belongs.

This identifier corresponds to the primary key of the customer entity and allows administrators to correlate credential status with the owning customer profile and activity.

credential_id.description:
Unique identifier of the underlying core credential record associated with this customer.

This value typically corresponds to the primary key of a shared credentials entity that may have subtype links for multiple actor roles such as customers, sellers, or platform administrators.

login_identifier.description:
Primary login handle used by the customer for authentication, as modeled in the credentials subsystem.

This is often an email address or username string and is the value the customer enters when attempting to sign in. The precise semantics (for example, whether it must be unique, or whether it must be an email) are defined by the core credential model and business rules.

credential_type.description:
Type of authentication credential associated with this customer.

Examples include values such as `password`, `oauth`, or `sso`, reflecting how the customer proves their identity. This field helps administrators understand which authentication mechanisms are configured and can influence policy enforcement and troubleshooting steps.

is_locked.description:
Flag indicating whether this credential is currently locked for authentication attempts.

When this value is true, the authentication layer should deny login attempts using this credential until an appropriate administrative or automated process clears the lock according to configured policy (for example, after investigation or a cooldown period).

mfa_enrolled.description:
Flag indicating whether the customer has multi-factor authentication (MFA) enrolled and active for this credential.

This value is derived from the MFA configuration associated with the underlying credentials and gives administrators a quick view of whether strong authentication is in place for the account.

risk_flags.description:
Array of risk or fraud-related flags currently associated with this customer's credential linkage.

Each element is a symbolic code or identifier that corresponds to risk configuration entries (for example, rules, lists, or manual annotations). These flags inform how strictly subsequent authentication or transaction flows should be treated and are useful during investigations and risk reviews.

last_successful_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful authentication using this credential, if available.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time value in UTC. This helps administrators understand how recently the account was used and whether it may be dormant or recently accessed during suspicious activity.

last_failed_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent failed authentication attempt associated with this credential, if available.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time value in UTC. This value, combined with failure counts and security events, helps detect brute-force attempts or other anomalous login behavior.

failed_login_attempts.description:
Number of consecutive failed login attempts recorded against this credential since the last successful login or administrative reset.

This counter is commonly used by lockout and throttling policies to determine when to temporarily or permanently block further attempts and is surfaced here for administrative visibility.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the linkage between the customer and the underlying credential record was established.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time value in UTC. This is typically set at customer registration time or when credentials were first attached to the customer account.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this aggregated credential view or its underlying linkage metadata was last updated.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time value in UTC. Changes that may update this value include lockout state changes, MFA enrollment updates, risk flag adjustments, or other credential-related administrative actions.

IShoppingMallAuthCredential.ISummary.description: Summary view of authentication credential metadata for an actor on the shopping mall platform, intended for administrative and security dashboards. This DTO exposes only non-secret credential information that is safe to show to platform administrators when inspecting the authentication state of a seller or platform administrator. It omits any sensitive secret material such as password hashes, salts, raw tokens, or refresh tokens.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authentication credential record in the shopping_mall_auth_credentials table.

actor_type.description: Logical actor type that owns this credential, such as customer, seller, or platformAdmin. This is used to understand which kind of account the credential belongs to for audit and security purposes.

actor_id.description: Unique identifier of the owning actor in its respective table (for example shopping_mall_seller, shopping_mall_customer, or shopping_mall_platformadmin).

credential_type.description: Type of credential used for authentication, such as email_password, oauth2, or external_idp. Useful for understanding how this actor authenticates to the platform.

identifier.description: Human-readable credential identifier such as login email or external identity handle. This must never include any secret values and should be safe for display in administrative UIs.

is_active.description: Indicates whether this credential is currently active and allowed to be used for authentication. When false, login attempts using this credential should be rejected.

is_locked.description: Indicates whether the credential is temporarily locked due to security reasons such as repeated failed login attempts. Locked credentials typically require an explicit unlock or cooldown period before reuse.

is_disabled.description: Indicates whether this credential has been administratively disabled. Disabled credentials cannot be used for authentication until explicitly re-enabled by an authorized administrator.

last_success_at.description: Timestamp of the last successful authentication using this credential, in ISO 8601 date-time format. Null when the credential has never successfully authenticated.

last_failure_at.description: Timestamp of the last failed authentication attempt using this credential, in ISO 8601 date-time format. Null when there has been no recorded failure.

failure_count.description: Number of consecutive failed authentication attempts since the last successful login or reset. Used in account lockout and risk evaluation logic.

risk_level.description: Optional high-level risk assessment label for this credential derived from shopping_mall_risk_flags, such as low, medium, or high. Null when no explicit risk classification is present.

risk_flags.description: List of textual risk flags or codes associated with this credential, consolidated from related records such as shopping_mall_risk_flags. Used by administrators to quickly see why a credential is considered risky.

IShoppingMallAuthLog.IRequest.description: Search and filter criteria for querying authentication history records from the shopping_mall_auth_logs table. This DTO is used by administrative endpoints to express complex filters such as actor type, event type, time ranges, success or failure flags, IP address, and user agent, together with pagination and sorting options.

page.description: One-based page index to retrieve when paginating authentication log search results. If omitted, the first page is typically returned by default.

limit.description: Maximum number of authentication log records to include in a single page of results. Server-side validation should enforce an upper bound to avoid excessively large pages.

sort_by.description: Field name used to sort authentication log records, such as created_at or event_type. When null, a sensible default ordering such as created_at is applied.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction for authentication log records, typically asc or desc. When null, the backend applies its default, usually desc for most-recent-first views.

actor_type.description: Optional filter for actor type whose authentication events should be returned, such as customer, seller, or platformAdmin. When null, logs for all actor types may be included if other filters allow it.

actor_id.description: Optional UUID of the specific actor whose authentication events are being queried. When provided, results are restricted to log entries whose actor_id matches this value.

event_types.description: Optional list of authentication event type codes to include in the results, such as login_success, login_failure, logout, token_refresh, password_reset_request, or password_reset_success. When omitted or empty, all event types may be returned.

success.description: Optional filter indicating whether to return only successful (true) or only failed (false) authentication events. When null, both successful and failed events may be included.

failure_reasons.description: Optional list of failure reason codes to filter failed authentication events, for example invalid_credentials or account_suspended. Only log entries whose failure_reason matches one of the provided codes are returned when this filter is present.

ip.description: Optional filter for the originating IP address recorded in authentication logs. This can be used to focus on events from a specific IP or network range, depending on how the backend implements matching.

user_agent.description: Optional filter for the user agent or device signature captured during authentication events. Useful for investigating activity from a specific browser, device, or automation tool.

created_from.description: Optional lower bound of the created_at timestamp range for authentication log records, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string. When provided, only events on or after this timestamp are included.

created_to.description: Optional upper bound of the created_at timestamp range for authentication log records, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string. When provided, only events on or before this timestamp are included.

IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics.IRequest.description:
Filter and grouping parameters that define the analysis window, actor segments, and severity thresholds for risk analytics.

This DTO represents the request body for the actor risk analytics endpoint used by platform administrators. It allows callers to specify the time window, actor types, severity filters, and grouping dimensions that control how aggregated risk statistics are computed from shopping_mall_risk_flags and related tables.

fromTimestamp.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the analysis time window in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Only risk flags, fraud rule violations, and related security events created at or after this timestamp are included in the analytics. When omitted, the implementation may default to a recent window such as the last 24 hours or a configuration-defined period.

toTimestamp.description:
Exclusive upper bound of the analysis time window in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Only risk flags, fraud rule violations, and related security events created before this timestamp are included in the analytics. When omitted, the implementation may default to the current server time.

actorTypes.description:
List of actor types to include in the risk analytics computation.

When empty or omitted, the implementation should include all supported actor types (customers, sellers, and platform administrators).

oneOf.description:
Type of actor for which risk analytics should be computed.

- `customer`: End customers who place orders on the shoppingMall platform.
- `seller`: Merchant accounts that operate stores and fulfill orders.
- `platformAdmin`: Platform administrators responsible for operations, moderation, and risk management.

riskCategories.description:
Optional list of logical risk categories to include in the analysis.

Typical categories represent business-defined groupings such as account_takeover, payment_fraud, chargeback_risk, abnormal_behavior, or policy_violation. When omitted or empty, all categories are included.

regionCodes.description:
Optional list of region codes, usually aligned with entries in shopping_mall_region_settings, used to restrict analytics to specific markets or geographies.

When omitted or empty, analytics are computed across all regions.

groupBy.description:
List of dimensions by which the analytics engine should group and break down aggregated results.

These grouping keys control the structure of breakdown arrays in the response. The backend may ignore unsupported values silently or respond with a validation error depending on implementation.

IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics.description:
Aggregated risk analytics metrics and breakdowns across actor types and optional dimensions.

This DTO represents the analytical response for the platform admin actor risk analytics endpoint. It is built from aggregated, read-only queries primarily over shopping_mall_risk_flags, shopping_mall_auth_credentials, actor subtype tables, and optionally fraud rule definitions and violations. The schema does not map directly to a single Prisma model but is a projection designed for dashboard visualization and operational monitoring.

summary.description:
Overall summary metrics for the requested analysis window and filters.

Contains top-level counts and derived indicators that provide a quick snapshot of the actor-related risk posture across the platform.

byActorType.description:
Breakdown of risk analytics metrics by actor type when such grouping is requested or supported.

Each element summarizes metrics for a specific actor type (customer, seller, or platformAdmin).

byRegion.description:
Breakdown of risk analytics metrics by region when region-based grouping is requested.

Regions typically correspond to configuration entries in shopping_mall_region_settings and represent logical markets or geographic areas.

bySeverity.description:
Breakdown of risk analytics metrics by severity when severity-based grouping is requested.

Each element captures metrics for a specific severity level such as low, medium, high, or critical.

byRiskCategory.description:
Breakdown of risk analytics metrics by risk category when category-based grouping is requested.

Each element aggregates metrics for a logical risk category such as account_takeover, payment_fraud, or chargeback_risk.

timeSeries.description:
Optional time-series representation of risk analytics when time-bucketed grouping is requested.

Each element corresponds to a time bucket (such as a specific hour or day) and includes metrics for that bucket. This structure is designed for charting trend lines in admin dashboards.

IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics.ISummary.description:
Top-level summary metrics for the actor risk analytics response.

These fields provide an at-a-glance overview of risk posture across all included actors in the analysis window. The values are typically computed from aggregated records in shopping_mall_risk_flags and related fraud rule violation tables.

totalActorsEvaluated.description:
Total number of distinct actors (customers, sellers, and platform administrators) that were evaluated within the analysis window and filters.

An actor is counted once even if it has multiple risk flags.

actorsWithActiveRiskFlags.description:
Number of distinct actors that currently have at least one active risk flag in shopping_mall_risk_flags within the analysis scope.

This metric helps indicate how broadly risk signals are distributed across the actor population.

totalRiskFlags.description:
Total count of risk flag records considered in the analytics for the requested filters.

This metric includes all severities and categories that match the filter criteria.

highSeverityActorCount.description:
Number of distinct actors that have at least one risk flag at or above the high severity level within the analysis scope.

This is often used as a key indicator for accounts requiring urgent review or mitigation.

criticalSeverityActorCount.description:
Number of distinct actors that have at least one risk flag at critical severity within the analysis scope.

Platform administrators typically prioritize these actors for immediate investigation or automatic protective actions.

IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics.IByActor.description:
Aggregated risk analytics metrics scoped to a single actor type.

Represents counts and severity distributions for either customers, sellers, or platform administrators within the requested analysis window and filters.

oneOf.description:
Actor type to which this aggregated metrics entry applies.

- `customer`: Authenticated buyers represented by shopping_mall_customer.
- `seller`: Merchant accounts represented by shopping_mall_seller.
- `platformAdmin`: Platform administrators represented by shopping_mall_platformadmin.

- `customer`: Authenticated buyers represented by shopping_mall_customer.
- `seller`: Merchant accounts represented by shopping_mall_seller.
- `platformAdmin`: Platform administrators represented by shopping_mall_platformadmin.

- `customer`: Authenticated buyers represented by shopping_mall_customer.
- `seller`: Merchant accounts represented by shopping_mall_seller.

actorType.description:

- `customer`: Authenticated buyers represented by shopping_mall_customer.
- `seller`: Merchant accounts represented by shopping_mall_seller.
- `platformAdmin`: Platform administrators represented by shopping_mall_platformadmin.

actorCount.description:
Total number of actors of this type evaluated within the analysis scope.

Actors are counted even if they do not currently have any risk flags.

actorsWithActiveRiskFlags.description: Number of actors of this type that have at least one active risk flag in the analysis scope.

totalRiskFlags.description: Total number of risk flag records associated with actors of this type that match the analysis filters.

highSeverityActorCount.description: Number of actors of this type that have at least one risk flag at or above high severity.

criticalSeverityActorCount.description: Number of actors of this type that have at least one risk flag at critical severity.

IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics.IByRegio.description:
Aggregated actor risk analytics metrics scoped to a single region.

Each instance represents one regional bucket within a larger `IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics` response, summarizing how many actors in that region are affected by different levels of risk flags. All metric fields are non‑negative integers and are always present; a value of `0` indicates that no matching actors or flags exist for that metric in the current analysis window.

regionCode.description:
Business code of the region or market segment for which these risk analytics were computed.

This value corresponds to a region entry in `shopping_mall_region_settings` (for example, a country or multi‑country market code) and acts as the grouping key when aggregating actor risk metrics by region.

actorCount.description:
Total number of distinct actors associated with this region that were included in the risk analytics computation.

This value is always a non‑negative integer. It is `0` when no actors in this region matched the analysis filters or fell into the considered actor population.

actorsWithActiveRiskFlags.description:
Number of distinct actors in this region that currently have at least one active risk flag within the analysis scope.

This count is always a non‑negative integer. It is `0` when no actors in the region have any active risk flags matching the filters used for this analytics run.

totalRiskFlags.description:
Total number of risk flag records attached to actors in this region that match the analytics filters.

This metric aggregates individual risk flag instances rather than distinct actors. It is always a non‑negative integer and is `0` when no matching risk flags exist for the regional bucket.

highSeverityActorCount.description:
Number of distinct actors in this region that have at least one risk flag at or above the platform‑defined high severity threshold.

The value is always a non‑negative integer. A value of `0` indicates that, within the analysis window and filters, no actors in this region carry high‑severity or higher risk flags.

criticalSeverityActorCount.description:
Number of distinct actors in this region that have at least one risk flag at critical severity.

This is always a non‑negative integer and is `0` when no actors in the region have any critical‑severity risk flags under the current analytics filters.

IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics.IBySever.description:
Aggregated actor risk analytics metrics scoped to a single severity level.

Each instance represents one severity bucket (for example `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`) within the overall `IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics` result. It summarizes how many actors and individual risk flag records fall into that severity band. All metric fields are non‑negative integers and are always present; a value of `0` indicates that no matching actors or flags exist for that severity in the analysis window.

oneOf.description:
Severity bucket for which the aggregated metrics are computed.

The value is one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`, representing the platform‑defined risk severity bands used to classify risk flags. This property is the grouping key when aggregating actor risk metrics by severity level.

The value is one of `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`, representing the platform‑defined risk severity bands used to classify risk flags. This property is the grouping key when aggregating actor risk metrics by severity level.

actorCount.description:
Number of distinct actors that have at least one risk flag at this severity level within the analysis scope.

This value is always a non‑negative integer. It is `0` when no actors have any risk flags whose severity falls into this bucket under the current filters.

totalRiskFlags.description:
Total number of individual risk flag records at this severity level that match the analytics filters.

The value is always a non‑negative integer and counts risk flag instances, not distinct actors. A value of `0` indicates that no risk flags at this severity were found for the selected analysis window and filters.

IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics.IByRiskC.description:
Aggregated risk analytics metrics scoped to a specific logical risk category.

Risk categories represent business-defined groupings of risk flags or rule violations such as account_takeover, payment_fraud, chargeback_risk, abnormal_behavior, or policy_violation.

riskCategory.description:
Logical risk category key for which the aggregated metrics are computed.

The concrete set of category keys is platform-specific and typically configured alongside fraud rules and risk flag definitions.

actorCount.description: Number of distinct actors that have at least one risk flag in this risk category within the analysis scope.

totalRiskFlags.description: Total number of risk flags categorized into this risk category that match the analysis filters.

IShoppingMallActorRiskAnalytics.ITimeBuc.description:
Time-bucketed metrics entry representing risk analytics for a specific period.

Each instance corresponds to one logical time bucket (for example, an hour or a day) and contains aggregated metrics for that period. This structure is designed for charting time-series trends in admin dashboards.

start.description: Inclusive start timestamp of the time bucket in ISO 8601 date-time format.

end.description: Exclusive end timestamp of the time bucket in ISO 8601 date-time format.

totalRiskFlags.description: Total number of risk flag records that fall within this time bucket and match the analysis filters.

actorsWithActiveRiskFlags.description: Number of distinct actors that have at least one risk flag in this time bucket.

highSeverityActorCount.description: Number of distinct actors that have at least one high or critical severity risk flag in this time bucket.

criticalSeverityActorCount.description: Number of distinct actors that have at least one critical severity risk flag in this time bucket.

IShoppingMallActorSecurityOverview.description:
Consolidated security overview across all main actor types in the ShoppingMall platform.

This analytical DTO aggregates high-level security metrics for customers, sellers, and platform administrators by querying multiple underlying Prisma models. It is used for admin dashboard views to monitor authentication activity, session status, and security events without exposing low-level implementation details.

The data is read-only and synthesized from identity tables (customers, sellers, platform admins), session tables, and security/auth log tables, giving platform administrators a single snapshot of the current security posture.

customer.description: Aggregated security metrics for customer actors derived from shopping_mall_customer, shopping_mall_customer_sessions, shopping_mall_security_events, and shopping_mall_auth_logs.

seller.description: Aggregated security metrics for seller actors derived from shopping_mall_seller, shopping_mall_seller_sessions, shopping_mall_security_events, and shopping_mall_auth_logs.

platformAdmin.description: Aggregated security metrics for platform administrator actors derived from shopping_mall_platformadmin, shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions, shopping_mall_security_events, and shopping_mall_auth_logs.

timeWindowMinutes.description:
Length of the recent time window, in minutes, used for calculating "recent" event and session metrics.

This is typically a configurable duration such as the last 60 minutes or last 24 hours that the backend uses when aggregating the counts of recent security events and active sessions.

IShoppingMallActorSecurityOverviewActorS.description:
Aggregated security metrics for a single actor type (customers, sellers, or platform administrators).

Each segment summarizes identity counts, session activity, and security event tallies for the corresponding actor group. These metrics are derived from the relevant identity table, session table, and security/auth log tables, and are optimized for admin dashboard visualizations.

totalActors.description:
Total number of actor identities of this type currently registered in the platform (for example, total customers or total sellers).

This count is typically derived from the corresponding identity table such as shopping_mall_customer, shopping_mall_seller, or shopping_mall_platformadmin.

activeSessions.description:
Current number of active sessions for this actor type.

This value is usually computed from the corresponding session table (for example, shopping_mall_customer_sessions) by counting sessions that are not yet expired or closed.

recentSessions.description:
Number of sessions for this actor type that have been created within the recent aggregation window defined by the overview (for example, the last 60 minutes).

This helps administrators understand short-term authentication activity trends.

failedLoginAttempts.description:
Total number of failed login attempts for this actor type within the recent aggregation window.

This is typically computed by counting failed authentication events in shopping_mall_security_events or shopping_mall_auth_logs.

successfulLogins.description:
Total number of successful logins for this actor type within the recent aggregation window.

This metric complements failedLoginAttempts to give a fuller picture of authentication outcomes.

lockedAccounts.description:
Number of actor identities of this type that are currently locked due to security policies such as too many failed login attempts or risk flags.

This is typically derived from flags or status fields in identity or credential tables.

mfaChallenges.description:
Number of multi-factor authentication (MFA) challenges that have been triggered for this actor type within the recent aggregation window.

This metric helps assess the frequency of elevated authentication flows for the actor group.

IShoppingMallBrand.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for retrieving brands from the `shopping_mall_brands` table.

This DTO is used by the storefront and admin UIs to request a paginated, filtered list of brand summaries. It supports flexible search by text, status filters, region filters, and sorting options while enforcing reasonable pagination defaults.

The `page` field represents a zero-based page index that maps to the `current` field of `IPage.IPagination` in responses, and `limit` maps directly to `IPage.IPagination.limit`. Together they control how many `IShoppingMallBrand.ISummary` records are returned per page in `IPageIShoppingMallBrand.ISummary` responses.

page.description:
Zero-based page index for pagination when listing brands.

If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default such as page 0. This value is translated to the `current` field of the `IPage.IPagination` structure in paginated responses.

limit.description:
Maximum number of brand records to return in a single page.

The backend should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessive result sizes even if the client supplies a large value. This value maps to `limit` in the `IPage.IPagination` structure of the response.

search.description:
Free-text search query applied to brand names, slugs, or descriptions.

This is typically used to implement simple search boxes where users type a fragment of the brand name or description, and the backend matches against relevant text columns in `shopping_mall_brands`.

isActive.description:
Optional filter indicating whether only active (visible) brands should be returned.

When true, the backend should restrict results to brands that are currently marked as active or visible in the catalog according to business rules (for example, filtering out soft-deleted records or brands flagged as hidden). When false or omitted, inactive brands may also be included depending on caller context (such as admin searches).

regionCode.description:
Optional region code used to filter brands that are visible or configured for a specific market or geographic region.

This should correspond to region identifiers used in `shopping_mall_region_settings` or related configuration tables so that only brands enabled for the requested market are returned.

oneOf.description:
Sort brands by their display name in alphabetical order.

This corresponds to ordering by the `name` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

Sort brands by their creation time.

This corresponds to ordering by the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_brands`, typically from oldest to newest or vice versa depending on `sortDirection`.

Sort brands by their last update time.

This corresponds to ordering by the `updated_at` column of `shopping_mall_brands` so that recently modified brands can be surfaced first.

sortBy.description:
Field used to sort the brand results.

Allowed values are `name`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`. The backend maps these values to the appropriate columns in `shopping_mall_brands` and applies them together with `sortDirection` to determine the final ordering.

oneOf.description:
Sort results in ascending order.

When combined with `sortBy`, this orders brands from A to Z or from oldest to newest depending on the selected sort field.

Sort results in descending order.

When combined with `sortBy`, this orders brands from Z to A or from newest to oldest depending on the selected sort field.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for the brand results.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default (for example, descending by creation time for discovery views).

IShoppingMallBrand.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a brand entity projected from the `shopping_mall_brands` Prisma model.

This summary DTO is used in catalog product summaries, brand listing grids, and other marketing or discovery contexts where a lightweight representation is sufficient. It exposes the primary key, human-readable brand name, stable slug used for SEO-friendly URLs, and an optional logo URL, while omitting internal timestamps and soft-delete markers.

The underlying `shopping_mall_brands` table includes `id`, `name`, `slug`, `description`, `logo_uri`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`. This summary focuses on the fields that are most relevant for list and thumbnail views and assumes that brands with `deleted_at` set are not returned by read operations that use this type.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the brand.

This value maps directly to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_brands` Prisma model and is generated as a UUID. It is used internally for precise reference to brand records across product relationships, analytics, and administrative tools.

name.description:
Display name of the brand as shown to customers.

This field corresponds to the `name` column in the `shopping_mall_brands` table and is required for every brand. It is used in brand lists, product detail pages, and search results to present a human-readable brand label.

slug.description:
SEO-friendly slug that uniquely identifies the brand in URLs.

This value is mapped from the non-nullable `slug` column of the `shopping_mall_brands` Prisma model. It is typically derived from the brand name and is used in routing and SEO contexts (for example, `/brands/{slug}`) so that brand-related pages have stable, human-readable URLs.

logo_url.description:
URL of the primary logo image representing this brand.

This field is a projection of the optional `logo_uri` column in the `shopping_mall_brands` table and should contain a fully qualified URL pointing to an image hosted on a CDN or media service. UI components such as brand badges or tiles can use this URL to render the brand logo; when null or absent, a placeholder graphic can be shown instead.

IShoppingMallBrand.description:
Brand entity used in the ShoppingMall catalog.

Represents a manufacturer, label, or brand that can be associated with products and SKUs for filtering, navigation, and merchandising. Includes core brand identity fields and public-facing metadata suitable for storefront display.

This DTO is directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_brands` Prisma model and therefore must only expose fields that exist on that table to avoid phantom-field security and integrity issues.

id.description:
Primary key for the brand record in the `shopping_mall_brands` table.

This value is generated and managed by the system and uniquely identifies the brand across all catalog and administrative operations.

name.description:
Display name of the brand as stored in the `name` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

This is the human‑readable label shown to customers and administrators when referencing the brand in product listings, filters, and detail views.

slug.description:
URL‑friendly, unique identifier for the brand stored in the `slug` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

This value is typically derived from the brand name and is used for SEO‑friendly routing, programmatic references, and integrations that need a stable business key.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text about the brand mapped from the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_brands`.

When present, this content is suitable for brand landing pages, product detail sections, or marketing placements that introduce the brand to customers.

logo_uri.description:
URI of the primary brand logo image stored in the `logo_uri` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

This typically points to a file in a media service or CDN and is used in brand carousels, product detail pages, and administrative UIs that display brand identity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp from the `created_at` column indicating when the brand record was first created.

The value is managed by the system or database layer and is useful for auditing and administrative reporting but is read‑only to API clients.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp from the `updated_at` column indicating when the brand record was last modified.

This value is maintained by the backend on every update and is returned to clients for audit and cache invalidation purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Nullable timestamp from the `deleted_at` column marking when the brand was soft‑deleted.

When this field is null, the brand is considered active from a data‑retention perspective. Non‑null values indicate logical deletion while preserving historical references from orders and reviews.

IShoppingMallBrand.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new brand in the ShoppingMall catalog.

This DTO is directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_brands` Prisma model and therefore only exposes writable columns from that table. System‑managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are excluded and populated exclusively by the backend.

Platform administrators and catalog operators use this structure to register brands that can be associated with products and SKUs across the catalog.

name.description:
Display name of the brand to be created, mapped to the non‑nullable `name` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

The value should be unique enough for customers and administrators to distinguish the brand and is subject to any length or formatting rules enforced at the database or application layer.

slug.description:
URL‑friendly, unique slug for the brand mapped directly to the non‑nullable `slug` column in `shopping_mall_brands`.

This value is used for SEO‑friendly URLs, integrations, and as a stable business key. It must satisfy uniqueness constraints defined on the `slug` column to prevent collisions between brands.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text for the brand mapped to the nullable `description` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

Administrators can use this field to provide marketing copy or background information that will appear on brand detail pages and other rich catalog views.

logo_uri.description:
Optional primary logo image URI for the brand mapped to the nullable `logo_uri` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

The URI should reference an image in a trusted media store or CDN and will be used wherever the brand’s logo is displayed in the storefront or administrative tools.

IShoppingMallBrand.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating an existing brand in the shoppingMall catalog.

Represents the subset of brand fields that are mutable after initial creation on the `shopping_mall_brands` Prisma model. System-managed fields such as primary key and timestamps are excluded. This DTO is used as the request body for administrative brand update operations (e.g., PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/brands/{brandId}).

All properties are optional to allow partial updates; the service layer is responsible for enforcing any business rules around which combinations must be provided.

name.description:
Display name of the brand as stored in the `name` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

This is the human‑readable label shown to customers and administrators when referencing the brand in product listings, filters, and detail views. When updated, it must continue to satisfy any uniqueness and formatting rules enforced by the application or database.

slug.description:
URL‑friendly, unique identifier for the brand stored in the `slug` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

Typically derived from the brand name, this value is used for SEO‑friendly routing, programmatic references, and integrations that require a stable business key. When changed, it must respect the unique index on `slug` and avoid collisions with other brands.

description.description:
Optional descriptive text about the brand mapped from the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_brands`.

Updates to this field allow administrators to refine or expand the marketing copy that appears on brand detail pages and other catalog views.

logo_uri.description:
URI of the primary brand logo image stored in the `logo_uri` column of `shopping_mall_brands`.

This typically points to a file in a media service or CDN and is used in brand carousels, product detail pages, and administrative UIs that display brand identity. When updated, the URI should remain resolvable and point to a valid image resource.

IShoppingMallProduct.IRequest.description:
Structured search, filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria for querying products from the shopping mall catalog.

This DTO is used as the request body for JSON-based product search endpoints backed by the `shopping_mall_products` Prisma model and its related catalog entities. It encapsulates free-text keyword search, category and brand filters, status filters, region and channel visibility context, and pagination controls such as page index and page size. The server translates this structure into Prisma queries against `shopping_mall_products`, optionally joining tables like `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, `shopping_mall_brands`, `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules`, and `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags`.

The shape of this DTO is optimized for flexible search scenarios rather than simple query-string filters, enabling complex combinations of constraints while remaining aligned with the underlying schema.

page.description: 1-based index of the result page to retrieve. Used together with `page_size` to implement paginated product listings.

page_size.description: Maximum number of product records to return in a single page. The service may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

sort_field.description: Logical field name to sort the results by, such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, `name`, or `code`. The service validates this against a whitelist of sortable fields backed by indexes in `shopping_mall_products`.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for the results. Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending. The service will default to `desc` when not provided or when using time-based fields.
Sort direction for the results. Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending. The service will default to `desc` when not provided or when using time-based fields.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction for the results. Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending. The service will default to `desc` when not provided or when using time-based fields.

keyword.description: Free-text keyword used to search across one or more indexed text fields such as product `name`, `short_description`, or `description`.

status.description: Filter products by lifecycle status, for example `draft`, `pending_review`, `active`, `inactive`, or `discontinued`, as defined in the `shopping_mall_products` model.

seller_id.description: Filter products to those belonging to a specific seller, identified by the seller's primary key. Used for seller back-office product lists and admin views scoped to a seller.

brand_id.description: Filter products associated with a specific brand, identified by the primary key of `shopping_mall_brands`.

category_ids.description: List of category identifiers used to restrict results to products assigned to any of the specified categories via `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`.

items.description: Identifier of a category node within the shopping mall category tree.

region_setting_id.description: Identifier of a `shopping_mall_region_settings` record indicating the regional market context for visibility and compliance evaluation.

channel.description: Logical sales channel used for visibility rules, such as `web`, `mobile_web`, or `mobile_app`, corresponding to values in `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules.channel`.

min_price.description: Lower bound for product price filter. Only products with effective prices greater than or equal to this value should be returned.

max_price.description: Upper bound for product price filter. Only products with effective prices less than or equal to this value should be returned.

in_stock_only.description: If true, restricts results to products that have at least one SKU with available inventory according to `shopping_mall_inventory_items` and `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations`.

compliance_flag_types.description: Optional list of compliance flag types to include or emphasize in results, based on values defined in `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.flag_type`. Used for compliance-focused catalog views.

items.description: Compliance flag type identifier, such as an internal code representing a particular regulatory or business rule.

IShoppingMallProduct.description:
Canonical product entity for the shoppingMall catalog, mapped directly to the shopping_mall_products Prisma model.

Represents a single catalog product row identified by a globally unique business-visible code. This DTO exposes core product attributes required by both storefront product detail pages and internal back-office tools.

In addition to scalar fields, it now transforms BELONGS-TO relations for seller and brand into summary association objects, eliminating raw foreign key identifiers and providing richer, atomic read semantics.

id.description:
System-generated unique identifier for the product row in shopping_mall_products.

This is the primary key and is not exposed in URL paths, which instead use the business-visible code field.

code.description:
Business-visible unique product code.

Globally unique identifier for the product across the shoppingMall platform. Used in URL paths as {productCode} instead of the internal UUID. Enforced as unique at the database level.

name.description:
Primary name of the product as shown in catalog listings and detail pages.

Should be human-readable and concise while clearly identifying the product.

short_description.description:
Optional short marketing description used in compact views such as tiles and search results.

Can be null when only the full description is maintained.

description.description:
Optional full product description used on detail pages.

May contain longer-form marketing copy and specifications serialized as rich text or markdown-compatible content.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the product within the catalog.

Typical values include draft, pending_review, active, inactive, or discontinued, as defined in the shopping_mall_products Prisma schema. Controls whether and how the product is exposed to end users.

is_multi_sku.description:
Indicates whether the product has multiple purchasable variants (SKUs).

When true, the product is configured with option types and associated SKUs; when false, it behaves as a single-variant product.

primary_image_uri.description:
URI of the primary image used to represent this product in listings and detail pages.

May be null when no primary image is configured. Should point to a pre-uploaded media asset managed by the media subsystem.

additional_data.description:
Optional JSON-encoded metadata stored as text for extensible product configuration.

Used for custom behaviors or integration-specific attributes that are not modeled as first-class columns.

seller.description:
Owning seller for this product represented as a lightweight summary.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key, providing enough context for catalog and back-office views without requiring additional lookups.

brand.description:
Optional brand associated with this product, exposed as a summary DTO.

When non-null, this replaces the raw `shopping_mall_brand_id` foreign key and provides brand context such as name and logo for catalog views.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the product record was first created in the catalog.

Managed exclusively by the backend and not modifiable by clients.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the product record was last updated.

Automatically maintained by the backend on each modification.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the product.

Null when the product is active in the catalog. Non-null values indicate the product has been logically removed and should generally be hidden from public-facing APIs.

IShoppingMallProduct.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new catalog product in the shopping_mall_products table.

Accepts only client-specifiable fields needed to register a product, such as seller association, optional brand, business-visible code, descriptive attributes, lifecycle status, multi-SKU configuration, primary image URI, and additional JSON metadata. System-managed fields like id and timestamps are excluded and handled by the backend.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller that will own this product.

Must reference an existing shopping_mall_seller record. In seller-facing APIs this is typically inferred from authentication context; in platformAdmin APIs it may be explicitly provided.

shopping_mall_brand_id.description:
Optional identifier of the brand associated with this product.

Must reference an existing shopping_mall_brands record when provided. Use null or omit this field if the product is not branded.

code.description:
Globally unique business-visible product code to assign to the new product.

Must be unique across all shopping_mall_products records. Attempts to reuse an existing code will be rejected by the backend.

name.description:
Primary catalog name of the product.

Required for all products and used in listings and detail pages.

short_description.description:
Optional short marketing description for the product.

Can be provided for improved search and list presentations or left null to rely on the full description only.

description.description:
Optional full description of the product.

Intended for long-form marketing copy and specification content on the product detail page.

status.description:
Initial lifecycle status for the new product.

Typical values include draft, pending_review, active, inactive, or discontinued, as defined in the shopping_mall_products Prisma model.

is_multi_sku.description:
Whether the new product supports multiple SKUs (variants).

Set to true when the product will have multiple variants defined via option types and SKUs; false for single-variant products.

primary_image_uri.description:
URI of the primary product image to associate at creation time.

Should reference a pre-uploaded media asset. Can be null when no primary image is yet available.

additional_data.description:
Optional JSON-encoded metadata describing additional product configuration or integration-specific attributes.

Stored as text in the underlying additional_data column.

IShoppingMallProduct.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for a shoppingMall catalog product backed by the `shopping_mall_products` Prisma model.

This DTO exposes only mutable columns such as `name`, `short_description`, `description`, lifecycle `status`, multi-SKU configuration flags, primary image URL, optional brand association, and JSON-encoded additional metadata. Immutable values like the primary key `id`, the business-visible product `code`, and system-managed timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`) are intentionally excluded and must be controlled exclusively by the backend.

The payload is designed for partial updates: all properties are optional and callers are encouraged to send only the fields that need to change for a given update operation.

name.description:
Display name of the product as shown in catalog listings and product detail pages.

Maps to the `name` column on the `shopping_mall_products` table and may be updated to reflect branding, merchandising, or localization changes over time.

shortDescription.description:
Short marketing description or teaser text used in list views, tiles, and other compact catalog components.

This value corresponds to the optional `short_description` column in `shopping_mall_products` and is typically concise, helping customers quickly understand the product at a glance.

description.description:
Full product description used on the product detail page, often including marketing copy, specifications, usage instructions, and other rich information.

Backed by the optional `description` column in `shopping_mall_products`. Implementations may store rich-text or markup content serialized as text in this field.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the product within the catalog, persisted in the `status` column of `shopping_mall_products`.

Typical values include business-level states such as `draft`, `pending_review`, `active`, `inactive`, or `discontinued` (the exact allowed set is enforced by domain rules and database constraints). The status controls whether the product is visible to customers, available for sale, or retired, and invalid values will be rejected by the service layer.

isMultiSku.description:
Indicates whether this product is managed as a multi-SKU product with distinct purchasable variants.

When set to `true`, the product is expected to have option types and SKUs defined in `shopping_mall_product_option_types` and `shopping_mall_product_skus`. When `false`, the product behaves like a single-variant item even if implemented using a single SKU internally. This flag maps to the `is_multi_sku` column in `shopping_mall_products`.

primaryImageUri.description:
URL of the primary image representing this product in the catalog.

The value maps to the `primary_image_uri` column of `shopping_mall_products` and must be a pre-uploaded, publicly reachable image URL (for example, a CDN or object storage URL). Binary or base64-encoded image data must never be sent in this field; only URL references are allowed.

oneOf.description:
Non-null brand identifier value.

When this branch is selected, it represents the UUID primary key of an existing brand in `shopping_mall_brands` that should be associated with the product.

Null brand identifier value.

When this branch is selected, any existing brand association on the product will be removed, leaving the product unbranded or treated as seller-branded according to business rules.

brandId.description:
Optional brand association for this product represented by the brand’s primary key.

This field controls the `shopping_mall_brand_id` foreign key on the `shopping_mall_products` table. Supplying a non-null UUID will associate the product with the corresponding brand record in `shopping_mall_brands`, while explicitly setting it to null will remove any existing brand linkage and treat the product as unbranded or seller-branded according to business rules.

oneOf.description:
JSON-encoded metadata string.

This branch holds arbitrary JSON content serialized as a string, which the backend persists in the `additional_data` column of `shopping_mall_products`.

Null value indicating no additional metadata is stored.

When this branch is selected, the `additional_data` column is treated as absent or cleared for this product.

additionalData.description:
Optional JSON-encoded metadata string storing extensible catalog attributes not modeled as first-class columns.

This property corresponds directly to the `additional_data` column in `shopping_mall_products`. The backend persists the value as text; its internal JSON structure (if any) is application-specific and may hold integration payloads, custom flags, or other configuration related to the product. Clients should serialize complex objects to JSON before assigning this value and deserialize on read as needed.

IShoppingMallProductCategoryAssignment.I.description:
Search and filter request payload for listing category assignments for a specific product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This DTO is used by PATCH `/shoppingMall/seller/products/{productCode}/categories` and `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/products/{productCode}/categories` to retrieve a paginated collection of records primarily sourced from the `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments` table, joined to `shopping_mall_categories` (and its `shopping_mall_category_trees` parent) for readable category information.

The request body focuses on pagination, sorting, and a small set of commonly used filters rather than mirroring the underlying Prisma models. All properties are optional so that the backend can apply sensible defaults when callers omit specific parameters.

page.description:
One-based page number for pagination when listing category assignments.

Combined with `limit` to determine which slice of the result set is returned. When omitted, the implementation typically falls back to a default page index (for example, 1).

limit.description:
Maximum number of category assignment records to return in a single page.

Together with `page`, this defines the paging window. Implementations normally enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large pages and to preserve database performance.

oneOf.description: Sort by the `created_at` timestamp on `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, ordering by when the assignment was initially created.
Sort by the `updated_at` timestamp on `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, ordering by the most recently modified assignments.
Sort by the `display_order` column on `shopping_mall_categories`, which controls ordering of categories among siblings in a tree. This requires joining assignments to their categories.
Sort by the `is_primary` flag on `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, typically to group primary assignments separately from secondary ones.

sortBy.description:
Field used to sort category assignments in the result set.

The value determines which column (or joined column) is used in the ORDER BY clause:
- `created_at`: uses `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments.created_at`.
- `updated_at`: uses `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments.updated_at`.
- `display_order`: uses `shopping_mall_categories.display_order` via a join to the category node.
- `is_primary`: uses `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments.is_primary` to surface primary vs secondary assignments.

oneOf.description: Sort results in ascending order for the selected `sortBy` field, such as oldest-to-newest or lowest-to-highest.
Sort results in descending order for the selected `sortBy` field, such as newest-to-oldest or highest-to-lowest.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied when ordering category assignments by `sortBy`.

`asc` sorts from smallest to largest (or earliest to latest), while `desc` sorts from largest to smallest (or latest to earliest). If omitted, the backend typically applies a default direction that is appropriate for the chosen `sortBy` field.

isPrimaryOnly.description:
When true, restricts the result set to only category assignments where the `is_primary` flag on `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments` is true for the product.

When false or omitted, both primary and secondary category assignments may be returned, subject to other filters and business-specific visibility rules.

categoryTreeCode.description:
Optional business code of the category tree used to filter assignments.

When supplied, only assignments whose categories belong to the `shopping_mall_category_trees` record with the matching `code` value are included. This allows callers to scope results to a specific catalog tree when multiple trees are configured.

activeOnly.description:
When true, restricts the result set to assignments whose linked categories are currently active.

In practice this typically means `shopping_mall_categories.active = true` and, depending on implementation, may also exclude categories where `deleted_at` is non-null. When false or omitted, both active and inactive categories may be returned, which can be useful for administrative review workloads.

IShoppingMallProductCategoryAssignment.description:
Product–category assignment entity for the shoppingMall catalog.

Represents a single linkage between a product and a category node, capturing whether the category is primary for that product and recording lifecycle timestamps for the junction record.

Assignments are stored in the `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments` Prisma model and are used by catalog navigation, search, and merchandising logic to determine under which categories a product appears.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product–category assignment record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments` row and is used by admin tools and backend services when updating or deleting an existing assignment.

product.description:
Product associated with this category assignment.

This is a transformed association reference to the catalog product entity (derived from `shopping_mall_products`), exposing only summary information such as product code, name, and key status fields needed for navigation and merchandising contexts.

category.description:
Category node within the catalog hierarchy to which the product is assigned.

This is a transformed association reference to the category entity (derived from `shopping_mall_categories`), exposing only summary information such as tree code, category code, and display label used in navigation and filtering UIs.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this category is the primary category for the product.

At most one assignment per product should have `is_primary = true`. Business logic ensures that when a new primary is set, any previous primary assignment for the same product is demoted.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this product–category assignment was created.

Recorded in UTC and used for auditing, debugging, and chronological analysis of catalog changes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this product–category assignment was last updated.

Changes to fields such as `is_primary` or other metadata update this value so that clients and administrators can detect recent modifications.

IShoppingMallProductCategoryAssignment.I.description:
Request DTO for creating or upserting a product–category assignment for a given product.

This type is used by operations such as `POST /shoppingMall/seller/products/{productCode}/categories` and `POST /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/products/{productCode}/categories`. The product to be modified is identified by the `productCode` path parameter, which maps to `shopping_mall_products.code`; therefore, clients do not send `shopping_mall_product_id` in the body.

The payload specifies which category to link and whether the link should be primary. The service resolves the foreign keys from the supplied identifiers and the surrounding path context and then creates or updates the corresponding row in `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, enforcing the uniqueness of the product–category pair and the business rule that at most one primary category exists per product.

shopping_mall_category_id.description:
Identifier of the target category node for this assignment.

This value references `shopping_mall_categories.id` and determines which category the product will be associated with. It must correspond to an existing, non-deleted category that satisfies any catalog policies such as being active or a leaf node.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this assignment should be treated as the primary category for the product.

When set to `true`, the backend must ensure that any existing primary assignment for the same product is demoted so that only one primary category remains. When `false`, the assignment is treated as a secondary category link.

IShoppingMallProductCategoryAssignment.I.description:
Update DTO for modifying mutable metadata of an existing product–category assignment row.

Unlike the response DTO and create DTO, this type is treated as a logical update contract and is not directly bound to a single Prisma model. Instead of mirroring the exact columns of `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, it exposes higher‑level business attributes that the service layer can translate into changes on `is_primary` and any other catalog configuration maintained around the junction table.

Structural identifiers such as the owning product and category, as well as system‑managed fields and foreign keys from `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`, remain under exclusive server control and are never accepted from the client in this schema. Backend logic is responsible for validating and persisting the requested changes in a way that remains consistent with the underlying Prisma model and catalog rules.

isPrimary.description:
Flag indicating whether this category assignment is the primary category for the product.

This is a higher‑level, camelCase update field that conceptually maps to the `is_primary` column on the `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments` Prisma model. When set to true, the assignment should be treated as the primary classification in navigation and search UIs for the associated product. Only one assignment per product should typically be marked as primary, but enforcement of that invariant is handled in the service or database layer rather than by this DTO.

sortOrder.description:
Numeric ordering value that controls the display position of the product within this category.

This field represents a logical sort index used by catalog and merchandising logic. Depending on the implementation, it may be backed by a dedicated ordering column on the assignment record or by related catalog structures. Lower numbers generally appear earlier in category listings, but the exact range, collision behavior, and storage mapping are defined by business logic rather than by this schema.

isVisibleInNavigation.description:
Optional flag indicating whether this product–category assignment should be visible in standard category navigation.

This is a logical visibility control rather than a direct projection of a single column on `shopping_mall_product_category_assignments`. When set to true or false, the service layer can interpret the value to update one or more underlying flags or to adjust how the assignment participates in navigation (for example, by combining it with global catalog rules or additional tables). When null, platform defaults or higher-level visibility rules apply and no explicit override is requested for this assignment.

isVisibleInSearch.description:
Optional flag indicating whether the product should be discoverable via search when accessed through this category context.

This filter is a business-level abstraction that may be implemented through search indexing rules, auxiliary tables, or derived conditions rather than a dedicated `is_visible_in_search` column on the junction table. A null value means that global and product-level visibility rules determine behavior, while a non-null value can be used to request an override for this specific assignment only.

activeFrom.description:
Optional start timestamp from which this assignment becomes active.

This value is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC and represents a business rule boundary used by catalog logic. The underlying persistence may store this value in a dedicated column, an auxiliary scheduling table, or a computed configuration. When provided, the assignment should only be treated as effective on or after this date-time. A null value means the assignment is active immediately unless constrained by other rules.

activeUntil.description:
Optional end timestamp after which this assignment is no longer considered active.

Like `activeFrom`, this is a logical scheduling attribute represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. The service layer is responsible for mapping it to the actual persistence mechanism. When provided, the assignment should be treated as inactive after this date-time. A null value means the assignment remains active indefinitely unless deactivated or overridden by other mechanisms.

IShoppingMallProductMedia.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying product media records associated with a specific product in the `shopping_mall_product_media` table.

This request type is used with PATCH-based search endpoints where the product context is provided via a path parameter (`productCode`). It supports flexible filtering, sorting, and pagination without duplicating the product identifier that already exists in the URL.

Most filters correspond to columns in the underlying Prisma model: for example, `mediaType` maps to the `media_type` column, `isPrimary` to the `is_primary` column, and `createdFrom` / `createdTo` to the `created_at` timestamp. Pagination controls (`page` and `limit`) are purely logical request parameters.

The `isVisible` filter is a higher-level visibility abstraction. In typical implementations, visible media records are those with `deleted_at IS NULL` or those that satisfy other catalog visibility rules. This DTO does not assume a dedicated `is_visible` column on `shopping_mall_product_media`; instead, the backend uses `isVisible` to decide how to constrain the query on `deleted_at` and related fields.

All fields are optional so that clients can supply only the criteria needed for a given search, and the backend can combine them into appropriate Prisma queries over `shopping_mall_product_media` rows linked to the resolved product.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated media listings.

When omitted, the backend should default to the first page (typically 1). Values less than 1 should be rejected or normalized to 1 by the service layer so that negative or zero page indices are never forwarded to the data access layer.

limit.description:
Maximum number of media records to return in a single page.

This controls the page size for the result set and does not correspond to any column in `shopping_mall_product_media`. The backend should enforce reasonable upper bounds to prevent excessively large responses, even if higher values are provided by clients, and should document any default limit applied when the value is omitted.

mediaType.description:
Optional media type filter used to restrict results to a specific classification such as image, video, or document.

This value maps conceptually to the `media_type` column of the `shopping_mall_product_media` Prisma model. When null or omitted, all media types are eligible. Typical values are implementation-defined but might include labels like "image", "thumbnail", "video", or other enumerated media classifications; the backend is responsible for validating allowed values.

isVisible.description:
Optional visibility flag filter indicating whether only visible or only hidden media records should be returned.

This field is a logical abstraction rather than a direct mapping to a dedicated `is_visible` column. In most implementations, "visible" corresponds to media records where `deleted_at` is null (and possibly additional business conditions). When `isVisible` is true, the query should typically constrain results to active/visible media (e.g., `deleted_at IS NULL`). When false, it may be used to retrieve soft-deleted or otherwise hidden records. When null or omitted, visibility is not used as a filter and both visible and hidden records may be included, subject to authorization rules.

isPrimary.description:
Optional filter to limit results to media records marked as primary for the product.

This flag corresponds to the `is_primary` column in the `shopping_mall_product_media` Prisma model. When true, only primary media items (such as gallery cover images) are returned. When false, only non-primary media are returned. When null, the primary designation is ignored as a filter and both primary and non-primary records are eligible.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for the media creation timestamp in UTC.

This value is used to constrain results based on the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_product_media`. When provided, only media records with a `created_at` value greater than or equal to this timestamp should be included in the results. A null value means no lower bound is applied and records are not filtered by a start date.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound for the media creation timestamp in UTC.

This value is applied to the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_product_media`. When provided, only media records with a `created_at` value less than or equal to this timestamp should be included in the results. A null value means no upper bound is applied and records are not filtered by an end date.

orderBy.description:
Optional sort field name indicating which column or logical field to use when ordering the result set.

Typical values might include "createdAt", "displayOrder", or "id", which the backend maps to the appropriate columns on `shopping_mall_product_media` (for example, `created_at`, `display_order`, or `id`). The service layer must validate the provided field name against a whitelist of supported options and fall back to a default ordering if the value is invalid or omitted.

orderDirection.description:
Optional sort direction for the ordered result set.

Expected values are implementation-defined but commonly include "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending ordering. When null or omitted, a default direction (often ascending) is applied by the backend. The chosen direction is applied to the field indicated by `orderBy`, or to the default ordering field when `orderBy` is not provided.

IShoppingMallProductMedia.description:
Detailed representation of a single product media asset associated with a catalog product in the shopping mall platform.

Represents an individual media resource such as an image or video that decorates a product in the catalog. Each record is linked to a parent product in shopping_mall_products and stores a URI pointing to the actual stored asset, accessibility text, media type classification, display ordering, and visibility flags.

This DTO is used for read operations that retrieve full media metadata for admin, seller, or public catalog views, and now also exposes the soft-delete state so that administrative tools can distinguish active records from logically deleted ones.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product media record.

Typically a UUID string that uniquely identifies this media asset row in the shopping_mall_product_media table and is used as the stable reference key for update and delete operations.

uri.description:
Absolute URI of the media resource, such as an HTTPS URL or storage bucket path.

This field must always be a valid URI string. It never contains binary data or base64-encoded content; the actual file is stored separately in a CDN or object storage service, and clients reference it only via this URI.

media_type.description:
Media type classification for this asset.

Common values include strings such as "image" or "video" and may be extended with additional categories according to platform configuration. The exact allowed values are enforced at the business logic or database constraint level so that the UI can choose appropriate rendering behavior.

alt_text.description:
Alternative text for the media asset used for accessibility and SEO.

When provided, this text should describe the content of the media in a concise human-readable form so that screen readers and search engines can understand the image or video. It may be null when no alt text has been configured, or when the alt text has been explicitly cleared as part of moderation or content updates.

display_order.description:
Integer value that controls the relative ordering of media assets for a product.

Within the scope of a single product, display_order values are expected to be unique so that the presentation order of media items is stable and deterministic across clients and sessions.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this media asset is the primary or main media for the product.

At most one media record per product should typically have is_primary set to true. Business rules may enforce that primary media is used for thumbnails and main product images in list and detail views.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this media record was created.

Represented in ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC. This value is set by the backend when the row is first inserted into shopping_mall_product_media and never decreases over time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the last time this media record was updated.

Represented in ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC. This value is refreshed on every successful update to the shopping_mall_product_media row, allowing clients and administrators to understand when metadata or flags were last changed.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this media record was soft-deleted.

When null, the media record is considered active and eligible to be shown in standard product galleries subject to other visibility rules. When set to a non-null ISO 8601 UTC date-time, the record has been logically deleted and should normally be excluded from customer-facing views while still remaining available for audit trails, historical references, or administrative recovery workflows.

product.description:
Summary representation of the parent catalog product that owns this media asset.

Provides basic product context—such as identity, name, and key display attributes—so that clients can understand which product this media belongs to without issuing an additional product lookup call. This avoids extra round trips when managing or rendering product media in admin and seller tools.

IShoppingMallProductMedia.ICreate.description:
