Request body schema for creating a new product media asset under an existing catalog product.

Used by seller or admin tooling to attach a single media resource (such as an image or video) to a product identified by its business-visible product code in the request path. The client provides a URI for the media, media type classification, ordering information, and optional accessibility text. System-managed fields such as identifiers and timestamps are generated by the backend.

uri.description:
Absolute URI of the media resource to associate with the product.

This must be a valid URI string pointing to a pre-uploaded asset (for example an HTTPS URL or object storage path). The client must not send binary content or base64-encoded data in this field.

media_type.description:
Media type classification for the new asset.

Typical values include strings like "image" or "video" and must conform to the allowed categories defined by the platform for shopping_mall_product_media.media_type.

alt_text.description:
Optional alternative text for the media asset used for accessibility and SEO.

When provided, this should concisely describe the visual or informational content of the media. Can be null when no alt text is configured.

display_order.description:
Integer specifying the desired display ordering of this media within the product's media set.

Within the context of a single product, display_order values are expected to be unique. If another media record already uses the same display order for this product, the backend should reject the request with a conflict-style error.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this newly created media asset should be marked as the primary media for the product.

When set to true, business logic may update other media records so that this becomes the single primary asset for the product.

IShoppingMallProductMedia.IUpdate.description:
Mutable fields for updating an existing product media asset associated with a catalog product in the shopping_mall_product_media table.

Used by seller or admin tools to modify metadata of an already existing media record, such as changing its URI, accessibility text, media type, display order within the product gallery, or whether it is marked as the primary media.

All fields are optional to allow partial updates. When a field is omitted from the request body, the corresponding value in the target record remains unchanged. When a field is provided, the backend overwrites the stored value with the new one, including the possibility of explicitly clearing nullable fields by sending null.

uri.description:
Absolute or resolvable URI of the media asset stored in the CDN or media storage layer.

When provided, must be a syntactically valid URI and should point to a previously uploaded and accessible asset. Changing this value effectively repoints the media record to a different underlying file or resource.

alt_text.description:
Human-readable alternative text describing the media asset for accessibility and SEO purposes.

When provided as a non-null string, this text is exposed to screen readers and used when the media cannot be rendered, and it should concisely describe the visual content or purpose of the asset. When provided explicitly as null, the existing alt text is cleared so that no alternative text is stored. If the property is omitted entirely from the update payload, the current alt text value is left unchanged.

media_type.description:
Logical type of the media asset used by the catalog and UI layers to determine how to render the asset.

Typical values include categories such as `image`, `video`, or `document`. The implementation should validate this against the allowed business-level media categories configured for the platform so that inconsistent or unsupported types are rejected.

display_order.description:
Ordering index of this media asset within the product’s media gallery.

Display order values are expected to be unique per product and typically form a dense ascending sequence starting from 0 or 1. When updated, the service must ensure that the new value does not conflict with another active media record for the same product according to business rules and database constraints.

is_primary.description:
Indicates whether this media asset is the primary media for the parent product.

When set to true, business logic should ensure that at most one media asset per product is marked as primary, potentially demoting any previously primary asset. The primary media is commonly used as the main product thumbnail or hero image in listings and detail pages.

IShoppingMallProductOptionType.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for listing option types defined for a specific product in the shopping_mall_product_option_types table.

Used by back-office catalog tooling and internal services to retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of option types (such as size or color dimensions) associated with the product identified by productCode in the request path. All fields are optional and act as filters or controls; omitted fields are treated as "no filter" or default behavior.

page.description:
1-based page index of the result set to retrieve.

If omitted, the implementation should fall back to a sensible default such as page 1. Values less than 1 should be rejected or normalized according to platform-wide pagination rules.

limit.description:
Maximum number of option type records to return in a single page of results.

If not provided, the service should use a platform default (for example, 20 or 50). Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets.

search.description:
Free-text search term used to match option type names, labels, or other indexed fields.

When provided, the backend applies it as a case-insensitive search across configured columns. An empty string should be treated as if no search filter were applied.

is_active.description:
Optional filter that, when provided, restricts results to option types whose active flag matches the given value.

This allows tooling to list only option types currently available for use in SKU definitions or to include inactive definitions for maintenance purposes.

order_by.description:
Logical field name to use for sorting the option types within the result set.

Common values include `display_order`, `created_at`, or `name`, but the exact accepted values are determined by the implementation. When omitted, a default ordering such as `display_order` ascending then `created_at` ascending is typically applied.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply to the chosen order_by field.

Expected values are semantic indicators such as `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending. When omitted, ascending order is typically assumed by default.

This field is intentionally modeled as a free-form string to allow future extension (for example, `asc_nulls_last`) while still being validated against allowed values at runtime.

IShoppingMallProductOptionType.description:
Product option type definition for a shoppingMall catalog product, mapped directly to the `shopping_mall_product_option_types` Prisma model.

This DTO exposes only fields that correspond to real columns on `shopping_mall_product_option_types`, ensuring that response payloads remain consistent with the underlying database schema and do not reference phantom fields.

The type is typically used by catalog management and product detail APIs to represent how a product’s option dimensions (such as Color or Size) are structured and ordered.

id.description:
Primary key of the product option type record as stored in the `shopping_mall_product_option_types` table.

This value uniquely identifies the option type row and is used as the stable identifier in update and lookup operations that target this specific option dimension for a product.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the option type, such as "Color" or "Size", persisted in the `name` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_types`.

This field is used by sellers and internal tools to identify the option dimension and may also be surfaced to end users in some UIs depending on configuration and localization rules.

display_name.description:
Optional user-facing label stored in the `display_name` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_types`.

When present, this value is typically used in storefront UIs and configuration screens instead of the raw `name` field to provide a more friendly or localized label. When null, clients may fall back to using `name` or another derived label according to business rules.

display_order.description:
Ordering index for this option type, backed by the `display_order` column in `shopping_mall_product_option_types`.

Lower values are rendered earlier when multiple option types are shown for the same product (for example, showing Color before Size). This value must be interpreted relative to other option types belonging to the same product.

created_at.description:
Timestamp from the `created_at` column indicating when this option type record was first created.

The value is managed by the system and reflects the creation time in the database, typically in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp from the `updated_at` column indicating when this option type record was last modified.

This system-managed value changes whenever mutable fields on the option type are updated, allowing clients and operators to understand the recency of configuration changes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete timestamp mapped from the `deleted_at` column of the `shopping_mall_product_option_types` table.

When this value is null, the option type is considered active and eligible for normal use in catalog configuration and storefront flows. When it holds a date-time value, the record has been soft-deleted and should typically be excluded from standard read operations, but may still be visible in administrative or auditing contexts to support recovery, analysis, or background cleanup workflows.

IShoppingMallProductOptionType.ICreate.description:
Request body DTO for creating a new product option type for a specific product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This schema maps directly to the `shopping_mall_product_option_types` Prisma model and exposes only fields that correspond to real columns on that model. The parent product is identified by the `productCode` path parameter of the API endpoint, so no product identifier appears in this body.

Use this DTO from seller or administrator tooling when defining a new option dimension (for example, "Color" or "Size") that will later be combined with product option values and SKUs.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the option type, such as "Color" or "Size".

This value is stored in the `name` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_types` and is used by sellers and internal tools to identify the option dimension. It is typically expected to be unique per product for clarity in configuration and SKU management flows.

display_name.description:
Optional user-facing label for the option type, persisted in the `display_name` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_types`.

When provided, this value is usually shown in storefront UIs and management consoles instead of the raw `name`, allowing more friendly or localized labels. When null, clients may fall back to displaying `name` or other derived text according to their UI rules.

display_order.description:
Ordering index for this option type, stored in the `display_order` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_types`.

Lower values are rendered earlier when multiple option types are configured for the same product (for example, showing Color before Size). The value must be chosen so that the complete set of option types for a product appears in a stable and intuitive sequence in variant selection UIs.

IShoppingMallProductOptionType.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for a product option type belonging to a specific product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This schema maps directly to the `shopping_mall_product_option_types` Prisma model and exposes only mutable columns. The target option type record is identified by the `productCode` and `productOptionTypeId` path parameters of the API endpoint, so no identifier fields appear in this body.

All properties are optional to support partial updates; any property omitted from the payload is interpreted as "no change" by the service layer.

name.description:
Updated internal name of the option type, mapped to the `name` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_types`.

Changing this value allows sellers or administrators to refine how the option dimension is labeled in back-office tools. Business rules may still enforce uniqueness within the product and may restrict changes if downstream SKUs already depend on the original naming.

display_name.description:
Updated user-facing label for the option type, mapped to the `display_name` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_types`.

Set this to a non-null value to provide a friendly or localized label used in storefront UIs. Explicitly setting it to null removes the custom label so that clients can fall back to `name` or other default display logic.

display_order.description:
Updated ordering index for this option type, mapped to the `display_order` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_types`.

Adjust this value to reorder how option types are presented relative to other option types for the same product. Lower numbers are rendered earlier and should be managed so that variant selection UIs show a stable, predictable sequence.

IShoppingMallProductOptionValue.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for listing product option values belonging to a specific option type of a product in the shopping mall catalog.

This schema is used as the request body for the read-only search endpoint `PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productCode}/optionTypes/{productOptionTypeId}/values`. Path parameters provide the parent context (product and option type), so this DTO MUST NOT duplicate `productCode` or `productOptionTypeId`. Instead, it only describes pagination, filtering, and sorting behavior for records in the `shopping_mall_product_option_values` Prisma model.

The field set is intentionally limited to common search and paging controls that can be implemented purely against the existing Prisma columns (`value`, `display_name`, `display_order`, `created_at`) without requiring any additional database fields. It is designed for use by both storefront experiences and back-office catalog tools that need to browse or manage product option values efficiently.

page.description:
1-based index of the result page to retrieve.

When omitted, the server should default to the first page. This value must be a positive integer greater than or equal to 1 so that pagination is well-defined and consistent with typical catalog browsing semantics across the platform.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

When omitted, the server should apply a sensible default and enforce an upper bound to protect performance. This value must be a positive integer greater than or equal to 1 so that each page can yield at least one option value record when matches exist.

oneOf.description: Free-text keyword used to match against human-readable fields of the option value, such as `value` or `display_name`. Implementations may apply case-insensitive or partial matching according to business rules.

No free-text search term is provided.

When null or omitted, the server does not apply any generic text search filter and instead relies purely on structured filters such as `value` or `display_name` if they are present.

search.description:
Optional free-text search keyword used to match against option value fields.

When provided as a non-empty string, the server should apply a text-based filter to fields such as `value` and `display_name`. When null or omitted, no generic text filter is applied.

oneOf.description:
Exact value of the `value` column in `shopping_mall_product_option_values` to filter by, for example `"RED"` or `"XL"`.

When supplied, the server should restrict results to option values whose canonical `value` matches this string exactly.

No exact `value` filter is applied.

When null or omitted, results are not restricted by the raw `value` field and may include any option values that satisfy other filters.

value.description:
Optional exact match filter for the raw option `value` field.

Use this when callers know the canonical value label (for example, `"RED"` or `"XL"`) and want to retrieve only that specific option value under the given option type.

oneOf.description:
Filter expression targeting the user-facing `display_name` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values`.

Implementations may treat this as an exact or partial match depending on business rules and indexing strategy.

No filter is applied on the `display_name` field.

When null or omitted, results are not restricted by the display name shown in UIs.

display_name.description:
Optional filter targeting the user-facing `display_name` of the option value.

This filter is typically used by management tools that need to locate values based on what is displayed in storefront UIs or localized labels.

oneOf.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether only active (`true`) or only inactive (`false`) option values should be returned.

Implementations usually derive this from lifecycle columns such as `deleted_at` in combination with any additional visibility rules.

No lifecycle filter is applied based purely on active status.

When null or omitted, both active and inactive option values may be returned, subject to higher-level visibility policies enforced by the application.

is_active.description:
Optional filter restricting results to active or inactive option values.

When set to `true`, only currently active values should be included. When set to `false`, only inactive or soft-deleted values should be included. When null or omitted, both are eligible to appear in the result set.

oneOf.description:
Sort by the `display_order` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values`.

This is the primary sort key for controlling how option values appear within an option type and is typically the default ordering used by storefront UIs.

Sort by the canonical `value` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values`.

This is commonly used when presenting option values in alphabetical or lexical order by their internal labels.

Sort by the `created_at` timestamp column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values`.

This sort key is useful for administrative workflows that need to see the newest or oldest option values first for review or cleanup.

No explicit sort field is specified.

When null or omitted, the server should default to a stable, sensible sort field, typically `display_order` ascending for a predictable user experience.

order_by.description:
Optional field name to use for sorting results.

When provided, it must be one of the supported sort keys: `display_order`, `value`, or `created_at`. When null or omitted, the server should default to a stable ordering such as `display_order` ascending.

oneOf.description:
Sort in ascending order for the chosen `order_by` field.

For example, lower `display_order` values appear first, earlier `created_at` timestamps appear first, or lexicographically smaller `value` strings appear first.

Sort in descending order for the chosen `order_by` field.

For example, higher `display_order` values appear first, later `created_at` timestamps appear first, or lexicographically larger `value` strings appear first.

No explicit sort direction is specified.

When null or omitted, the server should default to ascending order to ensure consistent and predictable list behavior.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the field specified in `order_by`.

When set, it must be either `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. When null or omitted, the server should default to ascending order.

IShoppingMallProductOptionValue.description:
Detailed representation of a single product option value belonging to a specific product option type within a product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This DTO maps to the `shopping_mall_product_option_values` Prisma model and exposes the option value’s identifiers, business value, display metadata, ordering information, activation flags, and audit timestamps. It also exposes the parent option type as a summary association so that clients can understand the option hierarchy without issuing additional lookups.

For lifecycle and audit scenarios, this type additionally exposes the underlying soft-delete timestamp so that clients can distinguish between active, soft-deleted, and merely hidden option values.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product option value (`shopping_mall_product_option_values.id`).

This identifier is used internally by the backend and in path parameters when addressing a specific option value resource.

value.description:
Internal key or raw value for this option (for example, a machine-friendly code such as "blue" or "xl").

This field corresponds to the `value` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values` and must be unique within the same option type. It is used as the stable key when composing SKU option assignments and for internal lookups.

display_name.description:
Human-friendly display label for this option value (for example, "Blue" or "XL").

This maps to the nullable `display_name` column on `shopping_mall_product_option_values`. When null, client applications may fall back to the `value` field for display or apply their own localization rules.

display_order.description:
Numeric sort index used to order option values within the same option type.

This corresponds to the `display_order` column on `shopping_mall_product_option_values`. Lower numbers typically appear first in UI lists, and the combination of option type and `display_order` is unique to avoid ambiguous ordering.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this option value is currently active and selectable in the catalog context.

When `true`, the value can be presented to shoppers and used in SKU configurations, subject to other visibility rules. When `false`, it may be hidden from storefront UIs while still preserved for historical SKUs or orders.

This flag is a derived lifecycle indicator that typically reflects whether the underlying soft-delete timestamp `deleted_at` is null, potentially combined with additional business rules (for example, compliance or visibility constraints). For full audit trails, clients should consider both `is_active` and `deleted_at` together to understand the exact lifecycle state of the value.

optionType.description:
Parent product option type that owns this option value, exposed as a summary association.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_product_option_type_id` foreign key relation to `shopping_mall_product_option_types`. It enables clients to understand which option dimension (for example, "Color" or "Size") this value belongs to without making additional API calls.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this option value was first created in the system.

The value is stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values` and follows the ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this option value was last updated.

This corresponds to the `updated_at` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values` and is automatically maintained by the backend to reflect the most recent change to the record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete timestamp for this option value, mapped from the nullable `deleted_at` column of the `shopping_mall_product_option_values` table.

When this field is `null`, the underlying record is considered not soft-deleted and can participate in normal catalog operations, subject to other business rules. When it contains a date-time value, the record has been soft-deleted and should generally be excluded from storefront experiences while remaining available for audit, reporting, or historical reconstruction.

IShoppingMallProductOptionValue.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new product option value under an existing product option type for a specific product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This DTO is used in seller-scoped catalog management operations where an authenticated seller (or platform admin) defines additional option values such as sizes or colors. It maps to the `shopping_mall_product_option_values` Prisma model for insert operations, excluding system-managed identifiers and audit fields.

The parent product and option type are provided via path parameters, so this DTO focuses solely on the business attributes of the new option value and its initial activation state.

value.description:
Internal key or raw value for this option (for example, a machine-friendly code such as "blue" or "xl"). Must be unique within the same option type.

This value is stored in the `value` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values` and is used as the canonical key when composing SKU option assignments and performing internal lookups.

display_name.description:
Human-friendly display label for this option value (for example, "Blue" or "XL").

This field maps to the nullable `display_name` column on `shopping_mall_product_option_values`. When omitted or explicitly set to null, clients and UIs may display the `value` instead or apply their own localization rules.

display_order.description:
Numeric sort index used to order option values within the same option type.

This value is written to the `display_order` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values`. Lower numbers typically appear first in UI lists, and the combination of option type and `display_order` is expected to be unique to avoid ambiguous ordering.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether the new option value should be active immediately after creation.

When `true`, the created value is treated as active and can be surfaced in storefront UIs (subject to other visibility rules). When `false`, the value is created but should typically be hidden from storefront UIs until explicitly activated.

If this property is omitted from the request body, the backend applies its default activation policy, which usually treats newly created option values as active unless otherwise configured by business rules.

IShoppingMallProductOptionValue.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for a product option value under a specific option type for a shopping mall product.

This schema represents the fields that a seller or catalog administrator is allowed to modify on an existing option value row in `shopping_mall_product_option_values`. The option value is already identified by the combination of the parent product, option type, and option value ID in the request path, so this DTO does not include any identifier or foreign key fields.

Only business-editable attributes such as the canonical value key, human-friendly display name, presentation order, and activation flag are exposed for partial update. System-managed fields like `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are excluded because they are controlled by the backend and should never be provided by the client.

value.description:
Canonical value key for the option value, such as "Red" or "XL".

This field corresponds to the `value` column of `shopping_mall_product_option_values`. It must be unique within the same option type and is used as the stable key when composing SKU option assignments. When omitted in an update request, the existing key is preserved.

Clients should respect any maximum length or normalization rules enforced at the database layer, and avoid sending leading or trailing whitespace.

display_name.description:
Optional human-friendly display label for the option value.

This maps to the nullable `display_name` column on `shopping_mall_product_option_values`. When set, it can provide localized or more user-facing text that differs from the canonical `value` key. When set to null, any existing display name is cleared, and UIs may fall back to the `value` field.

If omitted from the request body, the stored display name remains unchanged.

display_order.description:
Presentation order index of the option value within its option type.

This corresponds to the `display_order` column on `shopping_mall_product_option_values`. Lower numbers generally appear earlier in UI lists. The combination of `shopping_mall_product_option_type_id` and `display_order` is unique, so callers must avoid duplicates when reordering values.

When omitted from the update request, the existing ordering value is preserved.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this option value is currently active and selectable in the catalog.

Although the underlying row in `shopping_mall_product_option_values` may always exist for historical integrity, setting this field to `false` allows sellers or administrators to hide the value from new selections while keeping it available for existing SKUs or orders. When `true`, and subject to other catalog and inventory rules, the value can be presented in storefront UIs and used in SKU configurations.

If this property is omitted from the update request, the backend preserves the current activation state, enabling safe partial updates that only touch fields the client explicitly intends to change.

IShoppingMallProductSku.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating product SKUs belonging to a specific product.

This schema defines the filter, sorting, and pagination parameters used when querying the `shopping_mall_product_skus` table for a single product, typically via an endpoint scoped by product code such as `/shoppingMall/products/{productCode}/skus`. It does not include the product identifier itself, because that context is supplied in the URL path.

The DTO is intentionally generic so that the backend can apply additional catalog, inventory, and visibility rules based on these parameters. Clients can control page size, offset, sorting behavior, and business-level filters such as lifecycle status, sales channel, region, stock availability, and specific option value selections to retrieve the relevant subset of SKU variants for storefront or management UIs.

page.description:
Page number for pagination when listing SKUs.

This value is one-based in typical REST pagination semantics, where `1` refers to the first page of results. When omitted, implementations may default to the first page. Negative values should be rejected by validation.

Combined with `limit`, this controls the slice of `shopping_mall_product_skus` returned in the paginated response.

limit.description:
Maximum number of SKU records to return per page.

This value defines the page size when listing SKUs from `shopping_mall_product_skus`. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to protect backend resources, and may apply a sensible default when the client does not specify a value.

Used together with `page` to compute the underlying query offset.

status.description:
Optional lifecycle status filter for SKUs.

This field can be used to restrict results to SKUs in a particular state, such as `"active"`, `"inactive"`, or `"discontinued"`, matching the `status` column on `shopping_mall_product_skus`. The exact set of allowed values is defined by business rules and may be validated by the service layer.

When omitted, implementations typically return SKUs in all non-deleted states or apply a default filter appropriate for the calling context.

sort_key.description:
Optional sorting key that controls which attribute is used to order the result set.

Typical values include:
- `"price"`: sort SKUs by their `price_amount` field from `shopping_mall_product_skus`.
- `"created_at"`: sort by creation timestamp, showing newest or oldest variants first.
- `"availability"`: sort by an availability or stock-related signal derived from inventory tables.

The backend may support additional keys or map business-friendly values to underlying database columns. When this property is omitted, the implementation applies its default sort, such as creation date or SKU code order.

sort_order.description:
Optional sort direction used together with `sort_key` to order the SKU list.

Common values are `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. For example, `sort_key = "price"` and `sort_order = "asc"` would list SKUs from lowest to highest price.

If this property is omitted, the backend applies a default direction appropriate for the selected sort key, such as descending for `created_at` or ascending for `price`.

channel_code.description:
Optional sales channel code filter that restricts results to SKUs visible or relevant to a specific channel.

Examples include codes representing web storefront, mobile app, marketplace integrations, or other logical channels. Implementations typically map this value to visibility or listing rules defined in configuration tables such as product visibility rules.

When omitted, the backend may apply a default channel based on the caller context or return SKUs across all applicable channels.

region_code.description:
Optional region code filter that restricts results to SKUs available in a specific market or geographic area.

This value is conceptually aligned with region or market configuration entries (for example, `shopping_mall_region_settings`) and can be used to honor region-specific availability, pricing, or compliance rules when listing SKUs.

If not provided, the implementation may use a default region derived from the request context or return SKUs across all regions permitted for the caller.

in_stock_only.description:
Flag indicating whether only SKUs that currently have available stock should be returned.

When set to `true`, the backend should join or consult inventory state (for example, `shopping_mall_inventory_items`) and filter out SKUs that are out of stock or otherwise unavailable for purchase, according to business-defined thresholds.

When omitted or `false`, the response may include SKUs regardless of their current inventory level, which is useful for management UIs or analytics views.

option_value_ids.description:
Optional list of option value identifiers used to constrain the search to SKUs that match specific option selections.

Each entry should be the UUID of a row in `shopping_mall_product_option_values` that is related to the product referenced in the request path. Implementations can use this list to filter SKUs through junction tables such as `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments`, returning only variants that include all or some of the specified option values depending on the applied business rules.

If this array is omitted or empty, no filtering by option values is applied and SKUs for all combinations may be returned.

IShoppingMallProductSku.description:
Detailed SKU variant entity in the shopping mall catalog.

Represents a concrete purchasable variant of a product, identified by a business-level skuCode that is unique within the scope of its parent product. Each SKU corresponds to a row in the shopping_mall_product_skus Prisma model and may be joined with related entities such as option value assignments, inventory items, and visibility or compliance flags.

This DTO is used as the detail response type for operations that fetch a specific SKU under a product, and as the return type for create and update operations on SKUs.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SKU variant record.

This is the primary key of the shopping_mall_product_skus row and is stable for the lifetime of the SKU.

code.description:
Business-level unique code of the SKU within its parent product.

This corresponds to the `code` field on shopping_mall_product_skus and participates in a composite unique constraint together with the parent product ID.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the SKU variant.

Suitable for showing on product detail pages and catalog management tools to distinguish one variant from another.

listPrice.description:
Standard list price of the SKU before discounts, in the platform's base currency.

Used as the reference price for discount calculations and to display strike-through prices when a lower sale price applies.

salePrice.description:
Current effective sale price of the SKU in the platform's base currency.

When present and lower than listPrice, indicates a discounted price shown to customers and used in promotional calculations.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code representing the currency of listPrice and salePrice values.

Examples include "USD" or "KRW"; the allowed set of currencies is controlled by platform configuration.

isActive.description:
Flag indicating whether this SKU is currently active in the catalog.

Inactive SKUs are typically hidden from public shoppers and cannot be purchased, but their records remain for historical analytics and order references.

isPurchasable.description:
Flag indicating whether this SKU is currently purchasable.

A SKU may be active but temporarily not purchasable due to business rules, stock situations, or compliance constraints. When false, add-to-cart operations should be blocked.

productCode.description:
Business-level unique code of the parent product in shopping_mall_products.

This reflects the product context under which this SKU is defined and matches the `{productCode}` path parameter used by SKU endpoints.

product.description:
Summary representation of the parent product that owns this SKU.

Provides essential catalog context such as product name, brand, and primary media so that a client can fully render the SKU in a single call without performing an additional product lookup.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this SKU record was created in the catalog.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC, used for auditing and time-based analytics.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this SKU record was last updated.

Expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC, allowing clients to detect stale data and implement caching strategies.

IShoppingMallProductSku.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new SKU variant under an existing product.

This DTO maps to the shopping_mall_product_skus Prisma model and is used by seller or platform-admin catalog management tools to define new purchasable variants. It accepts only fields that are client-provided at creation time; system-managed fields like identifiers and timestamps are excluded.

code.description: Business-level unique code of the SKU within the referenced product. Must be unique in combination with the parent product and will participate in a composite unique constraint at the database level.

name.description: Human-readable display name of the SKU variant, used in product detail and management interfaces.

listPrice.description: Standard list price of the SKU before discounts, in the platform's base currency. Must be non-negative and align with business pricing rules.

salePrice.description: Effective sale price of the SKU in the platform's base currency. When lower than listPrice, indicates a discounted price. Must be non-negative and respect pricing validation rules.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code representing the currency of listPrice and salePrice values (for example, "USD" or "KRW"). Defaults to the platform base currency when omitted.

isActive.description: Initial active state of the SKU in the catalog. When true, the SKU is eligible to appear in listings, subject to visibility rules.

isPurchasable.description: Initial purchasable state of the SKU. When true, the SKU can be added to carts and purchased, assuming inventory and business conditions are satisfied.

IShoppingMallProductSku.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for a product SKU variant in the shoppingMall catalog.

Represents the subset of SKU fields in shopping_mall_product_skus that are mutable after creation, such as display attributes, pricing, SEO metadata and operational flags controlling availability and visibility.

Identity-defining fields like id, product_id and code, as well as structural option assignments, are intentionally excluded.

displayName.description:
Human-readable display name for this SKU variant as presented in catalog UIs.

Typically shown alongside or instead of the parent product name to distinguish variant characteristics (for example, "Blue / M").

listPrice.description:
Standard list price for this SKU before discounts, in the platform’s base currency.

This is the reference price shown when there is an active sale price or marketing promotion.

salePrice.description:
Optional discounted sale price for this SKU in the platform’s base currency.

When present and lower than listPrice, UI can show discount badges or strike-through pricing.

isActive.description:
Flag indicating whether this SKU is active in the catalog.

Inactive SKUs are hidden from search and purchase flows but may remain for historical order references.

isPurchasable.description:
Flag indicating whether this SKU can currently be purchased.

When false, the SKU may still be visible for informational or pre-launch purposes but cannot be added to cart or ordered.

channelVisibility.description:
Optional per-channel visibility overrides for this SKU.

Allows enabling or disabling visibility on specific sales channels (for example, web, mobile, marketplace integrations) without changing global activation flags.

seoTitle.description:
Optional SEO-friendly title for this SKU’s detail page.

Used in HTML <title> tags and search engine snippets to improve discoverability and click-through rates.

seoDescription.description:
Optional SEO-friendly meta description for this SKU.

Summarizes key attributes for search engine indexing and social sharing cards so that external previews accurately describe the variant.

metadata.description:
Free-form structured metadata for this SKU.

Used to store additional key-value attributes for integrations, analytics, or UI hints that are not first-class Prisma columns, while still keeping the shape centralized in a named type.

IShoppingMallSkuOptionValueAssignment.IR.description:
Search and filter DTO for listing SKU option value assignments under a specific product and SKU in the shoppingMall catalog.

Represents query parameters submitted in the request body when listing records from shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments. Supports generic pagination and sorting, as well as optional filters by option type or option value identity.

The product and SKU context are supplied via path parameters (productCode and skuCode) of the calling operation and must not be repeated here.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Starts from 1. Used together with pageSize to paginate through option value assignments for the targeted SKU.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of records to return per page. Used together with page to control pagination window when listing assignments.

sortBy.description: Field name used for sorting assignment results. Typical values include createdAt, updatedAt, or optionValueCode depending on Prisma schema naming.

oneOf.description: Sort direction applied to the sortBy field.
Sort direction applied to the sortBy field.

sortDirection.description: Sort direction applied to the sortBy field.

optionTypeCode.description: Optional filter restricting results to assignments that belong to a specific product option type, referenced by its business code in shopping_mall_product_option_types.

optionValueCode.description: Optional filter restricting results to assignments that reference a specific option value, referenced by its business code in shopping_mall_product_option_values.

createdFrom.description: Optional lower bound (inclusive) for filtering assignments based on their creation timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

createdTo.description: Optional upper bound (inclusive) for filtering assignments based on their creation timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

IShoppingMallSkuOptionValueAssignment.description:
Detailed representation of an option value assignment that connects a specific SKU (stock keeping unit) to a concrete product option value in the shoppingMall catalog.

This DTO is used in customer- and seller-facing read operations to expose how a SKU is linked to a specific option value (for example, Color: Red or Size: M). It reflects the underlying `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` Prisma model, while transforming foreign key fields into richer referenced objects that are safe and meaningful for API consumers.

The entity participates in variant configuration for products and is typically accessed in the context of a particular product and SKU, using product and SKU business codes in the API path. It should not expose any authentication or credential data and does not include system-only fields beyond identifiers and timestamps.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the SKU option value assignment record in `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments`.

productCode.description: Business-visible code of the product that the associated SKU belongs to. This mirrors the `code` field on the `shopping_mall_products` model and is included for convenience in read responses.

skuCode.description: Business-visible SKU code within the product scope, corresponding to the `code` field on `shopping_mall_product_skus`. Identifies which SKU this option value assignment belongs to.

productOptionTypeCode.description: Business-visible code of the product option type (for example, `COLOR` or `SIZE`) that this value belongs to. Mirrors the `code` field on `shopping_mall_product_option_types` when such a field exists.

productOptionValueCode.description: Business-visible code of the product option value (for example, `RED`, `M`) associated with this assignment. Mirrors the `code` field on `shopping_mall_product_option_values` when such a field exists.

oneOf.description: Optional ordering index for this assignment relative to other option value assignments of the same SKU. Used by clients to consistently order displayed option values.

orderIndex.description: Optional ordering index for this assignment relative to other option value assignments of the same SKU. Used by clients to consistently order displayed option values.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this SKU option value assignment was created. Maps to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` when present.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this SKU option value assignment was last updated. Maps to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` when present.

IShoppingMallSkuOptionValueAssignment.IC.description:
Request body shape for creating a new SKU option value assignment that connects a specific SKU to a concrete product option value in the shoppingMall catalog.

This DTO is used by seller-facing catalog management APIs when attaching an existing product option value (for example, Color: Red, Size: M) to a SKU identified in the path by its business `skuCode` under a product identified by `productCode`. It maps to the `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` Prisma model while only exposing client-controllable fields.

The owning product and SKU are derived from the path parameters (`productCode` and `skuCode`) and from authorization context, so their identifiers are intentionally omitted from this request body. System-managed fields such as `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are also excluded and will be set by the backend.

productOptionTypeCode.description: Business-visible code of the product option type (for example, `COLOR` or `SIZE`) under which the target product option value is defined. Must resolve to a valid option type for the product indicated by the path parameter `productCode`.

productOptionValueCode.description: Business-visible code of the product option value (for example, `RED`, `M`) to assign to the SKU identified by the path parameter `skuCode`. Must belong to the option type identified by `productOptionTypeCode` and to the same product as specified in the path.

oneOf.description: Optional ordering index for this assignment relative to other option value assignments of the same SKU. When omitted, the backend may derive a default ordering based on existing assignments.

orderIndex.description: Optional ordering index for this assignment relative to other option value assignments of the same SKU. When omitted, the backend may derive a default ordering based on existing assignments.

IShoppingMallSkuOptionValueAssignment.IU.description:
DTO for updating an existing SKU option value assignment that connects a product SKU to a specific option value.

This update type allows modification of mutable business fields of shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments while keeping system-managed and ownership fields controlled by the backend. It is used by sellers operating on a specific product and SKU context identified by path parameters, so the DTO does not include product or SKU identifiers.

product_option_value_id.description:
Identifier of the new product option value to be associated with this assignment.

This must reference a record in shopping_mall_product_option_values that belongs to the same product as the parent SKU and is not soft-deleted (its deleted_at field must be null). The backend will enforce that the (shopping_mall_product_sku_id, shopping_mall_product_option_value_id) pair remains unique.

IShoppingMallProductVisibilityRule.IRequ.description:
Search and filter DTO for listing product visibility rules of a specific product.

This request type is used as the body of PATCH /shoppingMall/*/products/{productCode}/visibilityRules operations. It provides structured filters and pagination options for querying records in shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules that belong to the product identified by the path parameter productCode. Path-level product identification is not duplicated here.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

The first page is usually 1. The backend may enforce a minimum of 1 and apply a sensible default when omitted.

limit.description:
Maximum number of visibility rule records to return per page.

The backend will typically enforce an upper bound to protect performance, and may apply a default when omitted.

region_code.description:
Optional filter restricting results to rules targeting a specific region.

The value should correspond to a region identifier or code defined in shopping_mall_region_settings, depending on how regions are modeled in the schema.

channel_code.description:
Optional filter restricting visibility rules to a specific sales or exposure channel.

The exact semantics depend on how channels are modeled in shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules, such as web, mobile, marketplace, or other custom channels.

is_active.description:
Optional tri-state filter indicating whether to restrict results to rules that are currently active.

When true, only active rules are returned. When false, only inactive rules are returned. When null or omitted, the filter is not applied.

starts_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the effective start date/time of visibility rules.

Rules whose effective period begins on or after this value should match. Use ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z).

starts_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the effective start date/time of visibility rules.

Rules whose effective period begins on or before this value should match. Use ISO 8601 date-time format.

expires_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the effective end date/time of visibility rules.

Rules whose effective period ends on or after this value should match. Use ISO 8601 date-time format.

expires_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the effective end date/time of visibility rules.

Rules whose effective period ends on or before this value should match. Use ISO 8601 date-time format.

order_by.description:
Field name to sort the visibility rules by.

Typical values might include created_at, updated_at, starts_at, or expires_at depending on the Prisma model definition. The backend should validate allowed fields.

order_direction.description:
Direction for sorting results.

Common values are asc for ascending or desc for descending. The backend should validate the value against supported options.

IShoppingMallProductVisibilityRule.description:
Product visibility rule entity for the shoppingMall catalog.

Represents a single configuration rule that controls where and to whom a product is visible in the catalog. Each rule is attached to exactly one product and may optionally scope visibility to a specific region setting and/or sales channel, and to a time window. The rule is primarily used by back-office and platform administrator tools to manage catalog exposure across markets and channels.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product visibility rule record.

Directly corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules.id` and is used as the primary key when addressing a specific rule from administrative tools and internal services.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that owns this visibility rule.

Maps to `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules.shopping_mall_product_id` and links to `shopping_mall_products.id`. This field ensures that each rule is evaluated only in the context of its owning product and is used by the service layer to verify product–rule relationships for security and data integrity.

shopping_mall_region_setting_id.description:
Optional reference to a region configuration that scopes where this visibility rule applies.

When non-null, the value is the primary key of a record in `shopping_mall_region_settings`, indicating that the rule is effective only within that specific region or market. When null, the rule is considered global with respect to region unless additional higher-level constraints are applied by the service layer.

region.description:
Resolved region configuration context for this visibility rule.

When non-null, this object is a lightweight summary of the `shopping_mall_region_settings` record referenced by `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` and describes the market or geographic region where the rule is effective. When null, the rule is considered region-agnostic and either applies globally or is further constrained by other configuration layers.

Clients can use this summary directly for administrative UIs without issuing an additional API call to load the full region configuration.

channel.description:
Optional sales channel identifier for which this rule applies.

Typical values include logical channel keys such as `"web"`, `"mobile"`, or identifiers used for marketplace feeds and partner integrations. When null, the rule is interpreted as channel-agnostic for the given product and region, allowing it to affect all channels unless additional business logic narrows the scope.

visibility.description:
Visibility state that this rule enforces for the product in the given region and channel context.

Business logic typically constrains this value to a small set of states such as `"visible"`, `"hidden"`, or `"restricted"`, though the exact allowed set is enforced at the service or database constraint level. The evaluation engine combines this state with product lifecycle status and compliance flags to determine final catalog exposure.

starts_at.description:
Optional start timestamp from which this rule becomes effective.

When non-null, this ISO 8601 date-time value indicates the earliest instant at which the rule should be considered during visibility evaluation. When null, the rule is treated as effective immediately from its creation or activation time. Implementations should ensure that, when both `starts_at` and `ends_at` are provided, `starts_at` is chronologically earlier than `ends_at`.

ends_at.description:
Optional end timestamp after which this rule is no longer effective.

When non-null, this ISO 8601 date-time value marks the moment after which the rule must be ignored by visibility evaluation logic. When null, the rule has no scheduled end and remains in effect until explicitly modified or deleted. Service implementations are responsible for enforcing any required ordering between `starts_at` and `ends_at`.

created_at.description:
Timestamp recording when this visibility rule was created.

This value mirrors the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules.created_at` column and is managed entirely by the persistence layer. It is exposed for audit, debugging, and administrative reporting, and should never be set or overridden by API consumers.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this visibility rule.

Mapped from `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules.updated_at`, this field is maintained by the database or application layer on every modification. It is useful for cache invalidation, synchronization, and audit trails, and is not writable by clients through the public API.

IShoppingMallProductVisibilityRule.ICrea.description:
DTO for creating a new product visibility rule for a catalog product.

Used as the request body of `POST /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/products/{productCode}/visibilityRules`. The product is identified by its business-visible code in the URL path, so this DTO does not contain any product identifier field. It captures region, channel, visibility, and effective period settings for the new rule.

All actor identity and audit fields (such as creator identifiers, session context, or timestamps) are supplied by backend infrastructure and must not be provided by clients.

shopping_mall_region_setting_id.description:
Optional region setting identifier that scopes the new rule to a specific region or market.

When supplied, the value must be a valid UUID corresponding to `shopping_mall_region_settings.id`. When `null` or omitted, the rule is interpreted as region-agnostic, allowing it to apply globally across regions subject to higher-level configuration or policy.

channel.description:
Optional sales channel key for which this rule applies.

Typical values include identifiers such as `"web"`, `"mobile"`, or internal channel codes used by the shoppingMall platform. When `null` or omitted, the rule is considered channel-agnostic for the associated product and region, applying across all channels unless restricted by additional logic.

visibility.description:
Visibility state to apply for the new rule in the product/region/channel context.

This value is persisted to `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules.visibility` and must conform to the set of states allowed by business and database constraints (for example, `"visible"`, `"hidden"`, or `"restricted"`). The combination of this state with product lifecycle and compliance flags determines whether and how the product is exposed to end users.

starts_at.description:
Optional start timestamp at which this visibility rule becomes effective.

When provided, this field must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string and represent the earliest moment when the rule should be considered during visibility evaluation. When `null` or omitted, the rule is treated as effective immediately upon creation. If both `starts_at` and `ends_at` are non-null, service logic should enforce that `starts_at` precedes `ends_at`.

ends_at.description:
Optional end timestamp after which this visibility rule should no longer be considered effective.

When provided, this field must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string and represent the point in time after which the rule is ignored by visibility logic. When `null` or omitted, the rule remains effective indefinitely until disabled or deleted. Implementations should validate that any non-null `ends_at` is later than a non-null `starts_at`.

IShoppingMallProductVisibilityRule.IUpda.description:
Update DTO for product visibility rules stored in the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` table.

Used as the request body of `PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/products/{productCode}/visibilityRules/{productVisibilityRuleId}`. This type exposes only columns that actually belong to the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` Prisma model and are conceptually mutable: region scope, channel, visibility, and effective period timestamps.

All fields are optional so that callers may perform partial updates. Server-side logic is responsible for ignoring undefined fields, applying nulls where appropriate, and enforcing any business rules such as valid visibility states and coherent time windows.

shopping_mall_region_setting_id.description:
Optional new region setting identifier for this visibility rule.

When supplied as a non-null UUID, the value must match an existing record in `shopping_mall_region_settings.id`, effectively scoping the rule to that region. When explicitly set to `null`, the region scope is cleared so that the rule becomes region-agnostic. If omitted, the existing region association remains unchanged.

channel.description:
Optional update to the sales channel key for which this rule applies.

Providing a non-null string replaces the existing channel with the specified identifier (for example `"web"` or `"mobile"`). Explicitly providing `null` clears the channel, making the rule channel-agnostic. When the field is omitted, the current channel value is preserved.

visibility.description:
Optional update to the visibility state enforced by this rule.

A non-null string value updates `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules.visibility` and must conform to the allowed visibility state set (for example `"visible"`, `"hidden"`, or `"restricted"`). Providing `null` may be interpreted by business logic as clearing or resetting visibility, depending on domain rules. When omitted, the existing visibility state is not changed.

starts_at.description:
Optional update to the start timestamp from which this rule becomes effective.

A non-null ISO 8601 date-time string replaces the existing `starts_at` value. Setting this field explicitly to `null` removes any scheduled start, causing the rule to be treated as effective immediately (subject to other conditions). When omitted, the existing start timestamp is left unchanged. Implementations must ensure that any non-null `starts_at` remains chronologically before a non-null `ends_at`.

ends_at.description:
Optional update to the end timestamp after which this rule is no longer effective.

A non-null ISO 8601 date-time string replaces the existing `ends_at` value. Setting this field explicitly to `null` removes the scheduled end, allowing the rule to remain effective indefinitely until further changes. When omitted, the current end timestamp is preserved. The service must validate that `ends_at`, if non-null, is later than any non-null `starts_at` value.

IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag.IRequ.description:
Search and filter request DTO for listing compliance flags associated with a specific product in the shoppingMall catalog.

This type is used by administrative tools to retrieve a paginated list of `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags` linked to a product resolved from `productCode`. It supports filtering by flag type, blocking behavior, creation date range, and standard pagination and sorting parameters.

The DTO does not include any identity or ownership fields; these are resolved from the path and authentication context. It is read-only and has no direct mapping to a single Prisma model row.

page.description:
Page index for pagination when listing compliance flags.

Typically 1-based, where `1` represents the first page of results. When omitted, the backend should fall back to a sensible default (for example, page 1).

limit.description:
Maximum number of compliance flag records to return in a single page.

Used together with `page` to control pagination. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses.

flag_type.description:
Optional filter for a specific compliance flag type.

Examples include `"age_restriction"`, `"hazardous_material"`, `"region_restricted"`, or other policy or regulatory categories defined by the business. When `null` or omitted, flags of all types are included.

is_blocking_sale.description:
Optional filter controlling whether only flags that block sale should be returned.

When `true`, only flags with `is_blocking_sale = true` are returned. When `false`, only non-blocking flags are returned. When `null` or omitted, both blocking and non-blocking flags are included.

created_from.description:
Optional lower bound for the creation timestamp of compliance flags to include in the result.

When provided, only flags with `created_at` greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are considered. When `null` or omitted, no lower time bound is applied.

created_to.description:
Optional upper bound for the creation timestamp of compliance flags to include in the result.

When provided, only flags with `created_at` less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are considered. When `null` or omitted, no upper time bound is applied.

order_by.description:
Optional field name used to sort the list of compliance flags.

Typical values include `"created_at"`, `"flag_type"`, or `"is_blocking_sale"`. When omitted or `null`, the backend uses its default ordering, which commonly is by creation time descending.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction for the `order_by` field.

Allowed values are `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. When omitted or `null`, the backend chooses a sensible default (often `"desc"` for time-based fields).

IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag.description:
Compliance and restriction metadata applied to a single catalog product within the shopping mall platform.

Represents a single compliance flag record stored in the Prisma model shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags. Each flag is attached to exactly one product and may optionally reference an age restriction policy. Flags indicate regulatory or policy constraints (for example age restrictions, hazardous material indicators, or region-based restrictions) and can optionally block sales when certain conditions are met.

This DTO is used as the detailed response body for operations that retrieve or mutate a specific product compliance flag. It exposes only business-relevant, non-sensitive fields and mirrors the underlying database columns without introducing phantom properties.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product compliance flag record.

This value maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.id and is generated by the system when the flag is created. Clients receive it in responses and use it in path parameters when addressing a specific compliance flag, but must never attempt to supply or modify it in create or update requests.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product to which this compliance flag is attached.

This value maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.shopping_mall_product_id and references shopping_mall_products.id. It is managed internally by the backend based on the product resolved from productCode in the request path and is not provided directly by API consumers.

shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id.description:
Optional identifier of the age restriction policy associated with this compliance flag.

This field maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id and, when present, references a row in shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies. It is null when no dedicated age restriction policy is linked.

flag_type.description:
Type of compliance flag applied to the product.

Maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.flag_type. Typical values include markers such as "age_restriction", "hazardous_material", or "region_restricted", but the exact set of values is governed by business rules and database constraints. Together with shopping_mall_product_id this field participates in a composite unique index, ensuring that a given product can have at most one compliance flag of each type.

flag_value.description:
Optional value providing more detailed regulatory or policy information for this flag.

Maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.flag_value. This may contain external regulation codes, internal policy identifiers, or additional structured tags encoded as strings. It is null when no extra value is required for the flag type.

is_blocking_sale.description:
Indicates whether this compliance flag can block sale of the associated product under configured conditions.

Maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.is_blocking_sale. When true, the product may be hidden from the catalog, excluded from checkout, or require additional verification steps before purchase. When false, the flag is informational or affects only limited aspects of the buying experience.

notes.description:
Optional internal notes providing additional context about why this compliance flag exists or how it should be interpreted.

Maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.notes. This is typically used by platform administrators or compliance officers to store free-form explanations, links to regulatory documents, or audit comments. It is not intended for display to end customers.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this compliance flag record was first created.

Maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.created_at. The value is generated and managed by the system and is useful for auditing and historical analysis.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the most recent time this compliance flag record was updated.

Maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.updated_at. This value is automatically updated by the system whenever mutable fields on the compliance flag change.

IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag.ICrea.description:
Request payload for creating a new compliance flag associated with an existing catalog product.

This DTO is used as the request body for POST operations that insert rows into the shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags Prisma model. The target product is identified externally by its business-visible code (shopping_mall_products.code) in the request path, so no product identifier fields appear in this body. Actor identity is derived from the authenticated platform administrator context and is never supplied by the client.

Clients provide the flag type, optional flag value, whether the flag can block sale, and optional notes and age restriction policy linkage. The backend enforces the composite uniqueness constraint on (shopping_mall_product_id, flag_type), resolves and sets foreign keys, and populates system-managed fields such as id and timestamps.

shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id.description:
Optional identifier of the age restriction policy to associate with this new compliance flag.

Maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id. When supplied, it must reference a valid row in shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies. When omitted or explicitly set to null, the compliance flag is created without a dedicated age restriction policy link.

flag_type.description:
Type of compliance flag to create for the target product.

This value is written to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.flag_type. Typical examples include values such as "age_restriction", "hazardous_material", or "region_restricted". The combination of the resolved product and flag_type must be unique across shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags due to a composite unique index on [shopping_mall_product_id, flag_type].

flag_value.description:
Optional compliance flag value providing more detailed regulatory or policy information.

Maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.flag_value. This field can carry external regulation codes, internal policy identifiers, or other flag-specific annotations required by business rules. Supply null or omit this property when no additional value is necessary for the chosen flag_type.

is_blocking_sale.description:
Whether this compliance flag should be treated as potentially blocking sales of the associated product under configured conditions.

This value populates shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.is_blocking_sale. When true, the platform may prevent listing or checkout of the product until specific criteria are satisfied. When false, the flag is informational or used only for limited visibility adjustments.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes explaining the purpose or context of the compliance flag being created.

Maps to shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.notes. Intended for internal administrative use, for example to reference legal justifications, tickets, or operational decisions. This text is not designed for customer-facing presentation.

IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag.IUpda.description:
DTO for updating an existing compliance flag record attached to a catalog product in shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.

Used by platform administrators to modify mutable compliance attributes such as flag type, value, blocking behavior, notes, and associated policy references while preserving immutable identifiers and creation metadata.

This DTO is consumed by the PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/products/{productCode}/complianceFlags/{productComplianceFlagId} operation, where the product and flag identity come from the path parameters, not from this body.

flag_type.description:
Type of compliance flag applied to the product.

Typically represents a semantic category such as "age_restriction", "hazardous_material", "region_restriction", or other policy-driven markers. When updated, the new value must not violate the unique constraint on (shopping_mall_product_id, flag_type) within the underlying Prisma model.

flag_value.description:
Value or payload associated with the compliance flag type.

Examples include specific age thresholds (for example, "18+"), region codes, hazard classifications, or other policy-dependent markers. Interpretation is determined by the active policy configuration for this flag type.

When provided as a non-empty string, it refines or qualifies the meaning of flag_type. When explicitly set to null, any previously stored value is cleared so that the flag no longer carries an additional code or annotation beyond its type.

is_blocking_sale.description:
Indicates whether this compliance flag should block sales for the associated product when the flag condition is not satisfied.

When true, checkout and order placement flows must enforce this flag to prevent purchase for the affected audiences or regions. When false, the flag is informational or used only for visibility and messaging adjustments.

notes.description:
Free-form human-readable notes explaining why this compliance flag exists or how it should be interpreted.

Typically used by platform administrators or compliance officers to document decisions, investigation results, or regulatory references. Nullable to allow clearing previously stored notes when set to null in an update request.

shopping_mall_age_restriction_policy_id.description:
Optional reference to an age restriction policy row that governs this compliance flag.

When present, it links to the shopping_mall_age_restriction_policies table and indicates that the product’s availability is constrained by that policy. When set to null in an update request, any previously linked age restriction policy is detached from this compliance flag.

IShoppingMallCatalogSearch.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for performing an advanced, multi-dimensional catalog search over shoppingMall products.

This structure captures free-text keywords, filter constraints, and pagination/sorting instructions used by the /shoppingMall/catalog/search endpoint to build SQL queries over products, SKUs, categories, brands, visibility configuration, and compliance metadata.

It is designed to power search boxes, category pages, and complex filter panels while keeping the wire format explicit and cache-friendly.

keyword.description:
Free-text search keyword used to match products by name, description, brand, or other indexed text fields.

When null, the search behaves like a pure filter-based catalog browse without keyword matching.

category_codes.description:
Optional list of category codes restricting results to products that are assigned to at least one of the specified categories.

Codes typically correspond to shopping_mall_categories.code values. When null, no explicit category filter is applied.

brand_ids.description:
Optional list of brand identifiers limiting results to products associated with one of the given brands.

Each value usually corresponds to shopping_mall_brands.id. When null, brand is not used as a filtering dimension.

min_price.description:
Lower bound for product pricing in the search results.

Represents the minimum allowed effective price (for example, across SKUs) for a product to be included in the result set. Nullable to omit a lower price constraint, in which case only other filters determine the minimum price boundary.

max_price.description:
Upper bound for product pricing in the search results.

Represents the maximum allowed effective price for a product to be included in the result set. Nullable to omit an upper price constraint so that high-priced products are only excluded by other filters.

in_stock_only.description:
When true, limits results to products that have at least one SKU currently available in inventory.

When false or null, out-of-stock products may still appear depending on other visibility rules and business decisions (for example, allowing backorderable items to remain visible).

region_code.description:
Region or market code representing the shopper’s context.

Used to enforce region-specific visibility, shipping availability, and compliance restrictions (for example, hiding products not allowed in a specific country or jurisdiction). Nullable to use platform default behavior derived from the request context.

sort_by.description:
Sort key applied to the search results.

Typical values include semantic options such as "relevance", "createdAt", "priceAsc", "priceDesc", or "ratingDesc". When null, the backend applies its default relevance-based ordering appropriate for the given query and storefront.

page.description:
1-based page index indicating which page of search results to return.

A value of 1 refers to the first page. Values less than 1 are rejected by validation. If the requested page is greater than the total number of available pages for the current criteria, the backend typically returns an empty `data` array while preserving accurate pagination metadata so clients can gracefully handle the end of the result set.

limit.description:
Maximum number of search result items to return in a single page.

Must be a positive integer. The backend may enforce a sensible upper bound (for example, a few hundred items) and clamp excessively large client-provided values down to that maximum to protect performance. Clients should choose limits that balance UX needs (fewer page transitions) with response size and latency considerations.

IShoppingMallCatalogStatistics.IBrandPro.description:
List of brand-level catalog statistics for the shoppingMall platform.
