Each array element represents a single brand and its aggregated count of active or otherwise countable products in the catalog. This DTO is designed for administrative dashboards and analytical views, not for end-customer product browsing.

Aggregated catalog statistics for a single brand within the shoppingMall platform.

Represents one row in the brand-level product count analytics, combining brand identification metadata with an aggregated count of products that are considered active or otherwise countable according to business rules. Used primarily in platform administrator dashboards and catalog operations tooling, not in customer-facing product listings.

brandId.description:
Unique identifier of the brand as stored in the shopping_mall_brands Prisma model.

This will typically correspond to the primary key of the brand entity (for example, a UUID string). It can be used by admin tools to navigate to brand detail pages or to join with richer brand metadata in other API responses or internal services.

brandCode.description:
Human-readable or system-wide unique code for the brand, if such a code exists in the shopping_mall_brands schema.

This field allows dashboards and reporting tools to reference brands using a stable code value instead of or in addition to the opaque brandId. If the underlying schema does not define a brand code, this property may be left empty or omitted at implementation time.

brandName.description:
Display name of the brand as visible to administrators.

This is typically the official brand name that appears in catalog management UIs and dashboards, making the analytics output easier to understand without requiring a separate lookup by brandId.

productCount.description:
Number of catalog products associated with this brand that qualify as "active" or otherwise countable according to platform business rules.

The aggregation should respect any visibility, status, or compliance filters defined in the shopping_mall_products schema (for example, excluding draft, archived, or fully hidden products).

IShoppingMallCatalogStatistics.IProductS.description:
Aggregated distribution of catalog products by status for the shoppingMall platform.

Provides a compact, read-only summary of how many products currently exist in each lifecycle or publication status bucket, such as draft, active, or archived. This DTO is intended for administrative dashboards and operational monitoring screens rather than customer-facing product search.

buckets.description:
List of status-level product count buckets across the entire catalog.

Each element represents a single product status value and the number of products that currently have that status in the shopping_mall_products table. The list can be used to render charts, KPIs, and workflow distribution visualizations.

totalCount.description:
Total number of products represented across all status buckets.

This is typically the sum of productCount values from all buckets. It is included to simplify dashboard implementations and to provide a single reference number for overall catalog size.

IShoppingMallCatalogStatistics.IProductS.description:
Single status-level bucket in the product status distribution summary.

Represents one status category and the corresponding count of products in the shopping_mall_products table that currently have that status. This DTO is used inside the IShoppingMallCatalogStatistics.IProductStatusSummary.buckets array.

status.description:
Logical product status label for this bucket.

Typical examples might include values such as "draft", "pendingReview", "active", "suspended", or "archived", depending on how the shopping_mall_products Prisma model encodes product lifecycle state. Implementations should map raw database status fields into stable, documented labels suitable for API consumers.

productCount.description:
Number of products whose status falls into this bucket.

The count is computed by grouping rows in the shopping_mall_products table by their status field and counting how many belong to each group. It must be a non-negative integer.

IShoppingMallGuestCart.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new guest shopping cart for an unauthenticated visitor.

Represents the minimal set of business fields required to insert a new row into the shopping_mall_guest_carts table for a guest user. System-managed fields such as identifiers and timestamps are excluded from this DTO. This DTO may carry optional metadata used to bind the cart to a client context (such as a guest identity token or region code) but does not itself contain any line items; items are added or synchronized through dedicated item or update operations.

guest_token.description:
Opaque client-generated token or browser identifier used to associate this guest cart with a specific anonymous visitor session.

This value typically originates from a cookie, local storage, or device identifier and allows the platform to relate subsequent cart operations to the same guest, even without authentication.

ip.description:
IP address captured when the guest cart is created or when a significant modification occurs, such as adding or removing items.

The value is used for security analysis, fraud detection, and geo-based business rules, and may also support compliance or audit requirements when investigating suspicious cart activity.

user_agent.description:
User agent string captured from the client when the guest cart is created or updated.

Implementations may store the full value or a truncated representation depending on storage and privacy constraints. This field is primarily used for analytics, device profiling, and troubleshooting guest cart behavior across different browsers and platforms.

referrer.description:
Initial referrer URL observed when the guest cart was first created, if available.

This URL helps describe where the guest originated from within or outside the platform and is useful for acquisition, funnel, and campaign analysis. When not available or intentionally omitted for privacy reasons, this field can be left unset.

region_code.description:
Business region or market code for this guest cart, such as a country, marketplace identifier, or internal region key.

This value is used by pricing, tax, catalog visibility, and shipping logic to determine which business rules apply to the cart contents and the customer journey, and may be inferred from IP, customer preferences, or explicit UI selection.

IShoppingMallGuestCart.description:
Full guest shopping cart representation as stored and returned from the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` table.

This DTO exposes the primary identifier, anonymous-session linkage, network and browser context, and lifecycle timestamps for a temporary cart owned by an unauthenticated visitor. It is the canonical read model used by guest-cart operations to render and synchronize the current server-side cart state.

In addition to scalar fields mapped directly from the Prisma model, the DTO includes a compositional `items` collection that aggregates the current line items stored in `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` for this cart, allowing clients to load a complete guest cart in a single response.

id.description:
Primary key of the guest cart in the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` table.

This UUID uniquely identifies a transient cart instance for an anonymous visitor and is required for all subsequent guest-cart operations such as retrieval, update, merge into a customer cart, or deletion.

guest_token.description:
Opaque token that identifies the anonymous visitor session associated with this guest cart.

Typically this matches a browser cookie or device-specific identifier and is used by the platform to restore the correct cart for a given unauthenticated session, even if the visitor has not created a full customer account.

ip.description:
IP address recorded for the guest at the time the cart was created or last significantly modified.

This value is captured from the incoming request and is used for security analysis, fraud detection, and geo-based business rules. It is optional and may be absent if the IP address cannot be reliably determined or stored.

user_agent.description:
User agent string associated with the client that created or last updated this guest cart.

The value usually corresponds to the HTTP `User-Agent` header and is stored for analytics, troubleshooting, and device classification purposes. It is not guaranteed to be present or well formed.

referrer.description:
Initial referrer URL observed when this guest cart was created, if available.

This URL helps the business understand acquisition channels and funnel behavior (for example, which campaign or landing page led to cart creation). It may be omitted when no reliable referrer information is available.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this guest cart record was created in the database.

The value is stored in UTC using an ISO 8601 date-time representation and is managed exclusively by the persistence layer. It does not change after initial insertion.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this guest cart was last updated in the database.

This value is refreshed whenever a material change occurs (for example, items are added or removed). It is stored in UTC using an ISO 8601 date-time representation and can be used for TTL or expiration logic on guest carts.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the guest cart.

When this field is set, the cart is considered logically removed or expired but may still be retained for audit, analytics, or debugging purposes. Active carts should have this field unset (null in the underlying Prisma model).

items.description:
Collection of line items that currently belong to this guest cart.

Each element corresponds to a record in the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table linked to this cart. This compositional relationship allows clients to render a complete guest cart—including all SKU selections and quantities—from a single API response.
Single guest cart line item belonging to this cart, mapped from a `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` row and enriched for API responses.

IShoppingMallGuestCartItem.description:
Guest cart line item entity for unauthenticated visitors, mapped to the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table.

Each instance represents a single SKU selection and quantity that a guest intends to purchase. The record maintains foreign keys to the owning guest cart and the underlying catalog product and SKU, along with quantity and lifecycle timestamps. It forms part of the guest cart aggregate and is not used independently of its parent cart.

This DTO is returned by guest-cart item operations as the canonical read model for individual line items, allowing clients to display and reconcile cart contents with the catalog.

id.description:
Primary key of the guest cart item in the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table.

This identifier uniquely distinguishes a specific SKU entry within a guest cart and is used by item-level operations such as retrieval, update, or deletion.

guest_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the owning guest cart in the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` table.

This foreign key links the line item back to its parent cart and is used by the backend to scope operations and enforce that items cannot be moved between unrelated carts without explicit business logic.

product_id.description:
Identifier of the base catalog product in the `shopping_mall_products` table that this cart item belongs to.

This value allows clients and backend services to correlate the cart item with the broader product entity for purposes such as displaying product information, enforcing product-level policies, or aggregating analytics.

product_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the specific SKU variant in the `shopping_mall_product_skus` table that the guest selected.

This internal UUID corresponds to the concrete sellable variant (for example, size and color). While some request DTOs use a more user-facing `sku_id` value, this field always exposes the canonical database identifier used for inventory, pricing, and fulfillment logic.

quantity.description:
Requested quantity of the selected SKU in the guest cart.

The value must be a positive integer and is validated against inventory limits, per-order restrictions, and other business rules. Increasing or decreasing this value may adjust temporary inventory reservations or affect downstream pricing calculations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this cart item record was created in the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table.

The value is stored in UTC using an ISO 8601 date-time representation and allows systems to understand when the guest first added the item to their cart.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this cart item was last updated.

This field is refreshed whenever the item changes in a material way, such as when its quantity is modified. It is stored in UTC using an ISO 8601 date-time representation and can be used for expiration and audit purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the guest cart item.

When populated, this field indicates that the item has been logically removed from the cart (for example, the guest deleted the item or the cart was cleared), but the record may still be retained for audit or analytics. Active items will have this field unset (null in the underlying Prisma model).

IShoppingMallGuestCart.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for replacing the full state of a guest shopping cart that is stored in the `shopping_mall_guest_carts` table.

This DTO is used with `PUT /shoppingMall/guestCarts/{guestCartId}` and represents an atomic, full-replacement update of the cart aggregate. The cart itself is identified exclusively by the `guestCartId` path parameter, so **no cart-level identifiers or foreign keys** (such as `id` or `shopping_mall_guest_cart_id`) appear in this request body. All such identifiers are resolved on the server side from the path parameter and internal context.

The `items` collection models a **strong composition** of guest cart items owned by the cart. When this DTO is processed, the backend loads the existing `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` rows for the target cart and reconciles them against the provided `items` array in a single transaction: items for SKUs not present in the request are removed, existing items are updated to the requested quantities, and new rows are created for newly referenced SKUs. This ensures the cart and its line items are updated atomically as a single aggregate.

The shape of this DTO is intentionally minimal and focused on client-controlled fields: currency and client metadata at the cart level, plus the compositional list of desired line items. Database identifiers, audit fields, and path-derived identifiers are intentionally excluded to avoid duplication and to keep ownership boundaries clear.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code that should be used to price and summarize this guest cart.

This value must correspond to a supported currency in the shoppingMall configuration. It is optional on update; if omitted, the existing `currency_code` value stored on the cart remains unchanged.

client_metadata.description:
Client-side metadata associated with the guest cart, such as device or user agent hints.

This object is treated as compositional metadata of the cart aggregate and is modeled as a separate structured type to avoid inline object definitions. It is persisted either in a JSON column or decomposed into separate fields, depending on implementation, and is never managed as an independent entity.

items.description:
Complete replacement list of desired guest cart items that belong to this cart.

This array defines the target state of the cart's composed line items. For the cart identified by the `guestCartId` path parameter, existing rows in `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` are reconciled against this list: items whose SKUs are omitted are deleted, items with matching SKUs are updated (for example, quantity changes), and items referencing new SKUs are inserted as new rows. This ensures the cart-to-items relationship is handled as a strong composition in a single atomic update.

IShoppingMallGuestCartClientMetadata.IUp.description:
Client-side metadata structure for a guest cart update.

This type represents optional contextual information about the anonymous visitor's environment (for example, browser or device characteristics) that can be attached to a guest cart for analytics, risk evaluation, or UX optimization.

`IShoppingMallGuestCartClientMetadata.IUpdate` is a pure value object: it is **not** directly mapped to a dedicated Prisma model and is typically stored either in a JSON column on `shopping_mall_guest_carts` or decomposed into separate primitive fields. It is fully owned by the cart aggregate and is not managed as an independent associated entity.

user_agent.description:
Raw `User-Agent` header string observed for the browser or client making the request when the cart was last updated.

This value helps with debugging, analytics, and device classification, but does not participate in any relational mappings.

device_type.description:
High-level classification of the client device, such as `"desktop"`, `"mobile"`, or `"tablet"`.

This string is used only for analytics and UX optimization and is stored as part of the cart’s compositional metadata rather than as a separate entity relation.

locale.description:
BCP 47 language tag that indicates the preferred locale of the guest, for example `"en-US"` or `"ko-KR"`.

This locale can influence localized messaging, pricing presentation, and other region- or language-sensitive behaviors, and is treated as part of the cart aggregate’s metadata.

IShoppingMallGuestCartItemForCart.IUpdat.description:
Guest cart item payload used inside IShoppingMallGuestCart.IUpdate to describe the desired state of each line item in the cart.

This DTO is focused strictly on SKU selection and target quantity. The owning cart identity and all system-managed fields, such as timestamps and internal identifiers, are derived from the surrounding cart context and are not accepted from the client.

It is typically used when the client sends a full cart update, allowing the backend to reconcile the requested SKU and quantity set with the existing guest cart items.

sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU that this cart line item refers to.

The backend resolves this to the corresponding `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` in the database. The client must not provide any internal database identifiers, only this external SKU identifier.

quantity.description:
Desired quantity of this SKU in the guest cart after the update operation completes.

This must be a positive integer and is subject to stock constraints, per-order limits, and other business rules. It does not allow the client to alter any system-managed audit or pricing fields.

IShoppingMallGuestCartItem.ICreate.description:
Creation payload for a new guest cart line item in shopping_mall_guest_cart_items under an existing guest cart referenced by guestCartId in the request path. This DTO is used with POST /shoppingMall/guestCarts/{guestCartId}/items.

The owning guest cart is selected exclusively via the `guestCartId` path parameter. The client must not attempt to send any cart identifier or system-managed fields in the body; those are derived and managed on the server side.

The DTO focuses on selecting a SKU and the desired quantity. Pricing and other server-managed attributes (such as price snapshots and timestamps) are computed and stored by the backend based on catalog and pricing rules.

sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU to add to the guest cart.

This value is a client-facing identifier that the backend maps to the underlying `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` column in the `shopping_mall_product_skus` table.

The value must reference an existing SKU that is visible and eligible for sale according to catalog, region, and age restriction policies.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the specified SKU to add to the guest cart.

The value must be a positive integer. The backend enforces inventory availability, per-cart limits, and any other business rules that constrain how many units can be added.

This field does not allow manipulation of any system-managed quantities; it only expresses the desired amount for this operation.

IShoppingMallGuestCartItem.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing guest cart line item in `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items`.

Allows modification of mutable fields such as quantity while preventing changes to immutable identifiers and system-managed snapshot metadata. Used as the request body for `PUT /shoppingMall/guestCarts/{guestCartId}/items/{guestCartItemId}`.

quantity.description: New quantity for this cart item. Must be at least 1 and is validated against current inventory and business rules.

IShoppingMallGuestCartMerge.ICreate.description:
Request body for merging a guest cart into an authenticated customer's persistent cart.

Carries the guest cart identifier to be merged and optional merge behavior hints. The identity of the target customer is derived exclusively from the authenticated context (JWT/session) of the caller and is not accepted from the request body.

guest_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the guest cart to be merged, corresponding to the primary key of a record in `shopping_mall_guest_carts`.

The backend uses this value to locate the temporary guest cart and its items before merging them into the authenticated customer's persistent cart.

merge_strategy.description:
Optional hint indicating how to handle duplicate SKUs when both the guest cart and the customer cart contain the same SKU.

Typical strategies include:
- `sum-quantities`: add quantities from guest and customer carts together
- `guest-wins`: prefer quantities from the guest cart
- `customer-wins`: keep existing customer cart quantities and ignore duplicates

If omitted, the service applies the platform's default merge behavior.

IShoppingMallCustomerCart.description:
Persistent shopping cart owned by an authenticated customer.

Represents the server-side cart state stored in `shopping_mall_customer_carts`, including identifying information, ownership via a customer association, active status flags, configuration, and monetary totals. It intentionally does not embed the full list of cart items; items are retrieved atomically via dedicated item listing endpoints that return paginated summaries.

Used as the primary cart representation in customer and admin flows where the caller needs to understand which customer owns the cart, its regional and currency configuration, whether it is currently active, and the current aggregate totals without incurring the cost of loading all items inline.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer cart record in `shopping_mall_customer_carts`.

This value is the primary key of the cart aggregate and is used as `customerCartId` in path parameters for cart- and cart-item–related operations.

customer.description:
Summary information about the customer who owns this cart.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key to expose a richer view of the owning customer (such as display name or account status) while preventing circular references and keeping the cart DTO focused on its aggregate root role.

status.description:
High-level lifecycle status of the cart.

Examples include:
- `active`: cart is in normal use and can be modified
- `abandoned`: cart has not been used for a configured period
- `converted`: cart has been converted into an order and is no longer editable

Exact status values are defined by business rules and may not be exhaustive in this documentation.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this cart is currently considered active for the customer.

When `true`, the cart is treated as part of the customer’s current shopping context and typically appears in default cart listings and summary computations. When `false`, the cart is logically archived or historical, and may be hidden from primary UIs or excluded from certain operations such as checkout.

This property reflects the non-nullable `is_active` column in the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` model and is always present in responses so that clients can reliably distinguish active carts from archived ones.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code representing the pricing currency for this cart (for example, `USD`, `EUR`, `KRW`).

All monetary totals exposed on this DTO, such as `subtotal_amount` or `total_amount`, are expressed in this currency. The value typically corresponds to a configured currency supported by the current region and payment settings.

region_code.description:
Business-specific code representing the region or market configuration applied to this cart.

Typically corresponds to a record in `shopping_mall_region_settings` and influences catalog availability, pricing, taxation, shipping options, and other policy-driven behavior. Examples include simple ISO-like region codes such as `US` or more fine-grained market codes such as `KR-Seoul`.

source_guest_token.description:
Optional token associated with a source guest cart that was merged into this customer cart.

When a guest user’s temporary cart (stored in `shopping_mall_guest_carts`) is merged into a newly authenticated customer’s persistent cart, the original guest cart identifier or tracking token may be persisted here. This allows analytics and support tooling to trace guest-to-customer cart conversions and understand how much revenue originated as guest activity.

If no merge from a guest cart has occurred, this field is typically omitted or left empty.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cart was first created.

Stored in UTC and managed exclusively by the backend. Useful for analytics and for determining whether a cart should be considered abandoned according to business rules, as well as for ordering historical records in administrative UIs.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this cart was last updated.

Updated whenever mutable properties or cart contents change, allowing clients and operators to reason about the freshness of the cart state. This includes changes to configuration attributes, item additions or removals, and status transitions that affect cart behavior.

oneOf.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the customer cart.

When set, this value indicates that the cart has been logically removed or archived in the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` table while still being retained for audit trails, analytics, or forensic analysis. The cart should generally be excluded from normal customer-facing operations once this value is non-null.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the customer cart.

When set, this value indicates that the cart has been logically removed or archived in the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` table while still being retained for audit trails, analytics, or forensic analysis. The cart should generally be excluded from normal customer-facing operations once this value is non-null.

subtotal_amount.description:
Calculated subtotal for all cart items before discounts, taxes, and shipping.

Typically represents the sum of line subtotals for all non-deleted items currently in the cart, expressed in the cart `currency_code`. This value is computed by the backend and allows clients to display consistent pre-discount totals without re-implementing pricing logic.

discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied to this cart from promotions, coupons, or other adjustments.

This may be zero when no active discounts apply. The discount is already reflected in `total_amount` but is exposed separately to support transparent pricing displays, such as showing “You saved X” banners or marketing messages.

tax_amount.description:
Total tax amount calculated for this cart based on applicable tax rules.

The tax calculation considers regional rules, product taxability, and customer-specific factors where applicable. The value is expressed in the cart `currency_code` and is included so that clients can present accurate tax breakdowns without running their own tax engines.

shipping_amount.description:
Total shipping cost amount applied to this cart based on the currently selected shipping option and region.

This value reflects the current shipping selection for the cart and may change if the customer updates their shipping address or delivery method. It is expressed in the cart `currency_code` and participates in the computation of `total_amount`.

total_amount.description:
Final total amount for this cart after applying discounts, taxes, and shipping.

This is the amount the customer is expected to pay if the cart is converted into an order at the current moment, assuming no further changes occur. It is expressed in the cart `currency_code` and represents the authoritative total used for downstream payment authorization and order creation.

IShoppingMallCustomerCartItem.description:
Full representation of a customer cart item stored in the `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items` table.

A customer cart item represents a single line item within a persistent customer cart in the shoppingMall platform. Each record links a specific SKU and its parent catalog product to a parent cart, along with the selected quantity and a snapshot of pricing information and any item-level metadata.

This DTO is returned by cart item read operations such as fetching a single item or returning the created/updated item after mutation. It exposes identifiers, foreign key references to the owning cart, base product, and SKU, a SKU summary association, quantity, pricing snapshot fields, timestamps used for display and troubleshooting, and soft-deletion metadata where applicable. Fields that are managed exclusively by the backend (identifiers, timestamps, and price snapshot values) are read-only from the client's perspective.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this cart item.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items` row and is used to address the item in subsequent update or delete operations. It is generated by the backend when the item is created.

customerCartId.description:
Identifier of the owning customer cart.

This links the cart item to a `shopping_mall_customer_carts` record that represents the persistent cart aggregate for the customer. It is used server-side to enforce ownership and to ensure that cart operations are scoped to the correct cart.

Although this foreign key exists in the database, the corresponding value is generally derived from path parameters and business logic rather than being provided directly by clients in creation or update request bodies.

productId.description:
Identifier of the base catalog product associated with this cart item.

This value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items` table and points to a record in `shopping_mall_products`. It allows back-office tools and analytics to join cart items back to the parent product independently of the specific SKU variant and is particularly useful when aggregating cart activity at the product level.

skuId.description:
Identifier of the SKU associated with this cart item.

This references a `shopping_mall_product_skus` record that defines the specific product variant the customer intends to purchase. The SKU identifier is used to resolve product details, inventory, and related catalog information when rendering cart and checkout views.

sku.description:
Summary information about the SKU associated with this cart item.

This association exposes human-readable SKU and variant information (such as option values) without requiring the client to perform a separate SKU lookup. It is derived from the `skuId` foreign key and uses the `.ISummary` pattern to avoid deep nesting and circular references.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the associated SKU currently in the cart for this line item.

The quantity is always a positive integer. It reflects the most recent state after any create or update operations and is used in conjunction with pricing snapshot fields to compute line subtotals and cart totals.

oneOf.description:
Unit price snapshot for a single unit of the associated SKU at the time this cart item was last updated.

This value is captured from pricing logic when the item is added or modified and may incorporate discounts, promotions, or region-specific price adjustments. It is used together with `quantity` to compute the line subtotal and may differ from the current catalog price if pricing rules have changed since the item was added.

unitPrice.description:
Unit price snapshot for a single unit of the associated SKU at the time this cart item was last updated.

This value is captured from pricing logic when the item is added or modified and may incorporate discounts, promotions, or region-specific price adjustments. It is used together with `quantity` to compute the line subtotal and may differ from the current catalog price if pricing rules have changed since the item was added.

oneOf.description:
Computed subtotal for this cart line based on the snapshot unit price and quantity.

This represents the pre-tax, pre-fee monetary amount for the line item, calculated by the backend from `unitPrice` and `quantity`. It is included to allow clients to render cart summaries without performing their own arithmetic.

lineSubtotal.description:
Computed subtotal for this cart line based on the snapshot unit price and quantity.

This represents the pre-tax, pre-fee monetary amount for the line item, calculated by the backend from `unitPrice` and `quantity`. It is included to allow clients to render cart summaries without performing their own arithmetic.

oneOf.description:
Optional free-form note attached to this cart item.

This mirrors the note entered when the item was created or last updated and may contain gift messages or special handling instructions. It is persisted with the item and surfaced in cart and checkout views.

note.description:
Optional free-form note attached to this cart item.

This mirrors the note entered when the item was created or last updated and may contain gift messages or special handling instructions. It is persisted with the item and surfaced in cart and checkout views.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this cart item was created.

The value is stored in UTC and represents the moment the `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items` row was first inserted. It is managed by the backend and is always present for persisted items, making it useful for debugging, ordering historical cart activity, and analyzing customer behavior over time.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this cart item was last updated.

The value is stored in UTC and is automatically maintained by the backend whenever mutable fields such as quantity or note are changed. It is always present for persisted items and helps clients and operators understand the recency of cart modifications and recalculate UI views accordingly.

oneOf.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this cart item.

When set, this value indicates that the item has been logically removed from the cart while still being retained in the `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items` table for audit and analytics. Soft-deleted items are typically excluded from active cart totals and customer-facing item lists.

deletedAt.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this cart item.

When set, this value indicates that the item has been logically removed from the cart while still being retained in the `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items` table for audit and analytics. Soft-deleted items are typically excluded from active cart totals and customer-facing item lists.

IShoppingMallCustomerCart.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying persistent customer carts in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is used by internal and administrative tools to retrieve a paginated list of carts from the shopping_mall_customer_carts table using a PATCH search endpoint. It encapsulates pagination, sorting, and flexible filters over cart headers (not line items), such as customer identity, lifecycle state, and activity date ranges.

The request focuses on header-level attributes suitable for index views, while detailed cart contents and item-level structures are retrieved via dedicated cart detail and cart item endpoints. All fields are optional so that callers can combine filters as needed for specific operational, analytical, or support use cases.

page.description:
Page number for paginated cart search results.

Pagination is one-based: the first page has value `1`. This field is used together with `limit` to control the window of results returned to the client.

limit.description:
Maximum number of cart records to return in a single page of results.

Used together with `page` for pagination. Reasonable limits should be chosen to balance UI needs against performance and resource usage.

customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer who owns the cart.

Used to restrict search results to carts belonging to a specific customer. This should reference the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer` model.

In administrative tooling, this value is typically supplied explicitly as part of search criteria; it is not automatically derived from the authenticated end-customer session.

customer_email.description:
Email address of the customer who owns the cart.

Allows searching for carts by customer email when the exact customer identifier is not known. This should match the canonical email stored for the associated `shopping_mall_customer` record. Implementations may normalize or lower-case the email address before applying filters.

items.description:
Cart state value indicating the lifecycle position of the cart.

Typical examples include states such as `active`, `abandoned`, or `converted` (when the cart has been turned into an order). Concrete allowed values are enforced in business logic and configuration, rather than at schema level, so that the platform can evolve state codes over time.

states.description:
Optional list of cart lifecycle states to include in the result set.

When provided, only carts whose state is one of the listed values will be returned. When omitted, carts of any state may be included, subject to other filter criteria.

min_item_count.description:
Minimum number of line items that a cart must contain to match the filter.

This filter is useful for focusing analysis or operational attention on more substantial carts, such as those with multiple products or high engagement, while ignoring trivially small carts.

max_item_count.description:
Maximum number of line items that a cart may contain to match the filter.

When combined with `min_item_count`, this defines a range of item counts for candidate carts, enabling targeted searches such as "carts with between 1 and 5 items".

created_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the cart creation timestamp.

Only carts created at or after this date-time are included in the results. The timestamp is expressed in ISO 8601 format and interpreted in UTC by the backend.

created_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the cart creation timestamp.

Only carts created at or before this date-time are included in the results. The timestamp is expressed in ISO 8601 format and interpreted in UTC by the backend.

updated_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the last updated timestamp of the cart.

Use this filter to find carts that have seen activity (such as item modifications or metadata changes) since a certain point in time. The timestamp is expressed in ISO 8601 format and interpreted in UTC.

updated_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the last updated timestamp of the cart.

Use this filter to restrict results to carts that have not been updated since a certain point in time, such as identifying older, potentially abandoned carts. The timestamp is expressed in ISO 8601 format and interpreted in UTC.

sort_by.description:
Field name to use for sorting cart search results.

Typical values include `created_at`, `updated_at`, or an implementation-specific last-activity field. The concrete set of allowed sort fields and their semantics are enforced at the service layer rather than at schema level, allowing the platform to evolve sorting options without changing the DTO contract.

oneOf.description:
Ascending sort order.

When used with `sort_by`, results will be ordered from smallest to largest or from oldest to newest, depending on the chosen field. This value is represented literally as the string `"asc"` in the request payload.

Descending sort order.

When used with `sort_by`, results will be ordered from largest to smallest or from newest to oldest, depending on the chosen field. This value is represented literally as the string `"desc"` in the request payload.

sort_direction.description:
Direction in which to sort search results.

Supported values are:
- `asc`: ascending order
- `desc`: descending order

When omitted, the implementation may default to a descending order, typically based on creation or last-update time, so that the most recent carts appear first.

is_active.description:
Filter flag indicating whether only carts with a particular active state should be returned.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `is_active` column on the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` Prisma model. When set to `true`, the search returns only carts that are currently marked as active. When set to `false`, the search returns only carts that have been explicitly marked as inactive or archived.

If this property is omitted, no filter on `is_active` is applied, and carts of any active state may be included in the results, subject to other criteria such as deletion status and date ranges.

include_deleted.description:
Controls whether carts that have been soft-deleted should be included in the result set.

Soft deletion is represented by the nullable `deleted_at` column on the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` Prisma model. When this flag is set to `true`, the search may include carts where `deleted_at` is non-null, in addition to non-deleted carts, enabling administrators to inspect historical or archived cart records.

When this flag is `false` or omitted, only carts with `deleted_at = null` (that is, carts that have not been soft-deleted) are returned. This default behavior aligns with typical operational and customer-facing views where deleted carts are hidden from normal listing flows.

IShoppingMallCustomerCart.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new persistent customer cart in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is used by authenticated customers (or privileged internal actors on their behalf) to establish a new cart record in the shopping_mall_customer_carts table. It carries configuration attributes such as regional and currency settings, along with lifecycle-related flags that control how the cart is treated immediately after creation.

The DTO deliberately omits ownership and system-managed fields such as customer identifiers, timestamps, and soft-deletion markers. Those values are derived from the authenticated context and backend logic, ensuring that clients can focus on business-level parameters while the platform enforces consistency and integrity rules.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code that determines the monetary context for prices and totals in this cart.

Typical examples include `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`. The value must correspond to a supported currency configured in the platform. If omitted, the backend may infer a sensible default from the customer profile, region, or overarching platform configuration.

region_code.description:
Code representing the regional or market context for this cart.

Often used to select applicable pricing, tax rules, and shipping options. The value should be one of the configured region identifiers (for example, `KR-Seoul` or `US-East`). When omitted, the backend may fall back to a default region associated with the customer, the channel, or a platform-wide default.

channel.description:
Identifier for the sales or access channel through which this cart is being created.

Examples include `web`, `mobile_web`, or `mobile_app`. This may influence available promotions, pricing strategies, and UX flows. When not provided, the backend can map the authenticated client type or request origin to a default channel value.

metadata.description:
Optional opaque metadata associated with the cart creation request.

Intended for lightweight, implementation-specific key-value pairs such as tracking tags, experiment identifiers, or A/B testing cohort information. The structure of this object is not interpreted at the schema level, but may be persisted for analytics, debugging, or troubleshooting.

Because keys and values are treated as arbitrary strings, higher-level services are responsible for imposing any additional structure or conventions on this metadata.

additionalProperties.description:
Metadata entry value associated with a metadata key.

All metadata values are persisted as strings for simplicity. Client and server components may agree on specific encodings or semantics, but such conventions are outside the scope of this schema.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether the newly created cart should be considered active immediately after creation.

This field conceptually maps to the non-nullable `is_active` column on the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` Prisma model. When set to `true`, the cart is treated as the customer's active working cart and is eligible for normal cart and checkout flows. When set to `false`, the cart can be created in an inactive or archived state for specialized workflows, such as pre-created draft carts or system-internal processing.

If this property is omitted, the backend applies its own default behavior, which typically treats new carts as active unless overridden by business rules or configuration. Clients that do not need to control the initial activity state can safely leave this field unspecified.

source_guest_token.description:
Anonymous guest cart token from which this persistent customer cart originates, when applicable.

This field corresponds to the nullable `source_guest_token` column on the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` Prisma model. It is primarily used in flows where an unauthenticated visitor has built up a guest cart and that cart is migrated into a persistent customer cart after the user signs up or logs in.

Providing this token allows the platform to trace and audit guest-to-customer cart migrations, reconcile analytics for conversion funnels, and perform cleanup of orphaned guest carts. When no guest cart is involved in the creation of this customer cart, this property should be omitted.

IShoppingMallCustomerCart.IUpdate.description:
Mutable fields that an authenticated customer or authorized operator may update on an existing persistent customer cart in the shopping_mall_customer_carts table.

This DTO is used by customer-facing and operator-facing cart management endpoints that allow changing configurable aspects of a cart while preserving its identity and ownership. It intentionally excludes system-managed identifiers, ownership links to shopping_mall_customer, and any fields that would alter lifecycle state such as checkout locking.

Typical usages include renaming a cart for UI display, changing the preferred region or currency when supported by the catalog configuration, and toggling flags that influence later checkout, pricing, or eligibility logic. All properties are optional to support partial updates; omitted properties are left unchanged on the server side.

display_name.description:
Human-friendly name for the cart used in customer-facing UIs.

This field allows customers to distinguish between multiple saved carts (for example, "Work items", "Holiday shopping", or "Gift ideas"). When provided, the backend updates the corresponding display name column of the shopping_mall_customer_carts row. Empty strings should be avoided; clients should either omit this field to keep the existing name or send a meaningful non-empty label.

region_code.description:
Business region code that indicates which market configuration this cart should use.

This value typically corresponds to a configured region in shopping_mall_region_settings and affects catalog visibility, pricing rules, taxation, and shipping options. Examples include ISO-like region identifiers such as "US", "EU", or more granular market codes like "KR-Seoul".

When omitted, the existing region association remains unchanged. Implementations may validate that the supplied code corresponds to an active region when updates are accepted.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code representing the customer’s preferred display and transaction currency for this cart.

Examples include "USD", "EUR", or "KRW". The platform may restrict allowed values to currencies supported by the customer’s region or by the payment configuration. Updating this field can influence price display, rounding, and eligible payment methods.

If not provided, the previous currency preference on the cart is preserved.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this cart is considered active for customer operations.

Active carts typically appear in default cart lists and may be eligible for checkout operations. Setting this to false can be used to archive or hide older carts without deleting them. A null value is treated as “no change” by the backend, while an explicit boolean toggles the corresponding flag on the shopping_mall_customer_carts record.

notes.description:
Optional free-form text field for customer or internal notes associated with the cart.

This can be used to capture reminders, special instructions, or internal comments visible only to support staff depending on UI design. Implementations may enforce a maximum length to prevent excessively large payloads. When omitted, existing notes remain unchanged.

IShoppingMallCustomerCartItem.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination criteria for retrieving items of a specific persistent customer cart from the shopping_mall_customer_cart_items table.

This DTO is used as the request body of PATCH endpoints that list cart items scoped by a customerCartId path parameter. It allows clients to request subsets of cart items based on SKU identity, creation timestamps, or status flags while also controlling paging and sort order.

All properties are optional. When no filters are provided, the backend should return the default first page of items for the given cart using its standard ordering. Implementations must enforce reasonable maximum page sizes and validate that any provided filter values are consistent with catalog and cart invariants.

page.description:
Zero-based index of the page of results to retrieve.

If omitted, the backend should default to the first page (typically 0). Negative values are invalid and should result in a validation error. Combined with limit, this determines which slice of cart items is returned from the underlying shopping_mall_customer_cart_items query.

limit.description:
Maximum number of cart item records to return in a single page.

Clients use this field to control how many items appear per page in cart UIs. Implementations should enforce an upper bound (for example, 50 or 100) to protect system performance. When not specified, a sensible default page size is applied by the backend.

sku_code.description:
Optional filter for limiting results to items corresponding to a specific product SKU.

This value typically matches a business-level SKU identifier on the shopping_mall_product_skus model rather than an internal numeric surrogate key. When provided, only cart items referencing this SKU code are included in the results.

status.description:
Optional filter representing a business-level status or classification of cart items.

Typical values could include internal states such as "normal", "promotion-only", or "invalidated", depending on how the platform models cart item eligibility. The exact set of allowed values is defined by business logic and may be enforced via validation or an enum at the implementation level.

created_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the item creation timestamp filter expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When provided, only items whose creation time is greater than or equal to this value are returned. This is useful for UIs that show only recently added items or support incremental loading scenarios.

created_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the item creation timestamp filter expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When provided together with created_from, it defines a date-time range for item creation time. Items created at or before this timestamp are eligible for inclusion in the result set.

sort_by.description:
Field name used to determine the primary sort order of the cart items in the response.

Common values may include "created_at" for chronological sorting or "sku_code" for grouping by SKU. The backend should validate that the requested sort field is supported and fall back to a default when an unsupported value is supplied.

sort_direction.description:
Requested sort direction applied to the primary sort field.

Typical accepted values are "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. Case-sensitive or insensitive handling should be defined by the implementation, and invalid values should result in a clear validation error or fallback to a safe default.

IShoppingMallCustomerCartItem.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new customer cart item within an existing persistent customer cart in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by authenticated customers to add a new line item to a specific cart identified by the path parameter `customerCartId`. It captures the SKU being added, the desired quantity, and any optional per-item notes or client-visible customization flags.

Server-side logic validates that the referenced SKU exists and is sellable, that the requested quantity is positive and within allowed limits, and that sufficient inventory is available. Ownership of the cart is validated via the authenticated customer context and the `customerCartId` path parameter. System-managed fields such as identifiers and timestamps are not included here and are generated by the backend on creation.

skuId.description:
Identifier of the SKU to add to the cart.

This corresponds to a `shopping_mall_product_skus` record that represents a concrete purchasable variant. The server uses this value to resolve pricing, inventory, and product metadata. The value must reference an active SKU that is visible and orderable for the current customer and region.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the specified SKU to add to the cart.

The quantity must be a positive integer greater than or equal to 1. The service layer may enforce additional upper bounds per SKU, per customer, or per policy configuration, and will validate that the requested quantity does not exceed available inventory or reservation limits.

oneOf.description:
Optional free-form note or message attached to this cart item.

This can be used for customer-facing annotations such as gift messages or special handling instructions. The content is not interpreted by the platform but may be displayed in checkout views and order summaries.

note.description:
Optional free-form note or message attached to this cart item.

This can be used for customer-facing annotations such as gift messages or special handling instructions. The content is not interpreted by the platform but may be displayed in checkout views and order summaries.

IShoppingMallCustomerCartItem.IUpdate.description:
Mutable fields for updating an existing customer cart item in a persistent shopping cart.

This DTO is used by the endpoint that updates a line item within a specific customer cart. It allows modifying only business-allowed attributes such as quantity and optional item-level notes, while system-managed identifiers and ownership fields remain immutable. The server uses path parameters and authentication context to determine which cart and item are being updated, so no identity or cart linkage fields are included here.

quantity.description:
New quantity of the SKU in the customer's cart.

Must be a positive integer and is validated against per-order and per-customer limits, as well as current stock levels from related inventory entities.

oneOf.description:
Optional customer-facing note or memo attached to this cart item.

Can be used for gift messages, internal reminders, or simple annotations that are displayed during checkout and order review.

note.description:
Optional customer-facing note or memo attached to this cart item.

When null, any existing note may be cleared, depending on implementation rules.

IShoppingMallWishlist.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for listing customer wishlists from the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table.

This DTO is used by the wishlist search endpoint, which accepts potentially complex filter and pagination data in the request body. It supports page-based navigation, free-text search, and structured filtering such as creation date ranges and default-wishlist flags so that an authenticated customer can efficiently browse their own wishlists.

The backend always scopes queries to the currently authenticated customer using the actor context; therefore, no direct customer identity fields are present in this DTO, and callers cannot use it to access other customers' wishlists.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination.

If omitted, the implementation should default to the first page. This value is used together with `limit` to determine which slice of wishlist summaries to return from the underlying `shopping_mall_wishlists` dataset.

limit.description:
Maximum number of wishlist summaries to return in a single page.

Implementations should enforce an upper bound to protect performance even if a larger value is supplied by the client. Typical defaults are defined at the application configuration layer rather than within this DTO itself.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to wishlist name or other searchable fields.

Used to quickly narrow down wishlists matching a keyword, for example by filtering by partial name matches or other text attributes supported by the underlying query implementation.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound of the wishlist creation timestamp range filter.

Only wishlists created at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp will be considered in the result set. This value is applied against the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound of the wishlist creation timestamp range filter.

Only wishlists created at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp will be considered in the result set. This value is applied against the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table.

isDefault.description:
Optional filter controlling whether only default or non-default wishlists are returned.

When set to `true`, the search returns only wishlists whose `is_default` column is true for the authenticated customer. When set to `false`, only non-default wishlists are returned. When null or omitted, no filter on the `is_default` flag is applied and both default and non-default wishlists may be included.

oneOf.description:
Field by which to sort wishlist results.

The value `created_at` sorts wishlists by their creation timestamp ascending or descending according to `orderDirection`.

Field by which to sort wishlist results.

The value `updated_at` sorts wishlists by their last update timestamp ascending or descending according to `orderDirection`.

Field by which to sort wishlist results.

The value `name` sorts wishlists lexicographically by their `name` column, allowing alphabetical ordering in user interfaces.

orderBy.description:
Field by which to sort wishlist results.

Supported values include creation time, last update time, and wishlist name. Actual database column mapping is handled in the service layer, but each value corresponds directly to a column in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order when ordering wishlist results by `created_at`, `updated_at`, or `name`.

Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field.

Use `desc` for descending order when ordering wishlist results by `created_at`, `updated_at`, or `name`.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the implementation may choose a sensible default such as descending by `created_at`.

IShoppingMallWishlist.description:
Represents a customer-owned wishlist within the shoppingMall platform.

A wishlist groups products or SKUs that a customer is interested in for future consideration. Each wishlist belongs to a single authenticated customer, is associated with exactly one `shopping_mall_customer` record, and stores both a human-readable name and lifecycle timestamps managed by the system.

The wishlist entity also indicates whether it is the customer's default wishlist. Platform business rules and database constraints ensure that at most one wishlist per customer is marked as default using the underlying `is_default` column. This DTO is used as the detailed response type for wishlist read operations and after create/update operations for wishlists stored in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` Prisma model. Scalar properties align with columns in that model, while nested relations such as `customer` and `items` represent related entities rather than standalone database columns.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the wishlist record in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table.

This value is generated by the backend or database layer and serves as the primary key for the wishlist. It is also used in API path parameters such as `{wishlistId}` when retrieving, updating, or deleting a specific wishlist.

customer.description:
Summary representation of the customer who owns this wishlist.

This relation corresponds to the non-nullable foreign key `shopping_mall_customer_id` in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` Prisma model. Instead of exposing the raw identifier, the API returns a lightweight customer summary so that list and detail views can immediately show ownership context without additional lookups.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the wishlist chosen by the customer.

Typical examples include labels like "Favorites", "Birthday Ideas", or "Summer Vacation". This value maps directly to the `name` column in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` model and is the primary way customers distinguish between multiple wishlists.

isDefault.description:
Flag indicating whether this wishlist is the customer's default wishlist.

This property maps to the non-nullable `is_default` column in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` Prisma model. Platform rules typically ensure that each customer has at most one wishlist with `is_default = true`, and many flows treat the default wishlist as the implicit target when a user saves items without explicitly choosing a wishlist.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the wishlist was first created, represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

This property reflects the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and is managed entirely by the system. Clients can use it to sort wishlists chronologically or to show when a particular wishlist was originally created.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the wishlist was most recently updated, represented as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

This property corresponds to the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and is automatically refreshed whenever mutable wishlist metadata or its items change. It allows clients to detect stale data and display "last updated" information in user interfaces.

items.description:
Collection of wishlist items associated with this wishlist.

Each entry represents a row from the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` model that links this wishlist to a target product or SKU in the catalog. Although `items` is not a scalar column on the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table, it is a nested relation used to present the contents of the wishlist in a single response payload in contexts where showing items is desirable.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ICreate.description:
Request body DTO for creating a new customer-owned wishlist in the shoppingMall platform.

This type includes only customer-controllable fields that are directly mapped to columns in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` Prisma model. Ownership information (link to the authenticated customer), default flags, identifiers, and audit timestamps are injected exclusively by the backend and MUST NOT be provided by the client.

The new wishlist record is persisted in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` Prisma model and returned as a full `IShoppingMallWishlist` entity on success.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the wishlist to create.

This value is stored directly in the `shopping_mall_wishlists.name` column and must clearly identify the wishlist for the customer, such as "Holiday Gifts" or "Work Equipment". The backend may enforce length and character constraints consistent with the underlying Prisma schema and database.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.description:
Wishlist item entity representing a single entry inside a customer-owned wishlist.

Each record in this model links a parent wishlist to a target in the catalog layer, referencing either a whole product or a specific SKU depending on platform configuration. Wishlist items have no independent lifecycle outside their parent wishlist and are used only for planning and discovery, not payment or fulfillment.

The schema exposes the parent wishlist reference, associated catalog entities as summary objects, and lifecycle timestamps used for display and audit scenarios. It is designed as a detailed view that complements the lighter `IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary` type used in list responses.

id.description:
Primary key of the wishlist item.

This value uniquely identifies a single entry in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table and is used as the authoritative identifier in path parameters such as `wishlistItemId`. It is generated by the backend and is always present on persisted records.

wishlist_id.description:
Identifier of the parent wishlist that owns this item.

This field represents the foreign key to the parent wishlist (`shopping_mall_wishlists.id`) and is used to ensure that the item is always resolved and validated within the correct wishlist context. It is kept as a raw identifier because the parent wishlist already exposes its items as a composition array, and duplicating the full parent object here would create circular references.

product.description:
Summary information for the product associated with this wishlist item.

This association replaces the low-level `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key and gives clients immediate access to key product attributes (such as name, brand, pricing range, and primary image) without requiring an additional catalog lookup call. It always refers to a valid catalog product in `shopping_mall_products`.

oneOf.description: Null when the wishlist operates at the product level and no specific SKU variant has been selected for this item.

sku.description:
Optional summary of the specific SKU variant associated with this wishlist item.

When present, this association identifies the exact purchasable variant (for example, a particular color and size) represented by the item and replaces the underlying `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` foreign key. When null, the item is considered to reference the product at a generic level rather than a specific SKU.

createdAt.description:
Creation timestamp of the wishlist item, as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

This value originates from `shopping_mall_wishlist_items.created_at` and records when the entry was initially added to the wishlist. It is managed by the backend and is useful for sorting, auditing, and understanding when a customer first showed interest in the catalog item.

updatedAt.description:
Last update timestamp of the wishlist item, as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_wishlist_items.updated_at` and is updated whenever mutable attributes of the wishlist item change. It helps clients detect stale data and supports synchronization logic between client caches and the backend.

deletedAt.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the wishlist item, as an ISO 8601 date-time string when present.

When null, the wishlist entry is considered active and should normally appear in customer views. When set to a non-null value, the item has been logically removed but may remain in storage for audit or analytics purposes, mirroring the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items.deleted_at` column.

IShoppingMallWishlist.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for modifying the editable display name of a customer-owned wishlist in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used when an authenticated customer renames an existing wishlist record stored in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table. It intentionally excludes all system-managed fields (such as identifiers, ownership, default flags, and timestamps) and focuses only on the single piece of wishlist metadata that customers are allowed to change directly through this API.

The wishlist to be updated is identified exclusively by the `wishlistId` path parameter on the corresponding endpoint, which maps to the primary key of `shopping_mall_wishlists`. The backend resolves the owning customer from the authentication context, verifies that the wishlist belongs to that customer, and then applies any provided changes to the `name` column while leaving all other columns untouched.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the wishlist as displayed in customer-facing UIs.

This value maps directly to the `name` column of the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and is the primary label customers use to distinguish between multiple wishlists (for example, "Favorites", "Gift Ideas", or "Work Setup"). Implementations should enforce a reasonable maximum length, trim unnecessary whitespace, and reject empty or purely whitespace-only values to maintain data quality.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.IRequest.description:
Request payload for listing and searching items contained within a specific customer wishlist.

This DTO is used as the body of a read-only PATCH operation that retrieves wishlist items from the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table for a given parent wishlist. It encapsulates pagination, sorting, and filtering options so that clients can control how wishlist contents are presented in the UI.

The parent wishlist is identified by the `wishlistId` path parameter of the endpoint, not by fields in this DTO. The backend ensures that the wishlist exists and is owned by the authenticated customer before applying any query options defined here.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve when using page/limit based pagination.

Page numbering is typically 1-based, where 1 refers to the first page of results. If omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of wishlist items to include in a single page of results.

Backends should enforce an upper bound to protect performance and may apply a sensible default when this field is not provided.

sortBy.description:
Field name or logical sort key that determines how wishlist items are ordered in the result set.

Common sort keys include values such as `"createdAt"` (date added to wishlist), `"productName"`, or `"price"`. The exact set of supported values is defined by the backend implementation. Unsupported values should result in a validation error.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering wishlist items.

Typical values are `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default, usually descending by creation date.

Sort direction to apply when ordering wishlist items.

Typical values are `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default, usually descending by creation date.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering wishlist items.

Typical values are `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default, usually descending by creation date.

onlyInStock.description:
Optional filter indicating whether to include only wishlist items whose referenced SKUs are currently in stock.

When true, the backend should exclude items referencing SKUs that have zero salable inventory based on `shopping_mall_inventory_items` and related inventory models. When false or omitted, no inventory-based filtering is applied.

categoryCode.description:
Optional category code filter used to restrict wishlist items to products or SKUs that belong to a specific catalog category.

The value should match a category code defined in the catalog models such as `shopping_mall_categories` or related category-tree entities. When provided, only items whose associated product or SKU is assigned to the given category (directly or through the category tree) should be returned.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new wishlist item under an existing customer wishlist.

This type is used as the request body for the `POST /shoppingMall/customer/wishlists/{wishlistId}/items` operation. The `wishlistId` path parameter supplies the parent wishlist identifier, so the DTO deliberately omits the `shopping_mall_wishlist_id` field to avoid duplication and potential conflicts.

The payload focuses on selecting the catalog target to be wishlisted, either at the product level or SKU level, and respects business rules derived from the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` Prisma model such as the uniqueness constraint on the combination of wishlist, product, and SKU.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Optional identifier of the product to be added to the wishlist.

When the platform operates in product-level wishlist mode, this field carries the UUID of the record in `shopping_mall_products.id` that the customer wants to keep for later. It may be null when the wishlist item is instead configured to target a specific SKU. Validation rules should ensure that at least one of the product or SKU reference is provided according to platform policy.

shopping_mall_product_sku_id.description:
Optional identifier of the SKU to be added to the wishlist.

In SKU-level wishlist configurations, this field contains the UUID of the record in `shopping_mall_product_skus.id` that the customer wishes to track. It may be null when the item is attached at the broader product level. Business logic and the unique index on `(shopping_mall_wishlist_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_product_sku_id)` should be used to avoid duplicate entries for the same target within a single wishlist.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.IUpdate.description:
DTO schema for updating a wishlist item within a specific customer wishlist on the shoppingMall platform.

This type represents the mutable catalog references of a wishlist entry in the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table. It allows switching the target between a product-level reference and a SKU-level reference, subject to platform rules and uniqueness constraints within the parent wishlist.

Ownership and parent-child relationships (wishlist and wishlist item IDs) are enforced via the `wishlistId` and `wishlistItemId` path parameters together with the authenticated customer context. The DTO itself only captures which catalog target the wishlist item should reference and any additional metadata fields that are actually stored on the wishlist item record.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the product that this wishlist item should reference at the product level, or null when the item is configured to target only a specific SKU.

When provided, the value must correspond to an existing, active product record in the `shopping_mall_products.id` column that is visible and purchasable according to catalog rules. This field is typically used when the platform supports product-level wishlists where a user favorites the base product rather than a specific SKU variant.

At least one of `shopping_mall_product_id` or `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` must be non-null according to platform configuration. Service logic must enforce this invariant and also prevent creation of duplicate wishlist items with the same effective target within the same wishlist, in line with the unique index on `(shopping_mall_wishlist_id, shopping_mall_product_id, shopping_mall_product_sku_id)`.

shopping_mall_product_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the specific SKU variant that this wishlist item should reference, or null when the item is configured to target only the product.

The value must match an existing, active SKU in the `shopping_mall_product_skus.id` column that is sellable and not discontinued. This field is primarily used when the platform supports SKU-level wishlists, enabling customers to track a concrete purchasable variant such as a specific size or color.

At least one of `shopping_mall_product_id` or `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` must be non-null in a valid update request. Handlers should reject combinations that violate business constraints and must prevent creation of duplicate wishlist items with the same effective target within the same wishlist, respecting the underlying unique constraint.

IShoppingMallCartSummary.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for computing a summarized view of the current shopping cart on the shoppingMall platform.

This type is used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/carts/summary endpoint to pass contextual parameters that influence how the cart summary is computed and presented. It does not identify the cart directly; the effective cart (guest or customer) MUST always be resolved from the caller's session or a secure guest token at the implementation layer.

Typical use cases include specifying the shopper's region for shipping and tax estimation, choosing a preferred currency, and toggling inclusion of optional computed sections such as promotion breakdowns or diagnostic information. The DTO is read-only with respect to cart state: using this type MUST NOT mutate cart contents or server-side configuration.

region_code.description:
Code representing the shopper's active region or market used for region-aware pricing, tax, and shipping estimation.

The value should align with region identifiers configured in shopping_mall_region_settings and may follow ISO country/region codes or a platform-specific scheme. When omitted, the backend uses the default region associated with the session or platform configuration.

currency_code.description:
Preferred ISO 4217 currency code (for example, "USD", "EUR", "KRW") to use when presenting cart totals and line item prices.
