If omitted, the platform's default currency for the resolved region is used. When specified, it must be one of the currencies supported by the platform and, if applicable, the shopper's region.

include_promotions.description:
Flag indicating whether promotion and discount breakdown information should be included in the computed cart summary response.

When true, the server attempts to evaluate applicable promotions, coupons, and discounts, and to surface corresponding line-level and cart-level adjustments in the summary. When false or omitted, the server may return only basic pricing information without detailed promotion metadata.

include_shipping_estimate.description:
Flag controlling whether estimated shipping fees and related breakdowns are included in the summary response.

When true, the server calculates shipping cost estimates based on the shopper's region and any available shipping address context, using configuration from shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings or similar tables. When omitted or false, the response may omit shipping sections or include only minimal placeholders.

include_diagnostics.description:
Optional flag used primarily by frontends or admin tools to request additional diagnostic information in the cart summary response.

When true, the server may include internal evaluation details such as which promotions were considered, why certain items were excluded from discounts, or warnings about invalid SKUs. This field should be used sparingly in production contexts to avoid leaking sensitive implementation details to end-users.

IShoppingMallCartSummary.description:
Denormalized, computed view of the active shopper's current cart on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO aggregates guest or customer cart line items with product and SKU metadata to present a user-facing cart summary used in cart and checkout UIs. It includes per-line pricing, quantities, and subtotals, along with overall totals such as item count, subtotal, estimated discounts, shipping estimates, and grand total. It is read-only and not mapped 1:1 to a single Prisma model.

items.description: List of cart line items included in the current cart summary. Each item combines cart quantity with product/SKU presentation data and computed line-level pricing.

totals.description: Aggregated cart totals including item count, subtotal, estimated discounts, estimated shipping, taxes (if applicable), and grand total.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code used for all monetary fields in this cart summary (for example, "USD" or "KRW").

oneOf.description: Business-defined region or market code used when computing region-aware pricing, shipping estimates, and eligibility rules.

regionCode.description: Business-defined region or market code used when computing region-aware pricing, shipping estimates, and eligibility rules.

hasErrors.description: Indicates whether the cart summary includes any blocking issues at the time of computation, such as disabled products or SKUs that can no longer be purchased.

warnings.description: Non-blocking warnings about the current cart state, such as low inventory, products nearing end-of-sale, or minor inconsistencies that do not prevent checkout.

errors.description: Blocking issues that prevent the cart from being directly eligible for checkout from the summary perspective (for example, disabled SKUs or items that are no longer sellable).

IShoppingMallCartSummaryItem.description:
Single cart line item in the computed shopping mall cart summary.

Each item represents a specific SKU selected by the shopper along with its quantity, pricing snapshot, and human-readable product information. It combines cart item state from guest or customer cart tables with product and SKU metadata for display.

cartItemId.description:
Opaque identifier of the underlying cart item row from either guest or customer cart items table.

The exact source table (guest vs customer) is internal to the implementation and not exposed to clients.

productId.description: Identifier of the base product record associated with this cart item.

skuId.description: Identifier of the specific SKU (variant) associated with this cart item.

productName.description: Display name of the product for this cart line, suitable for use in cart and checkout UIs.

skuName.description: Display name of the SKU or variant, typically including option selections (for example, size or color).

oneOf.description: URL of the primary product or SKU image used as thumbnail in cart and checkout UIs.

thumbnailUrl.description: URL of the primary product or SKU image used as thumbnail in cart and checkout UIs.

quantity.description:
Quantity of this SKU currently in the cart.

The value is always at least 1 and represents the number of units that will be considered when computing monetary fields such as lineSubtotal and lineTotal.

unitPrice.description:
Unit price for a single unit of this SKU at the time of summary computation, expressed in the summary currency.

This value is typically taken from the current effective catalog price after applying product- or SKU-level pricing rules but before any line- or cart-level discounts are applied.

lineSubtotal.description:
Subtotal for this line before discounts (unitPrice × quantity), expressed in the summary currency.

This field is computed by the backend and should be treated as read-only by clients; it represents the pre-discount monetary contribution of this cart line.

oneOf.description:
Total discount amount applied specifically to this line item, such as per-SKU promotions or coupons, expressed in the summary currency.

A positive value reduces the effective cost of this line. When null, it indicates that no line-specific discounts were applied.

lineDiscountTotal.description: Total discount amount applied specifically to this line item, such as per-SKU promotions or coupons, expressed in the summary currency.

lineTotal.description:
Final line total after applying line-specific discounts, expressed in the summary currency.

In most cases this is equal to lineSubtotal minus lineDiscountTotal (if any). Additional cart-level discounts or shipping costs may further affect the overall order total but are not reflected here.

options.description:
Human-readable option selections associated with this SKU (for example, size=L, color=Blue).

Entries correspond to the option dimensions configured on the product and the concrete values chosen for the SKU, making it easy to render variant details in cart and checkout UIs.

isAvailable.description:
Indicates whether this SKU is currently considered available for purchase based on product visibility and inventory rules evaluated during summary computation.

When false, the cart line may be non-checkoutable (for example, due to the product being disabled, out of stock, or restricted in the shopper's region).

oneOf.description:
Optional human-readable message describing the availability status of this cart line (for example, "Out of stock", "Limited quantity", or "Product no longer available").

This message is intended for direct display in the UI and may provide guidance on how the shopper can resolve or understand the unavailability state.

availabilityMessage.description: Optional human-readable message describing the availability status of this cart line (for example, "Out of stock", "Limited quantity", or "Product no longer available").

IShoppingMallCartSummaryItemOption.description:
Human-readable representation of a single option selection for a cart line item.

This typically corresponds to an option type (such as size or color) and the concrete option value chosen for the SKU in the cart.

name.description: Display name of the option dimension (for example, "Size" or "Color").

value.description: Display value selected for this option (for example, "L" or "Blue").

IShoppingMallCartSummaryTotals.description:
Aggregated monetary totals and counts for a computed cart summary.

All monetary fields are expressed in the currency indicated by the parent summary DTO.

itemCount.description: Total number of distinct cart lines currently included in the cart summary.

quantityTotal.description: Total quantity across all cart lines (sum of each line's quantity).

subtotal.description: Total pre-discount merchandise amount across all cart lines (sum of lineSubtotal values).

oneOf.description: Total discount amount applied to the cart from all sources, including line-level and cart-level promotions.

discountTotal.description: Total discount amount applied to the cart from all sources, including line-level and cart-level promotions.

oneOf.description: Estimated shipping fee for the current cart state and contextual parameters supplied in the summary request, if an estimate can be computed.

shippingEstimate.description: Estimated shipping fee for the current cart state and contextual parameters supplied in the summary request, if an estimate can be computed.

oneOf.description: Estimated tax amount for the current cart state and contextual parameters, if tax estimation is enabled and can be computed.

taxEstimate.description: Estimated tax amount for the current cart state and contextual parameters, if tax estimation is enabled and can be computed.

grandTotal.description: Final estimated payable amount for the cart including merchandise, discounts, shipping, and taxes as applicable.

IShoppingMallCartSummaryMessage.description:
Structured message representing a warning or blocking error related to the current cart summary.

Messages are suitable for direct display in cart or checkout UIs to help shoppers understand issues with their cart contents or configuration.

code.description: Machine-readable message code that uniquely identifies the validation rule or condition that produced this message.

message.description: Human-readable description of the issue or warning, suitable for display in user interfaces.

oneOf.description: Severity level for this message that indicates whether it is blocking (error) or non-blocking (warning).
Severity level for this message that indicates whether it is blocking (error) or non-blocking (warning).

severity.description: Severity level for this message that indicates whether it is blocking (error) or non-blocking (warning).

oneOf.description: Optional identifier of the cart line item to which this message specifically applies. When omitted, the message is interpreted as cart-level.

cartItemId.description: Optional identifier of the cart line item to which this message specifically applies. When omitted, the message is interpreted as cart-level.

IShoppingMallCartValidation.ICreate.description:
Request payload for triggering validation of the current shopper's cart.

Carries contextual parameters that influence validation logic, such as shipping destination, selected shipping method, intended payment method, and coupon or promotion codes. The cart identity itself is NOT supplied here and must be derived from the authenticated session or secure guest token by the backend implementation.

shippingAddress.description:
Candidate shipping address that will be used for validation.

Used to evaluate regional availability, shipping-zone compatibility, and potential address-related restrictions such as age or product compliance policies.

shippingMethodCode.description:
Optional code of the selected shipping method for this cart validation.

When provided, the validator will check whether this shipping method is available for the given address, cart contents, and region policies. Typical values correspond to configured shipping methods in shopping mall configuration tables.

paymentMethodCode.description:
Optional code of the intended payment method for this cart validation.

If provided, the validator confirms that this payment method is currently enabled for the shopper's region and for the cart currency/amounts, according to payment configuration and risk policies.

couponCodes.description:
List of coupon or promotion codes the shopper intends to apply to the current cart.

The validator checks each code for validity, applicability to the cart contents, expiration, and compatibility with other active promotions.

notes.description:
Optional free-form note or client-side context attached to this validation attempt.

Can be used for logging or diagnostic purposes, but is not interpreted by core validation rules.

IShoppingMallCartValidation.description:
Result of validating the current shopper's cart prior to checkout on the shoppingMall platform.

Represents a read-only snapshot of validation outcomes for the active cart (guest or customer). It indicates whether the cart is currently eligible for checkout and, if not, enumerates blocking errors and non-blocking warnings for individual cart lines and for cart-level conditions such as shipping, payment, and coupons.

This DTO is not directly mapped to a single Prisma model; rather, it aggregates information derived from cart tables (guest/customer carts and items), product and SKU definitions, inventory state, and policy tables such as age or regional restrictions.

isValid.description:
Overall validation result flag.

True when the cart is currently eligible to proceed to checkout without blocking issues. False when at least one blocking validation error exists for any cart line or cart-level rule.

blockingErrors.description:
Collection of blocking validation errors that prevent checkout.

Each entry describes a violation that must be resolved before the checkout process can continue, such as out-of-stock items, inactive products, unsupported shipping destinations, or invalid coupons.

warnings.description:
Collection of non-blocking warnings discovered during validation.

Warnings highlight potential issues or recommendations (e.g., low inventory, soon-to-expire promotions, or address normalization suggestions) that do not strictly block checkout but should be communicated to the shopper.

cartSnapshot.description:
Optional snapshot of the cart state at the time of validation.

Provides a lightweight view of cart lines, quantities, and their current availability status so that clients can render a consistent view of what was evaluated. This snapshot is derived from guest or customer cart tables and associated product/SKU records.

IShoppingMallOrder.IRequest.description:
Search/filter DTO for querying orders in the `shopping_mall_orders` table.

Used by both customer-facing and platform-admin order search APIs to express complex filters, pagination, and sorting criteria when retrieving paginated lists of orders. All filter fields must correspond to columns or supported computed criteria derived from the Prisma schema for `shopping_mall_orders` and related entities.

From a security perspective, this DTO must **never** be used to trust client-provided authentication context. In particular, when used on customer-facing endpoints, the effective customer scope MUST be derived from the authenticated actor (JWT/session) by the server, not from any `customerId` value supplied in the request body.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

The value must be a positive integer starting from 1. Together with `limit`, it determines which slice of the result set is returned.

If omitted, the server implementation may apply a sensible default (for example, page 1) according to platform-wide pagination conventions.

limit.description:
Maximum number of order records to return in a single page.

The value must be a positive integer. Implementations are expected to enforce a maximum upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets and protect the `shopping_mall_orders` table from unbounded scans.

When not provided, the server may apply a default page size consistent with the platform’s pagination guidelines.

id.description:
Optional exact filter on the primary key of the order.

When provided, this value must be a valid UUID corresponding to the `id` column of `shopping_mall_orders`. It is primarily intended for internal tools and administrative UIs that already know the order identifier and want to reuse the search endpoint for a precise lookup.

This filter can be combined with other filters such as status or date ranges, but many implementations will short‑circuit to an exact match query when `id` is supplied.

orderCode.description:
Optional exact or partial search term for the business order code.

This value is matched against the `order_code` column of `shopping_mall_orders`, which is uniquely indexed for human‑friendly lookup (for example, `ORD-20251114-0001`). Implementations may support exact, prefix, or contains matching depending on UI needs.

Order code search is commonly used in customer support workflows and self‑service order history views where the user inputs an order number from an email or receipt.

customerId.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to orders belonging to a specific customer.

This field maps to the foreign key `shopping_mall_customer_id` on `shopping_mall_orders`. It is useful in privileged contexts, such as platform‑admin tooling, to locate all orders for a specific customer.

For **customer‑actor** endpoints (where `authorizationActor` is `customer`), the effective customer scope **must always be derived from the authenticated actor identity (JWT/session)**. In those scenarios, the server should ignore or override this field to prevent customers from querying orders belonging to other customers.

currencyCode.description:
Optional filter on the currency used for the order monetary snapshot.

This corresponds to the `currency_code` column in the `shopping_mall_orders` table and should contain a valid ISO 4217 code such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`.

Multi‑currency deployments can use this field to restrict search results to orders denominated in a particular currency for reporting, operational review, or regional dashboards.

items.description:
Single order status value used in filtering.

Each value should correspond to a valid business status stored in the `order_status` column of `shopping_mall_orders`, such as `pending_payment`, `processing`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, or `refunded`.

orderStatuses.description:
Optional list of order status values to include in the result set.

When this array is provided and non‑empty, only orders whose `order_status` is in the supplied set are eligible to appear in the result. When omitted or empty, the server applies its default status filtering behavior (typically including all non‑deleted orders regardless of status).

items.description:
Single payment status value used in filtering.

Each value should correspond to a valid payment lifecycle state stored in the `payment_status` column of `shopping_mall_orders`, such as `payment_pending`, `payment_captured`, `payment_failed`, `partially_refunded`, or `refunded`.

paymentStatuses.description:
Optional list of payment status values to include in the result set.

This filter is commonly used for operational views that focus on outstanding payments, refund workflows, or reconciliation of paid orders.

placedAtFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for filtering orders by the `placed_at` timestamp.

When provided, only orders whose `placed_at` value is **greater than or equal to** this instant are included. The value must be a valid ISO 8601 date‑time string.

This filter is typically combined with `placedAtTo` to define a time window for orders that were actually placed during a given period.

placedAtTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for filtering orders by the `placed_at` timestamp.

When provided, only orders whose `placed_at` value is **less than or equal to** this instant are included. The value must be a valid ISO 8601 date‑time string.

Used together with `placedAtFrom`, this allows callers to request orders that were placed within a specific reporting or operational window.

createdAtFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for filtering orders by the `created_at` timestamp.

This value must be a valid ISO 8601 date‑time string and is applied to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_orders`. It is useful when the creation moment differs from the business `placed_at` time but still has reporting significance.

When both `createdAtFrom` and `placedAtFrom` are present, implementations should document which field takes precedence or support both as independent filters, depending on business requirements.

createdAtTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for filtering orders by the `created_at` timestamp.

This value must be a valid ISO 8601 date‑time string and is applied to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_orders`. Only orders created at or before this instant are returned.

Combined with `createdAtFrom`, this enables consumers to retrieve all orders that were inserted into the system within a particular time window, independent of their `placed_at` or lifecycle state.

itemsSubtotalAmountMin.description:
Inclusive lower bound for filtering by the `items_subtotal_amount` column.

When provided, only orders whose items subtotal (before discounts, taxes, and shipping) is **greater than or equal to** this amount are included. The value is interpreted using the order’s `currency_code`.

This field is typically used together with `itemsSubtotalAmountMax` to search for orders within a specific item‑subtotal price band.

itemsSubtotalAmountMax.description:
Inclusive upper bound for filtering by the `items_subtotal_amount` column.

When provided, only orders whose items subtotal is **less than or equal to** this amount are included. The value is interpreted using the order’s `currency_code`.

Consumers commonly provide both `itemsSubtotalAmountMin` and `itemsSubtotalAmountMax` to narrow results to orders within a desired range of line‑item totals.

discountTotalAmountMin.description:
Inclusive lower bound for filtering by the `discount_total_amount` column.

Only orders whose total discount amount is **greater than or equal to** this value are returned. This can be used to focus on heavily discounted orders for promotion analysis or fraud monitoring.

The value is expressed in the same currency as the order (`currency_code`).

discountTotalAmountMax.description:
Inclusive upper bound for filtering by the `discount_total_amount` column.

Only orders whose total discount amount is **less than or equal to** this value are included. Combined with `discountTotalAmountMin`, this allows callers to target orders within a band of applied discounts.

shippingTotalAmountMin.description:
Inclusive lower bound for filtering by the `shipping_total_amount` column.

When supplied, the query includes only orders whose total shipping cost across all seller segments is **greater than or equal to** this value. This can help identify high‑shipping‑cost orders for logistics review or customer support.

The value is expressed in the order’s `currency_code`.

shippingTotalAmountMax.description:
Inclusive upper bound for filtering by the `shipping_total_amount` column.

Only orders with a `shipping_total_amount` **less than or equal to** this value are returned. Used with `shippingTotalAmountMin`, it lets callers isolate orders with shipping fees in a particular range.

taxTotalAmountMin.description:
Inclusive lower bound for filtering by the `tax_total_amount` column.

Orders whose total tax is **greater than or equal to** this value will be included, allowing tax‑focused reporting or compliance checks.

The amount is interpreted using the `currency_code` associated with the order.

taxTotalAmountMax.description:
Inclusive upper bound for filtering by the `tax_total_amount` column.

Only orders whose total tax is **less than or equal to** this value are included. This field is often combined with `taxTotalAmountMin` when running analytics on tax ranges and thresholds.

grandTotalAmountMin.description:
Inclusive lower bound for filtering by the `grand_total_amount` column.

The grand total is defined as `items_subtotal_amount - discount_total_amount + shipping_total_amount + tax_total_amount` and represents the final payable amount at checkout. When this filter is provided, only orders with a grand total **greater than or equal to** this value are returned.

This is commonly used to segment orders by overall order value for analytics or operational prioritisation.

grandTotalAmountMax.description:
Inclusive upper bound for filtering by the `grand_total_amount` column.

Only orders whose `grand_total_amount` is **less than or equal to** this value are returned. In combination with `grandTotalAmountMin`, this allows clients to search for orders within a specific order‑value band, such as low‑value impulse purchases or high‑value VIP orders.

includeDeleted.description:
Optional flag indicating whether soft‑deleted orders should be included in the result set.

By default, implementations must **exclude** rows where the `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_orders` is not null, ensuring that ordinary listings show only active, non‑deleted orders.

When this flag is explicitly set to `true` on privileged endpoints (for example, platform administrator tools), the server may include soft‑deleted orders for audit, forensics, or recovery workflows. Customer‑facing endpoints should generally ignore this flag and continue to hide soft‑deleted records.

sortBy.description:
Field name used to sort the result set.

Typical values correspond to indexed columns on `shopping_mall_orders`, such as `created_at`, `placed_at`, or `order_code`. Implementations **must** validate that the supplied value is in an allowed whitelist before using it to build queries to avoid unsafe or inefficient sorts.

When omitted, servers usually default to sorting by a recency‑based field such as `created_at` or `placed_at` in descending order.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for the result set.

Common values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. The server should fall back to a sensible default (usually `desc`) when this property is not provided or when the client sends an unsupported value that is rejected during validation.

Sorting is applied together with `sortBy` to determine the final ordering of records within each page.

IShoppingMallCartValidation.IMessage.description:
Structured representation of a single cart validation message.

Used for both blocking errors and non-blocking warnings. Each message identifies the affected scope (cart-level or specific line), a machine-readable code for programmatic handling, and a human-readable message for display to end users.

scope.description:
Scope within the cart that this validation message applies to.

Typical values distinguish between cart-level and line-level issues, for example: `cart`, `line`, or other domain-specific scopes used by the implementation.

lineId.description:
Identifier of the affected cart line when this message pertains to a specific item.

Usually corresponds to the primary key or stable identifier of a cart item record. This field may be omitted or null for cart-level messages that are not tied to a single line.

code.description:
Machine-readable code representing the validation rule or error type.

Clients can use this code to implement localized messaging, automated remediation flows, or analytics on common validation failures.

message.description:
Human-readable description of the validation issue or warning.

Intended to be displayed directly to end users, possibly after localization, to explain why an item or the entire cart is not valid for checkout.

IShoppingMallCartValidation.ICartSnapsho.description:
Lightweight snapshot of cart contents as evaluated during a specific validation run.

This DTO is a read-only projection derived from the current state of guest or customer carts in the shopping mall backend (for example, from `shopping_mall_guest_carts` or `shopping_mall_customer_carts` and their related item tables). It does not represent a mutable cart entity itself, but rather a point-in-time view used by validation services.

The snapshot aggregates line-level information together with the outcomes of inventory and policy checks. It is primarily consumed by frontend or orchestration layers that need to understand which cart lines are currently purchasable and why certain lines may be blocked or require user attention.

lines.description:
Array of cart line snapshots evaluated during validation.

Each element in this collection corresponds to a single logical cart item record that exists in either a guest cart (e.g., `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items`) or a persistent customer cart (e.g., `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items`). The snapshot captures the line as it appears at validation time, including quantities and the result of inventory and policy evaluation.

The array is always present but may be empty if the underlying cart currently contains no items. Clients should handle the empty case gracefully, treating it as a valid representation of an empty cart at the moment of validation.

IShoppingMallCartValidation.ICartLineSna.description:
Summary of a single cart line at validation time.

This DTO represents one logical line item from a guest or customer cart at the exact moment validation is executed. It links back to the underlying cart item row as well as the associated catalog product and SKU records, providing enough information to reason about availability and policy decisions.

The line snapshot is intentionally lightweight and read-only. It omits large product detail payloads and instead focuses on identifiers, requested quantity, and a simple boolean flag that states whether the line can proceed to checkout under the current inventory and policy constraints.

lineId.description:
Identifier of the cart line in the underlying cart item table.

This value typically corresponds to the primary key of a row in either `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` or `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items`, depending on whether the shopper is a guest or an authenticated customer.

Client applications use this identifier to correlate validation feedback with specific UI line items, enabling targeted updates (such as highlighting an invalid line or displaying an error badge) without re-resolving the entire cart structure.

productId.description:
Identifier of the product associated with this cart line.

This usually maps directly to the primary key of a record in the `shopping_mall_products` table and is stable across SKUs that belong to the same product family.

The product identifier is used for higher-level catalog lookups, pricing rules, marketing content, and cross-cutting policy evaluations (for example, age restrictions, global visibility flags, or brand-level constraints) that apply at the product level rather than the SKU level.

skuId.description:
Identifier of the SKU (stock keeping unit) associated with this cart line.

The SKU identifier corresponds to a record in `shopping_mall_product_skus` and represents the concrete variant that the shopper intends to purchase (for example, a specific size, color, or configuration).

During validation, this field is used to join into inventory (`shopping_mall_inventory_items` and related movement/reservation tables) and variant-level configuration (such as per-SKU visibility overrides or compliance flags), ensuring that decisions about purchasability are made at the precise variant level.

quantity.description:
Requested quantity for this cart line at the time of validation.

The quantity reflects exactly what is stored in the underlying cart item row for this line and is what the validation service evaluates against available inventory and purchase-limit policies.

A minimum of `1` is enforced, which means a line with quantity `0` is not considered a valid cart entry in this view. If users attempt to reduce a quantity to zero, client code or cart APIs should remove the line entirely rather than representing it here as a zero-quantity snapshot.

isPurchasable.description:
Flag indicating whether this specific line is currently purchasable under the evaluated conditions.

A value of `true` means that, at validation time, the associated product and SKU are active and visible, the requested quantity does not violate inventory constraints or per-order limits, and no blocking compliance or business rules prevent purchase.

A value of `false` indicates that at least one blocking condition was detected—for example, the SKU is out of stock, the product is temporarily hidden for the shopper's region, the item violates age or restriction policies, or the quantity exceeds allowed thresholds. Client applications should use this flag to highlight problematic lines and may need to inspect separate validation message structures for detailed error reasons.

IShoppingMallCartValidation.IShippingAdd.description:
Shipping address supplied for cart validation.

Represents the destination that will be used to evaluate shipping zone eligibility, regional product restrictions, and address-dependent policies such as age restrictions or compliance flags.

countryCode.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the shipping destination.

Used to determine applicable regional policies, tax rules, and shipping zones.

postalCode.description:
Postal or ZIP code for the shipping address.

Used in conjunction with other address fields to determine shipping-zone membership and availability of services.

stateOrProvince.description:
State, province, or region component of the shipping address.

Optional depending on country, but when provided it can further refine regional policies and shipping options.

city.description:
City or locality component of the shipping address.

Used primarily for display and may play a role in fine-grained regional rules.

addressLine1.description: Primary street address line for the shipping destination.

addressLine2.description:
Secondary address information, such as apartment, suite, or building details.

Optional and used for display and precise delivery routing.

recipientName.description:
Full name of the person or entity receiving the shipment.

Used on shipping labels and for carrier delivery operations.

phoneNumber.description:
Contact phone number for the recipient at the shipping address.

May be required by some carriers or regions for delivery coordination and notifications.

IShoppingMallOrder.description:
Detailed master order entity for the shopping mall platform.

Represents a customer-facing master order stored in the `shopping_mall_orders` table. Aggregates items across multiple sellers for a single checkout, and carries monetary snapshots, lifecycle timestamps, and status fields. This type is used for detailed order views in back-office tools and customer portals.

id.description:
Primary key of the order in `shopping_mall_orders`.

This UUID value uniquely identifies the order across all subsystems and is used as the stable identifier in URLs, foreign keys, and audit logs.

customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer who owns this order.

This field corresponds directly to the non-nullable `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key column on the `shopping_mall_orders` table. It is the database-level reference behind the denormalized `customer` summary object and is useful for administrative queries and joins.

order_code.description:
Human-readable business order code, such as `ORD-20251114-0001`.

This code is typically unique and is shown to customers, support agents, and finance teams as the primary human-friendly reference to this order in emails, invoices, and phone conversations.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary snapshot amounts on this order (for example, `USD` or `KRW`).

Every monetary field in this DTO (`items_subtotal_amount`, `discount_total_amount`, `shipping_total_amount`, `tax_total_amount`, `grand_total_amount`) is denominated in this currency and represents an immutable snapshot captured at checkout.

items_subtotal_amount.description:
Subtotal of item line amounts before discounts, shipping, and tax.

Computed from the prices and quantities of all order lines at checkout time and stored as a snapshot on the order for auditability and financial reporting.

discount_total_amount.description:
Total amount of discounts applied to this order across items, promotions, coupons, and campaigns.

Captured as a snapshot field on the order, this value reflects all price reductions applied at the time the order was placed.

shipping_total_amount.description:
Total shipping charges applied to the order at checkout time.

This value aggregates shipping costs across all sellers and shipping options chosen during checkout and is stored as a snapshot on the order.

tax_total_amount.description:
Total tax amount applied to the order based on applicable tax rules at checkout time.

Includes all tax components such as VAT or sales tax that were calculated from the order lines and shipping charges at the time the order was placed.

grand_total_amount.description:
Final payable order total after applying discounts, shipping, and taxes.

This amount represents what the customer was expected to pay at checkout and is the basis for payment transactions, refunds, and downstream accounting.

order_status.description:
High-level lifecycle status of the order, such as `pending`, `processing`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, or `completed`.

The allowed values are defined by business configuration and encode where the order currently sits in the fulfillment pipeline.

payment_status.description:
Payment status for this order, such as `pending_payment`, `authorized`, `paid`, `partially_refunded`, `refunded`, or `chargeback`.

This field tracks the lifecycle of payment transactions associated with the order and is synchronized with the payment and refund subsystems.

origin_customer_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the customer cart from which this order was originally created, if applicable.

This field is a read-only projection of the nullable `shopping_mall_customer_cart_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_orders`. When present, it allows back-office tools and analytics to trace the order back to the cart state that generated it.

customer_note.description:
Free-form note entered by the customer when placing the order.

This value is persisted in the `customer_note` column of `shopping_mall_orders` and is typically visible to sellers and support staff to convey delivery instructions or contextual information about the purchase.

internal_note.description:
Internal note associated with this order, visible only to platform administrators and support personnel.

Stored in the `internal_note` column of `shopping_mall_orders`, this field can be used to record investigation outcomes, manual adjustments, or other internal commentary that should not be exposed to customers.

placed_at.description:
Timestamp when the order was successfully placed from checkout.

This marks the moment the `shopping_mall_orders` record was created and the order became part of the system’s order lifecycle, regardless of whether payment has fully settled.

confirmed_at.description:
Timestamp when the order was confirmed as ready for fulfillment.

Typically set after payment authorization and validation checks succeed. For orders that never reach this state, this value remains null.

cancelled_at.description:
Timestamp when the order was fully cancelled in accordance with the mall’s cancellation policies.

If the order has not been cancelled, this field remains null. When set, it indicates that the order has exited the normal fulfillment flow.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the order lifecycle was completed successfully beyond return and refund windows.

For example, this may be set when all items have been delivered and the configured return period has elapsed. Orders still in progress or cancelled will have this field null.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the `shopping_mall_orders` record was initially inserted.

Used for audit, reporting, and chronological ordering of records.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to the `shopping_mall_orders` record.

Any change to order-level data, including status transitions or note edits, should update this timestamp.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the order.

When this field is non-null, the order has been logically removed from standard listings while being retained for legal, audit, or internal reporting purposes.

customer.description:
Owning customer for this order, projected from the `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key.

This summary object provides a compact, non-sensitive view of the customer identity that is suitable for administrative and support UIs.

IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new master order in the shopping mall platform.

Represents validated checkout state submitted when a customer confirms purchase. Contains references to the originating cart and the selected shipping and billing address snapshots, as well as pricing snapshots that will be persisted into `shopping_mall_orders` and related tables. The authenticated customer identity is taken from the current session and MUST NOT be provided directly in this DTO.

customer_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the customer cart from which this order is being created.

This value maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_customer_cart_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_orders` and allows the backend to derive SKUs, quantities, and client-side pricing from the active cart when constructing the master order.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code to be used for this order, such as `USD` or `KRW`.

All monetary snapshot fields in this DTO are interpreted in this currency, and the backend validates that it is compatible with the selected payment method and regional settings.

items_subtotal_amount.description:
Subtotal amount for all cart line items before applying discounts, shipping, or tax.

Computed in the checkout flow from item prices and quantities and then validated or recomputed by the backend before persisting to `shopping_mall_orders`.

discount_total_amount.description:
Total discount amount expected to be applied to this order.

Includes item-level, cart-level, and promotion-based discounts that reduced the original items subtotal at checkout.

shipping_total_amount.description:
Total shipping charges expected for this order.

Represents the sum of per-seller and per-shipment shipping costs chosen during checkout and is validated against configured shipping rules before being stored on the order.

tax_total_amount.description:
Total tax amount expected to be charged for this order.

Derived from tax rules applied during checkout across items, shipping charges, and discounts and validated by the backend before snapshotting on the order record.

grand_total_amount.description:
Final payable order total expected by the client after discounts, shipping, and taxes.

The backend compares this value with its own authoritative calculation when creating the order. If there is a mismatch beyond allowed tolerances, the creation request is rejected as stale or inconsistent.

shipping_address_id.description:
Identifier of the selected shipping address snapshot to be applied to this order.

The backend uses this ID to look up a previously captured address snapshot and materializes it into `shopping_mall_order_addresses` as the shipping address for the new order.

billing_address_id.description:
Identifier of the selected billing address snapshot to be applied to this order.

Often this will match the shipping address, but it may differ for some customers. The backend copies the address data into `shopping_mall_order_addresses` as the billing address for the order.

customer_note.description:
Optional free-form note entered by the customer for this order.

When provided, this value is persisted into the `customer_note` column on `shopping_mall_orders` and is visible to sellers and support staff to convey delivery instructions or contextual information.

IShoppingMallOrder.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating a customer-facing master order in the shopping mall platform.

This schema represents the subset of fields on the `shopping_mall_orders` model that remain mutable after initial order creation. It is used by authenticated customers to edit safe, customer-visible attributes of their own orders before those orders reach a locked or terminal lifecycle state. Immutable workflow fields such as payment state, irreversible fulfillment transitions, and ownership information are intentionally excluded and controlled by internal services or administrator tools.

Only non-destructive updates such as contact details, memo fields, and other configurable metadata should be modeled here. System-managed identifiers and timestamps are not accepted in this DTO. Any changes that require cascading updates to subsidiary entities such as `shopping_mall_order_addresses` are handled server-side based on this input, not by accepting raw foreign keys or internal state flags from the client.

customer_memo.description:
Optional free-form memo entered by the customer for this order, such as delivery instructions or notes for the seller.

When supplied in this update DTO, the value will be written to the underlying `customer_note` column of the `shopping_mall_orders` Prisma model. Passing an empty string or omitting this field leaves existing content unchanged, while explicitly setting it to a non-empty string replaces the previous memo.

This field is customer-facing only and does not expose internal support notes; staff-only annotations continue to use the separate `internal_note` column managed by administrative tools.

IShoppingMallOrderSellerSegment.IRequest.description:
Filter and pagination parameters for searching seller-specific order segments that belong to a particular master order.

This schema is used as the request body for the PATCH /shoppingMall/orders/{orderId}/sellerSegments endpoint. It provides optional filters such as seller identity, segment lifecycle status, and creation date ranges, along with pagination and sorting options. The associated orderId path parameter determines which parent order in shopping_mall_orders is being queried; therefore this DTO MUST NOT duplicate the parent order identifier field.

The DTO is read-only in nature and is never used to mutate seller segments. It exists solely to describe how results from shopping_mall_order_seller_segments should be constrained, ordered, and paginated for list retrieval operations.

seller_id.description:
Optional filter that restricts results to seller segments owned by a specific seller.

When provided, only segments whose underlying `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.shopping_mall_seller_id` matches this UUID will be returned. This is typically used when a caller wants to focus on one seller's portion of a multi-seller order.

segment_statuses.description:
Optional list of segment lifecycle statuses to include in the result set.

Each value should correspond to a valid `segment_status` in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` (for example, `new`, `preparing`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`). When omitted, segments are not filtered by status; when supplied, only segments whose status is in this list are returned.

created_at_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) of the seller segment creation timestamp filter.

When set, only segments whose `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.created_at` is greater than or equal to this value are returned. Use an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or a clearly specified timezone.

created_at_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) of the seller segment creation timestamp filter.

When set together with `created_at_from`, the backend constrains results to segments created within the specified time window, based on `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.created_at`.

sort_field.description:
Logical field name used to order the seller segments in the response.

Typical values include creation and status-related fields such as `created_at`, `segment_status`, or `segment_code`. The exact set of supported sort fields is defined by the service implementation and may map to one or more columns in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments`.

sort_direction.description:
Direction in which results should be sorted.

Common values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. If omitted, the backend applies its default sorting strategy, usually descending by creation time or another operationally meaningful field.

page.description:
Zero-based index of the page to retrieve.

This field defines which slice of the filtered result set should be returned, aligning with the `current` property in `IPage.IPagination`. For example, `page = 0` is the first page, `page = 1` is the second page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to include in a single page of results.

This value corresponds to `limit` in `IPage.IPagination`. When omitted, the backend uses a sensible default page size. Clients may choose smaller limits for lightweight UIs or larger ones for bulk administrative tools, subject to server-enforced upper bounds.

IShoppingMallOrderSellerSegment.description:
Detailed representation of a per-seller segment within a multi-seller customer order, directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` Prisma model.

Each seller segment aggregates the portion of a customer-facing order that is handled by a single seller in the shoppingMall marketplace. It captures financial snapshots (item subtotal, discounts, shipping, tax, and grand total) and status information for that seller's share of the order.

This DTO is primarily used by platform administrators and internal tooling to inspect and manage per-seller breakdowns of a master order, including operational monitoring and financial reconciliation flows.

In addition to the parent order identifier, the DTO exposes a seller association as a summary object so that consumers can render seller context without additional lookups, following the BELONGS-TO `.ISummary` rule.

id.description:
Primary key of the seller segment.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.id` and uniquely identifies the per-seller segment record in the database.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the master order to which this seller segment belongs.

This maps directly to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.shopping_mall_order_id` and references `shopping_mall_orders.id`.

It is kept as a scalar hierarchical parent identifier so that the parent order DTO can own a collection of segments without introducing circular references.

segment_code.description:
Business-visible code that uniquely identifies this seller segment within the order context.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.segment_code` and is typically used in UIs and reports (for example, values like `ORD-20251114-0001-S1`).

segment_status.description:
Current fulfillment-oriented status for this seller segment.

This maps to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.segment_status` and represents lifecycle values such as `new`, `preparing`, `shipped`, `delivered`, or `cancelled`, as defined by business rules.

items_subtotal_amount.description:
Snapshot subtotal of all line items belonging to this seller segment before discounts, taxes, and shipping.

This field is a direct projection of `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.items_subtotal_amount` and is typically computed at checkout time.

discount_total_amount.description:
Snapshot total discount amount applied to this seller segment.

This maps to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.discount_total_amount` and aggregates all discounts affecting this segment, including item-level and segment-level discounts.

shipping_amount.description:
Snapshot shipping cost charged for this seller segment only.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.shipping_amount` and represents the portion of shipping attributable to this seller's items.

tax_amount.description:
Snapshot tax amount allocated to this seller segment.

This value comes from `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.tax_amount` and reflects taxes applied to the items, shipping, and any other taxable components in this segment.

grand_total_amount.description:
Snapshot grand total amount for this seller segment.

This field is mapped from `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.grand_total_amount` and is typically computed as `items_subtotal_amount - discount_total_amount + shipping_amount + tax_amount` at the time of order placement.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller responsible for this segment of the order.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key and follows the BELONGS-TO `.ISummary` rule so that callers can access key seller attributes (such as name and brand context) without additional API calls.

The underlying relation is `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.shopping_mall_seller_id` referencing `shopping_mall_seller.id`, but the DTO exposes it as a summary object to avoid redundant scalar IDs and to prevent circular reference expansion.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller segment record was created.

This maps directly to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.created_at` and is managed by the database or application layer.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller segment record was last updated.

This is a direct projection of `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.updated_at` and is updated whenever mutable operational fields for the segment change.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this seller segment.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.deleted_at`. When non-null, the record is considered soft-deleted and excluded from normal lists, while still being available for audit and historical reporting.

IShoppingMallOrderSellerSegment.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for mutable administrative and workflow-related fields of a seller segment within an order.

This DTO is used by platform administrators to change only those logical, admin-facing properties that are explicitly allowed to be edited after creation, such as reconciliation-related status or internal notes. It is intentionally **not** a direct 1:1 projection of the `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` Prisma model, but rather a higher-level administrative view mapped in the service layer.

Immutable identifiers, relationships, and financial snapshot fields remain managed exclusively by backend logic and are not exposed here, preserving financial integrity and auditability.

reconciliation_status.description:
Updated reconciliation status for this seller segment from an administrative perspective.

Typical values might include internal workflow states such as `pending`, `in_review`, or `reconciled`, as defined by business rules. This field is not a direct Prisma column but is mapped by the application layer onto appropriate persistent fields or related records.

admin_notes.description:
Updated administrative notes for this seller segment.

Allows platform administrators to capture free-form commentary about manual adjustments, investigations, or other internal context. Like `reconciliation_status`, this field is an administrative abstraction and may be stored in dedicated notes or audit structures rather than directly on the `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` row.

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.IRequest.description:
Request schema for searching and paginating order address snapshots for a specific order in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used as the request body of the PATCH `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/orders/{orderId}/addresses` endpoint and carries filtering, sorting, and pagination options. It never includes the parent order identifier itself, because `orderId` is supplied as a path parameter and must not be duplicated here.

page.description: Page number for pagination when listing order address snapshots for the specified order. Starts from 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of address snapshot records to return in a single page. Typical values range from 10 to 100 and the backend enforces an upper bound to protect performance.

sort_by.description: Field name used to sort order address snapshots within the given order scope. Typical supported values include `created_at`, `updated_at`, or `recipient_name`. The exact allowed field set is enforced server-side.

oneOf.description: Sort direction applied to the `sort_by` field. `asc` for ascending order, `desc` for descending order.
Sort direction applied to the `sort_by` field. `asc` for ascending order, `desc` for descending order.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction applied to the `sort_by` field. `asc` for ascending order, `desc` for descending order.

address_type.description: Optional discriminator for filtering address snapshots by their business role, such as `shipping` or `billing`. The exact set of allowed values is defined by the `address_type` enum in the `shopping_mall_order_addresses` Prisma model and validated on the server side.

country_code.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code used to filter address snapshots by destination country. Must be provided as a two-letter uppercase code such as `US`, `KR`, or `JP`.

postal_code.description: Optional postal or ZIP code filter applied to the order address snapshots. Allows administrators to narrow results to a specific postal region within the given order.

recipient_name.description: Optional free-text filter applied to the `recipient_name` column in `shopping_mall_order_addresses`. Administrators can use this to search for address snapshots whose recipient name contains the specified substring.

include_deleted.description: Flag indicating whether logically deleted address snapshots (rows with `deleted_at` set) should be included in search results. When omitted or false, soft-deleted rows are excluded by default.

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.description:
Detailed DTO representing an order address snapshot stored in the `shopping_mall_order_addresses` Prisma table.

This schema is used as the response body for operations that retrieve a single order address snapshot or return created/updated records. It reflects the denormalized address information captured at checkout time for an order in `shopping_mall_orders`. The DTO exposes only the address snapshot fields and lifecycle metadata, while the parent order relationship is supplied via operation path parameters or parent DTOs.

The entity is treated as a subsidiary snapshot resource: it preserves exactly what the customer or operator entered at the time of checkout or later administrative correction, even if the customer subsequently changes their profile address.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this order address snapshot record, corresponding to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_order_addresses` table.

This value is generated and managed exclusively by the backend or database layer and is never accepted from client request payloads. It is used to uniquely reference the snapshot in read operations and to ensure immutability of historical address records.

address_type.description:
Business role of this address snapshot for the order, such as `shipping` or `billing`.

Downstream fulfillment, invoicing, and taxation logic use this value to determine how the address should be interpreted. The underlying Prisma model typically constrains this column to a small set of allowed values, and a unique index ensures that at most one snapshot exists per (order, address_type) combination.

recipient_name.description:
Full name of the person or organization that will receive the shipment or invoice at this address.

The value is stored denormalized in the `shopping_mall_order_addresses` table to preserve the exact recipient name used at checkout, even if the customer later changes their profile information. Carriers, packing slips, and invoices rely on this snapshot for historical accuracy.

phone_number.description:
Contact phone number associated with this order address snapshot.

Carriers and support staff may rely on this number to resolve delivery issues, verify directions, or coordinate handoff with the recipient. It reflects the phone number as supplied at checkout time rather than any later profile updates.

country_code.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for this order address snapshot (for example, `US`, `KR`, or `JP`).

This field is critical for selecting applicable shipping methods, tax rules, customs handling, and localized address validation. The value is stored as entered or normalized at the time of order creation and is not automatically synchronized with subsequent profile changes.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code component of this order address snapshot.

The value must be suitable for the destination country or region so that carriers can route the shipment successfully. It is preserved exactly as captured at checkout to support auditing and to reproduce historical shipping labels when necessary.

region.description:
Region, state, or province component of the order address snapshot.

Combined with `city` and `postal_code`, this field helps define the full locality for routing, taxation, and compliance checks. The semantics of this field vary by country but are stored as free text corresponding to what was provided at checkout.

city.description:
City, locality, or municipality portion of the order address snapshot.

This text is used together with `region`, `postal_code`, and `country_code` to locate the destination and is preserved to ensure that historical shipping records remain reconstructable even if addressing standards change over time.

street_line1.description:
Primary street address line of this order address snapshot, typically including building number and street name.

This is the minimum address detail required for last‑mile delivery and routing. It is stored as free text as entered during checkout and may be validated for length or format constraints according to regional requirements.

street_line2.description:
Secondary street address line of this order address snapshot, commonly used for apartment, suite, floor, or building information.

Although optional in the underlying Prisma model, when present it provides additional routing and delivery context. The value is preserved exactly as provided to avoid ambiguity when reconstructing labels or resolving delivery disputes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this order address snapshot record was first created in `shopping_mall_order_addresses`.

The value is managed by the backend or database layer and is used to audit when the address snapshot became part of the order history. Clients never control or override this field in request payloads.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this order address snapshot record was last updated.

This field is maintained by the backend to reflect administrative corrections or system-driven normalizations applied after initial creation. It helps support audit trails and change history for address data associated with orders.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this address snapshot, or `null` when the record is considered active.

When populated, this field indicates that the snapshot has been logically removed from standard views while preserving it for audit, compliance, or forensic purposes. Client APIs should treat non-null values as indicating that the snapshot is no longer part of the active order surface.

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for capturing an order address snapshot at checkout time in the shoppingMall platform.

This type mirrors the mutable business fields of the shopping_mall_order_addresses model that a client must provide when creating a new address snapshot for a given order. It intentionally excludes system-managed identifiers and timestamps, as well as the foreign key to the parent order, which is supplied via the orderId path parameter.

The DTO is used in POST /shoppingMall/orders/{orderId}/addresses and supports both shipping and billing address snapshots depending on the address_type field. It preserves exactly what the customer or operator entered at the moment of checkout so that subsequent changes to a customer address book do not alter historical orders.

address_type.description:
Logical role of this address for the order, such as shipping or billing.

The value is used by downstream fulfillment, invoicing, and taxation logic to determine how this snapshot should be interpreted. Business rules and unique constraints in the shopping_mall_order_addresses model ensure that at most one snapshot exists per (order, address_type) combination.

recipient_name.description:
Recipient name for the order address snapshot.

This is the human-readable name that carriers and fulfillment partners will use on labels and packing slips. It is stored denormalized so that later changes to customer profile names do not affect this historical order.

street_line1.description:
Primary street address line for the order address snapshot.

Typically contains house number and street name or equivalent required information for last-mile delivery in the target country or region.

street_line2.description:
Optional secondary street address line for the order address snapshot.

Can include apartment, suite, building, floor, or any additional detail needed to reach the recipient. When omitted, the address is considered complete with street_line1 alone.

city.description:
City or locality component of the address at the time of order creation.

This value is captured as free-form text according to what the customer or operator entered, and it is not automatically synchronized with any later profile changes.

region.description:
Region, state, or province component of the order address snapshot.

Used together with city and postal_code to ensure correct routing for carriers and taxation engines. The exact naming convention depends on the country but is stored as plain text in this snapshot.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code associated with this order address snapshot.

Must be provided in a format acceptable for the target country or region to enable successful delivery. Validation logic may enforce pattern checks depending on deployment requirements.

country_code.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the order address snapshot.

Examples include "KR" for South Korea and "US" for the United States. This field is critical for selecting appropriate shipping options, tax logic, and carrier integrations.

phone_number.description:
Optional contact phone number associated with this order address snapshot.

Carriers and support staff may use this value to contact the recipient regarding delivery issues. When null or omitted, the order will not have a dedicated phone contact on this snapshot and may fall back to other contact information.

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing order address snapshot in the shoppingMall platform.

This type corresponds to mutable fields of the shopping_mall_order_addresses model that can be corrected after the original snapshot was created. It is used by administrative or backoffice flows, such as PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/orders/{orderId}/addresses/{orderAddressId}, to fix typos or adjust non-structural address details before fulfillment.

The DTO excludes the primary key, foreign key to shopping_mall_orders, and all system timestamps, which are managed exclusively by the backend. All fields are optional, enabling partial updates that change only the supplied properties while leaving other snapshot values intact.

address_type.description:
Updated logical role of this address for the order, such as shipping or billing.

Changing this may affect how the order is interpreted by fulfillment, invoicing, and taxation flows. Implementations should enforce any business rules or uniqueness constraints when the address_type is modified.

recipient_name.description:
Updated recipient name for the order address snapshot.

Use this to correct spelling or reflect a more accurate contact name while preserving the association with the original order.

street_line1.description:
Updated primary street address line for the order address snapshot.

Typically adjusted when a user or admin corrects an error in the house number or street name after the order was placed but before shipment.

street_line2.description:
Updated secondary street address line for the order address snapshot.

Can be set, changed, or cleared to refine apartment, suite, building, or floor information to help carriers complete delivery successfully.

city.description:
Updated city or locality component of the order address snapshot.

Used together with region and postal_code to determine delivery routing. This update should remain consistent with the target country’s addressing standards.

region.description:
Updated region, state, or province component of the order address snapshot.

Adjust this value when necessary to align with carrier or tax region conventions for the destination country.

postal_code.description:
Updated postal or ZIP code for the order address snapshot.

Should follow the correct format for the target country or region and be validated accordingly to avoid delivery failures.

country_code.description:
Updated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the order address snapshot.

Use with caution, as changing the destination country may have significant implications for shipping, customs, and tax handling. Implementations should enforce any related business constraints when this field is modified.

phone_number.description:
Updated contact phone number associated with this order address snapshot.

Can be set, changed, or cleared to help carriers or support staff reach the recipient regarding delivery and fulfillment questions.

IShoppingMallOrderLine.IRequest.description:
Filter, search, and pagination criteria for listing order line items that belong to a specific shopping_mall_orders record.

This DTO is used as the request body for PATCH /shoppingMall/*/orders/{orderId}/lines operations. It never includes the parent order identifier itself because that is provided exclusively by the path parameter `orderId`. The criteria defined here are applied only within the scope of that parent order.

page.description: 1-based page index for paginated order line search results. If omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of order line records to return in a single page. The backend may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

search.description: Free-text search keyword applied primarily to `product_name_snapshot` and possibly other textual snapshot fields of order lines within the scoped order.

line_statuses.description: Optional list of order line statuses to filter by. When provided, only lines whose `line_status` is included in this list are returned.

items.description: Single order line status value. The concrete enum values must align with the `line_status` column enum of the `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model.

created_from.description: Lower bound (inclusive) for filtering order lines by their `created_at` timestamp. Only lines created at or after this timestamp are included.

created_to.description: Upper bound (inclusive) for filtering order lines by their `created_at` timestamp. Only lines created at or before this timestamp are included.

order_by.description: Field name to sort results by. Typical values include `created_at`, `product_name_snapshot`, or `line_status`. Must map to a sortable column in `shopping_mall_order_lines`.

order_direction.description: Sort direction for the specified `order_by` field. Common values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending. The backend must validate and normalize this value.

IShoppingMallOrderLine.description:
Detailed representation of a single record from the `shopping_mall_order_lines` table.

This DTO is returned by GET /shoppingMall/*/orders/{orderId}/lines/{orderLineId} and by create/update operations on order lines. It exposes the snapshot view of the product and SKU at the time of ordering, quantitative details such as quantity and monetary amounts, and the current line status, while remaining consistent with the underlying Prisma model.

In addition to scalar snapshot fields, this type also exposes association summaries for the seller segment, seller, product, and SKU so that clients can render fully contextual order-line views without issuing additional lookup requests.

Foreign key identifiers to the parent order and related catalog entities are retained as IDs to avoid circular references, while contextual BELONGS-TO relations are transformed into `.ISummary` objects for rich but bounded context.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order line record, mapped from `shopping_mall_order_lines.id`.

This value is stable for the lifetime of the record and is used as the primary key when referencing a specific order line across APIs and internal services.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the parent order from the `shopping_mall_orders` table.

This value is always consistent with the `orderId` path parameter used to scope the line in API operations and is kept as a raw ID to avoid circular references between orders and their lines.

shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id.description:
Identifier of the seller-specific order segment that this line belongs to, mapped from `shopping_mall_order_lines.shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id`.

When the platform splits a multi-seller order into per-seller segments, this field links the line to the corresponding `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` record. For single-seller orders or scenarios where segmentation is not applied, this field can be null in the database and omitted from the DTO, indicating that the line is not associated with a distinct seller segment snapshot.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller that owns and fulfills this order line, mapped from `shopping_mall_order_lines.shopping_mall_seller_id`.

This is the raw foreign key pointing to `shopping_mall_seller.id` and is always present for active records. It provides a stable join key for internal services and analytics, while the richer `seller` summary object exposes human-friendly store information to clients.

shopping_mall_product_id.description:
Identifier of the catalog product from which this order line originates, mapped from `shopping_mall_order_lines.shopping_mall_product_id`.

This raw foreign key points to `shopping_mall_products.id` and is used for internal joins, reporting, and reconciliation. It complements the `product` summary object, which provides lightweight title and branding information for user interfaces.

shopping_mall_product_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the concrete SKU variant purchased in this line, mapped from `shopping_mall_order_lines.shopping_mall_product_sku_id`.

This value points to `shopping_mall_product_skus.id` and is the canonical link between the order line and inventory, pricing, and variant-level catalog data. It complements the `sku` summary object, which exposes a compact representation of the purchased variant for order detail views.

order_seller_segment.description:
Summary representation of the seller-specific segment that this order line belongs to.

This association references the per-seller order segment entity (mapped from `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments`) and provides enough context for clients to understand which seller segment is responsible for this portion of the order without requiring an extra lookup.

seller.description:
Summary representation of the seller responsible for fulfilling this order line.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key in the underlying table and exposes key seller attributes through `IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary`, enabling clients to show seller identity and branding alongside the line item.

product.description:
Summary representation of the catalog product from which this order line was created.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key and uses `IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary` to provide lightweight product context such as title and branding suitable for order detail views.

sku.description:
Summary representation of the specific SKU variant purchased in this order line.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` foreign key and uses `IShoppingMallProductSku.ISummary` to expose key variant attributes (such as code and option selections) without requiring an additional API call.

product_name_snapshot.description:
Product display name snapshot captured at the time the order line was created.

This value remains stable even if the underlying catalog product name changes later, ensuring historical order views remain consistent with what the customer originally saw during checkout.

sku_code_snapshot.description:
SKU code snapshot captured at the time of ordering.

The stored value preserves the exact variant code used during checkout, independent of later catalog changes, and is useful for audit, support, and reconciliation workflows.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the SKU represented by this line.

Quantity must be a positive integer and is validated against inventory and fulfillment rules. Business logic uses this value together with the unit price and discounts to compute monetary totals and fulfillment workloads.

unit_price_amount.description:
Unit price amount for a single SKU unit at the time of ordering, expressed in the order’s currency.

This value is a snapshot and should not change after order confirmation except through administrative corrections. It is used as the baseline for all subsequent monetary calculations on this line.

discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied to this line across all units.

This value may aggregate multiple discount sources, including coupons, campaigns, and price overrides. The field is stored as a snapshot to reflect the effective discount at the time the line was created or last adjusted.

tax_amount.description:
Total tax amount applied to this line across all units.

The tax amount reflects applicable tax rules at the time of ordering and is stored as a snapshot. It may be influenced by region, product tax category, and customer tax status.

line_total_amount.description:
Final total amount charged for this line after quantity, discounts, and taxes are applied.

The typical calculation is `quantity * unit_price_amount - discount_amount + tax_amount`, although the exact formula should align with the business rules applied by the pricing and taxation components.

line_status.description:
Current business status of the order line.

Typical values include states such as `pending`, `confirmed`, `fulfilled`, `cancelled`, or `returned`, and must align with the enum defined for `line_status` in the `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model. Downstream systems and UIs rely on this value to drive workflows and display the line’s lifecycle state.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order line was initially created.

The value is recorded at insertion time in the `shopping_mall_order_lines` table and is used for chronological sorting, auditing, and analytics on line creation patterns.

updated_at.description:
