Timestamp when this order line was last updated.

This value changes whenever mutable attributes such as quantity, discounts, or status are modified. It is used for change tracking, synchronization, and audit purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this order line, mapped from `shopping_mall_order_lines.deleted_at`.

When this value is non-null in the database, the line is considered logically deleted and should be excluded from normal customer-facing views and most operational workflows. Retaining the timestamp in analytics and administrative APIs allows auditors and support staff to trace when and why a line was removed from active consideration.

IShoppingMallOrderLine.ICreate.description:
Payload schema for creating a new order line (shopping_mall_order_lines) under an existing order.

Used as the request body for POST /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderId}/lines and POST /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/orders/{orderId}/lines. The parent orderId is provided as a path parameter and must NOT be duplicated in this DTO.

This DTO captures the SKU being purchased, the quantity, and the key pricing snapshot fields that need to be persisted on the line at creation time. It also allows associating the line to a seller segment when the order is multi-seller. Actor identity (customer or platformAdmin) is taken from authentication context and is never part of this DTO.

sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU being purchased, referencing `shopping_mall_product_skus.id`.

The SKU must be active and sellable in the context of the parent order (region, channel, and visibility rules). This field is required and is the core reference for inventory, pricing, and fulfillment rules applied to the line.

order_seller_segment_id.description:
Identifier of the seller segment record in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` that this line should belong to when the platform splits a single customer order into per-seller segments.

For multi-seller orders, this value binds the new line to the appropriate seller segment so that fulfillment, pricing, and payouts are correctly scoped. For single-seller orders or flows where segmentation has not been applied, this property may be omitted, in which case the backend will either infer the segment or leave the underlying `shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id` column null according to business rules.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the SKU to be purchased in this line.

Must be a positive integer. Business logic will validate the quantity against available inventory and backorder/preorder policies defined on inventory-related tables.

unit_price.description:
Unit price for the SKU at the time of order line creation.

This is a snapshot of the effective unit price (before tax and discounts) that should be used for this line when calculating totals. The value must be consistent with the pricing rules applied for the order’s region, channel, and any active promotions.

unit_tax_amount.description:
Tax amount per single unit of the SKU for this line.

Represents the tax portion of the price on a per-unit basis at the time of creation. This is stored as a snapshot to preserve historical correctness even if tax rules change later.

unit_discount_amount.description:
Discount amount per single unit of the SKU for this line, if any.

Represents the per-unit discount derived from coupons, promotions, or negotiated pricing. A value of 0 indicates no discount. This snapshot is used when computing line-level totals and reporting.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., "USD", "KRW") representing the currency for all monetary values stored on this line.

Must match the currency context of the parent order. The backend may normalize or validate this against allowed currencies for the shopping mall.

display_name.description:
Human-readable display name of the item at the time of order line creation.

Typically corresponds to the product title and selected variant descriptors. Stored as a snapshot so that order history remains stable even if the product name changes later.

display_image_url.description:
URL of the primary image to display for this order line.

The image should already be hosted on a CDN or file server; only the URL is stored. This is a snapshot field to ensure consistent order history display even if catalog media changes.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes associated with this order line.

May be used to capture customer-facing or internal notes about the item. Business rules may constrain whether this is visible to customers, sellers, or admins.

IShoppingMallOrderLine.IUpdate.description:
Payload schema for updating an existing order line (`shopping_mall_order_lines`) under a specific order.

This DTO is used as the request body for:
- `PUT /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderId}/lines/{orderLineId}`
- `PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/orders/{orderId}/lines/{orderLineId}`

It represents a partial update: all properties are optional, and the backend updates only the columns corresponding to the fields that are present in the payload. Immutable identifiers such as the parent order reference, seller and product foreign keys, and system-managed timestamps are never exposed here.

Business rules and the current fulfillment and inventory state determine at runtime which fields may actually be changed. For example, certain monetary or status adjustments may be permitted only for platform administrators or for lines that have not yet been fully fulfilled.

quantity.description:
Updated quantity of the SKU purchased in this line.

This property maps directly to the `quantity` column of the `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model. When supplied, the backend must validate the new value against existing fulfillments and inventory reservations.

Updates that would reduce the quantity below the number of units already shipped or otherwise reserved must be rejected, and systems may also enforce upper limits based on available stock and order status.

unit_price.description:
Updated unit price for a single SKU unit in this order line.

Although this field is named `unit_price` in the update DTO for readability, it conceptually maps to the `unit_price_amount` column in the `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model and aligns with the `unit_price_amount` property exposed in `IShoppingMallOrderLine`.

Providing a value here is typically restricted to administrative or support workflows where a pricing correction is required. When present, the backend should recompute any dependent monetary aggregates for the line (including `line_total_amount`) and, where policy allows, propagate adjustments to related order and seller-segment totals.

unit_tax_amount.description:
Updated per-unit tax amount for this order line.

This field represents a per-unit view of tax used for correction workflows and is ultimately reconciled against the `tax_amount` column in `shopping_mall_order_lines`, which stores the total tax across all units in the line.

When supplied, the backend is expected to translate this per-unit amount into a new total tax amount (for example, `quantity * unit_tax_amount`) and update the `tax_amount` column accordingly, while ensuring the change is consistent with tax rules and order status.

unit_discount_amount.description:
Updated per-unit discount amount for this order line.

While the Prisma model stores the aggregate discount in the `discount_amount` column on `shopping_mall_order_lines`, this update field expresses the adjustment in per-unit terms. When provided, the backend should recompute the line-level `discount_amount` (for example, `quantity * unit_discount_amount`) and persist the result.

A value of `0` removes discounts from the line; when this property is omitted, the existing stored discount amount is left unchanged.

currency_code.description:
Updated ISO 4217 currency code associated with monetary amounts on this line.

The `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model typically relies on the parent order’s `currency_code` stored in `shopping_mall_orders`, and many installations will not allow the line-level currency to diverge from that order-level setting.

This field therefore exists for advanced or specialized installations that persist per-line currency metadata. Most implementations will either reject changes that conflict with the order’s currency or ignore this field, favoring the order-level currency context instead.

display_name.description:
Updated product display name snapshot stored on this line.

This field corresponds conceptually to the `product_name_snapshot` column of the `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model and the `product_name_snapshot` property on `IShoppingMallOrderLine`. It is intended for rare corrections of historical display data—for example, fixing a typo that was captured when the order was placed.

Because snapshots are used for audit and customer history, changes to this field should be carefully controlled and typically limited to administrative tooling.

display_image_url.description:
Updated URL of the primary image to be used when rendering this order line in client applications.

The core `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma excerpt does not define an explicit image column; this property is intended to be stored in auxiliary metadata associated with the line (for example, a JSON metadata column or a linked media record) according to the installation’s data model.

The value must be a fully qualified URI pointing to a pre-uploaded image in a storage service or CDN. The backend may ignore or reject this field if per-line image overrides are not supported by the underlying schema or configuration.

notes.description:
Updated free-form notes associated with this order line.

Implementations typically map this field to a nullable text or JSON metadata column associated with the `shopping_mall_order_lines` record. It may contain internal remarks, customer-facing notes, or special handling instructions depending on business rules.

When omitted, any existing notes remain unchanged. Backends may restrict who can view or modify notes (for example, separating internal-only notes from customer-visible comments).

line_total_amount.description:
Explicitly updated final total amount for this order line after quantity, discounts, and taxes are accounted for.

This property maps to the `line_total_amount` column of the `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model and mirrors the `line_total_amount` property on `IShoppingMallOrderLine`. In most flows, `line_total_amount` is derived from `quantity`, `unit_price_amount`, `discount_amount`, and `tax_amount`, so this field should only be used in exceptional correction or reconciliation scenarios where the downstream value must be forced.

When present, the backend may validate that the supplied total is consistent with the rest of the line’s monetary fields or override those fields according to the installation’s business rules.

line_status.description:
Updated business status for this order line.

This property corresponds directly to the `line_status` column on the `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model and should use the same status vocabulary as the `line_status` property exposed in `IShoppingMallOrderLine` (for example, `pending`, `confirmed`, `fulfilled`, `cancelled`, `returned`).

Backends must enforce workflow rules for transitions. Some status changes may be restricted to administrators, and certain transitions will be blocked once related fulfillments, shipments, refunds, or disputes exist.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusEvent.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for retrieving a paginated and filterable list of order status history events for a specific order.

Used as the request body of the PATCH `/shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderId}/statusEvents` endpoint. Expresses pagination controls and optional filters such as status types, date ranges, and originator types. The `orderId` path parameter identifies the target order and MUST NOT be duplicated here.

page.description: 1-based page index to retrieve when paginating through status events. If omitted, the backend should default this to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of status events to return in a single page. If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

items.description: A high-level status code representing the resulting state of the order after this event (for example, `CREATED`, `PAID`, `SHIPPED`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, `REFUNDED`). Exact code set is defined by the business domain.

status_codes.description: Optional list of resulting order status codes to filter status events by. When provided, only events whose resulting status is one of the the given codes are returned.

items.description: Type of actor or system component that triggered the status change (for example, `customer`, `seller`, `platformAdmin`, `system`).

originator_types.description: Optional list of originator types to filter status events by. When provided, only events whose originator type matches one of the given values are returned.

from_timestamp.description: Lower bound (inclusive) for the event effective timestamp in ISO 8601 `date-time` format. When provided, only events occurring at or after this timestamp are included. Use `null` or omit to leave this bound open.

to_timestamp.description: Upper bound (inclusive) for the event effective timestamp in ISO 8601 `date-time` format. When provided, only events occurring at or before this timestamp are included. Use `null` or omit to leave this bound open.

oneOf.description: Direction in which to sort status events by their effective timestamp. `asc` sorts from oldest to newest, `desc` sorts from newest to oldest. If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default (typically `desc`).

Direction in which to sort status events by their effective timestamp. `asc` sorts from oldest to newest, `desc` sorts from newest to oldest. If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default (typically `desc`).

sort_direction.description: Direction in which to sort status events by their effective timestamp. `asc` sorts from oldest to newest, `desc` sorts from newest to oldest. If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default (typically `desc`).

IShoppingMallOrderStatusEvent.description:
Detailed representation of a single order status transition event from the `shopping_mall_order_status_events` table.

Returned by the `GET /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/orders/{orderId}/statusEvents/{statusEventId}` endpoint. Captures how the order's high-level status changed at a specific time, including the previous and new status values, originator information, and any human-readable codes or messages that describe the reason for the transition. The `orderId` and `statusEventId` path parameters identify the parent order and the specific event record; they MUST NOT be duplicated as separate properties here.

This DTO is intended primarily for administrative or support tooling where full detail about the transition is required, including internal notes and actor identifiers.

id.description: Unique identifier of this status event within the `shopping_mall_order_status_events` table.

order_id.description:
Identifier of the parent order to which this status event belongs.

This value maps directly to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_orders` table and is the foreign key that links a status event back to its owning order. It MUST always match the `orderId` path parameter used to retrieve this record via the status-events endpoint.

Consumers can use `order_id` to correlate this event with other order-related resources such as order summaries, line items, payments, and cancellations, without embedding a full order object and creating circular references in the API schema.

occurred_at.description: Timestamp when this status transition became effective, in ISO 8601 `date-time` format. Used for ordering events chronologically.

previous_status_code.description: High-level status code representing the order's state before this transition occurred (for example, `PENDING_PAYMENT`, `PAID`, `SHIPPED`). May be `null` when this event represents the initial creation of the order.

new_status_code.description: High-level status code representing the order's state after this transition (for example, `PAID`, `SHIPPED`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`, `REFUNDED`).

originator_type.description: Type of actor or system component that triggered this status transition (for example, `customer`, `seller`, `platformAdmin`, `system`).

originator_id.description: Identifier of the actor or system component that triggered this transition, when applicable. For human actors this typically references an internal ID for a customer, seller, or administrator. May be `null` for purely automated or system-wide events where no specific principal is recorded.

reason_code.description: Optional machine-readable code indicating the reason for this status change (for example, `PAYMENT_CAPTURED`, `CUSTOMER_REQUESTED_CANCELLATION`, `SELLER_CONFIRMED_SHIPMENT`). May be `null` when no specific reason code is stored.

reason_message.description: Optional human-readable description explaining why this status change occurred. Intended for administrative and support tooling; may contain internal operational notes.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationRequest.description:
Order cancellation request entity for the shoppingMall platform.

Represents a single cancellation request raised against an order or optionally a specific order line, regardless of whether the actor is a customer, seller, or platform administrator. It is the canonical record for the intent and lifecycle of cancelling all or part of an order.

The entity maintains references to the parent order and, when applicable, to the affected order line, along with business fields such as actor type, reason categorization, detailed explanation, status, and resolution information. Timestamps capture when the request was created, last updated, and when it reached a terminal resolution state.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cancellation request.

This value maps directly to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests` table and is used as the stable identifier in all read, update, and workflow operations.

order.description:
Parent order associated with this cancellation request.

This is a belongs-to reference to the `shopping_mall_orders` entity, presented as a summary view for context in cancellation detail screens and administrative tools.

oneOf.description: Null when the cancellation request targets the entire order rather than a specific line.

orderLine.description:
Optional order line targeted by this cancellation request.

When present, this references a specific line within the parent order, enabling line-level cancellation scenarios. When null, the request applies at the whole-order level.

actor_type.description:
Actor type that initiated this cancellation request.

Typical values distinguish between customers, sellers, and platform administrators (for example, `customer`, `seller`, `platformAdmin`). The exact vocabulary is constrained by business rules and used to decide which subtype table (customer or seller) holds actor-specific context.

request_reason_category.description:
Machine-readable category of the cancellation reason.

Examples include `changed_mind`, `ordered_by_mistake`, `stock_issue`, or `policy_violation`. This field supports analytics, reporting, and policy enforcement around cancellation behaviors.

request_reason_detail.description:
Free-text explanation of why the cancellation is being requested.

Typically authored by the initiating actor to provide additional detail beyond the structured `request_reason_category`. May be null when only categorical information is provided.

request_status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the cancellation request.

Common statuses include values such as `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `cancelled_by_actor`. Business workflows transition this status over time based on decisions and policy evaluation.

resolution_category.description:
Machine-readable category describing how the request was resolved.

Examples include `auto_approved`, `seller_approved`, `admin_override`, or `rejected_policy`. Null while the request is still in a non-terminal state such as `pending`.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request reached a terminal state.

This is set when the request is approved, rejected, or cancelled by the actor, and remains null while the request is still in progress.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation request record was created.

Recorded at insertion time into `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests` and used for ordering, auditing, and time-based filtering.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation request record was last updated.

Updated whenever mutable fields such as `request_reason_category`, `request_reason_detail`, `request_status`, or `resolution_category` are changed by business workflows.

oneOf.description: Null when the cancellation request was not initiated by a customer actor.

customer.description:
Customer who initiated this cancellation request, if applicable.

This summary view is populated when the actor type indicates a customer and a corresponding `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_customers` record exists.

oneOf.description: Null when the cancellation request originates from a non-customer actor or when no session was recorded.

customerSession.description:
Customer session used when submitting the request, if applicable.

Provides audit trail context such as connection metadata and device information tied to the cancellation event.

oneOf.description: Null when the cancellation request was not initiated by a seller actor.

seller.description:
Seller who initiated this cancellation request, if applicable.

This is populated when the actor is a seller and a corresponding `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_sellers` record exists, giving operators context about which merchant requested the change.

oneOf.description: Null when the cancellation request either did not originate from a seller or when no seller session record is associated.

sellerSession.description:
Seller session used when submitting the request, if applicable.

Captures seller-side authentication context for audits and risk analysis when a seller initiates the cancellation request.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationRequest.IR.description:
Search and filter request for listing order cancellation requests associated with a specific order.

Used by administrative tooling to query the `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests` table with rich criteria, including status filters, actor type, date ranges, and pagination settings. The results are scoped to a parent order via the path parameter and are returned as paginated summaries.

This DTO is read-only and does not correspond directly to a Prisma model. Instead, it expresses how clients can shape queries when invoking the cancellation request index endpoint.

page.description:
1-based index of the results page to retrieve.

Used together with `limit` to paginate through the list of cancellation requests. Defaults are applied by the server when omitted.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to include in a single page of results.

Typical values are constrained by platform-wide pagination limits to protect performance and prevent excessively large responses.

request_statuses.description:
Optional list of cancellation request statuses to filter by.

When provided, only requests whose `request_status` is included in this list are returned. When omitted, requests of any status may be included, subject to other filters.

actor_types.description:
Optional list of actor types to include in the search.

Each value should match the string stored in the `actor_type` column (for example, `customer`, `seller`, `platformAdmin`). Requests belonging to actors whose type is not in the list are excluded.

hasLineScope.description:
Flag indicating whether to restrict results based on line-level scope.

When `true`, only cancellation requests that target a specific `shopping_mall_order_lines` record are returned. When `false`, only order-level cancellations are returned. When null or omitted, both scopes are included.

created_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the creation timestamp window for filtering.

When provided together with `created_to`, limits results to requests whose `created_at` falls within the specified range.

created_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the creation timestamp window for filtering.

Used in combination with `created_from` to constrain search results to a specific time period.

sort_by.description:
Field name used to sort the results.

Common sort keys include `created_at`, `request_status`, or `resolved_at`. The actual set of supported values is enforced at the service layer.

sort_direction.description:
Direction in which to sort results.

Typically `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending ordering. When omitted, the service applies a sensible default, usually newest-first ordering.

IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary of a customer-facing order in the shopping mall platform.

Used in order list views such as "My Orders" and administrative overviews where only high-level details are required. This summary focuses on identifiers, status, pricing, and a compact representation of the primary items.

id.description: Unique identifier of the order at the customer level.

order_number.description: Human-friendly order number or code presented to customers in emails and order history pages.

customer.description: Summary information of the customer who placed the order. Provided as a reference object for administrative UIs; for customer-facing views this will typically refer to the current actor.

placed_at.description: Timestamp when the order was successfully placed, in ISO 8601 format.

status.description: High-level lifecycle status of the order (for example, pending, paid, fulfilled, cancelled). Concrete values are constrained at the application layer.

payment_status.description: Aggregated payment status for the order across all related payment transactions (for example, pending, paid, partially_refunded, refunded).

total_amount.description: Total monetary amount for the order including items, taxes, and shipping fees as visible to the customer.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code used for the order totals, such as "USD" or "KRW".

item_count.description: Total count of distinct line items across the order, aggregated from all seller segments and order lines.

thumbnail_items.description: Small subset of representative items from the order, used to render quick previews in order list views without loading the full order graph.

IShoppingMallOrderLine.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single order line within a shopping mall order.

This summary DTO is designed as a projection of the underlying `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model, focusing on fields needed to display line items in lists and order overviews. It keeps hierarchical parent identifiers as raw IDs while exposing contextual associations (seller, product, SKU) as summary objects.

From a business perspective, the schema exposes non-sensitive commercial information required to understand what was purchased in an order, at what price, and with which basic status. It intentionally omits any authentication secrets or actor identity fields beyond technical foreign keys, ensuring there is no risk of password or token leakage.

The type is primarily used in list views and embedded contexts, where consumers need a compact representation of order lines enriched with seller and catalog context, without requiring full relational expansion or separate lookups.

id.description:
Primary key of the order line record.

This UUID uniquely identifies a single row in the `shopping_mall_order_lines` table and is used to reference the line item from related entities, logs, and administrative tools.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent order.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_orders.id` and groups multiple line items under a single customer-facing order. It is kept as a raw ID because the parent order typically contains the lines array, and returning a full order object here would create a circular reference.

shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the seller-specific segment of the order.

In multi-seller scenarios, a single customer order can be split into several seller segments. This column links the line item to its segment record in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments`, which represents the portion of the order that a single seller is responsible for fulfilling.

seller.description:
Seller summary for the merchant that owns and fulfills this line item.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key exposed in read DTOs, providing immediate access to key seller display information (such as name and basic reputation) without requiring additional lookups.

product.description:
Product summary for the catalog product purchased on this line.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key in read responses, giving consumers direct access to core product display attributes (such as name and brand) suitable for rendering order details and analytics views.

sku.description:
SKU summary for the specific variant purchased on this line.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` foreign key in read responses and provides variant-level context (such as option selections or SKU code) needed to clearly identify what exact variant was ordered.

product_name_snapshot.description:
Snapshot of the product name at the time of ordering.

The system stores this value so that historical lines remain stable even if the product name is later edited in the catalog. This protects auditability and ensures customers and administrators see the name that was actually displayed at purchase time.

sku_code_snapshot.description:
Snapshot of the SKU code at the time of ordering.

This value preserves the seller-facing or internal SKU identifier used when the order was created. It is critical for reconciliation with external systems and for long-term analytics, even if catalog SKU metadata is later changed.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the SKU purchased in this line.

The value represents the quantity ordered, not necessarily the quantity shipped or returned. Fulfillment and after-sales flows can derive shipped or refunded quantities based on related tables, while this column remains the canonical ordered quantity.

unit_price_amount.description:
Per-unit price of the SKU at the time of order creation.

The amount is stored in the order currency and excludes discounts and taxes. Combined with `quantity`, `discount_amount`, and `tax_amount`, it allows the platform to reconstruct financial calculations without exposing any payment credentials.

discount_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied to this line across all units.

This value aggregates promotions, coupons, and manual adjustments applied specifically to this line item. It is used purely for financial calculation and reporting and does not contain any secret or token data.

tax_amount.description:
Total tax amount applied to this order line.

The platform uses this value for tax reporting, customer-visible breakdowns, and settlement. It represents the sum of tax charges for all units in this line in the order currency.

line_total_amount.description:
Final total amount charged for this line after discounts and taxes.

This is the authoritative monetary value for the line in the order currency and is used by financial reporting, settlement engines, and refund flows. It does not encode any authentication or session information.

line_status.description:
Current operational status of the order line.

Typical values include high-level states such as `pending`, `fulfilled`, `cancelled`, or `returned`, depending on the configured business workflow. This status guides fulfillment and customer service processes but does not grant any access rights by itself.

created_at.description:
Creation timestamp of the order line record.

Stored in ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC, this timestamp marks when the line was initially written to the database and is used for timelines, analytics, and auditing.

updated_at.description:
Last update timestamp of the order line record.

Also stored in ISO 8601 UTC format, this field is updated whenever mutable attributes of the order line change, providing a simple audit signal for operational tooling and reporting.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the order line, if applicable.

When this field is non-null in the underlying database, the line is considered logically deleted and should be excluded from normal user-facing queries, while remaining available for compliance, audit, and historical analysis.

IShoppingMallCustomerSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a customer authentication session in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is a direct projection of the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` Prisma model, trimmed for list and admin views. It exposes only benign connection metadata and timing information required for monitoring and analytics: it does **not** include any passwords, password hashes, salts, refresh tokens, or bearer tokens.

The parent customer context is always supplied via the endpoint path (for example, `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/customers/{customerId}/sessions`), so this summary does not redundantly repeat the customer identifier. Instead, it focuses on per-session identifiers and lifecycle fields used for security analysis and support workflows.

id.description:
Primary key of the customer session record.

This UUID uniquely identifies a single authenticated session row in the `shopping_mall_customer_sessions` table and is used to look up or correlate session-related security events.

ip.description:
IP address captured when the session was established.

This IP value is recorded from the incoming HTTP request at login or session creation time. It is used for security analytics, anomaly detection, fraud investigation, and compliance reporting, but does not by itself grant access to the system.

href.description:
URL or path that initiated the authenticated session.

Typically this is the login page URL or application route where the authentication flow completed. It helps correlate sessions with campaigns, entry points, and security-relevant flows without containing any password or token information.

referrer.description:
Referring URL when the session was created.

This field is used to trace the external or internal source of the login, such as marketing campaigns, partner sites, or internal redirects. It supports both business analytics and security investigations into unusual login patterns.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the customer session record was created.

Recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC, this marks the exact point at which authentication succeeded and the session was persisted.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expired or was explicitly terminated.

When null in the underlying database, the session is considered active; when set, it indicates the logical end of the session for authorization decisions and auditing. This field does not store any credential material—only lifecycle timing information.

IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a shopping mall seller account mapped to the `shopping_mall_seller` Prisma model.

This summary is optimized for list displays and reference embedding in other entities, exposing only stable identification and lifecycle fields that are safe to show in administrative or semi-public contexts. Sensitive authentication details remain in dedicated credential entities.

The fields included here are direct projections of the underlying Prisma columns `id`, `email`, `store_name`, and `status`, ensuring that the summary accurately reflects the persisted seller record and can be joined back to the full seller entity when required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller account.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_seller` record (`id` column) and is used to join with other tables such as products, SKUs, payouts, and audit logs that reference the seller. It is generated by the platform and is immutable for the lifetime of the seller account.

email.description:
Primary business email address for the seller, mapped from the `email` column of `shopping_mall_seller`.

This address is used for operational communications such as order notifications, payout updates, and policy changes. It may be aligned with the login email stored in the credentials subsystem but is modeled separately here to reflect seller-facing contact information and for use in administrative search and filtering scenarios.

store_name.description:
Public store or brand name shown to customers when viewing products and orders from this seller, mapped from the `store_name` column of `shopping_mall_seller`.

In list views and embedded references this value is typically displayed alongside product and rating information so that customers can quickly recognize which merchant they are interacting with. It should be unique enough to distinguish sellers but may differ from legal entity names maintained in back-office systems.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the seller account, mapped from the non-nullable `status` column of `shopping_mall_seller`.

Typical values indicate whether the seller is pending onboarding, active and allowed to list products and receive orders, temporarily suspended due to policy violations or risk flags, or permanently terminated. Downstream features such as catalog visibility and order acceptance logic use this status to decide whether the seller should appear in new purchase flows.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a shopping mall seller authentication session mapped to the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` Prisma model.

This summary is intended for administrative and analytical contexts where a concise indication of session existence, ownership, and lifecycle is required without exposing full connection metadata such as IP address, entry URL, or referrer. Those details remain available in the full session DTO and underlying log tables when deeper forensics are necessary.

The summary links directly to the owning seller via `seller`, which conceptually replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_seller_id`, and surfaces the key temporal fields `created_at` and `expired_at` to distinguish active versus closed sessions.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller session record.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` row (`id` column) and can be used to retrieve the full session entity or to correlate with security events, inventory changes, and administrative audits that reference this session.

seller.description:
Belongs-to association to the seller account that owns this session.

At the database level this association is represented by the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key on `shopping_mall_seller_sessions`. In this summary DTO the low-level foreign key is replaced by a lightweight seller summary so that dashboards and logs can immediately display which merchant the session belongs to without an additional lookup.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the seller session was created, mapped from the non-nullable `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_seller_sessions`.

This moment typically corresponds to successful authentication for the seller. It is used to order sessions chronologically, to compute session age, and to correlate session creation with concurrent security events or configuration changes.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the seller session expired or was explicitly terminated, mapped from the nullable `expired_at` column of `shopping_mall_seller_sessions`.

For active sessions this column remains null at the database level and the field may be absent from the summary representation, indicating that the session is still valid. For closed sessions it records the effective end of life of the session and is used by analytics and security tooling to measure session durations and inactivity windows.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationRequest.IC.description:
Create DTO for registering a new cancellation request against a customer-facing order.

This type is used by authenticated customers, sellers, or platform administrators when they initiate an order cancellation workflow through endpoints such as `POST /shoppingMall/{actorNamespace}/orders/{orderId}/cancellationRequests`. It captures the business intent, categorised reasons, and optional free-text explanations that become the initial state of a record in `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests`.

The DTO focuses only on fields that the caller is allowed to supply explicitly. Actor identity and actor type (customer, seller, or platformAdmin) are derived exclusively from the authenticated session and the operation’s `authorizationActor` configuration, and are persisted via subtype tables such as `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_customers` and `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_sellers`. Order linkage via `shopping_mall_order_id` is derived from the `orderId` path parameter instead of being supplied in the body, preventing duplication and inconsistencies.

request_reason_category.description:
Machine-readable category describing why the cancellation is being requested.

Examples include values such as `changed_mind`, `ordered_by_mistake`, `stock_issue`, or `policy_violation`. The exact vocabulary is governed by cancellation policy configuration tables and administrative tooling.

This category enables reporting, analytics, and automatic policy evaluation when determining whether to auto-approve, reject, or escalate cancellation requests.

oneOf.description:
Non-null free-text explanation provided by the actor to clarify the cancellation intent.

This branch represents the case where the actor supplies descriptive text explaining the circumstances of the cancellation request. It is persisted directly into the `request_reason_detail` column of `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests` and may be used by support agents or automated workflows when assessing the request.

Explicit null value indicating that the actor did not provide any free-text explanation.

This branch is used when the client intentionally omits descriptive text or clears previously entered text for the `request_reason_detail` column in `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests`. The absence of detail means that only the structured reason category and other contextual data will be available to evaluators.

request_reason_detail.description:
Optional free-text explanation provided by the actor to clarify the cancellation intent.

This field may contain customer- or seller-facing text that describes specific circumstances, such as delivery scheduling conflicts, order mistakes, or fulfillment constraints. It supplements the structured `request_reason_category` field for better human understanding.

When omitted from the request body or explicitly set to null, the platform will rely solely on the categorised reason and other contextual data when evaluating the cancellation request.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationRequest.IU.description:
Update DTO for modifying mutable fields of an existing order cancellation request.

This type is used by authenticated customers, sellers, or platform administrators when they adjust non-structural aspects of a cancellation request through endpoints such as `PUT /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderId}/cancellationRequests/{cancellationRequestId}`. Typical adjustments include refining the reason category or updating free-text explanations while the request remains in a pending or under-review state.

Immutable properties of `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests`—such as the primary key, related order reference, creation timestamps, and resolution metadata—are not exposed here and cannot be altered by this DTO. Business logic and policy models determine whether the current lifecycle state of the request allows modifications.

request_reason_category.description:
Optional updated machine-readable category describing why the cancellation is being requested.

Callers may use this field to change or refine the categorised reason after initial submission, for example moving from a generic `changed_mind` category to a more precise value. The new category must still align with the configured cancellation reason vocabulary.

If omitted, the existing reason category on the cancellation request record remains unchanged.

oneOf.description:
Non-null free-text explanation representing the updated cancellation reason detail.

Use this branch when providing new descriptive text to replace or extend any previously stored explanation. The value is stored in the `request_reason_detail` column and may be shown to support staff and other actors reviewing the request.

Explicit null value indicating the caller wants to clear any existing cancellation reason detail.

When this branch is used, the corresponding `request_reason_detail` column in `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests` is set to null, effectively removing prior descriptive text and leaving only the structured reason category and contextual data.

request_reason_detail.description:
Optional updated free-text explanation for the cancellation request.

Callers can use this field to correct, expand, or clear the original explanation, subject to business rules about when modifications are permitted. Providing a non-null string replaces the existing detail, whereas explicitly sending null clears the column.

If the property is not present in the request body, the existing explanation on the record is preserved without change.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationRequestOfC.description:
Customer-specific subtype entity that links an order cancellation request to the concrete customer identity and session that created it.

This DTO mirrors the `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_customers` Prisma model and is used as a read-only response payload when inspecting the customer side of an order cancellation request under a specific order. It provides traceability for who initiated the request and in which session, and is treated as a subsidiary record attached to the main cancellation request lifecycle.

id.description:
Primary key of the customer cancellation request subtype record.

This value uniquely identifies the row in `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_customers` and is generated by the database. It is used only for lookup and internal references and is never supplied by clients in request bodies.

shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request.description:
Identifier of the master cancellation request associated with this customer subtype.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests.id` and ensures that this record is in a strict 1:1 relationship with the parent cancellation request. It is used to join customer-specific context back to the main cancellation workflow and may be useful for internal diagnostics and joins even when the `cancellationRequest` association is provided.

shopping_mall_customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer who initiated the cancellation request.

This points to `shopping_mall_customer.id` and represents the buyer account under which the cancellation was raised. It is resolved from authentication context at creation time and is primarily used for internal joins and debugging; client applications should prefer the richer `customer` association object for display and business logic.

shopping_mall_customer_session_id.description:
Identifier of the customer session that was active when the cancellation request was submitted.

This refers to `shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id` and is used for audit, risk, and security analysis. It is retained for internal join and debugging purposes even though the richer `customerSession` association object is provided for client consumption.

cancellationRequest.description:
Summary view of the master order cancellation request that this customer subtype belongs to.

This association provides contextual information such as overall status, reason codes, and creation timestamps without requiring the client to perform an additional lookup on the main cancellation request entity.

customer.description:
Summary representation of the customer who initiated this cancellation request.

This association transforms the underlying `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key into a rich actor object that can be used directly for display, auditing, and business logic, while avoiding circular references by leveraging the `.ISummary` variant.

customerSession.description:
Summary representation of the customer authentication session that was active when this cancellation request was created.

This association exposes key session-level context—such as device, IP, or login timestamps—through the `.ISummary` view of `shopping_mall_customer_sessions`, enabling risk analysis and audit workflows without additional API calls.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this customer-specific cancellation subtype record was created.

The value is stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_customers` and reflects the moment the subtype link was first persisted. It is managed exclusively by the backend and is returned in responses for timeline reconstruction.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this customer-specific cancellation subtype record was last updated.

The value is stored in the `updated_at` column of `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_customers` and changes whenever the record is modified by backend processes. It is useful for understanding the latest maintenance activity on the subtype record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this customer-specific cancellation subtype record.

When `null`, the record is considered active. When set to a concrete date-time, it indicates that the subtype record has been soft-deleted while typically keeping it available for historical analysis and audit.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationRequestOfS.description:
Seller-specific subtype entity that links an order cancellation request to the seller identity and session that created or interacted with it.

This DTO mirrors the `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_sellers` Prisma model and is used as a read-only response payload when inspecting the seller side of an order cancellation request under a specific order. It provides traceability for which seller account and session are associated with the request, supporting after-sales workflows, dispute handling, and audit requirements.

id.description:
Primary key of the seller cancellation request subtype record.

This value uniquely identifies the row in `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_sellers` and is generated by the database. It is used for lookups and internal references only and is never provided by clients in request bodies.

shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request.description:
Identifier of the master cancellation request associated with this seller subtype.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests.id` and enforces the 1:1 relationship between the seller subtype row and the main cancellation request. It is retained as a raw foreign key for internal joins and diagnostics in addition to the richer `cancellationRequest` association.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller who is associated with this cancellation request.

This links to `shopping_mall_seller.id` and represents the merchant account that initiated or is responsible for the seller-side cancellation interaction. It is mainly used internally for joins and debugging; client applications should prefer the `seller` association object for business logic and display.

shopping_mall_seller_session_id.description:
Identifier of the seller session active when the cancellation request was submitted or handled by the seller.

This refers to `shopping_mall_seller_sessions.id` and captures the authentication context for the merchant. It remains available as a raw foreign key for internal usage, while the `sellerSession` association provides a summarized session view to clients.

cancellationRequest.description:
Summary view of the master order cancellation request that this seller subtype is attached to.

This association surfaces key information about the overall cancellation workflow—such as status, scope, and high-level reason codes—without requiring an additional API call to the main cancellation request endpoint.

seller.description:
Summary representation of the seller associated with this cancellation request.

This association converts the underlying `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key into a `.ISummary` actor object, providing essential seller details for dashboards, audit trails, and after-sales workflows while preventing circular references.

sellerSession.description:
Summary representation of the seller authentication session that was active when the seller interacted with this cancellation request.

Through this association, clients can inspect key session attributes—such as login time or origin information—via the `.ISummary` view of `shopping_mall_seller_sessions` without issuing a separate lookup call.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller-specific cancellation subtype record was created.

Stored in the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_sellers`, it indicates when the subtype link between the cancellation request and seller context was initially persisted by the backend.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller-specific cancellation subtype record was last updated.

This value is stored in the `updated_at` column of `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_request_of_sellers` and changes whenever backend processes modify the record. It is exposed in responses to help operators understand the latest changes applied to the subtype.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this seller-specific cancellation subtype record.

When `null`, the subtype record is active. When set, it marks the record as logically deleted while preserving it for historical and auditing scenarios in the shoppingMall platform.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequest.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for filtering order return requests that belong to a specific customer-facing master order.

Used by customer, seller, and platformAdmin scoped endpoints to retrieve paginated lists of return requests for a given order. This DTO encapsulates paging, sorting, and filter fields that can be applied when querying `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`. It is a search request envelope and does not directly map to a single Prisma model table.

page.description:
Page number for pagination when listing order return requests.

The first page is numbered as 1. If omitted, the service may default to page 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

A reasonable upper bound such as 100 is enforced for performance and to protect the database from excessively large result sets.

request_status.description:
Optional filter for the current status of the return request, aligned with the `request_status` column in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`.

Typical values include `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `awaiting_item`, `refunded`, or `closed`, and should match the status values exposed by the return workflow domain.

actor_type.description:
Optional filter indicating which actor type initiated the return request, aligned with the `actor_type` column in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`.

Common examples include `customer` for buyer-initiated requests and other values if the system is extended to additional actor types. This filter allows role-specific views of return requests in administrative and seller dashboards.

request_reason_category.description:
Optional filter on the categorized reason for the return, aligned with the `request_reason_category` column.

Use this filter to retrieve only those return requests that match a specific standardized reason such as `defective_item`, `wrong_item`, or `changed_mind` for analytics or operational review.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound of the creation timestamp range for filtering return requests.

When provided, only requests with `created_at` greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are included in the result set.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound of the creation timestamp range for filtering return requests.

When provided, only requests with `created_at` less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are included in the result set.

order_line_id.description:
Optional filter that limits results to return requests referencing a specific order line within the parent order.

This value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_order_line_id` foreign key in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` or related line-level tables.

sortBy.description:
Field name used to sort the return requests list.

Typical values include `created_at`, `request_status`, or other sortable attributes that the implementation chooses to expose. The server validates and coerces unknown values to a safe default sort order.

oneOf.description:
Sort results in ascending order based on the selected `sortBy` field.

Commonly used in conjunction with `created_at` to show oldest return requests first.

Sort results in descending order based on the selected `sortBy` field.

Commonly used to show the most recent or most urgent return requests first.

sortDirection.description:
Sorting direction for the list of return requests.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the service applies a sensible default direction, typically `desc` on `created_at`.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequest.description:
Detailed representation of an order return request in the shoppingMall domain.

Backed primarily by the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model, which records return or refund requests initiated for delivered order items. This DTO is used in detail read operations and after-creation responses to expose the full business state of a single return request, including identifiers, linkage to the parent order, actor type, status, reason information, requested resolution, line-level breakdown, evidence attachments, and key timestamps.

Sensitive authentication and session fields are intentionally excluded from this representation. Actor identity and session context are resolved from authentication middleware and from subtype tables such as `shopping_mall_order_return_request_of_customers`.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order return request record in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`.

This value is generated by the backend and is used as the primary reference when retrieving or updating a specific return request. It maps directly to the non-nullable `id` primary key column in the Prisma model.

order.description:
Summary representation of the parent order that this return request belongs to.

This replaces the raw foreign key field `shopping_mall_order_id` and provides enough context for clients to understand which checkout and fulfillment snapshot the return request is associated with, without causing circular references or requiring a separate order lookup for common views.

actor_type.description:
Actor type that initiated the return request, mirroring the non-nullable `actor_type` column in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`.

Typical values include `customer` when the buyer initiates the request directly from their order detail page, or other actor classifications if the model is extended in the future. This field is used by business logic and reporting to distinguish who started the return flow and to enforce role-specific rules and SLAs.

request_status.description:
Current workflow status of the return request, mapped from the non-nullable `request_status` column in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`.

Typical statuses include values such as `pending`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `awaiting_item`, `refunded`, or `closed`. Service logic uses this field to determine whether the customer may still edit the request, whether sellers or administrators must take action, and how the request appears in different dashboards.

request_reason_category.description:
Categorized reason for the return, mapped directly from the non-nullable `request_reason_category` column in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`.

Common examples include `defective_item`, `wrong_item`, `not_as_described`, `size_issue`, or `changed_mind`. These codes are configured at the policy level and are used for analytics, policy enforcement, and operational reporting about why returns are initiated.

oneOf.description:
Optional free-text explanation provided by the actor, mapped from the nullable `request_reason_detail` column.

This narrative elaborates on the selected `request_reason_category` and gives sellers and administrators detailed context when evaluating the request, such as how the item was damaged or why it does not meet expectations. When not provided, reviewers rely primarily on the categorized reason and attached evidence.

request_reason_detail.description:
Optional free-text explanation provided by the actor, mapped from the nullable `request_reason_detail` column.

This narrative elaborates on the selected `request_reason_category` and gives sellers and administrators detailed context when evaluating the request, such as how the item was damaged or why it does not meet expectations. When not provided, reviewers rely primarily on the categorized reason and attached evidence.

requested_resolution.description:
Requested resolution type for the return, mapped from the non-nullable `requested_resolution` column of `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`.

Typical values include `refund`, `replacement`, or `store_credit`, and may be extended with additional types according to platform policies. While this field reflects the actor's preference, the platform may apply a different resolution category based on eligibility rules and manual decisions.

oneOf.description:
Category describing how the return request was ultimately resolved, mapped from the nullable `resolution_category` column.

Examples include `refund_issued`, `replacement_shipped`, `denied_policy`, or other internal codes used by the returns workflow. This field remains null while the request is still open or under review and becomes populated when the request reaches a final outcome.

resolution_category.description:
Category describing how the return request was ultimately resolved, mapped from the nullable `resolution_category` column.

Examples include `refund_issued`, `replacement_shipped`, `denied_policy`, or other internal codes used by the returns workflow. This field remains null while the request is still open or under review and becomes populated when the request reaches a final outcome.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the request reached a final resolution state, mapped from the nullable `resolved_at` column.

For approved or refunded requests this is typically when the refund or replacement was committed; for denied requests it reflects when the denial decision was finalized. The value is null while the request is still in progress or awaiting action.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp when the request reached a final resolution state, mapped from the nullable `resolved_at` column.

For approved or refunded requests this is typically when the refund or replacement was committed; for denied requests it reflects when the denial decision was finalized. The value is null while the request is still in progress or awaiting action.

items.description:
Line-level breakdown of the items that are part of this return request.

Each element represents a single order line from the parent order together with the quantity that the customer has requested to return. This array is created and updated transactionally with the main return request entity and is used to derive refund amounts, inventory movements, and after-sales workflows. It logically complements the `shopping_mall_order_line_id` foreign key and any dependent tables that store per-line details.

evidence_attachments.description:
Evidence attachments submitted in support of this return request, such as photos of damaged items, packaging, or receipts.

Each element represents a single immutable file reference together with basic metadata. Attachments are stored and managed as compositional children of the return request and are loaded with it for review by sellers and administrators. Files are always referenced by URL and are never transmitted as raw binary or base64 data in this DTO.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the return request was created in the system, mapped from the non-nullable `created_at` column.

This is typically the moment when the customer successfully submitted the return request API call and it was persisted in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`. It is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the last time the return request record or any of its core attributes were updated, mapped from the non-nullable `updated_at` column.

This field allows clients to detect stale data and supports operational auditing of after-sales processes. It is updated whenever key properties of the return request or its attached structures change.

oneOf.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this return request, mapped from the nullable `deleted_at` column.

When null, the return request is considered active for operational views. When populated, the record has been logically removed from normal listings but is retained for audit, compliance, or analytics purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this return request, mapped from the nullable `deleted_at` column.

When null, the return request is considered active for operational views. When populated, the record has been logically removed from normal listings but is retained for audit, compliance, or analytics purposes.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequest.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new customer-initiated order return request associated with a specific order in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO captures the customer-provided business data for starting the return workflow, including which order lines are being returned, quantities, standardized reason codes, optional free-form explanations, evidence attachment URLs, and the preferred resolution type such as refund, replacement, or store credit.

Conceptually, `reason_code` corresponds to the `request_reason_category` column on the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model, `reason_text` corresponds to the nullable `request_reason_detail` column, and `preferred_resolution_type` maps to the `requested_resolution` column. System-managed fields such as `actor_type`, `request_status`, `resolution_category`, `resolved_at`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are set by the backend and are therefore not part of this request body.

Actor identity (customer) and session context are injected by authentication middleware and MUST NOT be part of this schema. Path parameters such as `orderId` supply the foreign key to `shopping_mall_orders` and are likewise excluded from the body DTO.

reason_code.description:
Standardized reason code that classifies why the customer is requesting a return (for example, WRONG_ITEM_SENT, DAMAGED_ITEM, SIZE_MISMATCH, CHANGED_MIND).

This value maps to the `request_reason_category` column on the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model. The allowed codes are enforced by the backend using an enum or lookup table, and clients should obtain them from configuration APIs instead of hard-coding arbitrary strings.

reason_text.description:
Optional free-form explanation provided by the customer that elaborates on the selected `reason_code`.

This text maps directly to the nullable `request_reason_detail` column on the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model and can include additional context such as what was wrong with the item, how it was damaged, or any other narrative details that help sellers and administrators evaluate the request.

preferred_resolution_type.description:
Customer’s preferred resolution for this return request, such as `refund`, `replacement`, or `store_credit`.

This value is persisted in the `requested_resolution` column on the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model. The backend may normalize or override this preference according to active refund policies and seller configuration, but a non-empty value is always required from the client.

items.description:
Array describing which concrete order line items and quantities are being requested for return.

Each element corresponds to a single order line from the parent order and specifies how many units of that line the customer wants to return. The backend validates that referenced order lines belong to the order identified by the path parameter and that requested quantities do not exceed eligible delivered quantities minus any already-returned amounts. Line-level data is stored in subsidiary entities linked to the main `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` record.

evidence_attachments.description:
Optional list of evidence attachments that support the return request, such as photos of damaged items or packaging.

Each attachment is represented by an immutable, already-uploaded file URL and classification metadata. The backend does not accept raw binary content in this DTO; clients must first upload files to a storage service and then provide their URLs here. Attachment metadata is persisted in child entities associated with the main `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` record.

metadata.description:
Optional key-value metadata supplied by the client to carry additional non-authoritative hints about the context of the return request.

This structure is intended for loosely structured information such as client-side tracking IDs or UI-specific flags and is not used for critical business decisions. All keys and values are plain strings, and the server may ignore or sanitize entries that violate platform policies. This field does not map directly to a dedicated Prisma column on `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` but is stored according to the implementation’s chosen metadata strategy.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequest.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing customer-initiated order return request associated with a specific order in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO exposes only customer-editable fields for a return request that is still in an editable workflow state. It allows adjustments such as changing reasons, updating free-form explanations, modifying requested quantities within allowed limits, or attaching additional evidence files.

The fields in this schema map to the same underlying Prisma columns as the create DTO: `reason_code` to `request_reason_category`, `reason_text` to the nullable `request_reason_detail`, and `preferred_resolution_type` to `requested_resolution` on the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` model. System-managed fields such as `actor_type`, `request_status`, `resolution_category`, `resolved_at`, and timestamp columns remain controlled by seller/admin workflows or internal automation and are not exposed here.

Immutable identifiers and ownership information are taken from the path parameters and authentication context and MUST NOT be part of this schema.

reason_code.description:
Updated standardized reason code for why the customer is requesting a return.

When provided, this value replaces the existing `request_reason_category` column on the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` record, subject to validation against the allowed reason codes configured in the system.

reason_text.description:
Updated free-form explanation for the return request.

When present, this value overwrites the existing `request_reason_detail` text stored on the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` record. It should provide more accurate or detailed information that helps reviewers understand the customer’s situation.

preferred_resolution_type.description:
Updated customer preference for how this return request should be resolved (for example, refund, replacement, or store credit).

If provided, this value replaces the `requested_resolution` column on the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` record. The backend still enforces policy rules and may accept or override the preference based on business constraints.

items.description:
Optional list of item-level adjustments for the return request.

When provided, this array allows the customer to modify quantities or selection of order lines being returned, within the constraints of the current workflow stage and policy rules. Concrete interpretation (full replacement vs. partial patch semantics) is defined by the service implementation and persists changes to the subsidiary entities that represent per-line return details.

evidence_attachments.description:
Optional updates to the set of evidence attachments associated with the return request.

Depending on business rules, this may represent a complete replacement of the attachment list or an additive set of new attachments that will be merged with the existing ones. The backend persists these changes in the child entities linked to the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` record.

metadata.description:
Optional updated key-value metadata for the return request.

When present, this metadata can be used to store additional client-side context or tracking information. The server may choose to merge or replace existing metadata based on its own rules, and may ignore entries that do not conform to platform policies. This field does not map directly to a dedicated Prisma column but is handled by the implementation’s metadata storage strategy.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequestItem.ICre.description:
Nested DTO representing a single order line item entry within a new order return request.

Each instance identifies a specific order line from the parent order and the number of units the customer is requesting to return for that line. The backend validates that the referenced order line belongs to the order identified in the path, that the line is eligible for returns according to policy, and that the requested quantity does not exceed the allowed limit.

order_line_id.description:
Unique identifier of the order line in the `shopping_mall_order_lines` table that this return entry refers to.

The backend uses this value to validate ownership, eligibility, and maximum returnable quantities for the associated SKU snapshot.

quantity.description:
Number of units from the specified order line that the customer is requesting to return.

This value must be greater than zero and is subject to validation so that it does not exceed the number of delivered units minus any quantities already associated with previously approved or pending return requests for the same order line.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequestItem.IUpd.description:
Nested DTO representing customer-editable updates for a single order line entry within an existing order return request.

This DTO allows modifications such as changing the requested quantity for a specific order line, provided that the request is still in an editable state and the new quantity respects all eligibility and policy constraints.

order_line_id.description:
Identifier of the order line in `shopping_mall_order_lines` that this update entry targets.

This value is used to match the update to an existing line-level entry inside the return request. The server may interpret the absence of this field according to its patch semantics, but when present it must correspond to a valid line item for the return request.

quantity.description:
Updated number of units from the referenced order line that the customer is requesting to return.

If provided, the value must be greater than zero and within the allowable range for that order line based on delivered quantities and prior returns.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequestAttachmen.description:
Nested DTO representing a single evidence attachment associated with a new order return request.

Attachments are typically images or documents that support the customer’s claim, such as photos of damaged products or shipping labels. Files must be uploaded to a storage service ahead of time and referenced here by URL; the API never accepts raw binary or base64 data.

name.description: Human-readable name or caption for this evidence attachment, displayed to reviewers and in customer-facing UIs.

extension.description:
File extension of the attached evidence resource, such as `jpg`, `png`, or `pdf`.

This field helps consumers infer the media type and may be used for basic validation or rendering decisions.

url.description:
Public or signed URL pointing to the immutable, already-uploaded file used as evidence for this return request.

The backend treats this URL as a reference and does not manage upload or storage lifecycle within this API.

type.description:
Optional classification of the attachment within the context of the return request, such as `product_photo`, `package_photo`, or `receipt`.

Allowed values are aligned with platform-level configuration. When omitted, the server may infer or default the type based on file metadata or other heuristics.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequestAttachmen.description:
Nested DTO representing updates to a single evidence attachment associated with an existing order return request.

This structure can be used to add new attachments or modify metadata for previously attached evidence, depending on how the server interprets the update semantics for the parent `IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequest.IUpdate` payload.

name.description:
Updated human-readable name or caption for the evidence attachment.

If provided, it replaces the existing name for the targeted attachment.

extension.description:
Updated file extension value for the attachment, if its classification needs correction.

In most flows this field is rarely changed after creation.

url.description:
URL of the evidence file. When adding new attachments through an update, this field points to the already-uploaded resource.

For existing attachments, changes to this field are typically restricted or interpreted as replacement, subject to business rules.

type.description:
Updated classification for the attachment (for example, `product_photo`, `package_photo`, or `receipt`).

When provided, this value replaces the existing type metadata for the attachment.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequestCustomerV.description:
Customer-facing view of an order return request associated with a specific order in the shoppingMall platform.
