This DTO is a read-only projection over the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model together with the customer subtype table `shopping_mall_order_return_request_of_customers`. It intentionally exposes only customer-relevant information such as status, reasons, requested refund amounts, attached evidence, and key timestamps, while omitting internal-only administrative fields (for example, risk flags, internal resolution_category, or soft deletion markers) that are not appropriate for the customer view.

The structure is optimized for UI consumption in both customer portals and administrative tools: it groups core return request state, a lightweight summary of the customer and order, and per-line details describing which items from the order are included in the request. It does not mirror every underlying column 1:1, but each property is derived in a traceable way from `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`, its subtype, and related order and line entities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order return request in the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` table.

This UUID is the primary key for the return request entity and is used throughout internal services, background jobs, logs, and integration messages to uniquely identify this specific return or refund request.

status.description:
Current business status of the return request as visible to the customer.

This field is derived from the non-nullable `request_status` column in the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model and may be normalized into a customer-friendly vocabulary such as `pending`, `under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `cancelled_by_customer`. Even when normalized, it must accurately reflect the underlying workflow state so that UIs and notifications show a truthful representation of how far the request has progressed.

reason_code.description:
Machine-readable reason code selected by the customer when initiating the return request.

In most implementations this code is mapped from `request_reason_category` on `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` and represents standardized categories such as `not_as_described`, `damaged_item`, `wrong_item_received`, or `changed_mind`. Internal analytics, policy enforcement rules, and reporting should rely on this normalized value rather than free-text comments to classify and aggregate return reasons.

reason_label.description:
Human-readable label for the selected reason code, suitable for direct display in customer-facing UIs.

This label is typically derived from `reason_code` / `request_reason_category` (and may incorporate hints from `request_reason_detail`) and localized into the customer’s language. It frees clients from having to maintain their own reason dictionaries, ensuring that order detail pages and return request screens can display consistent and up-to-date wording for the chosen reason.

customer_comment.description:
Free-form explanation or additional comments entered by the customer when submitting the return request.

This text usually corresponds to the nullable `request_reason_detail` column in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` or an equivalent free-text field and captures the customer’s own description of the problem (for example, where an item is damaged, how a product differs from the description, or why it no longer meets their needs). It may be empty when the customer only selects a standardized reason code, but when present it provides important context for sellers and support teams reviewing the case.

requested_refund_amount.description:
Total monetary amount that the customer has requested to be refunded for this return request, expressed in the order currency.

This value is typically computed by aggregating per-line refund intentions across the relevant `shopping_mall_order_lines` records, taking into account unit prices, applied discounts, tax allocations, and the set of lines actually included in the request. It does not necessarily correspond to a single raw column on `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`, but it must be consistent with downstream payment and refund subsystems, which will decide whether to fully grant, partially grant, or deny this requested refund amount.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code representing the currency of the requested refund amount (for example, `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`).

This code should match the currency used for the underlying order totals in `shopping_mall_orders`. Keeping the currency consistent ensures that refund amounts can be reconciled with payment transactions, accounting ledgers, and financial reporting without additional currency conversion or mapping at the API layer.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the return request was created, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value corresponds to the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model and marks when the customer (or other actor) first submitted the request. It is used to enforce return windows relative to order placement and delivery, to sort lists of return requests, and to support audit and compliance requirements.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent customer-visible update to this return request, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This is typically mapped from the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`. It changes whenever fields that matter to the customer—such as `status`, aggregated refund amounts, or reason/detail text—are modified. Clients can use it to highlight recently changed requests, while operational and compliance tooling can use it to detect stale or long-unattended cases.

customer.description:
Summary information about the customer who submitted the return request, derived through the `shopping_mall_order_return_request_of_customers` subtype linkage.

The summary follows the `IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary` structure backed by the `shopping_mall_customer` Prisma model and exposes only non-sensitive identity attributes (such as display name and avatar URL) sufficient for UIs and support dashboards. Sensitive authentication details, risk flags, and full profile information remain in separate security- and identity-focused DTOs.

order.description:
Summary representation of the parent order associated with this return request.

This object is a projection of the corresponding `shopping_mall_orders` record and effectively replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_order_id` from `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` in the API. It provides key context such as the human-readable order number, main timestamps, high-level order and payment statuses, and a small set of representative items. Embedding this summary lets clients render both the order and the return request details in a single round-trip without fetching the order separately.

lines.description:
Collection of order line entries that are covered by this return request, including quantities and per-line requested refund amounts for customer display.

Each element corresponds to a specific `shopping_mall_order_lines` record belonging to the parent order and describes how that line participates in this return request. The view captures product and SKU snapshots as they were at the time of ordering, together with the originally ordered quantity and the quantity that the customer is now requesting to return. This allows customer portals and support tooling to present a clear, item-by-item breakdown of the return request contents.

evidences.description:
List of evidence items (such as photos, screenshots, or documents) attached by the customer to support the return request.

Each evidence entry is represented by `IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequestEvidenceCustomerView` and follows the platform-wide URL-only file handling policy: files are uploaded to a storage or media service first, and the return request record stores only metadata (name and extension) plus a URL (`url` with `format: uri`) for preview and download. This keeps the return request payload compact, avoids binary data in JSON, and makes it easy for both customer-facing and admin-facing UIs to review supporting materials when evaluating the request.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequestLineCusto.description:
Customer-facing view of a single order line that is part of an order return request.

This DTO links a specific `shopping_mall_order_lines` record to its participation in an order return request and is always embedded inside `IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequestCustomerView.lines`. It provides a compact subset of line information—product identity, SKU code, the originally ordered quantity, the quantity the customer is requesting to return, and an optional per-line requested refund amount—so that customers and support staff can see exactly which items are affected by the return without loading the full order line entity.

order_line_id.description:
Unique identifier of the order line in the `shopping_mall_order_lines` table that this return request line refers to.

This value maps directly to the `id` column of the underlying order line record and allows backends and clients to correlate the return entry with other views and operations that reference the same line, such as full order details, shipment breakdowns, and per-line fulfillment or refund histories.

sku_code.description:
Human-readable SKU code of the product variant for this line, suitable for display in customer-facing UIs.

Typically this value originates from a snapshot field such as `sku_code_snapshot` on the order line or from the SKU `code` at the time the order was placed. Storing it here ensures that the correct variant identifier is shown even if catalog metadata or SKU definitions change later.

product_name.description:
Name of the product for the order line, as captured at the time of checkout.

This usually corresponds to a snapshot column (for example, `product_name_snapshot`) on the `shopping_mall_order_lines` record and preserves the product name as the customer saw it when they placed the order. This guarantees that return request views remain stable and understandable even if the product name is edited in the catalog after the order was created.

quantity_ordered.description:
Total quantity originally ordered for this line.

This value maps to the `quantity` column on the associated `shopping_mall_order_lines` record and represents the number of units that were successfully ordered for this SKU in the original order. It does not take returns or cancellations into account by itself; it is the baseline against which `quantity_requested_return` is interpreted.

quantity_requested_return.description:
Quantity from this line that the customer has requested to return in this order return request.

This number is always less than or equal to `quantity_ordered` and indicates how many units from the original line are included in this specific return request. It supports partial returns where only a subset of the originally ordered items are being sent back, and it allows back-office workflows to reconcile returns with the underlying order and inventory records.

line_requested_refund_amount.description:
Requested refund amount for this particular order line within the return request, expressed in the same currency as the parent order.

When present, this value represents the portion of the overall `requested_refund_amount` that is attributable to this line, after any distribution of discounts, taxes, and shipping costs that the business rules apply. Some implementations may leave this field undefined or exclude it from the response when per-line monetary breakdowns are not calculated or stored; in those cases, clients should rely on the aggregate `requested_refund_amount` on the parent return request instead of per-line amounts.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequestEvidenceC.description:
Customer-facing representation of a single evidence item attached to an order return request.

This DTO follows the URL-only file upload pattern and contains metadata required to render or download the evidence in client applications.

id.description: Unique identifier of this evidence record associated with the return request.

name.description: Display name or title of the evidence file as provided by the customer.

extension.description: File extension for the evidence asset (for example, `jpg`, `png`, or `pdf`).

url.description: Publicly accessible or signed URL pointing to the stored evidence file. The file itself is uploaded separately and referenced here by URL only.

IShoppingMallOrderDispute.IRequest.description:
Filter, sorting, and pagination criteria for listing disputes associated with a specific order in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is consumed by index/search endpoints such as `PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/orders/{orderId}/disputes` and encapsulates optional filters on dispute status, type, actor, creation period, and related order line identifiers, along with generic pagination and ordering options.

All fields are optional so that clients may submit an empty object to use default pagination and ordering, or combine specific filters as needed. This type does not map directly to a Prisma model because it represents search parameters rather than a stored entity.

page.description: Zero-based page index used for offset-based pagination. When omitted, the implementation should default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of dispute summary records to return in a single page. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to protect the system from excessively large page sizes.

status.description: Optional filter on the current status of disputes (for example, `open`, `under_review`, `resolved`, or `rejected`).

type.description: Optional filter on the dispute type or category (for example, `non_delivery`, `damaged_goods`, `wrong_item`, or `service_issue`).

oneOf.description: Optional filter specifying which actor opened the dispute, such as `customer` or `seller`. This allows clients to focus on disputes initiated by a particular side.
Optional filter specifying which actor opened the dispute, such as `customer` or `seller`. This allows clients to focus on disputes initiated by a particular side.

opened_by_actor.description: Optional filter specifying which actor opened the dispute, such as `customer` or `seller`. This allows clients to focus on disputes initiated by a particular side.

created_from.description: Inclusive lower bound of the dispute creation timestamp range filter, in ISO 8601 format.

created_to.description: Inclusive upper bound of the dispute creation timestamp range filter, in ISO 8601 format.

order_line_ids.description: Optional list of order line identifiers used to restrict results to disputes that involve one or more specific order lines within the parent order.

search.description: Free-text search term applied to dispute subjects, messages, or other indexed fields, depending on implementation.

sort_by.description: Field name used to sort dispute results (for example, `created_at` or `status`). The implementation should restrict this to a safe whitelist of sortable fields.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for ordered results. When provided, must be either `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending order.
Sort direction for ordered results. When provided, must be either `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending order.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction for ordered results. When provided, must be either `asc` for ascending or `desc` for descending order.

IShoppingMallOrderDispute.description:
Detailed dispute entity representing a single order-related dispute in the shopping mall domain.

This type models a complete dispute row from the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` Prisma model and is used as the primary response DTO when retrieving a single dispute for a given order. It captures identifiers, links to the parent order and optionally a specific order line, actor classification, business categorization of the issue, and the current dispute status.

The DTO also exposes important lifecycle timestamps such as creation, latest update, and optional resolution and soft-deletion moments. For API consumers, it provides both raw identifiers for low-level correlation and rich association objects for rendering dispute context without additional round trips.

Creation and update operations use the dedicated `.ICreate` and `.IUpdate` variants. Server-side logic manages ownership, actor/session information, and subtype entities such as `shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_customers` and `shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_sellers`, so those concerns remain outside this DTO.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` table and is generated by the system. Clients use it in path parameters such as `disputeId` to address a particular dispute.

It is immutable for the lifetime of the dispute record.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order that this dispute belongs to.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_orders.id` and links the dispute to its parent order context at the database level. Service implementations must ensure that the `orderId` path parameter and this field refer to the same record when retrieving or mutating disputes.

In response DTOs, this field is kept as a raw UUID to support technical correlation and troubleshooting, while the richer `order` association exposes the human-friendly view of the parent order.

shopping_mall_order_line_id.description:
Optional identifier of the specific order line that this dispute targets.

When this field is populated, it corresponds to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model and indicates that the dispute is line-level rather than purely order-level. This allows the platform to distinguish complaints about a particular item (for example, one damaged SKU) from disputes about shipping, payment, or the order as a whole.

When the value is `null`, the dispute is treated as relating to the overall order or to non-line-specific issues such as delivery delays or payment problems. In read responses, the richer `orderLine` association provides a summarized view of the affected line when this foreign key is set, while this field exposes the raw technical identifier needed for correlation and integration with back-office tooling.

actor_type.description:
Actor classification for the party that opened the dispute.

Typical values follow business-defined categories such as `customer`, `seller`, or `platform_admin`. This classification is used to route the dispute to appropriate workflows and to associate it with subtype records in `shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_customers` or `shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_sellers`.

Clients should treat this as an informational field driven by server-side logic rather than a user-editable property.

issue_category.description:
Business category describing the type of issue being disputed.

Examples include `non_delivery`, `damaged_item`, `incorrect_item`, `payment_issue`, or `policy_violation`. Exact allowed values are enforced by service logic or configuration rather than by this schema.

Downstream systems use this value to drive reporting, routing, and automation rules for dispute handling.

issue_title.description:
Short human-readable title summarizing the dispute.

This field is intended for use in lists and dashboards where a concise description of the dispute is needed. It should describe the core problem in a single sentence or phrase.

The value typically mirrors or is derived from the customer or seller input when the dispute was created.

issue_description.description:
Detailed narrative description of the disputed problem.

When present, this text explains the context, expectations, and symptoms of the issue, often provided by the initiating actor. It may include order details, delivery observations, or communication history.

When `null`, the dispute relies solely on structured fields like `issue_category` and `issue_title` to convey meaning.

dispute_status.description:
Current workflow status of the dispute.

Typical values follow a business-defined state machine such as `open`, `awaiting_seller`, `awaiting_customer`, `resolved_customer_favored`, `resolved_seller_favored`, or `closed_without_action`. The precise state transitions are enforced by backend workflows.

Clients should treat this as read-only status information that determines which subsequent actions are available in the UI.

resolution_category.description:
Outcome classification describing how the dispute was resolved.

Common examples include `refund_given`, `replacement_sent`, `claim_rejected`, or `goodwill_credit`. The value is typically set when the dispute reaches a terminal resolved state.

When `null`, the dispute is still unresolved or has not yet been assigned a resolution category.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the dispute reached a resolved state.

If set, this marks the moment when the platform or seller finalized the dispute according to business workflow rules. The timestamp is in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When `null`, the dispute is not yet resolved or is still in an intermediate state such as open or under review.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this dispute was created.

This field is recorded at the moment the dispute is opened in the system and remains immutable afterwards. It is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Clients can use it to order dispute timelines or display when the complaint was initially raised.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this dispute record was last updated.

Every mutation of the dispute, such as status changes or description edits, should update this field. It is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value helps clients understand how recently any changes were applied to the dispute.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this dispute record.

When set, the dispute is considered logically deleted and should be excluded from normal user-facing listings while remaining available for audit or administrative review. The timestamp is in ISO 8601 date-time format.

When `null`, the dispute is active or archived according to other lifecycle rules.

order.description:
Summary representation of the parent order associated with this dispute.

This association complements the raw `shopping_mall_order_id` field by exposing a human-friendly snapshot of the order, including key fields such as order number, monetary totals, and high-level status as defined in `IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary`.

Clients can use this object to render dispute context in a single response without issuing an additional request to retrieve the parent order. It follows the standard pattern where BELONGS-TO relations are represented by `.ISummary` types in response DTOs.

orderLine.description:
Optional summary of the specific order line targeted by this dispute when it is line-level.

When the dispute relates to a particular item within the order, this association exposes a concise view of that line based on `IShoppingMallOrderLine.ISummary`, including product, quantity, and pricing context.

If the dispute concerns the overall order or a non-line-specific issue (such as shipping or payment), this property may be omitted or set to null by the service implementation, allowing clients to distinguish between order-level and line-level disputes.

IShoppingMallOrderDispute.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new order dispute associated with an existing order.

This DTO is used by authenticated customers when calling the dispute creation endpoint for a given order. It captures the actor-provided details required to open a dispute while relying on server-side logic to attach actor identity and session context.

Only business-level fields such as dispute categorization, title, detailed description, and optional linkage to a specific order line are included. System-managed fields like primary keys, timestamps, and actor/session references are excluded from the client payload and are populated by the backend based on the current authentication and order context.

shopping_mall_order_line_id.description:
Optional identifier of a specific order line that this dispute targets.

When present, this value must correspond to `shopping_mall_order_lines.id` for a line that belongs to the order referenced by the `orderId` path parameter. It is used when the dispute concerns a particular item rather than the entire order.

When `null`, the dispute is treated as relating to the overall order, shipping experience, or a global payment issue.

issue_category.description:
Business category describing the type of dispute being opened.

Examples include `non_delivery`, `damaged_item`, `incorrect_item`, `payment_issue`, or `policy_violation`. The exact allowed values are governed by platform policy or configuration and validated server-side.

Clients should choose a value from the options presented in the UI; free-form values may be rejected depending on implementation.

issue_title.description:
Short summary title for the dispute.

This value appears in dispute lists and dashboards to help users quickly identify the nature of the complaint. It should succinctly describe the problem in one sentence or phrase, such as "Package never arrived" or "Wrong color item received".

The title is required when opening a dispute and becomes part of the persisted dispute record.

issue_description.description:
Optional detailed narrative description of the issue.

When provided, this text gives additional context and explanation about the dispute, including observed problems, expectations, or previous interactions. It is stored alongside the dispute and can be used by sellers and platform administrators to evaluate the claim.

When `null`, the dispute relies on the structured fields such as `issue_category` and `issue_title` to convey the complaint.

IShoppingMallOrderDispute.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing order dispute from the customer side.

This type is intentionally defined as a pure request-layer payload and is **not** directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` Prisma model. It only contains customer-editable narrative fields that the backend will translate into appropriate persistence operations and audit logs.

By avoiding a direct Prisma mapping here, we ensure that no phantom fields are assumed to exist on the database table and that clients remain isolated from low-level schema details. System-managed columns such as identifiers, actor types, workflow statuses, and timestamps remain fully controlled by the server and cannot be manipulated through this DTO.

description.description:
Free-form textual explanation from the customer describing the issue they are disputing.

May include details about non-delivery, damaged goods, incorrect items, or other service dissatisfaction. The backend may impose maximum length limits and perform content validation or sanitization, but those constraints are enforced server-side.

evidence_urls.description:
Collection of pre-uploaded evidence URLs that support the dispute.

Each entry should be a URL pointing to an image, document, or other artifact that has already been uploaded to a file storage service. The client is responsible for performing the upload separately and then passing only the resulting URLs in this field.

items.description: URL to a pre-uploaded evidence file associated with this dispute.

customer_note.description:
Optional additional note from the customer, such as follow-up clarifications or contextual information that supplements the main description.

This field is typically used when a customer updates a dispute after its initial creation to provide more context or respond to support inquiries.

IShoppingMallOrderDisputeCustomer.description:
Read-only view of a customer-associated subtype record for an order dispute, combining information from shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_customers and key fields from the parent dispute in shopping_mall_order_disputes.

Intended for administrative consoles and investigation tools where platform administrators need to see which customer opened the dispute, through which session, and a concise snapshot of the dispute context and current status.

id.description:
Primary key of the customer subtype record in shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_customers.

Uniquely identifies this customer-specific dispute linkage entry.

dispute_id.description:
Identifier of the parent dispute in shopping_mall_order_disputes that this customer subtype record is associated with.

This field is used to join back to the main dispute entity when additional details are needed.

customer_id.description:
Identifier of the customer (shopping_mall_customer.id) who opened the dispute.

Used for administrative review and correlation with other customer activity such as orders, returns, and risk evaluations.

customer_session_id.description:
Identifier of the customer session (shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id) under which the dispute was created.

Helps administrators trace the connection context, device, and approximate location associated with the dispute creation event.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this customer subtype record was created.

Reflects the moment the dispute was opened by the customer, in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the most recent update to this customer subtype record.

Updated whenever mutable fields on the subtype entity change, such as when additional metadata is attached.

dispute_status.description:
Current high-level status of the parent dispute, such as "open", "awaiting_customer_input", "in_review", or "resolved".

This value is typically mirrored from the shopping_mall_order_disputes table so that administrative tools can see the dispute state without performing an extra join.

issue_category.description:
Categorization of the dispute reason as stored on the parent dispute, for example "non_delivery", "damaged_goods", or "service_issue".

Used for reporting, routing, and analytics in administrative and support tooling.

resolution_category.description:
High-level resolution category for the dispute once a conclusion has been reached, such as "refund_issued", "replacement_shipped", or "rejected".

May be null or omitted when the dispute is still open or under review.

dispute.description:
Summary view of the parent dispute associated with this customer subtype record.

This nested summary provides key dispute context—such as title, issue category, current status, and important timestamps—so that administrators can understand the dispute in a single call without separately fetching the main dispute entity. It follows the standard .ISummary pattern to avoid circular references while still providing rich contextual information.

IShoppingMallOrderSummary.description:
High-level summary view of a specific customer order in the shoppingMall domain.

This projection is derived primarily from the `shopping_mall_orders` Prisma model and related order structures such as seller segments, order lines, payments, and fulfillments. It exposes the key information needed for order detail or overview screens without returning every underlying row, while staying semantically aligned with the underlying database columns like `order_status`, `payment_status`, `currency_code`, and the various monetary snapshot amounts.

Numeric totals such as `items_subtotal_amount`, `discount_total_amount`, `shipping_total_amount`, `tax_total_amount`, and `grand_total_amount` are represented here as aggregated snapshot fields and must reflect the same business meaning as documented in the Prisma schema. The DTO is designed to remain stable even if internal table structures evolve, as long as the same conceptual fields can be computed from the database and continue to match the intent of the `shopping_mall_orders` model.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order in the `shopping_mall_orders` table.

This corresponds directly to the primary key column `id` of the base order record and is used as the canonical identifier across all order-related APIs, foreign keys, and audit trails. The value is a UUID string generated by the persistence layer according to the Prisma model configuration.

code.description:
Human-friendly order code or number presented to customers and support staff.

Conceptually this mirrors the `order_code` column of the `shopping_mall_orders` model, which is typically unique within the platform and follows a business-specific pattern such as `ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNN`. The value is used in emails, support conversations, and search screens so clients should treat it as a stable, human-readable identifier rather than attempting to derive semantics from its structure.

customer.description:
Customer summary for the owner of this order.

Instead of exposing the raw `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key from the `shopping_mall_orders` table, this field returns a denormalized `IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary` projection. It allows clients to display key customer information—such as display name and avatar URL—without issuing a separate API call, while still respecting privacy rules and not exposing sensitive credential fields.

status.description:
Primary business status of the order derived from `shopping_mall_orders.order_status`.

This value represents the current high-level lifecycle state of the order, such as `pending_payment`, `processing`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`, or `refunded`, following the business vocabulary documented alongside the `order_status` column in the Prisma schema. Implementations should ensure this field remains consistent with status transition logic and order status history captured in `shopping_mall_order_status_events` so that clients can reliably drive UI state from it.

paymentStatus.description:
Aggregated payment state for the order based on `shopping_mall_orders.payment_status` and related payment records.

The value summarizes the current payment lifecycle for the order, typically using states such as `payment_pending`, `payment_authorized`, `payment_captured`, `payment_failed`, `partially_refunded`, or `refunded`. It must stay aligned with the `payment_status` column of the `shopping_mall_orders` model and the detailed transaction records in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` and `shopping_mall_payment_status_events`, so that finance reports and UI representations remain consistent.

fulfillmentStatus.description:
Aggregated fulfillment or shipping state for the order derived from fulfillment and shipment data.

This status summarizes the logistics side of the lifecycle, for example `unfulfilled`, `partially_fulfilled`, `fulfilled`, `shipped`, `delivered`, or `returned`. It is computed from fulfillment aggregates in `shopping_mall_fulfillments`, shipment records in `shopping_mall_shipments`, and related tracking events. Although it is not a direct column on `shopping_mall_orders`, it is expected to follow a stable, business-defined vocabulary that reflects how far the order has progressed operationally.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code used for monetary amounts in this summary, corresponding to `shopping_mall_orders.currency_code`.

All monetary fields in this DTO—such as subtotal, discounts, shipping, tax, and grand total—are expressed in this currency. The value must be a valid three-letter ISO 4217 code (for example, `USD` or `KRW`) consistent with the `currency_code` column in the Prisma model, and business rules around supported currencies and regional markets should be enforced when orders are created.

itemCount.description:
Total number of individual line items in the order across all seller segments.

This value is a computed aggregate rather than a direct column on `shopping_mall_orders`. It is typically derived from the quantities and line counts in `shopping_mall_order_lines` associated with the order, and is intended to give a quick overview for UI displays (for example, "3 items from 2 sellers") without loading every individual line item.

subtotalAmount.description:
Subtotal amount for the order before discounts, shipping, and taxes, mirroring `shopping_mall_orders.items_subtotal_amount`.

This snapshot represents the sum of per-line base prices multiplied by quantities at the time the order was placed. It is expressed in the currency indicated by the `currency`/`currency_code` field and should not be recomputed by clients, since server-side pricing rules and promotions may affect the exact value.

discountAmount.description:
Total discount amount applied to the order, corresponding to `shopping_mall_orders.discount_total_amount`.

The value includes all order-level and item-level promotions, coupons, and manual adjustments that reduce the effective order value. It is recorded as a snapshot at order creation and is expressed in the same currency as other monetary fields so that accounting reports and UI representations remain consistent over time.

shippingAmount.description:
Total shipping charges applied to the order, corresponding to `shopping_mall_orders.shipping_total_amount`.

This amount aggregates all shipping costs across seller segments, shipping methods, and regions for this order. It is stored as a snapshot in the `shipping_total_amount` column of `shopping_mall_orders` and expressed in the `currency` for the order, allowing consistent reconciliation with logistics and billing systems.

taxAmount.description:
Total tax amount applied to the order, corresponding to `shopping_mall_orders.tax_total_amount`.

The value represents the sum of all calculated tax components (such as VAT, sales tax, and regional surcharges) at the time of checkout. It is a snapshot stored in the `tax_total_amount` column and should reflect the tax rules and jurisdictions that were in effect when the order was placed.

grandTotalAmount.description:
Grand total amount that the customer is expected to pay for this order, matching `shopping_mall_orders.grand_total_amount`.

This field generally reflects the formula `items_subtotal_amount - discount_total_amount + shipping_total_amount + tax_total_amount` as captured by the `grand_total_amount` column in the `shopping_mall_orders` table. It is expressed in the `currency` for the order and should align with the amount authorized or captured by payment transactions so that financial records reconcile correctly.

createdAt.description:
Date and time when the order record was created, mapped from `shopping_mall_orders.created_at`.

The value is returned in ISO 8601 date-time format (for example, `2025-11-15T01:09:27.330Z`) and is typically stored in UTC according to the Prisma model configuration. It represents the moment when the order entity was first persisted, which may be slightly different from lower-level status transitions such as payment initiation or placement timestamps if those are tracked separately.

updatedAt.description:
Date and time when the order record was last updated, mapped from `shopping_mall_orders.updated_at`.

Like `createdAt`, this timestamp is returned in ISO 8601 date-time format and is generally stored in UTC. It is updated whenever significant order-level fields (such as status, payment status, or key monetary values) change, and it provides a convenient marker for cache invalidation, monitoring, or synchronization with external systems.

sellerSegments.description:
Shallow per-seller breakdowns for this order, corresponding conceptually to rows in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments`.

Each entry summarizes the portion of the order handled by a single seller, including per-seller item counts and monetary aggregates derived from `shopping_mall_order_lines` and related fulfillment and shipment records. This allows clients to present seller-grouped views (for example, one section per merchant) without loading full line-level or status history data, while still remaining aligned with the underlying Prisma models for seller segments and lines.

IShoppingMallOrderSellerSegmentSummary.description:
Summary information for a single seller's segment within a multi-seller order.

This projection is conceptually derived from the `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` Prisma model together with associated `shopping_mall_order_lines` and fulfillment/ shipment records. It exposes enough information to show how much of the order belongs to a specific seller and the operational status of that segment without returning every underlying row or event.

The DTO is intended for embedding inside order summaries and seller-facing dashboards, providing a concise, denormalized view of per-seller monetary totals and item counts that can be traced back to the underlying segment and line data when needed.

sellerId.description:
Unique identifier of the seller that owns this segment.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_seller` model, typically referenced through a foreign key on the `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` table. It is used to correlate the segment with seller-facing screens, analytics, and other APIs that operate on seller accounts.

sellerDisplayName.description:
Display name of the seller for this segment, derived from the seller profile.

The value is normally populated from a human-readable field on the `shopping_mall_seller` record (such as shop name or display name) and is intended for customer-facing UI labels. It should not be used as a stable technical identifier; consumers should rely on `sellerId` for joins and lookups.

segmentStatus.description:
Primary lifecycle status of this seller segment, derived from seller-segment and fulfillment data.

The field summarizes the high-level state of the seller-specific portion of the order, using a constrained business vocabulary such as `pending`, `accepted`, `in_fulfillment`, `shipped`, `delivered`, or `cancelled`. It is computed from fields on `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` and related fulfillment and shipment records, and it may differ from the overall order status when different sellers progress at different speeds.

itemCount.description:
Number of line items belonging to this seller segment.

This value is typically computed as the count of `shopping_mall_order_lines` (or the sum of their quantities) that are associated with this seller for the parent order. It allows customer and seller UIs to display how many items are contained in this segment without loading the full line-level dataset.

subtotalAmount.description:
Subtotal amount for this seller segment before discounts, shipping, and taxes.

Conceptually this is the portion of the order snapshot `items_subtotal_amount` that belongs to this seller, computed from the base prices and quantities of the `shopping_mall_order_lines` linked to this segment. It is expressed in the same currency as the parent order and provides a per-seller view of pre-discount merchandise value.

discountAmount.description:
Total discount amount applied to this seller segment.

The value aggregates all promotions, coupons, and adjustments that apply specifically to items from this seller. It conceptually partitions the master order’s `discount_total_amount` across sellers and is useful for per-seller revenue and promotion effectiveness reporting.

shippingAmount.description:
Total shipping charges for this seller segment.

This amount represents the shipping costs incurred for this seller's items, based on shipping methods, regions, and carrier rules that apply to the segment. It conceptually contributes to the overall `shipping_total_amount` on the master order and is expressed in the same currency as the order.

taxAmount.description:
Total tax amount for this seller segment.

The value reflects the aggregated tax computed for the items and shipping charges in this seller segment, partitioning the master order's `tax_total_amount` into per-seller components. It is expressed in the same currency as the parent order and follows the tax rules that were applied at checkout.

grandTotalAmount.description:
Grand total for this seller segment.

This amount represents the final payable total for items belonging to this seller after discounts, including shipping and taxes, expressed in the same currency as the parent order summary. Conceptually, the sum of `grandTotalAmount` across all seller segments will not exceed the master order `grand_total_amount` and can be used for per-seller settlement and payout calculations.

IShoppingMallOrderTimeline.description:
Chronological lifecycle timeline for a specific order in the shoppingMall domain.

This DTO represents an ordered collection of timeline entries that describe how an order evolved over time across multiple subsystems, including order status transitions, payment events, fulfillment and shipment updates, and dispute or cancellation milestones. It is a read-only analytical view composed from event- and history-oriented tables linked to the base `shopping_mall_orders` record.

orderId.description:
Unique identifier of the order whose timeline is represented.

This matches the primary key of the `shopping_mall_orders` model and is used to correlate timeline entries with the order summary and detail views.

entries.description:
Ordered list of timeline entries representing significant events in the lifecycle of the order.

Entries are typically sorted in ascending chronological order by their `occurredAt` timestamp, allowing clients to render a visual timeline of the order from creation to its current state.

IShoppingMallOrderTimelineEntry.description:
Single timeline entry representing a discrete event in the lifecycle of an order.

Entries are normalized projections derived from various event sources, such as order status change records, payment status events, shipment tracking updates, cancellation or return requests, and disputes. The structure is intentionally generic so that new event sources can be mapped into this DTO without changing the external contract.

id.description:
Stable identifier for this timeline entry within the context of the order.

This may be a synthetic identifier or derived from the underlying event record, and is used to support idempotent rendering and potential future interactions (for example, deep links to a specific event).

occurredAt.description:
Timestamp when this event occurred.

Expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC. For events that cannot be precisely timestamped, this should represent the best available approximation used for ordering in the timeline.

type.description:
Machine-readable type code that categorizes this timeline entry.

Examples include `order_status_change`, `payment_authorized`, `payment_captured`, `payment_failed`, `shipment_shipped`, `shipment_delivered`, `cancellation_requested`, `cancellation_approved`, `return_requested`, `dispute_opened`, or `dispute_resolved`. The exact vocabulary is defined by business logic but should remain stable over time for clients that rely on specific event types.

title.description:
Short, human-friendly title summarizing the event.

Used for primary labeling in timeline UIs, such as "Order placed", "Payment authorized", or "Shipment delivered".

description.description:
Optional longer-form description providing more context about the event.

May include status transitions, amounts, actor roles (customer, seller, admin), or logistics notes that help users understand what happened and why.

actorRole.description:
Role of the principal actor associated with this event, if applicable.

Typical values include `customer`, `seller`, `platform_admin`, or `system`. This allows clients to display who triggered or owns the event without exposing underlying actor identifiers.

metadata.description:
Optional structured metadata carrying event-specific details.

This is a flexible key-value container that can hold additional information such as previous and new statuses, payment method labels, tracking numbers, carrier names, or dispute reasons. The exact keys and value types are domain-specific and may evolve over time.

IShoppingMallOrderItemsOverview.description:
Consolidated overview of all items belonging to a specific customer-facing master order in the shopping mall system.

This DTO is a denormalized, read-only projection primarily derived from the `shopping_mall_orders` and `shopping_mall_order_lines` tables and optionally enriched with product, SKU, seller, and fulfillment snapshots. It is optimized for UI consumption so that a client can retrieve all item-level information for an order in a single call without additional joins or queries.

The structure intentionally avoids exposing low-level internal implementation details such as audit fields or risk flags, and it does not map 1:1 to any single Prisma model. Instead, it stabilizes the external contract even if underlying database schemas for orders, order lines, or SKUs evolve over time.

orderId.description: Unique identifier of the master order whose items are being summarized. This corresponds to the primary key of a record in `shopping_mall_orders`.

currency.description: Currency code used for all monetary amounts in this overview, typically an ISO 4217 currency code such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`.

items.description: Array of item-level overview entries, one per concrete order line. Each element aggregates SKU snapshot, product snapshot, quantity, pricing snapshot, and high-level status for a particular line within the order.

itemsCount.description: Total number of order lines represented in the `items` array for this order.

subtotalAmount.description: Subtotal monetary amount for this order computed as the sum of all item line totals before shipping fees, discounts, taxes, or refunds. Expressed in the currency indicated by `currency`.

discountAmount.description: Total discount amount applied across all items for this order, if available. This includes line-level discounts and order-level promotions. Expressed in the currency indicated by `currency`.

taxAmount.description: Total tax amount associated with all items in this order, if applicable and available. Expressed in the currency indicated by `currency`.

shippingFeeAmount.description: Total shipping fee amount associated with this order as it relates to the included items. Expressed in the currency indicated by `currency`.

grandTotalAmount.description: Grand total amount for the order items including subtotal, discounts, taxes, and shipping fees as captured at checkout time. This value is suitable for display on customer-facing order detail screens. Expressed in the currency indicated by `currency`.

IShoppingMallOrderItemsOverviewItem.description:
Single-line item overview entry within an `IShoppingMallOrderItemsOverview` response.

This DTO corresponds conceptually to a row in `shopping_mall_order_lines` enriched with denormalized snapshots from related entities such as products, SKUs, and seller segments. It provides enough information for a UI to display each purchased item within an order without issuing further lookups for product names, SKU codes, or basic seller information.

The structure is intentionally stable and does not expose low-level technical details or internal audit information.

orderLineId.description: Unique identifier of the underlying order line record, typically corresponding to the primary key of a row in `shopping_mall_order_lines`.

sellerSegmentId.description: Identifier of the seller segment within the master order that this line belongs to. Typically corresponds to a record in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` when the order involves multiple sellers.

sellerDisplayName.description: Human-readable name of the seller responsible for fulfilling this line item. This is a snapshot value suitable for display in customer order detail views.

productId.description: Identifier of the product associated with this line, corresponding to a record in `shopping_mall_products` at the time of ordering.

productName.description: Snapshot of the product name at the time of ordering, used for stable display even if the current catalog name changes later.

skuId.description: Identifier of the concrete SKU purchased for this line, generally referencing `shopping_mall_product_skus`.

skuCode.description: Snapshot of the SKU code associated with the purchased variant, used for display and support/troubleshooting workflows.

skuOptionsSummary.description: Human-readable concatenated summary of the option values chosen for this SKU (for example, `Color: Black / Size: M`). This is a snapshot to keep the overview self-contained.

quantity.description: Number of units of the SKU purchased on this order line.

unitPrice.description: Snapshot of the per-unit price captured for this order line at checkout time, before per-line discounts. Expressed in the same currency as the parent overview.

lineDiscountAmount.description: Total discount amount applied specifically to this order line, if applicable. Expressed in the same currency as the parent overview.

lineTotal.description: Total monetary amount for this line after line-level discounts but before proportional allocation of shipping or tax. Calculated from `quantity`, `unitPrice`, and `lineDiscountAmount` as captured at checkout. Expressed in the same currency as the parent overview.

oneOf.description: High-level fulfillment or shipment status for this line item (for example, `pending`, `preparing`, `shipped`, or `delivered`). The concrete values are derived from fulfillment or shipment records and are aligned with the platform's business-defined status vocabulary.

fulfillmentSummary.description: Optional human-readable summary of fulfillment state or shipment progress for this line item, such as `Shipped via DHL - Tracking #123456` or `Awaiting warehouse processing`.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusBreakdownStatist.description:
Aggregated analytical view of order counts grouped by business status for reporting and dashboard purposes.

This DTO is derived from aggregation queries over the `shopping_mall_orders` table and potentially related status history tables such as `shopping_mall_order_status_events`. It does not correspond directly to any single Prisma model, and all values are computed metrics rather than raw database columns.

The structure is designed for platform administrator dashboards to quickly assess the distribution of orders across lifecycle stages (for example, pending, confirmed, paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded) and to provide total counts and ratios that are safe to expose internally without leaking customer-identifying information.

totalOrders.description: Total number of orders included in this breakdown across all status buckets for the evaluated scope (for example, all-time or a default recent period such as the last 30 days).

pendingCount.description: Number of orders currently in a `pending` or `awaiting confirmation` state, before payment or seller confirmation is finalized.

confirmedCount.description: Number of orders that have been confirmed but not yet fully paid or moved to shipping preparation, depending on the platform's business lifecycle definition.

paidCount.description: Number of orders that have successfully completed payment but have not yet been fully shipped.

shippedCount.description: Number of orders that have been shipped but not yet confirmed as delivered to the customer.

deliveredCount.description: Number of orders that have been successfully delivered to customers according to fulfillment or shipment tracking records.

cancelledCount.description: Number of orders that have been cancelled at any stage of the lifecycle, regardless of whether they were paid before cancellation.

refundedCount.description: Number of orders that have completed a refund process, either partial or full, as tracked through payment and refund transaction entities.

pendingRatio.description: Fraction of orders in the `pending` bucket relative to `totalOrders`, represented as a value between 0 and 1.

confirmedRatio.description: Fraction of orders in the `confirmed` bucket relative to `totalOrders`, represented as a value between 0 and 1.

paidRatio.description: Fraction of orders in the `paid` bucket relative to `totalOrders`, represented as a value between 0 and 1.

shippedRatio.description: Fraction of orders in the `shipped` bucket relative to `totalOrders`, represented as a value between 0 and 1.

deliveredRatio.description: Fraction of orders in the `delivered` bucket relative to `totalOrders`, represented as a value between 0 and 1.

cancelledRatio.description: Fraction of orders in the `cancelled` bucket relative to `totalOrders`, represented as a value between 0 and 1.

refundedRatio.description: Fraction of orders in the `refunded` bucket relative to `totalOrders`, represented as a value between 0 and 1.

IShoppingMallOrderTrendStatistics.description:
Aggregated trend statistics over customer orders in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is a computed analytics view derived from the shopping_mall_orders table and related monetary snapshot fields. It is used by dashboards and reporting endpoints to understand how order volume and revenue evolve over time without exposing raw order rows.

The structure provides both overall summary metrics and time-bucketed series suitable for charts (for example, daily or monthly GMV and order counts grouped by placed_at or created_at). It never maps directly to a Prisma model and is read-only from the API consumer’s perspective.

overall.description: Overall aggregated statistics across the entire query range, such as total order count, total GMV, and average order value.

buckets.description: Time-bucketed trend metrics over the selected period. Each bucket represents a single time grain (for example, a day, week, or month) and includes counts and monetary totals.

IShoppingMallOrderTrendStatistics.IOvera.description:
Overall aggregated order trend statistics across the entire analysis period.

This object summarizes key KPIs such as total order count, total GMV, and average order value computed from shopping_mall_orders monetary snapshot fields (items_subtotal_amount, discount_total_amount, shipping_total_amount, tax_total_amount, grand_total_amount) and currency_code.

All monetary amounts in this structure are expressed in the same ISO 4217 currency indicated by `currency_code`, and they represent aggregates of the `grand_total_amount` values for the orders that fall into the analysis window and filter set.

It represents the headline numbers for an order analytics dashboard, providing a single, normalized snapshot that can be combined with more detailed time-bucketed trend data and per-status breakdowns.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code (for example, USD, EUR, KRW) used when computing monetary aggregates from shopping_mall_orders.

All monetary fields in this summary (such as `total_gmv_amount` and `average_order_amount`) are expressed in this currency and should be interpreted consistently with the platform’s pricing and settlement configuration.

total_order_count.description:
Total number of orders included in the statistics window.

This typically counts unique records in shopping_mall_orders that match the internal filters, such as time range, store scope, region, or additional analytics constraints.

total_gmv_amount.description:
Total GMV (Gross Merchandise Value) amount over the analysis period.

This value is typically computed as the sum of `grand_total_amount` from shopping_mall_orders for all included orders, expressed in the currency specified by `currency_code`.

average_order_amount.description:
Average order value over the analysis period.

This is usually computed as `total_gmv_amount` divided by `total_order_count`, and is expressed in the same currency as `currency_code`. Implementations may round to an appropriate number of decimal places for the configured currency.

status_counts.description:
Distribution of orders by `order_status` across the entire analysis period.

Each entry contains a status label and the corresponding order count, derived from the `order_status` column of shopping_mall_orders for orders that match the analytics filters.

IShoppingMallOrderTrendStatistics.IStatu.description:
Aggregate count of orders for a specific order_status over a given scope.

This is used both in overall summaries and in individual time buckets to show how many orders are currently or historically in a particular lifecycle state such as pending_payment, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled, or refunded.

order_status.description: Order lifecycle status label as recorded in shopping_mall_orders.order_status (for example, pending_payment, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded). The exact set of values is determined by the platform’s order status enum.

order_count.description: Number of orders that match this order_status in the relevant aggregation scope (overall or within a specific time bucket).

IShoppingMallOrderTrendStatistics.ITimeB.description:
Time-bucketed trend metrics computed from shopping_mall_orders over a specific time grain.

Each bucket corresponds to a single period in the selected time series (for example, a day, week, or month) and aggregates order counts and monetary totals for orders whose placed_at or created_at timestamps fall within that period.

These buckets are primarily used for plotting charts and graphs in analytics dashboards.

bucket_start.description: Start timestamp of the time bucket in ISO 8601 format. This typically corresponds to the beginning of the period (for example, 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z for a daily bucket).

bucket_end.description: End timestamp of the time bucket in ISO 8601 format. This typically corresponds to the end of the period (for example, 2025-01-01T23:59:59Z for a daily bucket). Implementations may choose either inclusive or exclusive semantics but should be consistent.

order_count.description: Total number of orders in this time bucket, usually counting records from shopping_mall_orders whose placed_at or created_at values fall within [bucket_start, bucket_end).

total_gmv_amount.description: Total GMV (grand_total_amount) aggregated for all orders in this bucket, expressed in the same currency_code as the overall summary.

average_order_amount.description: Average order value for this bucket, typically computed as total_gmv_amount divided by order_count. Implementations may return 0 or null when order_count is 0 depending on internal rules.

status_counts.description: Distribution of orders by order_status within this time bucket, aggregated from shopping_mall_orders.order_status.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationReasonStat.description:
Aggregated statistics about order cancellation reasons derived from the shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests table.

This DTO is used for analytics and reporting endpoints that help platform administrators and operations teams understand why orders are being cancelled, who is initiating the cancellations, and how resolution outcomes are distributed.

The structure contains overall counts as well as breakdowns by reason category and actor_type, enabling dashboards to visualize top cancellation reasons and their relative proportions.

total_cancellation_request_count.description: Total number of order cancellation requests considered in this statistics response. The count is derived from shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests records that match the internal filters and time window applied by the implementation.

reason_categories.description: Aggregated statistics per request_reason_category, showing how often each category appears and how it is distributed by actor_type and resolution outcome.

actor_segments.description: Aggregated statistics per actor_type, such as customer, seller, or platform_admin. Each segment describes how many cancellation requests the actor initiated and how these requests are distributed by reason and status.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationReasonStat.description:
Aggregate statistics for a single cancellation request_reason_category.

This object represents how often a particular reason category appears in shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests and provides breakdowns by actor_type and resolution outcome. It is useful for identifying dominant reasons for cancellations, such as changed_mind, ordered_by_mistake, stock_issue, or policy_violation.

request_reason_category.description: Cancellation reason category label as stored in shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests.request_reason_category (for example, changed_mind, ordered_by_mistake, stock_issue, policy_violation). The exact set of values is defined by the platform’s business rules.

request_count.description: Total number of cancellation requests that use this request_reason_category in the aggregation scope.

actor_type_counts.description: Distribution of this reason category by actor_type (for example, customer, seller, platform_admin). Each entry indicates how many requests in this category were initiated by each actor type.

resolution_counts.description: Distribution of resolution outcomes for this reason category, derived from request_status and resolution_category in shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests (for example, approved, rejected, auto_approved).

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationReasonStat.description:
Aggregate statistics for cancellation requests initiated by a specific actor_type.

This object focuses on how a particular actor segment (such as customer, seller, or platform_admin) behaves with respect to cancellations, including how many requests they raise and how those requests distribute across reason categories and resolution outcomes.

actor_type.description: Actor type that initiated the cancellation requests, matching shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests.actor_type (for example, customer, seller, platform_admin).

request_count.description: Total number of cancellation requests initiated by this actor_type in the aggregation scope.

reason_category_counts.description: Breakdown of this actor_type’s cancellation requests by request_reason_category, indicating which reasons this actor segment most frequently selects.

resolution_counts.description: Distribution of resolution outcomes for requests initiated by this actor_type, derived from request_status and resolution_category.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationReasonStat.description:
Count of cancellation requests for a specific actor_type within a given reason category.

This DTO is used inside IReasonCategoryStatistics to show how many requests for that category were initiated by customers, sellers, or platform administrators.

actor_type.description: Actor type value from shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests.actor_type (for example, customer, seller, platform_admin).

request_count.description: Number of cancellation requests in the enclosing aggregation (for example, a specific reason category) that were initiated by this actor_type.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationReasonStat.description:
Aggregate count of cancellation requests for a specific resolution outcome.

This object is used to capture how many requests ended in each resolution category (for example, approved, rejected, auto_approved, withdrawn), allowing analytics to show resolution distributions per reason category or per actor segment.

resolution_category.description: Resolution category label derived from shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests.resolution_category or from the combination of request_status and resolution_category (for example, approved, rejected, auto_approved, withdrawn). Implementations may normalize internal enums into human-readable values for this field.

request_count.description: Number of cancellation requests in the aggregation scope that ended with this resolution_category.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationReasonStat.description:
Count of cancellation requests for a specific `request_reason_category` within a single `actor_type` segment.

This DTO is a nested analytics bucket used inside higher‑level cancellation statistics responses such as `IShoppingMallOrderCancellationReasonStatistics.IActorSegmentStatistics`. Each instance represents how often a particular normalized cancellation reason category (for example, `changed_mind`, `ordered_by_mistake`, `stock_issue`, or `policy_violation`) appears for one specific actor type, such as a customer, seller, or platform administrator.

At the data layer, the `request_reason_category` value corresponds directly to the text stored in the `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests.request_reason_category` column. The `request_count` value is computed by grouping rows in `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests` by both `actor_type` and `request_reason_category` and then counting the number of records in each group. This makes the DTO strictly read‑only and suitable for dashboards, operational reports, and analytics tools that need to highlight which standardized cancellation reasons dominate within each actor segment.

request_reason_category.description:
Cancellation reason category label as stored in `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests.request_reason_category`.

Typical examples include normalized values such as `changed_mind`, `ordered_by_mistake`, `stock_issue`, or `policy_violation`. These categories allow the platform to group many individual free‑form explanations into a small set of analyzable buckets and to compare behavior across different actor types and time periods.

request_count.description:
Number of cancellation request records in `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests` for the enclosing actor segment that use this `request_reason_category`.

This value is produced by a group‑by aggregation over cancellation requests, counting how many rows share both the same `actor_type` and the same `request_reason_category`. It is always a non‑negative integer and is commonly used to sort reason categories by frequency or to compute percentages relative to the total number of cancellation requests for the actor segment.

IShoppingMallReturnReasonStatistics.description:
Aggregated statistics of order return reasons over a selected analysis window.

This DTO represents a read‑only analytical projection computed from the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model. Instead of exposing individual return request rows, it summarizes how frequently standardized return reason categories and fine‑grained reason codes occur within a specific time range and under optional filters such as seller, product, or region. The structure is designed for administrative dashboards, operational reports, and internal analytics tools, and it is never written directly to the database.

Internally, the analytics query scans `shopping_mall_order_return_requests`, applies the requested filters (including the `from`/`to` time bounds typically against the `created_at` column, and any seller, product, or region constraints), and then computes both a global total of matching rows and grouped metrics per reason. The `reasonGroups` collection is produced by grouping the filtered rows on normalized reason dimensions (for example, reason category and reason code) and counting the size of each group while also deriving a share ratio relative to `totalReturns`. This gives platform administrators a clear view of which return reasons dominate over the selected period and helps them detect spikes in product defects, size or fit issues, logistics problems, or change‑of‑mind returns.

totalReturns.description:
Total number of order return request records in `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` that match all applied filters for this statistics computation.

This count is the denominator used when deriving per‑reason share ratios in `reasonGroups`. It reflects the combination of the analysis time window defined by `from` and `to` (usually applied to the `created_at` column) and any additional filters such as seller, product, or region that the calling API may enforce or expose as query parameters.

from.description:
Inclusive start timestamp of the analysis window used to compute these statistics, expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time string.

In the underlying query, this value is typically applied as a lower bound on `shopping_mall_order_return_requests.created_at` (or an equivalent business timestamp). Only return requests whose creation time is greater than or equal to this boundary are included in `totalReturns` and in the aggregated `reasonGroups` metrics.

to.description:
Exclusive end timestamp of the analysis window used to compute these statistics, expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time string.

Together with `from`, this field defines the exact time range of `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` rows that participate in the aggregation. Return requests with a creation time greater than or equal to `from` but strictly earlier than `to` are counted. This ensures that repeated invocations of the analytics endpoint with adjacent windows do not double‑count the same records.

reasonGroups.description:
Array of aggregated statistics buckets, each representing a single standardized return reason or reason category.

For each bucket, the analytics layer groups matching rows from `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` by normalized reason dimensions (for example, a high‑level reason category such as `defective_product`, `wrong_item`, `size_or_fit`, `changed_mind`, or `shipping_issue`, and a finer‑grained reason code) and computes the total count of rows and their proportional share relative to `totalReturns`. Consumers can use this list to build charts, tables, and alerts that highlight which return reasons dominate across the selected time window and filter set.

IShoppingMallReturnReasonStatistics.IRea.description:
Single bucket of aggregated statistics for a specific standardized order return reason or reason category.

Represents a group of one or more rows from shopping_mall_order_return_requests that share the same normalized reason classification. It exposes machine-oriented identifiers and human-readable labels together with aggregate metrics such as total count and percentage share within the analysis window.

When actor-specific subtypes of shopping_mall_order_return_requests are available (for example, customer-initiated versus seller-initiated flows), this bucket can optionally include separate counts per actor type so that dashboards can show how a given reason is distributed across different initiators.

reasonCategory.description:
High-level normalized category identifier for this return reason bucket, such as defective_product, wrong_item, size_or_fit, changed_mind, or shipping_issue.

This value is derived from the canonical reason category fields stored in shopping_mall_order_return_requests and is intended to remain stable over time so that analytics and reporting tools can safely group by it.

reasonCode.description:
Fine-grained normalized code that uniquely identifies a particular return reason within a category.

Examples might include product_damaged, product_missing_parts, wrong_color, too_small, or delivery_delayed. This code is suitable for stable programmatic filtering and aggregation and should be aligned with the normalized reason code taxonomy stored in shopping_mall_order_return_requests.

reasonLabel.description:
Human-readable label for this return reason, intended for direct display on administrative dashboards and reports.

Upstream presentation layers may localize this label into different languages, so it should be treated as display text rather than a stable programmatic key. The underlying categorization should instead rely on reasonCategory and reasonCode.

returns.description:
Number of individual order return request records that fall into this reason bucket within the selected analysis window and applied filters.

This count is typically computed by grouping rows in shopping_mall_order_return_requests by the normalized reason fields and counting the number of matching records.

shareRatio.description:
Proportion of totalReturns represented by this reason bucket, expressed as a ratio between 0 and 1.

For example, a value of 0.25 means this reason accounts for 25% of all return requests included in the current aggregation scope. The denominator is usually the sum of returns across all buckets in the same response.

customerReturns.description:
Number of return requests in this reason bucket that were initiated by customers within the selected analysis window and filters.

This value is typically derived from shopping_mall_order_return_requests joined with its customer-specific subtype (for example, shopping_mall_order_return_request_of_customers) and indicates how many returns for this reason originated from customer-side flows. It may be omitted or left at zero in responses where actor-type breakdowns are not requested or not available.

sellerReturns.description:
Number of return requests in this reason bucket that were initiated by sellers or through seller-driven workflows within the selected analysis window and filters.

This value is computed from shopping_mall_order_return_requests combined with any seller-specific subtype, and it helps operations and risk teams understand how many returns for this reason are driven by seller-side actions such as proactive returns or adjustments. It may be omitted or left at zero when the analytics query does not compute actor-type breakdowns.

IShoppingMallDisputeReasonStatistics.description:
Aggregated statistics of order dispute reasons over a selected analysis window.

Represents a read-only analytical projection computed primarily from the shopping_mall_order_disputes Prisma model and, when necessary, its actor-specific subtype tables. Each instance describes overall aggregation metadata and a collection of per-reason statistics groups summarizing how frequently each standardized dispute reason appears. This DTO is intended for internal dashboards, risk monitoring tools, and management reports and is not directly persisted to any single database table.

totalDisputes.description: Total number of order disputes considered in this statistics computation after all filters are applied. This value is typically derived from counting rows in shopping_mall_order_disputes within the analysis window and serves as the denominator for percentage calculations.

from.description: ISO 8601 timestamp representing the inclusive start of the analysis window used to compute these dispute statistics. This window is applied against the relevant timestamp field in shopping_mall_order_disputes, such as created_at.

to.description: ISO 8601 timestamp representing the exclusive end of the analysis window used to compute these dispute statistics. Combined with the from field, it defines the time range of disputes included in this aggregation.

reasonGroups.description: Array of aggregated statistics per standardized dispute reason or category. Each entry groups multiple raw dispute records that share the same normalized reason dimensions and exposes counts and ratios for that bucket.

IShoppingMallDisputeReasonStatistics.IRe.description:
Single bucket of aggregated statistics for a specific standardized order dispute reason or reason category.

Represents a group of one or more rows from shopping_mall_order_disputes that share the same normalized dispute reason classification. It provides machine-oriented identifiers, human-readable labels, and aggregated metrics such as dispute count and share ratio. Optional fields can also summarize how disputes in this bucket are distributed across actor types.
