reasonCategory.description: High-level normalized category identifier for this dispute reason bucket, such as non_delivery, damaged_item, not_as_described, billing_issue, or service_quality. This value is derived from the canonical dispute reason category fields in shopping_mall_order_disputes.

reasonCode.description: Fine-grained normalized code that uniquely identifies a particular dispute reason within a category. Examples might include package_never_arrived, item_broken, item_incorrect_description, overcharged, or rude_support. This code is intended for stable programmatic analysis.

reasonLabel.description: Human-readable label for this dispute reason, intended for direct display in administrative dashboards and analytical reports. Upstream layers may localize this label for different languages.

disputes.description: Number of individual dispute records that fall into this reason bucket within the selected analysis window and applied filters.

shareRatio.description: Proportion of totalDisputes represented by this reason bucket, expressed as a ratio between 0 and 1. For example, 0.1 means this reason accounts for 10% of all considered disputes.

customerDisputes.description: Number of disputes in this reason bucket that were initiated by customers, computed from rows that have corresponding records in shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_customers. This metric is optional and may be zero if actor-specific breakdowns are not requested or available.

sellerDisputes.description: Number of disputes in this reason bucket that were initiated by sellers, derived from rows that have corresponding records in shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_sellers. This metric is optional and may be zero when actor-specific breakdowns are not computed.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering request DTO for listing shopping mall payment methods for platform administrators.

This schema allows internal admin UIs to specify complex search criteria, pagination, and sorting when querying configurable payment methods stored in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. It is not exposed to public checkout flows.

page.description: 1-based page index for paginated results. If omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return per page. The backend may enforce an upper bound (for example 200) regardless of the client-provided value.

code.description: Optional exact or prefix filter on the business code of the payment method (for example "card", "bank_transfer"). The matching behavior (exact vs LIKE) is defined by the backend implementation.

method_type.description: Optional filter for the logical payment method type. Typical values include "card", "bank", "wallet", or "offline" depending on the Prisma enum or string column definition.

is_active.description: Optional filter by activation status. When true, only currently active payment methods are returned. When false, only inactive methods are returned. When null or omitted, activation status is not used as a filter.

currency_restriction.description: Optional filter matching the currency restriction definition for a payment method, when such a restriction is modeled (for example a currency code or pattern).

min_amount_from.description: Optional lower bound filter for the configured minimum amount (inclusive). Only payment methods whose configured minimum amount is greater than or equal to this value will match. Expressed in the platform’s base currency units.

min_amount_to.description: Optional upper bound filter for the configured minimum amount (inclusive). Only payment methods whose configured minimum amount is less than or equal to this value will match.

max_amount_from.description: Optional lower bound filter for the configured maximum amount (inclusive). Only payment methods whose configured maximum amount is greater than or equal to this value will match.

max_amount_to.description: Optional upper bound filter for the configured maximum amount (inclusive). Only payment methods whose configured maximum amount is less than or equal to this value will match.

available_at_from.description: Optional lower bound of an availability window intersection filter. Only payment methods whose [starts_at, ends_at] window overlaps this instant will match, using this value as the start of the query window.

available_at_to.description: Optional upper bound of an availability window intersection filter. Only payment methods whose [starts_at, ends_at] window overlaps this instant will match, using this value as the end of the query window.

search.description: Optional free-text search term applied to display_name, description, or other text columns as defined by the backend implementation.

sort_field.description: Name of the column or logical sort key to order by. Typical values include "priority", "display_name", or "created_at". Unsupported values should be rejected by validation or ignored according to platform rules.

oneOf.description: Sort direction to apply to sort_field. Must be either "asc" for ascending or "desc" for descending ordering.
Sort direction to apply to sort_field. Must be either "asc" for ascending or "desc" for descending ordering.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction to apply to sort_field. Must be either "asc" for ascending or "desc" for descending ordering.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IRequest.descriptionExtra: No x-autobe-prisma-schema linkage is defined for IRequest types because they represent query parameter envelopes rather than a direct mapping to a single Prisma model.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.description:
Detailed configuration DTO for a single payment method defined in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table.

This schema is used by platform administrative APIs to return the full state of a configurable payment method, including its code, display characteristics, type classification, activation status, availability window, amount limits, lifecycle timestamps, and administrative ownership context.

The properties in this DTO map directly to columns in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma model, excluding secrets or credentials, and additionally surface the creating and last-updating platform administrators as summary association objects for rich back-office tooling.

id.description:
UUID primary key of the payment method configuration record in shopping_mall_payment_methods.

This identifier is stable over the lifetime of the configuration and is used by administrative APIs as the path parameter `paymentMethodId` when retrieving, updating, or deleting the payment method.

code.description:
Business-meaningful unique code that identifies this payment method.

Typical examples include short machine-readable codes such as `card`, `bank_transfer`, or provider-specific identifiers. The value participates in the unique index on `shopping_mall_payment_methods.code` and is used by internal routing, business rules, and integration logic to reference the method consistently.

display_name.description:
Human-readable label shown in administrative UIs and, when appropriate, in customer-facing selection screens.

This value is intended for display to humans, for example `Credit Card` or `Bank Transfer`, and should be localized or otherwise chosen so that operators and customers can easily understand which payment option they are interacting with.

description.description:
Optional longer description of the payment method, including business notes or explanations for administrators.

When present, this field can describe eligibility rules, operational caveats, or partner-specific information that is useful for internal staff. A null value indicates that no additional descriptive text has been configured beyond the display name.

provider_key.description:
Optional logical identifier that ties this payment method configuration to an underlying payment provider or gateway profile.

Typical values reference a payment gateway configuration key, a PSP profile identifier, or another integration-specific handle that the payment orchestration layer uses when executing authorize and capture flows. Null indicates that no provider mapping is recorded at the configuration level or that it is implied by other configuration.

method_type.description:
Logical classification of the payment method such as `card`, `bank`, `wallet`, or `offline`.

This value is used by business rules, analytics, and risk engines to group payment methods by behavior. The exact allowed values are controlled by the Prisma model and business constraints, and clients should treat this string as an opaque but stable classification token.

currency_restriction.description:
Optional currency restriction definition that constrains which currencies this payment method supports.

Implementations may store a delimited list or pattern of ISO currency codes, or another structured expression, depending on business design. When null, the method is treated as currency-agnostic at the configuration level and may be further constrained by other domain rules.

min_amount.description:
Optional minimum order amount at which this payment method may be offered, expressed in the platform’s base currency units.

Checkout logic should compare the order total against this threshold and suppress the method when the order value is below the configured minimum. A null value indicates that no method-level lower bound is applied.

max_amount.description:
Optional maximum order amount at which this payment method may be offered, expressed in the platform’s base currency units.

When set, this field is used to prevent the payment method from being shown or selected for orders exceeding the specified amount, which can help manage risk exposure for high-value transactions. A null value means there is no method-specific upper bound.

priority.description:
Integer used to control display ordering of this payment method relative to others.

Lower numeric values are typically rendered earlier in selection lists in both administrative and customer-facing UIs. This property does not affect functional behavior but influences the visual prominence of the method.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this payment method is currently active and eligible for new checkouts, subject to its availability window and other constraints.

When false, the method remains stored for historical reference and may still be associated with past payment transactions, but it will not be offered for new orders even if it falls within any configured date range.

starts_at.description:
Optional datetime when this payment method becomes available for use.

If set, the method should only be considered eligible for selection in checkouts when the current time is greater than or equal to this timestamp. A null value means there is no start-time gating and activation is governed solely by the `is_active` flag and other business rules.

ends_at.description:
Optional datetime after which this payment method is no longer available for new checkouts.

If set, the method should not be offered for orders with a current time beyond this timestamp, although historical transactions may continue to reference it. A null value indicates that there is no configured automatic end-of-availability date.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payment method configuration record was created in the system, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value is managed by the backend and reflects the moment the row was first inserted into `shopping_mall_payment_methods`. It is useful for audit trails and chronological reporting of configuration changes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last update to this payment method configuration record, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

The backend updates this value whenever mutable fields on the configuration are changed, enabling operators to see when the definition was most recently adjusted.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp used to logically remove this payment method from active configuration lists while preserving historical references.

When this value is non-null, the method should be treated as deleted for the purposes of configuration management and checkout eligibility. Historical payment transactions and audit logs continue to reference the record, allowing operators to analyze past behavior even after the method is no longer available for new use.

A null value indicates that the payment method has not been soft-deleted and should be evaluated for visibility according to `is_active`, date-based availability windows, and other business rules.

created_by_admin.description:
Summary of the platform administrator who initially created this payment method configuration.

This association is derived from the nullable foreign key `created_by_platformadmin_id` and the corresponding Prisma relation `createdByAdmin`. When null, it indicates that the creator is unknown in the current data set or that the configuration was seeded without a specific admin actor context.

updated_by_admin.description:
Summary of the platform administrator who most recently updated this payment method configuration.

This association is derived from the nullable foreign key `updated_by_platformadmin_id` and the Prisma relation `updatedByAdmin`. When null, it indicates that the configuration has not yet been updated since creation, or that the updater information is not available.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ICreate.description:
Creation DTO for defining a new payment method configuration on the shoppingMall platform.

This type mirrors the writable business columns of the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma model and is used exclusively by platform administrators when registering a new payment method that becomes available during checkout. It excludes system‑managed auditing and ownership fields so that the backend can populate them from the authenticated platformAdmin context.

Admin UIs send this structure in the request body of the creation endpoint, and the backend validates it against the Prisma model constraints such as required fields, unique code, and numeric ranges for optional amount limits.

code.description:
Business identifier for the payment method, unique across the platform.

Typical examples are short machine‑readable codes such as "card", "bank_transfer", or provider‑specific keys. The value must satisfy the unique index on shopping_mall_payment_methods.code and is used by internal logic and integrations to refer to the method in a stable way.

display_name.description:
Human readable name shown to customers at checkout.

This value is presented in checkout and backoffice UIs to describe the payment method in end‑user friendly terms, for example "Credit Card" or "Bank Transfer". It should be localized or selected so that customers can clearly understand which payment option they are selecting.

description.description:
Optional longer description of the payment method.

This field may contain additional guidance or business notes about when and how the method can be used, such as eligibility rules, expected processing times, or special restrictions. When null, no extra descriptive text is stored beyond the display name.

provider_key.description:
Identifier of the underlying payment provider configuration that backs this method.

The value typically maps to a gateway profile, PSP configuration key, or internal integration identifier that the payment processing layer uses to route authorize and capture requests. It must correspond to a valid provider configuration understood by the platform’s payment subsystem.

method_type.description:
Logical type of the payment method such as "card", "bank", "wallet", or "offline".

Business logic and reporting can use this string to group and filter methods by their high‑level behavior. Implementations should prefer a controlled vocabulary agreed within the platform so that analytics and rules engines can reliably reason over the values.

currency_restriction.description:
Optional expression describing which currencies this payment method supports.

Implementations may store a delimited list or pattern of ISO currency codes when the method is not globally available for all currencies. When null, the method is treated as currency‑agnostic and may be offered for any checkout currency according to other business rules.

min_amount.description:
Optional minimum order amount required to use this payment method.

When provided, the value is expressed in the platform’s primary currency and is used at checkout time to prevent customers from choosing the method for orders below the configured threshold. A null value means no lower bound is enforced at the payment method level.

max_amount.description:
Optional maximum order amount allowed when using this payment method.

If set, this value specifies an upper limit in the platform’s primary currency above which customers cannot select this method at checkout. A null value indicates that there is no method‑specific upper bound beyond any global or risk‑based limits applied elsewhere.

priority.description:
Display priority for this payment method in checkout lists.

Lower numeric values are shown earlier when presenting available payment methods to customers. Admins can adjust this integer to control ordering in the UI without impacting the functional behavior of the payment processing logic.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this payment method is currently available for new checkouts.

When true, and when within any configured active window, the method is considered eligible to be shown to customers. When false, the method is hidden from new checkout flows but remains in the database so that historical payment transactions can continue to reference it.

starts_at.description:
Optional datetime after which this payment method becomes eligible for use.

This field allows administrators to schedule activation in advance, for example for a promotional payment partner. When null, there is no start‑time gating and the method’s availability is controlled solely by is_active and business rules.

ends_at.description:
Optional datetime after which this payment method should no longer appear in checkout selections.

It can be used to schedule the end of a promotion or sunset a payment method gracefully. When null, there is no automatic end time and the method stays available as long as is_active remains true.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing payment method configuration on the shoppingMall platform.

This type exposes the subset of shopping_mall_payment_methods columns that platform administrators are allowed to change after a payment method has been created. All properties are optional so callers can perform partial updates while the backend enforces additional business rules such as immutability of certain critical attributes when needed.

The DTO is used in administrative configuration endpoints that adjust labels, activation windows, ordering, and gateway configuration without affecting historical payment transactions that already reference the method.

code.description:
New business identifier for the payment method when renaming or normalizing codes.

Changing this value must continue to satisfy the unique constraint on shopping_mall_payment_methods.code and should be done carefully because downstream integrations and configuration may rely on the code. Many deployments will choose to keep this immutable in practice even if the schema allows updates.

display_name.description:
Updated human readable name shown to customers at checkout.

Administrators can use this field to refine wording, apply localization strategies, or clarify the meaning of the payment option without affecting technical identifiers or historical records.

description.description:
Revised longer description of the payment method, or null to clear it.

This field can be adjusted to reflect new eligibility rules, marketing text, or operational guidance. Setting it to null removes any previously stored explanatory text.

provider_key.description:
Updated identifier of the underlying payment provider configuration.

This allows migration of a payment method to a different gateway profile or integration key. Implementations should ensure that any change preserves compatibility with in‑flight operations and adheres to risk and compliance policies.

method_type.description:
Updated logical type of the payment method such as "card", "bank", "wallet", or "offline".

Adjusting this value can influence reporting and rules engines that categorize payment behavior. Changes should be coordinated with the platform’s analytics and risk logic to avoid inconsistent classification.

currency_restriction.description:
New currency restriction expression for the payment method, or null to remove restrictions.

Administrators may refine which currencies are eligible for this method as business relationships evolve, for example enabling additional markets or narrowing support to specific regions.

min_amount.description:
Updated minimum order amount required to use this payment method.

Raising or lowering this threshold enables fine‑grained control over the order sizes for which the method can be selected. Setting the field to null removes any method‑specific minimum, deferring to global or product‑level constraints.

max_amount.description:
Updated maximum order amount allowed when using this payment method.

Changes to this field can be used to manage risk exposure for high‑value orders. A null value removes an existing cap so that larger orders may again use the method, subject to other risk controls.

priority.description:
New display priority for this payment method in checkout lists.

Administrators adjust this integer to reorder how methods appear to customers, with lower values placing the method earlier in the list. This has no impact on the technical behavior of the payment processing logic.

is_active.description:
Updated activation flag determining whether the payment method appears in new checkouts.

Toggling this value allows administrators to quickly enable or disable a payment method without deleting it, preserving its use in historical transactions while stopping new customers from selecting it when set to false.

starts_at.description:
New scheduled activation datetime for this payment method, or null to remove start‑time gating.

Updating this field allows administrators to shift the start of availability for promotional windows or delay activation if business requirements change.

ends_at.description:
New scheduled deactivation datetime for this payment method, or null to keep it available indefinitely.

Adjustments to this field are used to extend, shorten, or cancel planned sunset periods for the method’s visibility in checkout flows.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying payment transactions in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is used by platform administrators and internal tools to request a paginated, sorted list of payment transactions from the shopping_mall_payment_transactions table. It encapsulates rich search conditions including status filters, payment method, date ranges, amounts, currency, and identifiers for related entities such as orders or customers, along with pagination and sorting options.

The fields in this request are designed to map directly to columns in the `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` Prisma model (and its key relations) so that the backend can translate filters efficiently into indexed queries. By combining these filters, finance, risk, and support teams can quickly isolate transactions for reconciliation, incident investigation, and operational monitoring without overfetching unnecessary data.

page.description:
1-based page index used for pagination when querying payment transactions.

This value controls which slice of the overall result set is returned. It must be a positive integer, and together with `limit` it determines the offset into the `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` table or its derived view.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page.

This value constrains the page size for the result set and is typically capped to prevent excessively large responses that could impact performance. A reasonable default may be applied by the server when the client omits this field.

sortBy.description:
Field name to sort payment transactions by.

Typical values include logical column names such as `createdAt`, `status`, or `amount`, which the backend maps to the appropriate database columns like `created_at`, `payment_status`, or `captured_amount`. Implementations should restrict this to a safe allowlist to avoid accidental misuse or ambiguity.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for the specified `sortBy` field in ascending order.

Use this value when you want earlier or smaller values (for example older timestamps or lower amounts) to appear first in the result set.

Sort direction for the specified `sortBy` field in descending order.

Use this value when you want later or larger values (for example newer timestamps or higher amounts) to appear first in the result set.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for the specified `sortBy` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the backend may apply a sensible default such as descending by creation time so that the most recent transactions are shown first.

statusList.description:
Optional list of payment status values to include in the search results.

When provided, only transactions whose normalized business status (for example `payment_pending`, `payment_captured`, `payment_failed`, `partially_refunded`, or `refunded`) matches one of the values in this array are returned. The exact set of allowed values should align with the `payment_status` column and any documented status vocabulary.

paymentMethodId.description:
Identifier of the payment method to filter by.

This corresponds to the foreign key `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` on `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`. When provided, only transactions processed through the specified payment method configuration are included in the results.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code used to filter payment transactions by currency.

This should be an uppercase three-letter code such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`. When set, only transactions whose `currency` column matches this value are returned, which is useful when admins are focused on a particular settlement currency.

minAmount.description:
Inclusive minimum captured (or effective) amount filter.

Only payment transactions with a monetary amount greater than or equal to this value are returned. Implementations typically apply this filter against the captured amount or primary transactional amount column in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, depending on how monetary values are modeled.

maxAmount.description:
Inclusive maximum captured (or effective) amount filter.

Only payment transactions with a monetary amount less than or equal to this value are returned. This is often used together with `minAmount` to constrain results to a particular range for reconciliation or risk reviews.

customerId.description:
Identifier of the customer whose payment transactions should be included in the results.

When specified, the search is limited to transactions whose `shopping_mall_customer_id` matches this value. This is commonly used in customer support scenarios where all payments associated with a single customer must be inspected.

orderId.description:
Identifier of the order associated with the payment transactions to search for.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_id` on `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`. When provided, only payment transactions linked to the specified order are returned, which is useful when drilling into payment history for a particular order.

createdFrom.description:
Start of the creation date range filter for transactions (inclusive).

This must be an ISO 8601 date-time string (for example `2025-01-01T00:00:00Z`). Only payment transactions with `created_at` greater than or equal to this timestamp are considered, enabling time-window based reports and investigations.

createdTo.description:
End of the creation date range filter for transactions (inclusive).

This must be an ISO 8601 date-time string (for example `2025-01-31T23:59:59Z`). Only payment transactions with `created_at` less than or equal to this timestamp are included, typically in combination with `createdFrom` to define a bounded analysis period.

providerName.description:
Name or code of the payment provider (gateway) handling the transaction.

This filter maps to the `provider_name` column of `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`. Use it to restrict results to transactions processed by a particular gateway or provider integration when analyzing provider-specific behavior, incidents, or reconciliation tasks.

providerTransactionId.description:
External transaction identifier assigned by the payment provider.

This corresponds to the `provider_transaction_id` column in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` and is commonly used when a finance or support agent needs to locate the platform transaction that corresponds to a provider-side reference encountered in bank statements, provider dashboards, or support tickets.

paymentIntentKey.description:
Logical payment intent key that groups multiple provider interactions for the same conceptual payment.

This filter maps to the `payment_intent_key` column and can be used to retrieve all transactions associated with a single intent, such as multiple authorization attempts or retried captures, when investigating complex payment flows.

providerStatus.description:
Raw or provider-specific status code associated with the latest known state of the provider transaction.

This aligns with the `provider_status` column in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`. It allows operations and risk teams to search based on gateway-native statuses in addition to the normalized `payment_status` values managed by the platform.

failureReasonCode.description:
Code describing why the payment failed, using platform-defined or provider-defined categories.

This filter corresponds to the `failure_reason_code` column. It is particularly useful when analysts or support staff need to isolate transactions that failed for a specific technical or business reason, such as `card_declined`, `insufficient_funds`, or `risk_blocked`.

requiresManualReview.description:
Flag indicating whether the payment transaction requires manual review.

When set to `true`, only transactions whose `requires_manual_review` column is true are returned, which is ideal for driving manual review queues and operational dashboards. When set to `false`, callers can explicitly focus on transactions that do not require manual intervention.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.description:
Detailed representation of a payment transaction stored in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions table.

This DTO is used in administrative and internal views for inspecting the full state of a single payment transaction, including lifecycle amounts, provider information, and links to the associated order, customer, and payment method. It closely mirrors the underlying Prisma model to support reconciliation, monitoring, and operational support flows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment transaction in the `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` table.

This is the primary key of the record and is used as the canonical reference in all relations and API paths that operate on payment transactions.

orderId.description:
Identifier of the order that this payment transaction is associated with.

This value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key column and links the payment transaction to the customer-facing order in the shopping mall domain.

customerId.description:
Identifier of the customer who owns the order and initiated the payment.

This value corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key column. It may be null in edge cases where the customer record is unavailable or the transaction is not tied to a standard customer account.

paymentMethodId.description:
Identifier of the payment method configuration used for this transaction.

This value is derived from the `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` foreign key column and links the transaction to a row in the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` configuration table.

paymentMethod.description:
Summary information about the payment method used for this transaction.

This is a transformed association derived from the `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` foreign key and exposes key payment method metadata for administrative UIs without requiring an additional lookup.

paymentIntentKey.description:
Optional platform-side identifier that groups multiple provider interactions under a single logical payment intent.

This field corresponds to the `payment_intent_key` column and can be used to correlate authorizations, captures, and refunds belonging to the same high-level payment attempt.

providerName.description:
Name or code of the payment provider handling this transaction.

This field maps to the `provider_name` column and typically contains identifiers such as a gateway code or processor name used for routing, reporting, and reconciliation.

providerTransactionId.description:
Identifier of the transaction at the payment provider.

This value is derived from the `provider_transaction_id` column and is used when reconciling with provider reports, investigating issues with the payment gateway, or communicating with financial institutions.

currency.description:
ISO currency code for the monetary amounts associated with this transaction.

This corresponds to the `currency` column and should contain standard ISO 4217 currency codes such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`.

authorizedAmount.description:
Total amount that has been successfully authorized by the provider for this transaction.

This field is mapped from the `authorized_amount` column and represents funds that are reserved but not necessarily captured. It may be null if no authorization has been performed.

capturedAmount.description:
Total amount that has been successfully captured from the provider for this transaction.

This field is mapped from the `captured_amount` column and represents funds that have been successfully moved from the payer to the platform. It may be null if capture has not yet occurred.

refundedAmount.description:
Total amount that has been refunded against this payment transaction.

This value corresponds to the `refunded_amount` column and aggregates all related refund transactions, supporting reporting and customer service views.

paymentStatus.description:
Business payment status for the transaction.

This field is mapped from the `payment_status` column and typically uses values such as `payment_pending`, `payment_in_progress`, `payment_authorized`, `payment_captured`, `payment_failed`, `payment_expired`, `partially_refunded`, or `refunded` to describe the current lifecycle state.

providerStatus.description:
Latest known raw or provider-specific status code for the transaction.

This field maps to the `provider_status` column and contains gateway or processor status values that complement the normalized `paymentStatus` for troubleshooting and reconciliation.

failureReasonCode.description:
Optional code describing why the payment failed.

This corresponds to the `failure_reason_code` column and can use platform-defined or provider-defined categories to allow aggregated reporting on failure reasons.

failureReasonMessage.description:
Optional human-readable message explaining why the payment failed or could not be processed.

This field is derived from the `failure_reason_message` column and is used in administrative tools and logs to support investigation of payment issues.

requiresManualReview.description:
Indicates whether this payment transaction has been flagged for manual review.

This field maps to the `requires_manual_review` column and is typically set when fraud or risk checks detect anomalies, requiring a human operator to approve or reject the transaction.

metadataJson.description:
Optional JSON-encoded metadata associated with the transaction.

This corresponds to the `metadata_json` column and can contain arbitrary provider-specific payloads or business metadata. Interpretation is handled by application logic and operational tooling.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this payment transaction record was created.

This property reflects the `created_at` column and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this payment transaction record was last updated.

This property reflects the `updated_at` column and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new payment transaction record in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions table.

Used by internal orchestration services and platform administrators to register a new payment transaction attempt associated with an order. The DTO accepts foreign key identifiers for the related order, optional customer, and payment method, along with initial provider and lifecycle information required to persist the row.

orderId.description:
Identifier of the order that this payment transaction is associated with.

This value will be stored in the non-nullable `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key column and must reference an existing row in the `shopping_mall_orders` table.

customerId.description:
Optional identifier of the customer who owns the order and initiated the payment.

This value maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key column and, when provided, must reference an existing row in the `shopping_mall_customer` table.

paymentMethodId.description:
Identifier of the payment method configuration used for this transaction.

This field is persisted into the non-nullable `shopping_mall_payment_method_id` foreign key column and must reference an existing record in the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` table.

oneOf.description:
Optional platform-side identifier grouping multiple provider interactions for the same logical payment intent.

When provided, this value will be stored in the `payment_intent_key` column and can be used by orchestration logic to correlate authorization, capture, and refund flows belonging to the same intent.

paymentIntentKey.description:
Optional platform-side identifier grouping multiple provider interactions for the same logical payment intent.

When provided, this value will be stored in the `payment_intent_key` column and can be used by orchestration logic to correlate authorization, capture, and refund flows belonging to the same intent.

providerName.description:
Name or code of the payment provider handling this transaction.

This mandatory field maps to the `provider_name` column and should contain an integration-specific identifier such as the gateway or PSP name that will process the payment.

oneOf.description:
Optional identifier of the transaction at the payment provider.

When present, this value is stored in `provider_transaction_id` and typically represents the provider's transaction reference returned at authorization or capture time.

providerTransactionId.description:
Optional identifier of the transaction at the payment provider.

When present, this value is stored in `provider_transaction_id` and typically represents the provider's transaction reference returned at authorization or capture time.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for the amounts tracked in this payment transaction.

This field maps to the non-nullable `currency` column and must match the currency used by the associated order, such as `"USD"`, `"EUR"`, or `"KRW"`.

oneOf.description:
Total amount that has been authorized for this payment transaction at creation time, if known.

When provided, this value is stored in `authorized_amount` and describes the maximum amount that may later be captured from the provider.

authorizedAmount.description:
Total amount that has been authorized for this payment transaction at creation time, if known.

When provided, this value is stored in `authorized_amount` and describes the maximum amount that may later be captured from the provider.

oneOf.description:
Initial captured amount for this payment transaction at creation time, if any.

This field maps to the nullable `captured_amount` column and is typically left null when the flow is authorize-then-capture.

capturedAmount.description:
Initial captured amount for this payment transaction at creation time, if any.

This field maps to the nullable `captured_amount` column and is typically left null when the flow is authorize-then-capture.

paymentStatus.description:
Initial business payment status for this transaction.

This value is stored in the non-nullable `payment_status` column and should be set to a normalized status such as `"payment_pending"`, `"payment_in_progress"`, or `"payment_authorized"` according to platform rules.

oneOf.description:
Optional raw or provider-specific status code for the transaction at creation time.

This value is persisted into `provider_status` and is useful when the provider immediately returns a concrete status that needs to be retained for reconciliation.

providerStatus.description:
Optional raw or provider-specific status code for the transaction at creation time.

This value is persisted into `provider_status` and is useful when the provider immediately returns a concrete status that needs to be retained for reconciliation.

oneOf.description:
Optional code describing an initial failure state of the payment, if the transaction is created in a failed state.

Stored in `failure_reason_code`, and typically used when persisting records for failed attempts in retrospective processing or error reconciliation.

failureReasonCode.description:
Optional code describing an initial failure state of the payment, if the transaction is created in a failed state.

Stored in `failure_reason_code`, and typically used when persisting records for failed attempts in retrospective processing or error reconciliation.

oneOf.description:
Optional human-readable message describing an initial failure state of the payment.

This value maps to `failure_reason_message` and can help operators understand why a transaction was created with a failed status.

failureReasonMessage.description:
Optional human-readable message describing an initial failure state of the payment.

This value maps to `failure_reason_message` and can help operators understand why a transaction was created with a failed status.

oneOf.description:
Optional flag indicating whether this transaction should immediately be flagged for manual review.

If provided, this value is stored in `requires_manual_review`. When omitted, the backend may default this flag based on its own risk assessment rules.

requiresManualReview.description:
Optional flag indicating whether this transaction should immediately be flagged for manual review.

If provided, this value is stored in `requires_manual_review`. When omitted, the backend may default this flag based on its own risk assessment rules.

oneOf.description:
Optional JSON-encoded metadata from business logic or the provider to be stored alongside the payment transaction at creation time.

This field corresponds to `metadata_json` and allows callers to attach structured data for downstream processes and debugging.

metadataJson.description:
Optional JSON-encoded metadata from business logic or the provider to be stored alongside the payment transaction at creation time.

This field corresponds to `metadata_json` and allows callers to attach structured data for downstream processes and debugging.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating mutable fields of an existing payment transaction record in the `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` table.

This schema is used by platform administrator tools to adjust non-final attributes of a payment transaction, such as provider reference identifiers, diagnostic failure information, review flags, and metadata, while preserving core financial integrity, ownership relations, and immutable lifecycle amounts.

All properties are optional to support PATCH-style partial updates. Business logic in the service layer is responsible for enforcing valid state transitions and preventing unsafe changes.

paymentStatus.description:
Updated business payment status for the transaction.

This field maps to the `payment_status` column and should only be changed according to the allowed payment lifecycle (for example, from `payment_pending` to `payment_authorized` or `payment_captured`). Illegal or unsafe transitions must be rejected by business logic.

providerTransactionId.description:
Updated identifier of the transaction at the payment provider.

This corresponds to the `provider_transaction_id` column and may be corrected when reconciling with provider reports or adjusting to late gateway callbacks. Setting this to null clears the stored provider transaction reference.

providerStatus.description:
Updated raw or provider-specific status code for the transaction.

This field maps to the `provider_status` column and can be synchronized with the gateway or processor when out-of-band notifications or manual interventions occur.

failureReasonCode.description:
Updated failure reason code for the transaction.

This corresponds to the `failure_reason_code` column and allows administrators or automated processes to refine the categorization of why a payment failed. Setting this to null clears the stored failure reason code.

failureReasonMessage.description:
Updated human-readable failure explanation for the transaction.

This field maps to the `failure_reason_message` column and can be used to add or correct diagnostic messages that help support staff understand payment issues. Setting this to null clears the stored message.

requiresManualReview.description:
Updated manual review flag for the payment transaction.

This property is mapped to the `requires_manual_review` column and allows backoffice or risk tooling to mark a transaction as requiring manual investigation or to clear such a flag once review is complete.

metadataJson.description:
Updated JSON-encoded metadata payload associated with the transaction.

This corresponds to the `metadata_json` column and can be used to add, modify, or clear provider-specific or business-specific metadata. When set to null, any existing metadata is removed.

IShoppingMallPaymentAuthorization.IReque.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating payment authorization attempts for a specific payment transaction.

This schema is used by the PATCH `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/paymentTransactions/{paymentTransactionId}/authorizations` operation to express complex search filters, sorting options, and pagination parameters when listing rows from the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` table that belong to a given payment transaction.

It only represents query criteria and client-side paging configuration and therefore does not map directly to any Prisma model via `x-autobe-prisma-schema`. Business logic uses these fields to construct dynamic queries over the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` model, typically scoped by `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` from the path parameter.

page.description:
1‑based page index to retrieve when listing authorization attempts for the scoped payment transaction.

This value controls which slice of the result set is returned. When omitted, the backend should fall back to a sensible default such as page 1.

Must be a positive integer; values less than 1 should be rejected by validation logic.

limit.description:
Maximum number of authorization records to return in a single page for the current query.

This property is used together with `page` to implement server‑side pagination over `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations`. Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large pages for platform admin tools.

Typical values are in the range of 10–100 depending on UI needs and performance characteristics.

authorization_status.description:
Optional filter for the business‑level authorization status of attempts in `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations`.

Examples include values like `authorized`, `authorization_failed`, or `authorization_voided`, matching the semantics described in the Prisma column documentation.

When provided, only authorization attempts whose status matches this value are included in the response. When omitted, authorizations of all statuses for the transaction may be returned.

created_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the creation timestamp range for authorization attempts, expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time string.

When non‑null, only authorizations whose `created_at` in `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` is greater than or equal to this value are included. Use this to narrow searches to more recent authorization activity.

If null or omitted, no minimum creation time filter is applied.

created_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the creation timestamp range for authorization attempts, expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time string.

When non‑null, only authorizations whose `created_at` in `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` is less than or equal to this value are included in the result set.

If null or omitted, no maximum creation time filter is applied.

sort_by.description:
Optional field name used to sort the authorization list for the current query.

Typical values for this endpoint include `created_at` or `amount`, allowing platform administrators to view the most recent or largest authorization attempts first.

If omitted, the backend should default to ordering by `created_at` in descending order to show the latest attempts first.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction applied when `sort_by` is specified.

Expected values are `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. Implementations should validate the value and default to `desc` when omitted to show the most recent or largest authorization attempts first.

This property influences only presentation order and does not affect the underlying stored data.

IShoppingMallPaymentAuthorization.description:
Detailed DTO representing a single payment authorization attempt stored in the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` table.

Each instance models one interaction with an external payment provider where funds are requested for authorization against a parent payment transaction recorded in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`. The record captures identifiers, status, amounts, and provider‑specific metadata that together describe the outcome and lifecycle of that attempt.

This schema is typically returned by administrative endpoints such as `GET /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/paymentTransactions/{paymentTransactionId}/authorizations/{authorizationId}` and by create/update operations as their response body. It exposes operational information needed for troubleshooting, reconciliation, and audit while omitting any credential‑like secrets or tokens.

id.description:
Primary key of the payment authorization attempt.

This value corresponds to the `id` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` Prisma model and uniquely identifies a single authorization record within the system.

It is generated by the backend and is used as the `authorizationId` path parameter in detail and update operations.

paymentTransaction.description:
Summary representation of the parent payment transaction that this authorization attempt belongs to.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key in the read DTO so that platform operators can immediately see which logical payment this authorization is part of without issuing additional API calls.

The referenced summary DTO corresponds to a row in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` and typically includes key fields such as transaction identifier, high‑level status, amounts, and actor context needed for reconciliation and audit views.

provider_authorization_id.description:
Identifier of the authorization at the external payment provider, such as a gateway authorization code or reference token.

This value corresponds to the nullable `provider_authorization_id` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` table and is used when later capturing or voiding the authorization with the provider.

When the provider does not return a stable authorization reference or the attempt fails before such an identifier is created, this field may be null.

amount.description:
Monetary amount that was requested for authorization in the transaction currency.

This value comes from the non‑nullable `amount` column in `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` and represents the portion of the payment transaction that this specific authorization attempt is trying to reserve.

It should be interpreted in the smallest currency unit supported by downstream payment logic (for example, cents for many currencies) according to platform conventions and must be non‑negative.

currency.description:
ISO currency code for the authorized amount associated with this attempt.

This field maps to the non‑nullable `currency` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` table and should match the currency of the parent payment transaction in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`.

Examples include values like `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`, following standard three‑letter ISO 4217 codes.

authorization_status.description:
Business status representing the outcome or current state of this authorization attempt.

It maps to the non‑nullable `authorization_status` column in `shopping_mALL_payment_authorizations` and captures values such as `authorized`, `authorization_failed`, or `authorization_voided` as described in the Prisma schema comments.

Backoffice flows and reconciliation tools use this value to understand whether funds are available for capture, whether retries are needed, or whether the authorization lifecycle has ended.

provider_status.description:
Raw status or result code returned by the payment provider for this authorization attempt.

This property reflects the nullable `provider_status` column in `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` and is typically a gateway‑specific code, message key, or short text describing the provider’s interpretation of the attempt.

It is primarily used for diagnostics and mapping provider outcomes into the normalized `authorization_status` values used by the platform.

expires_at.description:
Datetime at which the authorization is expected to expire according to the payment provider’s rules.

This maps to the nullable `expires_at` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` table. Before this timestamp, funds are normally considered reserved and eligible for capture; after it, the provider may automatically release or void the authorization.

For providers that do not supply explicit expiry information, this field may be null and the platform will rely on default policy or provider documentation.

failure_reason_code.description:
Optional machine‑readable code describing why the authorization failed when `authorization_status` indicates a failure.

The value comes from the nullable `failure_reason_code` column in `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` and may be derived from gateway response codes, internal risk engine decisions, or business validation rules.

Administrative tools can use this code for filtering and analytics across large sets of failed authorizations.

failure_reason_message.description:
Optional human‑readable message explaining why the authorization failed.

This property maps to the nullable `failure_reason_message` column in `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` and may contain either provider‑supplied text or a normalized explanation generated by the platform.

It is primarily intended for operator and support staff consumption and may be surfaced in admin UIs to aid troubleshooting without exposing low‑level raw provider messages directly to end users.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this authorization record was created in the platform.

This corresponds to the non‑nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` table and represents the moment the platform persisted the authorization attempt.

It is used for ordering, time‑based filtering, and audit analysis of authorization activity across transactions.

IShoppingMallPaymentAuthorization.ICreat.description:
DTO schema for creating a new payment authorization attempt associated with an existing payment transaction in the shopping_mall_payment_authorizations table.

Used by internal platform admin or backend orchestration logic when recording a new authorization attempt against a specific payment transaction. Actor identity (platform admin) comes from authentication context, not from this DTO.

amount.description: Monetary amount requested for authorization for this attempt, expressed in the smallest currency unit or standard decimal representation as defined by the payment domain. Must not exceed the remaining payable amount on the parent payment transaction.

currency.description: Currency code for the authorization amount, typically an ISO 4217 currency code such as "USD" or "KRW".

gateway_code.description: Identifier of the payment gateway or processor used for this authorization attempt. Allows differentiating between multiple configured payment providers.

gateway_authorization_id.description: External identifier of the authorization in the payment gateway or processor system. Used to correlate platform records with provider-side authorization objects.

channel.description: Logical channel or context in which the authorization attempt was performed (for example, "web", "mobile", or an internal orchestration channel identifier).

risk_metadata.description: Optional structured risk or fraud-related metadata sent to or returned from the processor for this authorization attempt. This is a free-form JSON object whose structure is defined by the payment risk engine or gateway contract.

IShoppingMallPaymentAuthorization.IUpdat.description:
DTO schema for updating an existing payment authorization attempt record in the shopping_mall_payment_authorizations table.

Used by internal payment orchestration logic or platform administrators to modify mutable fields such as gateway response messages, processor status codes, or supplemental risk metadata. Immutable lifecycle fields (such as final capture state) must not be included here and are enforced at the service layer.

authorization_status.description:
Normalized business-level authorization status for this attempt as tracked by the platform.

This field maps directly to the `authorization_status` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` Prisma model and corresponds to the `authorization_status` property exposed on the `IShoppingMallPaymentAuthorization` read DTO.

Only certain lifecycle transitions are allowed according to the platform’s payment rules. Attempts to perform illegal transitions (for example, moving a terminal failure state back to an authorized state) are rejected by the service layer even though this field is writable in the update DTO.

gateway_status_code.description:
Status or result code reported by the external payment processor or gateway for this authorization attempt.

This value is typically a short code or symbolic identifier that can be mapped back to provider documentation or internal risk handling rules.

It is used primarily for diagnostics, reporting, and for driving automated workflows that respond to gateway outcomes.

gateway_status_message.description:
Human-readable status message or explanation returned by the payment gateway or processor for the latest state of this authorization.

This text can help operations and support staff understand why a particular authorization succeeded, failed, or entered an exceptional state.

The message content should generally come from the provider, but may also include normalized messages generated by the platform.

risk_metadata.description:
Updated structured risk or fraud-related metadata associated with this authorization attempt.

This field allows attaching or overwriting a structured JSON document that captures risk scoring results, rule hits, device fingerprints, or other fraud analysis signals relevant to the authorization.

Its internal structure is intentionally flexible to accommodate different risk engines and provider contracts, and is therefore represented as a generic JSON object wrapper type rather than a fixed set of strongly-typed properties.

IShoppingMallPaymentCapture.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for filtering payment capture records associated with a specific payment transaction.

This DTO is used by platform administrators to query capture attempts under a given payment transaction. It supports pagination, sorting, and field-based filtering mapped to the `shopping_mall_payment_captures` model and related status metadata.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve when paginating capture results.

This value must be a positive integer greater than or equal to 1. If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default (for example, page 1). Values less than 1 are treated as invalid and will result in a validation error.

pageSize.description:
Maximum number of capture records to return in a single page.

The backend enforces an upper bound (for example, 100 records per page) to protect performance. If a client supplies a value larger than the configured maximum, the request may either be rejected with a validation error or normalized down to the allowed maximum according to service policy.

sortKey.description:
Field used for sorting capture records in the result set.

Only a whitelisted set of sort keys is allowed, typically aligned with indexed columns in `shopping_mall_payment_captures`, such as `created_at` (capture creation timestamp), `amount`, or `capture_status`. Supplying an unsupported sort key will cause the service to return a validation error so that clients can adjust their requests.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the selected sort key.

`asc` sorts in ascending order, and `desc` sorts in descending order.

Sort direction applied to the selected sort key.

`asc` sorts in ascending order, and `desc` sorts in descending order.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction applied to the selected sort key.

`asc` sorts in ascending order, and `desc` sorts in descending order.

status.description:
Optional capture status filter.

When provided, limits results to captures in the specified normalized capture status used by the platform, such as `capture_succeeded` or `capture_failed`. These values typically map to the `capture_status` column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures`.

minAmount.description:
Optional lower bound on the captured amount.

When provided together with `maxAmount`, the backend returns captures whose captured amounts fall within the inclusive range between `minAmount` and `maxAmount`. The amount is interpreted in the currency of the underlying payment transaction.

maxAmount.description:
Optional upper bound on the captured amount.

When provided together with `minAmount`, the backend returns captures whose captured amounts fall within the inclusive range between `minAmount` and `maxAmount`. The amount is interpreted in the currency of the underlying payment transaction.

fromCapturedAt.description:
Start of the date-time range filter applied to the capture creation timestamp.

Captures created at or after this instant (inclusive) are eligible for inclusion in the result set. The value must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or a clearly specified timezone.

toCapturedAt.description:
End of the date-time range filter applied to the capture creation timestamp.

Captures created at or before this instant (inclusive) are eligible for inclusion in the result set. The value must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or a clearly specified timezone.

gatewayReference.description:
Optional payment gateway reference identifier filter.

When provided, restricts results to captures associated with the given provider capture identifier or a matching identifier fragment, typically corresponding to the `provider_capture_id` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_captures` table.

IShoppingMallPaymentCapture.description:
Detailed representation of a payment capture attempt recorded in the `shopping_mall_payment_captures` model.

A payment capture represents the movement of funds against a previously authorized payment transaction. Each capture belongs to a parent payment transaction and may reference a specific authorization. This DTO is used primarily by platform administrators and internal payment orchestration services to inspect the full details of a capture, including identifiers, amounts, status, timestamps, and gateway references.

Unlike the underlying Prisma model, this read model exposes associations to the payment transaction and authorization as summary objects instead of raw foreign key identifiers. It also surfaces key provider-facing fields such as provider capture identifiers, provider status codes, and failure diagnostics that map directly to columns on `shopping_mall_payment_captures`, while some timestamps like `requestedAt` and `completedAt` may be derived from payment status events or gateway metadata rather than being direct columns.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment capture record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of a row in `shopping_mall_payment_captures` and is used as the stable reference for capture-level operations such as detail retrieval and updates.

It is globally unique within the payment subsystem and is typically generated by the platform at creation time.

paymentTransaction.description:
Summary representation of the parent payment transaction that this capture belongs to.

This replaces the raw `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key from the Prisma model and provides sufficient context for backoffice users to understand which order-level payment this capture interacts with.

The summary typically includes identifiers, high-level status, and key monetary fields of the transaction without expanding into full order or customer graphs.

authorization.description:
Summary representation of the payment authorization that this capture draws funds from, when the capture is tied to a specific authorization record.

This replaces the optional `shopping_mall_payment_authorization_id` foreign key in the Prisma model and gives operators immediate insight into the underlying authorization without requiring an additional lookup.

When no standalone authorization record exists or the relationship is not used, this field is null.

amount.description:
Monetary amount captured from the underlying payment authorization.

This value corresponds to the `amount` column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures`. It is stored in the same currency as the parent payment transaction and reflects the requested capture amount for this specific attempt.

Business rules ensure that the amount is positive and does not exceed the sum of authorized minus already captured amounts for the transaction.

currency.description:
Currency code associated with the captured amount, represented as an ISO 4217 alpha-3 code such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`.

This value maps to the `currency` column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures` and mirrors the currency of the parent payment transaction.

It is used for both reporting and validation of capture amounts, and the platform typically normalizes this field to upper-case three-letter codes and rejects mismatched currency configurations at the time of capture creation.

status.description:
Current business status of the capture attempt within the payment lifecycle.

This property is the read-model projection of the `capture_status` column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures` and typically takes values such as `capture_pending`, `capture_succeeded`, or `capture_failed` according to the platform's payment status vocabulary.

It reflects the platform-level interpretation of the capture’s state, which may be derived from provider callbacks, internal workflows, or manual interventions, and it drives downstream behavior such as updating captured totals, triggering refunds, or flagging reconciliation issues in reporting dashboards.

gatewayReference.description:
Identifier or reference returned by the external payment gateway for this capture attempt.

This field is derived from the `provider_capture_id` column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures` and may mirror that value exactly. It is used during reconciliation, troubleshooting, and dispute handling to correlate platform records with the provider’s capture object or transaction.

The format and semantics of this field are provider-specific and should be treated as opaque by most consumers of the API.

providerCaptureId.description:
Raw provider capture identifier as stored on the `shopping_mall_payment_captures.provider_capture_id` column.

Whereas `gatewayReference` exposes a normalized or convenience view for operators, this field preserves the exact value persisted in the database for low-level reconciliation, debugging, or migration scenarios.

It is typically populated when the platform initiates a capture with the gateway or when an externally initiated capture is mirrored into the platform, but it may be null when no provider identifier is yet available.

providerStatus.description:
Raw status code returned by the payment provider that describes the capture’s state at the gateway level.

This property maps directly to the `provider_status` column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures` and is usually a provider-specific keyword or code such as `succeeded`, `pending`, or a detailed failure code.

It is primarily used for deep reconciliation and troubleshooting and is not necessarily suitable for end-user display without translation into the platform’s normalized `status` field.

failureReasonCode.description:
Machine-readable code that categorizes why the capture failed when the business `status` indicates a failure state.

This field corresponds to the `failure_reason_code` column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures` and can store either platform-defined error codes or provider-supplied failure categories, for example `insufficient_funds`, `card_declined`, or `risk_rejected`.

It supports downstream analysis and automated workflows such as retry policies, manual review queues, and risk analytics.

failureReasonMessage.description:
Human readable explanation describing why the capture failed or encountered issues.

This property maps directly to the `failure_reason_message` column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures` and can contain messages from the payment provider, internal validation errors, or operator-authored notes captured at the time the capture was recorded.

It is intended for support and operational users who need detailed context when investigating payment issues and is typically not shown directly to end customers.

requestedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the capture request was initiated by the platform.

Unlike `createdAt`, which is based on the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_payment_captures`, this field may be derived from payment status events or orchestration metadata that records the instant the platform decided to move funds, either by calling an external gateway API or by mirroring an externally initiated capture.

When the implementation does not track this separate timestamp, `requestedAt` may be null or simply match `createdAt`. Values are expressed as ISO 8601 date-time strings in UTC.

completedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the payment gateway reported the capture as completed, either successfully or with a definitive failure.

This field is typically derived from provider callbacks or payment status events rather than a dedicated column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures`. It becomes non-null once the provider confirms success or failure and is stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

The timestamp is commonly used in financial reconciliation and settlement calculations to align capture events with accounting periods; it remains null while the capture is still pending or its outcome is unknown.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the capture record was first created in the platform database.

This property maps directly to the `created_at` column on `shopping_mall_payment_captures` and is stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

It serves as the primary audit field for when the capture entity entered the system and is often used for sorting, filtering, and determining reporting windows.

IShoppingMallPaymentCapture.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new payment capture attempt under an existing payment transaction in the shoppingMall platform.

This request body maps to the `shopping_mall_payment_captures` Prisma model and contains only the business fields that clients are allowed to provide when initiating a capture. It is used by privileged backoffice or orchestration services to request that funds be captured against a previously authorized payment transaction.

The server supplements these values with system-managed identifiers, timestamps, and status transitions, and it enforces that the capture belongs to a valid `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` record and optionally to a valid `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations` record.

shopping_mall_payment_authorization_id.description:
Identifier of the payment authorization this capture is based on, when the platform or gateway requires an explicit authorization reference.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.shopping_mall_payment_authorization_id` and points to a row in `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations`. It is optional to support flows where the capture is initiated at the transaction level without a distinct authorization record.

When provided, the implementation must validate that the referenced authorization belongs to the same parent payment transaction as indicated by the endpoint path, and that the authorization is still eligible for capture according to provider rules.

provider_capture_id.description:
Identifier of the capture at the payment provider when the caller already holds a gateway-level capture reference.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.provider_capture_id` and may be used in reconciliation scenarios where the capture has been initiated externally and is being mirrored into the platform. The value is provider-specific and typically opaque to the platform.

When omitted or null, the platform or gateway integration may create and assign a provider capture ID during processing.

amount.description:
Monetary amount to capture from the previously authorized payment transaction, expressed in the transaction currency.

This maps to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.amount`. The value must be strictly greater than zero and must not exceed the remaining capturable balance on the parent `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` record once prior captures have been accounted for.

Business rules should ensure that the amount respects currency precision rules and the limits defined by the associated payment method and provider.

currency.description:
ISO currency code for the capture amount, such as "USD" or "EUR".

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.currency` and must match the currency stored on the parent `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` record. The platform should reject any attempt to capture in a currency that is inconsistent with the original transaction or the configured `shopping_mall_payment_methods` entry.

Validation logic should treat the value as case insensitive but persist it using a normalized representation such as upper-case three-letter codes.

capture_status.description:
Initial business status for this capture attempt, such as "capture_pending", "capture_in_progress", or an equivalent domain-specific value.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.capture_status` and records how the capture should be interpreted at creation time. Typical patterns include marking the capture as pending when it has been requested but not yet confirmed by the provider, or as succeeded when mirroring an already-completed capture from an external system.

The implementation should restrict acceptable values to the platform’s configured capture status vocabulary and transition the status as provider notifications and internal events occur.

provider_status.description:
Raw status code returned by the payment provider that describes the capture’s state at the gateway level.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.provider_status` and is usually a provider-specific keyword or code such as "succeeded", "pending", or gateway error codes. It is primarily used for deep reconciliation and troubleshooting and is not directly exposed to end users.

When set at creation time, it should reflect the latest known provider state associated with this capture attempt.

failure_reason_code.description:
Optional machine-readable code that categorizes why the capture failed when `capture_status` represents a failure state.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.failure_reason_code` and can store either platform-defined error codes or provider-supplied failure categories. It supports downstream analysis and automated workflows such as retry policies or manual review queues.

When the capture is created in a non-failed state, this field should generally remain null.

failure_reason_message.description:
Optional human readable explanation describing why the capture failed or encountered issues.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.failure_reason_message` and can contain messages from the payment provider, internal validation errors, or operator notes at the time the capture is recorded. It is intended for support and operational users rather than end customers.

When the capture is created in a successful or pending state without errors, this message is typically omitted or left null.

IShoppingMallPaymentCapture.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying mutable attributes of an existing payment capture attempt in the shoppingMall platform.

This schema maps to the `shopping_mall_payment_captures` Prisma model but includes only fields that business rules permit to change after initial creation, such as provider status, failure metadata, or certain status transitions.

It is intended for privileged internal services or platform administrators to correct or enrich capture records while preserving the integrity of core financial attributes such as the capture amount, currency, and parent transaction relationships.

provider_capture_id.description:
Updated identifier of the capture at the payment provider, when the gateway reference changes or is first learned after creation.
