This property corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.provider_capture_id`. It can be used to backfill or adjust the provider capture reference for reconciliation purposes when the value was not known at creation time or has been corrected by operational processes.

If omitted, the existing provider capture identifier on the record remains unchanged.

capture_status.description:
New business capture status describing the current state of the the capture attempt, such as transitioning from a pending to a succeeded or failed state.

This property maps to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.capture_status` and is used when internal processes or provider callbacks update the platform’s understanding of the capture. The implementation should ensure that transitions follow allowed status flows and that financial side effects (such as updating captured totals) are handled elsewhere in the payment domain logic.

When omitted, the capture retains its existing status value.

provider_status.description:
Updated raw status code received from the payment provider that reflects the most recent gateway-level state of the capture.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.provider_status` and is primarily for detailed reconciliation and debugging. It should track the exact provider codes without translation so that support teams can align logs and dashboards with external systems.

When omitted, the previously stored provider status remains unchanged.

failure_reason_code.description:
New or corrected machine-readable code that explains why the capture failed when the business status indicates a failure.

This maps to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.failure_reason_code` and may be set or revised as additional information becomes available from the gateway or internal risk systems. Typical usage includes categorizing errors into buckets such as insufficient_funds, card_declined, or risk_rejected.

If omitted, the existing failure reason code is retained.

failure_reason_message.description:
Updated human readable message that describes why the capture failed or encountered problems, useful for operators reviewing payment issues.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_captures.failure_reason_message`. It may be sourced from provider error messages, internal error logs, or admin-authored notes, and it should provide clear context for future troubleshooting.

When omitted, the previously stored message is left unchanged.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusEvent.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for listing payment status events associated with a specific payment transaction in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by platform administrators to query the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` audit table for a particular payment transaction. It supports pagination, sorting, and optional filters such as status code and created-at range. All results are automatically scoped to the payment transaction identified by the path parameter, so no transaction identifier appears in this schema.

page.description: 1-based page index for paginated search results. If omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return in a single page. Implementations should enforce an upper bound (for example 100) to protect the system from excessively large result sets.

status.description: Optional filter for the payment status value recorded in each status event. This should match the status enumeration used by the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` table (for example `initiated`, `authorized`, `captured`, `failed`, `refunded`, or other gateway-specific states).

origin.description: Optional filter indicating the origin of the status event, such as `gateway`, `system`, or `admin`, depending on how the payment status history is modeled in the Prisma schema comments.

fromCreatedAt.description: Inclusive lower bound for the event creation timestamp filter, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format. Events created before this timestamp are excluded.

toCreatedAt.description: Inclusive upper bound for the event creation timestamp filter, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format. Events created after this timestamp are excluded.

search.description: Optional free-text search term applied to human-readable message fields or metadata columns, allowing administrators to locate events by gateway references, error codes, or descriptive messages.

orderBy.description: Field name to use for sorting the result set. Typical values include `created_at` or `status`. If omitted, implementations should default to sorting by newest creation timestamp first.

oneOf.description: Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field. Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order.
Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field. Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order.

orderDirection.description: Sort direction applied to the `orderBy` field. Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusEvent.description:
Detailed representation of a single payment status event in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO models one row of the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` Prisma table, which records the chronological history of status changes for payment transactions stored in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`. Each status event captures the business payment status before and after the event, the categorized event type, any provider-specific identifiers, optional human-readable notes, and the timestamp when the event was recorded.

Instances of this type are returned by administrative or internal tooling endpoints that expose the payment status history to platform operators, risk teams, or customer support agents. They are read-only from the perspective of external clients; creation and modification are restricted to trusted backend flows.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment status event record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` table and uniquely distinguishes a single status history entry for a payment transaction.

It is generated and managed by the backend and is returned as part of read operations, but never accepted from clients in create or update DTOs.

payment_transaction_id.description:
Identifier of the parent payment transaction in the `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` table to which this status event belongs.

This field mirrors the `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key column in the Prisma model and establishes the hierarchical parent–child relationship between a payment transaction and its timeline of status events.

It is primarily useful for debugging and correlation in read models; write operations obtain the parent transaction context from path parameters rather than from the request body.

paymentTransaction.description:
Summary representation of the parent payment transaction that this status event belongs to.

This object provides key contextual information—such as transaction identifiers, high‑level status, amounts, and payment method details—without expanding into the full transaction graph. It allows administrative tools and dashboards to render a status event together with its associated payment transaction details in a single response.

The summary variant is used here instead of the full transaction DTO to prevent circular references and excessive payload size while still giving sufficient context for monitoring, audit, and customer support workflows.

previous_status.description:
Payment status before this event was applied, using the same business vocabulary as the `payment_status` field on the parent transaction.

This value is copied from the transaction’s prior effective payment status at the moment the event is recorded. It may be null for the first event in a transaction’s lifecycle, or when the previous status cannot be determined.

Support and analytics tooling can compare `previous_status` and `new_status` to understand how the payment state evolved over time.

new_status.description:
Payment status after this event was applied, using the same business vocabulary as the `payment_status` field on the parent transaction (for example `payment_pending`, `payment_authorized`, `payment_captured`, `payment_failed`, `partially_refunded`, or `refunded`).

This field mirrors the non-nullable `new_status` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` Prisma model and represents the effective business status of the payment immediately after this event.

It should be kept consistent with any subsequent updates to the parent transaction’s `payment_status` field so that history and aggregate views remain aligned.

event_type.description:
Categorized type of status event, such as `provider_webhook`, `manual_update`, or `system_transition`.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `event_type` column in `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` and classifies the operational origin or nature of the event in a controlled string vocabulary.

Downstream analytics and dashboards use this category to segment and filter status histories—for example, to separate gateway-driven changes from operator-driven overrides.

provider_event_code.description:
Optional raw event code from the payment provider when the event was triggered by an external notification.

This corresponds to the nullable `provider_event_code` column in the Prisma model and typically stores gateway-defined event or message codes that are meaningful for reconciliation and vendor-specific diagnostics.

When present, tools can use this value together with `provider_reference` to correlate status history with external provider logs.

provider_reference.description:
Optional reference identifier from the payment provider, such as an event ID, webhook notification ID, or provider-side trace identifier.

This field directly maps to the nullable `provider_reference` column in `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` and helps operators track a particular event back to external systems.

Combined with `provider_event_code`, it is often used for support investigations and dispute handling that involve third‑party payment gateways.

notes.description:
Optional human readable notes describing the reason or context for this status change.

This value corresponds to the nullable `notes` column in the Prisma model and is typically used for internal explanations, manual operator comments, or normalized gateway messages.

Although it can be exposed in admin UIs and audit reports, it should not be relied upon as a structured field for automated logic—use `event_type`, `provider_event_code`, and `provider_reference` for that purpose.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this status event was recorded in the system, expressed in ISO 8601 date‑time format.

This value mirrors the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` table and typically reflects the moment the platform persisted the event rather than the provider’s original event time.

It is used for ordering, audit timelines, and correlation with other operational logs and metrics.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusEvent.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new payment status event associated with a specific payment transaction in the shoppingMall platform.

This type is used by platform administrators or trusted internal services to append a new status entry into the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` timeline for a given `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` record. Callers provide the new business payment status, the event type categorizing the source or nature of the change, and any optional provider codes or human-readable notes.

The parent payment transaction is identified by the `paymentTransactionId` path parameter of the API operation, so no foreign key fields are present in this body. Immutable identifiers and system-managed timestamps such as `id` and `created_at` are generated by the backend and excluded from this DTO.

previous_status.description:
Optional payment status before this event was applied, using the same business vocabulary as the transaction’s `payment_status` field.

In many implementations the service layer can derive this value from the current `payment_status` on the transaction at the time of event creation, but this field is exposed to allow explicit overrides when necessary (for example, when reconstructing history from external logs).

If omitted or null, the backend may compute an appropriate previous status automatically based on existing status events for the transaction.

new_status.description:
Payment status after this event is applied, using the same normalized status vocabulary as the `payment_status` field on the parent transaction.

This value is required and maps directly to the non-nullable `new_status` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` table. Typical values include `payment_pending`, `payment_authorized`, `payment_captured`, `payment_failed`, `payment_expired`, `partially_refunded`, or `refunded`.

The service layer should validate that the transition from the previous effective status to this new status is allowed according to the platform’s payment state machine.

event_type.description:
Categorized type of status event, such as `provider_webhook`, `manual_update`, or `system_transition`.

This required field directly populates the non-nullable `event_type` column in `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` and describes how or why the status change occurred.

Back-office analytics and dashboards use this categorization to separate gateway-driven changes from operator-driven adjustments and system automation.

provider_event_code.description:
Optional raw event code supplied by the payment provider when the event originates from an external webhook or callback.

This value is mapped to the nullable `provider_event_code` column and is typically used for reconciliation, vendor support, and internal diagnostics that rely on provider-specific semantics.

Callers may omit this property when the event has no external provider source.

provider_reference.description:
Optional reference identifier from the payment provider associated with this status event, such as a webhook notification ID or provider-side trace ID.

This maps to the nullable `provider_reference` column in `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` and is helpful for correlating platform events with external system logs.

When provided together with `provider_event_code`, it allows precise cross-system tracing during investigations and audits.

notes.description:
Optional human-readable notes explaining the reason or context for this status change.

This field populates the nullable `notes` column and is suitable for free-form operator comments or normalized gateway messages that need to be stored for later review.

Although useful for admin UIs and reports, this field should not be used as a primary driver for automated logic because its structure and content may vary over time.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusEvent.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing payment status event record in the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` table.

This type is used by platform administrators or trusted backend services to correct or enrich previously stored status history entries for a payment transaction. Only mutable fields are included—primarily the before/after status strings, categorized event type, provider codes and references, and free-form notes.

Identifiers, foreign key references, and system-managed timestamps such as `id`, `payment_transaction_id`, and `created_at` are immutable from the API’s perspective and are therefore not part of this DTO. All properties are optional to support partial updates; the service layer is responsible for applying only the provided changes while enforcing audit and compliance rules.

previous_status.description:
Updated payment status before this event was applied, aligning with the `previous_status` column in the Prisma model.

This may be used to correct mis-recorded status transitions when historical data is reconciled or imported. When set to null, it indicates that the previous status is unknown or not applicable (for example, for the first event in a timeline).

Updates should be validated to ensure that the resulting transition from `previous_status` to `new_status` remains logically consistent with the platform’s payment state machine.

new_status.description:
Updated payment status after this event is applied, aligned with the `new_status` column.

While this field is non-nullable in the underlying Prisma model, the update DTO treats it as optional so that callers can perform partial updates without always specifying it. When provided, the new value must not violate business rules for allowed status transitions.

The implementation should ensure that any change here remains consistent with the parent transaction’s `payment_status` field and overall payment lifecycle.

event_type.description:
Updated event type categorizing the origin or nature of the status change, aligned with the `event_type` column.

This can be used to correct misclassified events, for example switching from `system_transition` to `manual_update` if an administrator later clarifies the event’s origin.

When null, the existing value is typically preserved; callers should only send this field when a meaningful change is required.

provider_event_code.description:
Updated raw event code from the payment provider, mapped to the `provider_event_code` column.

This may be adjusted when integrating with new provider semantics or when normalizing legacy data. Setting this field to null removes the stored provider event code.

Administrative tooling should only modify this value when there is a clear and traceable reason, to maintain the reliability of reconciliation workflows.

provider_reference.description:
Updated provider reference identifier associated with this status event, mapped to the `provider_reference` column.

This property is useful when correcting or re-linking events to external provider logs or when a provider supplies more accurate identifiers after initial ingestion.

Setting the value to null clears the previously stored reference.

notes.description:
Updated human-readable notes associated with this status event, mapped to the `notes` column.

Typical use cases include fixing typos, refining explanations, or removing sensitive information that should not be stored long term while still preserving the essential context of the event.

When set to null, the existing notes are cleared, which may be appropriate when redacting content under privacy or compliance requirements.

IShoppingMallRefundTransaction.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying refund transactions from the `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` table.

This type encapsulates filter criteria, sorting options, and pagination parameters used by administrative tools to locate refund transactions across the marketplace. It is intentionally read-only and does not represent any persisted database row.

The fields are aligned with the `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` Prisma model, focusing on typical search dimensions such as identifiers, status, actor type, reasons, amount ranges, and creation timestamps.

page.description:
1-based page index used for pagination when listing refund transactions.

Clients use this together with `limit` to navigate through large collections of refund transactions. Values less than 1 should be rejected or normalized to 1 by the server.

limit.description:
Maximum number of refund transaction records to return in a single page.

This value is used for pagination. The server should enforce an upper bound to protect performance, even if the client passes a larger number.

orderBy.description:
Field name used to sort refund transactions in the search result.

Typical values mirror columns on `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`, such as `created_at`, `requested_amount`, or `refund_status`. Servers may validate and restrict to a known whitelist.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied with `orderBy` when returning refund transactions.

Expected values are `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. If omitted, the server usually defaults to `desc` for date-based fields.

items.description:
Single refund status filter value applied when searching refund transactions.

Values are business-level status codes such as `refund_pending`, `refund_in_progress`, `refund_failed`, or `refund_completed`, matching the `refund_status` column semantics.

refundStatusList.description:
Optional list of refund status codes to filter results.

When provided, only refund transactions whose `refund_status` is contained in this list should be returned.

items.description:
Single actor type value indicating who initiated the refund.

Typical values are `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`, matching the `actor_type` column of `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`.

actorTypeList.description:
Optional list of actor types that initiated refunds.

When provided, results are filtered so that only refund transactions whose `actor_type` belongs to the list are returned.

items.description:
Single reason category value describing why the refund was created.

Examples include `customer_cancellation`, `seller_cancellation`, `return`, or `admin_adjustment`, corresponding to the `reason_category` column.

reasonCategoryList.description:
Optional list of reason categories to filter refund transactions.

Use this to restrict results to specific business reasons, such as only customer cancellations or only returns.

refundNumber.description:
Exact refund business identifier to search for.

This matches the `refund_number` column on `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`, which is unique per payment and used heavily in customer communication and reconciliation flows.

orderId.description:
Filter for refund transactions associated with a specific order.

This corresponds to the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` and is typically a UUID string.

paymentTransactionId.description:
Filter for refund transactions linked to a specific payment transaction.

This value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key and is usually a UUID string.

initiatorCustomerId.description:
Filter for refunds initiated by a specific customer.

This matches the `initiator_customer_id` foreign key column when populated and allows administrators to see all refunds requested by one buyer.

initiatorSellerId.description:
Filter for refunds initiated by a specific seller.

This corresponds to the `initiator_seller_id` foreign key column and is useful for inspecting refunds raised or approved by a particular merchant.

initiatorPlatformAdminId.description:
Filter for refunds initiated by a specific platform administrator.

This matches the `initiator_platformadmin_id` foreign key when refunds are created or adjusted directly by admin staff.

requestedAmountMin.description:
Lower bound for the requested refund amount when filtering.

Only refund transactions whose `requested_amount` is greater than or equal to this value should be returned.

requestedAmountMax.description:
Upper bound for the requested refund amount when filtering.

Only refund transactions whose `requested_amount` is less than or equal to this value should be returned.

createdAtFrom.description:
Start of the creation timestamp range filter.

Only refund transactions whose `created_at` is greater than or equal to this value are included in the results.

createdAtTo.description:
End of the creation timestamp range filter.

Only refund transactions whose `created_at` is less than or equal to this value are included in the results.

IShoppingMallRefundTransaction.description:
Detailed response DTO for a single refund transaction stored in the `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` table.

This type models a complete refund transaction row including business identifiers, references to the original payment transaction and order, actor and reason information, monetary amounts, currency, provider metadata, failure explanations, and lifecycle timestamps.

It is used as the response body for endpoints that retrieve or create individual refund transactions for administrative and financial workflows. Sensitive authentication details are excluded, but the entity exposes all fields required for reconciliation, support, and auditing based on the Prisma schema.

id.description:
Primary key of the refund transaction record.

This is an opaque unique identifier, typically generated as a UUID, and corresponds to the `id` column of `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`.

shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id.description:
Identifier of the payment transaction that this refund is applied to.

This is the raw foreign key value stored in the `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` column. It links the refund to the original payment context persisted in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` and is always present for a valid refund transaction.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order whose financial amounts are being refunded.

This is the raw foreign key value stored in the `shopping_mall_order_id` column and links the refund transaction back to the corresponding row in `shopping_mall_orders`. For all valid refund records this field is non-null.

initiator_customer_id.description:
Customer who initiated the refund request when it originates from the buyer.

This value corresponds to the `initiator_customer_id` foreign key. It is non-null only when `actor_type` is `"customer"`; in all other cases it will be null.

initiator_seller_id.description:
Seller who initiated the refund when the request originates from the merchant side.

This value corresponds to the `initiator_seller_id` foreign key. It is non-null only when `actor_type` is `"seller"`; in all other cases it will be null.

initiator_platformadmin_id.description:
Platform administrator who initiated or approved the refund when it is an admin-driven adjustment.

This value corresponds to the `initiator_platformadmin_id` foreign key. It is non-null only when `actor_type` is `"admin"`; in all other cases it will be null.

refund_number.description:
Business identifier for the refund transaction, unique per payment for audit and communication.

This value is used in correspondence with customers, sellers, and financial providers to reference a specific refund event and maps directly to the `refund_number` column.

refund_status.description:
Business status of the refund transaction.

Typical values include `refund_pending`, `refund_in_progress`, `refund_failed`, and `refund_completed`, describing the lifecycle of the refund from request through settlement or failure. This is backed by the `refund_status` column in the Prisma model.

actor_type.description:
Categorical type of the actor that initiated the refund.

Example values include `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`, mirroring the `actor_type` column and used in reporting and policy enforcement to distinguish the origin of the refund.

reason_category.description:
Categorized reason for the refund.

Values such as `customer_cancellation`, `seller_cancellation`, `return`, or `admin_adjustment` describe the high-level business reason associated with the refund and are stored in the `reason_category` column.

reason_message.description:
Optional free text explanation describing why the refund was requested or approved.

This field allows operators or automated systems to store additional narrative context alongside the structured `reason_category` and corresponds to the nullable `reason_message` column.

requested_amount.description:
Amount initially requested to be refunded in the payment currency.

This reflects the original requested refund amount before any approvals or partial adjustments, aligned with the `requested_amount` column of the Prisma model.

approved_amount.description:
Amount that was approved for refund according to policy.

This may be less than `requested_amount` when only part of the requested refund is granted. It corresponds to the nullable `approved_amount` column and may remain null while a refund is pending review.

refunded_amount.description:
Amount actually refunded through the payment provider once the refund is completed.

This reflects the final settled amount captured from the payment gateway, mapped to the nullable `refunded_amount` column and remaining null until the refund is executed or confirmed.

currency.description:
ISO currency code for all recorded amounts on this refund transaction.

This field mirrors the `currency` column and must be consistent with the original payment transaction’s currency for accurate reconciliation.

provider_refund_id.description:
Identifier for this refund at the external payment provider.

This value is used to cross-reference the refund in payment gateway dashboards, dispute tools, and financial exports, and corresponds to the nullable `provider_refund_id` column.

provider_status.description:
Raw status code from the payment provider describing the current state of the refund.

This may contain gateway-specific codes that complement the platform-level `refund_status` for debugging and reconciliation purposes and is stored in the nullable `provider_status` column.

failure_reason_code.description:
Optional machine-readable code describing why the refund failed.

When `refund_status` reflects a failure, this field stores the error or rejection code returned by the payment provider or internal validation. It maps to the nullable `failure_reason_code` column.

failure_reason_message.description:
Optional human-readable message giving more detail about a refund failure.

This is designed to support operator understanding and may be surfaced partially in support tools, aligning with the nullable `failure_reason_message` column.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund transaction record was created.

This value reflects when the refund request was first registered in the system and is stored in the `created_at` column.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund transaction record was last updated.

Any change to status, amounts, or provider metadata should update this field, mirroring the `updated_at` column on the Prisma model.

paymentTransaction.description:
Summary information about the payment transaction that this refund is applied to.

This association transforms the `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key into a rich, human-readable context using the `IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ISummary` DTO, so that administrative and finance tools can understand the payment context in a single API response.

order.description:
Summary view of the order whose financial amounts are being refunded.

This association transforms the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key into an `IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary` object, enabling consumers to access order-level context (such as order number, customer, and status) without issuing additional API calls.

initiatorCustomer.description:
Customer summary for the actor who initiated the refund when the originator is a buyer.

This association is populated when `actor_type` is `"customer"` and corresponds to the `initiator_customer_id` foreign key. It exposes a lightweight `IShoppingMallCustomer.ISummary` view so that administrators can see who requested the refund without an extra lookup.

initiatorSeller.description:
Seller summary for the actor who initiated the refund when the originator is a merchant.

This association is populated when `actor_type` is `"seller"` and corresponds to the `initiator_seller_id` foreign key. It exposes a lightweight `IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary` view that provides seller-level context for the refund.

initiatorPlatformAdmin.description:
Platform administrator summary when the refund was initiated or approved by an admin.

This association is populated when `actor_type` is `"admin"` and corresponds to the `initiator_platformadmin_id` foreign key. It exposes a lightweight `IShoppingMallPlatformAdmin.ISummary` view for audit and support tooling so that staff can see which admin user created or approved the refund.

IShoppingMallRefundTransaction.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new refund transaction in the shopping mall domain.

This type captures the input fields required to register a refund against an existing order and payment transaction. It focuses on the business-facing scalar columns of the `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` Prisma model that are set at creation time, including foreign keys to the payment transaction and order, reason information, requested amounts, and initial status and actor classification.

System-managed fields such as the primary key (`id`), audit timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`), and initiator linkage columns (`initiator_customer_id`, `initiator_seller_id`, `initiator_platformadmin_id`) are intentionally excluded from this DTO. Those values are derived from the authenticated context or persistence layer and must never be supplied by callers.

The DTO is intended for internal tools and services that initiate refunds as part of customer support, dispute resolution, or finance workflows. Server-side logic validates that requested refund amounts are allowed by the current order and payment state and by configured refund policies before persisting a new row in `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`.

shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id.description:
Identifier of the payment transaction that this refund is applied to.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` and links the refund to the original payment context stored in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`. The value must be a valid UUID of an existing payment transaction associated with the target order.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order whose financial amounts are being refunded.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.shopping_mall_order_id` and should reference an existing row in `shopping_mall_orders`. Business logic will validate that the order belongs to the same customer and payment transaction as the refund being created.

refund_number.description:
Business identifier for the refund transaction, unique per payment for audit and communication.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.refund_number`. It is used in customer-facing messages, back-office tools, and reconciliation reports to track individual refund events. Implementations should ensure uniqueness at least within the scope of a single payment transaction.

refund_status.description:
Initial business status of the refund transaction.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.refund_status` and typically uses values such as `"refund_pending"`, `"refund_in_progress"`, or `"refund_completed"` depending on the integration flow. At creation time this is usually set to a pending or requested status that indicates the refund has not yet been fully processed by the payment provider.

actor_type.description:
Categorical type of the actor that initiated the refund.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.actor_type` and is used for reporting and policy enforcement. Typical values include `"customer"`, `"seller"`, and `"admin"` indicating whether the refund was initiated by the buyer, a merchant, or a platform administrator. The concrete actor identity is resolved by the backend from authentication context rather than being provided directly in this DTO.

reason_category.description:
Categorized reason for the refund as a stable business code.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.reason_category` and helps downstream analytics and policy checks. Example values include `"customer_cancellation"`, `"seller_cancellation"`, `"return"`, and `"admin_adjustment"`.

The platform should manage the allowed category codes centrally so that client applications send only supported values.

reason_message.description:
Optional free-text explanation describing why the refund was requested or approved.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.reason_message`. When present, it should provide human-readable context for customer support agents and auditors. When no additional explanation is needed, this field can be null.

requested_amount.description:
Amount initially requested to be refunded in the payment currency.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.requested_amount`. It must be a non-negative numeric value and is typically validated so that it does not exceed the refundable balance computed from order and payment data.

approved_amount.description:
Amount that has been approved for refund, which may be less than the requested amount.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.approved_amount`. At creation time this may be set when a review step already determined the allowed refund amount, or left null to indicate that approval is still pending.

refunded_amount.description:
Amount that has actually been refunded through the payment provider once processing completes.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.refunded_amount`. For newly created refunds this value is usually null and will be filled later when the provider confirms settlement.

currency.description:
ISO currency code for all monetary amounts in this refund.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.currency` and must match the currency of the associated payment transaction. Typical values follow ISO 4217 codes such as `"USD"`, `"EUR"`, or `"KRW"`.

provider_refund_id.description:
Identifier for this refund at the external payment provider, if already known.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.provider_refund_id` and is used for reconciliation and support. It may be null at creation time if the provider reference is assigned asynchronously after the initial refund request is submitted.

provider_status.description:
Raw status code from the payment provider describing the current state of the refund.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.provider_status`. At creation time this may mirror the initial provider status if the refund is created in response to an immediate provider event, or be null when the refund has not yet been submitted.

failure_reason_code.description:
Optional code describing why the refund failed at the payment provider.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.failure_reason_code`. It is typically left null when the refund is first created and only populated if the provider later reports a failure or rejection.

failure_reason_message.description:
Optional human-readable message giving more detail about a refund failure.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.failure_reason_message`. It is intended for support staff and auditing, and is usually null when the refund is initially registered.

IShoppingMallRefundTransaction.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing refund transaction in the shopping mall domain.

This type represents the subset of `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` fields that are considered mutable after creation and that are safe to expose for updates via the API. It is used by administrative tools and internal services to adjust descriptive information, lifecycle statuses, provider metadata, and failure diagnostics, while preserving the integrity of the original financial snapshot.

Creation-time financial input fields such as `requested_amount` and `currency`, as well as structural linkage columns like `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id`, `shopping_mall_order_id`, and initiator foreign keys, are intentionally excluded from this DTO. Those values define the core financial context of the refund and must not be modified via general update operations.

All properties in this DTO are optional to support partial updates. System-managed fields such as the primary key and audit timestamps remain controlled by the persistence layer and are not exposed for direct modification.

refund_status.description:
Updated business status of the refund transaction.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.refund_status` and may be changed by administrators or automated workflows to reflect lifecycle transitions such as moving from pending to completed or failed.

actor_type.description:
Updated categorical type of the actor associated with this refund, if reclassified.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.actor_type`. While rarely changed, it can be adjusted in edge cases where the original classification of the initiator (for example, customer vs admin) was incorrect. The concrete actor identity remains server-controlled and is not directly updated via this DTO.

reason_category.description:
Updated categorized reason code for the refund.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.reason_category`. Administrators may correct or refine this code for reporting and policy reasons, for example changing a generic cancellation reason to a more specific return category.

reason_message.description:
Updated free-text explanation for the refund.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.reason_message` and can be edited to clarify why the refund was issued or to correct earlier notes.

approved_amount.description:
Updated amount that has been approved for refund.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.approved_amount` and may be set or adjusted as part of administrative approval workflows when the business decides to grant a different amount than originally requested.

refunded_amount.description:
Updated amount that has actually been refunded via the payment provider.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.refunded_amount` and is typically synchronized with provider notifications or reconciliation processes.

provider_refund_id.description:
Updated identifier for this refund at the payment provider.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.provider_refund_id` and may be populated after creation when the provider reference becomes available or corrected if it was entered incorrectly.

provider_status.description:
Updated raw status code reported by the payment provider.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.provider_status` and should reflect the latest known provider state for this refund.

failure_reason_code.description:
Updated failure reason code when the refund is rejected or fails at the provider.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.failure_reason_code` and is typically set only in error scenarios to support troubleshooting and reporting.

failure_reason_message.description:
Updated human-readable failure explanation from the provider or internal systems.

This maps to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions.failure_reason_message` and can be edited to improve clarity for support staff.

IShoppingMallRefundItem.description:
Refund item entity representing a single line-level component of a refund transaction in the shoppingMall payment and refund domain.

Each record models one granular component of a refund, such as the refunded portion of an order line, a tax adjustment, a shipping refund, or an additional manual adjustment entered by back-office operators. It is always owned by a parent refund transaction in the `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` model and may optionally point to specific order lines or seller segments to preserve traceability between refunds and the original order breakdown.

These rows are used to explain to customers, sellers, and financial systems how the total refund amount is composed. They support reconciliation, reporting, and integration with payment processors by clearly separating gross, tax, shipping, and net amounts. The schema mirrors the Prisma model `shopping_mall_refund_items` and must not introduce any fields that are not present in that model.

id.description:
Primary key of the refund item.

This identifier uniquely distinguishes each line-level refund component row inside the `shopping_mall_refund_items` table. It is generated by the database or application layer when the record is created and is used to reference this refund item from API responses, logs, and administration tools.

Clients treat this value as an opaque UUID and must not attempt to infer business meaning from its structure.

shopping_mall_refund_transaction_id.description:
Identifier of the parent refund transaction that owns this refund item.

This field links the refund item to a row in the `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` model and establishes the aggregate refund event context. All refund items under the same transaction ID together describe the full composition of the refund that will be posted back to the original payment.

In read DTOs this field is preserved to allow low-level reconciliation and joins against transaction views; create and update DTOs rely on the enclosing endpoint path parameter for this association.

shopping_mall_order_line_id.description:
Optional identifier of the related order line in `shopping_mall_order_lines` when this refund component targets a specific line item.

When present, this field points to the order line whose price, tax, or other line-specific amount is being refunded. This enables detailed reporting of how each order line was refunded over time and prevents double-refunds against the same underlying order item.

It is nullable to support refund components that are not tied to a single order line, such as shipping refunds or platform-level adjustments.

shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id.description:
Optional identifier of the related seller segment in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` when the refund is computed at seller scope rather than per line.

Seller segment references allow the system to express refunds that are aggregated across multiple lines for a given seller, for example when reversing all items handled by a particular merchant but not the entire multi-seller order.

The field is nullable so that refund components that are global to the order or unrelated to a single seller segment can still be represented.

component_type.description:
Type of amount being refunded for this line-level component.

Typical values include conceptual categories such as `item_price`, `tax`, `shipping`, or `adjustment`, expressing whether the refund relates to product charges, taxes, logistics costs, or manual corrections. The exact enumeration and validation rules are enforced at the business logic layer based on the platform's refund policy settings.

Clients and reporting systems can use this field to group and summarize refund items by category when presenting statements or analytics.

description.description:
Optional human-readable description of this refund component for explanatory purposes.

This text is suitable for customer-facing or operator-facing views and can provide details such as "Refund of shipping fee due to delayed delivery" or "Manual goodwill adjustment". It helps explain why a particular refund amount exists and how it was determined.

When null, the component is still fully valid and can be understood from its `component_type` and amount fields alone.

gross_amount.description:
Gross amount of this refund component before subtracting any fees, expressed in the currency used by the parent refund transaction.

This value typically mirrors the original charged amount for the referenced item portion, tax segment, or shipping fee that is being refunded. It is always stored as a numeric field and should respect the platform's monetary precision conventions, such as two decimal places for standard currencies.

Business rules ensure that the sum of `gross_amount` values under a refund transaction does not exceed the original captured amounts for the associated order or payment.

tax_amount.description:
Amount of tax included in this refund component when tax must be reported separately.

This field allows the platform to break out the tax portion of a refund for regulatory reporting or bookkeeping, especially in jurisdictions where tax refunds must be tracked distinct from product or service amounts.

When null, either no tax is associated with this component or tax is not being tracked separately for the given refund scenario.

shipping_amount.description:
Portion of shipping cost that is included in this refund component, when applicable.

If the refund is specifically refunding shipping charges (for example due to service-level failures or partial non-delivery), this field records how much of the shipping fee is being returned to the customer.

It is nullable so that non-shipping-related components, such as item price or general adjustments, do not need to populate a shipping-specific amount.

net_amount.description:
Net amount of this refund component after subtracting any non-refundable fees or adjustments.

The net amount reflects what is effectively returned to the customer for this component once card network fees, platform fees, or other non-refundable portions have been accounted for according to configured business rules.

When null, the application may infer net amount from gross and fee configuration, or the concept of net versus gross may not be applicable for this particular refund component type.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund item record was created in the system.

The value is stored in UTC using ISO 8601 date-time format and reflects the moment the refund component was first persisted. It does not change after creation and is used for chronological analysis, audit trails, and reconciliation with external payment processor logs.

Analytics and reporting tools often rely on this timestamp to group refund activity by day, week, or accounting period.

order_line.description:
Summary view of the order line that this refund item is associated with, when the refund targets a specific line item.

This object is derived from the underlying `shopping_mall_order_line_id` foreign key and provides enough information to display which product, SKU, or service is being refunded without requiring an extra API call.

When null, either no specific order line is associated with this refund component or the association is not relevant for the current view.

order_seller_segment.description:
Summary view of the seller segment this refund item pertains to, when the refund is calculated at seller-segment granularity.

This object is derived from the `shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id` foreign key and provides contextual information about the seller-specific portion of the order that is being refunded.

When null, the refund component is either not tied to a single seller segment or such context is not needed for the current representation.

IShoppingMallRefundItem.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for listing refund items belonging to a specific refund transaction.

This DTO is used as the request body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/refundTransactions/{refundTransactionId}/items endpoint. It encapsulates pagination, sorting, and business-level filters such as status, reason code, amount ranges, and linkage to order lines or SKUs. The path parameter refundTransactionId scopes the search to a single parent refund transaction, so this request type does not carry the transaction identifier itself.

The shape is purposely aligned with common list/search DTO patterns in the shopping mall backend so that platform administrators can flexibly drill down into refund item details while keeping the API contract stable.

page.description: 1-based page index for paginated listing of refund items. If omitted, the implementation should assume the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of refund item records to return in a single page. The backend should enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

sort_by.description: Column or logical field name used for sorting the refund items (for example, created_at, refund_amount, or status). Concrete allowed values are constrained by the implementation.

oneOf.description: Sorting direction to apply when ordering results by the sort_by field. Typically either ascending or descending.
Sorting direction to apply when ordering results by the sort_by field. Typically either ascending or descending.

sort_direction.description: Sorting direction to apply when ordering results by the sort_by field. Typically either ascending or descending.

status.description: Optional filter for the refund item processing status, restricting results to a specific status such as requested, approved, succeeded, or failed.

reason_code.description: Optional filter for the refund reason code so the caller can view only refund items matching a specific business reason.

min_refund_amount.description: Optional lower bound filter for the refund_amount field, expressed in the same currency as the refund transaction.

max_refund_amount.description: Optional upper bound filter for the refund_amount field, expressed in the same currency as the refund transaction.

order_line_id.description: Optional filter to restrict results to refund items that are tied to a specific order line.

sku_id.description: Optional filter to restrict results to refund items that are tied to a specific SKU.

IShoppingMallRefundItem.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new refund item row under an existing refund transaction in the shoppingMall payment and refund subsystem.

This request body is used by privileged backend actors, such as platform administrators or automated refund orchestration services, when they need to add line-level breakdown entries into the `shopping_mall_refund_items` table. The parent refund transaction is identified by the `refundTransactionId` path parameter on the endpoint, so this DTO does not contain the parent foreign key field.

Only business fields that are client-controlled or operator-controlled are included here. Identity fields and system-managed timestamps are excluded and are populated by the backend when persisting the new record. Validation must ensure that referenced order lines or seller segments belong to the same logical context as the parent refund transaction and that the monetary values are consistent with original payments and refund policies.

shopping_mall_order_line_id.description:
Optional identifier of the related order line in `shopping_mall_order_lines` when this refund component targets a specific order line.

When supplied, the referenced line item must belong to an order associated with the parent refund transaction identified in the path. This ensures that refunds cannot be misapplied across unrelated orders.

Null is allowed for refund components that are not tied to a single line, such as generalized shipping or adjustment refunds.

shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id.description:
Optional identifier of the related seller segment in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` when the refund is computed at seller scope.

If provided, it must reference a seller segment that participates in the order covered by the parent refund transaction. This allows the platform to allocate refunds at seller granularity without enumerating each individual line.

Null is permitted for refund components that are independent of a particular seller segment.

component_type.description:
Type of amount being refunded for this component.

Typical values include `item_price`, `tax`, `shipping`, or `adjustment`, classifying whether the component relates to merchandise, taxation, logistics, or manual corrections. The precise allowed set is governed by refund policy configuration and should be validated by the backend service.

This field is required because downstream financial reconciliation and reporting logic depend on consistent categorization across refund items.

description.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of this refund component suitable for operator or customer-facing views.

Callers may use this text to clarify why the refund is being granted, such as referencing a service incident, a policy clause, or a manual approval note. It is stored alongside the refund item for later inspection in customer service tools and statements.

When null, the reason for the refund is inferred from higher-level refund transaction metadata or from the component type alone.

gross_amount.description:
Gross monetary amount of this refund component before any non-refundable fees, expressed in the currency of the parent refund transaction.

This value must not exceed the portion of the original charge that is eligible for refund for the associated line, seller segment, or fee type. The backend enforces these constraints by cross-checking against order, payment, and previously created refund items.

It is required because the platform cannot create a refund item without a defined monetary amount.

tax_amount.description:
Tax portion associated with this refund component when tax is tracked separately.

If the component represents a tax refund, or if the platform must explicitly record the tax share of a refunded amount, callers should supply this field according to the tax calculation logic used at order time.

Null indicates that either no tax applies to this component or that the platform does not require separate tax tracking for this particular refund scenario.

shipping_amount.description:
Portion of shipping cost being refunded as part of this component, when applicable.

For example, when refunding shipping fees due to a delivery failure or service-level agreement breach, this field records the exact shipping amount being returned to the customer.

Null is allowed when the component is not related to shipping charges.

net_amount.description:
Net amount effectively returned to the customer for this component after accounting for any non-refundable fees.

Callers may supply this value when the platform exposes explicit control over net refund amounts at the item level. In other configurations, the backend may derive net amounts from gross amounts and internal fee policies.

Null is permitted to support scenarios where net versus gross separation is computed server-side rather than specified at creation time.

IShoppingMallRefundItem.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing refund item record in the `shopping_mall_refund_items` table for a given refund transaction.

This request body is used by trusted backend actors to adjust the details of a previously created refund component, for example to correct an amount, change a classification, or fix a reference to an order line or seller segment. The target refund item and its parent transaction are identified via path parameters; therefore this DTO does not include the primary key or the parent foreign key fields.

All properties are optional to support partial updates. Domain logic must ensure that any applied changes keep the refund transaction financially valid, do not exceed original payment amounts when aggregated with other items, and maintain referential integrity with related order entities.

shopping_mall_order_line_id.description:
New or cleared reference to the related order line in `shopping_mall_order_lines` for this refund component.

When provided with a non-null UUID, the platform re-associates the refund item with the specified order line after validating that the line belongs to the order covered by the parent refund transaction. When explicitly set to null, any existing association with a specific order line is removed.

If omitted, the current order line linkage is left unchanged.

shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id.description:
New or cleared reference to the related seller segment in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` for this refund component.

A non-null UUID rebinds the refund item to the given seller segment after validation that the segment is compatible with the parent transaction context. A null value removes any existing seller-segment-level association.

If the property is omitted, the seller segment association remains as-is.

component_type.description:
Updated classification of the refund component type, such as switching between `item_price`, `tax`, `shipping`, or `adjustment` according to refined business assessment.

Changing this field can affect how the refund is reported and reconciled, so the backend must enforce any policy constraints that restrict type changes after certain workflow stages.

When set to null, some implementations may treat it as clearing the classification and require recalculation or correction by operators; if omitted, the existing value is preserved.

description.description:
Updated human-readable explanation of this refund item for audit and customer-facing purposes.

Providing a new non-null value overwrites the previously stored description, allowing operators to clarify the reason for the refund after additional investigation. Explicitly setting the field to null removes any existing description from the record.

When the field is omitted from the payload, the description remains unchanged.

gross_amount.description:
Updated gross refund amount for this component before non-refundable fees.

A non-null value replaces the current gross amount, and the backend must revalidate that the new amount remains consistent with original payment amounts and other refund items under the same transaction. Setting this property explicitly to null may be used in certain configurations to indicate that the gross amount should be recalculated or temporarily cleared, subject to domain rules.

If the property is absent, the existing gross amount is not modified.

tax_amount.description:
Updated tax amount associated with this refund component.

Non-null values overwrite the previous tax allocation, while an explicit null removes any stored tax value. The platform may enforce consistency between `tax_amount`, `component_type`, and other tax-related structures when processing this change.

Omitting this field leaves the current tax amount unchanged.

shipping_amount.description:
Updated shipping amount associated with this refund component.

A non-null value updates the stored shipping portion of the refund, whereas an explicit null clears any previously recorded shipping amount. Backend validation should confirm that changes remain aligned with the underlying order's shipping charges and applicable policies.

If this property is not present in the request, the existing shipping amount is preserved.

net_amount.description:
Updated net amount of this refund component after non-refundable fees.

Providing a non-null value sets a new net amount, which may trigger recalculation of aggregates or reconciliation checks for the parent refund transaction. Setting the property to null clears the net amount value, potentially causing the backend to recompute it based on current gross amounts and fee configurations.

When omitted, the net amount remains as currently stored in the database.

IShoppingMallPaymentChargeback.IRequest.description:
Filter, sorting, and pagination criteria for querying payment chargebacks.

This request DTO is used by platform administrators and risk-operations tooling to search and list payment chargebacks recorded in the shoppingMall platform. It encapsulates page and size controls, sort options, and flexible filters such as status, reason codes, transaction references, order identifiers, date ranges, and internal or provider case references.

All fields are optional so that callers can progressively refine queries without being forced to specify every parameter.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve.

When omitted, implementations typically default to the first page so that callers can simply supply filters without explicit paging in simple UIs.

limit.description:
Maximum number of chargeback records to return in a single page.

The server may enforce an upper bound (for example 100) regardless of the client-specified value to protect performance while still allowing reasonable page sizes for back-office grids.

sortBy.description:
Field name used for sorting payment chargebacks in the result set.

Typical values include `created_at`, `updated_at`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`, or `disputed_amount`, but the exact set of supported fields is defined by the provider implementation. When omitted, a sensible default such as `created_at` descending is usually applied.

oneOf.description:
Sorting direction applied to the sortBy field.

Use `asc` for ascending order so that older or smaller values appear first in the result set.

Sorting direction applied to the sortBy field.

Use `desc` for descending order so that newer or larger values appear first in the result set.

sortDirection.description:
Sorting direction applied to the sortBy field.

The value must be either `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. When omitted, implementations typically default to `desc` for time-based sorts so that the newest chargebacks are shown first.

statusList.description:
Optional list of chargeback lifecycle statuses to filter by.

Each value corresponds to the business-level status stored in the `chargeback_status` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` model. When provided, only chargebacks whose status is contained in this list will be returned.

reasonCodeList.description:
Optional list of chargeback reason codes supplied by financial institutions.

Values in this list are used to filter on the `reason_code` column of `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`. Only chargebacks whose reason code matches one of the supplied values will be included in the result set.

paymentTransactionId.description:
Filter by the unique identifier of the related payment transaction.

This value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and allows administrators to list all chargebacks opened against a particular payment transaction.

orderId.description:
Filter by the unique identifier of the related customer order.

This value corresponds to the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key column on `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and is commonly used to view chargeback history for a specific order in support or dispute workflows.

caseReference.description:
Filter by the internal platform-side chargeback case reference.

This value corresponds to the `case_reference` column in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and is typically unique per payment transaction. Administrators can use it to quickly retrieve a single chargeback case when they know the internal reference from an email, export, or previous screen.

providerCaseId.description:
Filter by the chargeback case identifier used by the payment provider or card network.

This value corresponds to the optional `provider_case_id` column in `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`. It is useful when back-office teams receive a case identifier from the acquirer, issuer, or gateway and need to locate the matching record in the platform.

financialInstitutionReference.description:
Filter by an external reference identifier assigned by the financial institution or payment gateway.

Implementations may map this to the same value as `provider_case_id` or to a related reference code depending on integration specifics. It is intended to support flexible searching when only external identifiers are known.

createdFrom.description:
Start of the creation timestamp range for chargebacks to include, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When provided together with `createdTo`, only chargebacks whose `created_at` value falls within the inclusive range will be returned. This is useful for building date-based reports and back-office work queues.

createdTo.description:
End of the creation timestamp range for chargebacks to include, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

Typically used together with `createdFrom` to bound queries by creation time. If only `createdTo` is provided, implementations usually interpret it as "created at or before this timestamp".

resolvedFrom.description:
Start of the resolution timestamp range for chargebacks to include, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

This filter is applied to the `closed_at` column on `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` and is meaningful only for chargebacks that have reached a terminal status such as won or lost.

resolvedTo.description:
End of the resolution timestamp range for chargebacks to include, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

When used with `resolvedFrom`, it allows users to find chargebacks that were closed within a particular time window, such as the current reconciliation period.

q.description:
Free-text search term applied to implementation-defined fields such as internal notes, external references, or reason descriptions.

This field is intentionally loosely specified so that implementations can provide convenient fuzzy search across multiple text columns while keeping the structured filters focused on precise attributes.

IShoppingMallPaymentChargeback.description:
Detailed representation of a single payment chargeback recorded in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO maps one-to-one to a row in the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` Prisma model and is returned by administrative read and mutation endpoints that expose the full state of a chargeback. It includes identifiers for the associated payment transaction, order, and (optionally) customer, as well as internal and provider case identifiers, disputed monetary information, chargeback status, reason metadata, and lifecycle timestamps.

Because this type reflects the persisted state, it surfaces both business-facing fields (such as `status`, `disputedAmount`, and `reasonCode`) and system-managed audit timestamps (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`). All property descriptions explicitly reference the underlying Prisma columns to make the relationship between the API surface and the database schema transparent for maintainers and integrators.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment chargeback record in the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` column and is generated by the persistence layer when a new chargeback row is inserted. It is used in all path parameters and foreign-key relationships that need to reference a specific chargeback.

paymentTransactionId.description:
Identifier of the related payment transaction record that this chargeback is disputing.

This field maps to the non-nullable `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` column and references a row in the `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` table. Back-office staff use this link to inspect the original authorization, capture, and status-history details when analyzing the chargeback.

orderId.description:
Identifier of the customer-facing order whose payment is under dispute.

The property value is stored in the non-nullable `shopping_mall_order_id` column and links the chargeback to a master order in the `shopping_mall_orders` table. This association allows reporting and workflows to aggregate chargebacks by order, customer, and seller segments.

customerId.description:
Identifier of the customer associated with the disputed order, if available.

This property mirrors the nullable `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key column and references a row in the `shopping_mall_customer` table when present. It is used for customer-centric analytics, risk assessment, and support tooling that needs to navigate from a chargeback back to the owning customer account.

caseReference.description:
Platform-side case reference used to uniquely identify the chargeback within the shoppingMall system.

This value is persisted in the non-nullable `case_reference` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table and typically follows a business-defined format (for example, incorporating the payment transaction id, date, or channel information). Internal tools rely on this reference for search, reconciliation, and cross-system correlation of chargeback cases.

providerCaseId.description:
External case identifier for the chargeback as assigned by the payment provider, card network, or acquiring bank.

This field corresponds to the nullable `provider_case_id` column and usually contains values such as acquirer reference numbers (ARNs), dispute case IDs, or gateway-specific dispute identifiers. It is essential for reconciling platform data with provider reports and for communicating about specific cases with external partners.

disputedAmount.description:
Monetary amount that has been disputed through the chargeback, expressed in units of the chargeback currency.

This property maps directly onto the non-nullable `disputed_amount` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table. From a domain standpoint, the disputed amount should not exceed the total captured amount for the associated payment transaction, and service logic may enforce this and other limits such as minimum amounts or rounding conventions.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code representing the currency of the disputed amount (for example, `"USD"`, `"EUR"`, or `"KRW"`).

The value is stored in the non-nullable `currency` column and usually matches the currency of the underlying payment transaction. Reporting, analytics, and financial export processes rely on this field to correctly aggregate and interpret chargeback amounts across different currencies.

status.description:
Current business status of the chargeback such as "chargeback_open", "chargeback_under_review", "chargeback_won", or "chargeback_lost".

This field is backed by the non-nullable `chargeback_status` column and participates in the platform’s chargeback lifecycle state machine. Service logic and administrative tools use it to determine whether a chargeback is still active, awaiting documentation, in representment, or fully resolved, and certain state transitions may trigger downstream effects on refunds, seller payouts, or risk scoring.

reasonCode.description:
Provider or scheme-specific reason code indicating why the chargeback was initiated.

This property mirrors the non-nullable `reason_code` column and usually stores a machine-readable code from the payment network or gateway that classifies the dispute (for example, fraud, non-receipt of goods, duplicate charge, or processing error). Downstream analytics and reporting can group chargebacks by reason code or normalized reason categories for operational insight.

reasonDescription.description:
Human-readable explanation or label associated with the chargeback reason code.

This field corresponds to the nullable `reason_message` column and may contain descriptive text from the payment provider, card network, or internal operations teams. It helps analysts quickly understand the nature of the dispute without consulting external documentation for the raw reason code.

openedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the chargeback was first opened or recorded in the shoppingMall platform.

This value is stored in the non-nullable `opened_at` column as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. It serves as the main chronological anchor for the chargeback lifecycle and is used for SLA monitoring, dashboards that track chargeback volume over time, and alignment with external provider timelines.

resolvedAt.description:
Timestamp representing when the chargeback reached a terminal state such as won, lost, or written off.

This property maps to the nullable `closed_at` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table. When null, the chargeback is considered open or in-progress; when populated, it signals that the dispute outcome is final. Reporting and analytics commonly rely on this timestamp to bucket chargebacks into historical periods based on resolution time.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this chargeback record was created in the database.

It is sourced from the non-nullable `created_at` column and is typically set automatically by the persistence layer at insert time. This field is primarily used for auditing, debugging, and understanding the delay between the external chargeback event and its registration within the platform.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this chargeback record was last updated in the database.

This property reflects the non-nullable `updated_at` column, which is usually maintained by the ORM or database triggers on every update. It allows consumers to detect stale data, synchronize with external systems, and troubleshoot reconciliation workflows where chargeback details evolve over time.

IShoppingMallPaymentChargeback.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new payment chargeback record in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO maps directly onto the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` Prisma model and is used by platform administrator or internal system actors to register a chargeback raised by a financial institution against an existing payment transaction. The client supplies identifiers for the related payment transaction and order, the disputed monetary amount and currency, and core classification metadata such as the internal case reference, provider reason code, and initial chargeback status.

On the persistence side, each field in this object corresponds to a specific column in the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table (for example, `paymentTransactionId` → `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id`, `caseReference` → `case_reference`, `disputedAmount` → `disputed_amount`, and `openedAt` → `opened_at`). This tight alignment ensures that validation and mapping logic in the service layer remains simple and transparent, and that the API surface accurately reflects the underlying storage schema and business rules around chargeback creation.

paymentTransactionId.description:
Identifier of the original payment transaction that is being charged back.

This value maps to the non-nullable `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` column on the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table and must reference an existing row in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` that is in a state where chargebacks are allowed (for example, a successfully captured payment).

orderId.description:
Identifier of the customer-facing order associated with the charged-back payment.

This property is persisted into the non-nullable `shopping_mall_order_id` column and links the chargeback to the master order in the `shopping_mall_orders` table for reporting, reconciliation, and dispute workflows. The referenced order should correspond to, or be derivable from, the associated payment transaction.

caseReference.description:
Platform-side identifier for the chargeback case that is unique per payment transaction for internal tracking.

This field is stored in the non-nullable `case_reference` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table and is typically used as the primary business key when back-office teams search, reconcile, or reference chargebacks. Business rules often enforce uniqueness of this reference within the scope of a single payment transaction to prevent duplicate case registration.

providerCaseId.description:
Identifier for the chargeback case in the payment provider, card network, or acquiring bank system.

This value maps to the optional `provider_case_id` column and allows the platform to correlate the internal chargeback record with external dispute cases or acquirer reference numbers (ARNs).
