When supplied, it is used extensively in reconciliation processes, support communication with providers, and external reporting.

disputedAmount.description:
Amount that is being disputed through the chargeback, expressed in the payment currency.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable `disputed_amount` column and must be a non-negative numeric value. From a domain perspective, the disputed amount should not exceed the captured amount of the associated payment transaction, and service-level validation should enforce this constraint and any rounding rules used by the platform.

currency.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code representing the currency of the disputed amount, usually matching the original payment currency.

This value is stored in the non-nullable `currency` column and is used for financial reporting, reconciliation, and conversion logic. Typical examples include `"USD"`, `"EUR"`, or `"KRW"`, and service validation should reject unknown or unsupported currency codes according to platform policy.

status.description:
Initial business status of the chargeback at the time of registration.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `chargeback_status` column on the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table. Typical values represent states such as "chargeback_open", "chargeback_under_review", "chargeback_won", or "chargeback_lost" depending on the platform’s internal status model. The service layer is responsible for validating that the provided status is part of the allowed chargeback status enumeration and for applying any additional lifecycle rules.

reasonCode.description:
Provider or scheme reason code indicating why the chargeback was opened, such as fraud, non-receipt, or product dissatisfaction.

This property is written to the non-nullable `reason_code` column and typically contains a network- or gateway-specific code supplied by the financial institution. Business logic may normalize or categorize these codes for analytics, but the raw code is preserved for auditability and reconciliation with provider documentation.

reasonMessage.description:
Optional human-readable explanation or description associated with the chargeback reason code.

This value maps to the nullable `reason_message` column and may contain additional narrative provided by the payment provider, card network, or internal operations teams. It helps back-office and risk analysts quickly understand the context of the dispute without needing to cross-reference external documentation for the reason code.

openedAt.description:
Datetime when the chargeback was first reported to the platform or officially opened by the financial institution.

This property populates the non-nullable `opened_at` column as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. It is used to order chargebacks chronologically, compute service-level agreements (SLAs), and anchor time-based analytics such as chargeback volume by period.

IShoppingMallPaymentChargeback.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing payment chargeback record in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by platform administrator actors and back-office tools to modify mutable properties of a chargeback, such as its status, reference identifiers, reason details, disputed amount, and key lifecycle timestamps after the record has been created. It corresponds to the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` Prisma model and exposes only those columns that are realistically subject to change as part of dispute handling and reconciliation workflows.

All properties in this type are optional, allowing callers to send partial updates. The primary key `id` and audit timestamps are not included because they are managed by the persistence layer. The service implementation is responsible for enforcing business rules, including allowed status transitions, immutability of certain fields in terminal states, and consistency with the associated payment transaction and order records.

caseReference.description:
Updated platform-side case identifier for the chargeback.

When provided, this value is written to the `case_reference` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table. It allows administrators to correct or normalize case references used internally for search and reconciliation. Business logic may restrict changes to this field once the chargeback reaches certain terminal statuses to preserve auditability.

providerCaseId.description:
Updated provider-side case identifier or acquirer reference number (ARN) associated with the chargeback.

This property updates the nullable `provider_case_id` column and is typically changed when more accurate dispute reference information becomes available from the payment provider or card network. It helps maintain a consistent linkage between internal chargeback records and external dispute cases.

disputedAmount.description:
Updated disputed amount for the chargeback, expressed in the same currency as the original payment.

This value updates the `disputed_amount` column. Depending on business rules, the platform may limit changes to this field once the chargeback has progressed beyond certain lifecycle stages (for example, after final judgment) or enforce that the amount cannot exceed the captured amount or drop below zero.

currency.description:
Updated ISO 4217 currency code for the disputed amount if a correction is required.

This property maps to the `currency` column of the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table. In most cases, currency should remain aligned with the original payment transaction currency, and service-level validation may reject changes that would break this invariant.

status.description:
New lifecycle status for the chargeback.

This field updates the `chargeback_status` column and must follow the platform’s chargeback state machine. Examples of valid transitions include moving from an open or under-review state to a final outcome such as "chargeback_won" or "chargeback_lost". The service layer should reject illegal transitions (for example, attempting to reopen a finalized chargeback) and ensure that related entities like refunds and seller payouts remain consistent.

reasonCode.description:
Revised structured reason code for the chargeback supplied by the financial institution or derived from internal categorization.

Updating this property changes the `reason_code` column and may be necessary when a dispute is reclassified based on additional provider feedback or internal investigation outcomes. Changes should be tracked in audit logs so that reason-code evolution over the life of a chargeback is transparent.

reasonMessage.description:
Updated human-readable explanation associated with the chargeback reason.

This field updates the nullable `reason_message` column and can be used to capture richer narrative context obtained after the initial chargeback registration, such as additional comments from the provider or notes from internal analysts summarizing the precise issue.

openedAt.description:
Corrected or updated timestamp representing when the chargeback was opened.

This value updates the `opened_at` column. While the field is normally set at creation time, some operational processes may require fixing the timestamp when initial data was incomplete or inaccurate. All timestamps are expressed as ISO 8601 date-time strings in UTC.

resolvedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the chargeback reached a terminal state such as won, lost, or written off.

This property writes to the nullable `closed_at` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` table and is used alongside `status` to determine whether the chargeback is considered open or closed. Service logic should ensure that this timestamp is set consistently with the status and that it is not cleared once a final outcome is recorded.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for retrieving a paginated list of seller payout batches from the shopping_mall_seller_payouts table.

This DTO encapsulates complex search criteria, sorting options, and pagination settings used by platform administrators to locate specific seller payouts. It is used as the request body of the PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/sellerPayouts endpoint and does not map directly to a single Prisma table column set; instead, the service implementation translates these filters into the appropriate date and status constraints over payouts and related entities.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Starts from 1.

Used together with `limit` to control which slice of seller payout batches is returned in the result set.

limit.description:
Maximum number of seller payout summaries to return per page.

The value is capped to a reasonable upper bound to protect the system from overly large responses and to ensure consistent user experience in administrative UIs.

sellerId.description:
Identifier of the target seller whose payout batches should be included in the result set.

When provided, only payouts associated with this seller identifier (referencing `shopping_mall_seller.id`) are returned.

payoutStatus.description:
Filter by payout status.

Represents the current lifecycle state of the payout batch, such as `payout_pending`, `payout_in_progress`, `payout_failed`, or `payout_sent`. Exact allowed values are defined by the domain model and Prisma enum for the payout status field, and the service will map this value into the appropriate `payout_status` constraints when building the query.

fromCreatedAt.description:
Start of the creation timestamp range filter.

Only payout batches with `created_at` greater than or equal to this value are included in the search results. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

toCreatedAt.description:
End of the creation timestamp range filter.

Only payout batches with `created_at` less than or equal to this value are included in the search results. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

fromScheduledAt.description:
Lower bound of the logical scheduled payout time interval filter.

This field does not correspond to a single concrete column on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. Instead, the implementation interprets it as the earliest intended payout time, derived from scheduling metadata or related domain events, and applies the appropriate conditions when querying payouts.

toScheduledAt.description:
Upper bound of the logical scheduled payout time interval filter.

The service implementation uses this value, together with `fromScheduledAt`, to limit payouts to those whose intended execution or settlement time falls on or before the specified instant, based on scheduling metadata or related domain events rather than a single direct column on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`.

fromExecutedAt.description:
Lower bound of the logical executed payout time interval filter.

This value indicates the earliest time at which a payout is considered to have been executed or confirmed. The implementation may derive this from payout status transition timestamps or related payment transaction records, not necessarily from a single column on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`.

toExecutedAt.description:
Upper bound of the logical executed payout time interval filter.

This value indicates the latest time at which a payout is considered to have been executed or confirmed. The implementation uses it together with `fromExecutedAt` to restrict results to payouts whose execution window is within the specified range, based on domain-specific execution timestamps.

orderBy.description:
Sorting field for search results.

Typical logical values include `createdAt`, `periodStart`, `periodEnd`, or amounts such as `netAmount`. The exact mapping to database columns or expressions is enforced at the service layer based on supported sortable fields for seller payouts.

oneOf.description:
Sorting direction for the selected `orderBy` field.

`asc` indicates ascending order, for example from oldest to newest or from smallest to largest value.

Sorting direction for the selected `orderBy` field.

`desc` indicates descending order, for example from newest to oldest or from largest to smallest value.

orderDirection.description:
Sorting direction for the selected `orderBy` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. Any other value is invalid and will be rejected by validation logic.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.description:
Detailed representation of a single seller payout batch stored in the shopping_mall_seller_payouts table.

This DTO is used as the response body for GET /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/sellerPayouts/{sellerPayoutId} and POST/PUT operations that create or update payout batches. It exposes all administratively relevant fields from the Prisma model while ensuring that only columns that actually exist on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` are represented, preventing phantom-field inconsistencies between API and database.

Platform administrators use this representation to review, reconcile, and audit seller payouts, including financial amounts, payout lifecycle status, and failure details when applicable. Sensitive authentication credentials or secrets are never exposed by this DTO.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller payout batch.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` record and is typically implemented as a UUID or other opaque identifier that has no inherent business meaning. It is used throughout the system and in API paths as the stable handle for this payout batch.

sellerId.description:
Identifier of the seller who receives this payout batch.

This field is derived from the `shopping_mall_seller_id` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model. It references the primary key of a seller in the `shopping_mall_seller` table and lets administrators correlate payouts with the owning seller account and related analytics such as seller performance summaries.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller who receives this payout batch.

This is a BELONGS-TO association transformed to a summary DTO, allowing platform administrators to see key seller details (such as name and business identifiers) together with the payout without performing additional API calls.

payoutCode.description:
Business-facing payout reference code used by administrators and financial operators.

Conceptually aligns with the `payout_number` column of the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` table. It typically follows an internal convention such as `SP-YYYYMMDD-NNNN` and is used on reports, exports, and reconciliation processes to cross-reference payouts with external banking or accounting systems.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this payout batch.

This field maps to the `currency` column of `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. All financial figures such as `grossAmount`, `feeAmount`, `adjustmentAmount`, and `netAmount` are expressed in this single settlement currency, which reflects the configuration agreed upon with the seller for this payout.

grossAmount.description:
Total gross amount of all positive earnings included in this payout before fees and adjustments.

This value corresponds to the `gross_amount` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` table and typically represents the sum of eligible order- and line-level earnings assigned to this payout batch for the seller. It is stored as a numeric type that can accurately represent currency values.

feeAmount.description:
Total amount of platform fees or commissions deducted from the seller as part of this payout.

This field maps to the nullable `fee_amount` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` schema. When present, it aggregates platform commissions, processing fees, or other deductions applied against the seller's gross earnings for this specific payout batch. When null, it indicates that no explicit fee amount has been recorded for this payout.

adjustmentAmount.description:
Net effect of manual or automatic adjustments that are not part of standard platform fee calculations.

This property reflects the nullable `adjustment_amount` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. Positive values typically represent additional credits (for example, manual goodwill credits), while negative values represent debits (for example, manual corrections or clawbacks) applied to this payout batch. When null, it indicates that no separate adjustment amount has been recorded.

netAmount.description:
Net amount that is actually owed to the seller for this payout batch after fees and adjustments.

This field maps to the `net_amount` column on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. It normally equals `grossAmount - feeAmount + adjustmentAmount` following the business rules for the platform, with null fee or adjustment values treated as zero. This is the amount referenced when funding the actual remittance to the seller.

periodStart.description:
Optional start of the earnings period covered by this payout batch.

Directly reflects the nullable `period_start` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` table. When set, it indicates the earliest event or order date included in the financial aggregation computed for this payout, which is useful for reporting and reconciliation across payout cycles. When null, the payout is not explicitly tied to a single calendar window start.

periodEnd.description:
Optional end of the earnings period covered by this payout batch.

Directly reflects the nullable `period_end` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` table. When set together with `periodStart`, it defines the closed or semi-open date interval used to compute the payout, enabling period-based reporting and settlement reconciliation. When null, the payout may represent an open-ended or implicitly defined period.

providerName.description:
Name or code of the external payment provider or bank used to send this payout.

Maps to the nullable `provider_name` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` schema. Typical values might include processor names, bank identifiers, or internal codes that let finance teams trace payouts through external payment rails. When null, either the payout has not yet been associated with a concrete provider or the information is not tracked.

providerPayoutId.description:
Identifier for this payout at the external payment provider or bank.

Aligns with the nullable `provider_payout_id` column of the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. This is used to reconcile payouts with bank statements or provider-level transaction reports and is critical for tracing specific remittances in case of issues or disputes. When null, the payout may not yet have been submitted to the provider or may not support provider-side identifiers.

failureReasonCode.description:
Optional machine-friendly code describing why the payout failed when the payout status indicates failure.

This property maps to the nullable `failure_reason_code` column in the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` table. It enables programmatic analysis of failure patterns, categorization of issues, and integration with automated retry or escalation workflows. When null, either the payout has not failed or no standardized failure code is available.

failureReasonMessage.description:
Optional human-readable description giving more information about a payout failure.

This corresponds to the nullable `failure_reason_message` column of `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. It is typically written by the payment integration layer or backoffice operators to capture free-form explanations that help in manual investigation and customer support. When null, there is no additional narrative beyond the failure code or status itself.

payoutStatus.description:
Current status of the payout batch from the platform's perspective.

This field directly reflects the `payout_status` column of the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model. Allowed values are controlled at the database or domain layer and commonly include states such as `payout_pending`, `payout_in_progress`, `payout_failed`, or `payout_sent`, enabling lifecycle tracking and reporting for each payout.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this payout record was created.

Maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. It records when the payout batch was first registered in the system and is used for chronological sorting, audit trails, and reporting.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this payout record was last updated.

Maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. It is automatically maintained by the system whenever mutable fields of the payout are changed, supporting audit requirements and helping operators understand recent activity on the payout batch.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new seller payout batch in the shopping_mall_seller_payouts table.

This DTO is used by platform administrators or backoffice financial systems to register a new payout for a specific seller. It captures the seller reference, payout monetary totals, settlement currency, optional earnings period boundaries, an optional initial payout status, and scheduling information required to initialize a seller payout record.

Authentication context provides the admin identity; therefore no admin id fields appear here. The fields in this DTO are mapped directly to columns on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model such as `shopping_mall_seller_id`, `currency`, `gross_amount`, `fee_amount`, `adjustment_amount`, `net_amount`, `period_start`, `period_end`, and `payout_status`, with `scheduled_payout_at` and `memo` acting as operational metadata.

seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller receiving this payout.

This value must reference an existing record in the `shopping_mall_seller` table and conceptually maps to the `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. The platform uses this identifier to aggregate earnings and link the payout batch to seller-facing reporting and analytics.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code in which the payout is denominated (for example, "USD" or "KRW").

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `currency` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model. All monetary amounts in this DTO (`gross_amount`, `fee_amount`, `adjustment_amount`, and `net_amount`) are expressed in this settlement currency. Validation must ensure that only supported currency codes are used according to platform configuration.

gross_amount.description:
Total gross payout amount before platform fees and adjustments.

This value maps to the non-nullable `gross_amount` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model and typically represents the sum of all positive earnings that have been selected for inclusion in this payout batch. It must be a non-negative monetary value expressed in the specified settlement currency and should reflect the aggregation logic applied to underlying order or payout item rows.

fee_amount.description:
Total fee amount retained by the platform for this payout batch.

This field corresponds to the nullable `fee_amount` column on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. It aggregates platform commissions, transaction fees, or other deductions applied to the seller’s gross earnings. When omitted, the default value is treated as zero at the business-logic layer; when provided, it must be a non-negative monetary value that participates in the calculation of the net payout amount.

adjustment_amount.description:
Net effect of manual or automatic adjustments that are not part of the standard platform fee calculation.

This value maps to the nullable `adjustment_amount` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model. Positive values typically represent additional credits applied to the seller (for example, manual goodwill credits), while negative values represent debits (for example, manual corrections or clawbacks). This field provides flexibility for finance teams when reconciling complex settlement scenarios.

net_amount.description:
Net payout amount that will actually be remitted to the seller after fees and adjustments.

This field maps to the non-nullable `net_amount` column on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. In most business flows, it should satisfy the relationship `net_amount = gross_amount - fee_amount + adjustment_amount`, with any omitted optional components treated as zero. It must be a non-negative monetary value in the settlement currency and is the amount used when instructing the external payment provider or bank.

period_start.description:
Optional start of the earnings period covered by this payout batch.

This value maps to the nullable `period_start` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. When provided, it marks the earliest event or order date included in the financial aggregation for this payout. Finance and reporting tools rely on this field to understand which portion of the seller’s activity is being settled by the payout.

period_end.description:
Optional end of the earnings period covered by this payout batch.

This value maps to the nullable `period_end` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. When provided together with `period_start`, it defines the closed or semi-open date interval used to compute the payout amounts. This enables clear reporting on settlement cycles and makes reconciliation with external accounting systems more transparent.

payout_status.description:
Initial lifecycle status of the payout batch at creation time.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable `payout_status` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model. Typical values are platform-defined states such as `payout_pending`, `payout_in_progress`, `payout_failed`, or `payout_sent`. When omitted, the implementation should assign a sensible default (for example, `payout_pending`) that satisfies database constraints while aligning with the platform’s payout state machine.

scheduled_payout_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this payout is scheduled to be executed.

This field represents the intended execution time for initiating the transfer to the seller, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. The underlying Prisma model does not contain a dedicated scheduled timestamp column; instead, this value is typically used by job schedulers or integration components and persisted as part of payout-related metadata managed by the application.

memo.description:
Optional internal memo or notes associated with this payout batch.

This free-form text field does not map to a dedicated column in the loaded Prisma model but is commonly persisted in an auxiliary metadata structure or a generic notes column. Finance operators can use this memo to capture reconciliation notes, explanations for adjustments, or other operational comments that help contextualize the payout over time.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing seller payout batch in the shopping_mall_seller_payouts table.

This DTO is used by platform administrators to modify mutable attributes of a seller payout after creation. It allows changing lifecycle status, adjusting monetary fields when permitted by business rules, updating earnings period boundaries, maintaining execution timestamps, enriching provider metadata, refining failure details, and updating internal memos.

All properties are optional so that clients can submit partial updates. Immutable identifiers such as the payout primary key and seller association are not exposed here and must not be changed by this operation. The fields map directly onto columns of the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model, with `scheduled_payout_at` serving as operational scheduling metadata rather than a dedicated column.

payout_status.description:
Lifecycle status of the payout batch.

This value maps directly to the non-nullable `payout_status` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. Typical values are business-defined states such as `payout_pending`, `payout_in_progress`, `payout_failed`, or `payout_sent`. Updating this field reflects the current step in the payout processing lifecycle and must obey the platform’s configured state transition rules.

gross_amount.description:
Updated total gross payout amount before platform fees and adjustments.

This field maps to the `gross_amount` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. It should only be modified when business rules allow recalculation of the earnings included in this payout batch, for example during manual corrections or reconciliation activities. The value must remain a non-negative monetary amount expressed in the payout’s settlement currency.

fee_amount.description:
Updated total fee amount retained by the platform for this payout batch.

This property corresponds to the nullable `fee_amount` column on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. It allows administrators to correct or refine the aggregate of platform commissions and other deductions applied to the seller’s gross earnings. When omitted, the pre-existing database value is preserved.

adjustment_amount.description:
Updated net adjustment amount representing manual credits or debits applied to the payout.

This property maps to the nullable `adjustment_amount` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model. Positive values represent additional credits granted to the seller, while negative values represent debits or clawbacks. Adjustments are typically performed by finance or risk teams to correct previous settlement calculations.

net_amount.description:
Updated net payout amount that will actually be remitted to the seller after applying fees and adjustments.

This value maps to the `net_amount` column on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. When modifying gross, fee, or adjustment values, the implementation must ensure that `net_amount` remains consistent with the platform’s business rules, usually reflecting `gross_amount - fee_amount + adjustment_amount` with consideration for omitted optional components.

period_start.description:
Updated start of the earnings period covered by this payout batch.

This property corresponds to the nullable `period_start` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. It allows administrators to correct the earliest event or order date included in the payout when reconciliation discovers that the initial range was inaccurate.

period_end.description:
Updated end of the earnings period covered by this payout batch.

This property corresponds to the nullable `period_end` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. Together with `period_start`, it defines the corrected earnings period over which this payout’s amounts have been calculated.

scheduled_payout_at.description:
Next scheduled execution time for this payout batch.

This field represents an operational scheduling hint that may be used by background jobs or orchestration services to determine when to initiate or retry the payout. Although the underlying Prisma model does not have a dedicated scheduled timestamp column, this value is typically persisted as part of the payout’s metadata or in a related scheduling structure managed by the application.

executed_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this payout was actually executed and funds were remitted to the seller.

This value reflects operational execution metadata and is stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. It is used for reconciliation against banking statements and for calculating performance metrics such as settlement delay and payout processing latency.

provider_name.description:
Name or code of the external payment provider or bank used to send this payout.

This property maps to the nullable `provider_name` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. Updating it allows administrators or integrations to reflect which settlement channel handled the payout if the provider changes after initial creation or if additional detail becomes available.

provider_payout_id.description:
Identifier for this payout at the external payment provider or bank.

This property maps to the nullable `provider_payout_id` column and is used to reconcile payout records in the platform with corresponding entries in provider dashboards, bank statements, or settlement reports. It should typically hold the provider’s transaction or batch identifier for the remittance and can be updated if corrected identifiers are obtained from the provider.

failure_reason_code.description:
Machine-friendly code describing why the payout failed when the payout status indicates failure.

This property maps directly to the nullable `failure_reason_code` column on the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` model. It is used for programmatic categorization of failure causes, analytics, and automated retry or escalation workflows. Updating this value lets operators refine the classification of a failure if new diagnostic information becomes available.

failure_reason_message.description:
Human-readable description giving more information about a payout failure.

This property maps to the nullable `failure_reason_message` column. It is typically populated by the payment integration layer or backoffice operators and captures free-form details that help explain why the payout failed and what corrective actions may be required. Updates are useful when adding clarifications or correcting earlier, less precise messages.

memo.description:
Optional memo or descriptive note attached to this payout batch.

This free-form text field is used by financial operators for reconciliation, audit, or communication notes. Updating the memo allows teams to keep a running explanation of decisions, adjustments, or external correspondence related to the payout’s lifecycle.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, sorting, and pagination criteria for listing seller payout item components that belong to a specific seller payout batch.

This DTO is used by platform administrators when calling PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/sellerPayouts/{sellerPayoutId}/items to retrieve a paginated list of payout item summaries from the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table.

Each field in this request maps directly to a column of `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` or to common list request metadata (page, limit, ordering). All properties are optional so that callers can progressively refine queries for back‑office grids, while the path parameter `sellerPayoutId` scopes results to a single parent payout batch.

page.description:
1‑based page index for pagination.

When omitted, the implementation typically defaults to the first page. This field does not map to any Prisma column; it strictly controls paging behaviour in the query layer.

limit.description:
Maximum number of payout items to return in a single page.

Service implementations usually enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses. This field is a paging hint and not persisted in the database.

orderBy.description:
Field name to use for sorting payout items within the page.

Typical values correspond to sortable projections of `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` columns, such as:

- `createdAt` → `created_at`
- `grossAmount` → `gross_amount`
- `netAmount` → `net_amount`

The exact set of allowed values is enforced by the service layer; this string simply carries the caller’s preference.

oneOf.description: Sort records in ascending order with respect to the `orderBy` field.
Sort records in descending order with respect to the `orderBy` field.

orderDirection.description:
Sorting direction for the `orderBy` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order. The default direction is defined by the implementation when this field is omitted.

componentType.description:
Filter for the payout component type stored in `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.component_type`.

Typical values include business categories such as `item_revenue`, `shipping_revenue`, `refund_deduction`, or `manual_adjustment`. When provided, only items whose `component_type` matches this value are returned.

minGrossAmount.description:
Lower bound filter for the gross amount of payout items, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.gross_amount`.

When specified, only items whose `gross_amount` is greater than or equal to this value in the payout currency are included.

maxGrossAmount.description:
Upper bound filter for the gross amount of payout items, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.gross_amount`.

When specified, only items whose `gross_amount` is less than or equal to this value in the payout currency are included.

minFeeAmount.description:
Lower bound filter for the fee amount allocated to payout items, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.fee_amount`.

Only items whose `fee_amount` is greater than or equal to this value are returned. Records with a NULL `fee_amount` are typically excluded from this filter unless the implementation explicitly treats NULL as zero.

maxFeeAmount.description:
Upper bound filter for the fee amount allocated to payout items, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.fee_amount`.

Only items whose `fee_amount` is less than or equal to this value are returned. Records with a NULL `fee_amount` may be excluded or handled specially depending on business rules.

minNetAmount.description:
Lower bound filter for the net amount of payout items, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.net_amount`.

When specified, only items whose `net_amount` is greater than or equal to this value are included. This is the primary filter for selecting items that have at least a certain contribution to the seller payout.

maxNetAmount.description:
Upper bound filter for the net amount of payout items, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.net_amount`.

When specified, only items whose `net_amount` is less than or equal to this value are included. Negative values can be used to focus on refund‑ or deduction‑oriented components.

orderId.description:
Filter for payout items associated with a specific customer order, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.shopping_mall_order_id`.

When provided, only payout items whose `shopping_mall_order_id` equals this value are returned. This makes it easy to inspect the payout composition for a single order within the context of a payout batch.

orderSellerSegmentId.description:
Filter for payout items associated with a specific seller segment of an order, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id`.

This is useful when reconciling or debugging payout allocation for a particular seller segment in a multi‑seller order.

orderLineId.description:
Filter for payout items associated with a specific order line, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.shopping_mall_order_line_id`.

When provided, only payout items tied to this line‑level identifier are returned, which is helpful for SKU‑level reconciliation and dispute handling.

createdFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound for the creation timestamp of payout items, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.created_at`.

Only items whose `created_at` is greater than or equal to this timestamp (in ISO 8601 date‑time format, UTC recommended) are returned.

createdTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound for the creation timestamp of payout items, mapped to `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.created_at`.

Only items whose `created_at` is less than or equal to this timestamp are returned. Combined with `createdFrom`, this allows administrators to focus on payout items created within a specific analysis window.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem.description:
Detailed seller payout item component that belongs to a seller payout batch in the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table.

Each record represents a granular piece of a seller payout, typically linked to upstream financial entities such as orders, order segments, and order lines. The DTO exposes read‑only identifiers, monetary breakdowns, and contextual references needed for administrative reconciliation and accounting.

This type is returned by endpoints such as:
- GET /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/sellerPayouts/{sellerPayoutId}/items/{sellerPayoutItemId}
- POST /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/sellerPayouts/{sellerPayoutId}/items
- PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/sellerPayouts/{sellerPayoutId}/items/{sellerPayoutItemId}

The schema is a read‑side projection of the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` Prisma model enriched with summary views of related entities so that finance and operations staff can understand payout composition without additional lookups.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller payout item record within the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table.

This value is generated by the persistence layer and is the primary key used when addressing a specific payout component from administrative tools, reports, or internal services.

sellerPayout.description:
Parent seller payout batch that this payout item belongs to.

This is a read‑side projection of the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_id` foreign key referencing `shopping_mall_seller_payouts.id`. It provides the high‑level settlement context, including the seller, payout period, and lifecycle status for the overall transfer.

oneOf.description: No concrete order is associated with this payout item.

order.description:
Customer‑facing order from which this payout component was derived, when applicable.

When present, this association corresponds to the `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key pointing to `shopping_mall_orders.id`. It allows finance or support staff to trace the payout item back to the originating order. When null, the payout component may represent a general adjustment or correction that is not tied to a single order.

oneOf.description: The payout component is not tracked at a specific seller segment level.

orderSellerSegment.description:
Seller segment of the order to which this payout item is attributed, when allocation is tracked at segment level.

This is a read‑side projection of the `shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id` foreign key referencing `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.id`. It is particularly important in multi‑seller orders where the payout batch aggregates amounts for multiple sellers.

oneOf.description: No particular order line is associated; the component applies at a higher aggregation level or is a general adjustment.

orderLine.description:
Specific order line that this payout item settles, when the payout is calculated at line level.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_order_line_id` foreign key referencing `shopping_mall_order_lines.id`. It enables SKU‑level profitability analysis, dispute resolution, and fine‑grained reconciliation of payout amounts back to the exact purchased item.

componentType.description:
Business classification of the payout component, mapped from `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.component_type`.

Typical values include categories such as `item_revenue`, `shipping_revenue`, `refund_deduction`, or `manual_adjustment`, as defined by the settlement logic. This value is crucial for understanding how the component contributes to the seller’s payout and for grouping items in statements and reports.

oneOf.description: Descriptive text explaining the purpose or origin of this payout component.
No explicit description is stored for this payout item.

description.description:
Optional explanation stored in `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.description`.

This field is used for human‑readable notes that appear in seller statements or internal reconciliation tools, giving more context such as promotion names, reason codes, or manual adjustment explanations.

grossAmount.description:
Gross monetary amount for this payout component before platform fees and other deductions, mapped from `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.gross_amount`.

This value typically corresponds to the full revenue, charge, or adjustment amount associated with the component in the payout’s settlement currency. It is the starting point for calculating the seller’s net proceeds for this component.

oneOf.description: Concrete fee amount allocated to this payout component.
No fee amount is explicitly recorded for this component.

feeAmount.description:
Amount of platform or processing fees allocated to this payout component, mapped from `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.fee_amount`.

When present, this amount represents the share of commissions, payment processing costs, or other platform‑level deductions that are attributed to the component. When null, the platform has not recorded a separate fee at this item level, and any fee effect is reflected elsewhere.

netAmount.description:
Net amount from this payout component that contributes to the seller’s payout, mapped from `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.net_amount`.

For revenue components, this is typically `gross_amount - fee_amount` following the platform’s settlement rules. For deduction or refund components, the value is often negative, reducing the seller’s payout. Summing `netAmount` over all items in the batch reconciles with the parent payout’s net total.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this payout item record was created, mapped from `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.created_at`.

Stored in ISO 8601 date‑time format (UTC recommended), this value indicates when the payout component was first persisted, which is useful for chronological analysis and audit trails.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when this payout item record was last updated, mapped from `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items.updated_at`.

Any administrative edits, reconciliation changes, or other updates to the payout item should refresh this timestamp so that tools and auditors can identify recent modifications.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for a seller payout item in the shopping mall platform.

This request body is used by internal financial tooling or platform administrator workflows to append a new payout component row into the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table under an existing seller payout batch. Each record represents a single contribution to the seller’s payout, such as revenue from a specific order line, a shipping revenue component, a refund deduction, or a manual adjustment applied during reconciliation.

Only business-input fields that are not system managed are exposed here. Identifiers for the parent payout and the new row’s primary key are derived from the path and persistence layer respectively. Monetary amounts submitted here are validated against the payout state and business rules, and will later participate in aggregate calculations for the seller payout summary.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the related order in `shopping_mall_orders` that produced this payout component.
No concrete order is associated with this payout component, for example a general manual adjustment or correction entry.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Optional reference to the customer-facing order that this payout item is derived from.

When populated, this links the payout component back to a specific record in the `shopping_mall_orders` table so that finance and support can trace settlement flows from orders to seller payouts. This field is nullable because some payout items may represent manual adjustments or technical corrections that are not tied to any single order.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the seller segment in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` that this payout item is attributed to.
The payout component is not tracked at the seller-segment level or the linkage is intentionally omitted.

shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id.description:
Optional reference to the seller-segment portion of an order that this payout item relates to.

When provided, this points to a row in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` and is typically used when a multi-seller order is split into per-seller segments for settlement. This linkage helps reconcile payout items back to the correct seller segment in complex marketplace scenarios.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the related order line in `shopping_mall_order_lines` for which this payout component was calculated.
No particular order line is associated; the component applies at a higher aggregation level such as the whole order or payout.

shopping_mall_order_line_id.description:
Optional reference to the specific order line that generated this payout item.

Use this when the payout component is computed at the SKU or line level, such as per-item revenue, discounts, or refunds, so that each payout line can be traced back to the exact purchased item for audit and support flows.

componentType.description:
Business classification of the payout component.

Typical values include categories such as `item_revenue`, `shipping_revenue`, `refund_deduction`, `commission_fee`, or `manual_adjustment`. Implementations should enforce an allowed set of component types at the application layer to keep payout statements consistent and to support downstream reporting and accounting mappings.

The property name follows the camelCase conventions used by `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem` so that the same business concept is addressed consistently across create, update, and read variants.

oneOf.description: A free-form text description that explains the nature, origin, or rationale of this payout component in a way that is meaningful to finance staff and possibly the seller.
No explicit textual description is stored; consumers infer meaning from the component type and related order references.

description.description:
Optional human-readable explanation for this payout component.

This value is displayed in internal financial tools and may also appear on seller-facing payout statements to clarify why the amount exists, what transaction or adjustment it relates to, or any special handling applied by finance, risk, or operations teams.

currency.description:
Currency code in which all monetary values for this payout component are expressed.

The value should follow ISO 4217 alpha-3 currency codes such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW` and must be consistent with the settlement currency used by the parent seller payout batch in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. Service logic is expected to validate that the currency matches the payout’s currency to avoid mixing currencies within a single payout.

Aligning this field with the `currency` property of `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem` ensures that create payloads and read models share the same semantics and are easy to reason about for developers and financial analysts.

grossAmount.description:
Gross monetary amount for this payout component before any platform fees are deducted.

This value typically represents the full revenue, charge, or adjustment amount associated with the component in the payout’s settlement currency. It is used together with `feeAmount`, `taxAmount`, and `netAmount` to explain the financial breakdown of a payout item, and must obey business rules such as sign conventions and non-negative constraints where applicable.

The camelCase name `grossAmount` aligns with the corresponding property on `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem`, providing a consistent field name across create and read DTOs.

oneOf.description: Concrete fee amount assigned to this payout component, typically non-negative and expressed in the same currency as `grossAmount`, `taxAmount`, and `netAmount`.
No fee amount is directly recorded for this component; any fees are handled at a different aggregation level or in other payout items.

feeAmount.description:
Optional portion of platform or processing fees allocated specifically to this payout component.

When present, this value represents the share of commissions, payment processing costs, or other deductions that are attributed to the component. It is used in reconciliation logic to explain the difference between gross and net amounts. When omitted or null, downstream logic may interpret that no fee was explicitly allocated at this level.

The name `feeAmount` mirrors the corresponding property on `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem`, ensuring field consistency between create, update, and read models.

taxAmount.description:
Tax amount associated with this payout component, when applicable.

Depending on the platform’s tax configuration, this may include VAT, sales tax, or other tax components that are applied to the underlying order or order line. A value of zero is common for non-taxable components. Together with `grossAmount` and `feeAmount`, this field allows the platform to reconstruct and explain the relationship between gross and net amounts for each payout item.

The property name is aligned with the `taxAmount` field on `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem`, giving a consistent representation of tax across all DTO variants.

netAmount.description:
Net monetary amount from this component that contributes to the seller’s payout after fees and taxes are considered.

For revenue components, this is typically `grossAmount - feeAmount` plus or minus any applicable `taxAmount`, following the platform’s settlement formulas. For deduction or refund components, it is often negative to reduce the seller’s payout in line with business rules and settlement formulas.

Using the camelCase name `netAmount` keeps the field consistent with the main `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem` DTO and allows consumers to easily map create payloads to the resulting read model.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for a seller payout item in the shopping mall platform.

This request body is used to amend mutable attributes of an existing record in the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` table that belongs to a particular seller payout batch. It is intended for internal finance operations or platform administrators who need to adjust descriptive metadata, fine-tune allocated fee values, or correct the split between gross, tax, and net amounts before a payout is finalized.

Identifiers for the parent payout and the payout item itself are supplied via path parameters and therefore are not present in this DTO. Only fields that are considered editable while the parent payout is still in a modifiable state are exposed here. Once the parent payout is locked or finalized, the service layer should reject updates using this schema according to business rules and audit requirements.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the order in `shopping_mall_orders` that should be considered the new source for this payout component.
Clear the existing order association from this payout item, provided that business rules allow such detachment during reconciliation.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Optional updated reference to the source order for this payout item.

This field should only be used in exceptional reconciliation scenarios where a payout item was initially linked to the wrong order or when a manual adjustment needs to be reattached to a different order context. Implementations may further restrict whether this field is truly mutable depending on audit and compliance requirements.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the seller segment in `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` that should now own this payout component.
Remove the explicit seller-segment linkage from this payout item when corrections dictate that it should no longer be tied to any specific segment.

shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id.description:
Optional updated reference to the seller segment within an order that this payout item is associated with.

Administrators can adjust this linkage when re-attributing amounts to the correct seller segment in a multi-seller order, for example after correcting an automated allocation that targeted the wrong seller partition.

oneOf.description: Identifier of the order line in `shopping_mall_order_lines` that should be treated as the correct origin for this payout component.
Drop any existing order line association to reclassify the component as a more general adjustment not tied to a single line.

shopping_mall_order_line_id.description:
Optional updated reference to the specific order line that generated this payout item.

Finance staff may touch this field when fixing misattributed line-level amounts so that statements and audit trails correctly map payout components to the underlying order lines that produced them.

componentType.description:
Updated business classification for the payout component.

This allows finance teams to reclassify a payout item, for example changing a generic `manual_adjustment` to a more specific category once the underlying cause is understood. Application logic should validate allowed values and may restrict reclassification based on the payout’s current lifecycle stage.

The property name follows the same camelCase convention (`componentType`) used in the create and read DTOs so that the same concept is represented consistently everywhere.

oneOf.description: New or revised textual description that clarifies the nature of this payout component after reconciliation or investigation.
Clear the existing description from this payout item when it is no longer needed or should not appear on derived statements.

description.description:
Updated human-readable explanation for this payout component.

Administrators can use this field to add or refine commentary that appears in internal tools or seller-facing statements, improving transparency around the reason and origin of the payout line over time.

currency.description:
Updated currency code for this payout component.

In most cases, the currency of a payout item should match the settlement currency of the parent seller payout batch and will be immutable once created. This optional field is provided for edge cases where an earlier record was stored with the wrong currency and must be corrected under strict business controls. Service logic should enforce whether a change is allowed based on payout status and audit requirements.

grossAmount.description:
Adjusted gross amount for this payout component before fees and taxes.

This field enables controlled corrections to the original gross amount when earlier settlement calculations or source data were incorrect. Any changes must remain consistent with business rules, currency constraints, and the aggregated totals expected for the parent payout batch. The naming is aligned with the `grossAmount` field on `IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem` and `ICreate` for cross-variant consistency.

oneOf.description: New fee amount to assign to this payout component, expressed in the same currency as the associated gross, tax, and net amounts.
Remove the existing fee allocation for this component and rely on higher-level logic or alternative records for fee representation, subject to business rules.

feeAmount.description:
Revised fee amount allocated to this payout component.

Finance staff may update this when rebalancing platform commissions, payment costs, or other deductions between individual payout items so that the breakdown matches accounting requirements and external reports. Clearing this value may indicate that fees should be considered at another level of aggregation instead.

The camelCase `feeAmount` name keeps the update DTO consistent with the main payout item entity and the create DTO.

taxAmount.description:
Updated tax amount associated with this payout component.

This field allows reconciliation against upstream tax calculations when correcting settlement records. Adjustments may be necessary if tax was initially misallocated between items or if the tax regime for the underlying transaction changed. As with other monetary fields, the service layer should validate consistency with business rules before accepting updates.

netAmount.description:
Updated net amount from this payout component that impacts the seller’s payout.

When `grossAmount`, `feeAmount`, or `taxAmount` have been adjusted, this field can be updated to remain consistent with the platform’s settlement formulae. Negative values can represent deductions or refunds, subject to validation rules applied in the service layer and the lifecycle status of the parent payout. The naming is aligned with the `netAmount` field on the main payout item DTO for clarity.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusStatistics.description:
Aggregated payment transaction statistics grouped by payment status for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a computed, read-only view built from many rows of the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma model rather than a single persisted entity. Each record in the statistics captures how many payment transactions share a given status value (for example pending, authorized, captured, failed, or refunded) and the corresponding monetary totals associated with that status.

The structure is designed for internal dashboards and administrative tools where financial and operational stakeholders need an at-a-glance overview of payment health and cash flow across the platform. It intentionally does not expose any per-transaction or PII details, and therefore can be safely used in reporting contexts where only aggregated information is required.

buckets.description:
List of aggregated payment statistics grouped by payment status.

Each bucket represents a single payment status value and contains the count of transactions and the total monetary volume for that status. When there are no payment transactions in the underlying data set, this array SHOULD be empty rather than null.

overall.description:
Overall aggregate statistics computed across all payment transactions included in this view.

This object contains summary values such as the total number of transactions and the total amount across every status bucket. It is helpful for quickly understanding the global scale of payment activity without having to manually sum bucket-level values on the client side.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusStatistics.IBu.description:
Single aggregated statistics bucket for a specific payment status in the shoppingMall platform.

A bucket groups all payment transactions that share the same status value (for example pending, authorized, captured, failed, cancelled, or refunded depending on the final schema and business rules). It exposes the number of transactions in that status and the total monetary volume represented by those transactions.

status.description:
Payment status value for this bucket.

This string corresponds to the status column in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions model. Typical examples include values such as "pending", "authorized", "captured", "failed", "cancelled", or "refunded". The exact set of allowed values is defined by the payment domain and may evolve over time.

transactionCount.description:
Number of payment transactions that currently have this status.

This is a non-negative integer representing how many rows in shopping_mall_payment_transactions are grouped into this bucket.

totalAmount.description:
Total monetary amount associated with all transactions in this status bucket.

The amount is expressed in the platform's canonical currency (for example, a configured base currency such as USD). Implementations may compute this as the sum of the captured or authorized amounts for all transactions having the given status, depending on business rules.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusStatistics.IOv.description:
Overall aggregate payment statistics across all payment transactions in the shoppingMall platform.

This object provides top-level metrics derived from the same data set used to construct the individual status buckets. It is intended to give stakeholders a quick, single-place summary of overall payment activity without inspecting each bucket individually.

totalTransactionCount.description:
Total number of payment transactions included in this statistics view across all statuses.

This value is typically equal to the sum of transactionCount across every bucket in IShoppingMallPaymentStatusStatistics.buckets.

totalAmount.description:
Total monetary amount represented by all payment transactions across every status bucket.

This value is typically equal to the sum of totalAmount across every bucket in IShoppingMallPaymentStatusStatistics.buckets and is expressed in the platform's canonical currency.

IShoppingMallRefundReasonStatistics.description:
Aggregated refund statistics grouped by refund reason for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO models a computed, read-only view over many rows of the shopping_mall_refund_transactions Prisma model (and, where applicable, related reason-code or classification tables). Each bucket in the statistics corresponds to a particular refund reason and exposes both the number of refunds and the total refunded amount for that reason.

The structure is intended for internal dashboards, analytics tools, and administrative reports where stakeholders need to understand why refunds are being issued. It deliberately exposes only high-level aggregates and reason labels, not individual refund records or sensitive payment details.

buckets.description:
List of aggregated refund statistics buckets grouped by refund reason.

Each bucket represents one business-level reason (or reason code) for issuing refunds and contains the total count of refunds and aggregate refunded amount for that reason. When there are no matching refund transactions, this array SHOULD be empty rather than null.

overall.description:
Overall aggregate refund statistics across all reasons.

This object summarizes the total number of refund transactions and the total refunded amount over the entire data set included in the view, making it easy to understand the global scale of refund activity without manually summing individual buckets.

IShoppingMallRefundReasonStatistics.IBuc.description:
Single aggregated refund statistics bucket for a specific refund reason in the shoppingMall platform.

A refund reason bucket groups all refund transactions that share the same reason or reason code, such as customer remorse, product defect, shipping delay, payment error, or other business-defined categories. It exposes the number of refunds assigned to that reason and the total refunded monetary amount for that group.

reasonCode.description:
Machine-friendly refund reason identifier or reason code.

This may correspond to a code stored directly on shopping_mall_refund_transactions (for example, "CUSTOMER_REMORSE", "PRODUCT_DEFECT", or "SHIPPING_DELAY") or a key into a dedicated reason-code table. It is optimized for stable programmatic usage and analytics.

reasonLabel.description:
Human-readable label describing the refund reason in a way suitable for display in dashboards or reports.

Typical examples might include strings such as "Customer remorse", "Product quality issue", or "Late delivery". This label is not required to be unique and may be localized at the presentation layer.

refundCount.description:
Number of refund transactions that have this refund reason.

This is a non-negative integer representing how many rows in shopping_mall_refund_transactions are grouped into this reason bucket.

totalRefundAmount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded for all transactions in this reason bucket.

The amount is expressed in the platform's canonical currency (for example, a configured base currency such as USD). Implementations typically compute this as the sum of refund amounts from shopping_mall_refund_transactions that share the same refund reason.

IShoppingMallRefundReasonStatistics.IOve.description:
Overall aggregate refund statistics across all refund reasons for the shoppingMall platform.

This object contains top-level metrics derived from the same data set used to build individual reason buckets. It is designed to provide a concise summary of global refund activity over a specified time window or filter set.

totalRefundCount.description:
Total number of refund transactions included in this statistics view across all refund reasons.

This value is typically equal to the sum of refundCount across every bucket in IShoppingMallRefundReasonStatistics.buckets.

totalRefundAmount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded across every reason bucket in this statistics view.

This value is typically equal to the sum of totalRefundAmount across all buckets in IShoppingMallRefundReasonStatistics.buckets and is expressed in the platform's canonical currency.

IShoppingMallChargebackStatusStatistics.description:
Aggregated statistics of payment chargebacks grouped by their status for back-office risk and finance dashboards.

Represents an analytical, status-centric view derived from the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` Prisma model. Each entry in the `items` array corresponds to a distinct chargeback status and contains aggregate metrics such as count of chargebacks and total disputed amount for that status. This DTO is read-only and does not expose raw chargeback records.

items.description: List of aggregated metrics per distinct chargeback status. Each element represents one status bucket with its aggregated values.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when these chargeback status statistics were generated. Useful for dashboards to know the recency of the aggregates.

IShoppingMallChargebackStatusStatisticsI.description:
Aggregated metrics for a single chargeback status derived from `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`.

Each instance represents one status bucket (for example, `pending`, `in_review`, or `resolved`) and contains the count of chargebacks in that status and the total disputed amount for those chargebacks. Implementations may extend this type in the future with additional per-status indicators such as average age or percentage share, but those are not required for the core contract.

status.description: Chargeback status value for this aggregate bucket. The exact set of statuses is defined by the `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks` Prisma model and business rules (for example, `pending`, `in_review`, `reversed`, `lost`).

chargebackCount.description: Total number of chargeback records currently in this status.

totalDisputedAmount.description: Sum of the disputed monetary amounts for all chargebacks in this status, expressed in the platform's base currency (for example, cents of USD).

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutPeriodStatistic.description:
Filter and aggregation parameters for computing seller payout statistics over a period using `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` as the primary data source.

This DTO allows platform administrators and finance tools to specify the time window, optional seller and region filters, and desired aggregation granularity (for example, daily or monthly). The backend uses these parameters to compute an analytical time series of seller payout activity. The request is read-only and does not modify any payout records.

from.description: Inclusive start of the time window for which payout statistics should be computed. Uses ISO 8601 date-time in UTC.

to.description: Exclusive end of the time window for which payout statistics should be computed. Uses ISO 8601 date-time in UTC.

sellerId.description: Optional filter to restrict statistics to a single seller. When omitted, aggregates are computed across all sellers.

regionCode.description: Optional filter to restrict statistics to a specific region or market as defined in region and payout configuration. When omitted, aggregates include all regions.

oneOf.description: Time grain used to bucket payouts when aggregating statistics over the requested period. Determines how the backend groups `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` rows by time.
Time grain used to bucket payouts when aggregating statistics over the requested period. Determines how the backend groups `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` rows by time.
Time grain used to bucket payouts when aggregating statistics over the requested period. Determines how the backend groups `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` rows by time.

granularity.description: Time grain used to bucket payouts when aggregating statistics over the requested period. Determines how the backend groups `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` rows by time.

page.description: Page index for paginating over the aggregated period buckets, starting from 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of aggregated period buckets to return in a single response page.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutPeriodStatistic.description:
Aggregated payout statistics for a seller over a specific settlement period.

Used for dashboards, reports, and admin views to understand how much volume and revenue a seller generated and how much will be paid out in a given period.

sellerId.description:
Identifier of the seller for whom the statistics are calculated.

This field does not correspond to a single column of the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` table but instead represents the seller identity for which the aggregated metrics in this object have been computed across one or more payout records.

periodStart.description:
Inclusive start timestamp of the settlement period for which these statistics are aggregated.

The value usually corresponds to a boundary aligned with the requested granularity (for example, the first second of a day, week, or month) instead of a raw `period_start` column value for a single payout row.

periodEnd.description:
Exclusive end timestamp of the settlement period for which these statistics are aggregated.

Like `periodStart`, this is derived as a period boundary used for grouping data across multiple `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` records rather than being copied from a single database row.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code in which all aggregated monetary fields are expressed.

The currency is typically determined from the underlying payout records within the group. In most implementations, a single currency per seller and period is enforced for consistency of reporting.

orderCount.description:
Total number of customer orders that resulted in at least one payout item for this seller in the period.

This value is computed from order-related tables joined with `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` and is not a direct column on the payout table itself.

orderLineCount.description:
Total number of order lines included in payout items for this seller in the period.

This is an aggregated count derived from order line and payout item tables and is used for understanding item-level volume contributing to payouts.

grossSalesAmount.description:
Total gross sales amount for the seller across all relevant orders and order lines in the period, before any fees or adjustments.

This value is an analytical aggregate, typically computed as the sum of item-level or order-level gross prices associated with payout items in the selected period.

platformFeeAmount.description:
Total platform fees charged to the seller across the entire period.

This value is derived from platform fee fields in order, payout item, or financial posting tables and represents how much the platform retained in fees for the seller's activity during the period.

otherAdjustmentsAmount.description:
Net sum of all other adjustments (promotions, manual corrections, chargebacks, etc.) applied to the seller in the period.

This is an aggregate of non-fee, non-gross components that affect the seller's final payout, such as manual ledger adjustments or promotional subsidies reconciled through payout data.

netPayoutAmount.description:
Total net payout amount to the seller over the period after subtracting platform fees and adjustments from gross sales.

This value is typically computed as `grossSalesAmount - platformFeeAmount + otherAdjustmentsAmount` and used as the key metric for how much the seller actually receives for the period.

pendingPayoutAmount.description:
Total net payout amount for this period that has not yet been marked as paid out to the seller.

This field summarizes the portion of `netPayoutAmount` that is still in pending or in-progress payout states in the underlying `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` records and is useful for cash-flow and liability monitoring.

paidPayoutAmount.description:
Total net payout amount for this period that has already been paid out to the seller.

This field summarizes the portion of `netPayoutAmount` that is associated with payouts whose status indicates that the transfer to the seller has been successfully completed.

IShoppingMallPaymentFunnelAnalytics.IReq.description:
Search, filter, and segmentation criteria for computing payment funnel analytics over a specified time range on the shoppingMall platform.

This request DTO allows platform administrators and internal stakeholders to describe which subset of orders and payment transactions should be included in the analytics calculation and how the results should be segmented. It captures temporal boundaries, optional segmentation dimensions such as region or payment method, and additional filters on order and payment attributes to narrow the scope of the analytics query.

The backend uses this structure to query multiple payment-related tables (orders, payment transactions, authorizations, captures, refunds, and chargebacks) and compute funnel stage counts, monetary totals, and conversion rates.

timeRange.description:
Time window over which to compute the payment funnel analytics.

Implementations typically apply this window to order creation timestamps, checkout completion dates, or payment initiation times depending on configuration. The range must be bounded and reasonable to avoid excessively heavy analytical queries.

segmentations.description:
List of segmentation dimensions to apply when aggregating funnel analytics.

Each specified dimension instructs the analytics engine to split the results by that axis (for example, by region, payment method, or seller). Combining several dimensions produces multi-dimensional segment keys in the response. Implementations may impose limits on the number of simultaneous segmentations to avoid excessive cardinality.

orderFilters.description:
Optional additional filters applied at the order level before computing funnel metrics.

These filters can constrain which orders are considered in scope based on properties such as order status, minimum or maximum order total, region, or seller. They are applied prior to joining with payment-related tables.

paymentFilters.description:
Optional additional filters applied at the payment transaction level.

These filters can constrain which payment attempts are considered, for example limiting to specific payment methods, currencies, payment providers, or risk flags. They are applied after joining orders to payments but before aggregating funnel stages.

maxSegmentCount.description:
Maximum number of distinct segment combinations to return in the response.

This parameter allows callers and the backend to control the cardinality of the result set when many segmentation dimensions are requested. If the number of possible segment keys exceeds this limit, the backend may truncate low-volume segments or aggregate them into an "other" bucket according to implementation-specific rules.

IShoppingMallAnalyticsTimeRange.description:
Common time range structure used by analytics request and response DTOs for the ShoppingMall platform.
