Represents either an explicit closed interval between start and end timestamps or a normalized interval derived from a preset (such as last_24_hours). All timestamps are expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

start.description: Inclusive start timestamp of the analytics window in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

end.description:
Exclusive end timestamp of the analytics window in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

Implementations should ensure that end is strictly later than start.

oneOf.description:
Segmentation dimension that groups payment funnel metrics by customer or order region.

This dimension typically corresponds to business-level region or market codes derived from configuration such as shopping_mall_region_settings, shipping address, billing address, or explicit region routing rules.

Segmentation dimension that groups payment funnel metrics by payment method.

Common examples include distinct methods such as credit card, bank transfer, virtual account, digital wallet, or local alternative payment methods configured in shopping_mall_payment_methods.

Segmentation dimension that groups payment funnel metrics by seller or merchant account.

This is typically used to compare conversion performance, drop-off points, and payment health across different sellers on the marketplace.

Segmentation dimension that groups payment funnel metrics by device type or client platform.

Typical device or platform categories include desktop web, mobile web, and native mobile applications, enabling UX and performance comparisons across surfaces.

Segmentation dimension that groups payment funnel metrics by acquisition or sales channel.

Channels can represent marketing or traffic sources such as organic, paid ads, affiliates, email campaigns, or in-app placements, allowing analysis of funnel performance by traffic origin.

IShoppingMallPaymentFunnelSegmentationDi.description:
Enumeration of supported segmentation dimensions for payment funnel analytics on the shoppingMall platform.

Each value represents an axis along which the analytics engine can split aggregated funnel metrics. Combining several dimensions leads to multi-dimensional segment keys, which are represented in the response as structured segment descriptors.

IShoppingMallPaymentFunnelOrderFilter.description:
Optional filter criteria applied to orders before computing payment funnel analytics.

These filters restrict the universe of orders considered in the funnel to those matching specific attributes such as status, monetary range, or associated region or seller. They are evaluated on order-level data prior to joining with payment transactions. When multiple filter fields are provided, they are combined using logical AND semantics, so an order must satisfy all supplied criteria to be included.

orderStatusIn.description:
Optional list of allowed order statuses used to constrain the analysis set.

When provided and non-empty, only orders whose status field is included in this list are considered in-scope for the analytics. The exact set of supported status codes is defined by the order domain model (for example: `created`, `pendingPayment`, `paid`, `fulfilled`, `cancelled`). If the array is omitted or empty, no additional status-based restriction is applied.

minOrderTotal.description:
Optional lower bound on the gross order total used to filter orders by monetary amount.

Orders whose total monetary amount is strictly below this threshold are excluded from the analytics. This value is expressed in the platform's base currency or a configured reporting currency. When used together with `maxOrderTotal`, the two values define a closed numeric range that orders must fall within; callers should ensure that `minOrderTotal` is less than or equal to `maxOrderTotal` when both are provided.

maxOrderTotal.description:
Optional upper bound on the gross order total used to filter orders by monetary amount.

Orders whose total monetary amount exceeds this threshold are excluded from the analytics. This value is expressed in the platform's base currency or a configured reporting currency. When used together with `minOrderTotal`, the two values define a closed numeric range that orders must fall within; callers should ensure that `minOrderTotal` is less than or equal to `maxOrderTotal` when both are provided.

regionCodes.description:
Optional list of region codes used to filter orders by market or geography.

When provided and non-empty, only orders whose effective region (for example, derived from shipping address, billing address, or explicit region setting from shopping_mall_region_settings) matches one of the specified codes are considered. If omitted or empty, analytics are not restricted by region.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers used to constrain the analytics to specific merchants.

When provided and non-empty, only orders whose primary seller or associated seller segment belongs to this set are considered in-scope. This filter is typically used for seller-level performance dashboards or investigations. If omitted or empty, no seller-level restriction is applied and all sellers are included.

IShoppingMallPaymentFunnelPaymentFilter.description:
Optional filter criteria applied to payment transactions before aggregating funnel metrics.

These filters operate on payment-level attributes such as payment method, currency, provider, or risk flags. They are evaluated after joining orders to payment transactions but before computing aggregated counts and monetary totals per funnel stage.

paymentMethodCodes.description:
Optional list of payment method codes to include in the analytics.

Only payment transactions whose method is in this list are considered in-scope. Examples might include `card`, `bank_transfer`, `wallet`, or integration-specific method identifiers.

currencyCodes.description:
Optional list of three-letter ISO 4217 currency codes to include.

When provided, only payment transactions whose currency matches one of the specified codes are included in the analytics. This allows focusing on specific reporting currencies or regions.

providerCodes.description:
Optional list of payment provider identifiers to filter transactions by processor or gateway.

Typical values might correspond to PSP names, acquiring banks, or internal routing keys used in the payment stack.

includeRiskFlaggedOnly.description:
When true, restrict analytics to payment transactions that have been flagged by risk or fraud systems.

This allows analysts to compute funnel behavior specifically for high-risk cohorts, for example to evaluate additional friction or control strategies. When false or omitted, both flagged and unflagged transactions are included.

IShoppingMallPaymentFunnelAnalytics.description:
Aggregated payment funnel analytics for the shoppingMall platform, computed over a specified time window and optional segmentation dimensions.

This DTO summarizes how orders and payment transactions progress through key funnel stages such as order creation, payment initiation, authorization, capture, refund, and chargeback. It is intended for use in internal dashboards and reporting tools for platform administrators, finance teams, and risk analysts.

The response contains an overall summary across all segments, as well as per-segment analytics when segmentation dimensions are requested. Each analytics item exposes counts, monetary totals, and conversion rates between successive funnel stages, enabling stakeholders to identify bottlenecks, diagnose anomalies, and track the impact of configuration changes over time.

No per-customer or per-transaction personal data is exposed in this structure. All metrics are aggregated and anonymized to avoid leaking sensitive payment information.

timeRange.description:
The effective time window over which analytics were computed.

This may reflect the requested range from the query or a normalized range used by the backend after validation and truncation. It documents the temporal scope of the aggregated funnel metrics.

segmentations.description:
List of segmentation dimensions that were applied when computing this analytics response.

This reflects the effective set of dimensions used by the backend, which may be a subset of the requested dimensions if some were not supported or were pruned to control cardinality.

overall.description:
Aggregated funnel analytics across the entire selected scope without any segmentation applied.

Provides top-level counts and monetary totals for each funnel stage and the derived conversion rates between them.

segments.description:
Per-segment payment funnel analytics records.

Each element represents metrics for a particular combination of segmentation dimension values (for example, a specific region and payment method). The `segment` property describes the segment key, and `metrics` contains the funnel statistics for that slice.

IShoppingMallPaymentFunnelAnalyticsItem.description:
Aggregated payment funnel statistics for a single scope (either overall or for a specific segment) on the shoppingMall platform.

Represents counts and monetary totals at key funnel stages, together with conversion rates between sequential stages. All metrics are aggregated and do not reveal individual customer or transaction details.

ordersCreatedCount.description:
Number of orders created within the analytics scope.

This is typically the first stage of the payment funnel, representing the universe of orders that could potentially lead to payment attempts.

paymentsInitiatedCount.description:
Number of payment transactions initiated within the analytics scope.

Includes initial payment attempts linked to in-scope orders, regardless of whether they were subsequently authorized, captured, refunded, or charged back.

authorizationsApprovedCount.description:
Number of payment authorizations that were successfully approved within the analytics scope.

This stage reflects the subset of initiated payments that passed initial authorization checks by the payment provider or issuer.

capturesCompletedCount.description:
Number of payment captures that were successfully completed within the analytics scope.

Represents the subset of approved authorizations where funds were actually captured and booked.

refundsProcessedCount.description:
Number of refund transactions processed within the analytics scope.

This includes both full and partial refunds associated with captured payments that fall into the time window and filter criteria.

chargebacksRecordedCount.description:
Number of payment chargebacks recorded within the analytics scope.

Represents disputes or reversals initiated through financial institutions against previously captured payments.

ordersTotalAmount.description:
Total monetary amount of orders created within the analytics scope.

Expressed in the reporting currency chosen by the backend for this analytics response. Typically represents the sum of order grand totals before payment fees and external adjustments.

authorizedTotalAmount.description:
Total monetary amount of payment authorizations that were approved within the analytics scope.

Represents the volume of funds for which authorization succeeded, even if later captures, refunds, or chargebacks changed the net settled amount.

capturedTotalAmount.description:
Total monetary amount of captures completed within the analytics scope.

Represents the volume of funds actually captured and booked for in-scope payments.

refundedTotalAmount.description:
Total monetary amount refunded within the analytics scope.

Includes both full and partial refunds associated with in-scope payments and orders, expressed in the reporting currency.

chargebackTotalAmount.description:
Total monetary amount of chargebacks recorded within the analytics scope.

Represents the volume of disputed funds that have been charged back by financial institutions.

orderToPaymentConversionRate.description:
Conversion rate from orders created to payments initiated.

Computed as `paymentsInitiatedCount / max(1, ordersCreatedCount)` and expressed as a value between 0 and 1. Represents how effectively created orders progress to payment attempts.

paymentToAuthorizationConversionRate.description:
Conversion rate from payments initiated to authorizations approved.

Computed as `authorizationsApprovedCount / max(1, paymentsInitiatedCount)` and expressed as a value between 0 and 1. Highlights authorization success rates and potential issues with fraud or issuer decline rates.

authorizationToCaptureConversionRate.description:
Conversion rate from authorizations approved to captures completed.

Computed as `capturesCompletedCount / max(1, authorizationsApprovedCount)` and expressed as a value between 0 and 1. Indicates to what extent successful authorizations lead to actual fund capture.

netCapturedAmount.description:
Net captured amount after subtracting refunds and chargebacks from captured volume within the analytics scope.

Computed as `capturedTotalAmount - refundedTotalAmount - chargebackTotalAmount`, truncated at zero if negative. Provides a summary indicator of effective net revenue for the analyzed funnel slice.

IShoppingMallPaymentFunnelSegmentAnalyti.description:
Payment funnel analytics for a single segment key defined by one or more segmentation dimensions on the shoppingMall platform.

Couples a structured segment descriptor with aggregated funnel metrics for that specific slice, enabling dashboards to break down performance by region, payment method, seller, device, channel, or combinations thereof.

segment.description:
Descriptor of the segment for which these funnel metrics were computed.

Contains one or more dimension values corresponding to the segmentation dimensions used in the analytics request (for example, a region code and payment method code).

metrics.description:
Aggregated payment funnel statistics for this specific segment.

Contains counts, monetary totals, and conversion rates for each funnel stage, computed after applying all filters and segmentation criteria.

IShoppingMallPaymentFunnelSegmentKey.description:
Structured identifier for a segment used in payment funnel analytics on the shoppingMall platform.

Represents the combination of dimension values (such as region, payment method, seller, device, or channel) that define a single analytics slice. Only dimensions requested in the analytics query and supported by the backend will appear in this object.

regionCode.description:
Region code associated with this segment, if region segmentation was requested and applicable.

Typically corresponds to a configured market or geographic region identifier used in platform configuration and reporting.

paymentMethodCode.description:
Payment method code for this segment, if payment method segmentation was requested and applicable.

Typical values might include high-level categories such as `card`, `bank_transfer`, or `wallet`, or more granular method identifiers defined in the payment configuration tables.

sellerId.description:
Identifier of the seller associated with this segment, if seller segmentation was requested and applicable.

Represents the merchant account whose orders and payments are included in this analytics slice.

deviceType.description:
Device type associated with this segment, if device segmentation was requested and applicable.

Examples might include `desktop`, `mobile_web`, or `mobile_app`, depending on how the platform records client device information.

channelCode.description:
Sales or traffic channel code associated with this segment, if channel segmentation was requested and applicable.

Examples might include `web`, `ios_app`, `android_app`, or other channel identifiers used in analytics and attribution.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.IRe.description:
Search, filter, and segmentation criteria for computing seller earnings analytics over a selected time range on the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by the administrative analytics endpoint that aggregates seller earnings across payouts, orders, refunds, and related financial entities. It allows platform administrators to specify reporting windows, seller selection criteria, segmentation dimensions, and sorting options.

The backend uses this structure to build analytics queries against multiple Prisma models, including seller payouts, payout items, orders, order segments, order lines, refunds, and seller performance summaries. It is read-only and does not map directly to a single Prisma model table.

timeRange.description:
Primary reporting window for the analytics query.

The time range is typically applied to payout creation time, order completion time, or a configured reference timestamp depending on the implementation. The backend should validate reasonable bounds to avoid excessively large queries.

compareToPreviousPeriod.description:
Whether the analytics response should include comparative metrics against a previous period.

When true, the backend may compute trend indicators (such as percentage change compared to the immediately preceding period of equal length) for GMV, net earnings, refunds, and other financial metrics.

sellerScope.description:
Definition of which sellers are included in this analytics request.

This can represent all sellers on the platform, a specific subset of sellers by identifier, or a filtered segment such as by brand, region, or performance criteria. The backend must still enforce authorization so that the caller only sees allowed seller scopes.

segmentations.description:
List of segmentation dimensions to break down analytics results.

Each entry describes a dimension such as region, category, payout cycle, or custom tags. The backend may limit the number of simultaneous segmentations to ensure query performance.

orderBy.description:
Primary sorting field for the aggregated seller analytics results.

Typical values include:
- `totalGmv` – sort by gross merchandise value
- `netEarnings` – sort by net earnings after fees and refunds
- `refundRate` – sort by percentage of refunded amounts vs GMV
- `sellerName` – sort alphabetically by seller display name

The backend should validate that the value is one of the allowed fields and apply sensible defaults when omitted.

oneOf.description:
Sorting direction for the analytics results.

Expected values are:
- `asc` – ascending order
- `desc` – descending order

When omitted, the backend typically defaults to `desc` for financial metrics such as GMV or net earnings.

Sorting direction for the analytics results.

Expected values are:
- `asc` – ascending order
- `desc` – descending order

When omitted, the backend typically defaults to `desc` for financial metrics such as GMV or net earnings.

orderDirection.description:
Sorting direction for the analytics results.

Expected values are:
- `asc` – ascending order
- `desc` – descending order

When omitted, the backend typically defaults to `desc` for financial metrics such as GMV or net earnings.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated analytics results.

Used together with `limit` to paginate seller-level result sets. If omitted, the backend should default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of sellers (or seller segments) to return in a single analytics page.

The backend should enforce a reasonable maximum to protect performance (for example, 50 or 100 records per page).

filters.description:
Additional filter conditions applied to the analytics query.

Filters can restrict the dataset by payout status, order status, region, product category, or other attributes derived from the underlying Prisma models. These constraints refine which financial records are included in the aggregation.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.ITi.description:
Time range selection for seller earnings analytics.

Represents the primary reporting window used to aggregate payouts, orders, and refunds. Implementations typically apply this range to either payout creation timestamps or order completion timestamps, depending on product requirements.

The range is inclusive of the start and end instants and must use ISO 8601 date-time strings in UTC or with explicit offsets.

start.description:
Start of the reporting window in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This timestamp defines the earliest instant from which payouts, orders, and related financial records should be considered for analytics. It is inclusive and should be expressed in UTC or include an explicit time zone offset.

end.description:
End of the reporting window in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This timestamp defines the latest instant up to which financial records are included in the analytics computation. It is inclusive and should be expressed in UTC or include an explicit time zone offset.

The backend should validate that `end` is greater than or equal to `start` and that the overall window does not exceed configured maximum duration limits.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.ISe.description:
Scope definition describing which sellers are included in a seller earnings analytics request.

This structure allows platform administrators to select all sellers, a specific set of seller IDs, or dynamically filtered segments such as by region or performance tier.

Authorization enforcement must ensure that the requester is allowed to view analytics for the chosen seller set, especially if a future variant is exposed directly to sellers.

oneOf.description:
Mode describing how sellers are selected for this analytics request.

Supported values include:
- `all` – include all sellers in the platform
- `byIds` – include only the specific sellers listed in `sellerIds`
- `byFilter` – include sellers matching the criteria in `sellerFilter`

The backend must validate that required companion fields are present based on the selected mode.

Supported values include:

- `byIds` – include only the specific sellers listed in `sellerIds`
- `byFilter` – include sellers matching the criteria in `sellerFilter`

The backend must validate that required companion fields are present based on the selected mode.

The backend must validate that required companion fields are present based on the selected mode.

mode.description:
Mode describing how sellers are selected for this analytics request.

Supported values include:
- `all` – include all sellers in the platform
- `byIds` – include only the specific sellers listed in `sellerIds`
- `byFilter` – include sellers matching the criteria in `sellerFilter`

The backend must validate that required companion fields are present based on the selected mode.

sellerIds.description:
List of seller identifiers when `mode` is `byIds`.

Each identifier refers to a seller account in the shopping_mall_seller model. The backend should treat this list as authoritative for which sellers to include when this mode is selected.

sellerFilter.description:
Dynamic seller filter criteria when `mode` is `byFilter`.

Allows administrators to define selection criteria such as region, brand, performance tier, or risk flags. The exact mapping to Prisma queries is implementation-specific.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.ISe.description:
Dynamic seller filtering criteria used when `sellerScope.mode` is `byFilter` in seller earnings analytics requests.

This filter object narrows down which sellers are included in the aggregation window by applying optional constraints such as brand affiliation, operating region, performance tier, and risk flag status. All properties are optional and can be combined; omitting a property means that particular dimension is not used to restrict the seller cohort.

The effective seller set is derived from marketplace account and analytics tables such as `shopping_mall_seller`, `shopping_mall_brands`, `shopping_mall_region_settings`, `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries`, and `shopping_mall_risk_flags`. The filter does not perform any mutation; it only scopes read-only analytical computations.

brandIds.description:
Optional list of brand identifiers used to filter sellers that are associated with specific brands in the catalog.

When provided, only sellers that have at least one active product mapped to one of the specified brands (for example, through records in `shopping_mall_brands` and related product tables) are included in the analytics results. Each entry in this array is expected to be a stable brand primary key value such as `shopping_mall_brands.id`. Duplicate identifiers are ignored by the backend.

items.description:
Identifier of a brand used in seller earnings analytics filters.

The value typically corresponds to a primary key or business identifier from the `shopping_mall_brands` table and must reference an existing brand for the filter to be effective.

regionCodes.description:
Optional list of region codes used to filter sellers that operate in specific geographic or market regions.

Region codes generally correspond to configuration entries in the `shopping_mall_region_settings` table (for example, `region_code` or an equivalent business key). When supplied, only sellers that are configured to sell into at least one of the listed regions are considered in the analytics aggregation.

items.description:
Region code value used to restrict seller earnings analytics to specific markets.

This should match a configured region code in `shopping_mall_region_settings` or an equivalent region configuration source so that the backend can resolve the seller-to-region relationship correctly.

oneOf.description:
Filter sellers whose current performance tier has been classified as `gold`.

This tier is typically computed from periodic snapshots such as `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries` and indicates the highest performance band according to business rules.

Filter sellers whose current performance tier has been classified as `silver`.

This tier represents an intermediate performance band as derived from performance summary tables such as `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries`.

Filter sellers whose current performance tier has been classified as `bronze`.

This tier usually denotes the baseline performance band as determined by seller performance summary data.

performanceTier.description:
Optional performance tier constraint applied to the seller cohort before computing earnings analytics.

When this field is present, only sellers whose current performance tier matches one of the supported values (`gold`, `silver`, or `bronze`) as derived from performance analytics tables (for example, `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries`) are included. When omitted, sellers of all performance tiers are considered.

riskFlaggedOnly.description:
Flag indicating whether the seller earnings analytics should be restricted to sellers with active risk or fraud flags.

When set to `true`, the backend limits the seller cohort to those that currently have one or more active entries in risk-related tables such as `shopping_mall_risk_flags` or equivalent fraud monitoring structures. When `false` or omitted, sellers are not filtered by risk state and both flagged and unflagged sellers are included in the analysis.

oneOf.description:
No segmentation: compute a single aggregate over the entire filtered seller cohort.

This option instructs the analytics engine to return overall earnings metrics without grouping results by any secondary dimension.

Segment seller earnings analytics by operating region.

With this option, aggregated metrics are grouped by region code or market as derived from configuration such as `shopping_mall_region_settings`, allowing comparison of seller performance across regions.

Segment seller earnings analytics by catalog category.

Using this dimension, the analytics output is grouped by high-level or leaf catalog categories associated with each seller's products, enabling category-level earnings insights.

Segment seller earnings analytics by payout cycle or settlement period.

In this mode, aggregated metrics are grouped by payout cycle identifiers (for example, monthly or weekly settlement batches) derived from payout-related tables such as `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`.

Segment seller earnings analytics by seller performance tier.

When selected, earnings metrics are grouped by the performance bands (for example, `gold`, `silver`, `bronze`) assigned in performance summary tables such as `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries`, enabling comparison across tiers.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.IES.description:
Segmentation dimension used to group seller earnings analytics results.

Each value represents a supported dimension by which the backend can break down aggregated metrics, such as operating region, catalog category, payout cycle, or performance tier. Selecting `none` returns a single unsegmented aggregate, while the other options produce multiple grouped entries in the analytics response.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.IFi.description:
Additional filter constraints applied to seller earnings analytics queries.

These filters operate at the level of underlying payouts, orders, and related financial records to include or exclude specific subsets of data. All fields are optional and may be combined.

minNetEarnings.description:

Sellers whose net earnings fall below this threshold may be excluded from the response. Values should be expressed in the platform's base currency units.

maxNetEarnings.description:

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.description:
Aggregated seller earnings analytics for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents the response from an administrative analytics endpoint that composes data from multiple financial and operational Prisma models, including seller payouts, payout items, orders, order segments, order lines, refunds, refund items, and seller performance summaries.

The structure is designed for dashboard and reporting use cases, offering per-seller and optionally segmented metrics such as gross merchandise value (GMV), fees, refunds, net earnings, and payout statuses. It does not map directly to a single Prisma table, but instead acts as a projection tailored for analytics.

timeRange.description:
Effective reporting window used for the analytics computation.

Echoes or normalizes the requested time range so that clients know exactly which period the metrics cover.

sellerScope.description:
Effective seller scope used in this analytics response.

This may mirror the request or be normalized/expanded by the backend (for example, when aliases or groups are resolved into explicit seller identifiers).

segmentations.description:
Segmentation dimensions actually used in this analytics computation.

Typically mirrors the requested segmentation dimensions but may be reduced by the backend if certain combinations are not supported or exceed allowed cardinality.

summary.description:
Global summary metrics across all included sellers and segments.

Provides high-level figures such as total gross merchandise value, total platform fees, total refunds, and total net earnings for the selected period and scope.

items.description:
Per-seller (and optionally per-segment) analytics records.

Each item contains metrics for a single seller or seller+segment combination, including GMV, fees, refunded amounts, net earnings, and payout status distributions.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.ISu.description:
Global aggregate metrics for seller earnings analytics.

Summarizes high-level financial figures across all sellers and segments included in the analytics response. These values are suitable for top-level KPIs in dashboards and reports.

totalGmv.description:
Total gross merchandise value (GMV) across all relevant orders for the selected sellers and time range.

Expressed in the platform's base currency units.

totalPlatformFees.description:
Total platform fees and commissions charged across all relevant transactions in the analytics scope.

Includes seller commissions and any other platform-specific charges as appropriate.

totalRefundAmount.description:
Total amount refunded to customers within the analytics scope.

Includes full and partial refunds associated with orders and order lines included in the reporting window.

totalChargebackAmount.description:
Total amount associated with chargebacks applied against previously captured payments within the analytics scope.

This value may be zero if chargebacks are rare or not modeled for the given period.

totalNetEarnings.description:
Total net earnings for all sellers combined across the analytics scope.

Typically calculated as GMV minus platform fees, discounts, refunds, and chargebacks, depending on business rules.

sellerCount.description:
Number of distinct sellers included in the analytics computation.

Useful for contextualizing aggregate metrics such as average earnings per seller.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.IIt.description:
Per-seller (and optionally per-segment) earnings analytics record.

Each instance represents aggregated financial metrics for a single seller or seller plus an additional segment (such as region or category) within the selected reporting window.

This structure is optimized for use in tables and charts on administrative dashboards.

seller.description:
Summary information for the seller to which these analytics metrics belong.

This is a belongs-to association to the seller entity and exposes a lightweight view of the seller, including its identifier and key display fields, instead of separate scalar `sellerId` and `sellerName` fields.

Using `IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary` ensures consistent relation modeling across the API and allows future expansion of seller summary data without changing the analytics item shape.

segment.description:
Optional segment descriptor when results are broken down by a specific segmentation dimension.

For example, if segmenting by region, this will describe the region; if segmenting by category, it will describe the category.

gmv.description:
Gross merchandise value (GMV) for this seller (and segment, if applicable) in the selected time range.

Represents the sum of order line amounts before fees, discounts, and refunds.

platformFees.description: Total platform fees and commissions charged for this seller (and segment, if applicable).

refundAmount.description: Total refunded amount associated with this seller (and segment, if applicable) within the analytics scope.

chargebackAmount.description: Total chargeback amount impacting this seller's earnings within the analytics scope.

netEarnings.description: Net earnings for this seller (and segment, if applicable) after subtracting fees, refunds, and chargebacks from GMV according to business rules.

orderCount.description:
Number of orders contributing to this analytics record.

May be the count of master orders, seller segments, or another order-level unit depending on implementation details.

payoutCompletedAmount.description: Total amount that has already been paid out to the seller in completed payout batches within the analytics scope.

payoutPendingAmount.description: Total amount that is accrued for the seller but not yet paid out (for example, in pending or processing payouts).

refundRate.description:
Refund rate for this seller (and segment, if applicable) expressed as a proportion of GMV.

Typically represented as a number between 0 and 1, where 0.1 represents a 10% refund rate.

chargebackRate.description:
Chargeback rate for this seller (and segment, if applicable) expressed as a proportion of GMV.

Typically represented as a number between 0 and 1.

IShoppingMallSellerEarningsAnalytics.ISe.description:
Descriptor for a single segmentation bucket in seller earnings analytics.

When analytics results are segmented (for example, by region or category), this structure provides the identifying information for the segment that a particular item belongs to.

The meaning of the fields depends on the active segmentation dimension. For example, when segmenting by region, `code` might hold a region code and `label` the human-readable region name.

dimension.description:
Segmentation dimension that this segment belongs to.

Must match one of the requested or effective segmentation dimensions from the analytics request.

code.description:
Machine-readable code identifying the segment within its dimension.

Examples:
- Region code such as `KR`, `US`, or `EU-NORTH`
- Category identifier or slug
- Payout cycle identifier

label.description:
Human-readable label for the segment, suitable for display in dashboards and reports.

Examples:
- `Korea`
- `United States`
- `Electronics`
- `March 2025 Payout Cycle`

IShoppingMallPaymentSettlementReport.IRe.description:
Filter and configuration parameters for generating the shopping mall payment settlement report.

This request DTO encapsulates the reporting window, scoping, and aggregation options for building a settlement-oriented view across payment transactions, refunds, chargebacks, and seller payouts. It is read-only and does not correspond to a single Prisma table; instead, it is used to parameterize analytical queries over multiple payment and settlement models.

The API uses this type in a PATCH operation because the filter structure can be complex and nested, and is therefore supplied in the request body rather than as simple query parameters.

dateRange.description:
Inclusive date/time range that defines which payment-side events are considered in the settlement report.

Typical implementations use either the payment transaction creation timestamp, capture timestamp, or payout settlement timestamp as the primary axis, depending on business rules. If omitted, the backend may apply a sensible default window such as the last 7 days.

timeZone.description:
IANA time zone identifier used to interpret the provided date range and to normalize timestamps in the report, for example "Asia/Seoul" or "UTC".

Providing an explicit time zone ensures that financial periods such as days or months align with business expectations. If omitted, the backend may fall back to a platform default time zone.

paymentMethodCodes.description:
Optional list of payment method codes to include in the settlement report.

Each entry typically corresponds to a configured payment method record (for example, `card_visa`, `card_master`, `bank_transfer`, `virtual_account`). When provided, only settlement data originating from the specified methods will be included.

currencies.description:
Optional list of ISO 4217 currency codes (such as "KRW", "USD", "EUR") to include in the report.

If omitted, the report may include all currencies or apply a platform default. When multiple currencies are requested, the report usually does not attempt currency conversion; values are reported in their native currency.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers to scope the settlement report to specific merchants.

When provided, only transactions, refunds, chargebacks, and payouts that involve one of the listed sellers are considered. This is primarily used by platform administrators to focus on particular sellers; sellers themselves typically receive scoping via authentication context and may leave this unset.

includePendingRefunds.description:
Flag indicating whether pending or in-progress refund transactions should be included in the report.

When `true`, rows may include amounts related to refunds that have been requested but not yet fully settled by the payment processor. When `false`, only fully completed refunds are incorporated into the aggregated amounts.

includePendingPayouts.description:
Flag indicating whether payout batches that are scheduled or processing, but not yet fully completed, should be included.

This allows finance users to examine future or in-flight settlements in addition to already completed payouts. When omitted, the backend may default to completed-only payouts for conservative reconciliation.

statusFilters.description:
Optional list of high-level settlement status values to include in the report.

These statuses represent normalized states computed from underlying payment, refund, chargeback, and payout data, such as whether a settlement unit is fully settled, partially refunded, in dispute, or chargebacked.

minGrossAmount.description:
Optional lower bound filter on gross payment amount for included settlement rows.

When provided, only rows whose gross amount is greater than or equal to this value are returned. This is often used to focus on higher-value transactions during reconciliation or investigation.

maxGrossAmount.description:
Optional upper bound filter on gross payment amount for included settlement rows.

When provided together with `minGrossAmount`, this defines a gross-amount range for the report. If omitted, no upper bound is applied.

page.description:
Page index for paginated settlement results, starting from 1.

Used together with `limit` to control which slice of the report is returned. If omitted, the backend may default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of settlement rows to return in a single page.

The backend may enforce an upper bound for performance reasons. Typical defaults range from 20 to 100 items per page.

sort.description:
Sorting configuration that controls the ordering of settlement rows in the response.

Callers can choose to sort by transaction time, settlement time, gross amount, net amount, or other supported fields and specify ascending or descending order.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutStatementReport.description:
Filter and configuration parameters for generating seller payout statement reports in the shopping mall platform.

This request DTO is used to retrieve payout-oriented analytical views that explain how seller payout batches were computed from orders, payment transactions, refunds, chargebacks, and other adjustments. It does not map directly to a single Prisma model; instead, it controls the query window and scoping across payout and order-related tables.

The API uses a PATCH method with a request body because the filter structure can be moderately complex and is better expressed as JSON than as flat query parameters.

dateRange.description:
Primary date/time window for selecting payout batches or associated orders that should be included in the statement.

Implementations may apply this range to payout creation time, payout completion time, or order completion time depending on configured business rules and the report mode. When omitted, the backend may fall back to a sensible default window such as the most recent settlement period configured for the tenant.

timeZone.description:
IANA time zone identifier used to interpret the date range and normalize timestamps within the payout statement, such as "Asia/Seoul" or "UTC".

Providing a consistent time zone ensures that daily and monthly payout periods align with both platform and seller expectations. When this field is omitted, the backend typically uses the platform’s default reporting time zone.

items.description:
Unique identifier of a seller account whose payouts should be included in the report.

These UUIDs correspond to primary keys from the seller actor model and allow the report to be scoped to specific merchants.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers to include in the payout statement.

Platform administrators may specify one or more sellers to inspect, whereas individual sellers typically see only their own data and may omit this field. When provided, only payout batches and items belonging to the listed sellers are included; duplicates and unknown IDs are silently ignored by the backend implementation.

payoutStatusFilters.description:
Optional list of payout status values to filter the statement, such as scheduled, processing, or completed.

This allows callers to focus on payouts that have been fully processed, those that are upcoming, or a mixture of both depending on reconciliation needs. When omitted, the report includes all payout statuses that are relevant for the selected time window.

items.description:
Single ISO 4217 currency code such as "USD", "KRW", or "EUR".

Each entry identifies one settlement currency that should be included when computing and aggregating payout rows.

currencies.description:
Optional list of ISO 4217 currency codes for which payout information should be returned.

If omitted, the backend typically includes payouts in all supported settlement currencies or defaults to the tenant’s primary currency, depending on configuration. Duplicate currency codes are ignored, and any unknown or unsupported codes are safely discarded without causing the request to fail.

includeOrderBreakdown.description:
Flag indicating whether the statement should include per-order or per-order-line level breakdown inside each payout row.

When `true`, the underlying implementation may join additional order and order line data so that each payout row exposes detailed composition suitable for deep reconciliation. When `false`, a more compact batch-level summary is returned for efficiency and faster response times.

includeRefundAndChargebackImpact.description:
Flag indicating whether refund and chargeback effects should be explicitly broken out in the payout statement rows.

When `true`, rows may contain or be backed by separate fields for refunded amounts, chargeback amounts, and adjustments that reduced the final payout amount, enabling fine-grained financial analysis. When `false`, those effects may only be visible through the net payout amount without exposing intermediate components in the report payload.

page.description:
Page index for the paginated payout statement results, starting from 1.

Used together with `limit` to navigate through the full result set. If this field is omitted, the backend typically defaults to the first page (value `1`), ensuring a deterministic starting point for callers that do not explicitly manage pagination state.

limit.description:
Maximum number of payout statement rows to return in a single page.

This value controls page size and therefore the number of rows in the `data` array of the paginated response. The backend may impose an upper bound to protect system resources and, when this field is omitted, may apply a sensible default page size such as 20 or 50 rows per page depending on platform configuration.

sort.description:
Sorting configuration that defines the ordering of payout statement rows.

Callers can choose to sort by payout creation time, completion time, seller identifier, gross amount, or other supported attributes, and can specify ascending or descending order. When omitted, the backend uses a stable default ordering, typically by payout creation or completion time in descending order so that the most recent payouts appear first.

IShoppingMallReportDateRange.description:
Generic date/time range used to scope analytical reports in the shopping mall domain.

This type is reused across multiple reporting endpoints, including payment settlement and seller payout statements, to consistently express an inclusive time window in ISO 8601 format.

Both bounds are required so that reports can be computed deterministically, and the range is interpreted in combination with the effective report time zone (either provided explicitly in the request or derived from platform configuration). This ensures that day, week, and month boundaries are handled consistently across different analytics endpoints.

from.description:
Inclusive start of the reporting window, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

The backend interprets this timestamp in conjunction with the report’s effective time zone, which may be supplied separately in the request. All events or rows whose timestamps fall on or after this instant are considered within the window.

to.description:
Inclusive end of the reporting window, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

The backend interprets this timestamp in conjunction with the report’s effective time zone and may normalize the range internally to match the granularity of the specific report (for example, treating the end as the end of a calendar day when a date-only value is supplied by clients). Events or rows whose timestamps fall on or before this instant are considered part of the window for most reports, unless a particular endpoint explicitly documents a different convention.

IShoppingMallSettlementReportSort.description:
Sorting configuration for payment settlement reports in the shopping mall platform.

This type allows callers to specify the primary sort field and direction for settlement rows, enabling common views such as most recent first, highest gross amount first, highest gross amount, highest net amount, or by normalized settlement status. Only the explicitly documented field and direction values are accepted; any other value is considered invalid and will be rejected at validation time.

oneOf.description:
Field of the settlement row used as the primary sort key.

The `transactionCreatedAt` option sorts settlement rows based on the time when the underlying payment transaction was originally created, typically used to inspect the chronological intake of payments.

Field of the settlement row used as the primary sort key.

The `transactionCapturedAt` option sorts settlement rows by the time when funds were successfully captured, which is useful for finance and settlement operations focusing on confirmed payments.

Field of the settlement row used as the primary sort key.

The `settlementDate` option orders rows by the date on which settlement is considered effective in the ledger or payout cycle, enabling chronological settlement views.

Field of the settlement row used as the primary sort key.

The `grossAmount` option sorts rows by the gross transaction amount before fees or adjustments, supporting views such as highest or lowest gross amounts first.

Field of the settlement row used as the primary sort key.

The `netAmount` option sorts rows by the net amount after fees, refunds, or adjustments, which is frequently used in financial reconciliation views.

Field of the settlement row used as the primary sort key.

The `status` option groups and sorts settlement rows according to their normalized settlement status (for example, pending, in_progress, settled, or failed), which is useful when reviewing workflow states.

field.description:
Field of the settlement row used as the primary sort key.

Supported values are a closed set of string literals that indicate which business field drives the ordering: `transactionCreatedAt`, `transactionCapturedAt`, `settlementDate`, `grossAmount`, `netAmount`, or `status`. Values outside this set are not allowed and will be rejected by the API.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the chosen field.

The `asc` option orders rows in ascending order for the selected field and is equivalent in meaning to `ascending` for clients that prefer abbreviated values.

Sort direction applied to the chosen field.

The `desc` option orders rows in descending order for the selected field and is equivalent in meaning to `descending` for clients that prefer abbreviated values.

Sort direction applied to the chosen field.

The `ascending` option orders rows in ascending order for the selected field and is semantically equivalent to `asc`, provided for clients that prefer more descriptive values.

Sort direction applied to the chosen field.

The `descending` option orders rows in descending order for the selected field and is semantically equivalent to `desc`, provided for clients that prefer more descriptive values.

direction.description:
Sort direction applied to the chosen field.

The allowed values form a closed set: `asc`, `desc`, `ascending`, or `descending`. `asc` and `ascending` are treated equivalently as ascending order; `desc` and `descending` are treated equivalently as descending order. Any other value is invalid and will be rejected.

IShoppingMallPayoutStatementSort.description:
Sorting configuration for seller payout statement reports in the shopping mall platform.

This type enables callers to sort payout statement rows consistently, for example by payout creation time, completion time, seller identifier, gross amount, or net payout amount. Only the documented field and direction values are accepted; any other value is invalid and rejected during validation.

oneOf.description:
Field of the payout statement row used as the primary sort key.

The `payoutCreatedAt` option sorts payout statement rows by the timestamp when the payout batch or statement record was created, useful for reviewing recently generated payout runs.

Field of the payout statement row used as the primary sort key.

The `payoutCompletedAt` option sorts rows by the completion or settlement timestamp of the payout, often used by finance teams to analyze when sellers actually received funds.

Field of the payout statement row used as the primary sort key.

The `sellerId` option groups and orders rows by seller identifier, which helps when reviewing payouts per seller or aligning with external seller accounting references.

Field of the payout statement row used as the primary sort key.

The `grossAmount` option sorts payout statement rows by the gross amount of payouts before fees or adjustments, supporting views such as largest or smallest gross payout first.

Field of the payout statement row used as the primary sort key.

The `netPayoutAmount` option sorts rows based on the net amount that will actually be transferred to the seller after fees, refunds, or other adjustments, which is typically the most important business amount for settlement analysis.

field.description:
Field of the payout statement row used as the primary sort key.

Supported values are a closed set of string literals: `payoutCreatedAt`, `payoutCompletedAt`, `sellerId`, `grossAmount`, or `netPayoutAmount`. Any other value is considered invalid and will be rejected by the API.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the chosen sort field.

The `asc` option orders rows in ascending order for the selected field and is equivalent in meaning to `ascending` for clients that prefer abbreviated values.

Sort direction applied to the chosen sort field.

The `desc` option orders rows in descending order for the selected field and is equivalent in meaning to `descending` for clients that prefer abbreviated values.

Sort direction applied to the chosen sort field.

The `ascending` option orders rows in ascending order for the selected field and is semantically equivalent to `asc`, provided for clients that prefer more descriptive values.

Sort direction applied to the chosen sort field.

The `descending` option orders rows in descending order for the selected field and is semantically equivalent to `desc`, provided for clients that prefer more descriptive values.

direction.description:
Sort direction applied to the chosen sort field.

The allowed values form a closed set: `asc`, `desc`, `ascending`, or `descending`. `asc` and `ascending` both represent ascending order; `desc` and `descending` both represent descending order. Any other value is not permitted and will be rejected by the API.

oneOf.description:
The settlement row is in an initial or in-progress state where the underlying payment transaction has been authorized or initiated but has not yet reached a final settled, refunded, or chargebacked outcome.

This status is useful when analyzing work-in-progress settlement items that may still move into capture, partial settlement, or other terminal states and should typically be excluded from finalized revenue or payout figures.

The settlement row represents a case where only a portion of the original payment amount has been successfully settled, often because some items have shipped or completed while others remain pending, cancelled, or disputed.

This status is typically used for analytics where the business needs to distinguish partially realized revenue or payout amounts from fully settled orders, especially in multi-shipment or multi-seller scenarios.

The settlement row represents a fully settled case where the effective net amount has been captured and no further refunds or chargebacks are currently pending.

This status is usually treated as a terminal state for revenue recognition and payout calculations, and rows in this state are commonly included in settlement totals and financial reporting snapshots.

The settlement row represents a case where part of the original settled amount has been refunded, but another part remains recognized as completed revenue and/or subject to payout.

This status is useful for distinguishing mixed outcomes—such as partial item returns or partial service failures—from fully refunded cases, enabling more granular refund and margin analysis.

The settlement row represents a case where the entire effective amount has been refunded, resulting in no remaining recognized revenue or payout for this settlement unit.

This status is typically treated as a terminal negative outcome for revenue analysis and may be highlighted in refund and customer satisfaction reporting.

The settlement row is associated with a chargeback process that has been initiated but not yet resolved, such as a dispute raised with a card network or financial institution.

This status allows finance and risk teams to track exposure to potential chargeback losses separately from standard refund flows while the final outcome is still unknown.

The settlement row represents a case where a chargeback has been finalized against the merchant or platform, reducing or eliminating the originally settled amount from the platform's perspective.

This status is typically used in risk and loss reporting, as well as in reconciliation between payment providers, merchants, and the platform's internal ledgers.

IEShoppingMallPaymentSettlementStatus.description:
Normalized high-level status for a payment settlement row in the shopping mall platform.

These values summarize the combined state of payments, refunds, chargebacks, and payouts for a given logical settlement unit. They are used for filtering and aggregating in payment settlement reports rather than mapping directly to a single underlying record.

oneOf.description:
The seller payout batch has been calculated and scheduled but the transfer or disbursement has not yet started processing in banking or payments infrastructure.

This status is commonly used to represent upcoming payouts in dashboards and statements so that sellers and finance staff can anticipate future cash flows by date and amount.

The seller payout batch is currently undergoing processing, such as being submitted to a payment provider, undergoing internal checks, or waiting for confirmation from banking rails.

This status indicates the payout is actively moving through the pipeline and may be transient; it is useful for operational monitoring and for explaining short-term differences between expected and actually received payouts.

The seller payout batch has been successfully completed and the corresponding funds have been disbursed to the seller according to the configured payout method.

This status is typically treated as a terminal state in payout statements and financial reporting and is the primary basis for recognizing that a seller has actually received funds for the included orders or line items.

The seller payout batch failed during processing—for example due to invalid bank details, payment provider errors, or internal validation failures—and the disbursement did not complete.

This status is important for exception handling workflows, prompting reconfiguration of payout details, retries of the batch, or manual intervention by support or finance teams.

The seller payout batch is intentionally put on hold and not allowed to advance to processing, often due to risk, compliance, or manual review reasons such as fraud investigation or negative balance checks.

This status allows the platform to explicitly separate payouts blocked by policy or review from those that are simply pending or failed for technical reasons, and it should be surfaced clearly to internal operators and, when appropriate, to sellers.

IEShoppingMallSellerPayoutStatus.description:
High-level status for seller payout batches in the shopping mall platform.

These values are used to filter and describe payout statement rows, indicating whether a batch is upcoming, currently being processed, successfully completed, has failed, or is temporarily on hold for manual review or investigation.

IShoppingMallPaymentsOverview.description:
Aggregated payments overview metrics for the shoppingMall platform.

Represents high-level analytical KPIs derived from payment-related Prisma tables such as `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, `shopping_mall_payment_status_events`, and `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`. This DTO is optimized for admin dashboard visualizations and does not expose individual transaction records or personally identifiable customer information.

totalProcessedAmount.description:
Total payment volume processed in the selected analysis window across all successful payment transactions.

This value is typically computed as the sum of captured payment amounts from `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, expressed in the platform's base currency.

successfulTransactionCount.description:
Number of successfully completed payment transactions in the analysis window.

Usually corresponds to transactions whose latest status in `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` is a terminal success state.

failedTransactionCount.description:
Number of failed payment transactions in the analysis window.

Includes transactions that ended in error, were declined, or otherwise did not reach a successful completion state.

pendingTransactionCount.description:
Number of payment transactions that are currently pending or in-progress in the analysis window.

Corresponds to transactions that have not yet reached a terminal success or failure state at the time of aggregation.

refundCount.description:
Number of refund transactions recorded in `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` during the analysis window.

Includes both full and partial refunds associated with one or more original payment transactions.

totalRefundAmount.description:
Total refunded amount over the analysis window, computed from `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`.

This typically reflects how much volume has been returned to customers for all or part of their orders, expressed in the platform's base currency.

refundRate.description:
Ratio of refunded volume relative to processed payment volume in the analysis window.

Implementations commonly compute this as `totalRefundAmount / totalProcessedAmount` and may clamp or handle zero-division cases appropriately when no processed volume exists in the window.

byStatus.description:
Breakdown of payment transactions by high-level status category (such as succeeded, failed, pending) for the analysis window.

This array is always present in the response. When there is no data for the selected time window, it will be an empty array rather than being omitted or null, allowing dashboard clients to render consistent structures without additional null checks.

byMethod.description:
Breakdown of payment metrics grouped by payment method (for example, credit card, bank transfer, e-wallet).

This array is always present in the response. If no transactions match the selected time window or filters, the array will be empty so that consumers can safely iterate without defensive presence checks.

byDay.description:
Time-series breakdown of processed payments for recent days within the analysis window.

Each element represents aggregated metrics for a single day, enabling dashboard charts of trends. The array itself is always present; when no data falls into the configured window, it is returned as an empty array so that time-series visualizations can still operate on a predictable structure.

IShoppingMallPaymentsOverviewByStatus.description:
Aggregated payment metrics for a single high-level payment status within the analysis window.

Typically represents a rollup over many rows from `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, grouped by a normalized status such as `succeeded`, `failed`, or `pending`. Designed for use inside `IShoppingMallPaymentsOverview.byStatus`.

status.description: Normalized payment status bucket for this aggregation entry. Common values might include `succeeded`, `failed`, and `pending`, but the concrete set is determined by business rules mapped from raw transaction states.

transactionCount.description: Number of payment transactions whose latest status maps into this status bucket for the analysis period.

totalAmount.description: Total monetary volume associated with transactions in this status bucket over the analysis period. For `succeeded`, this often reflects captured amounts; for other statuses it may be authorization amounts or attempted amounts, depending on implementation.

IShoppingMallPaymentsOverviewByMethod.description:
Aggregated payment metrics for a single payment method within the analysis window.

Used to show how different payment methods contribute to overall volume, success rates, failure counts, and refund volume on an admin dashboard. Derived from `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` and related tables grouped by configured payment method identifiers.

methodCode.description:
Internal payment method code used by the platform configuration, such as `card`, `bank_transfer`, or a gateway-specific identifier.

This code references configuration in tables like `shopping_mall_payment_methods` but is not itself a foreign key here; it is shipped as a denormalized key to allow frontends and reporting tools to join or map to additional metadata if needed.

methodLabel.description:
Human-readable label for the payment method suitable for display on an admin dashboard chart or legend, such as `Credit Card` or `Bank Transfer`.

The label is generally derived from the corresponding record in `shopping_mall_payment_methods` and is expected to be stable for the life of the dashboard snapshot so that time-series comparisons remain meaningful.

transactionCount.description:
Total number of payment transactions processed with this payment method during the analysis window.

This count typically includes all terminal outcomes (such as successful, failed, or cancelled transactions) that belong to the selected filter set for the overview query.

totalAmount.description:
Total processed payment volume for this method over the analysis window, typically based on captured amounts from successful payment transactions.

The value is expressed in the platform's base currency (for example, KRW or another configured settlement currency) and is already aggregated for the selected filters and time range.

successRate.description:
Proportion of this method's transactions that completed successfully in the analysis window.

The value is expressed as a fraction between 0 and 1 (inclusive) and is commonly computed as `successfulTransactionCount / transactionCount` when `transactionCount > 0`. Implementations may define the value as `0` when `transactionCount` is zero to avoid division by zero while preserving a consistent numeric type for clients.

failedTransactionCount.description:
Number of payment transactions using this method that reached a terminal failed state during the analysis window.

This count is useful for monitoring reliability of a specific payment method, identifying gateway or acquirer issues, and comparing failure rates across methods in the admin dashboard.

refundAmount.description:
Total amount refunded for transactions originally processed with this payment method during the analysis window.

The value is expressed in the same platform base currency as `totalAmount` and aggregates monetary values from refund-related records (for example, rows in `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`) that are associated with this payment method and fall within the selected filters.

IShoppingMallPaymentsOverviewByDay.description:
Daily aggregated payment metrics for trend visualization in dashboards.

Each instance represents a single calendar day within the analysis window and aggregates payment and refund metrics for that day. Intended for use in `IShoppingMallPaymentsOverview.byDay` to draw time-series charts and to support drill-down into per-day payment performance.

date.description:
Calendar date in ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD` format representing the day for which the aggregated metrics are calculated.

The date is always expressed in the platform's configured reporting timezone so that daily buckets align with business reporting expectations rather than raw UTC boundaries.

totalProcessedAmount.description:
Total processed payment volume for this date, based on successful transactions captured on that day.

The value is expressed in the platform's base currency (for example, KRW or another configured settlement currency) and is aggregated from captured payment transaction records that match the analytics filters and fall on the given calendar date.

successfulTransactionCount.description:
Number of successful payment transactions on this date.

This count generally includes all transactions that reached a terminal success state (such as `SUCCEEDED` or equivalent) according to the business rules in the payments subsystem.

failedTransactionCount.description:
Number of failed payment transactions on this date.

This metric captures transactions that reached a terminal failed state (for example, authorization failure, capture failure, or gateway error) and is useful for identifying reliability issues or incident windows in the payment infrastructure.

refundAmount.description:
Total amount refunded on this date as recorded in `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` and related tables.

The value is expressed in the same platform base currency as `totalProcessedAmount` and aggregates refund transactions whose effective refund date falls on this calendar day under the reporting timezone configuration.

IShoppingMallPayoutsOverview.description:
Aggregated payouts overview metrics for the shoppingMall platform.

Provides high-level financial KPIs derived from seller payout–related Prisma tables such as `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`, `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`, and optionally contextual data from `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries`. This DTO is intended for use in platform admin dashboards and does not expose individual payout records or per-seller personally identifiable information.

totalPayoutAmount.description: Total amount of funds paid out or scheduled to be paid out to sellers within the analysis window. Typically computed as the sum of completed payout batch amounts in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` for the selected period.

completedPayoutCount.description: Number of payout batches that have reached a completed or paid status within the analysis window.

pendingPayoutCount.description: Number of payout batches that are currently pending or scheduled but not yet completed within the analysis window.

failedPayoutCount.description: Number of payout attempts or batches that have failed or been rejected in the analysis window, based on payout status fields in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`.

averagePayoutPerSeller.description: Average payout amount per seller over the analysis window. Implementations commonly compute this as `totalPayoutAmount / distinct_seller_count` for sellers that received at least one payout during the window.

byStatus.description: Breakdown of payout batches by high-level status category (for example, completed, pending, failed) within the analysis window.

byPeriod.description: Time-series aggregation of payouts over recent periods (for example, per day or per week) to support trend charts in admin dashboards.

bySellerSegment.description: Optional breakdown of payout metrics by logical seller segment or tier (for example, `top_sellers`, `new_sellers`), potentially derived from `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries`. Useful for understanding how performance categories relate to payout volume.

IShoppingMallPayoutsOverviewByStatus.description:
Aggregated payout metrics for a single high-level payout status within the analysis window.

Designed for use in `IShoppingMallPayoutsOverview.byStatus` on admin dashboards, summarizing how many payout batches fall into each status and what total amounts they represent.

status.description: Normalized payout status bucket for this aggregation entry, such as `completed`, `pending`, or `failed`. Concrete values are determined by mapping platform-specific payout status codes into these categories.

payoutCount.description: Number of payout batches whose status maps into this normalized status bucket during the analysis window.

totalAmount.description: Total monetary volume of payouts included in this status bucket for the analysis window.

IShoppingMallPayoutsOverviewByPeriod.description:
Aggregated payout metrics for a specific time period within the analysis window.

The period granularity (day, week, month) is determined by the server-side configuration for the payouts overview endpoint. Each instance represents trend data for one period and is intended for use in `IShoppingMallPayoutsOverview.byPeriod`.

periodStart.description: Start timestamp of the aggregation period in ISO 8601 date-time format. Represents the beginning of the time bucket for which these payout metrics are computed.

periodEnd.description: End timestamp of the aggregation period in ISO 8601 date-time format. Represents the end of the time bucket for which these payout metrics are computed.

totalPayoutAmount.description: Total amount of payouts completed within this period.

payoutCount.description: Number of payout batches that were completed in this period.

IShoppingMallPayoutsOverviewBySellerSegm.description:
Aggregated payout metrics for a logical seller segment or tier.

Segments are typically derived from `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries` or related configuration and might categorize sellers by performance, risk, or lifecycle stage. This type is used within `IShoppingMallPayoutsOverview.bySellerSegment`.

segmentCode.description: Internal code for the seller segment, such as `top_sellers`, `new_sellers`, or `at_risk`. Exact codes are defined by business configuration for seller performance segmentation.

segmentLabel.description: Human-readable label for this seller segment, suitable for display in dashboards and reports.

sellerCount.description: Number of distinct sellers included in this segment that have payout activity within the analysis window.

totalPayoutAmount.description: Total payout volume attributed to sellers in this segment over the analysis window.

IShoppingMallInventoryItem.description:
Full response DTO representing an inventory item record from the shopping_mall_inventory_items table.

An inventory item models per-SKU inventory state for a specific sellable variant within the shoppingMall platform. It links to a product SKU and tracks core quantities such as current on-hand stock and reserved units, along with safety thresholds and configuration flags controlling backorder and preorder behavior.

This DTO is returned from inventory creation, update, and retrieval operations and serves as the authoritative snapshot of stock state for administrative dashboards, seller tools, and integrations. It is structurally aligned with the underlying Prisma model, including foreign key and configuration field names, so that code generation and maintenance remain straightforward.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the inventory item record in the shopping_mall_inventory_items table.

This value is generated by the system when the inventory item is created and is used as the primary key for updates, retrievals, and deletions.

product_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the product SKU in the shopping_mall_product_skus table to which this inventory item belongs.

This foreign key corresponds directly to the product_sku_id column in the Prisma model and uniquely associates this inventory record with a specific sellable variant. The referenced SKU is managed by catalog-related APIs.

on_hand_quantity.description:
Current on-hand stock quantity for this SKU as tracked by the inventory system.

This represents the number of units physically available in storage and not yet consumed by completed or reserved transactions. It is updated by inventory movements, adjustments, and synchronization processes.

reserved_quantity.description:
Current quantity of this SKU that is reserved for pending orders or other reservations.

Reserved units are not available for new allocations until associated orders are completed, cancelled, or the reservations are explicitly released. This field reflects the aggregate of active reservations in shopping_mall_inventory_reservations and related flows.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Configured low-stock threshold for this inventory item, or null when no explicit per-SKU threshold has been configured.

When a non-null value is set, and when on_hand_quantity minus reserved_quantity falls at or below this threshold, the platform may trigger low-stock alerts, change stock status, or adjust catalog visibility depending on configuration and business rules. When null, the SKU relies on global or category-level defaults, or is treated as having no explicit low-stock limit.

stock_status.description:
Current stock status flag for this inventory item such as in_stock, low_stock, out_of_stock, backorder_allowed, or preorder_only.

The exact value is derived and maintained according to business logic using on-hand, reserved quantities, thresholds, and policy settings. Clients can use this field to drive UI labels, disable purchase actions, or filter inventory lists without reimplementing stock classification rules.

backorder_enabled.description:
Indicates whether backorders are allowed for this inventory item given its configuration and applicable policies.

When true, the platform may accept orders that exceed current available stock, subject to limits and settings defined in shopping_mall_backorder_settings or global policies. When false, the system prevents overselling beyond available units.

preorder_enabled.description:
Indicates whether this inventory item currently participates in preorder flows before normal stock becomes available.

When true, customers may place orders ahead of availability as configured in shopping_mall_preorder_settings and related entities. When false, the SKU follows standard in-stock behavior and cannot be preordered.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory item record was created in the system.

This value reflects the moment the row was first inserted into shopping_mall_inventory_items and is useful for auditing, synchronization, and operational reporting.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory item record was last updated.

Any change to mutable inventory fields, such as quantities or configuration flags, results in this value being refreshed. It allows clients and batch jobs to detect recent modifications without re-reading all records.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory item record was soft-deleted, or null when the record is active.

Soft deletion preserves historical inventory state for reporting and reconciliation while excluding deleted records from normal operational queries. Consumers should treat non-null values as logically deleted items that are no longer used for active stock management.

IShoppingMallInventoryItem.IRequest.description:
