Search and filter request DTO for inventory items in the shoppingMall platform.

This type encapsulates the criteria used by the `/shoppingMall/inventoryItems` PATCH endpoint to filter and paginate results from the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` table. It allows callers to constrain results by SKU identifier, stock status, and quantity ranges, while also controlling page size, page index, and sort ordering.

Consumers use this DTO when building backoffice search forms, seller inventory consoles, or automated monitoring jobs that need to scan subsets of inventory records based on operational thresholds or status flags.

page.description:
Zero-based page index for pagination when listing inventory items.

This value controls which page of results should be returned by the inventory search operation. A value of 0 typically represents the first page, and higher values request subsequent pages.

If omitted, the implementation may default to the first page according to platform conventions.

limit.description:
Maximum number of inventory item records to return in a single page.

This parameter allows clients to control page size for the `/shoppingMall/inventoryItems` search endpoint. It should be a positive integer and may be capped by server-side limits to protect performance.

When not provided, the service may apply a default limit consistent with platform-wide pagination standards.

product_sku_id.description:
Optional filter for inventory records belonging to a specific SKU.

When provided, this field restricts results to inventory items whose `product_sku_id` matches the given UUID, corresponding to a single `shopping_mall_product_skus.id` value. A null value indicates that no SKU-specific filter is applied.

This filter is typically used when an operator wants to inspect the inventory state for a single SKU while still leveraging paginated and sorted views.

stock_status.description:
Optional filter for inventory items matching a specific stock status flag.

This field can be set to values such as `in_stock`, `low_stock`, `out_of_stock`, `backorder_allowed`, or `preorder_only`, depending on the statuses supported by the business logic and stored in the `stock_status` column. When null, the search does not restrict results by status.

It is commonly used by dashboards and monitoring tools to quickly retrieve items in particular operational states, such as all low stock or out-of-stock SKUs.

min_on_hand_quantity.description:
Minimum on-hand quantity threshold for filtering inventory items.

When set, only records whose `on_hand_quantity` is greater than or equal to this value will be included in the search results. A null value indicates that there is no lower bound filter on on-hand quantity.

This is useful for identifying SKUs that have sufficient stock or for excluding items that are nearly or completely depleted.

max_on_hand_quantity.description:
Maximum on-hand quantity threshold for filtering inventory items.

If provided, the search will restrict results to inventory items whose `on_hand_quantity` is less than or equal to this value. A null value means no upper bound is applied.

Operational users can use this filter to find SKUs with low or moderate stock levels that may require attention or replenishment.

min_reserved_quantity.description:
Minimum reserved quantity threshold for filtering inventory items.

When specified, the search returns only records whose `reserved_quantity` is greater than or equal to the provided value. Null indicates that the filter should not constrain by a minimum reserved quantity.

This parameter is often used to identify SKUs with high levels of pending reservations that might impact fulfillment capacity or risk overselling.

max_reserved_quantity.description:
Maximum reserved quantity threshold for filtering inventory items.

If set, only inventory records whose `reserved_quantity` is less than or equal to this value are returned. A null value means that there is no upper bound filter applied to reserved quantities.

Monitoring tools can use this filter to focus on SKUs with moderate reservation levels or to exclude heavily reserved items from certain views.

order_by.description:
Sort key used to order inventory search results.

This string indicates which column or logical field should be used for ordering, such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, `on_hand_quantity`, or `stock_status`. The exact set of supported values is defined by the implementation of the `/shoppingMall/inventoryItems` search endpoint.

When null, a default sort order is applied, typically by recency or an operationally relevant field.

order_direction.description:
Direction of the sort order applied to inventory search results.

Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending, indicating how the field specified in `order_by` should be ordered. A null value allows the service to fall back to a default direction associated with the chosen sort key.

Clients can use this parameter in combination with `order_by` to implement flexible sorting options in inventory list views.

IShoppingMallInventoryItem.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new inventory item record in the shopping_mall_inventory_items table.

This DTO is used by authorized sellers or platform administrators to initialize per-SKU inventory state when onboarding a new sellable variant. It captures the target SKU identifier, the initial on-hand quantity, and configuration flags that control whether the SKU can participate in backorder or preorder flows.

Actor identity such as seller linkage is derived from the authenticated context (JWT/session) and MUST NOT be provided by clients in this schema. System-managed fields such as identifiers, reserved quantities, stock status, and timestamps are excluded and maintained exclusively by the backend.

product_sku_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product SKU in the shopping_mall_product_skus table for which this inventory item is being created.

The referenced SKU must already exist and belong to the authenticated seller or otherwise be manageable by the current actor. The platform typically enforces uniqueness of inventory items per SKU using this foreign key.

on_hand_quantity.description:
Initial on-hand stock quantity for the SKU when the inventory item is first created.

This value represents the number of units physically available in storage at the time of creation. It must be a non-negative integer, and additional business rules or validation logic may further constrain maximum values based on platform configuration or seller policies.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Optional threshold at or below which this SKU should be considered low stock for alerts and catalog signals.

When provided, this value is stored in the low_stock_threshold column of the shopping_mall_inventory_items table and must be a non-negative integer. When omitted, the platform may apply a default threshold or treat the SKU as having no explicit low-stock limit.

backorder_enabled.description:
Indicates whether backorders are allowed for this SKU based on current configuration and policies.

When true, the platform may continue to accept orders even when effective available stock reaches zero, subject to additional constraints defined in shopping_mall_backorder_settings and related policy entities. When false, the system will prevent overselling beyond available stock.

preorder_enabled.description:
Indicates whether this SKU is currently available for preorder before normal stock is available.

When true, customers may place orders in advance based on expected future availability, subject to configuration in shopping_mall_preorder_settings and applicable regional or policy constraints. When false, the SKU follows regular in-stock behavior only.

IShoppingMallInventoryItem.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing inventory item record in the shopping_mall_inventory_items table.

This DTO allows authorized sellers or platform administrators to adjust mutable aspects of per-SKU inventory state such as current on-hand quantity, low-stock threshold, or configuration flags that govern whether the SKU can participate in backorder or preorder flows.

Only business-manageable fields are exposed; identifiers, foreign keys, reserved quantity snapshots, stock status flags, and system-managed timestamps are excluded to preserve data integrity and prevent client-side manipulation of internal state.

on_hand_quantity.description:
Updated on-hand stock quantity for the inventory item.

Must be a non-negative integer. This field is typically used for manual corrections or synchronization with external inventory systems. When omitted from the request, the existing on-hand quantity is preserved.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Updated low-stock threshold for this inventory item.

Must be a non-negative integer. Adjusting this value affects how close to depletion the platform is willing to operate before triggering alerts or constraining purchasing behavior. When omitted, the existing threshold value is preserved.

backorder_enabled.description:
Updated configuration flag indicating whether backorders should be allowed for this inventory item.

When provided, this value overrides the current setting stored in the backorder_enabled column. The platform validates that enabling or disabling backorders remains consistent with shopping_mall_backorder_settings and other policy entities.

preorder_enabled.description:
Updated configuration flag indicating whether preorders should be allowed for this inventory item.

When provided, this value overrides the current setting stored in the preorder_enabled column. The platform validates that enabling or disabling preorders remains consistent with shopping_mall_preorder_settings and other policy entities.

IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.IReque.description:
Search and filtering criteria for inventory reservations associated with a specific inventory item in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is used as the request body for the PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}/reservations endpoint. It enables platform administrators and internal tools to query rows in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table with complex, structured filters instead of relying on query string parameters.

All filter fields are optional. Callers may provide any combination of criteria such as reservation status, creation date range, expiration date range, or related order identifiers, together with pagination and sorting options. When pagination fields are omitted, service-level defaults (for example, page 1 with a configured default page size) are applied by the implementation.

page.description:
Page index for paginated results.

The value must be a positive integer starting from 1. When omitted, the service applies its own default page index (typically 1). This value is used together with `pageSize` to determine which slice of reservation summaries is returned.

pageSize.description:
Number of records to return per page.

Controls the maximum number of inventory reservation summaries returned in a single page. When omitted, the service applies a configured default page size. Implementations should also enforce a reasonable upper bound (for example, 100 or 200) to prevent excessively large result sets.

status.description:
Filter by reservation status.

Represents the logical state of the reservation, such as `active`, `released`, `expired`, `pending`, or `cancelled`, as defined for the `reservation_state` column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations model. Implementations should validate the provided value against the actual status set used in the domain and ignore or reject unknown values according to business rules.

orderId.description:
Optional filter by related order identifier.

When provided, restricts results to reservations whose `order_id` matches the specified UUID from the shopping_mall_orders table. This is useful when investigating reservations tied to a particular customer order.

orderLineId.description:
Optional filter by related order line identifier.

When provided, limits the result set to reservations linked to a single order line in `shopping_mall_order_lines`. This enables fine-grained inspection of how a specific line item consumes inventory.

createdFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the reservation creation timestamp filter.

Reservations whose `created_at` value is on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp are eligible to appear in the result set. When omitted, no lower bound is applied to the creation time dimension.

createdTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the reservation creation timestamp filter.

Reservations whose `created_at` value is on or before this ISO 8601 timestamp are eligible to appear in the result set. When omitted, no upper bound is applied to the creation time dimension.

expiresFrom.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for reservation expiration timestamp filtering.

Reservations whose `expires_at` value is on or after this ISO 8601 timestamp are eligible to appear in the result set. When omitted, no lower bound is applied to the expiration time dimension.

expiresTo.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for reservation expiration timestamp filtering.

Reservations whose `expires_at` value is on or before this ISO 8601 timestamp are eligible to appear in the result set. When omitted, no upper bound is applied to the expiration time dimension.

sortBy.description:
Field name to use for sorting the reservation results.

Typical and recommended values include column names or logical sort keys such as `created_at`, `expires_at`, or `reservation_state`. The service layer is responsible for validating the supplied value against an allowed set of sortable fields to prevent arbitrary column access or unsafe ordering expressions.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for the ordered result set.

When set to `asc`, reservations are sorted in ascending order (for example, oldest to newest when sorting by `created_at`).

Sort direction for the ordered result set.

When set to `desc`, reservations are sorted in descending order (for example, newest to oldest when sorting by `created_at`).

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for the ordered result set.

Must be either `asc` or `desc`. When omitted, the service applies a default direction that is typically descending for time-based fields such as `created_at` or `expires_at`.

IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.description:
Detailed representation of an inventory reservation for a specific inventory item within the shopping mall platform.

This DTO mirrors a row in the `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` Prisma model and is used as the response body for operations that inspect or manage reservations, such as GET /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}/reservations/{reservationId} and POST/PUT reservation endpoints.

Each reservation represents a temporary hold of a quantity of stock for a SKU-level inventory item, typically associated with carts, checkouts, or pending orders. The reservation ensures that the reserved quantity is not double-sold while the associated business flow is in progress. Depending on configuration, a reservation may carry a fixed expiration timestamp or rely on rule-based expiration logic, in which case the `expires_at` field can be null.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the inventory reservation.

Corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` record and is used to locate, update, or delete the reservation across all related operations.

inventory_item_id.description:
Identifier of the inventory item (`shopping_mall_inventory_items`) to which this reservation belongs.

This value scopes the reservation to a specific SKU-level inventory record and is used together with the parent path parameter `inventoryItemId` to validate that the reservation is nested under the correct inventory item in resource-oriented APIs.

inventory_item.description:
Summary information for the inventory item that this reservation holds quantity against.

Provides essential context such as product and SKU identifiers and human-readable labels so that administrators can understand which catalog item is affected without issuing additional inventory item queries.

order_id.description:
Identifier of the order associated with this reservation.

This value references `shopping_mall_orders.id` and indicates which customer order ultimately owns the reserved quantity. For reservations created before an order record exists, the platform may use draft orders or other upstream entities to populate this field once the master order is confirmed.

order.description:
Summary information about the order that owns this reservation.

Exposes key order fields such as order number, lifecycle status, and relevant timestamps, enabling administrators and internal tools to understand the business context of the reservation without issuing a separate order lookup.

order_line_id.description:
Identifier of the order line associated with this reservation.

This value references `shopping_mall_order_lines.id` and ties the reserved quantity to a specific SKU and quantity within the order. It supports precise reconciliation and after-sales workflows at the line-item level.

order_line.description:
Summary information about the specific order line that consumes this reservation.

Allows tooling and dashboards to show which product, SKU, and quantity within the order are linked to the reservation while keeping the payload compact and avoiding deep object graphs in list views.

reserved_quantity.description:
Quantity of inventory units reserved for this reservation.

The value is a positive integer representing how many units of the associated inventory item are temporarily held. Service logic must ensure that the sum of active reservations plus any immediately consumable quantities does not exceed the available stock recorded in `shopping_mall_inventory_items`.

reservation_state.description:
Current logical state of the reservation.

This field maps directly to the `reservation_state` column in the `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` table and typically takes values such as `pending`, `active`, `consumed`, `expired`, or `cancelled` depending on the reservation lifecycle configuration in the domain. Implementations use this value to decide whether the reserved quantity should be considered blocking for new allocations.

oneOf.description:
Date and time at which this reservation is scheduled to expire, expressed as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.

When present, this timestamp indicates the point after which the reservation may be automatically released if payment, checkout, or subsequent order processing has not completed successfully.

Null value indicating that this reservation does not have a fixed expiration timestamp.

In this case, expiration is governed by other business rules or background processes, such as session timeouts, manual administrative actions, or workflow-specific deadlines.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp at which this reservation is scheduled to expire, or null when no fixed expiry is configured.

The underlying Prisma column `expires_at` is nullable. When non-null, it stores the ISO 8601 date-time at which the platform may automatically release or re-evaluate the reservation if the associated business flow has not progressed. When null, the reservation follows rule-based or manual expiration behavior.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this reservation record was created in the system.

Represents the moment the inventory units were first reserved. Stored as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, and used for audits, reporting, and time-based search filters.

consumed_at.description:
Timestamp when this reservation was consumed into a paid or otherwise finalized order.

A non-null value indicates that the reserved quantity has been converted into a committed order and corresponding inventory movements. Null means the reservation has not yet been consumed and is either pending, active, expired, or cancelled.

cancelled_at.description:
Timestamp when this reservation was cancelled without being consumed.

When non-null, the reservation should be treated as inactive, and its quantity considered released back into available inventory. Null indicates that the reservation is still active, pending consumption, or has been consumed rather than cancelled.

IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.ICreat.description:
Create DTO for inventory reservations in the shopping mall platform.

This schema is used when a trusted platform actor or internal workflow creates a new temporary reservation of stock for a specific inventory item. It maps directly to the `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` Prisma model but includes only fields that must be supplied by the caller, while identifiers and system timestamps are managed by the backend.

Reservations created through this DTO are typically associated with carts, checkouts, or order flows, and are later either consumed, expired, or cancelled according to business rules.

inventory_item_id.description:
Identifier of the inventory item whose stock is being reserved.

This value must reference an existing `shopping_mall_inventory_items.id` row and links the reservation to the underlying SKU-level inventory record. In the API surface, it is normally supplied by the `inventoryItemId` path parameter and echoed into this field at the service layer so that the reservation row has a strong foreign-key association to the correct inventory item.

order_id.description:
Identifier of the customer order for which this reservation is being created.

This should reference an existing row in `shopping_mall_orders.id`. It allows the system to track which order owns the reserved quantity and to later consume or release the reservation when the order is finalized or cancelled.

order_line_id.description:
Identifier of the specific order line that consumes this reservation.

This must reference an existing record in `shopping_mall_order_lines.id`. It ties the reserved quantity to a particular SKU and quantity within the order, enabling accurate reconciliation between ordered items and inventory reservations.

reserved_quantity.description:
Number of units being reserved for the associated order line.

This value must be a positive integer greater than zero. Service logic will validate that the requested quantity does not exceed the available capacity of the related `shopping_mall_inventory_items` record once existing active reservations are taken into account.

reservation_state.description:
Initial state of the reservation at the time of creation.

Typical values include business-level states such as `pending`, `active`, or other configured reservation lifecycle markers. The specific allowed values are governed by business logic and validations at the service layer rather than by this schema.

expires_at.description:
Optional expiration timestamp for this reservation.

When provided, this is the date and time after which the reservation may be treated as expired if payment or checkout is not completed. A null value indicates that expiration is managed by other business rules or background jobs rather than a fixed timestamp.

consumed_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when this reservation is already considered consumed at creation time.

In normal customer flows this field is left null and is later set by order-completion logic when the reserved quantity is converted into a committed, paid order. For administrative or data-migration scenarios, it may be populated at creation to reflect an already-consumed reservation state that needs to be reconstructed historically.

cancelled_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when this reservation was cancelled without being consumed.

Under standard flows this value is null at creation and is later set by cancellation logic when the reserved quantity is released back into available inventory. Administrative tools or migration scripts may populate it at creation time when reconstructing reservations that are already known to be cancelled.

IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.IUpdat.description:
Update DTO for inventory reservations in the shopping mall platform.

This schema is used to modify mutable aspects of an existing reservation record in `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations`. It is typically called by backend order management or fulfillment services when adjusting quantities, changing lifecycle state, or updating expiration behavior after the initial creation.

Only business fields that are expected to change over time are included here. Identifier fields and creation timestamps remain immutable and are not exposed for modification through this DTO.

order_id.description:
Updated identifier of the order associated with this reservation.

This field mirrors the `order_id` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` and, when provided, should reference an existing `shopping_mall_orders.id` value. In normal flows the owning order is fixed once the reservation is created, but backoffice tooling may use this field to correct or attach reservations to the appropriate order in exceptional situations.

order_line_id.description:
Updated identifier of the specific order line that consumes this reservation.

This field mirrors the `order_line_id` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` and must reference an existing `shopping_mall_order_lines.id` row when supplied. Operationally, it enables controlled corrections where a reservation was mistakenly linked to the wrong line or needs to be associated with a newly created line in the same order.

reserved_quantity.description:
Updated reserved unit count for the associated order line.

When present, this value must be a positive integer. Service logic validates that increasing the quantity does not cause the sum of active reservations to exceed the available capacity of the corresponding `shopping_mall_inventory_items` record.

reservation_state.description:
New lifecycle state for the reservation.

Typical examples include transitions such as moving from `pending` to `active`, marking as `consumed` when tied to a paid order, or setting to `cancelled` when the reservation is released. Exact allowed values and transitions are enforced by domain rules rather than this schema.

expires_at.description:
Updated expiration timestamp for this reservation, or null to clear it.

Providing a timestamp adjusts when the reservation is considered eligible for automatic expiration if payment is not completed. Setting this field to null indicates that the reservation will follow other business rules or background processes for expiration handling.

consumed_at.description:
Timestamp marking when this reservation has been consumed into a paid or otherwise finalized order.

Service logic should set this field when the reserved quantity is converted into a committed sale, and clients may update it through this DTO in administrative or corrective flows. A null value indicates that the reservation has not yet been consumed.

cancelled_at.description:
Timestamp marking when this reservation was cancelled without being consumed.

When set, this field indicates that the reservation is no longer active and that its quantity should be treated as released back into available inventory. A null value means that the reservation is still active or has been consumed instead of cancelled.

IShoppingMallInventoryMovement.IRequest.description:
Search, filtering, and pagination criteria for querying inventory movements associated with a specific inventory item.

Used by the PATCH /shoppingMall/inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}/movements endpoint to retrieve a paginated, filterable list of inventory movement records scoped to a single inventory item. All foreign key based filters use IDs only, keeping this DTO as a pure search filter without nested relation objects.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

The first page is typically 1. When omitted, backend implementations may apply a sensible default such as 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page.

Controls the page size for inventory movement search results. When not provided, the service may enforce a default and/or upper bound to protect performance.

fromDate.description:
Optional lower bound of the movement timestamp range filter.

Only movements whose `created_at` value is greater than or equal to this timestamp will be included in the result set.

toDate.description:
Optional upper bound of the movement timestamp range filter.

Only movements whose `created_at` value is less than or equal to this timestamp will be included in the result set.

movementTypes.description:
Optional set of movement type codes to include in the result.

When provided, only movements whose `movement_type` is one of the specified values will be returned. This allows callers to, for example, focus on reservation-related movements or manual adjustments.

oneOf.description: Filter to include only movements that increased stock quantities.
Filter to include only movements that decreased stock quantities.

direction.description:
Optional direction filter used to distinguish between inventory increases and decreases.

This filter is interpreted based on the sign of `quantity_delta` and possibly `reserved_delta` in the underlying records.

order_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to movements associated with a specific order.

When provided, only movements whose `order_id` matches this value will be returned.

order_line_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to movements associated with a specific order line.

When set, only movements referencing this `order_line_id` will be returned, enabling fine-grained diagnostics per order line.

reservation_id.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to movements associated with a specific inventory reservation.

When present, only movements whose `reservation_id` matches this value will be included in the response.

oneOf.description: Sort by the movement creation timestamp, typically newest first.
Sort by movement type code for grouping similar movement categories together.

sortBy.description:
Field name used for sorting results.

If omitted, implementations typically default to sorting by `created_at` in descending order to show the most recent movements first.

oneOf.description: Ascending sort order.
Descending sort order.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction for the result set.

Combined with `sortBy`, this controls whether records are returned in ascending or descending order for the chosen field.

IShoppingMallInventoryMovement.description:
Detailed inventory movement record associated with a specific inventory item in the shopping mall backend.

This DTO represents a single atomic change in inventory state for a SKU/location combination modeled by `shopping_mall_inventory_items`. It reflects the persisted row in the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` table, including the movement deltas and resulting quantity snapshots, along with optional foreign key references to related commercial entities such as orders or reservations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the inventory movement record.

This is the primary key of the underlying row in the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` table and is used to uniquely reference this movement in detail APIs and audit tooling.

inventory_item_id.description:
Identifier of the parent inventory item whose quantities were changed by this movement.

This is a hierarchical parent foreign key referencing `shopping_mall_inventory_items.id`. It is kept as a raw ID in this DTO to avoid circular references, because inventory item detail views may contain arrays of movement records.

movement_type.description:
Category of the inventory movement.

Typical values include `restock`, `manual_adjustment`, `sale_capture`, `cancellation_release`, `return_restock`, or other domain-specific movement codes.

The exact allowed values are governed by business rules and correspond to the `movement_type` column on the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` model.

quantity_delta.description:
Signed change applied to on-hand stock for the inventory item.

Positive values increase on-hand quantity (for example, restock or return-to-stock events), while negative values decrease on-hand quantity (for example, sales capture or damage write-offs).

This value is persisted in the `quantity_delta` column of `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` and is the result of applying high-level intent such as direction and quantity.

reserved_delta.description:
Signed change applied to reserved quantity for the inventory item.

Positive values increase reserved quantity (for example, when orders reserve stock) and negative values decrease reserved quantity (for example, on cancellation or reservation release).

The value corresponds to the `reserved_delta` column in the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` model and is used together with `quantity_delta` to maintain the integrity of inventory reservations.

resulting_on_hand_quantity.description:
On-hand quantity for the inventory item immediately after this movement was applied.

This snapshot is stored in `resulting_on_hand_quantity` and allows auditors, reports, and reconciliation processes to understand the exact stock level after this specific movement without replaying the entire movement history.

resulting_reserved_quantity.description:
Reserved quantity for the inventory item immediately after this movement was applied.

The value is persisted in `resulting_reserved_quantity` and represents the total units currently reserved for open orders after this movement has been processed.

resulting_available_to_sell_quantity.description:
Available-to-sell quantity for the inventory item immediately after this movement was applied.

This corresponds to the `resulting_available_to_sell_quantity` column and is typically computed from on-hand and reserved quantities according to business rules. It represents how many units are immediately sellable after accounting for reservations and backorder settings.

order_id.description:
Optional order identifier related to this inventory movement.

When present, this foreign key points to `shopping_mall_orders.id` and indicates that the movement was triggered by order lifecycle events such as placement, cancellation, or refund processing.

Consumers can use this ID to correlate stock changes with specific customer orders via order APIs.

order_line_id.description:
Optional order line identifier related to this inventory movement.

When populated, this foreign key references `shopping_mall_order_lines.id` and provides more granular linkage between quantity changes and specific line items in an order.

This is particularly useful for diagnostics that need to reason about which SKU or line triggered a stock movement.

reservation_id.description:
Optional reservation identifier related to this movement.

When set, this foreign key references `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations.id` and indicates that the movement is associated with a reservation being created, consumed, or released.

Reservation-related movements usually modify `reserved_delta` and may also adjust available-to-sell quantities.

reason.description:
Optional human-readable reason or note explaining why this inventory movement occurred.

This free-form text is populated by operational actors or automated processes and is intended for internal audit trails and back-office tools. It can reference business events such as "cycle count adjustment", "damage during handling", or "manual correction".

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this movement record was created and applied to the inventory state.

This value maps to the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` and is typically recorded in UTC. It is used for chronological sorting and historical analysis of stock changes.

IShoppingMallInventoryMovement.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new inventory movement (stock change event) for a specific inventory item in `shopping_mall_inventory_movements`.

This payload is used by authenticated sellers or internal operators to register increases or decreases in on-hand and/or reserved quantity for an inventory item identified by the `inventoryItemId` path parameter. The service derives the signed `quantity_delta` and `reserved_delta` fields, as well as resulting quantity snapshots, from the business intent expressed in this DTO and the current state of the parent `shopping_mall_inventory_items` row.

Only business-input fields are exposed here. Identity fields such as `id`, `inventory_item_id`, and system-maintained snapshot fields like `resulting_on_hand_quantity` are not part of the request and are populated by the backend. Optional foreign key references allow the movement to be traced back to orders, order lines, or reservations using the corresponding Prisma columns.

direction.description:
Direction of the inventory movement relative to on-hand quantity.

Typical values include business-defined enums such as `increase` or `decrease` to indicate whether stock is being added to or removed from the inventory item. The backend uses this direction together with the provided `quantity` to compute the signed `quantity_delta` that is stored in the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements.quantity_delta` column and to update the aggregate quantities on the parent `shopping_mall_inventory_items` record.

quantity.description:
Number of units affected by this inventory movement.

Must be a positive integer. When combined with the `direction` field, this quantity determines how on-hand and available-to-sell quantities change for the associated inventory item. The backend converts this into a signed `quantity_delta` value in the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` table and enforces business rules such as preventing invalid negative stock when backorders are disabled.

movementType.description:
Classification of the stock change event.

Represents the functional reason for the movement, such as `initial_stock`, `manual_adjustment`, `damage_writeoff`, `inbound_receipt`, or other configured codes. These values are persisted in the `movement_type` column of the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` model and are used for reporting, audit, and policy enforcement.

reason.description:
Optional human-readable explanation or note describing why this inventory movement was recorded.

This free-form text is mapped to the nullable `reason` column of the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` table. It is typically used by backoffice operators and auditors to understand the context of manual adjustments or exceptional events, and is not intended for shopper-facing UIs.

order_id.description:
Optional identifier of an order associated with this inventory movement.

When provided, this value is written to the nullable `order_id` foreign key column of the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` table and should correspond to `shopping_mall_orders.id`. It allows reporting and audit tools to correlate stock changes with specific customer orders.

order_line_id.description:
Optional identifier of a specific order line associated with this inventory movement.

When set, this value is stored in the nullable `order_line_id` foreign key column and should reference `shopping_mall_order_lines.id`. It provides more granular context for diagnostics that need to understand which line item caused the movement.

reservation_id.description:
Optional identifier of an inventory reservation related to this movement.

If present, this value is stored in the nullable `reservation_id` foreign key column of `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` and should reference `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations.id`. It is typically used when movements are triggered by reservation creation, consumption, or release.

IShoppingMallBackorderSetting.description:
Full representation of per-inventory-item backorder configuration stored in shopping_mall_backorder_settings.

Backorder settings define how the platform handles orders that exceed current on-hand stock for a specific inventory item, including whether backorders are allowed at all, the maximum allowed quantity, and any customer-facing messaging to explain extended fulfillment timelines. Each record is uniquely associated with a single inventory item in shopping_mall_inventory_items via a non-null, unique inventory_item_id.

This DTO is returned to admin and seller tooling after creation or update operations so that UIs and integration consumers can display the authoritative configuration, including identifiers and lifecycle timestamps.

In response contexts, the association to the parent inventory item is exposed as an inventory item summary object instead of a raw foreign key, enabling consumers to render basic inventory context without additional API calls.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this backorder settings record in shopping_mall_backorder_settings.

Generated by the system when the settings record is created and immutable for the lifetime of the record.

inventoryItem.description:
Summary representation of the inventory item in shopping_mall_inventory_items that these backorder settings apply to.

This replaces the raw foreign key inventory_item_id in response DTOs and provides enough context for administrative and seller UIs to render which SKU and location the backorder configuration belongs to without issuing additional inventory item lookups.

allow_backorder.description:
Flag indicating whether this inventory item may accept customer orders when available-to-sell stock is insufficient.

When true, checkout and inventory reservation logic may permit quantities that exceed current on-hand stock, subject to max_backorder_quantity and broader policy constraints. When false, orders must be constrained to available inventory only.

max_backorder_quantity.description:
Optional cap on the total number of units that may be placed on backorder for this inventory item across all customers.

When null, the platform may treat backorders as unbounded or apply higher-level policy defaults. When provided, the value must be a non-negative integer and is enforced by checkout and inventory reservation flows whenever allow_backorder is true.

backorder_message.description:
Optional customer-facing message explaining backorder behavior and expected fulfillment timelines for this inventory item.

Frontends and communication templates may display this message when an order includes backordered units to help set customer expectations about delivery timing.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this backorder settings record was first created.

Set by the system and useful for audit, debugging, and historical analysis of configuration changes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this backorder settings record.

Automatically maintained by the system whenever a writable field such as allow_backorder, max_backorder_quantity, or backorder_message is changed.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-deletion timestamp for this backorder settings record.

When null, the record is considered active. When set to a date-time value, the record is treated as logically deleted and should not be used for new checkout or inventory decisions, though it may still be retained for audit and historical reporting.

IShoppingMallBackorderSetting.ICreate.description:
Creation payload for per-inventory-item backorder configuration in shopping_mall_backorder_settings.

Used by admin or seller tooling when first attaching backorder rules to an existing inventory item. Only writable business fields are exposed; identifiers and lifecycle timestamps are system-managed and therefore excluded from this DTO.

allow_backorder.description:
Flag indicating whether this inventory item may accept customer orders when available-to-sell stock is insufficient.

When true, checkout and inventory reservation logic may permit quantities that exceed current on-hand stock, subject to max_backorder_quantity and other policy constraints. When false, orders must be constrained to available inventory only.

max_backorder_quantity.description:
Optional cap on the total number of units that may be placed on backorder for this inventory item across all customers.

When null, the platform may treat backorders as unbounded or apply higher-level policy defaults. When provided, the value must be a non-negative integer and is enforced by checkout and inventory reservation flows whenever allow_backorder is true.

backorder_message.description:
Optional customer-facing message explaining backorder behavior and expected fulfillment timelines for this inventory item.

Typical content includes information about extended shipping times, estimated restock dates, or special conditions that apply to backordered units. When null, the storefront may fall back to generic messaging or hide backorder-specific copy.

IShoppingMallBackorderSetting.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for per-inventory-item backorder configuration in shopping_mall_backorder_settings.

Used by seller dashboards or platform admin tools to modify existing backorder rules attached to an inventory item. All fields are optional to support partial updates; identifiers and lifecycle timestamps remain system-managed and are not exposed for direct modification.

allow_backorder.description:
Flag indicating whether this inventory item may accept customer orders when available-to-sell stock is insufficient.

When omitted, the current allow_backorder value persists unchanged. When present, the updated value is enforced by checkout and inventory reservation logic.

max_backorder_quantity.description:
Updated cap on the total number of units that may be placed on backorder for this inventory item across all customers.

When set to a non-negative integer, downstream logic must enforce this limit whenever allow_backorder is true. When explicitly set to null, any existing cap is cleared and the platform may treat backorders as unbounded or apply higher-level policy defaults.

backorder_message.description:
Updated customer-facing message describing backorder behavior and expected fulfillment timelines.

When set to a non-empty string, this text is used by storefronts and communication templates to explain extended delivery expectations. When explicitly set to null, any existing custom message is cleared and generic platform messaging may be used instead.

IShoppingMallPreorderSettings.description:
Preorder configuration settings for a specific inventory item in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO represents a subsidiary 1:1 configuration child of the primary inventory entity stored in `shopping_mall_inventory_items`, with each inventory item owning at most one preorder-settings record in `shopping_mall_preorder_settings` via the `inventory_item_id` foreign key. It is primarily used as the detailed response model for endpoints such as `GET /shoppingMall/inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}/preorderSettings`, where the parent inventory item is already identified by the path parameter.

From an API perspective, this type exposes business-facing preorder configuration fields—such as the enable flag, optional preorder window, maximum preorder quantity, and expected release date—while also including both its own primary key and the relational foreign key back to the inventory item. The `inventory_item_id` field is managed exclusively by the backend and mirrors the parent `inventoryItemId` path parameter; clients must not attempt to control or override it through request bodies. System-managed audit and soft-delete fields are read-only and reflect lifecycle timestamps when available in the underlying Prisma model.

This type should be used as a detailed response object and referenced from other components via `$ref` only when preorder configuration needs to be shown inlined under an already-known inventory item context, not as a standalone identity separate from its parent.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the preorder settings record.

This field maps directly to `shopping_mall_preorder_settings.id` and uniquely identifies a single preorder configuration row for an inventory item. It serves as the canonical handle for debugging, logging, and administrative tooling that need to reference a specific preorder-settings record independently of the parent inventory item.

Clients typically discover this identifier via read APIs rather than constructing it themselves and should treat it as an opaque UUID value without encoding business logic into the identifier.

inventory_item_id.description:
Identifier of the inventory item that these preorder settings belong to.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_inventory_items.id` and is the parent side of a strict 1:1 relation from `shopping_mall_preorder_settings` to `shopping_mall_inventory_items` enforced by a unique constraint on `shopping_mall_preorder_settings.inventory_item_id`.

In HTTP APIs, the parent inventory item is always provided via the `inventoryItemId` path parameter (for example, `/shoppingMall/inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}/preorderSettings`), and the backend populates `inventory_item_id` from that parent context. Clients must treat this field as read-only relational metadata and should not attempt to set, modify, or rely on it when creating or updating preorder settings.

allow_preorder.description:
Flag indicating whether this inventory item is allowed to be sold as a preorder.

When true, the item can accept orders before its release date, subject to any configured preorder window and maximum preorder quantity. When false, the item behaves as a regular in-stock or out-of-stock item and preorder-specific behavior is disabled.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when the preorder window starts for this inventory item.

When present, this is an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC specifying the earliest moment when customers are allowed to place preorder purchases for the item. It must be earlier than `preorder_end_at` when both are provided to avoid an invalid preorder window configuration.

preorder_start_at.description:
Optional start timestamp of the preorder window for this inventory item.

If null, the preorder window may be considered open immediately when `allow_preorder` is true, subject to platform-wide defaults and higher-level business rules. When provided together with `preorder_end_at`, it defines the inclusive start boundary of when preorder sales are permitted.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when the preorder window ends for this inventory item.

When present, this is an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC specifying the latest moment when customers are allowed to place preorder purchases. It must be later than `preorder_start_at` when both values are provided so that the preorder window has a positive duration.

preorder_end_at.description:
Optional end timestamp of the preorder window for this inventory item.

If null, the preorder window may be open indefinitely or governed by higher-level policy when `allow_preorder` is true and no explicit end is configured here. When combined with `preorder_start_at`, it defines the end boundary after which preorder sales should be rejected or converted into regular sales behavior.

oneOf.description:
Maximum total quantity of units that may be sold as preorder for this inventory item.

When present, this positive integer limits the cumulative preorder units that can be confirmed before the item transitions to regular sale or preorder is disabled for capacity reasons. It is evaluated across all customers and orders, not per-customer.

max_preorder_quantity.description:
Optional cap on the total number of units that can be sold through preorder for this inventory item.

When null, no explicit preorder quantity cap is enforced by this configuration and platform defaults or other inventory controls may apply. When set, business logic should ensure that additional preorder attempts beyond this quantity are rejected or queued according to policy.

oneOf.description:
Planned release or availability timestamp for this inventory item.

This is an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC used for customer-facing communication about when preorder items are expected to ship or become fully available. It may be surfaced on product detail pages, confirmation emails, and order tracking views so that customers have a clear expectation of delivery timing.

release_date.description:
Optional expected release date for this inventory item while in preorder.

If present, this value communicates to customers when the item is expected to be shipped or become fully available; if null, the platform may omit release-date messaging or derive it from other catalog metadata. Operational processes may also use this date for planning fulfillment and inventory movements.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when this preorder settings record was first created.

This field is managed by the backend and reflects the creation time in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC) taken from `shopping_mall_preorder_settings.created_at` when available. It is useful for audit trails and understanding when preorder behavior was first configured for a particular inventory item.

created_at.description:
System-managed creation timestamp for the preorder settings record.

In most deployments this will be set automatically to the time the row was inserted and remain unchanged for the life of the record. It may be null if the underlying database model or migration history does not populate creation timestamps consistently.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when this preorder settings record was last updated.

This field is managed by the backend and reflects the most recent modification time in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC) from `shopping_mall_preorder_settings.updated_at` when available. It allows operators and tools to determine how fresh the configuration is and to detect recent changes.

updated_at.description:
System-managed last update timestamp for the preorder settings record.

Each successful modification of preorder configuration typically refreshes this timestamp. It may be null if the record has never been modified after creation or if the underlying schema does not store update timestamps for this configuration entity.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when this preorder settings record was soft-deleted.

This value is taken from `shopping_mall_preorder_settings.deleted_at` and, when present, indicates the point in time at which the preorder configuration row was logically removed from active use while remaining in the database for audit or recovery purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft-delete timestamp for the preorder settings record.

When null, the preorder configuration is considered active and eligible for use by inventory and checkout flows. When non-null, the record is treated as logically deleted and should normally be excluded from active configuration lookups, although it may still appear in administrative or audit-focused endpoints so that historical behavior and change history can be reconstructed.

IShoppingMallPreorderSettings.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating or replacing preorder settings for a specific inventory item.

This DTO represents the writable subset of fields for shopping_mall_preorder_settings and is used by the POST /shoppingMall/inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}/preorderSettings endpoint. The inventory item context is provided exclusively by the path parameter inventoryItemId and is NOT included in the request body.

Clients provide preorder configuration such as whether preorders are allowed, the optional preorder window, the maximum preorder quantity, and the expected release date. System-managed fields like inventory_item_id, created_at, and updated_at are ignored if sent and should not be modeled in the request.

The backend is responsible for validating time window consistency (preorder_start_at before preorder_end_at), ensuring positive max_preorder_quantity when specified, and enforcing that the configuration is compatible with the current inventory state.

allow_preorder.description:
Flag indicating whether this inventory item should allow preorder sales.

When set to true, the item can accept preorder purchases subject to any configured preorder window and quantity cap. When set to false, preorder behavior is disabled for the item.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the preorder window should start for this inventory item.

Must be an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. When provided together with preorder_end_at, it must be strictly earlier than preorder_end_at.

preorder_start_at.description:
Optional start timestamp of the preorder window to configure for this inventory item.

If null, the platform may treat the preorder window as starting immediately upon enabling allow_preorder or apply default behavior.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the preorder window should end for this inventory item.

Must be an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. When provided together with preorder_start_at, it must be strictly later than preorder_start_at.

preorder_end_at.description:
Optional end timestamp of the preorder window to configure for this inventory item.

If null, the preorder window may remain open until other business rules disable it, subject to platform policies.

oneOf.description:
Maximum total quantity of units that may be sold as preorder for this inventory item.

When set, this positive integer defines a hard cap on the cumulative preorder units that can be confirmed before preorder is closed or converted to regular sales.

max_preorder_quantity.description:
Optional cap on the total number of units that can be sold as preorder for this inventory item.

If null, no explicit preorder quantity limit is enforced by this configuration and other inventory controls or platform defaults may apply.

oneOf.description:
Planned release or availability timestamp for this inventory item while it is in preorder.

Must be an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC and is typically used for customer-facing communication such as "Expected to ship on" messages.

release_date.description:
Optional expected release date for the preorder inventory item.

If provided, this value is used for setting customer expectations around shipping or availability timelines; if null, the platform may fall back to other metadata or omit release date messaging.

IShoppingMallPreorderSetting.description:
Preorder configuration for a single inventory item in the shopping mall catalog.

This entity stores per-inventory-item rules that control whether and how customers can place preorders for a specific SKU before regular stock becomes available. It is in a 1:1 relationship with `shopping_mall_inventory_items` and acts as subsidiary configuration data that drives preorder availability, quantity caps, and temporal windows.

Business logic uses this model in conjunction with inventory, reservation, and order flows to determine if preorder checkout is allowed for a given SKU at a specific point in time, and to compute remaining preorder capacity based on historical preorder volume and configured limits.

id.description:
Primary key for the preorder settings record.

This identifier uniquely distinguishes each preorder configuration row in `shopping_mall_preorder_settings` and is used internally by the system for joins, auditing, and diagnostics.

Clients generally do not need to operate on this value directly, as preorder settings are accessed via their parent inventory item context rather than by raw ID.

inventory_item_id.description:
Identifier of the inventory item that these preorder settings apply to.

This is a foreign key referencing `shopping_mall_inventory_items.id` and establishes a strict 1:1 relationship between an inventory record and its preorder configuration.

In API design, this field is typically derived from the path parameter (e.g. `/inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}/preorderSettings`) and is not supplied by clients in request bodies.

allow_preorder.description:
Flag indicating whether the associated inventory item can currently be sold as a preorder.

When `true`, customers may place orders for this SKU even if regular stock is not yet available, subject to additional constraints such as preorder windows and quantity limits.

When `false`, preorder behavior for this item is disabled and the item must follow standard in-stock ordering rules.

preorder_start_at.description:
Timestamp when preorder sales are allowed to begin for this inventory item.

When set to a non-null value, preorder checkout for the associated SKU must not be permitted before this point in time. This supports scheduled launches where preorders open at a specific date.

When null, the start of preorder availability may be controlled by broader policies, flags, or manual administrative actions rather than a fixed timestamp.

preorder_end_at.description:
Timestamp after which preorder sales are no longer allowed for this inventory item.

When set, new preorders must not be accepted after this time, although existing preorders remain valid and must be fulfilled according to shipping and release policies.

When null, preorder availability may remain open-ended or be constrained by other business rules, such as inventory caps or manual scheduling.

max_preorder_quantity.description:
Maximum number of units that may be sold as preorders for this inventory item across all customers.

When set to a non-null integer, the platform must ensure that the total quantity of preorder line items referencing this SKU does not exceed this cap, including past and pending orders.

When null, there is no explicit per-item preorder quantity limit at the configuration level, and capacity may instead be governed by higher-level policies or inventory projections.

release_date.description:
Expected release or availability date for the preorder inventory item.

This timestamp is primarily used for customer communication and fulfillment planning, indicating when preordered items are expected to ship or become deliverable.

When null, the release timeline may be managed externally or communicated through other catalog metadata, but preorder enablement is still controlled by the other settings in this entity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this preorder settings record was initially created.

The value is set by the system at insertion time and represents the moment the preorder configuration was first established for the associated inventory item.

It is useful for auditing configuration history and understanding when preorder behavior was introduced for a given SKU.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this preorder settings record was most recently updated.

The system updates this value whenever any editable field of the preorder configuration changes, allowing operators to track the latest modification time.

This field is used for change tracking, debugging, and external synchronization scenarios where consumers need to detect configuration updates.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when this preorder settings record was soft-deleted, or null when the configuration is currently active.

Soft deletion allows the platform to retain historical preorder configuration data for reporting and audit purposes even after the configuration is no longer in effect.

When non-null, business logic should treat the preorder settings as inactive and typically behave as though the inventory item has no explicit preorder configuration.

IShoppingMallPreorderSetting.IUpdate.description:
Editable preorder configuration payload for a specific inventory item.

This DTO is used as the request body when creating or updating preorder settings for an inventory item via APIs such as `PUT /inventoryItems/{inventoryItemId}/preorderSettings`. It mirrors the configurable columns of `shopping_mall_preorder_settings` that may be changed by authorized actors.

Identification and ownership fields such as the foreign key to `shopping_mall_inventory_items` and audit timestamps are excluded from this shape, as they are derived from path parameters and managed by the backend. Clients provide only the desired preorder rules, and the system persists them while enforcing business validation around quantity limits and date windows.

allow_preorder.description:
Flag indicating whether the associated inventory item should be eligible for preorder.

When set to `true`, the item can be sold as a preorder subject to the configured temporal and quantity constraints. When `false`, preorder behavior is disabled and the item must rely on standard stock-based sale flows.

This property is required in the update payload because the backend needs an explicit decision about whether preorder is currently enabled for the inventory item.

preorder_start_at.description:
Desired timestamp when preorder sales are allowed to begin for this inventory item.

Providing a non-null value instructs the platform to block preorder checkout before this moment, supporting scheduled preorder launches. A null value indicates that there is no explicit start constraint at the configuration level and that higher-level policies or manual controls may govern availability.

Clients should ensure that this value, when present, is earlier than or equal to `preorder_end_at` if an end timestamp is also provided.

preorder_end_at.description:
Desired timestamp after which preorder sales should no longer be accepted for this inventory item.

If non-null, new preorder orders for the SKU must not be allowed once this time has passed, although existing preorders remain valid. When null, preorder availability may continue indefinitely or be constrained by other rules.

Implementations should validate that this value is not earlier than `preorder_start_at` when both are supplied in the same payload.

max_preorder_quantity.description:
Upper limit on the total number of units that may be sold as preorders for this inventory item across all customers.

Clients can use this field to cap preorder volume for a SKU to manage production risk or marketing commitments. When set, the backend should prevent further preorder creation once cumulative preorder quantity meets or exceeds this threshold.

A null value indicates that no explicit per-item preorder quantity cap is configured at this level and that other mechanisms may govern capacity.

release_date.description:
Expected release or availability date communicated for the preorder inventory item.

Setting this value allows the platform to display a target release or shipping date to customers and to coordinate fulfillment scheduling around that point in time.

When null, the release timeline may be omitted from customer-facing experiences or derived from other catalog metadata, but preorder enablement is still governed by the other fields in this DTO.

IShoppingMallFulfillment.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for listing fulfillment aggregates associated with a specific order in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used as the request body for the `PATCH /shoppingMall/orders/{orderId}/fulfillments` endpoint. It allows clients to provide optional filters, sorting, and pagination hints when retrieving fulfillment records from the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` table scoped to a single order. The path parameter `orderId` identifies the parent order and MUST NOT be duplicated as a property here.

All fields in this schema are optional so that clients can simply omit the body or send an empty object to retrieve the default listing for the order. The server is responsible for applying sensible defaults for pagination and sorting when corresponding properties are not provided.

page.description:
Page number for paginated listing of fulfillments scoped to a single order.

If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default such as page 1. This value works together with the `limit` property to control which window of results is returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of fulfillment records to return in a single page.

If omitted, the backend applies a service-level default page size. Clients can tune this value within allowed bounds to balance payload size and number of network round trips.

status.description:
Optional filter for fulfillment status.

Represents a high-level state of the fulfillment aggregate, such as `pending`, `in_progress`, `shipped`, or `delivered`. The exact set of statuses is defined by the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` Prisma model and platform policy. When provided, only fulfillments matching the given status are returned.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the fulfillment creation timestamp filter.

When provided together with `createdTo`, only fulfillments whose creation timestamps fall within the specified time range are included in the result. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the fulfillment creation timestamp filter.

When provided together with `createdFrom`, only fulfillments whose creation timestamps fall within the specified time range are included in the result. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string.

sortBy.description:
Field name used to sort the list of fulfillments.

Typical values include `createdAt` or `status`. The exact set of allowed sort keys is defined by the service implementation. When omitted, the backend uses a default sort order such as newest-first by creation time.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the field specified in `sortBy`.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the backend applies its default sort direction for the selected sort key.

Sort direction applied to the field specified in `sortBy`.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the backend applies its default sort direction for the selected sort key.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the field specified in `sortBy`.

Use `asc` for ascending order and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the backend applies its default sort direction for the selected sort key.

IShoppingMallFulfillment.description:
Detailed representation of a single fulfillment aggregate in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO models the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` Prisma entity and composes key information required to display the full physical processing state of one segment of an order. A fulfillment aggregate typically represents the processing of one or more order lines, and can be linked to shipments and tracking events via related tables.

The schema intentionally avoids exposing actor identity fields from the request side and focuses on read-only data required by client applications for tracking and status display. Ownership and authorization are enforced at the service layer based on the associated order and seller segments.

id.description:
Unique identifier of this fulfillment aggregate.

This is the primary key of the corresponding record in the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` table. It is generated by the system and is immutable for the lifetime of the record.

orderId.description:
Identifier of the order in `shopping_mall_orders` to which this fulfillment belongs.

This value corresponds to the order path parameter used in fulfillment-related endpoints and is used to ensure the fulfillment is always resolved within the correct order context.

status.description:
Current high-level status of the fulfillment.

Typical values include states such as `pending`, `in_progress`, `shipped`, and `delivered`. The exact set of statuses is defined in the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` Prisma model and platform policy. Clients use this field to render fulfillment progress indicators in user interfaces.

packedQuantity.description:
Number of units from the associated order line or lines that have reached the packed state within this fulfillment.

This value maps to the non-nullable `packed_quantity` column in the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` table. It increases when items are successfully packed and ready to be handed over to a carrier, and is used together with `shippedQuantity` and `deliveredQuantity` to understand partial fulfillment progress.

shippedQuantity.description:
Number of units from this fulfillment that have been dispatched across all related shipments.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable `shipped_quantity` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments`. It represents the total quantity that has left the warehouse in one or more shipments, regardless of whether those shipments have already been delivered.

deliveredQuantity.description:
Number of units from this fulfillment that have been confirmed as delivered to the customer.

This value is mapped from the non-nullable `delivered_quantity` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments`. It reflects the quantity that has completed the physical delivery lifecycle and is a key indicator for post-delivery flows such as returns and reviews.

lastStatusReason.description:
Optional human-readable explanation associated with the current fulfillment status.

This field maps to the nullable `last_status_reason` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments`. It is typically used to capture failure reasons (for example, delivery failed or address not found) or internal notes explaining why the fulfillment is in an exceptional state, and may be surfaced in administrative or customer support tools.

packedAt.description:
Timestamp when this fulfillment first reached a packed state.

This value corresponds to the nullable `packed_at` column in the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` table. It marks the time when all items included in the fulfillment were considered packed and ready for shipment preparation.

firstShippedAt.description:
Timestamp when units in this fulfillment were first shipped.

This field is derived from the nullable `first_shipped_at` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments`. It records the moment when any quantity allocated to this fulfillment was first handed over to a carrier, which is useful for SLA calculations and shipment tracking analytics.

lastDeliveredAt.description:
Timestamp when units in this fulfillment were most recently marked as delivered.

This maps to the nullable `last_delivered_at` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments`. It is updated whenever additional quantities from this fulfillment are confirmed delivered, providing an anchor point for return windows and post-delivery communication.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this fulfillment record was created.

The value is stored in the database as the non-nullable `created_at` column on the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` row and reflects when physical processing for the associated items was initiated.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating the last time this fulfillment record was updated.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and reflects the most recent modification to the fulfillment’s state or metadata, such as status transitions, shipment associations, or tracking updates.

carrier.description:
Optional carrier identifier or name associated with this fulfillment.

When the fulfillment is tied to a physical shipment handled by a logistics provider, this field contains a short code or the name of the carrier (for example, `UPS`, `FedEx`, or a regional courier name). It is modeled as an API-level convenience and may be derived from one or more underlying shipment records.

trackingNumber.description:
Optional tracking number assigned by the carrier for this fulfillment.

Clients can display this value to end users and link to the carrier’s tracking portal when supported. In some implementations, this may be derived from the primary tracking number of the dominant shipment associated with this fulfillment aggregate.

trackingUrl.description:
Optional URL for externally tracking this fulfillment.

When available, this URL points to a carrier or platform tracking page where real-time shipment updates can be viewed. Clients may render this as a clickable link in order detail screens. The URL is treated as a read-only convenience derived from carrier and tracking configuration.

items.description:
Collection of per-line fulfillment items associated with this fulfillment aggregate.

Each item typically represents the fulfillment status and quantity for a specific order line from `shopping_mall_order_lines`. This is a compositional relation: fulfillment items are created and managed in the same lifecycle as their parent fulfillment and are used to allocate quantities from order lines into shipments.

shipments.description:
List of shipments associated with this fulfillment.

Each entry summarizes a shipment entity that groups one or more fulfillment items for physical dispatch. Detailed shipment tracking information, such as full tracking history and delivery attempts, can be obtained via dedicated shipment endpoints when needed.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentItem.description:
Represents a single fulfillment–shipment junction record stored in the `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` table.

Each row describes how much of a specific fulfillment aggregate is included in a particular shipment. The record connects a fulfillment (`shopping_mall_fulfillments`) to a shipment (`shopping_mall_shipments`) using foreign keys and a concrete `quantity`, allowing the system to support partial shipments and multiple shipments for the same fulfillment.

This DTO is returned by read operations that expose fulfillment item details to clients, such as when listing the items attached to a fulfillment or inspecting how a shipment is composed of multiple fulfillment items.

id.description:
Primary key for the fulfillment item record in the `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` table.

This value is generated by the backend when the junction record is created and uniquely identifies the relationship between a fulfillment and a shipment for a specific quantity of goods.

fulfillment_id.description:
Identifier of the parent fulfillment aggregate in the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` table.

The referenced fulfillment represents the operational unit that groups one or more items to be shipped for a particular order, and this field ties the junction record back to that aggregate.

shipment_id.description:
Identifier of the shipment in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table that carries part or all of the parent fulfillment.

By linking to a shipment, this field enables the system to track which physical shipment instance is responsible for delivering the quantity declared in this fulfillment item record.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the fulfillment’s order line that is included in the referenced shipment.

This value must be a positive integer and, at the business-logic level, must not exceed the remaining fulfillable quantity for the related order line when all fulfillment items and reservations are taken into account.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this fulfillment item junction record was created.

The value is stored in the database as a non-nullable `DateTime` and is managed exclusively by the backend, providing an audit trail for when the fulfillment–shipment linkage was established.

IShoppingMallShipmentSummary.description:
Summary representation of a shipment associated with one or more fulfillment items.
