This DTO is used inside `IShoppingMallFulfillment` to provide lightweight information about shipments without inlining the full shipment entity or all tracking events. Clients can use the identifiers here to navigate to more detailed shipment endpoints when necessary.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipment record.

This corresponds to the primary key of a row in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

carrier.description:
Carrier identifier or name for this shipment.

When the shipment is handed off to a third-party logistics provider, this field contains the carrier name or code that clients can display to end users.

trackingNumber.description:
Tracking number associated with this shipment.

The format depends on the carrier and is used by clients to present tracking information in UI or link to carrier portals.

shippedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this shipment was dispatched.

When present, this value helps users understand when the physical hand-off to the carrier occurred.

IShoppingMallFulfillment.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new fulfillment aggregate for a specific order in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used by sellers or platform administrators to initiate physical processing for one or more order lines belonging to an existing order. It captures which order lines will be fulfilled and the quantities for each line within this fulfillment. It may also include initial shipment or carrier preferences at the fulfillment level.

Actor identity (seller or platform admin) and order ownership are validated from the authentication and path context, not from this DTO. System-managed fields such as IDs, timestamps, and status history are excluded from this request schema.

order_line_fulfillments.description:
Collection of order-line level fulfillment instructions that define which items from the order should be processed in this fulfillment.

Each entry references a concrete order line within the target order and specifies the quantity to be fulfilled as part of this aggregate. The backend validates that the referenced order line belongs to the order from the path, that the requested quantity does not exceed the remaining fulfillable quantity, and that the line is in a state that allows fulfillment.

carrier_code.description:
Optional carrier identifier or shipping service code requested for this fulfillment.

This can be used by sellers or platform administrators to indicate which carrier or shipping method should be used when shipments are later created from this fulfillment. It is a free-form but conventionally structured string such as an integration code or short carrier name.

requested_ship_date.description:
Optional requested ship date and time for the items covered by this fulfillment.

When provided, this timestamp expresses when the seller or fulfillment center intends to hand over the shipment to the carrier or have the items leave the warehouse. It is used for planning and customer communication but does not directly enforce scheduling guarantees.

warehouse_code.description:
Optional warehouse or fulfillment center code indicating from where this fulfillment will be processed.

This code helps route the fulfillment to the appropriate physical location or virtual warehouse configuration. It should correspond to a warehouse or location known by the seller or marketplace, but is modeled as a simple string in the API layer.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes for internal handling of this fulfillment.

These notes may include packing instructions, special handling information, or additional context for warehouse staff. They are not typically exposed directly to customers.

IShoppingMallFulfillment.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing fulfillment aggregate for a specific order in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO allows authorized sellers or platform administrators to adjust fulfillment-level metadata such as status transitions, carrier or tracking information, planned shipment timing, and internal handling notes. It does not allow changing the owning order, actor identity, or other immutable system-managed fields.

All properties are optional and represent partial updates; only provided fields are considered for modification. Business rules and Prisma schema constraints are enforced by the backend, including allowed status transitions and consistency checks with related shipments and tracking events.

status.description:
New high-level status for this fulfillment aggregate.

Typical examples include values such as `pending`, `in_progress`, `shipped`, `delivered`, or `canceled`, though the exact set of allowed status literals is enforced by the backend according to the Prisma schema and business rules. Status changes may trigger additional side effects such as recording status events or sending notifications.

carrier_code.description:
Updated carrier identifier or shipping service code for this fulfillment.

This can be used to change or set which carrier or shipping product is associated with the shipments relating to this fulfillment. It is a free-form but conventionally structured integration or carrier code.

tracking_number.description:
Primary tracking number associated with this fulfillment once items have been handed off to a carrier.

This value is typically displayed to customers and used to generate tracking links. Multiple tracking events or secondary tracking numbers are usually recorded in related shipment or tracking event tables, while this field exposes the main tracking reference at the fulfillment level.

requested_ship_date.description:
Updated requested ship date and time for the items covered by this fulfillment.

This timestamp communicates revised expectations about when the items will leave the warehouse or be handed over to a carrier. It does not by itself guarantee actual dispatch time but is used for planning and customer communication.

warehouse_code.description:
Updated warehouse or fulfillment center code indicating from where this fulfillment will be processed.

Changing this value may only be permitted while the fulfillment is in early states such as `pending`, subject to backend business rules aligned with the Prisma schema.

notes.description:
Updated internal handling notes for this fulfillment.

This field can be used to adjust or append instructions for warehouse staff, such as packaging details or special handling requirements. It is not typically visible to customers.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentOrderLine.ICreat.description:
Nested request schema representing a single order-line level fulfillment instruction within a new fulfillment aggregate.

Each object identifies an order line belonging to the target order and specifies the quantity from that line to be processed in the current fulfillment. The backend validates that the order line exists, belongs to the order identified in the path, and that the requested quantity is positive and does not exceed the remaining fulfillable quantity for that line.

Actor identity and order ownership are enforced using the authentication context and the order path parameter, not via this nested DTO.

This DTO is logically mapped to the `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` Prisma model through its `quantity` field, which corresponds to `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items.quantity`. Other physical columns on that model, such as `id`, `fulfillment_id`, `shipment_id`, and `created_at`, are intentionally omitted because they are derived from the parent fulfillment and shipment context or generated by the database.

The `order_line_id` field is a foreign reference to `shopping_mall_order_lines.id` used by the fulfillment creation logic to determine which order line is being fulfilled, rather than a direct column on `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items`.

order_line_id.description:
Identifier of the order line in `shopping_mall_order_lines` that is being fulfilled as part of this fulfillment.

The referenced order line must belong to the order identified by the `orderId` path parameter of the parent endpoint. The backend enforces that linkage and rejects references to order lines from other orders.

quantity.description:
Number of units from the referenced order line to include in this fulfillment.

The quantity must be a positive integer greater than zero and must not exceed the remaining fulfillable quantity on the order line after accounting for prior fulfillments or cancellations.

This field maps directly to the `quantity` column on the `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` Prisma model and is always stored as a non-null integer, reflecting the number of units that this specific fulfillment item is responsible for processing.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentItem.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for retrieving fulfillment items belonging to a specific fulfillment in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used as the request body for PATCH /shoppingMall/customer/fulfillments/{fulfillmentId}/items and expresses how clients want to page, sort, and filter the `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` records belonging to a given parent fulfillment. It is purely a query-parameter carrier and does not map directly to a Prisma model table.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination when listing fulfillment items under a fulfillment.

If omitted, the backend typically defaults this value to the first page (1), ensuring that callers who do not supply pagination still receive a deterministic slice of results.

limit.description:
Maximum number of fulfillment item summaries to return in a single page.

Typical values are between 10 and 50. The backend enforces an upper bound of 100 to protect performance and avoid excessively large result payloads.

orderBy.description:
Logical field name to sort fulfillment items by within the parent fulfillment scope.

Common options include fields derived from `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` such as `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or domain-specific keys like `status` or `requestedQuantity`, depending on how the backend exposes sortable attributes.

oneOf.description:
Ascending sort direction for fulfillment item query results.

When combined with a field such as `createdAt` or `updatedAt` in `orderBy`, this returns the earliest or oldest fulfillment items first. This is useful for chronological reviews, audit workflows, and scenarios where operators want to process items in the order they were created.

Clients can also use ascending ordering on numeric fields (for example quantities or sequence numbers) to surface the smallest values first, making it easier to identify low-quantity or low-priority items within a fulfillment.

Descending sort direction for fulfillment item query results.

When used with timestamp fields such as `createdAt` or `updatedAt`, this returns the most recent fulfillment items first, which is typically desirable for dashboards, monitoring views, and troubleshooting UIs that focus on the latest operational activity.

Descending ordering can also be applied to numeric fields so that the largest quantities or highest-priority items appear at the top of the list, helping operators quickly identify fulfillment items that represent significant workload or impact.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering fulfillment items.

Use `"asc"` for ascending order and `"desc"` for descending order. The chosen direction is applied to the field specified in `orderBy`, allowing clients to control whether earlier/older or later/newer records appear first in the paginated result set.

orderLineId.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to fulfillment items that are tied to a specific order line in the `shopping_mall_order_lines` table.

When provided, only fulfillment items referencing the given order line are included in the result set, making it easier to investigate how a particular line item has been fulfilled across shipments.

shipmentId.description:
Optional filter to restrict results to fulfillment items that are linked to a specific shipment record in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

This is helpful when analyzing which fulfillment items are included in a single shipment or when troubleshooting shipping- and carrier-related issues for a particular shipment identifier.

status.description:
Optional filter for the fulfillment item status.

Example values might include domain-specific states such as `pending`, `picking`, `packed`, `shipped`, or `cancelled`. The exact allowed values and transitions are governed by backend business rules and are intentionally not restricted as an OpenAPI enum so that the status vocabulary can evolve without requiring a schema change.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentItem.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new fulfillment–shipment junction record under an existing fulfillment in the shoppingMall system.

This request body is used by operations such as `POST /shoppingMall/seller/fulfillments/{fulfillmentId}/items` and `POST /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/fulfillments/{fulfillmentId}/items`. The `fulfillmentId` is supplied as a path parameter and identifies the parent fulfillment aggregate in `shopping_mall_fulfillments`, while this payload supplies the shipment and quantity information needed to create a row in `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items`.

Server-managed fields such as the primary key `id`, the `fulfillment_id` derived from the path parameter, and the `created_at` timestamp are not part of this DTO and are populated by the backend when the record is persisted.

shipment_id.description:
Identifier of the shipment in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table that will carry part or all of the specified fulfillment.

The shipment referenced here must already exist and be compatible with the parent fulfillment (for example, belonging to the same order context). This field populates the non-nullable `shipment_id` column in the `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` table.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the fulfillment’s underlying order line that should be associated with the given shipment.

This value must be a positive integer. Business logic will ensure that the requested quantity does not exceed the remaining fulfillable quantity for the associated fulfillment and order line when considering existing fulfillment items and inventory reservations.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentItem.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing fulfillment–shipment junction record under a fulfillment aggregate in the shoppingMall logistics subsystem.

This payload is used by operations such as `PUT /shoppingMall/seller/fulfillments/{fulfillmentId}/items/{fulfillmentItemId}` and `PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/fulfillments/{fulfillmentId}/items/{fulfillmentItemId}`. It represents the subset of `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` columns that business rules may allow to change after creation, while immutable identifiers like the parent `fulfillment_id` are managed via path parameters and not exposed for modification in the body.

All properties in this DTO are optional, enabling partial updates. The backend will enforce additional invariants—for example, preventing shipment reassignment in terminal states or rejecting quantity changes that would violate inventory or order constraints.

shipment_id.description:
Updated shipment identifier for this fulfillment item, referencing a row in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

Implementations may use this to move the allocated quantity from one shipment to another when allowed by business rules (for example, before shipments are locked or dispatched).

quantity.description:
Updated quantity of the fulfillment’s order line that is associated with this fulfillment item.

The new quantity must remain a positive integer and must continue to respect order and inventory constraints, including limits on the total fulfillable quantity across all fulfillment items for the underlying order line.

IShoppingMallShipment.IRequest.description:
Search and filter request DTO for listing shipments associated with a specific customer order.

This request body is used by the PATCH `/shoppingMall/orders/{orderId}/shipments` operation instead of query-string parameters so that complex search criteria can be expressed in a structured way. It ultimately drives a query over the `shopping_mall_shipments` Prisma model but is scoped by the `orderId` path parameter rather than carrying the order identifier as a property.

The DTO focuses on pagination, sorting, and a small set of business-relevant filters that map directly to columns in `shopping_mall_shipments`, such as `shipment_status`, `carrier_name`, `created_at`, and `shipped_at`. All properties are optional so that callers can combine only the filters they need for a particular UI screen or report.

page.description:
Page index for pagination, starting from 1.

This value controls the logical page number when retrieving a paginated response of type `IPageIShoppingMallShipment.ISummary`. If omitted, the backend typically defaults to the first page, but the exact default behavior is defined by the implementation and may be documented in API-level guidelines.

limit.description:
Maximum number of shipment records to return per page.

This value is used to limit the page size in the paginated result and should be a positive integer. Backends commonly enforce an upper bound (for example, 100) to protect performance and memory usage; this DTO reflects such a constraint via its `maximum` value.

sortBy.description:
Field name used to sort the shipment list within the result set.

Typical values include column-oriented names such as `created_at`, `shipped_at`, or a derived field like `latest_tracking_timestamp`, depending on what the implementation supports. The actual set of allowed sort keys is determined by the service and should be documented alongside the endpoint. When null or omitted, a sensible default ordering (often by `created_at desc`) is applied.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the field specified by `sortBy`.

Use `asc` for ascending ordering or `desc` for descending ordering. When null or omitted, the backend will typically choose a default (commonly `desc` for time-based fields). The available values are intentionally constrained to the two canonical sort directions.

shipmentStatus.description:
Optional filter for shipment lifecycle status, mapped directly to the `shipment_status` column of the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

Typical values include high-level statuses such as `pending`, `ready_to_ship`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, or `lost`, mirroring the business vocabulary defined in the Prisma model description. When this property is null or omitted, shipments of all statuses are considered by the underlying query.

carrierName.description:
Optional filter for the carrier handling the shipment, mapped to the `carrier_name` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`.

Examples include carrier or logistics provider names such as `UPS`, `FedEx`, `DHL`, or local couriers. When provided, only shipments whose `carrier_name` column matches (typically using a case-insensitive comparison, depending on implementation) are returned. When null or omitted, no carrier-based filtering is applied.

fromCreatedAt.description:
Inclusive lower bound for shipment creation timestamp filtering, mapped to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. Only shipments whose `created_at` timestamp is greater than or equal to this value are included when the property is set. When null or omitted, no lower bound on `created_at` is enforced.

toCreatedAt.description:
Inclusive upper bound for shipment creation timestamp filtering, mapped to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. Only shipments whose `created_at` timestamp is less than or equal to this value are included when the property is set. When null or omitted, no upper bound on `created_at` is enforced.

fromShippedAt.description:
Inclusive lower bound for the `shipped_at` timestamp used to filter shipments by when they were handed over to the carrier.

This value maps directly to the `shipped_at` column of the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. Only shipments with `shipped_at` greater than or equal to this value are included when provided. When null or omitted, no lower bound on `shipped_at` is enforced.

toShippedAt.description:
Inclusive upper bound for the `shipped_at` timestamp used to filter shipments by when they were handed over to the carrier.

This value maps directly to the `shipped_at` column of the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. Only shipments with `shipped_at` less than or equal to this value are included when provided. When null or omitted, no upper bound on `shipped_at` is enforced.

IShoppingMallShipment.description:
Detailed shipment DTO representing a physical or logical shipment unit in the shopping mall order fulfillment domain.

This type models a single row of the `shopping_mall_shipments` Prisma model, enriched with related context suitable for detailed shipment views. Each shipment is associated with exactly one customer-facing order via the `order` reference (derived from the non-null `order_id` column) and one seller segment via the `sellerSegment` reference (derived from the non-null `order_seller_segment_id` column), and it groups one or more fulfillment items that will be transported together.

The DTO exposes core shipment fields such as lifecycle status, carrier metadata, tracking identifiers, and lifecycle timestamps directly mapped from Prisma columns, as well as derived fields like `latest_tracking_status` and `latest_tracking_timestamp` that summarize data from `shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events`. Audit timestamps and the soft deletion marker are also included to support operational tracing and debugging.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipment record in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

This value maps directly to the primary key column `id` and is used as the stable identifier in URLs, logs, and internal references throughout the logistics subsystem.

order.description:
Summary view of the customer-facing order that owns this shipment.

This field is a rich projection that replaces the raw foreign key `order_id` in the `shopping_mall_shipments` model, providing enough context about the master order for UI rendering and analytics without requiring an additional API call to resolve the order entity.

sellerSegment.description:
Summary representation of the seller-specific segment within the owning order that this shipment serves.

This projection replaces the raw foreign key `order_seller_segment_id` in the `shopping_mall_shipments` table and allows clients to understand which seller segment and portion of the order is being shipped by this shipment.

shipment_status.description:
High-level shipment lifecycle status as stored in the `shipment_status` column of the `shopping_mall_shipments` table.

Typical values include `pending`, `ready_to_ship`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, or `lost`, mirroring the business vocabulary documented in the Prisma schema. Service-layer logic must enforce valid transitions between these states to maintain a consistent shipment lifecycle and reliable downstream analytics.

carrier_name.description:
Name of the carrier handling this shipment, mapped from the nullable `carrier_name` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`.

Examples include global logistics providers such as `UPS`, `FedEx`, `DHL`, or regional couriers. The value is null while a shipment exists in a pre-assignment state where a specific carrier has not yet been selected or recorded.

carrier_service_level.description:
Optional service level or product name exposed by the carrier for this shipment, mapped from the nullable `carrier_service_level` column.

Typical examples include `standard`, `express`, `next_day`, or other carrier-specific labels. When null, no explicit service level has been recorded, and the effective behavior may be implied by other configuration or default business rules.

tracking_number.description:
Primary tracking identifier assigned by the carrier for this shipment, mapped from the nullable `tracking_number` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`.

This value is used for both internal tracking operations and customer-facing tracking links. It may be null when the shipment has been created but not yet manifested with the carrier or when tracking is not available for the shipping method used.

latest_tracking_status.description:
Optional synthesized status derived from the most recent tracking event in the `shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events` table.

Common examples include values such as `label_created`, `picked_up`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, or `delivered`, depending on how the integration normalizes carrier event codes. This field does not correspond to a single Prisma column; instead, it is a computed projection maintained by the application to provide an at-a-glance view of shipment progress.

latest_tracking_timestamp.description:
Timestamp of the most recent tracking event used to derive `latest_tracking_status`, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

Like `latest_tracking_status`, this field is not a direct column on the `shopping_mall_shipments` model. It is computed from the event history in `shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events` and is null when no tracking events are available or aggregation has not yet been performed.

shipped_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment was handed over to the carrier, mapped from the nullable `shipped_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

This value remains null while the shipment is still in preparation and is typically set when the shipment status transitions to a shipped or in-transit state. Once populated, it represents the historical time of physical departure from the seller or fulfillment center.

delivered_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment was confirmed delivered to the customer or final destination, mapped from the nullable `delivered_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

The field remains null until a delivery confirmation is recorded, either from the carrier or via manual back-office input, and should generally only be set when the `shipment_status` reflects a delivered or equivalent terminal state.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment record was created in the system, mapped from the non-null `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`.

The value is stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC and is set once at insertion time. It is used for audit, troubleshooting, and sorting shipments chronologically in operational dashboards and reports.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment record was last updated, mapped from the non-null `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments`.

This value is stored as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC and is refreshed on each mutation of the shipment record, including status transitions and carrier metadata updates. It supports audit trails and helps detect stale data in caches or downstream systems.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the shipment record, mapped from the nullable `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_shipments` and expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

When this value is null, the shipment is considered active and should participate in normal business flows and queries. When populated, the shipment is treated as logically deleted—excluded from standard listings and operations, but still retained for legal, audit, and historical analytics purposes.

IShoppingMallShipment.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new shipment record associated with an existing order in the shopping mall backend.

This DTO is used by sellers when calling POST /shoppingMall/orders/{orderId}/shipments to register a new shipment for a specific order and seller segment. It carries seller-segment context and optional carrier and tracking information required to initialize shipment processing.

order_seller_segment_id.description:
Identifier of the order seller segment that this shipment belongs to.

This must reference a row in shopping_mall_order_seller_segments that is linked to the order specified by the orderId path parameter. It scopes the shipment to the portion of the order handled by a single seller.

shipment_status.description:
Initial status of the shipment within the shipment lifecycle.

Typical values, as documented in the Prisma model comments, include states such as `pending`, `ready_to_ship`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, or `lost`. Business rules may restrict which of these values are allowed at creation time (for example, usually `pending` or `ready_to_ship`).

carrier_name.description:
Name of the shipping carrier that will handle this shipment.

Examples include logistics providers such as "UPS", "FedEx", or local courier services. This field is optional at creation time when the carrier has not yet been assigned.

carrier_service_level.description:
Service level or method provided by the shipping carrier for this shipment.

Examples include values such as "standard", "express", "overnight", or carrier-specific service codes. This field is optional and may be provided or updated later as shipping arrangements are finalized.

tracking_number.description:
Tracking number assigned by the carrier to this shipment.

This identifier enables both the platform and customers to track shipment progress through the carrier’s tracking systems. It is optional at creation time and may be supplied or updated later.

shipped_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the shipment physically left the warehouse or fulfillment center.

This value is typically null when the shipment is first created and is populated once the package has actually shipped. When provided, it must be an ISO 8601 date-time string.

IShoppingMallShipment.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing shipment record associated with an order in the shopping mall backend.

This DTO is used by sellers when calling PUT /shoppingMall/orders/{orderId}/shipments/{shipmentId} to adjust shipment status and carrier metadata over the course of the shipment lifecycle. All fields are optional so that callers can perform partial updates.

shipment_status.description:
Updated status of the shipment within the shipment lifecycle.

Typical values include `pending`, `ready_to_ship`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, or `lost`. The service layer must enforce valid status transitions, such as preventing a move from `delivered` back to `pending`.

carrier_name.description:
Updated name of the shipping carrier handling this shipment.

Use this field to correct or specify the carrier name after creation. Examples include "UPS", "FedEx", or local courier providers.

carrier_service_level.description:
Updated service level or method provided by the carrier for this shipment.

Examples include "standard", "express", or other carrier-specific service codes. This can be changed if shipping arrangements are modified.

tracking_number.description:
Updated tracking number assigned by the carrier to this shipment.

Use this field if the tracking number was not known at creation time or needs correction.

shipped_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the shipment physically left the warehouse or fulfillment center.

If provided, it must be an ISO 8601 date-time string. This field can be set once the shipment is handed over to the carrier.

delivered_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the shipment was successfully delivered to the customer.

If provided, it must be an ISO 8601 date-time string. Business rules should ensure that this value is set only when the shipment_status represents a delivered state and is not earlier than shipped_at.

IShoppingMallShipmentTrackingEvent.IRequ.description:
Filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for querying shipment tracking events associated with a specific shipment.

Used by PATCH /shoppingMall/shipments/{shipmentId}/trackingEvents to search tracking events stored in shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events for the given shipment. This DTO is strictly read-only and expresses how to filter and page through existing tracking events; it never creates or updates data.

page.description: Page number to retrieve, starting from 1. Used together with limit to page through tracking events for the shipment.

limit.description: Number of tracking events to return per page. Combined with page, controls pagination over the result set.

fromOccurredAt.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the tracking event occurrence time window.

When provided, only events whose occurred_at is greater than or equal to this value are returned. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

toOccurredAt.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the tracking event occurrence time window.

When provided, only events whose occurred_at is less than or equal to this value are returned. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

oneOf.description: Normalized shipment tracking status, such as shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, delivery_failed, or exception.

status.description:
Normalized shipment tracking status used to filter tracking events.

When set, only events whose status exactly matches the given value are returned. Typical values include shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, delivery_failed, and exception.

carrierStatusCode.description:
Raw carrier-specific status code filter.

When provided, restricts results to events whose carrier_status_code matches this value. Useful for debugging or carrier-specific workflows.

locationSearch.description:
Free-text search term applied to location-related fields such as location_description.

Intended for partial matching (implementation-specific) to find events mentioning a particular city, region, or facility.

messageSearch.description:
Free-text search term applied to textual message fields such as carrier_raw_message.

Used to find tracking events containing particular phrases or keywords from the carrier or internal system.

orderBy.description:
Field by which to sort tracking events.

Common values include occurred_at and created_at. When omitted, implementations typically default to occurred_at descending to show most recent events first.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction to apply to the orderBy field.

When provided, must be either "asc" for ascending or "desc" for descending order. If omitted, implementations usually default to "desc" for most recent events first.

IShoppingMallShipmentTrackingEvent.description:
Shipment tracking event entity representing a single milestone in the lifecycle of a shipment in the shoppingMall platform.

Instances of this type correspond to rows in the shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events Prisma model and are associated with a specific shipment in shopping_mall_shipments via the shipment_id foreign key. The model is append-only and forms an immutable history of how a shipment progressed over time.

This DTO is returned from APIs that create or retrieve tracking events and includes system-managed fields such as id and created_at in addition to the business fields captured at event creation time.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipment tracking event.

This value is generated by the system when the tracking event row is inserted into shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events and is used to uniquely reference this specific milestone.

shipment_id.description:
Identifier of the shipment in shopping_mall_shipments that this tracking event belongs to.

This is a foreign key referencing shopping_mall_shipments.id and is derived from the shipmentId path parameter in related API operations. It is read-only from the perspective of external clients.

status.description:
Normalized tracking status for the shipment at the time of this event.

Typical values include: "shipped", "in_transit", "out_for_delivery", "delivered", "delivery_failed", or "exception". Implementations may restrict this field to a known enum in code, but the underlying column is modeled as a string.

carrier_status_code.description:
Optional carrier-specific status code or shorthand representing the raw status supplied by the logistics carrier.

This field may be null when the carrier does not provide a structured status code or when only a free-text message is available.

location_description.description:
Optional human-readable description of the shipment's location at the time of the event.

Examples include city names, regions, or facility labels such as "Seoul, KR" or "Central Distribution Center". When location information is not available, this field is null.

carrier_raw_message.description:
Optional raw message payload received from the carrier or underlying logistics system for this tracking event.

Typically contains unstructured or localized text such as "Arrived at sorting center" or "Recipient not available". This field is useful for audit and debugging but may require processing before being shown to end users.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this tracking event occurred according to the carrier or internal logistics system, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

Represents the business event time and may differ from when the event was recorded by the shoppingMall platform.

created_at.description:
System-managed timestamp recording when this tracking event record was created in the shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events table.

Stored in ISO 8601 date-time format and used to maintain an immutable, append-only history of shipment progress updates.

IShoppingMallShipmentTrackingEvent.ICrea.description:
Request payload for creating a new shipment tracking event associated with a specific shipment in shopping_mall_shipments.

This DTO captures the business-relevant fields that the caller can provide when appending a new tracking milestone, excluding system-managed fields like id, shipment_id, and created_at which are handled by the backend using the path parameter and database defaults.

It is used as the request body for POST operations that create rows in shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events for a given shipment.

status.description:
Normalized tracking status for the shipment at the time of this event.

Typical values include: "shipped", "in_transit", "out_for_delivery", "delivered", "delivery_failed", or "exception". Implementations may use an enum in code, but the database column is modeled as a string. This value should represent a normalized, platform-wide status, not the raw carrier status text.

carrier_status_code.description:
Optional carrier-specific status code or shorthand representing the raw status supplied by the logistics carrier.

This field is useful for debugging and audit purposes and may contain codes such as "IM" (in movement) or carrier-specific event codes. When not provided, it should be null.

location_description.description:
Optional human-readable description of the shipment's location at the time of the event.

Examples include city names (e.g., "Seoul, KR"), facility names (e.g., "Incheon Hub"), or short free-text descriptions supplied by the carrier. When unavailable, this field should be null.

carrier_raw_message.description:
Optional raw message payload received from the carrier or underlying logistics system for this tracking event.

This may include localized text or free-form notes such as "Arrived at sorting center" or "Recipient not available". It is stored mainly for audit and troubleshooting purposes and may not be displayed directly to end users without sanitization.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this tracking event occurred according to the carrier or internal logistics system, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This is distinct from the system-managed created_at and is intended to reflect the business event time, which may precede the time when the platform received and stored the event.

IShoppingMallInventoryStockStatistics.description:
Aggregated inventory stock level statistics computed from the shopping_mall_inventory_items Prisma model and related catalog entities.

This DTO is designed for dashboards and reporting endpoints that provide a high-level overview of inventory health across the shoppingMall platform. Rather than returning individual inventory item records, it summarizes key quantities and counts such as total on-hand, reserved, and available units, as well as SKU-level counts for different stock states.

It does not map directly to a single database table row but instead represents the result of aggregation queries over shopping_mall_inventory_items (and optionally joins to related models such as shopping_mall_product_skus, shopping_mall_products, and shopping_mall_region_settings).

total_on_hand_units.description:
Total on-hand inventory units across all considered SKUs, aggregated from shopping_mall_inventory_items.

Represents the sum of the on-hand quantity (before reservations) over the filtered inventory scope. This value is always a non-negative integer.

total_reserved_units.description:
Total reserved inventory units across all considered SKUs.

Typically derived from shopping_mall_inventory_items or related reservation tables, this value represents units that have been reserved for orders but not yet shipped and is always a non-negative integer.

total_available_units.description:
Total available inventory units across all considered SKUs, usually calculated as on-hand minus reserved quantities.

This metric represents the number of units that can still be sold, aggregated over the filtered inventory scope. It is expected to be non-negative, though implementations should guard against negative values if data inconsistencies occur.

low_stock_sku_count.description:
Number of SKUs currently considered low-stock within the aggregation scope.

"Low-stock" is defined by business rules or configuration (for example, available quantity below a configurable threshold) and is computed by the reporting query. This count is useful for quickly identifying catalog items that may require replenishment.

out_of_stock_sku_count.description:
Number of SKUs that are currently out of stock within the aggregation scope.

Typically defined as SKUs with zero available units. This count is used to understand the breadth of the catalog that is not currently sellable.

sku_count.description:
Total number of distinct SKUs included in this statistic snapshot.

This may represent all SKUs in the system or only those matching filter criteria such as seller, product category, or region. It allows consumers to interpret other counts and ratios in context.

IShoppingMallInventoryLowStockStatistics.description:
Aggregated low-stock inventory statistics across SKUs and related dimensions for the shopping mall inventory domain.

This DTO represents an analytics projection derived primarily from shopping_mall_inventory_items joined with shopping_mall_product_skus, shopping_mall_products, and potentially configuration tables such as shopping_mall_backorder_settings and shopping_mall_preorder_settings.
It is designed for read-only dashboard and monitoring use cases, helping sellers and platform administrators quickly identify SKUs that are approaching or have crossed their low-stock thresholds.

The structure is intentionally normalized for API consumption: top-level metadata about the computation, followed by an array of per-SKU statistics entries that include identifying fields (such as SKU code and product name), stock quantities and thresholds, and optional grouping dimensions like seller or warehouse.
No write or mutation semantics are expressed through this DTO.

generated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when these low-stock statistics were generated.

This is an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC. Consumers can use this field to understand the freshness of the statistics, cache behavior, and potential drift from real-time inventory levels.

items.description:
List of low-stock statistic entries, each representing the low-stock status for a specific SKU and optional inventory dimensions such as seller, warehouse, or region.

Each entry aggregates information about on-hand, reserved, and available quantities, as well as the threshold that defines what counts as "low stock" for that particular SKU and context.

IShoppingMallInventoryLowStockStatistics.description:
Single low-stock statistics record for a specific SKU and optional inventory dimensions.

This DTO combines SKU-identifying information (such as SKU code and product references) with aggregated inventory quantities and threshold information.
It is designed for use in dashboard tables, alerts, and exports that show which SKUs require replenishment.

All identifiers are expressed as strings; client applications can use them to navigate to SKU or product detail APIs for deeper inspection.

sku_id.description:
Internal identifier of the SKU in shopping_mall_product_skus.

This is typically a UUID or database-generated primary key represented as a string. It uniquely identifies the purchasable variant associated with this low-stock entry.

sku_code.description:
Human-readable SKU code used by sellers and back-office systems to reference this specific product variant.

This is usually unique per seller or catalog context and is suitable for display in UIs and exports.

product_id.description:
Identifier of the product in shopping_mall_products that this SKU belongs to.

This field allows clients to navigate from SKU-level statistics back to the base product entity for additional details such as description and media.

product_name.description:
Display name of the product associated with this SKU.

This field is included to make analytics results usable directly in dashboards without requiring an additional product lookup.

brand_name.description:
Optional brand name associated with the product, derived from shopping_mall_brands when available.

When present, this field helps categorize and filter low-stock entries by brand in monitoring tools.

seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller who owns this SKU and its inventory records.

For seller-facing statistics endpoints, this corresponds to the authenticated seller. For platform-admin endpoints, multiple distinct seller identifiers may appear in the results.

warehouse_id.description:
Identifier of the warehouse or fulfillment location where this inventory item is stored.

This field allows low-stock statistics to be segmented by location, enabling more precise replenishment and logistics planning.

region_code.description:
Optional region or market code associated with this inventory context.

Implementations may derive this from shopping_mall_region_settings or related models to support geographically segmented low-stock views.

on_hand_quantity.description:
Current on-hand quantity for this SKU in the given inventory context.

This represents the number of units physically available in stock, including items that may be reserved but not yet shipped.

reserved_quantity.description:
Quantity of this SKU that is currently reserved or allocated to orders but not yet shipped.

This is typically derived from shopping_mall_inventory_reservations and related order entities, and is used to compute the effectively available quantity.

available_quantity.description:
Effective available quantity that can be promised for new orders.

This is usually computed as on_hand_quantity minus reserved_quantity, but the exact formula may vary by implementation. Consumers should treat this as the primary metric for determining if a SKU is effectively low in stock.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Threshold quantity at or below which this SKU is considered low in stock for this inventory context.

This value may be stored directly on the inventory item or derived from configuration models such as shopping_mall_backorder_settings or shopping_mall_preorder_settings. When available_quantity is less than or equal to this threshold, the SKU should be treated as low-stock in dashboards and alerts.

is_low_stock.description:
Indicates whether this SKU is currently considered low in stock under the configured threshold.

Typically computed as available_quantity <= low_stock_threshold. This flag allows clients to easily filter or highlight entries that require immediate attention.

IShoppingMallInventoryMovementStatistics.description:
Search and filter criteria for retrieving inventory movement statistics derived from shopping_mall_inventory_movements.

This DTO is used as the request body for analytics endpoints that expose history or aggregated metrics of stock movements such as inbound shipments, sales, returns, adjustments, and corrections. It supports filtering by SKU, product, seller, warehouse/location, movement type, and date range, as well as pagination and sorting parameters.

The structure is designed to be expressive but safe: clients can combine multiple filters to narrow down movement statistics while the backend enforces sensible defaults and maximum limits for performance. All identifier fields are strings corresponding to underlying database IDs or codes.

Note that this is a query DTO only and has no direct x-autobe-prisma-schema mapping because it does not directly represent a single Prisma model row.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated results.

If omitted, the implementation should default to the first page. Combined with the limit field, this controls which slice of the paginated statistics is returned.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page.

Implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessive result sizes. If omitted, a sensible default (for example, 20 or 50) should be applied by the backend.

sku_ids.description:
Optional list of SKU identifiers to restrict the statistics to specific variants.

When provided, only inventory movements related to these SKU IDs will be included in the result set. This is typically based on identifiers from shopping_mall_product_skus.

product_ids.description:
Optional list of product identifiers to restrict the statistics to specific catalog products.

When provided, movements for SKUs belonging to these products will be included. This enables product-centric movement analytics even when SKUs are numerous.

seller_ids.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers used to filter movement statistics by owning merchant accounts.

For seller-facing endpoints, the implementation typically constrains results to the authenticated seller regardless of this field. For platform-admin endpoints, this field can be used to focus on specific sellers.

warehouse_ids.description:
Optional list of warehouse or fulfillment location identifiers used to filter movement statistics.

When provided, only inventory movements occurring in these locations (for example, specific warehouses or fulfillment centers) will be considered.

movement_types.description:
Optional list of movement type codes that indicate which kinds of inventory movements should be included.

Typical movement types might include values such as inbound, sale, return, adjustment, or correction. The concrete enumeration is implementation-specific; this field simply carries the selected type codes.

date_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the date/time range for movement statistics, as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

When provided together with date_to, only movements whose timestamps fall within [date_from, date_to] are included. Implementations may enforce limits on the maximum allowed range for performance and cost control.

date_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the date/time range for movement statistics, as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

When provided together with date_from, only movements whose timestamps fall within [date_from, date_to] are included.

sort_by.description:
Optional field specifying which logical column to sort the statistics by.

Typical values might include 'timestamp', 'sku_code', or 'quantity', though the exact set of allowed values is implementation-specific. If omitted, the backend applies a default sort order, often by most recent movement first.

sort_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering the statistics.

Expected values are 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order. If omitted, the backend applies its default direction, which is typically descending for time-based sorts.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOvervie.description:
Aggregated fulfillment dashboard overview for platform administrators.

Represents a denormalized, read-optimized view that consolidates operational metrics from fulfillments, shipments, shipment tracking events, orders, and inventory. Designed specifically to power dashboard cards, charts, and summary tables rather than to mirror any single Prisma model.

Data is read-only and computed from underlying entities such as shopping_mall_fulfillments, shopping_mall_shipments, shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events, shopping_mall_orders, shopping_mall_order_status_events, shopping_mall_inventory_items, shopping_mall_backorder_settings, and shopping_mall_preorder_settings.

totalFulfillments.description: Total number of fulfillment aggregates currently tracked across the platform, regardless of status.

fulfillmentsByStatus.description: Breakdown of fulfillments grouped by current operational status for dashboard charts and tables.

shipmentsByStatus.description: Breakdown of physical shipments grouped by shipping status for high-level shipping workload monitoring.

shipmentsByCarrier.description: Aggregated counts of shipments grouped by carrier to monitor carrier load distribution and potential carrier-specific issues.

slaRiskIndicators.description: Key SLA and delay risk indicators calculated from shipment tracking events and expected delivery windows. Used to highlight potential SLA breaches.

backorderSummary.description: Aggregated metrics describing current backorder load across SKUs and regions.

preorderSummary.description: Aggregated metrics describing current preorder load that will convert into future fulfillment work.

recentThroughput.description: Recent fulfillment and shipment throughput metrics for trend and performance analysis.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when this dashboard overview snapshot was generated on the server.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOvervie.description:
Single bucket entry in the fulfillment status distribution that powers the ShoppingMall fulfillment dashboard.

Each instance represents the number of fulfillment aggregates that currently share the same high‑level operational status at the time the dashboard query is executed. Typical use cases include rendering status distribution charts (for example, stacked bars or doughnut charts) and KPI tiles that highlight operational load.

Values in this structure are derived from the underlying fulfillment and shipment data as a point‑in‑time snapshot. Counts may change quickly as orders progress, so clients must treat the data as volatile and non‑authoritative for auditing purposes.

status.description:
Fulfillment status key that identifies the bucket.

This value is a backend‑defined business status code, typically mapped from an internal enumeration that describes the current lifecycle state of a fulfillment aggregate (for example: `pending`, `ready_to_pack`, `packed`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`). The exact vocabulary may evolve over time or be extended per deployment.

Client applications should not hard‑code assumptions about the full list of possible values. Instead, they should handle unknown or unexpected status codes defensively (for example, by grouping them into an "other" category or displaying the raw code) to remain forward compatible with new status values introduced in the backend.

count.description:
Number of fulfillment aggregates that currently belong to this `status` bucket.

This is a non‑negative integer aggregate computed from the live fulfillment dataset at the time the dashboard query is evaluated. A value of `0` is valid and simply indicates that no fulfillments are in this status at the moment.

Because this is a snapshot value, counts can fluctuate between requests as orders progress through the fulfillment pipeline. The field is intended for monitoring, alerting, and visualization rather than as a source of exact historical audit counts.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOvervie.description:
Single bucket entry in the shipment status distribution used by ShoppingMall logistics and fulfillment dashboards.

Each instance captures how many shipment records currently share the same high‑level shipping or carrier status at the time of the query. These buckets are typically consumed by dashboards to visualize shipment progress, bottlenecks, and carrier performance across the platform.

Values are aggregated from shipment and tracking data as a point‑in‑time snapshot. They are designed for operational monitoring and reporting and should not be treated as immutable or historical totals.

status.description:
Shipment status key that identifies the bucket.

The value is a backend‑defined shipping lifecycle status code, often mapped from carrier events or internal logistics state (for example: `pending`, `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `returned`). Deployments may introduce additional status codes or refine existing ones as carrier integrations evolve.

Client applications must assume that the set of possible values is open‑ended and should handle unknown or newly introduced status codes gracefully, for example by displaying the raw code or grouping them into an "other" bucket in charts.

count.description:
Number of shipment records that currently belong to this `status` bucket.

This is a non‑negative integer that represents an aggregated count of shipments in the given status at the moment the dashboard or reporting query is executed. A value of `0` is valid and simply indicates that no shipments are presently in that status.

Because this value is recalculated on each request, it may vary over time as shipments progress through their lifecycle or as new events are ingested from carriers. It is intended for monitoring and analytical views rather than for exact historical reconciliation.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOvervie.description: Aggregated shipment metrics grouped by carrier.

carrierCode.description: Normalized carrier code used internally to identify the shipping carrier (for example: `UPS`, `FEDEX`, `DHL`, `LOCAL_COURIER`).

shipmentCount.description: Number of shipments currently associated with this carrier.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOvervie.description:
SLA and delay risk indicator derived from shipment tracking events and order status history.

Each indicator represents a specific slice of operational risk, such as shipments approaching their promised delivery deadline or fulfillments stuck in a particular status beyond a threshold.

code.description: Machine-friendly risk code that identifies the indicator type (for example: `shipments_at_risk`, `overdue_deliveries`, `fulfillments_stuck_in_picking`).

label.description: Human-readable label suitable for display in dashboard widgets and charts.

count.description: Number of items (fulfillments, shipments, or orders) currently affected by this risk condition.

trend.description: Optional qualitative trend indicator for this risk metric (for example: `up`, `down`, `stable`). May be omitted or left as a neutral value when trend data is not computed.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOvervie.description:
Aggregated metrics about the current backorder load across inventory items for the ShoppingMall fulfillment dashboard.

This analytics DTO summarizes how many distinct SKUs and how many total units are currently backordered across the catalog, based on inventory items, reservations, and order/fulfillment state. It is optimized for read‑only dashboard consumption rather than direct persistence, and is typically computed from inventory and order data over a configurable snapshot window.

In addition to global metrics, this model can optionally expose regional segmentation through the `regions` collection. When present, regional buckets allow platform administrators and operations teams to quickly see which markets or logistics regions are under the highest backorder pressure and to prioritize remediation actions such as inventory rebalancing or supply chain escalations.

totalBackorderSkus.description:
Number of distinct SKUs that currently have at least one backordered unit in the analysis scope.

This count aggregates over all relevant inventory items and orders, and treats each SKU as a single entry regardless of how many orders or inventory records are involved. It is used in dashboards to indicate the breadth of the backorder problem across the catalog rather than the magnitude of units involved.

totalBackorderUnits.description:
Total number of individual units across all SKUs that are currently backordered in the analysis scope.

This value represents the sum of all backordered quantities over every affected SKU and order line included in the snapshot. It is typically used as a primary KPI for understanding the overall volume of unmet demand that is waiting on replenishment or fulfillment actions.

regions.description:
Optional list of per‑region backorder aggregation buckets used when the dashboard segments operational load geographically.

Each entry in this array corresponds to a single region or market and provides backorder counts localized to that region. When omitted or empty, the caller is either not interested in regional breakdowns or the underlying data source cannot reliably attribute backorders to specific regions.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOvervie.description:
Backorder metrics for a specific region or market used in geographic segmentation of fulfillment load.

This DTO represents a single aggregation bucket within the fulfillment dashboard that groups backorder counts by a region identifier. It is typically produced as part of a larger `IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOverview.IBackorderSummary` response and allows visualizations such as heatmaps or per‑region bar charts for operational analysis.

Regional buckets are read‑only analytics views that help administrators understand where demand is outpacing supply, taking into account region configuration, shipping zones, and inventory distribution strategies configured elsewhere in the platform.

regionCode.description:
Region or market code used in the platform’s region configuration (for example: `KR`, `US`, `EU-NORTH`).

The value should match a configured region identifier from the region settings domain so that the dashboard can consistently label and group backorder metrics by the same codes used in other operational and reporting views.

backorderSkuCount.description:
Number of distinct SKUs with one or more backordered units in this specific region.

This metric mirrors the semantics of `totalBackorderSkus` from the parent summary but is scoped to a single region identified by `regionCode`. It is commonly used to compare how widely the backorder issue affects the assortment in each market.

backorderUnitCount.description:
Total number of units currently backordered in this specific region.

This metric mirrors the semantics of `totalBackorderUnits` from the parent summary but is scoped to a single region identified by `regionCode`. It indicates the magnitude of backordered demand in the region and can be used alongside other KPIs such as fulfillment throughput and inventory coverage to prioritize interventions.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOvervie.description:
Aggregated metrics about current preorder demand across inventory items in the ShoppingMall fulfillment domain.

This DTO is designed for use in administrative and operational dashboards where teams need a quick snapshot of how much of the current workload is tied to preorder activity rather than immediately shippable stock. It focuses on the breadth and depth of preorder demand at a point in time, independent of any single order or customer.

The values returned in this structure are typically computed by analytics queries over order lines and inventory settings. They may be further scoped by higher‑level filters such as seller, region, catalog segment, or time window, which are defined by the parent request or surrounding response envelope rather than by this object itself.

totalPreorderSkus.description:
Total number of distinct SKUs that currently have at least one unit on preorder.

Each counted SKU must have non‑zero preorder demand at the time of calculation, regardless of how many units are involved. This metric helps operators understand how widely preorder demand is spread across the catalog, which can influence assortment decisions, marketing focus, and inbound inventory planning.

totalPreorderUnits.description:
Total number of units currently on preorder across all SKUs included in the aggregation.

This value is the sum of preorder quantities for every SKU that is eligible for preorder within the scope of the calculation. It gives a sense of the depth of backlog that will need to be fulfilled once inventory becomes available, and is often used for capacity planning, supplier communication, and monitoring whether preorder volume remains within acceptable operational thresholds.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentDashboardOvervie.description:
Recent throughput metrics summarizing how many fulfillments and shipments have been processed in a specific time window within the ShoppingMall fulfillment and logistics pipeline.

This DTO is intended for use in dashboards and monitoring views that compare short‑term operational performance against historical baselines. By looking at completed fulfillments and dispatched shipments in a bounded window, operators can quickly assess whether the system is processing orders at expected rates, falling behind, or experiencing unusual spikes in volume.

The exact time window and any additional filters (such as seller, region, shipping service level, or sales channel) are defined by the caller or outer analytics context. This object focuses purely on representing the aggregated counts for that window in a concise, dashboard‑friendly form.

windowLabel.description:
Human‑readable label that identifies the time window over which throughput metrics were calculated.

Common examples include semantic labels such as `last_24_hours`, `last_7_days`, or `today`, as well as more explicit labels derived from a specific date range (for example, `2025-01-01_to_2025-01-07`). The label is meant for display in dashboards and reports, while the precise time boundaries and filters are typically carried elsewhere in the analytics request or surrounding response.

fulfillmentsCompleted.description:
Number of fulfillment aggregates that reached a completed state within the referenced time window.

A single fulfillment aggregate may cover one or more order lines, depending on how the fulfillment engine groups work. This count reflects how many such aggregates completed all required processing steps (for example, picked, packed, and ready for shipment or delivered) during the window, optionally constrained by dimensions such as seller, region, or channel defined in the broader analytics query.

shipmentsDispatched.description:
Number of shipments that were dispatched or handed off to a carrier within the same time window.

Each counted shipment represents a physical or logical shipment unit that has transitioned into an in‑transit state (for example, handed over to a carrier, moved out of the fulfillment center, or otherwise marked as dispatched). This metric complements `fulfillmentsCompleted` by focusing on outbound logistics activity and is commonly used to track whether shipping operations keep pace with order fulfillment.

IShoppingMallInventoryAndFulfillmentSear.description:
Search criteria, filters, pagination, and sorting options for querying combined inventory and fulfillment data.

This DTO encapsulates the parameters sent by platform administrators when searching across inventory items, SKUs/products, fulfillments, shipments, and related operational data. It is optimized for flexible back-office search and does not map directly to a single Prisma model.

page.description: Page number for paginated search results. Starts from 1 when provided.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return per page. The backend should enforce an upper bound to protect system performance.

skuCode.description: Exact SKU code used to filter results to a specific product SKU, when known.

productCode.description: Product-level code used to filter results to all SKUs belonging to a specific product.

fulfillmentStatus.description: Filter for a single fulfillment status (for example: `pending`, `ready_to_pack`, `packed`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `cancelled`).

shipmentStatus.description: Filter for a single shipment status (for example: `pending`, `label_created`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `returned`).

regionCode.description: Region or market code as defined in region configuration tables, used to scope results geographically (for example: `KR`, `US`, `EU-NORTH`).

warehouseCode.description: Identifier of a warehouse or fulfillment center used to scope inventory and fulfillment records to a specific physical location.

backorderOnly.description: If true, restricts results to inventory and fulfillment records associated with backordered demand.

preorderOnly.description: If true, restricts results to inventory and fulfillment records associated with preorder demand.

createdFrom.description: Start of the creation date range filter applied to underlying entities such as inventory items, fulfillments, or shipments.

createdTo.description: End of the creation date range filter applied to underlying entities such as inventory items, fulfillments, or shipments.

sortField.description: Field name used for sorting search results (for example: `skuCode`, `availableQuantity`, `reservedQuantity`, `latestFulfillmentCreatedAt`).

sortDirection.description: Sort direction applied to the chosen sort field. Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order.

IShoppingMallInventoryAndFulfillmentSear.description:
Summary DTO for combined inventory and fulfillment search results in the shopping mall platform.

Represents a single summarized row returned from inventory and fulfillment search operations, combining key inventory state, reservation, and fulfillment/shipping information for a specific product SKU in a specific context.

Optimized for list and dashboard views where operators or admins quickly scan stock health, reservation pressure, and fulfillment status without needing full detail records.

sku_id.description: Unique identifier of the SKU whose inventory and fulfillment state is being summarized.

sku_code.description: Human-readable code of the SKU (for example a variant code or SKU code) used in operator tools to identify the sellable variant.

product_id.description: Unique identifier of the product that owns this SKU.

product_name.description:
Display name of the product that this SKU belongs to.

Used for listing and search result displays so that operators can quickly recognize the item without fetching full product detail.

seller_id.description: Unique identifier of the seller that owns the inventory for this SKU.

seller_name.description: Display name of the seller that owns this inventory and fulfills this SKU.

region_code.description:
Business region code representing the market or geographic area where this inventory and fulfillment state applies.

Examples include country codes, market region identifiers, or logistics region codes used in shipping configuration.

total_stock_quantity.description:
Total on-hand stock quantity for this SKU in the given region across all warehouses and inventory locations.

Represents the sum of all positive inventory quantities before reservations are applied.

reserved_quantity.description:
Total quantity currently reserved for active orders, pre-orders, or checkouts in progress.

Used to understand how much inventory is already committed and not available for new orders.

available_quantity.description:
Effective available inventory quantity for new orders after subtracting reservations from total stock.

This value is typically computed as `total_stock_quantity - reserved_quantity` and reflects the quantity that can be safely sold.

backorder_allowed.description:
Indicates whether backorders are allowed for this SKU according to the applicable backorder settings.

When true, orders may still be accepted even if available quantity is zero or negative, subject to business rules.

preorder_active.description:
Indicates whether this SKU is currently in a preorder phase according to preorder configuration.

When true, customers may place orders that will be fulfilled starting from the configured release date.

earliest_inbound_date.description:
Nullable field indicating the earliest expected inbound inventory date for this SKU in the given region.

When non-null, this is an ISO 8601 timestamp that allows operators to estimate when additional stock is expected to arrive based on purchase orders, transfers, or production schedules.

When null, there is no confirmed inbound date available.

open_fulfillment_count.description:
Number of open fulfillment records for this SKU that are not yet completed.

This typically counts fulfillments in states such as picking, packing, or ready-to-ship.

in_transit_shipment_count.description:
Number of shipments that currently contain this SKU in an in-transit state.

Used by operations and support teams to understand how many units are already on the way to customers.

last_fulfilled_at.description:
Nullable field indicating the most recent time this SKU was successfully fulfilled (for example, delivered or otherwise completed) in the given region.

When non-null, this is an ISO 8601 timestamp used for operational monitoring and reporting.

When null, the SKU has not yet been fulfilled or the information is not available.

last_stock_movement_at.description:
Nullable field representing the timestamp of the latest inventory movement that affected this SKU in the given region.

This may reflect stock increases, decreases, adjustments, or warehouse transfers and is expressed as an ISO 8601 timestamp when present.

When null, no inventory movement has been recorded yet or the information is unavailable.

status.description:
High-level derived status that summarizes the current inventory and fulfillment health for this SKU.

Typical values might include application-specific statuses such as "healthy", "low_stock", "out_of_stock", "backorder", or "preorder".

The exact value set is determined by business rules and is not enforced as an enum here to allow configuration.

IShoppingMallProductReview.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for querying product reviews stored in the shopping_mall_product_reviews table.

This DTO is used by multiple PATCH collection endpoints that search reviews globally or scoped by product or SKU. It encapsulates all client-controllable query options such as pagination, sorting, rating filters, date windows, and simple content flags, without including any identity or system-managed fields from the underlying Prisma model.

page.description: 1-based page index to retrieve when paginating through product reviews. Must be a positive integer; defaults are applied by the server when omitted.

limit.description: Maximum number of review summaries to return in a single page of results. The server may enforce an upper bound (for example, 100) to protect performance.

oneOf.description:
Sorting key used to order the review results.
- "createdAt": sort by review creation time (default, most recent first)
- "rating": sort by numeric rating value
- "helpfulness": sort by a precomputed helpfulness or relevance score if available.

Sorting key used to order the review results.
- "createdAt": sort by review creation time (default, most recent first)
- "rating": sort by numeric rating value
- "helpfulness": sort by a precomputed helpfulness or relevance score if available.

Sorting key used to order the review results.
- "createdAt": sort by review creation time (default, most recent first)
- "rating": sort by numeric rating value
- "helpfulness": sort by a precomputed helpfulness or relevance score if available.

orderBy.description:
Sorting key used to order the review results.
- "createdAt": sort by review creation time (default, most recent first)
- "rating": sort by numeric rating value
- "helpfulness": sort by a precomputed helpfulness or relevance score if available.

oneOf.description:
Direction for sorting the result set when combined with orderBy.
- "asc": ascending order
- "desc": descending order (default for most list views).

Direction for sorting the result set when combined with orderBy.
- "asc": ascending order
- "desc": descending order (default for most list views).

orderDirection.description:
Direction for sorting the result set when combined with orderBy.
- "asc": ascending order
- "desc": descending order (default for most list views).

minRating.description: Minimum star rating (inclusive) used to filter reviews. Must be between 1 and 5, matching the allowed rating range for reviews.

maxRating.description: Maximum star rating (inclusive) used to filter reviews. Must be between 1 and 5 and greater than or equal to minRating when both are provided.

fromCreatedAt.description: Lower bound (inclusive) for the review creation timestamp filter, in ISO 8601 date-time format. Only reviews created at or after this instant are included.

toCreatedAt.description: Upper bound (inclusive) for the review creation timestamp filter, in ISO 8601 date-time format. Only reviews created at or before this instant are included.

hasMedia.description: When true, restricts results to reviews that include associated media such as images or videos. When false, restricts to text-only reviews. When omitted, both types may be returned.

verifiedPurchaseOnly.description: When true, returns only reviews marked as verified purchases (for example, reviews written by customers who actually bought the product or SKU in a completed order). When false or omitted, both verified and unverified reviews may be included, subject to platform policy.

oneOf.description:
High-level moderation or visibility status of reviews to include in the search.
- "published": reviews currently visible to shoppers
- "pending": reviews awaiting moderation
- "hidden": reviews that are not publicly visible but may be accessible to privileged actors.

High-level moderation or visibility status of reviews to include in the search.
- "published": reviews currently visible to shoppers
- "pending": reviews awaiting moderation
- "hidden": reviews that are not publicly visible but may be accessible to privileged actors.
