- "published": reviews currently visible to shoppers
- "pending": reviews awaiting moderation
- "hidden": reviews that are not publicly visible but may be accessible to privileged actors.

status.description:
High-level moderation or visibility status of reviews to include in the search.
- "published": reviews currently visible to shoppers
- "pending": reviews awaiting moderation
- "hidden": reviews that are not publicly visible but may be accessible to privileged actors.

IShoppingMallProductReview.description:
Detailed representation of a single customer-authored product review from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table.

This DTO models the canonical review entity exposed by the ShoppingMall API. It includes the review identifier, rating, textual content, visibility and moderation-related fields, and association summaries for the related product and optional SKU.

Sensitive security or privacy-critical data such as internal customer identifiers, passwords, tokens, soft-delete flags, or internal-only moderation metadata are never exposed through this DTO. Administrative tools that require direct customer linkage should rely on dedicated admin-facing DTOs and endpoints instead of this public-facing representation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product review in the shopping_mall_product_reviews table.

This value is a server-generated UUID that uniquely distinguishes the review record and can be used in URLs and API calls that operate on a single review resource.

product.description:
Summary representation of the product being reviewed.

This association replaces the raw `product_id` foreign key and provides the essential catalog context (such as product name and code) needed to render review information in a single, atomic response without requiring an additional product lookup.

sku.description:
Optional summary of the specific SKU variant being reviewed.

When non-null, this association represents the exact purchasable variant (for example, size or color) that the review refers to, replacing the raw `product_sku_id` foreign key. When null, the review is considered to apply to the product in general rather than a particular SKU.

rating.description:
Star rating value given by the customer, within the allowed rating range (typically 1 to 5 inclusive).

This numeric score is used in product detail displays, review lists, and aggregate rating calculations for products and SKUs.

title.description:
Optional short title or headline of the review provided by the customer.

This field maps to the nullable `title` column on `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. It is intended for brief summary text shown in list views above or alongside the main review body, helping shoppers quickly understand the overall sentiment.

When null, no separate title was provided and UIs should rely solely on the body content when rendering the review.

body.description:
Optional main textual content of the review, containing the customer's detailed feedback about the product or SKU.

This property corresponds to the nullable `body` column on `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. A non-empty string contains the free-form review text, while a null value indicates that the customer submitted a rating (and possibly a title) without a full-text body.

The free-form text may be length-limited according to platform policy and is subject to moderation and content rules such as prohibited expressions and legal compliance requirements.

hasMedia.description:
Indicates whether this review is associated with one or more media attachments such as images or videos.

The media resources themselves are not embedded in this DTO and should be retrieved via dedicated media endpoints or related DTOs when needed for richer displays.

verifiedPurchase.description:
True if the review has been verified as originating from a customer who purchased the product or SKU in a qualifying order.

This flag allows UIs to highlight "verified purchase" badges and supports downstream analytics that treat verified reviews differently from unverified ones.

oneOf.description:
Current moderation or visibility status of the review.
- "published": visible to eligible shoppers
- "pending": awaiting moderation or review
- "hidden": not visible to general shoppers due to moderation decisions or policy rules.

Current moderation or visibility status of the review.
- "published": visible to eligible shoppers
- "pending": awaiting moderation or review
- "hidden": not visible to general shoppers due to moderation decisions or policy rules.

Current moderation or visibility status of the review.
- "published": visible to eligible shoppers
- "pending": awaiting moderation or review
- "hidden": not visible to general shoppers due to moderation decisions or policy rules.

status.description:
Current moderation or lifecycle status of the review from the platform's perspective.

Typical values include:
- "published": visible to eligible shoppers
- "pending": awaiting moderation or review
- "hidden": not visible to general shoppers due to moderation decisions or policy rules.

This status is derived from the underlying `status` column on `shopping_mall_product_reviews` and is used together with `isPublic` to control which reviews appear in public listings.

isPublic.description:
Indicates whether the review is currently eligible to be shown in public review lists.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `is_public` column on `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. While `status` models the higher-level moderation and workflow state, `isPublic` represents the effective public visibility flag used for filtering in read APIs.

Typical implementations derive `isPublic` from the combination of `status` and policy logic and then persist it in the database for efficient querying.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the review was first created, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value is derived from the corresponding `created_at` column in the shopping_mall_product_reviews table and is used for sorting, filtering, and displaying review age in user interfaces.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the review was last updated, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This field reflects the most recent modification to rating, content, or status fields and allows clients to show when a review was edited compared to its original creation time. It is mapped from the non-nullable `updated_at` column on `shopping_mall_product_reviews` and is therefore always present for persisted reviews.

IShoppingMallProductReview.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for customer-authored product reviews in the shoppingMall catalog.

This schema represents the client-provided payload required to insert a new row into the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table. It captures the business data that a customer can explicitly control when writing a review, such as the star rating, optional title, and free-form body text.

Identity, authorship, and audit fields like `customer_id`, `product_id`, `product_sku_id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are intentionally excluded from this DTO because they are derived from the authenticated customer context, URL path parameters, and server-side logic rather than being accepted from the client.

The DTO is designed to work with endpoints where the product and optional SKU are identified via path parameters (for example, POST `/shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/reviews` and POST `/shoppingMall/customer/products/{productId}/skus/{skuId}/reviews`). In those cases, the server MUST treat the path parameters as the sole sources of truth for product and SKU context and MUST NOT expect or accept duplicate foreign key fields in the request body.

This contract prevents clients from attempting to redirect reviews to a different product or SKU than indicated in the URL while still allowing atomic creation of the review content itself in a single API call.

rating.description:
Star rating value provided by the customer.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable `rating` column on `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. It typically uses a fixed integer scale from 1 to 5, where lower values represent worse experiences and higher values represent better experiences.

The service layer must validate that the rating falls within the configured bounds before creating the review and may normalize or round values according to business rules for aggregate computations. Clients cannot bypass these constraints and any out-of-range value must result in a validation error.

title.description:
Optional short summary or headline for the review.

This field maps to the nullable `title` column and provides a concise description of the customer's sentiment. It is commonly displayed in review list views and product detail sections where space is limited.

When provided, the title should respect reasonable length limits to avoid layout issues. When omitted or null, UIs should rely solely on the body content for display. Content moderation and profanity filtering rules defined by the platform MUST be applied server-side to this field before persistence.

body.description:
Optional free-form text comment describing the customer experience.

This property corresponds to the nullable `body` column. It allows customers to explain their rating, highlight strengths and weaknesses, or provide contextual information about their purchase and usage.

Implementations should enforce maximum length constraints and apply content rules such as profanity filtering or disallowed phrase detection according to platform review policies. Server-side validation is responsible for preventing injection of malicious content or markup into this field.

IShoppingMallProductReview.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying existing customer-authored product reviews in the shoppingMall catalog.

This schema represents the set of fields that a client is allowed to change on an existing `shopping_mall_product_reviews` row. It is used as the request body for review edit operations across customer, seller, and admin contexts.

Immutable fields such as `id`, `customer_id`, `product_id`, `product_sku_id`, `created_at`, and `deleted_at` are intentionally excluded to preserve referential integrity and historical accuracy. Only the rating and content-related properties are exposed for editing, and all properties are optional to support partial updates.

Business logic must additionally enforce higher-level rules such as edit windows, moderation state restrictions, and authorization checks based on the authenticated actor type and ownership of the review.

rating.description:
Optional updated star rating value for the review.

When present, this field replaces the existing `rating` value on the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` row. It must still respect the allowed integer scale, typically from 1 to 5 inclusive.

If omitted, the rating remains unchanged. When updated, downstream systems may need to recalculate aggregate statistics in tables such as `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates`.

title.description:
Optional updated short summary or headline for the review.

This field updates the `title` column and can be used to refine or correct the review headline. Providing null explicitly clears an existing title, whereas omitting the property leaves the current title unchanged.

Length limits and content rules applied at creation time should be re-applied when updating to maintain consistency across reviews.

body.description:
Optional updated free-form text describing the customer experience.

This property modifies the `body` column of the review. A non-empty string replaces the existing body text, while an explicit null clears it. When the property is omitted, the existing body remains unchanged.

The service must enforce the same validation rules as on creation, including maximum length enforcement and any configured content filtering policies.

is_public.description:
Optional override of the public visibility flag for the review.

This field corresponds to the `is_public` column on `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. It is included in the update DTO to support workflows where visibility can be toggled, such as moderation actions or customer-driven hiding of their own reviews.

When provided, a boolean value explicitly sets the visibility, while null may be interpreted by the service as "no change" or "reset to policy default" depending on implementation. Clients should follow the API documentation for the exact semantics in their environment.

IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.IReques.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for listing product review reports (abuse flags) associated with a specific product review in the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used as the request body for the platform admin reports index endpoint (PATCH /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/reviews/{reviewId}/reports). It allows admin and moderation tools to specify page size, page index, sort options, and filtering criteria such as reporter type, reason code, status, and created-at ranges.

All fields are optional, enabling callers to combine only the filters they need. Pagination parameters are bounded to prevent excessive load, and filter fields are designed to map directly to columns in the shopping_mall_product_review_reports table (such as reporter_actor_type, reason_code, and created_at) without exposing internal-only implementation details.

page.description:
1-based page index for the paginated result set.

Defaults to 1 when omitted. Platform admin UIs should increment this value when requesting subsequent pages of report results so that they can page through large sets of reports tied to a single review.

limit.description:
Maximum number of report records to return in a single page.

Defaults to a reasonable page size (for example, 20) when omitted. A hard upper bound of 100 is enforced to protect the system from excessively large pages and to keep response payload sizes manageable for admin consoles.

sortField.description:
Logical field name to sort the reports by within the shopping_mall_product_review_reports table.

Typical values include domain-specific fields such as createdAt or reasonCode. Implementations must validate and whitelist acceptable values to prevent misuse or injection attempts, and should fall back to a sensible default (for example, createdAt descending) when an unsupported field is requested.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the specified sortField in ascending order.

Use this value when you want earlier or smaller values first, such as oldest reports at the top of the list.

Sort direction applied to the specified sortField in descending order.

Use this value when you want later or larger values first, such as newest reports at the top of the list.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction applied to the specified sortField.

Use "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. If omitted, the backend should apply its default ordering, typically descending by creation time so that the most recent reports appear first.

reporterType.description:
Optional filter indicating the type of actor who submitted the report.

Typical values may include customer, seller, platformAdmin, or automatedSystem, mirroring the reporter_actor_type column in shopping_mall_product_review_reports.

When provided, only reports created by the specified actor category are returned, which helps moderation staff focus on particular sources such as customer complaints or automated detection systems.

reasonCode.description:
Optional filter for a specific structured reason code describing why the product review was reported.

This field corresponds to the reason_code column in shopping_mall_product_review_reports and accepts the same business-defined codes that are exposed in the IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.reasonCode property.

When set, only reports whose reason code matches the provided value are returned, allowing moderation tools to focus on particular problem categories such as spam or offensive_content.

status.description:
Optional filter for the moderation or handling status of the report.

Typical values include states such as pending, in_review, accepted, rejected, or dismissed, depending on the moderation workflow defined for the platform. The exact set of statuses is enforced by service-layer validation rather than as an enum here.

When provided, only reports whose status matches the specified value are included in the result set, enabling administrators to focus on unresolved or recently closed reports.

createdFrom.description:
Optional lower bound for the report creation timestamp, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time value.

When provided and non-null, only reports with created_at greater than or equal to this value are returned. Use null or omit the field entirely to disable this lower bound filter.

This is useful for limiting queries to recent reports during investigations or when paging through historical data in chronological windows.

createdTo.description:
Optional upper bound for the report creation timestamp, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time value.

When provided and non-null, only reports with created_at less than or equal to this value are returned. Use null or omit the field entirely to disable this upper bound filter.

Combined with createdFrom, this allows moderation tools to constrain queries to a particular time window, such as a specific day, week, or incident period.

IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.description:
Detailed representation of a single product review report (abuse flag) in the ShoppingMall platform.

Instances of this DTO correspond to rows in the shopping_mall_product_review_reports Prisma model, which stores reports raised against product reviews in shopping_mall_product_reviews. Each report captures which review was reported, who reported it, why it was reported, and when it was created or last updated.

This type is used in admin and moderation contexts where a platform administrator inspects report details for a specific product review. It exposes identifying fields, the structured reason code, optional free-text description, reporter identity references, audit timestamps, an optional soft-delete timestamp, and—when available—a lightweight summary of the associated product review to avoid extra lookup calls in moderation tools.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product review report, corresponding to the primary key of the shopping_mall_product_review_reports table.

This value is generated by the backend when the report is created and remains immutable for the lifetime of the record.

It is used as the stable handle for referencing this report from other APIs and internal workflows.

reviewId.description:
Identifier of the product review in shopping_mall_product_reviews that this report targets.

This field is the direct foreign key from shopping_mall_product_review_reports to shopping_mall_product_reviews and is used to enforce referential integrity at the database level.

In most client and moderation contexts, this value is primarily useful for deep-linking, debugging, or cross-checking, while the `review` association provides richer display information.

reasonCode.description:
Machine-readable reason or category code describing why the product review was reported (for example, spam, offensive_content, or false_information).

This value maps to the reason_code column in the shopping_mall_product_review_reports model and is driven by business configuration that defines the allowed set of reason codes.

Moderation tooling and analytics use this code to categorize reports, generate statistics, and enforce policy-specific workflows.

description.description:
Optional free-text explanation provided by the reporter describing the issue with the product review in more detail.

This value reflects the comment column in the shopping_mall_product_review_reports model and may contain user-supplied content with additional context, such as specific sentences, links, or circumstances surrounding the problem.

Because it is user-generated and nullable in the database, admin and moderation UIs should treat this property as optional, rendering it only when present and applying any necessary escaping or content-safety measures.

reporterType.description:
Type of actor who submitted the report, such as customer, seller, platformAdmin, or automatedSystem.

This field is a read-only projection of the reporter_actor_type column in the shopping_mall_product_review_reports model and determines how `reporterId` should be interpreted at the application layer.

It enables moderation and security tools to distinguish between different reporter categories when performing analytics, triage, or escalation flows.

reporterId.description:
Identifier of the actor who submitted the report.

The specific table and entity this ID refers to is determined by `reporterType` and may be a customer, seller, platform administrator, or system identity record.

This value is exposed primarily for internal tooling, audit trails, and deep-linking into per-actor views rather than for public-facing APIs.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the report was created in the system, recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value is mapped from the created_at column in the shopping_mall_product_review_reports model and provides the canonical creation time for the report.

It is commonly used for sorting reports chronologically, building timelines in moderation tools, and applying time-based retention or archival policies.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp when the report was last updated in the system, recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value reflects the updated_at column of the shopping_mall_product_review_reports model and is updated whenever mutable fields such as status, moderator notes, or resolution attributes are changed.

It allows moderators and auditors to track the most recent handling activity for each report.

deletedAt.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when the report was soft-deleted or logically cleared, recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format.

This value mirrors the deleted_at column in the shopping_mall_product_review_reports model. While it is null for active reports, it is set when a report is logically removed from normal workflows—for example, after being merged, withdrawn, or purged according to retention policies.

Moderation and audit tooling can use this field to distinguish active reports from those that have been cleared or archived without physically deleting the underlying row.

review.description:
Lightweight summary of the product review that this report targets.

When populated, this association allows moderation and administrative tools to display key information about the underlying review—such as rating, a short excerpt, and product context—without issuing a separate API call to fetch the review.

The summary is read-only, derived from the shopping_mall_product_reviews table, and is intended solely for contextual display alongside the report; it does not replace full review retrieval when deep inspection is required.

IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.ICreate.description:
Data required for a customer to submit a new abuse or issue report against a specific product review.

This DTO is used by the customer‑scoped POST /shoppingMall/customer/reviews/{reviewId}/reports endpoint to create a new row in the shopping_mall_product_review_reports table. It contains only business‑level fields that the reporter can control, such as the reason category and optional free‑text explanation.

System‑managed fields like the report identifier, creation timestamps, reporter identity, and foreign key to the target product review are injected by the backend from the path parameter and authenticated session, and therefore are not accepted from the client in this request body.

reason_code.description:
Machine‑processable code representing the primary category of the report.

Typical examples include values such as "spam", "abusive", "offensive_language", "hate_speech", "false_information", or other platform‑defined reason identifiers. The concrete allowed values are defined by business configuration and enforced at the service layer.

Clients should select one of the supported reason codes exposed via UI or configuration APIs, and must not attempt to send arbitrary free‑form text here.

description.description:
Optional free‑text explanation provided by the reporter describing why the product review is being reported.

This field is intended for human moderators and may contain details that supplement the structured reason_code, such as specific sentences, context around the incident, or additional clarifications.

The platform may impose length limits or content validation rules (for example maximum characters or profanity filtering) at the service layer.

metadata.description:
Optional structured metadata related to the report, represented as an arbitrary JSON object.

This can be used to store client‑side or feature‑specific details that help moderation and automated pipelines, such as UI context flags, locale, or additional classification hints. The exact shape of this object is not constrained at the schema level and is treated as opaque key‑value data by the backend.

If not needed, this field can be omitted from the request body.

IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.IUpdate.description:
Fields that a platform administrator can modify on an existing product review report.

This DTO is used by the admin‑scoped PUT /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/reviews/{reviewId}/reports/{reportId} endpoint to update rows in the shopping_mall_product_review_reports table. It models only business‑updatable columns such as status, moderator notes, and classification fields.

Immutable identifiers (such as the report primary key, foreign keys to the product review or reporter, and creation metadata) are not present here and cannot be changed through this DTO. All properties are optional to support partial updates; the service layer will update only the fields that are provided.

status.description:
Moderation status of the report within the review handling workflow.

Typical values include states such as "pending", "in_review", "accepted", "rejected", or other platform‑defined statuses. The exact enumeration and allowed transitions are enforced by the business logic and may be described in the Prisma comments.

Updating this field allows moderators to progress the report through the abuse handling lifecycle.

moderator_note.description:
Optional internal note left by the moderator or administrator explaining the decision or providing additional context about how the report was handled.

This note is not intended for the original reporter or the public, but rather for internal audit and future reviewers. The platform may enforce maximum length or content rules at the service layer.

resolution_category.description:
Optional structured category that classifies how the report was resolved.

Examples might include values such as "no_action", "review_removed", "review_edited", "user_warned", or other platform‑specific resolution outcomes. This field helps with analytics and policy compliance reporting.

If omitted, the resolution category remains unchanged.

IShoppingMallProductReviewModerationEven.description:
Filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria for querying moderation events associated with a specific product review in shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events.

Used by platform administrators to retrieve a paginated and filterable history of moderation actions for a given product review. Supports time range filters, action-type filters, actor filters, free-text search over moderator notes, and pagination/sorting controls.

page.description: Page index for pagination, starting from 1. Determines which slice of the moderation event history is returned.

limit.description: Maximum number of moderation event records to return per page. Used for pagination control to prevent excessively large responses.

sort_by.description: Field name used to sort moderation events in the result set. Typical values include created_at or action, depending on business requirements.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for the moderation events, either ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Commonly used with created_at to show newest or oldest events first.
Sort direction for the moderation events, either ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Commonly used with created_at to show newest or oldest events first.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction for the moderation events, either ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Commonly used with created_at to show newest or oldest events first.

from.description:
Lower bound of the moderation event creation timestamp filter.

When provided, only moderation events whose created_at is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are included in the results. When set to null, no lower bound is applied and events from the earliest recorded time may be returned.

to.description:
Upper bound of the moderation event creation timestamp filter.

When provided, only moderation events whose created_at is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time value are included in the results. When set to null, no upper bound is applied and events up to the most recent record may be returned.

items.description: Moderation action type to filter by, such as approve, hide, reject, or edit. The concrete set of values must align with the action enum defined in the Prisma model.

action_types.description: Optional list of moderation action types to include in the result set. When provided, only events whose action type is in this list are returned.

items.description: Identifier of the actor (typically a platform administrator or automated system identity) that performed a moderation action.

actor_ids.description: Optional list of actor identifiers to filter by. When provided, only events performed by one of the specified actors are included.

search.description: Free-text search term applied over moderator notes or other text fields to help find moderation events matching specific reasoning or comments.

IShoppingMallProductReviewModerationEven.description:
Detailed representation of a single moderation event for a product review in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO maps directly to a row in the `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` Prisma model, which stores immutable records of moderation actions applied to `shopping_mall_product_reviews`. Each event captures which review was moderated, what status change occurred, who performed the action, why it was taken, and when it was recorded.

It is exposed only through read-only, administrator‑restricted endpoints to support audit, compliance, and moderation tooling, and does not contain any password, token, or other sensitive authentication data.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the moderation event record in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`.

This value is generated automatically by the system and acts as the primary key for the moderation event row. It is used by detail endpoints and internal services whenever a specific moderation event must be retrieved or referenced unambiguously.

review_id.description:
Identifier of the product review in `shopping_mall_product_reviews` to which this moderation event belongs.

This foreign key binds the moderation event to a single review, ensuring that the event is always interpreted in the correct context. It enables timelines of moderation history to be rendered per review and prevents accidental cross-review data leakage when querying events.

actor_id.description:
Identifier of the actor who performed the moderation action.

For manual moderation flows, this typically corresponds to the platform administrator identifier that is persisted in the `platformadmin_id` column of the `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` table. For automated or system-initiated actions, it may reference a special system identity used solely for audit and traceability purposes.

actor_type.description:
Classification of the actor that performed the moderation, such as `platformAdmin` or `system`.

Even though the underlying table stores a concrete foreign key to `shopping_mall_platformadmin`, this higher-level type helps distinguish human administrator actions from automated rule engine decisions or other system actors when reviewing history in administrative consoles or reports.

oneOf.description:
Previous moderation status of the review before this event was applied.

This value corresponds to the `from_status` column in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`. It is `null` for the first moderation event on a review when there is no prior status, and otherwise records the status the review transitioned from (for example `pending_review`, `visible`, or `hidden`).
Represents the absence of a previous moderation status for the review when this event is the first recorded moderation action in the history timeline.

from_status.description:
Previous moderation status of the review before this event was applied.

This value corresponds to the `from_status` column in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`. It is `null` for the first moderation event on a review when there is no prior status, and otherwise records the status the review transitioned from (for example `pending_review`, `visible`, or `hidden`).

to_status.description:
New moderation status of the review after this event.

This value corresponds to the `to_status` column in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` and records the outcome of the moderation decision. Common examples include `approved`, `hidden`, `rejected`, or `removed`, and downstream systems rely on this status to determine how the review should be displayed or suppressed across the platform.

oneOf.description:
Structured reason code describing why this moderation action was taken, such as `policy_violation`, `abuse`, `spam`, or `legal_request`.

The value should align with configured policy or rule identifiers so that analytics and audit tools can group and summarize moderation decisions consistently.
Represents the absence of a structured reason code when the moderation event was recorded without linking it to a predefined policy or rule identifier.

reason_code.description:
Optional structured reason code describing why this moderation action was taken.

This field maps to the `reason_code` column in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` and typically references configured policy or rule identifiers, such as `policy_violation`, `abuse`, `spam`, or `legal_request`. When `null`, the action was taken without associating a specific structured reason, and reviewers must rely on free-form notes or surrounding context to understand the decision.

oneOf.description:
Free‑form notes recorded by the moderator or system that provide additional context for this moderation decision.

Typical content may include investigation details, links to supporting evidence, or explanations of how specific policies were applied in this case.
Represents the absence of free‑form explanatory notes when the moderation event was recorded without additional commentary beyond structured status and reason codes.

notes.description:
Optional free‑form notes recorded by the moderator or system with additional context for this decision.

This property corresponds to the `note` column in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` and is used to capture human-readable explanations, investigative details, or operational comments that can assist later audits and dispute handling. When `null`, no additional commentary was stored alongside the structured reason code.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this moderation event was created and recorded in the database.

This maps directly to the `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events` and is stored as an ISO 8601 date-time value. It is primarily used to order events chronologically when reconstructing moderation timelines for a review or when generating time-based moderation reports.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp indicating the last time this moderation event row was updated in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`.

In the common append-only usage pattern, moderation events are created once and rarely modified, so `updated_at` will often match `created_at`. However, when a moderator or automated process needs to correct or clarify an existing event—for example, by refining `notes` or adjusting a `reason_code` to a more accurate value—this column is refreshed to capture the time of that correction.

Administrative and audit tooling can use `updated_at` to detect recently edited moderation records, drive synchronization with downstream analytics systems, or help operators distinguish between original decisions and later amendments in detailed history views.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp indicating when this moderation event was logically deleted or retired from active views.

The value is written when a soft-delete operation is performed on the row in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`, allowing the platform to hide the event from everyday moderation timelines while still retaining it for deeper compliance and forensic analysis.
Represents that the moderation event has not been logically deleted and should be treated as active in standard moderation timelines and administrative user interfaces.

deleted_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when this moderation event was logically deleted or retired from active views.

This property reflects the `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_product_review_moderation_events`. When `null`, the moderation event is considered active and is typically included in standard moderation timelines for the associated review. When set to a concrete date-time value, the event has been soft-deleted or retired—common list and detail queries may omit it, while specialized compliance, forensics, or archival reporting queries may still include it to provide a complete historical record.

This soft-deletion pattern allows the platform to hide superseded or erroneous moderation events from everyday user interfaces without losing the underlying audit trail that may be required for regulatory or internal governance purposes.

IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse.description:
Seller-authored response to a specific product review within the shoppingMall platform.

Represents the persisted reply that a seller posts in response to a customer-authored product review. Each record is logically attached to exactly one review in the `shopping_mall_product_reviews` table and, through that, to a specific product and seller.

This DTO is used as the full read model returned by review-related APIs when exposing seller responses to clients and now returns association objects instead of raw foreign key identifiers for its contextual relations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller response record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` row and is used to uniquely reference this response in internal systems and logs.

body.description:
Main textual content of the seller's response.

Contains the reply that will be displayed to customers alongside the corresponding product review. Platform-level review policies may enforce maximum length and content rules on this field.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller response was first created.

Represents the moment the seller's reply was initially persisted. The value is managed by the backend and is returned in ISO 8601 date-time format.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller response was last updated.

Reflects the most recent modification time of the response content fields. Managed by the backend and returned in ISO 8601 date-time format.

review.description:
Summary representation of the product review that this seller response is attached to.

Provides the minimal context needed to understand which review is being replied to (for example, rating, headline, or creation time) without requiring an additional API call. This is a BELONGS-TO association transformed into a `.ISummary` reference instead of exposing the raw `review_id` foreign key.

seller.description:
Summary representation of the seller account that authored this response.

Exposes human-readable seller information such as display name and high-level status via the existing seller summary type, replacing the previous raw `seller_id` foreign key. This follows the BELONGS-TO-as-Summary rule for contextual associations in read DTOs.

IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse.description:
Request payload for creating or overwriting a seller-authored response to a product review.

Used by seller-facing APIs when a seller posts a reply to a customer review for a product they own. The DTO contains only the fields that a seller is allowed to provide directly at creation time, such as the response body text.

It intentionally omits identifiers and foreign keys like `id`, `review_id`, and `seller_id`, which are resolved from the path parameter and authenticated seller context inside the backend service. System-managed timestamps are also excluded and will be set automatically by the persistence layer.

body.description:
Textual content of the seller's response.

This is the main reply text that will be shown to customers beneath the associated product review. It must comply with platform review policies regarding length, language, and prohibited content.

IShoppingMallProductReviewSellerResponse.description:
DTO for creating or updating a seller-authored response to a specific product review on the shoppingMall platform.

Used as the request body for the PUT /shoppingMall/seller/reviews/{reviewId}/sellerResponse endpoint. Carries only the editable business field for the seller response body. Actor identity (seller) and the target review are derived from authentication context and the path parameter, not from this DTO.

This type is directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_product_review_seller_responses` Prisma model and therefore only exposes the `body` column as a client-editable field, keeping identifiers and timestamps fully server-managed.

body.description:
Public textual content of the seller’s response that will be shown alongside the associated product review.

The content must comply with marketplace content guidelines and may be subject to maximum length and moderation rules enforced by the backend. This is the only client-editable column for the seller response; all linkage and audit fields are derived server-side.

IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.description:
Materialized aggregate rating snapshot for a product or a specific SKU in the shoppingMall catalog.

Backed by the shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates Prisma model, this entity provides precomputed metrics derived from individual customer reviews (stored in shopping_mall_product_reviews). It enables clients to quickly display rating summaries on product detail pages and catalog listings without recomputing aggregates at query time.

Aggregate rows may be scoped at the product level (no SKU context) or at the SKU level (for a specific variant), depending on whether `sku` is present. This type is returned by the rating-aggregate read APIs:
- GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/ratingAggregates
- PATCH /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/ratingAggregates
- GET /shoppingMall/products/{productId}/skus/{skuId}/ratingAggregates

id.description:
Primary identifier of the rating aggregate record in the shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates table.

The exact format (UUID or other) follows the underlying Prisma model definition. It is used internally to distinguish individual aggregate snapshots and for administrative tooling that inspects or repairs aggregate data.

product.description:
Associated product for which this aggregate rating snapshot has been computed.

This is a contextual association to the catalog product entity rather than a mere foreign key. Using the summary form provides enough information for list and detail UIs (for example, product code, name, and status) without requiring an additional lookup based on a raw `product_id` column.

oneOf.description: Null when the aggregate is computed at product level and not scoped to an individual SKU variant.

sku.description:
Associated SKU (product variant) when this aggregate is scoped at the SKU level.

When present, this summary object identifies the precise purchasable variant whose reviews were aggregated. When null, the aggregate is product-level, representing reviews across all SKUs of the product. This association replaces the raw `product_sku_id` foreign key from the underlying Prisma model.

average_rating.description:
Average rating value computed from all qualifying reviews included in this aggregate.

Typically represented as a floating-point number between the allowed rating bounds (for example, 1.0 to 5.0). It may be null when no reviews exist yet, in which case the count fields will be zero.

review_count.description:
Total number of customer reviews that contributed to this aggregate snapshot.

This count represents the number of reviews considered when computing `average_rating` and the per-rating buckets. It is zero when the product or SKU has not received any reviews.

rating_1_count.description:
Number of reviews that gave the lowest rating value (for example, 1 star), as counted in this aggregate snapshot.

This value is used together with the other rating_*_count fields to build rating distribution charts and to recompute averages when needed.

rating_2_count.description:
Number of reviews that gave the second-lowest rating value (for example, 2 stars), as counted in this aggregate snapshot.

It is part of the discrete rating distribution metadata used by search, ranking, and analytics features.

rating_3_count.description:
Number of reviews that gave the middle rating value (for example, 3 stars), as counted in this aggregate snapshot.

This bucket often represents neutral sentiment in rating distributions and can be used in quality and satisfaction analytics.

rating_4_count.description:
Number of reviews that gave the second-highest rating value (for example, 4 stars), as counted in this aggregate snapshot.

Together with the 5-star bucket, it helps represent positive review share in analytic views.

rating_5_count.description:
Number of reviews that gave the highest rating value (for example, 5 stars), as counted in this aggregate snapshot.

A high value here relative to lower buckets often indicates strong customer satisfaction and can influence merchandising and ranking algorithms.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this rating aggregate record was created or initially materialized.

Recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). It indicates when the aggregate row was first inserted into the materialized aggregate table, which may differ from the timestamps of the reviews that contributed to it.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the latest refresh of this rating aggregate snapshot.

Recorded in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). Implementation logic typically updates this value whenever new reviews are added, existing reviews are modified or moderated, or backfill jobs recompute aggregates for consistency.

deleted_at.description:
Optional timestamp indicating when this aggregate record was logically removed or superseded.

When null, the aggregate is considered active and eligible for use in catalog and analytics queries. When non-null, the row has been soft-deleted—for example, because the underlying product or SKU has been retired or aggregate data has been consolidated—and should typically be ignored by standard read paths except in administrative or forensic tooling.

IShoppingMallProductRatingAggregate.IReq.description:
Request parameters for retrieving rating aggregate information for a specific product.

Used as the JSON request body of the PATCH `/shoppingMall/products/{productId}/ratingAggregates` endpoint. Allows the client to control which aggregate records are returned for the target product, such as filtering by region, channel, or time window, and whether SKU-level breakdowns should be included.

This DTO does not map directly to a Prisma model and therefore has no `x-autobe-prisma-schema` linkage. It is strictly a query/filter specification used by the backend to construct analytic queries against `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and related tables.

regionCode.description:
Optional region code filter that restricts rating aggregates to a particular geographic region or market segment.

When provided, only aggregates whose region or market identifier matches this code should be considered in the computation. The exact semantics and valid values depend on how regions are modeled (for example via `shopping_mall_region_settings`), but typical values are ISO country codes or platform-specific region identifiers.

channelCode.description:
Optional sales channel code filter that limits rating aggregates to a specific channel.

Examples include web, mobile, marketplace partner channels, or other channel identifiers supported by the platform. When omitted, aggregates across all channels are included.

fromTimestamp.description:
Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the time window used when aggregating ratings.

Represents an ISO 8601 timestamp. Only reviews or aggregate snapshots whose effective time is on or after this value should be considered. When omitted, there is no explicit lower time bound.

toTimestamp.description:
Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the time window used when aggregating ratings.

Represents an ISO 8601 timestamp. Only reviews or aggregate snapshots whose effective time is on or before this value should be considered. When omitted, there is no explicit upper time bound.

includeSkuBreakdown.description:
Flag that controls whether SKU-level rating aggregates should be included in the response.

When `true`, the backend should attempt to compute and return per-SKU rating statistics in addition to any overall product-level aggregates. When `false` or omitted, only product-level aggregates are returned.

IShoppingMallReviewStatisticsSummary.description:
Platform-wide review and rating statistics summary for the shopping mall service.

Returned as the response body of the GET `/shoppingMall/reviews/statistics/summary` endpoint. Represents a computed snapshot of global review health metrics derived from tables such as `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and `shopping_mall_product_reviews`.

This DTO is an aggregate view that does not correspond to a single Prisma model row. Instead, it contains precomputed totals, averages, and distributions that can be used by dashboards, reporting tools, or public overview pages.

totalReviewCount.description:
Total number of product reviews recorded across the entire platform.

This count typically corresponds to the number of rows in `shopping_mall_product_reviews`, possibly subject to internal visibility or moderation filters (for example, excluding removed or hidden reviews).

totalRatedProductCount.description:
Total number of distinct products that have at least one visible review.

This value helps indicate how broadly reviews are distributed across the catalog.

globalAverageRating.description:
Average rating score across all considered reviews on the platform.

Usually computed as the sum of all rating values divided by `totalReviewCount`. The exact scale depends on business rules (for example 1–5 stars). When there are no reviews, this may be `0` or omitted depending on implementation.

ratingDistribution.description:
Distribution of review counts across individual rating values.

Each entry describes how many reviews fall into a specific rating bucket (for example 1-star, 2-star, etc.). The order of buckets is typically from lowest rating to highest rating.

recentReviewCount.description:
Number of reviews created within a recent time window such as the last 30 days.

The precise window is defined by business requirements, but the metric is intended to show current review activity rather than lifetime totals.

IShoppingMallReviewStatisticsSummary.IRa.description:
Single rating bucket entry used to describe how many reviews fall into a specific rating value for platform-wide statistics.

Instances of this type are contained in the `ratingDistribution` array on `IShoppingMallReviewStatisticsSummary`.

ratingValue.description:
Discrete rating value represented by this bucket.

Common values are integers from 1 to 5 when using a 5-star rating system, but the actual range depends on the platform's rating scale.

reviewCount.description: Number of reviews whose rating exactly matches `ratingValue` within the scope of the aggregation used for the summary.

IShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsByPr.description:
Filter, grouping, and pagination criteria used by internal analytics tools to compute product-level review statistics from shopping_mall_product_reviews.

Consumers of this DTO are platform admin and seller dashboards that need to scope statistics across many products with flexible filters while keeping the operation strictly read-only. The payload controls which reviews are included in aggregation and how the result pages are ordered.

productIds.description:
Optional list of product identifiers to restrict aggregation to a specific set of products.

When omitted, filtering by product is driven by other criteria such as seller, category, or text search. Each identifier must be a valid product primary key as stored in shopping_mall_products and is represented as a UUID string.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers used to restrict aggregation to products owned by specific sellers.

Each value must match a seller primary key from shopping_mall_seller and is represented as a UUID string. When provided together with productIds, the intersection of the filters is applied.

skuIds.description:
Optional list of SKU identifiers to narrow statistics down to specific variants within products.

Each identifier corresponds to a primary key from shopping_mall_product_skus and is represented as a UUID string. When omitted, statistics are computed at the whole-product level based on all related SKUs.

categoryIds.description:
Optional list of category identifiers to include only products that belong to the specified catalog categories.

Category identifiers map to shopping_mall_categories and are represented as UUID strings. When multiple IDs are provided, a product is included if it is assigned to at least one of them.

minRating.description:
Optional minimum star rating threshold used to include only reviews with rating greater than or equal to this value.

Ratings are expressed on a 1–5 scale. When both minRating and maxRating are provided, minRating must be less than or equal to maxRating; otherwise the request is considered invalid.

maxRating.description:
Optional maximum star rating threshold used to include only reviews with rating less than or equal to this value.

Ratings are expressed on a 1–5 scale. When both minRating and maxRating are provided, maxRating must be greater than or equal to minRating; otherwise the request is considered invalid.

fromCreatedAt.description:
Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the review creation timestamp.

Only reviews with created_at greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are considered for aggregation.

toCreatedAt.description:
Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the review creation timestamp.

Only reviews with created_at less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are considered for aggregation.

includePending.description:
Flag indicating whether to include reviews that are still in a pending or unmoderated state, depending on the moderation model.

When false, only reviews that are published/visible are typically included.

includeRejected.description:
Flag indicating whether to include reviews that have been rejected, hidden, or otherwise marked as not publicly visible.

These records are often required for internal quality or fraud analysis, but are excluded from user-facing aggregates by default.

regionCodes.description:
Optional list of region codes representing markets or geographic areas in which the reviews or products are relevant.

Values typically correspond to region identifiers or ISO-like codes managed via shopping_mall_region_settings. No strict pattern is enforced at the schema level so that business-specific codes remain flexible.

limit.description:
Maximum number of product statistic records to return in a single page.

The value must be at least 1. Service implementations typically enforce an upper bound (for example 100 or 1000) to protect resources; callers are encouraged to stay within those documented limits.

offset.description:
Zero-based index of the first record to return in the current page.

The value must be a non‑negative integer. Used together with limit for simple, offset-based pagination. For large data sets, cursor-based pagination may be added as a future enhancement.

oneOf.description:
Field name that determines how the product statistic rows are sorted in the response.

Allowed values are:
- "productId": order by the product identifier for stable, deterministic pagination.
- "averageRating": order by the aggregated average rating per product.
- "reviewCount": order by the total number of reviews contributing to each product’s statistics.
- "latestReviewCreatedAt": order by the timestamp of the most recent review included in each product’s statistics.

Any value outside this set is rejected during request validation.
