IShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsBySe.description:
Filter, grouping, and pagination criteria used by analytics and operational tooling to compute seller-level review statistics from shopping_mall_product_reviews.

Consumers of this DTO include platform admin consoles and seller performance dashboards that need to evaluate review volume and quality per seller under various temporal, catalog, and moderation filters.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifiers used to restrict aggregation to a subset of sellers.

Each identifier corresponds to a row in shopping_mall_seller. When omitted, other filters such as category or region determine which sellers are included.

productIds.description:
Optional list of product identifiers to limit statistics to reviews associated with particular products.

Each identifier must match a primary key from shopping_mall_products. When used together with sellerIds, sellers are evaluated only over the filtered product set.

categoryIds.description:
Optional list of category identifiers that restrict aggregation to reviews for products in the specified categories.

Category identifiers map to shopping_mall_categories. A review is included if its associated product belongs to at least one of the provided categories.

minRating.description:
Optional minimum star rating threshold used to include only reviews with rating greater than or equal to this value.

Commonly used to focus on low-rating distributions for quality analysis when combined with upper bounds or status filters.

maxRating.description:
Optional maximum star rating threshold used to include only reviews with rating less than or equal to this value.

Frequently used in conjunction with minRating to define a rating band for analysis, such as "1–3 stars".

fromCreatedAt.description:
Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the review creation timestamp.

Only reviews with created_at greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are considered when computing seller-level statistics.

toCreatedAt.description:
Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the review creation timestamp.

Only reviews with created_at less than or equal to this ISO 8601 date-time are considered when computing seller-level statistics.

includePending.description:
Flag indicating whether to include reviews that are pending moderation or otherwise not yet publicly visible.

Useful for internal review queues and seller self-monitoring of unapproved feedback.

includeRejected.description:
Flag indicating whether to include reviews that have been rejected, hidden, or otherwise excluded from public aggregates.

Typically enabled only for admin-facing tools or internal quality monitoring dashboards.

regionCodes.description:
Optional list of region codes representing markets, locales, or fulfillment regions in which the reviewed products were sold or visible.

Values typically align with region identifiers or ISO-like codes managed via shopping_mall_region_settings.

limit.description:
Maximum number of seller statistic records to return in a single page.

Used together with offset for offset-based pagination. Implementations should enforce a sane maximum value for performance reasons.

offset.description:
Zero-based index of the first seller statistic record to return in the current page.

Used together with limit to implement offset-based pagination for analytics views.

orderBy.description:
Field name that determines how the seller statistic rows are sorted in the response.

Typical values include 'sellerId', 'averageRating', 'reviewCount', or 'latestReviewCreatedAt'. The concrete supported list is defined by the service implementation, and invalid inputs must be rejected.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied to the selected orderBy field.

Supported values are 'asc' for ascending and 'desc' for descending. Any other value should be treated as invalid input.

IShoppingMallAdminActionAudit.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination criteria for querying administrator action audit records from the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` table.

Used by platform administrators to filter and page through admin action audit logs for compliance, security, and operational investigations. The DTO supports filtering by acting administrator, action category, target resource information, time range, and outcome status, as well as pagination and sorting options.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated results.

If omitted, the backend should default to the first page. Must be a positive integer when provided.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

Used together with `page` to control pagination size. The backend should enforce a reasonable upper bound to protect performance.

sortBy.description:
Field name to use for sorting admin action audit records.

Common values include `occurredAt`, `createdAt`, `actionType`, or `adminCode`. The exact supported values are determined by the implementation, and unsupported values should be rejected with a validation error.

oneOf.description:
Direction of sorting for the result set.

`asc` orders from oldest to newest or alphabetically ascending based on `sortBy`. `desc` orders from newest to oldest or alphabetically descending.

Direction of sorting for the result set.

`asc` orders from oldest to newest or alphabetically ascending based on `sortBy`. `desc` orders from newest to oldest or alphabetically descending.

sortDirection.description:
Direction of sorting for the result set.

`asc` orders from oldest to newest or alphabetically ascending based on `sortBy`. `desc` orders from newest to oldest or alphabetically descending.

adminId.description:
Identifier of the platform administrator who performed the actions to include in the result set.

When provided, only audit records for this administrator are returned. This is typically the primary key of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` table.

adminCode.description:
Human-friendly code or login identifier of the acting platform administrator to filter by.

This is useful when an operator knows the admin code but not the underlying UUID identifier.

actionTypes.description:
List of action type codes to include in the result set.

Each value corresponds to a high-level category of admin action, such as `PRODUCT_UPDATE`, `REVIEW_MODERATION`, `DISPUTE_RESOLUTION`, `CONFIGURATION_CHANGE`, or similar domain-specific codes.

resourceTypes.description:
List of resource type codes to include in the result set.

Resource types describe which kind of entity an admin action targeted, for example `PRODUCT`, `ORDER`, `SELLER`, `CUSTOMER`, `POLICY`, or `PAYMENT`.

If provided, only audit records whose target resource type is in this list are returned.

resourceId.description:
Identifier of the primary target resource affected by the admin actions.

This may be a UUID string or another business identifier depending on the target resource type (for example, product ID, order ID, or seller ID). When set, only audit records referencing this target resource are returned.

resultStatuses.description:
List of result status codes to filter audit records by.

Typical values include `SUCCESS`, `FAILURE`, or more granular outcome codes depending on business requirements. When provided, only records whose result status is in this list are included.

occurredFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the action occurrence timestamp filter.

Only audit records with an occurrence time greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with explicit offset.

occurredTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the action occurrence timestamp filter.

Only audit records with an occurrence time less than or equal to this timestamp are included. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with explicit offset.

createdFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the record creation timestamp filter.

Useful when the log ingestion time differs from the action occurrence time, such as for asynchronous audit processing.

createdTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the record creation timestamp filter.

Only audit records whose creation time is less than or equal to this value are included. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format.

search.description:
Free-text search term applied across selected fields of the audit records.

Typical implementations search within action titles, descriptive messages, and metadata snippets, enabling admins to quickly locate relevant actions based on partial text.

IShoppingMallAdminActionAudit.description:
Complete administrator action audit record entity aligned with the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` Prisma model.

Represents an immutable log entry recording a significant action performed by a platform administrator. Each record captures who acted, when they acted, what action type was performed, which primary resource was targeted, and the outcome status, along with optional contextual metadata and before/after snapshots.

Most core fields are direct projections of columns in the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` table, such as `action_type`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `action_subtype`, `secondary_target_type`, `secondary_target_id`, `request_context`, `before_snapshot`, `after_snapshot`, `action_summary`, and `created_at`. Additional fields like `adminCode`, `occurredAt`, `resultStatus`, `ipAddress`, `userAgent`, `sessionId`, and enriched `metadata` may be populated from related admin, session, or logging tables to provide a richer investigative view.

This DTO is intended for detailed drill-down views in admin consoles and internal tools. It exposes all non-sensitive fields that are safe for platform administrators to inspect, while excluding any credential or secret information. Audit records are created by the system automatically and must never be modified or deleted through normal business APIs.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin action audit record.

Corresponds to the primary key `id` of the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` table.

adminId.description:
Identifier of the platform administrator who performed the action.

This is the foreign key projection of `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and typically references `shopping_mall_platformadmin.id`.

adminCode.description:
Human-readable code, username, or login identifier of the acting platform administrator.

Captured at the time of the action so that audit records remain readable even if the underlying admin account metadata later changes. This value is derived from the associated admin identity rather than a dedicated column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits`.

actionType.description:
High-level action type or category code describing what the administrator did.

This is a direct projection of the `action_type` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits`. Examples include values such as `user_status_change`, `product_visibility_update`, `refund_approval`, `seller_suspension`, or other domain-specific codes configured by the platform.

actionSubtype.description:
Optional more granular subtype or reason code for the admin action.

This corresponds to the nullable `action_subtype` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and is used to distinguish specific flows or variants within a broader `actionType` (for example, different flavors of configuration updates or dispute resolutions).

resourceType.description:
Business type of the primary target resource of this action.

This is a semantic projection of the `target_type` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits`. Typical values include `customer`, `seller`, `product`, `order`, `payment`, `review`, `configuration`, or other entity types defined by the platform's admin domain model.

resourceId.description:
Opaque identifier string of the primary target resource affected by the action.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `target_id` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits`, which stores the ID value from the target table as text to avoid polymorphic foreign keys. It may contain a UUID, a business code, or another identifier format depending on the resource type.

secondaryResourceType.description:
Optional business type of a secondary target resource affected by the admin action.

This is a projection of the nullable `secondary_target_type` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and is populated when the operation logically spans two entities (for example, linking a seller to a brand or updating relationships between configuration profiles).

secondaryResourceId.description:
Optional opaque identifier string of a secondary target resource affected by the admin action.

This corresponds to the nullable `secondary_target_id` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and stores the identifier of the secondary entity involved in the action as text.

occurredAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrator action actually occurred from a business perspective.

Stored as an ISO 8601 date-time value in UTC or with explicit offset. While `createdAt` reflects when the audit record was persisted, `occurredAt` expresses when the underlying operation took place and may be derived from request or event timestamps where necessary.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this admin action audit record was created in the database.

This is a direct projection of the non-nullable `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and is typically set to the time the audit entry was recorded by the system.

resultStatus.description:
Outcome status code for the admin action.

Represents a logical result of the operation, such as `SUCCESS`, `FAILURE`, `PARTIAL_SUCCESS`, or other outcome codes defined by the platform. This may be derived from error handling and workflow logic around the audited action rather than a dedicated column in the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` table.

ipAddress.description:
IP address observed for the administrator session when the action was performed.

Used for security investigations and anomaly detection. Stored as a string to support both IPv4 and IPv6 textual representations. This value is typically sourced from request context or related logging tables, not from a dedicated Prisma column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits`.

userAgent.description:
User agent string reported by the client used by the administrator when performing the action.

Helps identify the device, browser, or integration client involved in the action. As with `ipAddress`, this value is usually captured from HTTP request context or external logs rather than stored directly in the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` table.

sessionId.description:
Identifier of the administrator session associated with this action, if available.

Typically references a record in `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` or an equivalent session table and helps correlate multiple actions within the same authenticated session for forensic analysis.

requestContext.description:
Optional serialized context about the request that triggered the admin action.

This is a direct projection of the nullable `request_context` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and usually stores JSON or another encoded structure containing details such as IP address, user agent, dashboard module, or correlation IDs as captured at the time of the operation.

beforeSnapshot.description:
Optional snapshot of key fields from before the admin action was applied.

Maps to the nullable `before_snapshot` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and typically stores a JSON string describing the prior state of important business attributes, enabling before/after comparisons during audit and troubleshooting.

afterSnapshot.description:
Optional snapshot of key fields from after the admin action was applied.

Maps to the nullable `after_snapshot` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and usually stores a JSON string describing the post-change state of important business attributes, paired with `beforeSnapshot` to support diff-style investigations.

summary.description:
Human-readable summary of the admin action suitable for list views and quick scanning.

This value is backed by the `action_summary` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and should provide a concise but meaningful description such as "Updated product pricing", "Approved refund request", or "Suspended seller account" so that operators can understand the gist without inspecting snapshots.

metadata.description:
Structured or semi-structured metadata payload capturing additional context for the admin action.

This field can contain enriched JSON or serialized data that combines information from `request_context`, `before_snapshot`, `after_snapshot`, or external systems (such as correlation IDs and error payloads). It is intended for advanced investigative tools that need to drill into raw details beyond the primary audit columns.

IShoppingMallAdminConfigurationChangeLog.description:
Search and filter request DTO for querying administrative configuration change log records stored in the `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` table.

This type is used by platform administrators to perform analytics-style and audit searches over historical configuration changes in the shoppingMall platform. It encapsulates pagination, sorting, and rich filter conditions such as configuration domains, scopes, time windows, and keyword search over change summaries and reasons.

All properties are optional to allow flexible combination of filters. When a property is omitted, that particular filter is not applied by the backend. The server should enforce sensible maximum limits even if the client provides very large `limit` values.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated results.

If omitted, the backend should default to the first page. Must be a positive integer when provided.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page.

If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default (for example 20 or 50) and enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

sortBy.description:
Field name used for sorting configuration change logs.

Typical values include `"created_at"` for recency-based sorting or logical fields such as `"config_domain"` or `"config_scope"`. The backend should validate allowed sort fields against the `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` columns and fall back to a safe default if an unsupported value is provided.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for ordered results.

`"asc"` sorts in ascending order and `"desc"` sorts in descending order. When omitted, the backend should default to descending order by created timestamp so the latest configuration changes appear first.

Sort direction for ordered results.

`"asc"` sorts in ascending order and `"desc"` sorts in descending order. When omitted, the backend should default to descending order by created timestamp so the latest configuration changes appear first.

sortDirection.description:
Sort direction for ordered results.

`"asc"` sorts in ascending order and `"desc"` sorts in descending order. When omitted, the backend should default to descending order by `created_at` so the latest configuration changes from `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` appear first.

configDomains.description:
Optional inclusion filter over configuration domains.

Each element in this array is compared against the `config_domain` column of `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs`. Only log records whose `config_domain` value belongs to this set should be returned, enabling queries such as "only cancellation policy changes" or "only inventory settings updates".

configScope.description:
Optional exact or partial filter for the configuration scope associated with a change.

This value is matched against the `config_scope` column in `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs`, which may contain region codes, category identifiers, or seller-specific scopes. Implementations may support either exact matching or partial/LIKE matching as long as the behavior is clearly documented for API consumers.

adminId.description:
Optional filter for the acting platform administrator who performed the configuration change.

Represents the UUID identifier of a `shopping_mall_platformadmin` record that is associated with the change log entry via the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` foreign key in `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs`. When provided, only logs created by the specified administrator are returned.

changedKeysKeyword.description:
Optional keyword used to search within the `changed_keys_summary` field.

This allows administrators to quickly find configuration changes that mention particular keys, sections, or features. Implementations should leverage search capabilities or the GIN index on `changed_keys_summary` in the `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` table when available for efficient querying.

reasonKeyword.description:
Optional keyword used to search within the human-entered `reason` text field.

This filter helps administrators locate changes based on the justifications or explanations provided at the time of modification, such as incident IDs, campaign names, or policy references stored in the `reason` column of `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs`.

createdAtFrom.description:
Start of the time window for the configuration change creation timestamp.

Only records whose `created_at` value in `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` is greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are included. When omitted, there is no lower bound on the time range.

createdAtTo.description:
End of the time window for the configuration change creation timestamp.

Only records whose `created_at` value in `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` is less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are included. When omitted, there is no upper bound on the time range.

IShoppingMallAdminConfigurationChangeLog.description:
Detailed DTO representing a single administrative configuration change log entry stored in the `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` table.

Each record captures a single configuration change performed by a platform administrator, including the configuration domain and optional scope, a concise summary of which keys were affected, serialized representations of the configuration before and after the change, an optional human-entered reason, and the timestamp of when the change was recorded.

This type is typically returned by detail retrieval endpoints such as `GET /shoppingMall/platformAdmin/adminConfigurationChangeLogs/{adminConfigurationChangeLogId}` and is used for forensic analysis, compliance verification, and operational troubleshooting.

In addition, it now exposes the acting administrator as a summary association object instead of a raw foreign key identifier, allowing clients to render relevant admin context without extra lookup calls.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the configuration change log record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` Prisma model and is typically a UUID string.

admin.description:
Summary representation of the platform administrator who performed the configuration change.

This association replaces the raw foreign key field to `shopping_mall_platformadmin.id` and provides enough context for audit UIs to display who made the change (for example, name, handle, or primary identifiers) without requiring additional API calls.

configDomain.description:
Logical configuration domain that was modified by this change.

Examples include high-level areas such as `"cancellation_policy"`, `"refund_policy"`, `"review_policy"`, `"inventory_settings"`, or `"risk_settings"`. The exact value is persisted in the `config_domain` column of the underlying table.

configScope.description:
Optional scope string that narrows the configuration context affected by the change.

This may represent a region code, category identifier, seller-specific override key, or similar scoping information. When empty or null in the database, this field may be omitted or represented as an empty string in the DTO, depending on implementation.

changedKeysSummary.description:
Concise text summary describing which configuration keys or sections were modified.

This field is designed for quick human scanning in audit views and is often indexed using text or GIN indexes to support keyword-based searches.

beforeValue.description:
Serialized representation of the configuration value before the change.

Typically stored as a JSON string capturing the previous configuration structure. Consumers may choose to parse this value into a JSON object for diffing or visualization, but at the DTO level it is represented as an opaque string for maximum flexibility.

afterValue.description:
Serialized representation of the configuration value after the change.

Typically stored as a JSON string capturing the updated configuration structure. Together with `beforeValue`, this enables detailed comparison of configuration changes over time.

reason.description:
Optional human-entered explanation or justification for the configuration change.

Administrators may use this field to record incident references, campaign identifiers, policy references, or free-form notes that provide context for why the change was made.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the configuration change log was created.

Stored as an ISO 8601 date-time value and usually corresponds to the moment when the change was successfully persisted and the audit record appended.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSummary.IR.description:
Search and analytics request DTO for querying seller performance summary snapshots from the shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries table.

This type encapsulates rich filter criteria, metric thresholds, risk filters, and pagination/sorting parameters that platform administrators use to locate and analyze seller performance snapshots over specified periods. It is designed for complex, body-based search APIs (PATCH) rather than simple query-string filters.

The DTO focuses on selecting rows from the shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries model and related seller context, without exposing any mutable fields or write capabilities. It supports safe, read-only exploration of precomputed metrics and risk indicators for back-office analytics and monitoring workflows.

sellerIds.description:
Optional list of seller identifier values to restrict the search to specific sellers.

Each item corresponds to the foreign key shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.shopping_mall_seller_id. When provided, only summary rows belonging to the listed sellers are eligible to appear in the result set. When omitted or empty, summaries for all sellers may be considered, subject to other filters.

This filter is typically used by platform administrators when investigating one or more particular sellers or when drilling down from an external seller selection context.

items.description:
Identifier of a seller whose performance summaries should be included in the search scope.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_seller.id and is used to match the foreign key shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.shopping_mall_seller_id in the underlying table.

It must be a valid UUID string and should represent an existing seller in the system.

oneOf.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the summary period_start field when filtering by reporting window.

When specified, only records whose period_start is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. This allows administrators to limit analytics to recent periods or a specific analysis horizon.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z).

Null value indicates that there is no explicit lower bound filter on period_start.

When null, the search may include summaries from any earlier period_start, subject to other filters.

periodStartFrom.description:
Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the period_start field used to limit which summary windows are considered.

This filter is useful when administrators want to analyze only summaries generated after a particular start date, such as the beginning of a month or quarter. If left null, there is effectively no minimum period_start constraint applied by this criterion.

oneOf.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the summary period_start field when filtering by reporting window.

When specified, only records whose period_start is less than or equal to this timestamp are included. This allows administrators to cap the analysis window at a certain point in time.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., 2025-01-31T23:59:59Z).

Null value indicates that there is no explicit upper bound filter on period_start.

When null, the search may include summaries whose period_start is greater than any particular date, subject to other filters.

periodStartTo.description:
Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the period_start field used to cap the reporting window of the search.

Together with periodStartFrom, this allows administrators to select summaries that fall within a specific time range, such as a particular month, quarter, or custom analysis period.

oneOf.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) for the period_end field when filtering by the end of the reporting window.

When specified, only records whose period_end is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. This is typically used for selecting summaries that complete on or after a certain date.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string.

Null value indicates that there is no explicit lower bound filter on period_end.

When null, the search may include summaries ending at any earlier time, subject to other filters.

periodEndFrom.description:
Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the period_end field when performing time-range analytics.

This filter helps administrators focus on summaries whose reporting period ends on or after a specific date, for example summaries that cover at least part of a recent month or week.

oneOf.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) for the period_end field when filtering by the end of the reporting window.

When specified, only records whose period_end is less than or equal to this timestamp are included. This defines the maximum end date for included summary periods.

The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string.

Null value indicates that there is no explicit upper bound filter on period_end.

When null, the search may include summaries whose reporting period ends after any particular date, subject to other filters.

periodEndTo.description:
Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the period_end field used to cap the reporting window of the search.

Combined with periodEndFrom, this enables precise selection of summary periods, such as analytics for a specific calendar month or fiscal quarter.

oneOf.description:
Minimum acceptable value for orders_count when filtering seller performance summaries by activity level.

When provided, only records with orders_count greater than or equal to this value are considered. This helps administrators focus on sellers with substantial order volume rather than those with only incidental activity.

The value must be zero or a positive integer.

Null value indicates that there is no minimum threshold filter on orders_count.

When null, summaries with any orders_count value, including zero, may be included, subject to other filters.

minOrdersCount.description:
Optional lower bound for the orders_count metric in shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.

This filter is commonly used to restrict analytics to sellers who have processed at least a certain number of orders within the period, which reduces noise from low-activity sellers.

oneOf.description:
Maximum acceptable value for orders_count when filtering seller performance summaries.

When provided, only records with orders_count less than or equal to this value are included. While less common, this can be used in specific analyses, such as reviewing performance of small or emerging sellers.

The value must be zero or a positive integer.

Null value indicates that there is no upper bound filter on orders_count.

When null, summaries with any orders_count value may be included, subject to other filters.

maxOrdersCount.description:
Optional upper bound for the orders_count metric in shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.

This filter can be used for targeted analyses of low- to medium-volume sellers or for specific risk or performance studies that focus on certain order volume bands.

oneOf.description:
Minimum acceptable value for the average_rating metric when filtering seller performance summaries.

When provided, only records with average_rating greater than or equal to this value are included. It is typically used to find well-performing sellers or to enforce minimum quality thresholds.

The field average_rating in shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries is a nullable double, so records where average_rating is null are usually excluded from this filter unless additional logic is applied by the implementation.

Null value indicates that there is no minimum threshold filter on average_rating.

When null, summaries with any average_rating value, including null, may be included, subject to other filters.

minAverageRating.description:
Optional lower bound for the average_rating metric derived from product reviews during the summary period.

Risk and operations teams often use this filter to surface only sellers whose average rating meets or exceeds an acceptable threshold, such as 3.5 or 4.0 stars.

oneOf.description:
Maximum acceptable value for the average_rating metric when filtering seller performance summaries.

When provided, only records with average_rating less than or equal to this value are included. This is often used in conjunction with minAverageRating to select sellers within a particular rating band.

Because average_rating may be null in the underlying table when no reviews exist, such records are typically handled separately in business logic.

Null value indicates that there is no upper bound filter on average_rating.

When null, summaries with any average_rating value, including null, may be included, subject to other filters.

maxAverageRating.description:
Optional upper bound for the average_rating metric derived from product reviews during the summary period.

This filter can be used to identify under-performing sellers or rating bands of interest when investigating marketplace health or planning interventions.

riskLevels.description:
Optional list of risk_level category values to include in the search results.

Each element corresponds to the risk_level column in shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries, which is a categorical string classifying seller risk (for example, low, medium, high, or critical). When this array is non-empty, only summaries whose risk_level is one of the specified values are returned.

This filter is a primary tool for risk and operations teams to focus on specific risk bands, such as high and critical sellers needing immediate attention.

items.description:
Single risk_level value that should be included when filtering seller performance summaries.

Typical examples include human-readable categories such as "low", "medium", "high", or "critical". The concrete vocabulary is determined by the business rules used when generating the summaries.

The value must match one of the configured risk categories in the analytics pipeline.

oneOf.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether to filter based on presence of a risk_reason_summary.

When true, only records where risk_reason_summary is non-null and non-empty should be returned. When false, implementations may choose to return only records without a risk_reason_summary.

This enables administrators to quickly identify sellers where the analytics pipeline has generated a human-readable explanation for the assigned risk_level.

Null value indicates that no filter is applied based on the existence of a risk_reason_summary.

When null, records are included regardless of whether risk_reason_summary is populated.

hasRiskReasonSummary.description:
Optional tri-state flag used to filter seller performance summaries by whether a risk_reason_summary explanation exists.

It is commonly set to true when administrators want to review summaries that have explicit human-readable risk annotations generated by analytics or manual processes.

oneOf.description:
Page index for paginated results, using a 1-based numbering scheme.

When provided, this value determines which page of results is returned. A value of 1 represents the first page. Implementations should enforce minimum value constraints and may apply defaults when the value is missing or invalid.

This property controls pagination together with pageSize.

Null value indicates that no explicit page index was provided.

In this case, the implementation should fall back to its default page index, typically 1.

page.description:
Optional page index used to select which slice of the paginated result set should be returned.

This property is part of the standard pagination controls for analytics and list-style endpoints and is interpreted together with pageSize.

oneOf.description:
Maximum number of records to include in a single page of results.

When provided, this value directly influences the size of the data array in the paginated response. Implementations should enforce sensible upper bounds to protect performance and may apply defaults when the value is missing.

Typical values include 20, 50, or 100, depending on dashboard requirements.

Null value indicates that no explicit page size was provided.

In this scenario, the implementation should apply a default page size configured for the platform, ensuring predictable behavior for clients that omit this field.

pageSize.description:
Optional page size limit determining how many seller performance summaries are returned per page.

This property gives admin clients control over the volume of data retrieved in one request while allowing the backend to enforce maximums for performance and stability.

oneOf.description:
Name of the field used to sort seller performance summaries in the result set.

Typical values include database-derived fields such as "created_at", "period_start", "orders_count", "average_rating", or "risk_level". The exact set of allowed values is determined by the implementation, which should reject unsupported field names.

Sorting is usually applied in combination with orderDirection to define ascending or descending order.

Null value indicates that no explicit sort column was requested.

When null, the implementation should apply a default ordering, such as created_at descending or period_start descending, tailored to the primary analysis use case.

orderBy.description:
Optional sort column specifier indicating which summary field should be used to order the results.

This property is commonly used by admin dashboards to sort sellers by most recent snapshot, highest risk, most orders, or other key metrics.

oneOf.description:
Direction in which to sort the result set by the selected orderBy field.

Allowed values are typically "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending order. The implementation should validate and normalize this value, falling back to a default when invalid.

Combined with orderBy, this property controls how seller performance summaries are presented to administrators in analytic views.

Null value indicates that no explicit sort direction was provided.

In this case, the implementation should use a default direction, often "desc" for metrics like created_at or period_start, to surface the most recent or most critical summaries first.

orderDirection.description:
Optional sort direction used together with orderBy to define the ordering of paginated analytics results.

This property allows admin users to toggle between ascending and descending views for fields such as created_at, period_start, or numeric performance metrics.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSummary.description:
Detailed seller performance summary DTO mapped to the shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries Prisma model.

Each instance represents an aggregated snapshot of how a single seller has performed over a defined time window, including order counts, cancellation and refund activity, dispute and resolution metrics, review-based ratings, and an overall risk classification. These snapshots are produced by background analytics or batch processes and are typically append-only records rather than live counters.

The DTO is designed for administrative and operational dashboards where platform administrators need to monitor marketplace health, identify problematic sellers, and review historical performance trends. It exposes all relevant metrics from the underlying table in a structured, read-only format suitable for detail views and drill-down workflows.

id.description:
Primary key of the seller performance summary record.

This value corresponds directly to shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.id and uniquely identifies a single snapshot of seller performance for a specific period.

It is used as the path parameter in detail retrieval operations and as a stable identifier when linking from list or analytics views.

seller.description:
Seller summary associated with this performance snapshot.

This object replaces the raw `shopping_mall_seller_id` foreign key from the Prisma model and provides a BELONGS-TO association reference to the seller entity in a safe, summary form.

By embedding a summary instead of just an ID, administrative dashboards and analytics screens can display key seller context (such as seller name or status) without issuing additional API calls, while still avoiding circular references and oversized payloads.

period_start.description:
Start timestamp of the reporting window that this performance summary covers.

The value corresponds to shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.period_start and marks the beginning of the interval over which metrics such as orders_count and average_rating were computed.

It is typically treated as inclusive, meaning events occurring at or after this timestamp are included in the aggregation, subject to the exact reporting conventions used by analytics jobs.

period_end.description:
End timestamp of the reporting window that this performance summary covers.

This value corresponds to shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.period_end and marks the boundary at which aggregation for this snapshot stops. It may be interpreted as exclusive or inclusive based on the reporting strategy, but is consistently applied across all summaries.

Together with period_start, this field indicates the time span of seller activity being analyzed, such as a calendar day, week, or month.

orders_count.description:
Total count of orders that contained this seller’s items during the reporting period.

This value is taken from shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.orders_count and reflects all orders where the seller participated, regardless of whether they were subsequently cancelled or refunded.

It serves as a baseline volume metric for understanding the scale of the seller’s activity during the snapshot window.

cancelled_orders_count.description:
Count of orders or order segments associated with this seller that were cancelled during the reporting period.

The value comes from shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.cancelled_orders_count and may be computed at either full-order or per-seller-segment granularity, depending on the platform’s order model.

High values relative to orders_count can be an indicator of operational or customer satisfaction issues that warrant further review.

refunded_orders_count.description:
Count of orders or order segments for this seller that had refunds processed during the reporting period.

This value is sourced from shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.refunded_orders_count and captures how frequently monetary adjustments were made in favor of customers for the seller’s transactions.

Elevated refund counts may highlight quality problems, fulfillment issues, or policy non-compliance that require investigation.

dispute_opened_count.description:
Number of disputes opened against this seller’s orders during the reporting period.

The value reflects shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.dispute_opened_count and aggregates dispute records from related order and dispute tables for the time window defined by period_start and period_end.

This metric helps risk and operations teams identify sellers who are generating a high volume of complaints, chargebacks, or service-related issues.

dispute_resolved_against_seller_count.description:
Number of disputes resolved against the seller (favoring the customer) during the reporting period.

This value comes from shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.dispute_resolved_against_seller_count and represents cases where resolution outcomes found the seller to be at fault or obligated to provide compensation.

A high ratio of disputes resolved against the seller compared to dispute_opened_count is a strong risk signal and may factor directly into the risk_level classification.

oneOf.description:
Average product review rating for this seller’s products during the reporting period.

This numeric value mirrors shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.average_rating and is typically computed as an average over star ratings from shopping_mall_product_reviews created within the summary window.

The value usually falls within a bounded range such as 1.0–5.0 and provides a customer sentiment indicator that complements operational metrics like cancellations and disputes.

Null value indicates that no relevant product reviews were available for this seller during the reporting period.

In this case, the analytics pipeline could not compute a meaningful average_rating, either because there were zero reviews or because the data did not meet minimum sample-size thresholds.

average_rating.description:
Average review rating for the seller during the reporting period, or null when no qualifying reviews exist.

This metric helps correlate operational behavior with customer satisfaction and is commonly used in dashboards to visually highlight sellers with poor ratings or rapidly changing sentiment.

low_rating_review_count.description:
Count of low-rated product reviews (for example, 1–2 star ratings) associated with this seller’s products during the reporting period.

This value is taken from shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.low_rating_review_count and focuses on explicitly negative feedback, rather than neutral or positive reviews.

It provides a sharper signal of potential quality issues and is often combined with average_rating and dispute metrics to determine risk_level.

risk_level.description:
Categorical risk classification assigned to this seller performance snapshot.

The value corresponds to shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.risk_level and is derived from a combination of metrics such as cancellation rates, refund ratios, dispute outcomes, and review-related indicators. Typical categories include labels like "low", "medium", "high", or "critical", but the exact vocabulary is defined by the platform’s risk policy.

Risk-level classifications are used by platform administrators and automated workflows to prioritize investigations, apply additional monitoring, or enforce policy-driven interventions.

oneOf.description:
Human-readable summary explaining why the seller was assigned the given risk_level for this period.

This text corresponds to shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.risk_reason_summary and may summarize key contributing factors, such as high dispute volumes, an unusual spike in refunds, or a surge in low-star reviews.

It is intended to help operations and risk analysts quickly understand the rationale behind the classification without manually reviewing raw metrics.

Null value indicates that no human-readable explanation was stored for this summary.

In this case, risk_level may still be meaningful, but analysts may need to examine the raw metrics or external documentation to understand the classification.

risk_reason_summary.description:
Optional explanation describing the reasoning or rules that led to the risk_level classification for this seller.

Where available, this helps streamline manual review by giving administrators immediate context and narrative behind the numeric indicators and categorical risk label.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this performance summary snapshot was generated.

This field corresponds to shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries.created_at and records when the analytics or batch job produced the row, which may be after the end of the reporting period itself.

It is frequently used as a sort key in analytics endpoints to surface the most recently generated summaries first and to track the evolution of risk and performance over time.

IShoppingMallDisputeResolutionLog.IReque.description:
Filter, sorting, and pagination parameters for querying dispute resolution logs from the shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs table.

This DTO is used by platform administrators and internal support tools to search the dispute resolution history. It supports filtering by dispute, actor category, human actor (platform admin or seller), resolution outcome, and time range, along with standard pagination and sorting options. All properties are optional, allowing callers to combine them flexibly as needed.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results. The first page is 1.

If omitted, the implementation should default to the first page.

limit.description:
Maximum number of log records to return per page.

If omitted, the implementation should apply a sensible default and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

orderBy.description:
Field used to sort dispute resolution logs.

Currently restricted to created_at to keep ordering semantics predictable and index-friendly.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for the selected orderBy field.

- asc: Oldest records first
- desc: Newest records first

Sort direction for the selected orderBy field.

- asc: Oldest records first
- desc: Newest records first

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction for the selected orderBy field.

- asc: Oldest records first
- desc: Newest records first

disputeId.description:
Filter logs by the associated order dispute identifier.

When provided, only resolution logs belonging to the specified dispute are returned.

oneOf.description:
Filter logs by the type of actor that produced the resolution event.

- seller: Resolution action taken by a seller
- platform_admin: Resolution action taken by a platform administrator
- automated_rule: Resolution automatically applied by a risk or business rule engine

actorType.description:
Filter logs by the type of actor that produced the resolution event.

- seller: Resolution action taken by a seller
- platform_admin: Resolution action taken by a platform administrator
- automated_rule: Resolution automatically applied by a risk or business rule engine

platformAdminId.description:
Filter logs by the platform administrator who created the resolution event.

Only applicable when actorType is platform_admin; other entries are excluded when this filter is present.

sellerId.description:
Filter logs by the seller who created the resolution event.

Only applicable when actorType is seller; other entries are excluded when this filter is present.

resolutionOutcome.description:
Filter logs by a specific resolution outcome value.

Typical values include decisions such as refund_approved_full, refund_approved_partial, refund_rejected, adjustment_applied, or escalation_required. Exact allowed values are defined by the business logic and stored in the shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs table.

createdFrom.description:
Start of the creation timestamp range filter (inclusive).

When provided together with createdTo, only logs whose created_at is between createdFrom and createdTo are returned.

createdTo.description:
End of the creation timestamp range filter (inclusive).

When provided together with createdFrom, only logs whose created_at is between createdFrom and createdTo are returned.

IShoppingMallDisputeResolutionLog.description:
Detailed representation of a single dispute resolution log entry from the shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs table.

Each log records one resolution decision or event applied to an order dispute, including which actor took the action, the outcome, and optionally the rationale and internal notes. It is used for audit, compliance, and support analysis to understand how disputes were handled over time.

This DTO is designed as a detail response type for administrative tooling. It embeds summary views of the associated order dispute and human actors (seller or platform administrator) so that a single API call provides all necessary context for reviewing the resolution history.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute resolution log record in shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs.

This value is the primary key of the underlying database row and is used as the path parameter `disputeResolutionLogId` in the detail retrieval endpoint.

oneOf.description:
Type of actor that produced this resolution event.

- seller: Action taken by a seller account
- platform_admin: Action taken by a platform administrator account
- automated_rule: Action taken automatically by a configured fraud or business rule

Type of actor that produced this resolution event.

- seller: Action taken by a seller account
- platform_admin: Action taken by a platform administrator account
- automated_rule: Action taken automatically by a configured fraud or business rule

Type of actor that produced this resolution event.

- seller: Action taken by a seller account
- platform_admin: Action taken by a platform administrator account
- automated_rule: Action taken automatically by a configured fraud or business rule

actorType.description:
Type of actor that produced this resolution event.

- seller: Action taken by a seller account
- platform_admin: Action taken by a platform administrator account
- automated_rule: Action taken automatically by a configured fraud or business rule

orderDispute.description:
Summary of the order dispute to which this resolution event belongs.

This replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_order_dispute_id` and provides enough context (such as dispute status, reason, and key identifiers) for platform administrators to understand which dispute this log entry refers to without additional API calls.

platformAdmin.description:
Summary of the platform administrator who created or approved this resolution event when `actorType` is `platform_admin`.

When the event was not performed by a platform administrator (for example, `seller` or `automated_rule`), this field is `null`. This replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` with a structured summary of the admin actor.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller who created this resolution event when `actorType` is `seller`.

When the event was not performed by a seller (for example, `platform_admin` or `automated_rule`), this field is `null`. This replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_seller_id` with a structured summary of the seller actor.

resolutionOutcome.description:
Machine-readable code describing the outcome of this resolution decision.

Examples include values such as `refund_approved_full`, `refund_approved_partial`, `refund_rejected`, `adjustment_applied`, or `escalation_required`. Exact allowed values are defined by business rules and stored in the disputes subsystem.

resolutionRationale.description:
Human-readable explanation for why this resolution outcome was chosen.

May be null when the decision was automated, when the rationale was captured in external systems, or when no additional explanation was provided.

notesInternal.description:
Internal-only notes associated with this resolution event.

Intended for platform administrators and compliance staff. This field may contain sensitive commentary and is never exposed to end customers or sellers. It is null when no internal notes were recorded.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this resolution event was recorded in the system.

The value is stored in UTC and represents the creation time of the underlying database row in `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs`.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleDefinition.description:
Main entity DTO representing a persisted fraud rule definition in the shoppingMall platform.

This type maps to a row in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` Prisma model, which stores configurable fraud and risk rules evaluated against orders, payments, customer accounts, seller accounts, or other events. Each rule is uniquely identified by a stable business-level `ruleCode` string and includes metadata such as a display name, description, category, severity, technical scope, activation flag, the serialized rule expression interpreted by the fraud engine, and lifecycle timestamps.

The DTO is used primarily as a response type for creation, update, and detail retrieval operations. It exposes the non-nullable core columns of the Prisma model—including `scope`, `is_enabled`, `rule_expression`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`—so that administrators and risk analysts can fully understand how the rule is configured, where it applies, and when it was last changed. Nullable columns like the free-form textual description are represented as optional business metadata rather than required fields, reflecting database nullability while still providing rich documentation when present.

id.description:
Primary key identifier of this fraud rule definition record.

This value corresponds directly to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` Prisma model, which is typically implemented as a UUID generated by the database or application layer. It is exposed in admin APIs so that internal tools and logs can unambiguously reference and correlate this rule definition across audit trails, configuration change logs, and monitoring systems.

ruleCode.description:
Globally unique business identifier for this fraud rule definition.

This field maps to the `rule_code` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` and is enforced as unique at the database level. It is a stable, human-readable code—such as `HIGH_REFUND_RATE` or `MULTIPLE_CARDS_SAME_IP`—used across admin interfaces, exports, configuration bundles, and incident tickets to refer to the rule without exposing the internal primary key.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the fraud rule definition.

The value comes from the non-nullable `name` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` table and is shown prominently in back-office tools, rule lists, and detail views. It should succinctly summarize the rule’s purpose so that risk operators can quickly recognize it when scanning large rule sets.

description.description:
Detailed explanation of what this fraud rule does and under which conditions it is expected to trigger.

This text corresponds to the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`. It may be omitted or empty for simple rules, but when present, it should provide business context, examples, and guidance for how the rule should be interpreted and maintained over time. Admin UIs can treat an empty or missing description as an indication that further documentation is recommended.

category.description:
High-level logical category or domain of the fraud rule from the platform’s perspective.

Unlike `scope`, which is stored in the Prisma model as a technical scope column, this field provides an optional business grouping layer—such as `payment`, `account`, `logistics`, or `session`—used in dashboards, filters, and reports. It is not required for every rule and may be left unset when the platform chooses to rely solely on `scope` and severity for classification.

severity.description:
Severity level of this fraud rule, representing how risky it is when the rule triggers.

This property reflects the non-nullable `severity` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` and is typically constrained by business logic to values such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. Downstream workflows, alerting policies, and dashboards use this value to prioritize violations and determine which teams must respond and how quickly.

scope.description:
Technical scope describing which entity domain this fraud rule applies to.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `scope` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` Prisma model. Typical values indicate the primary evaluation context of the rule, such as `order`, `payment`, `customer_account`, `seller_account`, or `session_activity`. Risk analytics, rule search filters, and execution engines use this scope to determine which events or records should be evaluated against the rule and how to group rules in administrative views.

isEnabled.description:
Flag indicating whether this fraud rule is currently active and evaluated by the fraud engine.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable `is_enabled` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`. When `true`, the rule is loaded into the fraud engine and evaluated against matching events or entities according to its scope and condition. When `false`, the rule definition remains stored for history and potential reuse, but it does not contribute to current risk decisions or generate new violations.

condition.description:
Serialized representation of the rule’s condition or expression definition as understood by the fraud engine.

This field is a direct projection of the non-nullable `rule_expression` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`. It typically contains a JSON payload or domain-specific language (DSL) string that encodes thresholds, field references, and logical operators that the fraud engine uses to determine whether a rule is triggered. Provider implementations must validate that this expression is syntactically and semantically valid for the configured engine before persisting it, and any errors should be surfaced as validation failures to the caller.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this fraud rule definition record was first created.

This property exposes the non-nullable `created_at` column from the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` Prisma model and is returned as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string. Administrators and risk analysts can use it to understand how long a rule has been in effect, correlate rule introductions with incident timelines, and audit configuration changes over time.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this fraud rule definition was last updated.

This value corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` and is returned as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string. It changes whenever mutable attributes such as `name`, `description`, `severity`, `scope`, `is_enabled`, or `rule_expression` are modified. Admin consoles and audit reports rely on this field to highlight recently changed rules and to support change approval workflows.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleDefinition.IReques.description:
Search, filtering, and pagination parameters for querying fraud rule definitions in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` table.

This schema is used as the request body for the PATCH `/shoppingMall/platformAdmin/fraudRuleDefinitions` endpoint. Each property corresponds to one or more columns in the underlying Prisma model, such as `rule_code`, `name`, `description`, `severity`, `scope`, `is_enabled`, and `updated_at`, and allows platform administrators and risk operators to retrieve a tailored, paginated subset of fraud and risk rules for analysis and management.

rule_code_prefix.description:
Optional prefix filter applied to the `rule_code` column.

When this value is provided, the search returns only those fraud rule definitions whose `rule_code` begins with the given prefix. This is especially useful when rules follow naming conventions or are grouped by a shared prefix representing a feature area or risk category.

scopes.description:
Optional list of rule scopes to include in the result set.

Each entry should match a value stored in the `scope` column of `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`, such as `order`, `payment`, `customer_account`, `seller_account`, or `session_activity`. When this array is provided and non-empty, only rules whose `scope` is contained in this list will be returned.

severities.description:
Optional list of severity levels to filter on.

Values should correspond to those stored in the `severity` column, typically strings like `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. When supplied, the query restricts results to rules whose `severity` is one of the provided values, allowing administrators to focus on higher- or lower-severity rules as needed.

is_enabled.description:
Optional filter on the `is_enabled` activation status of rules.

When this property is present, only fraud rule definitions whose `is_enabled` column matches the given boolean value are returned. For example, setting this to `true` retrieves only currently active rules, while `false` returns only disabled rules retained for audit or future review.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to human-readable fields.

Implementations typically apply this term to the `name` and `description` columns using case-insensitive containment or full‑text search. This allows operators to find rules based on keywords or phrases without knowing the exact `rule_code` or other structured attributes.

page.description:
1-based page index used for paginating the list of matching fraud rule definitions.

If omitted, servers may default this value to 1, representing the first page of results. Combined with `limit`, it determines which slice of the overall result set is returned to the caller.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return in a single page of results.

This value works together with `page` to implement pagination. Service implementations should enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large responses and to maintain predictable performance characteristics.

sort_by.description:
Name of the column used to sort the result set.

Typical sortable fields include `rule_code`, `name`, `severity`, `scope`, and `updated_at`. Implementations should restrict this value to a controlled set of safe, indexed columns to avoid malformed queries or inefficient full table scans.

oneOf.description:
Sort the result set in ascending order based on the selected `sort_by` column.

Commonly used when listing rules alphabetically, by oldest creation date, or from lowest to highest severity.

Sort the result set in descending order based on the selected `sort_by` column.

Commonly used to show the most recently updated rules first, or to list higher severity rules before lower severity entries so that risk operators can focus on the most critical items.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction applied to the ordered result set.

This property is used together with `sort_by`. When omitted, servers may choose a sensible default, such as sorting by `updated_at` in descending order to surface the most recently changed rules at the top of the list.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleDefinition.ISummar.description:
Summary view of a fraud rule definition configured in the shopping mall risk engine.

This schema provides a lightweight projection of the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` Prisma model that is optimized for list views, dashboards, and embedded references from other entities such as fraud rule violations. It exposes the most important identifying and status-related attributes administrators and risk operators need to quickly understand which rules exist and how they are currently configured.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the fraud rule definition record.

This value maps directly to the `id` primary key column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` table and is generated by the database. It is mainly used internally for joins, lookups, and audit trails rather than as a human-friendly business identifier.

rule_code.description:
Stable business code for the fraud or risk rule.

This property corresponds to the non-null, unique `rule_code` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`. External systems, configuration tools, log messages, and analytics dashboards reference rules using this code, with typical examples such as `HIGH_REFUND_RATE`, `MULTIPLE_CARDS_SAME_IP`, or `ABUSE_ORDER_VELOCITY`.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the fraud rule definition.

The value is mapped from the non-null `name` column and is shown in administrative UIs, search results, and reports so that risk operators can quickly understand the purpose of a rule without inspecting its underlying configuration expression.

description.description:
Short textual description of what the rule is designed to detect and how it should be handled.

It is sourced from the optional `description` column and usually summarizes the detection logic at a business level, for example highlighting suspicious payment patterns, abnormal order volumes, or account takeover indicators. When not provided, consumers should not rely on this field being present.

scope.description:
Scope of entities or events that this fraud rule evaluates.

This value maps to the non-null `scope` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` table and indicates which domain object the rule targets, such as `order`, `payment`, `customer_account`, `seller_account`, or `session_activity`. Administrative search filters and dashboards frequently group and filter rules by this scope to focus on specific parts of the platform.

is_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether this fraud rule definition is currently active in the risk engine.

This property is derived from the non-null `is_enabled` column and determines whether the rule is evaluated against live data. When `true`, the evaluation engine should consider this rule during fraud checks. When `false`, the rule is logically disabled but retained for history, audit, or future reactivation.

severity.description:
Configured business severity level of the rule when it triggers.

The value is stored in the non-null `severity` column and typically belongs to a controlled set of strings such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. Higher-severity rules may drive stronger enforcement actions, higher alert priority, or stricter manual review workflows within the shopping mall risk operations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this fraud rule definition was first created.

This property mirrors the non-null `created_at` column and is recorded in UTC. It helps administrators and auditors understand when a rule entered the system and supports filtering or sorting rules based on their creation time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this fraud rule definition was most recently updated.

The value maps to the non-null `updated_at` column and is recorded in UTC. Admin tools commonly sort by this field to surface recently changed rules and to support review workflows focused on rules modified within a particular time window.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleDefinition.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for defining a new fraud or risk rule in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used to insert a new row into the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` Prisma model and requires all non-nullable business columns that must be supplied by the caller: `rule_code` (ruleCode), `name`, `scope`, `severity`, `rule_expression` (ruleExpression), and `is_enabled` (isEnabled). System-managed columns such as the primary key, timestamps, and admin actor references are intentionally excluded from this contract.

Fraud rules created through this DTO are later evaluated by the fraud engine against entities in the configured `scope` (for example, order, payment, customer_account, seller_account, or session_activity) using the serialized `ruleExpression` stored in the `rule_expression` column.

ruleCode.description:
Globally unique business identifier for this fraud rule definition.

This value maps to the `rule_code` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` and must be stable and unique so that it can be referenced reliably from admin tools, configuration exports, and fraud analytics dashboards.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the fraud rule definition.

This value maps to the `name` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` and is used throughout administration UIs and reports to help operators quickly understand the purpose of the rule.

description.description:
Detailed explanation of what this fraud rule does and under which conditions it is expected to trigger.

This text maps to the nullable `description` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` and should explain the business intent, examples of suspicious behavior it detects, and any operational guidance for handling alerts produced by this rule.

scope.description:
Scope of entities the rule applies to, mapped to the non-nullable `scope` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

Typical examples include `order`, `payment`, `customer_account`, `seller_account`, or `session_activity`. The scope is used by backoffice search, analytics, and rule execution pipelines to determine where this rule should be evaluated.

severity.description:
Configured severity level of this fraud rule, mapped to the non-nullable `severity` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

Severity is used for prioritization and alerting. Implementations usually restrict this to an allowed set such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`, and downstream dashboards aggregate statistics based on this level.

ruleExpression.description:
Machine-interpretable expression or configuration payload that encodes the rule logic, mapped to the non-nullable `rule_expression` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

This serialized payload (often JSON or a domain-specific expression language) is consumed by the fraud engine to decide whether the rule is triggered for a given entity in the configured scope. Provider implementations must validate that the structure and referenced attributes are compatible with the evaluation engine before persisting it.

isEnabled.description:
Flag indicating whether this rule is currently active, mapped to the non-nullable `is_enabled` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

When `true`, the rule participates in fraud evaluation for matching events. When `false`, the rule is excluded from real-time evaluation but remains stored for historical reference and potential reactivation.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleDefinition.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing fraud rule definition in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is used together with a `ruleCode` path parameter that identifies the target row in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` Prisma model by its unique `rule_code` value. All properties on this type are optional so that callers can perform partial updates; any field that is omitted leaves the corresponding column value unchanged.

Typical use cases include changing the rule’s display name, description, scope, severity, activation flag, or the serialized `ruleExpression` logic. After updates, any in-memory rule caches or compiled rule sets maintained by the fraud engine should be refreshed to keep runtime evaluation in sync with the stored configuration.

name.description:
Updated human-readable display name of the fraud rule definition.

If provided, this value overwrites the `name` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`. If omitted, the existing name remains unchanged.

description.description:
Updated detailed description for the fraud rule.

When supplied, this replaces the existing value in the nullable `description` column, allowing risk operators to refine the explanation and handling guidelines. If omitted, the current description is preserved.

scope.description:
Updated scope of entities the rule applies to, mapped to the `scope` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

Use this field to retarget the rule to a different logical domain, such as switching from `order` to `payment` monitoring. If this property is not included in the request body, the existing scope continues to be used by the fraud engine.

severity.description:
Updated severity level for this fraud rule, mapped to the `severity` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

This value influences operational prioritization and alert routing. When omitted, the previously stored severity value is kept as-is.

ruleExpression.description:
Updated serialized condition or expression definition for the fraud rule, mapped to the `rule_expression` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

When provided, the implementation must validate the new payload according to the fraud engine’s schema and semantics before saving it, to avoid deploying malformed rules. If omitted, the existing serialized ruleExpression continues to be used for evaluation.

isEnabled.description:
Updated activation flag for the fraud rule, mapped to the `is_enabled` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

Set to `true` to enable evaluation of this rule or to `false` to disable it while keeping the configuration for historical or future use. If this property is not present in the payload, the current enablement state is left unchanged.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleViolation.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying fraud rule violations recorded in the shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations table.

This DTO is used by administrative and risk-operations endpoints to express complex analytical filters, sorting options, and pagination controls when searching the fraud rule violation log. It does not represent a database row directly and therefore does not include x-autobe-prisma-schema.

page.description: 1-based page index to retrieve when paginating fraud rule violation search results. Must be a positive integer.

limit.description: Maximum number of violation summaries to return per page. Must be at least 1 and should be capped to a reasonable upper bound (e.g., 200) to protect performance.

sortBy.description: Field name used to sort fraud rule violation results. Typical values include violation timestamp, severity, or rule priority. Exact supported values are enforced server-side.

oneOf.description: Sort direction to apply when ordering fraud rule violation results.
Sort direction to apply when ordering fraud rule violation results.

sortOrder.description: Sort direction to apply when ordering fraud rule violation results.

ruleCodes.description: Optional list of fraud or risk rule codes to include in the search. When provided, only violations associated with these rule codes will be returned.

excludeRuleCodes.description: Optional list of fraud or risk rule codes to explicitly exclude from the search results.
