entityTypes.description: Optional list of entity types that the fraud rules were evaluated against, such as 'order', 'paymentTransaction', 'customer', or 'seller'. Filters results to violations involving these entity types.

entityIds.description: Optional list of concrete entity identifiers (for example, order IDs or payment transaction IDs). When provided, the search is restricted to violations that reference at least one of these entities.

minSeverity.description: Optional minimum severity or risk score threshold. Only violations whose severity is greater than or equal to this value will be included.

maxSeverity.description: Optional maximum severity or risk score threshold. Only violations whose severity is less than or equal to this value will be included.

status.description: Optional list of workflow or review statuses to filter by, for example 'open', 'inReview', or 'resolved'. Only violations whose status is one of the specified values are returned.

decisionOutcomes.description: Optional list of decision outcomes associated with the violation, such as 'allow', 'review', or 'block'. Filters results to violations with one of the given outcomes.

createdFrom.description: Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the violation creation timestamp filter, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string. Only violations created at or after this timestamp are returned.

createdTo.description: Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the violation creation timestamp filter, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string. Only violations created at or before this timestamp are returned.

updatedFrom.description: Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the last-updated timestamp filter, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

updatedTo.description: Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the last-updated timestamp filter, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

search.description: Optional free-text search term used to match against descriptive fields on the fraud rule violations, such as notes, rule descriptions, or evaluation context.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleViolation.description:
Detailed DTO representing a single fraud rule violation recorded in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table.

This type is used by administrative and risk-operations tooling when retrieving the full context of a specific fraud rule violation event. It exposes identifiers, references to the violated rule and impacted entity, severity information, workflow state, temporal details about when the violation occurred and was logged, and optional explanatory notes derived from the rule evaluation payload.

The structure aligns with the underlying Prisma model `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` while presenting fields in a consumer-friendly way (for example, using `entityType` and `entityId` instead of the raw `actor_type` and `actor_id` columns).

id.description:
Unique identifier of the fraud rule violation record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the row in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and is used to retrieve a specific violation for detailed inspection.

ruleCode.description:
Business-facing code of the fraud or risk rule that was violated.

This value is derived from the associated record in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions.rule_code` and is used by analysts to recognize which configured rule fired without needing to load the full rule definition separately.

ruleName.description:
Human-readable name or short description of the fraud or risk rule that was violated.

This is a denormalized convenience field derived from `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions.name` so that risk dashboards and detail views can display the rule name without an additional lookup.

ruleDefinition.description:
Summary view of the fraud rule definition that this violation instance is associated with.

This is the BELONGS-TO association for the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definition_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and provides compact contextual information about the rule that fired, such as business code, name, configured severity, and enabled state.

entityType.description:
Type of the entity that the rule evaluated when the violation occurred.

This field corresponds conceptually to the `actor_type` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and uses logical values such as `order`, `paymentTransaction`, `customer`, or `seller` so that consumers can easily understand what kind of object the violation is attached to.

entityId.description:
Identifier of the concrete entity instance that triggered the violation.

This value is derived from the `actor_id` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and contains an opaque identifier such as an order ID, payment transaction ID, customer ID, or seller ID, depending on `entityType`.

severity.description:
Severity classification string for this violation instance, mapped from the `violation_severity` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations`.

Typical values include semantic levels such as `info`, `warning`, `high`, or `critical` (or another configured severity vocabulary). Risk tools use this classification to prioritize queues and dashboards, and it directly reflects how the rule engine evaluated the underlying signals for this event.

status.description:
Current workflow or review status of the violation, such as `open`, `inReview`, or `resolved`.

This value represents the handling state of the violation within risk-operations workflows. It may be backed by additional workflow tables or materialized views rather than a single physical column on `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations`, and as such it can be omitted when no workflow has been applied yet.

decisionOutcome.description:
Decision outcome that the fraud engine or risk workflow applied in response to this violation.

Typical values include `allow`, `review`, or `block`, indicating how the platform reacted when the violation was evaluated. This outcome may be persisted in separate decision or payment tables and exposed here as a convenient, denormalized view for investigators. Implementations may omit this field when no explicit decision has been recorded yet.

occurredAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the rule evaluation that produced this violation occurred.

This is a direct mapping of the `occurred_at` column in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` and represents the business time at which the suspicious activity or policy violation was detected by the fraud engine.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this fraud rule violation record was stored.

This corresponds to the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and may be slightly later than `occurredAt` depending on processing latency and persistence batch behavior.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this fraud rule violation record was last updated in the risk or workflow subsystem.

Unlike `createdAt`, this field is usually maintained by higher-level workflows (for example, status changes or note updates) rather than a dedicated `updated_at` column. It may be omitted when no subsequent updates have been performed after the record was first created.

notes.description:
Optional free-form notes or descriptive text providing additional context about the violation.

This field consolidates human-readable explanation content derived primarily from the `violation_reason` column and, where appropriate, key highlights from `evaluation_context` in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table. It typically explains why the rule fired, including relevant metric values, threshold comparisons, or evaluation details captured at the time of detection to support manual investigation.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IRequest.description:
Filter, segmentation, and granularity options for computing dispute analytics over the shopping_mall_order_disputes data set.

This DTO is used by platform administrators and risk analysts to request aggregated dispute statistics across the entire shopping mall. It represents a purely analytical, read-only query contract and does not map directly to a single Prisma model. Instead, its fields control how underlying shopping_mall_order_disputes and related tables are filtered and grouped for analytics.

All fields are optional; when omitted, the backend applies sensible defaults such as a recent time window and standard aggregation granularity.

dateRange.description:
Time window over which disputes are analyzed.

If omitted, the implementation may default to a recent period such as the last 30 days. Both start and end timestamps are inclusive and must follow ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

statusFilters.description:
Optional list of dispute statuses to include in the analytics.

When provided, only disputes whose status is one of the specified values are included. If omitted or empty, all statuses are considered.

reasonCategoryFilters.description:
Optional list of high-level dispute reason categories to filter on, such as non_delivery, damaged_item, wrong_item, or service_issue.

Exact values are platform-defined and should match the categorical reason codes stored on disputes.

sellerSegments.description:
Optional segmentation filters describing which seller cohorts to include in analytics.

Each segment filter can represent a logical cohort such as high_volume_sellers, new_sellers, or certain performance bands.

customerSegments.description:
Optional segmentation filters describing which customer cohorts to include in analytics.

Typical segments include new_customers, repeat_customers, high_value_customers, or specific risk bands.

orderConstraints.description:
Optional constraints that limit disputes to those associated with orders matching specific characteristics.

Examples include filtering by payment method, fulfillment status, or minimum order amount.

timeGranularity.description:
Requested granularity for time-series aggregations.

Determines whether analytics should be bucketed by day, week, or month. If omitted, the implementation may choose a default based on the dateRange length.

includeSellerBreakdown.description:
Whether to include seller-level breakdowns in the analytics response.

When true, the response may include per-seller dispute counts, rates, and performance metrics. When false, these breakdowns are omitted for performance.

includeCustomerBreakdown.description:
Whether to include customer-level breakdowns in the analytics response.

When true, the response may include segment-level analytics for customer cohorts such as dispute rates by segment. When false, these breakdowns are omitted.

includeReasonBreakdown.description:
Whether to include dispute reason category breakdowns in the analytics response.

When true, the response includes counts and rates grouped by dispute reason categories. When false, these aggregations are omitted.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IDateRange.description:
Date range boundaries for dispute analytics queries.

Represents an inclusive time window used to select disputes based on creation or event timestamps. The exact timestamp field used by the backend (e.g., created_at or opened_at) is implementation-defined but consistent across usages of this DTO.

start.description:
Inclusive lower bound timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC) for the analytics time window.

Disputes whose relevant timestamp is on or after this value are included.

end.description:
Inclusive upper bound timestamp (ISO 8601, UTC) for the analytics time window.

Disputes whose relevant timestamp is on or before this value are included.

oneOf.description:
Dispute has been created and recorded in `shopping_mall_order_disputes` but has not yet been substantively reviewed.

Typical examples include newly submitted complaints where the platform or seller has not started an investigation or taken action beyond initial acknowledgment.

Dispute is actively being reviewed or investigated by a seller, platform administrator, or automated workflow.

Evidence may be collected, communication with the customer or seller is in progress, and a final decision has not yet been recorded in the system.

Dispute has reached a logged resolution outcome and any associated operational steps (such as refunds, replacements, or adjustments) have been decided and recorded.

At this stage, the system considers the underlying issue addressed, although related financial or fulfillment actions may still be in progress elsewhere in the platform.

Dispute has been escalated beyond the normal handling path, for example to a specialized support team, higher‑tier platform administrator, or external review process.

Escalation typically indicates increased complexity or risk, such as high‑value orders, repeated complaints, or potential fraud indicators, and may feed into separate risk and compliance reporting.

Dispute has been closed and is no longer actively handled in operational workflows.

Closure can occur after a resolution has been completed and any cooling‑off period has passed, or when the dispute is withdrawn or otherwise deemed finished. Closed disputes remain available for historical analytics, trend reporting, and auditing.

IShoppingMallDisputeStatus.description:
Normalized lifecycle status for order-related disputes in the shoppingMall platform.

These values categorize disputes into high-level stages such as newly opened, under active review, resolved, escalated for special handling, or fully closed. They are derived from underlying fields on the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` model and are intended for use in analytics, dashboards, and reporting rather than direct persistence.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.ISellerSeg.description:
Segmentation filter describing a cohort of sellers to include in dispute analytics.

This structure allows admin dashboards to slice dispute metrics by seller characteristics such as performance tier, region, or business category. It is purely analytical and does not map to a single Prisma model.

segmentKey.description:
Identifier for the seller segment dimension, such as performance_tier, seller_region, or business_category.

The exact keys are platform-defined and must be recognized by the analytics implementation.

segmentValues.description:
One or more values within the specified seller segment dimension to include in analytics.

For example, ["gold","platinum"] for performance_tier, or ["KR","US"] for seller_region.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.ICustomerS.description:
Segmentation filter describing a cohort of customers to include when computing dispute analytics.

This structure focuses on customer-centric attributes such as lifecycle stage, risk band, or loyalty tier and is evaluated against the customer identity associated with each dispute, not directly against order rows. It is designed as a reusable analytics helper so that different endpoints can share consistent customer segmentation logic.

In practice, this filter is usually combined with other analytical dimensions such as date ranges, seller segments, and order-level constraint filters. Only disputes whose associated customers satisfy this segment filter (in addition to any other active filters) are included in the analytics result set.

segmentKey.description:
Identifier for the customer segment dimension that this filter applies to, such as `lifecycle_stage`, `risk_band`, or `loyalty_tier`.

The value must match a platform-defined analytics dimension key that the backend recognizes when resolving customer attributes for dispute analytics. Implementations are expected to validate this key against a configured catalog of supported segment dimensions and either reject unsupported values or apply a clearly documented fallback.

Typical examples include:
- `lifecycle_stage` to segment new, returning, and dormant customers
- `risk_band` to differentiate low-, medium-, and high-risk customers
- `loyalty_tier` to represent loyalty program levels or spend tiers.

items.description:
Single value within the chosen customer segment dimension.

Each value must belong to the same logical dimension identified by `segmentKey` and should correspond to a value the analytics backend can resolve from customer profiles (for example a known lifecycle stage or risk band). Providing values that do not match any known customers will typically result in empty or very small result sets for the affected filters.

segmentValues.description:
One or more values within the specified customer segment dimension to include in analytics.

Within this list the semantics are logical OR: a customer is considered part of the cohort if their attribute value for the selected `segmentKey` matches **any** of the entries in `segmentValues`. All values must belong to the same dimension named by `segmentKey`; mixing values from different conceptual dimensions (for example lifecycle and risk band) is not supported and should be prevented at the caller or validation layer.

Callers should ensure that the provided values stay synchronized with the platform configuration that defines lifecycle stages, risk bands, loyalty tiers, or other segment values. Misspelled or deprecated values may lead to confusing analytics where the filter technically applies but yields no matching customers.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IOrderCons.description:
Optional order-level constraints applied when computing dispute analytics.

This DTO does not mirror a single Prisma model; instead it bundles together filters on attributes that conceptually originate from orders, payments, and fulfillment entities. When present, these constraints are layered on top of the base dispute selection so that only disputes linked to orders matching the specified criteria are included in the analysis window.

Common scenarios include restricting analytics to specific payment instruments (for example, card vs. wallet), focusing on disputes for orders that have reached particular fulfillment states (such as delivered or partially delivered), or analyzing disputes only for orders within certain monetary bands using `minOrderAmount` and `maxOrderAmount`.

items.description:
Single payment method business code associated with an order.

Each value should correspond to a code defined in the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` configuration table, such as `CARD_VISA`, `CARD_MASTERCARD`, `BANK_TRANSFER`, or a local wallet code. These codes are what the analytics pipeline uses when joining disputes to payment transactions.

paymentMethodCodes.description:
Optional list of payment method codes restricting analytics to disputes arising from orders paid with specific methods.

When this field is omitted, the analytics engine does not restrict by payment method and considers disputes for orders paid with any supported instrument. When it is supplied with one or more codes, only disputes for orders whose payment method matches **at least one** of the codes in this list are included in the result.

Client applications should keep these codes synchronized with entries in the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` table to avoid filters that technically run but inadvertently yield no results. Implementations should document whether an explicitly empty array is treated as "no restriction" or a degenerate filter and, in general, callers should prefer omitting the field to represent "no restriction".

items.description:
Single fulfillment or shipping status code representing the operational state of an order or its associated fulfillment aggregates.

The exact values are platform-defined and should align with the fulfillment and shipment status model, such as `PENDING`, `SHIPPED`, `DELIVERED`, `PARTIALLY_DELIVERED`, or `CANCELLED`. These codes are typically derived from `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and `shopping_mall_shipments` when building analytics views.

fulfillmentStatuses.description:
Optional list of fulfillment status codes restricting analytics to disputes associated with orders in certain fulfillment states.

If this field is omitted, dispute analytics include orders regardless of their current fulfillment or shipping state, from pre-shipment through delivery or cancellation. When provided, only disputes tied to orders whose effective fulfillment status matches **any** of the entries in this list are included.

Typical usage patterns include focusing on disputes after delivery (for example using only `DELIVERED` states) or diagnosing operational issues for in-transit orders. Callers should use status values that exactly match the platform’s canonical status codes so that filters behave predictably.

minOrderAmount.description:
Optional minimum order total amount threshold for including a dispute in analytics.

When specified, only disputes whose associated orders have a total value **greater than or equal to** this amount are counted. The currency and unit are determined by the surrounding analytics configuration (for example the platform base currency or a report-specific currency), and callers must ensure that this threshold is expressed in the same context as other monetary parameters used in the request.

Backends should define how they handle edge cases such as extremely large values or combinations where `minOrderAmount` exceeds `maxOrderAmount`, either by returning a validation error or by treating such ranges as yielding an empty result set.

maxOrderAmount.description:
Optional maximum order total amount threshold for including a dispute in analytics.

When specified, only disputes whose associated orders have a total value **less than or equal to** this amount are counted. As with `minOrderAmount`, the numeric value must use the same currency and unit conventions as the rest of the analytics request so that the resulting filters are interpretable by operators.

When both `minOrderAmount` and `maxOrderAmount` are provided, they define an inclusive monetary band on the order total. Clients should take care to configure ranges where `minOrderAmount` is less than or equal to `maxOrderAmount` in order to avoid unintentionally excluding all disputes from the analysis.

oneOf.description:
Enumeration of supported time-series aggregation granularities for dispute analytics.

Determines the size of time buckets when generating time-series metrics such as dispute counts over time.

Enumeration of supported time-series aggregation granularities for dispute analytics.

Determines the size of time buckets when generating time-series metrics such as dispute counts over time.

Enumeration of supported time-series aggregation granularities for dispute analytics.

Determines the size of time buckets when generating time-series metrics such as dispute counts over time.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IETimeGran.description:
Enumeration of supported time-series aggregation granularities for dispute analytics.

Determines the size of time buckets when generating time-series metrics such as dispute counts over time.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IResponse.description:
Aggregated dispute analytics metrics and breakdowns derived from the shopping_mall_order_disputes and related tables.

This DTO is returned by the platform-wide dispute analytics endpoint used in admin dashboards and risk monitoring tools. It encapsulates total volumes, distributions by status and reason, time-series trends, and optional breakdowns by seller and customer segments.

All fields represent computed, read-only values. The DTO does not map directly to a single Prisma model; instead, it aggregates data from shopping_mall_order_disputes, shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_customers, shopping_mall_order_dispute_of_sellers, shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs, and related order/payment tables.

totalDisputes.description: Total number of disputes matching the requested filters within the selected time window.

openDisputes.description: Number of disputes currently in the open status within the filtered set.

underReviewDisputes.description: Number of disputes currently in the under_review status within the filtered set.

resolvedDisputes.description: Number of disputes currently in the resolved status within the filtered set.

escalatedDisputes.description: Number of disputes currently in the escalated status within the filtered set.

closedDisputes.description: Number of disputes currently in the closed status within the filtered set.

disputeRatePerThousandOrders.description:
Dispute rate expressed as the number of disputes per 1,000 orders in the filtered time window.

The denominator is the total number of orders that satisfy the same filters as the disputes.

averageResolutionTimeHours.description:
Average time required to resolve disputes, measured in hours.

Calculated using resolution timestamps from shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs for disputes that have been resolved within the filtered set.

p90ResolutionTimeHours.description:
90th percentile of resolution time in hours for resolved disputes within the filtered set.

Useful for understanding worst-case resolution performance.

statusDistribution.description:
Distribution of disputes by status, represented as counts and optional percentages.

This structure provides a more detailed breakdown than the top-level counts.

reasonDistribution.description:
Distribution of disputes by reason category, represented as counts and optional percentages for each category.

Only populated when the request asked to include reason breakdowns.

timeSeries.description:
Time-series of dispute metrics over the requested date range, bucketed using the requested granularity.

Each point represents aggregated values for a single day, week, or month.

topSellersByDisputeRate.description:
Optional list of sellers with the highest dispute rates within the filtered window.

Only populated when the request includes seller breakdowns and the backend is configured to compute these metrics.

topCustomerSegmentsByDisputeRate.description:
Optional list of customer segments that exhibit the highest dispute rates in the filtered window.

Only populated when the request includes customer breakdowns.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IStatusDis.description:
Distribution of order-related disputes by their normalized business status, computed from the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` table and any joined analytical views.

This object represents the result of an analytics query for a specific filter set (such as date range, seller segment, customer cohort, or region). The `byStatus` collection contains one bucket per dispute status that has at least one matching record in the filtered population.

Consumers MUST NOT assume that all possible dispute statuses will appear in the `byStatus` array. If no disputes exist for a given status in the filtered set, that status may simply be omitted. Likewise, the array may legitimately be empty when the filter criteria match no disputes at all.

The order of elements in `byStatus` is not guaranteed and should not be relied upon for business logic. Client dashboards are expected to sort or group the buckets as needed for visualization.

This DTO is a read-only analytical projection and is never persisted directly; it is derived at query time from transactional data models rather than mapped one-to-one to a single Prisma entity.

byStatus.description:
Collection of per-status analytics buckets for the current dispute query.

Each bucket corresponds to a single `IShoppingMallDisputeStatus` value that appears at least once in the filtered dispute set and exposes the absolute count of disputes in that status and, optionally, the percentage of the total.

The set of buckets is determined entirely by the upstream analytics filters (for example, date range, seller, customer segment, or region). Implementations SHOULD treat this array as the authoritative source for per-status counts for the given query, rather than re‑deriving the distribution on the client side.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IStatusBuc.description:
Single analytics bucket aggregating disputes that currently share a specific normalized business status.

Each bucket originates from one or more rows in the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` table that satisfy the analytics request filters and whose status is mapped to the given `IShoppingMallDisputeStatus` value.

This structure is optimized for charting and tabular reporting: `count` exposes the raw number of matching disputes, while `percentage`, when present, expresses the relative share of this status among all disputes in the filtered set.

status.description:
Normalized business status assigned to all disputes represented by this bucket.

This value is derived from the underlying dispute lifecycle fields on the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` model and indicates where the dispute currently resides in the after‑sales handling process (for example, newly opened, under active review, escalated for special handling, resolved, or fully closed).

count.description:
Total number of disputes in this status within the current analytics filter scope.

This is a non‑negative integer calculated over the subset of disputes that match the request criteria (such as date window, seller, customer segment, or region). Client code may sum the `count` values across all buckets to obtain the total dispute volume for the query.

percentage.description:
Optional percentage share of this status out of the total number of disputes in the filtered analytics set.

The value is typically expressed as a real number between 0 and 100 inclusive. Implementations may apply rounding, so the sum of `percentage` values across all buckets may not equal exactly 100. Consumers should treat this field as a convenience for visualization rather than a source of exact high‑precision ratios.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IReasonDis.description:
Distribution of disputes by reason category within a given analytics scope.

This type represents an aggregated view computed from the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` table and related entities after all filters and constraints from the dispute analytics request have been applied (for example, date range, seller or customer cohorts, order constraints, and time granularity).

The distribution groups all matching disputes by their primary business reason code, such as `non_delivery`, `damaged_item`, or `service_issue`, and summarizes how frequently each category occurs. Consumers typically use this DTO to power dashboards, reports, or monitoring views that highlight the dominant causes of disputes in the selected slice of data.

byReason.description:
Array of aggregated dispute buckets grouped by reason category for the current analytics scope.

Each element in this collection represents a single logical dispute reason category and contains both raw counts and optional percentage information for that category. Implementations SHOULD ensure that each reason category appears at most once in this array for a given response so clients do not need to merge duplicate buckets.

When no disputes match the analytics request filters, this array is returned as an empty list. Buckets are commonly ordered in descending order of `count` to make the most frequent reasons appear first, but clients must not rely on a specific ordering unless explicitly documented by the corresponding API operation.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IReasonBuc.description:
Single aggregated analytics bucket for a specific dispute reason category.

Each bucket summarizes how many disputes fall into a particular business reason category within the analytics scope defined by the parent request (for example, date range, seller or customer segment, and other filters). The bucket may additionally expose the percentage share of that reason relative to all disputes in the same filtered data set.

These buckets are computed from `shopping_mall_order_disputes` records and related tables and are intended for read‑only analytics and reporting. They do not correspond to a single row in the database but rather to an aggregate projection over many disputes.

reasonCategory.description:
Dispute reason category code represented by this bucket.

This value is a platform-defined, machine-oriented code (typically in `snake_case`) that classifies the primary cause of the dispute, for example `non_delivery`, `damaged_item`, `wrong_item_received`, or `service_quality_issue`. It MUST correspond to one of the supported reason codes attached to dispute records in the underlying data model.

Client applications should treat this field as an opaque code and resolve it to human‑readable labels and localized descriptions using their own mapping tables or configuration, rather than attempting to parse or infer meaning directly from the code string.

count.description:
Number of disputes in the analytics result set that are classified with this reason category.

The count is computed AFTER applying all filters from the surrounding analytics request, including date range, seller or customer segments, order constraints, and any additional conditions. Therefore, it always represents the number of matching disputes for this specific bucket within the same filtered population and not a global, platform‑wide count.

The value is always a non‑negative integer (0 or greater). A value of `0` is uncommon but can appear in edge cases where a bucket key is included for completeness even though no disputes currently match it in the filtered data.

percentage.description:
Optional percentage share of disputes in this bucket relative to the total number of disputes in the same filtered analytics scope.

The value is expressed as a numeric percentage in the inclusive range from 0 to 100, for example `37.5` for thirty‑seven and a half percent. Implementations typically compute this value as `(bucket_count / total_count) * 100` and MAY apply rounding to a reasonable number of decimal places. Because of rounding and possible exclusion of certain categories, the sum of percentages across all buckets in a distribution may not be exactly 100.

This field may be omitted when the API chooses not to compute percentage information, for example to optimize performance for large data sets or when only raw counts are required by the client.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.ITimeSerie.description:
Aggregated dispute analytics for a single time bucket within a dispute time series.

This object is a derived analytical projection built over the underlying shopping_mall_order_disputes data set and related order tables. It does not correspond to a single Prisma row but instead summarizes how many disputes occurred and how frequently they occurred relative to order volume within a specific bucket of the overall analysis window.

The size and alignment of each bucket (for example, day, week, or month boundaries) are controlled by the time granularity and date range parameters in the parent IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IRequest that produced this result.

bucketStart.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC representing the inclusive start of this analytical time bucket.

All disputes whose relevant timestamp (typically the dispute creation timestamp, or a configured business timestamp in the analytics request) is greater than or equal to this value and strictly less than the next bucket's start belong to this bucket.

bucketEnd.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC representing the inclusive end boundary used to materialize this time bucket.

The [bucketStart, bucketEnd] pair defines the exact interval of the analysis window covered by this point. Implementations typically treat bucketEnd as the last instant included in the bucket when computing dispute and order aggregates.

totalDisputes.description:
Total number of disputes whose relevant timestamp falls inside this time bucket.

The relevant timestamp is usually the dispute creation time or another primary business timestamp as defined by the analytics query. This value is an aggregate count across all qualifying orders and actors, not the count of rows from a single Prisma table only.

disputeRatePerThousandOrders.description:
Dispute rate per 1,000 qualifying orders observed within this time bucket.

This value is computed as:

`(number of disputes in this bucket / number of successfully placed orders in this bucket) * 1000`.

The numerator and denominator both respect the same filters, actor scopes, and date range that were specified in the parent dispute analytics request, so clients can safely compare this rate across buckets within the same response.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.ISellerDis.description:
Analytics metrics for a specific seller within a dispute analytics response.

Each instance represents aggregated dispute behaviour for a single seller over the same filtered time window and constraints that were used in the parent IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.IRequest.

These metrics are computed at query time from shopping_mall_order_disputes and related order/payment data and are exposed as read-only analytics values that help operators and reporting tools compare seller performance and risk levels.

sellerId.description:
Unique identifier of the seller whose metrics are represented by this record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_seller Prisma model and is used by clients to correlate analytics data with seller account details in other parts of the API.

sellerDisplayName.description:
Human-readable display name of the seller, typically the seller's brand name or store name as resolved at query time.

Because this value is derived from mutable seller profile data, it may change over time even though historical analytics rows remain associated with the same sellerId.

totalDisputes.description:
Total number of disputes associated with this seller within the filtered analytics window.

The count respects the same date range, dispute filters, and segmentation (for example, by reason category or status) that were applied in the parent dispute analytics request, and includes only disputes where this seller is the responsible party for the underlying order lines.

disputeRatePerThousandOrders.description:
Number of disputes per 1,000 orders handled by this seller within the filtered analytics window.

This metric is calculated as:

`(dispute count for this seller / number of completed or otherwise counted orders for this seller) * 1000`,

using the same time range and filter criteria defined in the dispute analytics request. It is intended for relative comparisons between sellers rather than as a raw count.

IShoppingMallDisputeAnalytics.ICustomerS.description:
Analytics metrics for a specific customer segment within the dispute analytics result.

Represents how a defined customer cohort contributes to overall dispute volume and rate.

segmentKey.description:
Identifier of the customer segment dimension represented by this metric record.

Must match a segmentKey used in customer segmentation configuration, such as lifecycle_stage or risk_band.

segmentValue.description: Specific segment value within the dimension represented by this metric record, such as "new", "returning", or "high".

totalDisputes.description: Total number of disputes associated with customers in this segment within the filtered time window.

disputeRatePerThousandOrders.description: Number of disputes per 1,000 orders placed by customers in this segment within the filtered time window.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleAnalytics.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for querying fraud rule analytics and performance metrics.

This schema captures all filter and segmentation options that platform administrators can use to compute analytics for fraud rule definitions and their recorded violations. It is purely an analytics filter object and does not correspond to any single Prisma model.

from.description:
Start of the analysis time window in ISO 8601 date-time format (inclusive).

All fraud rule violations with timestamps greater than or equal to this value are considered for analytics. Typically represents the beginning of the period being analyzed, such as the start of a day, week, or month.

to.description:
End of the analysis time window in ISO 8601 date-time format (exclusive).

All fraud rule violations with timestamps strictly less than this value are considered for analytics. Together with `from`, defines the analysis period.

oneOf.description:
Time-series granularity used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics.

Determines how violation counts and other analytics are grouped over time. For example, `hour` produces per-hour data points, while `day` and `week` produce coarser aggregates.

Time-series granularity used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics.

Determines how violation counts and other analytics are grouped over time. For example, `hour` produces per-hour data points, while `day` and `week` produce coarser aggregates.

Time-series granularity used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics.

Determines how violation counts and other analytics are grouped over time. For example, `hour` produces per-hour data points, while `day` and `week` produce coarser aggregates.

Time-series granularity used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics.

Determines how violation counts and other analytics are grouped over time. For example, `hour` produces per-hour data points, while `day` and `week` produce coarser aggregates.

timeGranularity.description:
Time-series granularity used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics.

Determines how violation counts and other analytics are grouped over time. For example, `hour` produces per-hour data points, while `day` and `week` produce coarser aggregates.

ruleIds.description:
Optional list of specific fraud rule identifiers to focus the analytics on.

When provided, analytics are computed only for the referenced rules. When omitted, analytics consider all active rules in the system.

ruleCategories.description:
Optional list of rule categories to include in the analysis.

Categories are logical groupings such as `device_fingerprint`, `velocity`, `ip_reputation`, or `behavioral`. When provided, only violations for rules within these categories are analyzed.

severities.description:
Optional list of violation severity levels to include.

Severity values typically represent how risky or critical the rule hit is considered (for example, `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`). When provided, analytics are limited to violations whose severity is one of the selected levels.

eventTypes.description:
Optional list of event types against which fraud rules are evaluated.

Common examples include `order`, `payment`, `account`, or `session`. When provided, analytics are computed only for violations tied to these event types.

includePerRuleBreakdown.description:
Flag indicating whether to include detailed per-rule breakdown tables in the analytics response.

When true, the response will contain per-rule metrics such as hit counts, hit rate, and severity distributions. When false, only high-level aggregates and time-series data may be returned.

includeTimeSeries.description:
Flag indicating whether to include time-series data in the analytics response.

When true, the response includes arrays of time-bucketed metrics that can be rendered as charts. When false, time-series sections may be omitted to reduce payload size.

includeSeverityBreakdown.description:
Flag indicating whether to include violation counts grouped by severity.

When true, the analytics response includes aggregated counts of violations per severity level across the selected period and filters.

includeRuleCategoryBreakdown.description:
Flag indicating whether to include violation counts grouped by rule category.

When true, the analytics response includes aggregated counts of violations per rule category across the selected period and filters.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleAnalytics.IRuleMet.description:
Per-rule analytics metrics for a single fraud rule.

Represents aggregated performance information for a specific fraud rule over the requested analysis period. Metrics are derived from `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` joined to `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` and related transaction entities.

ruleId.description:
Unique identifier of the fraud rule for which these metrics were computed.

This value corresponds to the primary key of a record in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

ruleName.description:
Human-readable name of the fraud rule.

Typically comes from `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions` and is used for display in dashboards and reports.

ruleCategory.description:
Logical category of the fraud rule.

Examples might include `device_fingerprint`, `velocity`, `ip_reputation`, `behavioral`, or other domain-specific groupings used by risk teams.

severity.description:
Configured default severity level of this rule.

Represents the typical risk level assigned when this rule is triggered, such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`.

totalViolations.description: Total number of times this rule was triggered (violations) within the requested analysis period and filters.

uniqueEntitiesAffected.description:
Number of unique entities affected by this rule during the analysis period.

Depending on how analytics is implemented, this might represent unique customers, orders, or payment transactions that triggered the rule.

hitRatePerThousand.description:
Approximate hit rate of this rule per 1,000 evaluated events within the selected period.

Calculated as `(total violations / total evaluated events) * 1000` and used to compare rule activity normalized for traffic volume.

falsePositiveRate.description:
Estimated false-positive rate for this rule over the analysis period.

Computed using downstream labels or decision outcomes when available (for example, cases where the rule fired but the transaction was ultimately approved as legitimate). A value between 0 and 1, where 0 means no known false positives and 1 means all recorded hits are deemed false positives.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleAnalytics.ITimeSer.description:
Single time-series data point aggregating fraud rule violations over a specific time bucket.

Time buckets are defined based on the `timeGranularity` specified in the request (for example, hourly, daily, or weekly).

bucketStart.description: Start timestamp of the time bucket represented by this data point, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

bucketEnd.description: End timestamp of the time bucket represented by this data point, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

totalViolations.description: Total number of fraud rule violations recorded within this time bucket, across all rules that match the current filters.

uniqueRulesTriggered.description: Number of distinct fraud rules that triggered at least once within this time bucket.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleAnalytics.ISeverit.description:
Analytics bucket aggregating fraud rule violations for a specific severity level.

This type is used only in analytics responses and is not persisted directly in the database. Each instance represents a computed summary over a caller-defined analysis period and filter set, such as time range, actor segments, or rule subsets.

The `severity` value corresponds to a logical severity label defined by the fraud and risk engine (for example `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`). The `totalViolations` field represents the aggregated count of fraud rule violations that were classified at this severity level within the effective analysis window and filters.

severity.description:
Logical severity label for this bucket.

Typical values are severity levels defined in the fraud and risk configuration such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`. The exact set of supported severities is determined by the platform’s fraud rule configuration and may be extended over time.

Clients should treat this as a displayable label and should not assume it is an enum enforced at the API contract level.

totalViolations.description:
Total count of fraud rule violations that fall into this severity level.

This value is computed over the requested analysis period and any active filters (such as actor type, region, or rule subset). It represents the number of violation events observed, not the number of unique actors or orders.

The count is non‑negative and may be zero when no violations of this severity were detected in the selected window.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleAnalytics.IRuleCat.description:
Analytics bucket aggregating fraud rule violations for a specific rule category.

This DTO is produced by fraud rule analytics queries and is not a direct projection of a single database row. Each instance groups together all violations for one logical fraud rule category over the requested analysis period and filter set.

The `ruleCategory` value should align with the business-facing category identifiers used when defining fraud rules (for example `device_fingerprint`, `velocity`, `ip_reputation`, or other configured categories). The `totalViolations` field is the aggregated count of violation events attributed to rules in this category within the analysis scope.

ruleCategory.description:
Business-facing identifier of the fraud rule category represented by this bucket.

Examples include categories such as `device_fingerprint`, `velocity`, `ip_reputation`, or other logical groupings defined in the platform’s fraud and risk configuration. The value is treated as an opaque string by the API but should match a known category key on the server side.

Clients typically use this field for labeling charts, tables, or dashboards that break down fraud activity by category.

totalViolations.description:
Total number of fraud rule violation events attributed to rules in this category.

This count is computed over the analysis period and filters supplied in the analytics request, aggregating all violations generated by rules whose category matches `ruleCategory`.

The value is always a non‑negative integer and may be zero when no violations for this category were recorded in the selected time window.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleAnalytics.IRespons.description:
Response DTO containing fraud rule analytics and performance metrics.

This schema represents a denormalized analytics view derived from `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`, `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations`, and related order/payment/account tables. It is designed to be rendered directly on risk dashboards used by platform administrators.

The response does not map to a single Prisma model and therefore omits `x-autobe-prisma-schema`. All fields are computed or aggregated values, not raw database rows.

from.description: Echo of the start of the analysis time window used to compute these analytics, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

to.description: Echo of the end of the analysis time window used to compute these analytics, in ISO 8601 date-time format.

oneOf.description: Time-series granularity actually used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics for this response.
Time-series granularity actually used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics for this response.
Time-series granularity actually used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics for this response.
Time-series granularity actually used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics for this response.

timeGranularity.description: Time-series granularity actually used when computing trend charts and time-bucketed metrics for this response.

totalViolations.description: Total number of fraud rule violations recorded within the requested analysis period and filters.

uniqueRulesTriggered.description: Number of distinct fraud rules that triggered at least once during the analysis period.

perRuleMetrics.description:
Optional array of per-rule analytics metrics, one element per fraud rule that matches the current filters.

Included when the request asked for per-rule breakdowns (`includePerRuleBreakdown = true`). Each entry summarizes key performance metrics for a single rule, such as total violations and hit rate.

timeSeries.description:
Optional array of time-series data points describing how overall fraud rule activity changed over time.

Included when the request asked for time-series data (`includeTimeSeries = true`). Each element corresponds to a discrete time bucket defined by the chosen `timeGranularity`.

severityBreakdown.description:
Optional array of severity-level buckets describing how violations are distributed by severity across the selected period.

Included when the request asked for severity breakdowns (`includeSeverityBreakdown = true`).

ruleCategoryBreakdown.description:
Optional array of rule-category buckets describing how violations are distributed across different categories of fraud rules.

Included when the request asked for rule category breakdowns (`includeRuleCategoryBreakdown = true`).

IShoppingMallAdminOpsOverview.description:
Administrative operations overview snapshot aggregating key metrics and counts for the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO is designed for dashboard use by platform administrators and aggregates high-level operational metrics from multiple underlying Prisma models such as orders, cancellations, returns, disputes, refunds, seller performance summaries, and audit logs. It intentionally exposes structured summary sections instead of raw table rows so that admin UIs can render tiles, charts, and widgets directly from this single response object.

orderPipeline.description:
Summary statistics for the current order pipeline across the marketplace.

Typically includes counts of orders in key lifecycle stages such as newly placed, in processing, shipped, delivered, and cancelled over a recent business period (for example, today or last 7 days).

afterSales.description:
Aggregated metrics for after-sales issues such as cancellations, returns, and disputes.

This section surfaces the current operational load and backlog of unresolved after-sales requests so administrators can quickly assess service quality and potential bottlenecks.

refunds.description:
Aggregated refund-related metrics for the platform.

Includes counts and recent volume of refund transactions to help administrators monitor refund ratios and financial impact of cancellations and returns.

sellerPerformance.description:
High-level seller performance indicators derived from seller performance summaries and related analytics.

Provides counts and key metrics for healthy, under-performing, and high-risk sellers so administrators can take proactive actions.

recentAdminActivities.description:
Recent administrative activities and actions performed by platform administrators.

This section summarizes recent entries that would typically be written into admin audit or configuration change log tables so that operators can see what critical changes were made recently.

IShoppingMallAdminOpsOverview.IOrderPipe.description:
Order pipeline statistics section for the admin operations overview dashboard.

This object groups together high-level counts of customer-facing orders in various lifecycle states so that administrators can quickly see the current operational load and distribution of orders across the processing pipeline.

totalOrders.description:
Total number of customer orders considered in the pipeline snapshot.

The exact time range (for example, today, last 24 hours, or a configured rolling window) is defined by business rules and not specified by the API contract.

newOrders.description:
Number of newly placed orders that have entered the system in the relevant snapshot window.

Typically corresponds to orders that have been created but not yet moved to processing or fulfillment stages.

inProcessingOrders.description:
Number of orders that are currently in processing, picking, packing, or otherwise being prepared for shipment.

These orders have progressed beyond initial placement but have not yet been shipped or completed.

shippedOrders.description:
Number of orders that have been shipped but not yet marked as delivered.

This helps administrators understand how many orders are currently in transit.

deliveredOrders.description:
Number of orders that have been successfully delivered to customers in the snapshot window.

Depending on the business configuration this may represent recently delivered orders or all orders currently in delivered status.

cancelledOrders.description:
Number of orders that are currently in a cancelled status.

This includes orders cancelled by customers, sellers, or the platform, and gives a high-level sense of cancellation volume.

IShoppingMallAdminOpsOverview.IAfterSale.description:
After-sales issues summary section for the admin operations overview dashboard.

This section aggregates counts of open and recently handled after-sales interactions such as cancellation requests, return requests, and order disputes. It is designed to surface operational workload and service quality concerns at a glance.

openCancellationRequests.description:
Number of active cancellation requests that are still pending review or processing.

Derived from entities such as shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests and related subtype tables.

openReturnRequests.description:
Number of active return requests that are still pending approval, inspection, or refund processing.

Derived from tables such as shopping_mall_order_return_requests and related subtype entities.

openDisputes.description:
Number of order-related disputes that are currently open and not yet resolved.

Typically based on shopping_mall_order_disputes and may include disputes opened by customers or sellers.

recentlyResolvedCancellationRequests.description:
Number of cancellation requests that have been resolved within a recent business period (for example, last 7 days).

This metric helps administrators understand the throughput and effectiveness of the cancellation handling process.

recentlyResolvedReturnRequests.description:
Number of return requests that have been resolved within a recent business period.

This includes returns that reached a terminal state such as approved and refunded or rejected after review.

recentlyResolvedDisputes.description:
Number of disputes that have been resolved within a recent business period.

The resolution outcome is not encoded here; the objective is to provide a quick view of dispute handling throughput.

IShoppingMallAdminOpsOverview.IRefundSec.description:
Refund and chargeback summary section for the admin operations overview dashboard.

This object represents a pre-aggregated analytics snapshot over a specific analysis window (for example, the last 24 hours, the last 7 days, or a custom reporting period) rather than a raw list of refund or chargeback transactions.

All monetary values in this section are expressed in the platform’s primary settlement currency as configured by the shoppingMall platform. The counts and totals are typically derived from refund-related entities such as refund transactions, refund line items, and payment chargebacks, and they are optimized for quick, at-a-glance assessment of refund volume and potential revenue leakage on administrative dashboards.

totalRefundTransactions.description:
Total number of refund transactions that fall within the current analysis window.

This count is typically derived from refund transaction records (for example, rows conceptually similar to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions`) and may aggregate across multiple orders, customers, and sellers. A value of `0` is valid and indicates that no refund transactions were recorded during the selected analysis window.

totalRefundAmount.description:
Aggregate monetary amount of refund transactions within the current analysis window.

The amount is generally computed as the sum of refund transaction and line-level amounts (for example, from entities analogous to `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` and related refund items) and is expressed in the platform’s primary settlement currency. A value of `0` is valid and indicates that no refund amounts were processed in the selected period.

totalChargebacks.description:
Total number of chargeback records raised by financial institutions during the current analysis window.

This count is based on payment chargeback data (for example, entities conceptually similar to `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`) and helps administrators understand how often completed payments are being challenged or reversed. A value of `0` is valid and indicates that no chargebacks were recorded within the selected window.

totalChargebackAmount.description:
Aggregate monetary amount of chargeback transactions within the current analysis window.

This amount represents funds that have been or may be reclaimed by financial institutions and is computed from chargeback-related records in the payments domain (for example, data analogous to `shopping_mall_payment_chargebacks`). The value is expressed in the platform’s primary settlement currency. A value of `0` is valid and indicates that there were no chargeback amounts during the selected period.

IShoppingMallAdminOpsOverview.ISellerPer.description:
Seller performance and risk summary section for the admin operations overview dashboard.

This object provides a pre-aggregated snapshot of key seller performance and risk indicators over a specific analysis window (such as the last day, week, or another reporting period), enabling platform administrators to quickly assess marketplace health.

The counts are derived from seller account data, seller performance summaries, risk flags, order disputes, chargebacks, fraud rule violations, and related signals. Exact classification rules that determine whether a seller is considered active, high risk, under review, or suspended are defined by business configuration and risk policies outside of this DTO; this type simply surfaces the resulting aggregate counts for dashboard and analytics use cases.

totalActiveSellers.description:
Total number of sellers that are currently considered active in the marketplace within the context of the selected analysis window.

"Active" is defined by business configuration and may include criteria such as having at least one live listing, recent sales activity, or meeting minimum performance thresholds. This field is an aggregate count only and does not return seller details. A value of `0` is valid and indicates that, according to the configured rules and the selected window, no sellers qualify as active.

highRiskSellers.description:
Number of sellers that are currently classified as high risk during the analysis window.

High-risk classification typically takes into account factors such as accumulated risk flags, elevated refund or chargeback ratios, repeated policy violations, or suspicious activity detected by fraud and risk rules. The exact thresholds and signals are configured in the platform’s risk and compliance policies. This value is an aggregate count, and `0` indicates that no sellers meet the high-risk criteria for the selected period.

underReviewSellers.description:
Number of sellers whose accounts are currently under manual or automated review in the selected analysis window.

Sellers may enter an "under review" state due to unusual performance metrics, dispute patterns, fraud alerts, onboarding checks, or escalations by administrators. This count aggregates all such sellers based on the platform’s review workflows and status fields. A value of `0` is valid and indicates that no sellers are actively under review in the chosen window.

suspendedSellers.description:
Number of sellers whose accounts are currently suspended or otherwise prevented from operating normally on the platform during the analysis window.

Suspensions are usually triggered by severe policy violations, unresolved risk concerns, regulatory issues, or manual administrative actions. This field is an aggregate count only and does not return individual seller identifiers. A value of `0` is valid and indicates that, for the selected period, there are no sellers marked as suspended according to the platform’s status and enforcement rules.

IShoppingMallAdminOpsOverview.IRecentAdm.description:
Recent administrative activities section for the admin operations overview dashboard.

This section provides a compact, chronologically ordered window into the most recent actions taken by platform administrators, such as configuration changes, seller moderation decisions, and risk rule updates. It is designed specifically for use in dashboard widgets and overview screens, where operators need to quickly understand what has changed on the platform without navigating into full audit log views.

The data for this section is typically sourced from one or more underlying admin audit and configuration change log tables. Implementations are expected to apply appropriate recency limits (for example, the last 10–50 events) and to respect any access control rules that determine which activities a given administrator is allowed to see in the UI.

recentActions.description:
Chronologically ordered list of recent administrator actions and configuration changes displayed in the overview dashboard.

Each element is a lightweight summary rather than a full audit record, optimized for quick scanning in a dashboard widget. Implementations should typically order this list by `occurredAt` in descending order so that the most recent actions appear first. When no recent actions exist within the configured time window, this array SHOULD be empty rather than omitted, allowing clients to render an explicit "no recent activity" state.

IShoppingMallAdminOpsOverview.IAdminActi.description:
Summary of a single administrative action or configuration change for use in admin operations overview dashboards.

This DTO is a compact projection of a deeper audit or configuration change log record. It is intentionally limited to the key identifiers and descriptive fields that operators need to quickly understand what happened, who performed the action, and when it occurred, without loading the full technical payload of the change.

Typical usages include lists of recent actions on the admin home screen, sidebars in risk or policy dashboards, or inline contexts where a small number of the latest admin activities provide operational awareness. Clients can use the `actionId` to navigate to a more detailed audit view when an operator needs to investigate a specific change.

actionId.description:
Unique identifier of the administrative action or audit log entry that this summary represents.

In most implementations this will map to a UUID or primary-key value from the underlying `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` or configuration change log table. Client applications can store and reuse this identifier to navigate to a full-detail audit view, correlate the action with related events, or include it in incident and support tickets.

adminDisplayName.description:
Display name or identifier of the administrator who performed the action.

This value is intended to be human-friendly so that operators can immediately recognize the actor. It is typically derived from a username, email address, or full name stored in the administrator profile. The exact formatting is left to the implementation but should be consistent across admin-facing dashboards.

actionType.description:
Short machine-readable code representing the type of action that was performed.

Examples include values such as `CONFIG_UPDATE`, `SELLER_SUSPEND`, `RISK_RULE_CHANGE`, or `REFUND_POLICY_EDIT`. The concrete code set is defined by the platform’s auditing strategy and should be stable over time so that dashboards, filters, and analytics can reliably group and analyze actions by type.

summary.description:
Human-readable summary that describes what the administrator did in a concise sentence or phrase.

The summary should provide enough information for an operator to understand the nature of the change at a glance, for example "Updated refund policy REFUND_STD_001" or "Suspended seller SELLER-123 due to repeated violations". Implementations may localize this text based on the viewer’s locale, but should keep the message brief enough to fit naturally inside dashboard list items and widgets.

occurredAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrative action occurred, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string with timezone information.

This field is used both for ordering recent actions (typically in descending order by recency) and for displaying relative times such as "5 minutes ago" in the UI. The value should reflect the canonical event time recorded in the underlying audit or configuration change log, not the time at which the summary was generated.

IShoppingMallRiskOverviewDashboard.description:
Aggregated risk overview metrics and breakdowns for the shoppingMall platform suitable for an admin dashboard.

This DTO is a read-only analytic projection that composes high-level KPIs and trend information from multiple risk- and fraud-related entities such as risk flags, seller performance summaries, fraud rule definitions and violations, order disputes, and dispute resolution logs. It is designed to give security and operations administrators a single at-a-glance view of the current risk posture of the marketplace.

highLevelKpis.description:
Top-level risk KPIs that summarize the current risk posture of the marketplace.

This typically includes counts of high-risk accounts, open disputes, and recent fraud rule violations aggregated over a recent time window.

riskFlagBreakdown.description:
Breakdown of active risk flags across customers, sellers, or credentials.

Allows administrators to see how many actors fall into different risk categories or severity bands.

fraudRuleViolations.description:
Summary of recent fraud and risk rule violations grouped by rule or category.

This section is derived from fraud rule definition and violation entities and is intended to highlight which rules are most frequently triggered.

disputeAndResolutionStats.description:
Aggregated statistics for order disputes and their resolution outcomes.

Provides a risk-relevant view of dispute volumes and resolution patterns over a recent period.

IShoppingMallRiskOverviewDashboard.IHigh.description:
High-level risk KPIs section for the risk overview dashboard.

This object surfaces a handful of key figures that quickly communicate the current overall risk level on the platform, including counts of high-risk accounts, recent fraud rule violations, and open disputes. All values are computed as part of a read-only analytics query and are intended for dashboard visualization rather than for direct persistence.

activeHighRiskAccounts.description:
Number of accounts (customers, sellers, or underlying authentication credentials) that are currently classified as high risk at the time the dashboard snapshot is generated.

This non-negative count is derived from risk-related entities such as `shopping_mall_risk_flags` and `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries` over the dashboard’s analysis window. Platform administrators use this KPI to understand how many actors are presently considered high risk by the platform’s risk and fraud models.

recentFraudRuleViolations.description:
Number of fraud or risk rule violations recorded within the configured snapshot window for the dashboard.

This metric aggregates violation events from `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` in the context of rule definitions stored in `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`. It is a non-negative count that indicates the recent intensity of fraud- and risk-related activity across the marketplace, helping administrators prioritize investigation and mitigation efforts.

openDisputes.description:
Number of order disputes that are currently open and unresolved when the risk overview dashboard snapshot is produced.

This non-negative count is derived from `shopping_mall_order_disputes` and related subtype entities that track customer, seller, and platform perspectives on disputes. It serves as a high-level KPI for the current backlog of dispute handling work and the overall health of after‑sales and risk operations.

IShoppingMallRiskOverviewDashboard.IRisk.description:
Breakdown of active risk flags by severity and by category for the risk overview dashboard.

This section is a read-only, aggregated snapshot derived from underlying risk flag entities (for example, records stored in shopping_mall_risk_flags and related tables) at the time the dashboard is generated. It does not represent a persisted row by itself, but rather summarized analytics intended to guide administrators.

When either the bySeverity or byCategory arrays are empty, it indicates that there are currently no active risk flags for that dimension in the evaluated time window or scope. This allows the UI to clearly distinguish between "no data" and "zero risk" scenarios.

The breakdown section is typically embedded as part of the broader IShoppingMallRiskOverviewDashboard response, alongside other sections such as high-level KPIs and fraud rule violation summaries. Together, these sections help security and risk operators quickly understand where risk is concentrated across actors, severities, and risk categories, and to prioritize follow-up investigations or policy changes.

bySeverity.description:
Array of entries describing how many active risk flags exist for each severity level within the current dashboard snapshot.

Each element corresponds to a single logical severity bucket (for example, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL) as defined by the platform’s risk classification configuration. Only flags that are considered active at the time of the snapshot are counted, so historical or resolved flags are excluded from these totals.

The array may be empty when there are no active risk flags for any severity during the evaluated period or in the selected filter scope. Dashboard consumers can safely treat an empty array as "no active flagged entities by severity".

byCategory.description:
Array of entries describing how many active risk flags exist for each risk category or type within the current dashboard snapshot.

Category codes are business-defined (for example, PAYMENT_FRAUD, ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER, ABUSE, or other custom risk domains) and usually align with fraud rule definitions or policy taxonomies configured in the platform. Each element aggregates active flags across all actors that fall into the same category code at snapshot time.

The array may be empty if there are no active risk flags for any category in the evaluated time window or filter scope. In that case, dashboards can present this as an absence of currently active categorized risk rather than as an error condition.

IShoppingMallRiskOverviewDashboard.IRisk.description:
Single severity-level aggregation entry for active risk flags in the risk overview dashboard.

Each instance represents one severity bucket, such as LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL, and the total number of currently active risk flags that fall into that bucket at the time the dashboard snapshot is computed.

These entries are typically used to render charts, tables, or badges that allow administrators to quickly assess how risk is distributed across different severity levels, and to drill down into the most critical segments when necessary.

severityCode.description:
Code representing the severity level of the risk flags grouped in this entry.

Typical examples include "LOW", "MEDIUM", "HIGH", or "CRITICAL", but the actual allowed values are governed by the platform’s centralized risk classification scheme. The same severity codes should be used consistently across risk flags, fraud rules, and dashboards so that operators can compare metrics across different views.

Client applications should treat this as an opaque code suitable for display and grouping, and rely on separate configuration or localization layers to provide human-friendly labels when needed.

activeFlagCount.description:
Number of active risk flags that currently have this severity level at the time the dashboard snapshot is computed.

The count aggregates across all relevant actors (such as customers, sellers, and authentication credentials) that have one or more active flags mapped to the given severityCode. Historical, resolved, or expired flags are not included, so the value always reflects the current operational risk load for this severity bucket.

This field is guaranteed to be a non-negative integer. A value of 0 is possible when the bucket is included for completeness even though no active flags are present.

IShoppingMallRiskOverviewDashboard.IRisk.description:
Single category-level aggregation entry for risk flags on the ShoppingMall platform.

This DTO represents a read-only, aggregated projection that groups active risk flags by a logical risk category or type for the current dashboard snapshot. The aggregation is typically derived from rows in the `shopping_mall_risk_flags` table joined with related authentication credential and actor entities, rather than being stored as a dedicated table.

It is used exclusively in analytical responses such as `IShoppingMallRiskOverviewDashboard`, enabling administrators and risk analysts to see how many active flags exist for each category (for example, account takeover risk vs. payment fraud risk) within the currently evaluated time window or filter context.

categoryCode.description:
Code representing the risk category for the grouped flags.

This value corresponds to a logical risk category dimension used when aggregating rows from `shopping_mall_risk_flags` (and related security domain tables). Typical examples include values such as `PAYMENT_FRAUD`, `ACCOUNT_TAKEOVER`, `ABUSE`, or other business-defined categories that may be configured in policy or risk rule definitions.

The code should be stable enough to be used as a key in dashboard visualizations and drill-down links, but it is not necessarily constrained to a fixed enum; the set of valid codes is usually governed by configuration and risk modeling in the backend rather than by this DTO.

activeFlagCount.description:
Number of active risk flags that currently fall into this risk category within the snapshot being queried.

This value is a non-negative aggregated count computed from `shopping_mall_risk_flags` and related records, typically counting only flags that are currently active or open according to the risk engine’s lifecycle rules. Closed, expired, or superseded flags are usually excluded unless the analytics query explicitly asks for historical data.

The count is designed for use in charts and summary tiles on administrative dashboards, helping operators quickly understand where the highest concentration of active risk exists across different categories.

IShoppingMallRiskOverviewDashboard.IFrau.description:
Fraud and risk rule violation summary section for the shoppingMall risk overview dashboard.

This DTO aggregates recent fraud and risk rule violation activity, grouping incidents by rule so that administrators can immediately identify which configured rules are most frequently triggered. The underlying data is typically sourced from the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table joined with rule definitions from `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definitions`.

The time window, actor scoping, and other filters that define "recent" are controlled either by the analytics API request parameters or by backend configuration. The section is read-only and returned as part of a larger `IShoppingMallRiskOverviewDashboard` response to support monitoring, tuning of fraud rules, and investigation workflows.

totalViolations.description:
