IShoppingMallConfig.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a ShoppingMall platform configuration entry backed by the `shopping_mall_configs` Prisma model.

This DTO is optimized for list and overview screens where platform administrators browse configuration namespaces, keys, current effective values, and activation state without loading full descriptions or audit history.

It surfaces a carefully selected subset of columns: `id`, `namespace`, `key`, the current `value` as a human‑readable `valuePreview`, `active` as `isActive`, and `updated_at` as `updatedAt`. Other columns such as `description`, `created_at`, and `deleted_at` are intentionally omitted from this summary representation to keep payloads compact and focused on operational configuration management.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the configuration entry.

This value corresponds to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_configs` Prisma model and is used internally by the service layer and APIs to reference a specific configuration row in an immutable way.

namespace.description:
Logical namespace that groups related configuration keys, such as `checkout`, `payment`, or `reviews`.

This property maps directly to the `namespace` column in the `shopping_mall_configs` table and, together with `key`, participates in the business uniqueness constraint `(namespace, key)`. Administrators typically use this field to filter and organize configuration entries in list views and search screens.

key.description:
Canonical configuration key that identifies this setting within its namespace.

This property maps to the `key` column in the `shopping_mall_configs` Prisma model. Keys are typically hierarchical strings such as `payment.gateway.timeout`, `orders.cancellation.defaultPolicy`, or `reviews.moderation.autoFlagThreshold` and are unique within a given `namespace`.

valuePreview.description:
Short, human‑readable preview of the current configuration value.

This field is derived from the non‑nullable `value` column of the `shopping_mall_configs` table. Backends should truncate or summarize large or structured values (for example JSON blobs) so that this preview remains suitable for compact list displays while still giving administrators a quick sense of the effective setting.

isActive.description:
Indicates whether this configuration entry is currently active for runtime evaluation.

This property mirrors the non‑nullable `active` boolean column in the `shopping_mall_configs` Prisma model. Inactive entries are typically deprecated or scheduled for removal and should generally be excluded from normal configuration resolution logic while remaining available for audit and rollback.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this configuration entry.

This property maps to the non‑nullable `updated_at` column of the `shopping_mall_configs` Prisma model and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time in UTC. It allows administrators to quickly assess when a configuration value was last changed and to correlate configuration changes with operational incidents or behavior changes in dependent systems.

IShoppingMallRegionSetting.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a region configuration entry within the ShoppingMall platform backed by the `shopping_mall_region_settings` Prisma model.

This summary DTO is used when embedding region context into other entities, such as shipping zones or catalog visibility rules, without incurring the cost of returning the full region configuration. It focuses on the primary identifying fields and activation flag that are most useful for administrative UIs and configuration overviews.

Optional metadata columns like `iso_country_code`, `currency_code`, and `timezone`, as well as audit fields such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`, are intentionally omitted to keep this representation compact while still allowing operators to recognize and select the correct region.

id.description:
System‑generated UUID primary key for the region configuration entry.

This field maps to the `id` column of the `shopping_mall_region_settings` Prisma model and uniquely identifies a region record for internal joins, references from other tables, and API operations.

code.description:
Business‑meaningful unique code for the region, such as an ISO country code (for example `US` or `KR`) or a platform‑defined market identifier like `EU_MARKET`.

This property maps to the `code` column in the `shopping_mall_region_settings` table and is typically used in administrative screens, URLs, and integration points as a stable, human‑recognizable identifier for the region.

name.description:
Human‑readable display name of the region used in administrative tools, configuration UIs, and reports.

This field maps directly to the `name` column of the `shopping_mall_region_settings` Prisma model and usually contains values such as `United States`, `European Union`, or localized market names that clearly describe the geographic or business scope represented by the region configuration.

active.description:
Indicates whether this region configuration is active and can be referenced by new policies, shipping zones, or other configuration entries.

This flag mirrors the non‑nullable `active` column in the `shopping_mall_region_settings` table. Inactive regions are typically retained for audit and historical references but should generally be hidden from selection lists and prevented from being used in new configuration assignments.

IShoppingMallShippingZoneSetting.ISummar.description:
Lightweight summary view of a shopping mall shipping zone configuration mapped from the `shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings` Prisma model.

This summary is designed for list responses and as an embedded context object in other DTOs when only core zone identification, activation status, and primary region context are required. It intentionally omits audit timestamps and soft-deletion metadata to keep the payload small while still providing all information typically needed in administrative selection lists and configuration screens.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipping zone setting.

This value corresponds directly to the primary key `id` column of the `shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings` Prisma model and is used as the canonical reference for joins, updates, and deletes in shipping configuration workflows.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the shipping zone.

This maps to the `name` column in `shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings` and is the primary label shown in administrative UIs and internal configuration tools. It is also used in text searches (via the configured GIN or text index) so that operators can quickly locate zones by their descriptive titles.

code.description:
Short, stable business code that uniquely identifies the shipping zone.

This value maps to the `code` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings` table, which has a unique index to guarantee that no two zones share the same code. The code is intended for programmatic references in configuration, routing, integration, and automation logic where a human-readable but stable identifier is preferred over the UUID primary key.

active.description:
Flag indicating whether this shipping zone configuration is currently active.

This field is backed by the non-nullable `active` column in the `shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings` model. When `true`, the zone can be used for shipping method configuration, rate calculation, and administrative selection lists. When `false`, the zone is logically inactive or retired and should normally be excluded from new assignments, although it may still appear in historical records and internal reports.

region.description:
Primary region associated with this shipping zone, represented as a lightweight region summary.

This property is derived from the optional foreign key column `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` on the `shopping_mall_shipping_zone_settings` Prisma model. When present, it provides immediate context about the market or geographic area the zone primarily targets without requiring a separate region lookup. When null or absent, the zone either applies globally or is associated with regions through other configuration mechanisms.

IShoppingMallCategoryTree.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a category tree configuration in the shopping mall catalog, mapped from the `shopping_mall_category_trees` Prisma model.

This summary is intended for list responses, dropdowns, and cross-entity references where clients need to distinguish between catalog trees using their identifiers, codes, names, activation status, and basic descriptive context, without loading full tree configuration or audit metadata.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the category tree.

This value maps to the `id` primary key in the `shopping_mall_category_trees` model and is used as the canonical reference when associating categories, catalog rules, or navigation structures with a specific tree.

name.description:
Display name of the category tree.

This corresponds to the `name` column in `shopping_mall_category_trees` and is the primary label used in administrative tools and configuration screens. The name is typically indexed for text search so that operators can quickly find the correct tree when managing catalog structures.

code.description:
Short, unique business code identifying the category tree.

This field maps to the `code` column in the `shopping_mall_category_trees` table, which is constrained by a unique index to prevent duplicates. The code is intended for programmatic use in routing, configuration, and integration flows where a stable, human-readable identifier is preferable to the UUID primary key.

active.description:
Indicates whether this category tree is currently active and used in catalog flows.

When `true`, the tree is eligible to be used for product navigation, classification, and catalog search. When `false`, the tree is logically retired or disabled and should generally be hidden from end-user experiences while still being available for historical references and administrative review.

description.description:
Optional detailed description of the purpose and scope of this category tree.

This property aligns with the nullable `description` column on the `shopping_mall_category_trees` Prisma model and is typically used to document which products, storefronts, or markets the tree serves, aiding administrators in understanding how and where the tree should be applied.

default_locale.description:
Optional locale identifier that represents the primary language of category labels in this tree.

This value corresponds to the nullable `default_locale` column in the `shopping_mall_category_trees` model and typically contains BCP 47 locale tags such as `en-US` or `ko-KR`. It helps clients and administrative tools choose appropriate localized labels when displaying categories from this tree.

IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a category node within a category tree used when embedding category information into other entities.

Provides enough information to label and link to the category without loading the full tree structure or all children, while also exposing minimal context about the owning category tree as a summary association.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the category node.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_categories` record and is used as the canonical identifier when referencing this category from other DTOs and APIs.

code.description:
Business code that uniquely identifies this category within the shoppingMall platform.

This value maps to the non-nullable `code` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model and is commonly used by integrations, configuration rules, and admin tooling as a stable, human-readable identifier that is safer to expose than the raw UUID `id`.

name.description:
Display name of the category as shown to customers in navigation, filters, and search results.

This value comes from the `name` column of `shopping_mall_categories` and is intended to be human‑readable and localized as appropriate for the storefront.

slug.description:
URL‑friendly unique slug used in category navigation and SEO‑friendly URLs.

Within a single category tree, the combination of tree context and slug is unique, allowing frontends to build stable, readable category URLs without exposing raw identifiers.

fullPath.description:
Human‑readable category path from the tree root to this node, such as "Electronics / Laptops".

This value is typically derived by traversing the `parent_id` chain of `shopping_mall_categories` within a specific `shopping_mall_category_trees` record and concatenating ancestor names. It is denormalized as a scalar to support efficient list rendering and search result display without re-traversing the tree.

active.description:
Indicates whether this category is currently active and visible in catalog navigation and search.

This property reflects the non-nullable `active` column in the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model and allows clients to quickly determine if a category can be used for browsing, product assignment, or filtering without inspecting additional configuration or historical records.

categoryTree.description:
Summary information about the category tree to which this category node belongs.

This is a BELONGS‑TO association that replaces the raw `shopping_mall_category_tree_id` foreign key from the `shopping_mall_categories` Prisma model. It provides minimal context (such as tree code and name) without embedding the full tree structure, and follows the universal `.ISummary` rule for parent references to avoid circular references and over‑fetching.

IShoppingMallPolicySearchResult.description: Aggregated search result view for policy‑related configuration entries in the shopping mall platform. Represents a single hit in a policy search listing, combining minimal information about the matched policy and the configuration scope in which it applies.

policyType.description: High‑level policy type key indicating which policy domain this entry belongs to, such as cancellation, refund, review, or age restriction. Used by clients to branch UI behavior or link to the appropriate detail view.

policyId.description: Unique identifier of the matched policy entity. This value can be used to fetch the full detail of the policy via dedicated policy endpoints.

policyCode.description:
Optional business-level code that identifies the policy within its own policy family, such as a cancellation policy code or refund policy code.

When present, this value corresponds to the `*_policy_code` or similar code column on the underlying policy table and provides a stable, human-readable identifier that is convenient for administrators, routing, and configuration UIs, complementing the opaque `policyId` UUID.

name.description: Human‑readable name or title of the policy, suitable for display in search result rows and administrative lists.

description.description: Short textual summary of the policy content or purpose, usually limited to a brief explanation for quick scanning in search result UIs.

isActive.description: Indicates whether this policy is currently active and considered during runtime evaluations (for example, when validating cancellations, refunds, reviews, or age restrictions).

scope.description: Optional policy scope descriptor indicating the configuration level or targeting, such as global mall‑wide policy, region‑specific policy, category‑specific policy, or seller‑specific override.

priority.description: Numeric priority used when multiple policies could apply to the same situation. Higher priority values typically take precedence during rule evaluation.

IShoppingMallGuestUser.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a guest user entity in the shopping mall platform.

Provides minimal identification and contextual information for unauthenticated visitors that are tracked as guest users. Intended for use in list views, embeddings inside other entities, and situations where only basic guest identity information is required rather than the full guest user record.

This summary type intentionally excludes any sensitive authentication data and low-level tracking fields. It focuses on stable identifiers, display-friendly attributes, and core lifecycle timestamps that can be safely exposed to client applications while still supporting analytics and retention logic.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user record.

This is a stable UUID generated by the system when the guest user entity is created. It is used as the primary reference for associating guest carts, temporary preferences, or other transient data with this guest identity and may appear in logs, analytics, and internal references.

displayName.description:
Human-readable label for the guest user when a name-like value is required.

For most guest flows this may be a generated alias (for example, "Guest-20251115-1234") or a value derived from partial profile information if the guest has provided it. Client applications should treat this field as an easily replaceable label and not as a formally verified real name.

createdAt.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when this guest user record was first created.

Represents the moment when the platform first established a persistent guest identity, such as when a guest cart was initialized or when tracking information was promoted from an ephemeral context into the database. This value is useful for measuring guest lifetime and for applying policies that depend on account age.

updatedAt.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating when this guest user record was last updated.

This field mirrors the non-nullable `updated_at` column on the `shopping_mall_guestuser` Prisma model and changes whenever significant attributes of the guest identity are modified. It is commonly used for analytics, support diagnostics, and data retention or cleanup tasks that operate on "last touched" time rather than initial creation time.

IShoppingMallPlatformadminSession.ISumma.description:
Summary view of a shopping mall platform administrator authentication session.

Provides lightweight information about a specific platform admin session for use in audit logs, security overviews, and administrative session listings. This summary intentionally omits sensitive credential material while exposing identifiers and high-level context needed to trace activity and review security posture.

The owning administrator is represented through an embedded platform administrator summary rather than a raw foreign key, and core connection context such as IP address, entry URL, referrer, and lifecycle timestamps are exposed to support effective monitoring and forensics.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the platform administrator session.

This value is generated by the system when the session is created and is used as the primary key for referencing the session across logs, audits, analytics, and administrative tooling.

platformAdmin.description:
Owning platform administrator account for this session.

This replaces the raw `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` foreign key from the underlying Prisma model with a structured summary representation of the administrator entity. It provides enough context for audit and monitoring views without requiring an additional lookup of the full administrator record.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the session was created.

Recorded as an ISO 8601 UTC datetime. This represents the moment when the administrator successfully authenticated and the session became active, and it is often used as the starting point for session duration and activity analytics.

expiredAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the session expired or was explicitly invalidated.

This field corresponds to the nullable `expired_at` column on the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` Prisma model. When present, it marks the moment after which the session is no longer trusted for authenticated operations. When null, the session may still be considered active subject to additional idle-timeout and revocation rules enforced by the platform.

lastActivityAt.description:
Timestamp of the most recent activity associated with this admin session.

Unlike `createdAt` and `expiredAt`, this value is typically derived from related logging and telemetry data rather than a single Prisma column. It reflects the last time the session was observed making an authenticated request and is used for idle timeout calculations, security monitoring, and investigations into potentially dormant or hijacked sessions. It may be absent or out-of-date if no activity has been recorded recently or if the underlying analytics pipeline has not yet processed newer events.

ipAddress.description:
IP address from which the administrator established this session.

This value originates from the non-nullable `ip` column on the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` Prisma model and records the client IP observed at login time. It is critical for security analysis, anomaly detection, and forensic investigation of suspicious activity and may represent either an IPv4 or IPv6 address as captured by the platform.

href.description:
Entry URL that initiated the admin login session.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `href` column in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` Prisma model and captures the full URL or route that triggered the authentication flow. It provides important context for understanding which part of the administrative console or which deep-linked resource caused the administrator to sign in.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL at the time of admin login creation.

This value mirrors the non-nullable `referrer` column on the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_sessions` Prisma model and records where the admin navigated from when starting the login flow. It is useful for tracing cross-application navigation paths, detecting unusual referral patterns, and supporting security and UX analytics.

userAgent.description:
User agent string reported by the administrator's client when the session was created.

It typically contains browser, operating system, and device information, and may be sourced from related logging tables rather than the core session record. This field is used to support device tracking, security reviews, and troubleshooting issues that depend on specific client environments.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether the session is currently considered active by the platform.

This is a derived boolean that summarizes the current state of the session based on `expiredAt` and any additional internal revocation or idle-timeout rules. In typical implementations it is `true` while `expiredAt` is null or in the future and the session has not been explicitly revoked, and `false` once the session has expired, been terminated, or otherwise lost its ability to authorize new requests.

IShoppingMallEmailVerificationToken.ISum.description:
Summary view of an email verification token issued for an actor in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO intentionally exposes only non-sensitive metadata such as identifiers and timestamps. It never includes the raw verification `token` value from the underlying `shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens` table, ensuring that verification secrets cannot be reconstructed from API responses or logs.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the email verification token record.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens` Prisma model and is used only for administrative lookup and troubleshooting in privileged tooling.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this verification token expires and becomes invalid for completing email verification.

The value maps directly to the `expires_at` column in the `shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens` table and is returned as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this email verification token record was created.

This value comes from the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens` table and allows administrators to understand when the verification flow was initiated.

IShoppingMallPasswordResetToken.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shopping mall password reset token used during the credential recovery flow.

This DTO provides non-sensitive, high-level information for administrative listings, security monitoring, and audit contexts without exposing the raw token value itself. In particular, it never returns the underlying `token` column from the `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens` Prisma model.

The `status` field is a **derived lifecycle indicator**, computed by business logic from timestamps such as `expires_at` and `used_at` (mapped from the `consumed_at` column) and from any additional invalidation rules. It is not a physical column in the `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens` table, but a convenient summary of the token's current usability state for dashboards and tools.

The `authCredentials` association replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_auth_credentials_id` with a lightweight summary of the owning credentials record, allowing atomic reads that include both token metadata and its owning identity without exposing sensitive credential details directly.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the password reset token record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens` Prisma model and is used as the canonical reference for this token in administrative tools, logs, and debugging workflows.

authCredentials.description:
Summary of the authentication credentials record that this reset token is associated with.

This object provides contextual information about the login identity (such as actor type and identifier) without exposing sensitive credential fields. It replaces the raw foreign key field `shopping_mall_auth_credentials_id` from the underlying Prisma model to enable richer, atomic read operations without additional lookups.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this password reset token becomes invalid.

After this moment, the token can no longer be used to reset a password and any attempt to consume it must be rejected by the backend. The value is stored in the `expires_at` column of the `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens` table and returned as an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this password reset token record was created.

This value comes from the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens` table and is useful for auditing when the reset flow was initiated and for understanding token age in administrative listings.

used_at.description:
Timestamp when this password reset token was successfully consumed to reset a password.

This field is a DTO-level naming of the underlying nullable `consumed_at` column on the `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens` Prisma model. It is null while the token is still pending and has not been used, and it is populated only once the reset operation completes successfully.

By exposing this value in a read-only fashion, administrative and security tooling can reconstruct when the token was actually used, supporting audit trails, anomaly detection, and incident investigations.

status.description:
High-level lifecycle status of the password reset token.

Typical examples include values such as `pending`, `used`, or `expired`. The exact set of statuses is defined by business rules and can evolve over time. This field is **derived** by the application (for example, from `expires_at`, `used_at`/`consumed_at`, and any soft-invalidation flags) rather than being stored as a dedicated column in the `shopping_mall_password_reset_tokens` table.

Exposing a single lifecycle status string allows administrative tooling and monitoring dashboards to quickly understand whether the token is currently usable, has already been consumed, or has become invalid without having to interpret raw timestamps for each record.

IShoppingMallAdminRole.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an administrator role within the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is backed by the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma model, whose core columns include `id`, `code`, `name`, the optional `description_text`, and lifecycle timestamps such as `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`. The summary intentionally exposes only a subset of those fields that are most relevant for list views, role pickers, and embedding into other entities.

In particular, it surfaces the identity and display attributes (`id`, `code`, `name`), an optional business description sourced from `description_text`, and a derived `is_system` flag that indicates whether the role is a built-in system role or a custom role created by administrators. Internal timestamps and soft‑delete markers remain hidden to keep the payload compact while still allowing administrators to understand and manage role assignments effectively.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrator role.

This value corresponds directly to the `id` primary key column in the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma model and is used as the stable reference for role assignments, audit records, and configuration references across the platform.

code.description:
Stable, unique code for this administrator role.

This property maps to the non-nullable `code` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table. It is a machine-friendly identifier used in configuration and authorization logic, such as `platform_super_admin`, `support_agent`, or `catalog_manager`. The code must remain stable over time so that policy rules, automation scripts, and configuration entries that reference it do not break.

Administrators typically use this value when defining access control lists, feature toggles, or custom workflows that depend on role identity rather than human-readable names.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the administrator role.

This property is backed by the `name` column in `shopping_mall_admin_roles` and is displayed in management consoles, role selection dialogs, and audit trails. It should be concise yet descriptive enough that operators can easily understand the purpose of the role without reading the full description.

Typical examples include labels like "Platform Super Administrator", "Customer Support Agent", or "Catalog Content Manager".

description.description:
Optional detailed description of what responsibilities and permissions this role entails.

This field is a projection of the nullable `description_text` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` Prisma model. Because the underlying column allows null, some roles may not have a stored description, and in those cases this property may be omitted from the summary DTO.

When present, the description helps administrators understand how and when the role should be used, document governance rules, and communicate the scope of permissions to other stakeholders. It is especially useful in environments with many custom roles or complex compliance requirements.

is_system.description:
Indicates whether this role is a system-defined, built-in role that cannot be arbitrarily modified or deleted.

Unlike `id`, `code`, and `name`, this field is a derived, virtual property and does not correspond to a dedicated column in the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` table. Backend logic typically computes this flag based on configuration, reserved codes, or other internal rules maintained by the platform.

A value of `true` identifies protected roles that are part of the core platform configuration and are usually only manageable by platform maintainers. A value of `false` indicates a custom role created by administrators, which may be edited or retired according to business policy and lifecycle rules.

IShoppingMallAdminRoleAssignment.ISummar.description:
Lightweight summary view of a platform administrator role assignment in the shopping mall system.

This DTO is backed by the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments` Prisma model, whose key columns include `id`, `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id`, `shopping_mall_admin_role_id`, the non-nullable `assigned_at`, and the nullable `revoked_at`. Instead of exposing raw foreign key identifiers, the summary embeds the associated platform administrator and admin role as nested summary objects.

The goal of this projection is to provide enough information for admin management and audit screens to see which administrator holds which role, when the assignment became effective, whether an end time has been recorded, and whether the assignment is currently active. Callers can use this summary without performing additional joins or lookups while still preserving a clear mapping back to the underlying database records.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin role assignment record.

This value maps to the `id` primary key column in `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments` and is used to address, update, or revoke a specific role assignment in administrative operations and audit tools.

platform_admin.description:
Summary information about the platform administrator who receives this role assignment.

Internally this summary is selected based on the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments` table and resolves to the corresponding record in the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` model. It gives consumers enough identity and display fields to render who holds the role without making additional API calls or exposing low-level foreign key identifiers.

admin_role.description:
Summary information about the administrator role granted to the platform administrator.

This object is populated from the `shopping_mall_admin_role_id` foreign key column pointing to the `shopping_mall_admin_roles` model. It exposes the role code, name, and key attributes so that clients can render a human-readable representation of the assigned role directly within the assignment summary, without separately fetching the role entity.

assigned_at.description:
Timestamp when this role assignment became effective for the administrator.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable `assigned_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments` Prisma model and represents the exact moment the assignment was created or activated in system time. It is commonly used in audit views, historical permission analysis, and checks that depend on the age of an assignment.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when this role assignment expired or was revoked.

This value is a projection of the nullable `revoked_at` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments` Prisma model. When populated, it marks the point in time after which the assignment should no longer be considered effective for permission evaluations.

Null when the underlying `revoked_at` column is null and the role assignment does not have a recorded expiry.

In this case, the assignment is considered open‑ended and remains valid until an explicit revocation or policy change occurs.

expires_at.description:
Expiration timestamp for the role assignment.

Although the backing database column is named `revoked_at`, this projection uses the more intuitive name `expires_at` for API consumers. The `date-time | null` union mirrors the nullable nature of `revoked_at` in the Prisma schema and allows clients to distinguish between assignments that have a recorded end time and those that are still open.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this role assignment is currently active for the associated platform administrator.

This field is a derived, virtual property and is not stored as a dedicated column in the `shopping_mall_admin_role_assignments` table. Backend logic typically computes it from a combination of `assigned_at`, the nullable `revoked_at` value (exposed here as `expires_at`), the current time, and any additional business rules around temporary assignments or scheduled deactivations.

A value of `true` means the assignment is in effect and should be considered when evaluating the administrator's permissions. A value of `false` means the assignment has expired, been revoked, or otherwise deactivated and should no longer contribute permissions in authorization checks.

IShoppingMallSecurityEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a security event recorded within the shopping mall platform.

Used for security dashboards, audit overviews, and quick lists where a concise view of security‑relevant activity is required without loading full event payloads or internal diagnostic details. This summary focuses on who was affected in high-level terms, what happened, where it originated, and when it occurred.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the security event record.

This value maps directly to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_security_events` table and is used to uniquely reference a single logged security event across dashboards and APIs.

occurredAt.description:
Timestamp when the security event was recorded in the system, expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC).

This field is derived from the `created_at` column of the `shopping_mall_security_events` Prisma model but is exposed using camelCase JSON naming conventions to remain consistent with other DTOs such as authentication logs and order history. It provides a stable point in time for sorting, filtering, and correlating security events across different views.

actor_type.description:
High‑level type of actor associated with this security event.

Typical values indicate whether the event is related to a customer, seller, platform administrator, guest user, or a system‑level process. Concrete allowed values and semantics are defined at the application layer and may evolve over time, so this field is intentionally modeled as a free‑form string here.

event_type.description:
Short code indicating the security event type.

Examples include values such as `LOGIN_SUCCESS`, `LOGIN_FAILURE`, `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUEST`, `TOKEN_REVOKED`, or `SUSPICIOUS_ACTIVITY`. Exact allowed values are governed by business rules and stored in the `event_type` column of the `shopping_mall_security_events` Prisma model.

oneOf.description:
Client IP address associated with the security event.

Represents the remote IP from which the action originated, using either IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation derived from the `ip` column in the `shopping_mall_security_events` table.

Null when no reliable IP address is available for this event.

This can occur when the originating IP could not be determined or when the event was generated by an internal background process rather than an external client connection.

ip_address.description:
Client IP address from which the security‑relevant action originated, when available.

This connection metadata is used for threat detection, correlation of events across sessions, and forensic investigation, but it does not contain any credential or secret material.

oneOf.description:
User‑agent string reported by the client that triggered the event.

Typically contains browser, operating system, and device information and is derived from the `user_agent` column of the `shopping_mall_security_events` table.

Null when the user‑agent is not available or not applicable.

For example, certain infrastructure‑level events or backend‑initiated tasks may not have an associated user‑agent string.

user_agent.description:
User‑agent header associated with the request that produced the security event, when available.

This metadata supports anomaly detection, device fingerprinting, and troubleshooting without exposing any credential or secret information.

IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary of a product in the shopping mall catalog.

Used wherever a compact product representation is required, such as wishlist lists, cart summaries, and product search results.

id.description: Unique identifier of the product.

name.description: Display name of the product shown to customers across the storefront.

brand.description: Brand associated with the product, exposed as a summary for quick recognition and filtering.

primary_image_url.description: URL of the primary or thumbnail image used to represent the product in list views.

min_price.description: Minimum current selling price across all active SKUs for this product. Used to display "from" pricing in summaries.

max_price.description: Maximum current selling price across all active SKUs for this product.

average_rating.description: Average star rating value for this product, typically aggregated from all eligible reviews.

review_count.description: Total number of published reviews contributing to the aggregated rating.

IShoppingMallProductCategoryAssignment.I.description:
Summary representation of a product-to-category assignment within the shopping mall catalog.

Used primarily in administrative and analytical contexts to inspect which categories a given product is associated with, without loading full product or category details.

id.description: Unique identifier of this product-category assignment record.

product.description: Product participating in this assignment. In summary contexts, this may be a lightweight representation sufficient to identify the product.

category.description: Category to which the product is assigned.

isPrimary.description: Indicates whether this category is considered the primary category for the product within its category tree.

IShoppingMallProductMedia.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a single product media asset in the shoppingMall catalog.

This summary DTO is designed for embedding in product detail or listing responses where only minimal identification and display ordering information about the media asset is required. It is intentionally smaller than the full media DTO and focuses on the fields that directly influence client-side rendering order and media handling.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product media record.

This value corresponds directly to `shopping_mall_product_media.id` and is used to reference or fetch the full media entity when needed.

uri.description:
URI pointing to the media asset (image, video thumbnail, etc.) in storage or CDN.

This is a direct projection of `shopping_mall_product_media.uri` and is what clients should use to display the media resource in the UI.

media_type.description:
Type of media such as `image`, `video`, or other supported categories.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_media.media_type` and allows clients to decide which UI component or player to use when rendering the asset.

is_primary.description:
Flag indicating whether this media asset is the primary one for the product.

When `true`, this record typically represents the main thumbnail or hero image for the product in product list and detail pages.

display_order.description:
Order index used to sort media assets for display.

This is mapped from `shopping_mall_product_media.display_order`. Lower values usually appear first when rendering media carousels or grids.

IShoppingMallProductOptionType.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a single product option type in the shoppingMall catalog.

Each record represents an option dimension such as color, size, or material that is scoped to a single product. This summary form is intended for list views and lightweight embeddings, where only identity and the basic display label and ordering are required, and not the full option type configuration.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product option type record.

Directly corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_option_types.id` and is used to reference the option type in detail views or when managing option values.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the option type, such as `Color`, `Size`, or `Material`.

This is taken from `shopping_mall_product_option_types.name` and is the primary label rendered in product configuration UIs.

display_name.description:
Optional display name or label that is shown to end users when selecting options for a product.

This property maps directly to `shopping_mall_product_option_types.display_name` and is typically used when the internal `name` field is more technical or constrained, while `display_name` can be localized or made more user-friendly.

When this value is `null` in the underlying Prisma model, client applications should normally fall back to the `name` property when rendering labels in the UI, ensuring that option types are always presented with a meaningful caption.

display_order.description:
Ordering index specifying the sequence in which option types appear for the product.

Mapped from `shopping_mall_product_option_types.display_order`. Lower numbers indicate that the option type should be shown earlier in the configuration UI.

IShoppingMallProductOptionValue.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single option value that belongs to a product option type in the shopping mall catalog.

This DTO is used in lists and as a lightweight reference from SKU summaries and product detail views, providing just enough information to render a human‑readable option label such as "Red" or "XL" without fetching the full option value record.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product option value.

This UUID is the primary key of the underlying `shopping_mall_product_option_values` record and is used internally for joins and references between catalog entities.

value.description:
Canonical value label for the option, such as "Red", "Blue", "Small", or "XL".

This field corresponds to the `value` column in `shopping_mall_product_option_values` and is unique within a given option type. It is the primary business identifier used to distinguish different selectable values within the same option dimension.

displayName.description:
Optional display label for this option value used in customer‑facing UIs.

When present, this field corresponds to the nullable `display_name` column in `shopping_mall_product_option_values` and can contain localized or more user‑friendly text. When absent, clients should fall back to using `value` for display purposes.

IShoppingMallProductSku.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a specific product SKU (variant) in the shopping mall catalog.

This DTO is used when a concrete purchasable variant is referenced from other entities such as wishlist items, cart items, order lines, or inventory snapshots. It exposes just enough information to identify and price the SKU without loading the full SKU detail record.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SKU.

This UUID is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_product_skus` record and is used internally for joins, inventory linkage, and order line references.

code.description:
Business‑defined SKU code used in inventory systems, order lines, and external integrations.

This field maps to the `code` column in `shopping_mall_product_skus` and is unique per product. It is the human‑readable identifier typically shown in administrative UIs and used in reports and exports.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the SKU such as `active`, `inactive`, or `discontinued`.

This field reflects the `status` column in `shopping_mall_product_skus` and, together with the parent product and inventory status, determines whether the SKU is visible in the catalog and eligible for checkout.

priceAmount.description:
Current unit price for the SKU in the configured currency.

This field corresponds to the `price_amount` column in `shopping_mall_product_skus`. It represents the effective unit selling price that cart items, wishlist previews, and order lines commonly display without needing to fetch the full SKU detail.

currencyCode.description:
Currency code for the SKU price, such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`.

This field maps directly to the non‑nullable `currency_code` column in `shopping_mall_product_skus` and identifies the ISO‑like currency context in which `priceAmount` (and any compare‑at prices in fuller DTOs) are expressed. Clients must always interpret `priceAmount` together with `currencyCode` when displaying prices, performing currency‑aware calculations, or aggregating monetary values across SKUs.

IShoppingMallSkuOptionValueAssignment.IS.description:
Summary view of a SKU option value assignment within the shopping mall catalog.

This summary object represents a single row of the `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` table, but instead of exposing raw foreign key UUIDs it embeds lightweight summaries of the related SKU and option value.
It is optimized for list and embedded contexts where callers need to understand which variant and which option value are linked, without loading the full assignment entity or all relational details.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the SKU option value assignment record.

This value directly corresponds to the primary key `id` column of the `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` table and is used to uniquely identify the assignment row across the system.
Clients can safely rely on this identifier when requesting or referencing a specific assignment in subsequent API calls.

sku.description:
Summary information for the SKU to which this option value assignment belongs.

This is a projection of the `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` foreign key column and embeds an `IShoppingMallProductSku.ISummary` instead of returning only the raw UUID.
It allows clients to render which concrete product variant (for example, a given combination of options) the assignment is associated with, without performing a separate lookup using the SKU identifier.

option_value.description:
Summary information for the concrete product option value included in this assignment.

This is a projection of the `shopping_mall_product_option_value_id` foreign key column and embeds an `IShoppingMallProductOptionValue.ISummary` instead of exposing only the underlying UUID.
Clients typically use this object to render the human‑readable option value (for example, a specific color or size) that participates in the SKU’s variant definition.

display_name.description:
Human‑readable label representing the selected option value for display in customer‑facing UIs (for example, "Color: Red").

This field is **derived** by the application layer and is **not** a direct column in the `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` table. It is usually constructed from the related option type and option value (and may incorporate localization or branding rules) to provide a concise description of the assignment.
Consumers should treat `display_name` as a presentation‑oriented convenience value and rely on `id`, `sku.id`, and `option_value.id` for programmatic identity and joins rather than parsing this string.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this SKU option value assignment was created.

The value corresponds to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` and is stored in ISO 8601 date‑time format in UTC.
It is primarily used for auditing and ordering in administrative tooling or in internal synchronization processes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this SKU option value assignment was last updated.

The value corresponds to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_sku_option_value_assignments` and is stored in ISO 8601 date‑time format in UTC.
Clients can use this field to detect recent configuration changes to the SKU’s option assignments or to implement cache invalidation strategies in consumer applications.

IShoppingMallProductVisibilityRule.ISumm.description:
Summary view of a product visibility rule in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO provides a concise representation of a record from the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` table, embedding the related product and optional region information and exposing the **effective** visibility decision as a boolean.
It is intended for list pages, dashboards, and embedded contexts where operators or services need to quickly understand where and when a product is visible without inspecting the full rule definition or raw `visibility` string values.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product visibility rule.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` column of the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` table and uniquely identifies a single visibility configuration row.
It can be used as the stable handle when fetching, updating, or deleting a specific rule.

product.description:
Summary of the product that this visibility rule applies to.

This object is a projection of the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key column and embeds `IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary` instead of exposing only the raw UUID.
It enables clients to immediately see which catalog item is governed by the rule (for example, by product code, name, and brand) without issuing an additional product lookup.

region_setting.description:
Optional region configuration that scopes this visibility rule to a specific geographic region.

When non‑null, this object represents the `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` foreign key column and embeds `IShoppingMallRegionSetting.ISummary`, indicating that the rule applies only within that region (for example, a single country or market).
When `null`, the underlying `shopping_mall_region_setting_id` column is also null and the rule is considered **global** with respect to region, meaning it is not restricted to any single region configuration and may be combined with other rules during catalog evaluation.

channel.description:
Logical sales or presentation channel that this visibility rule targets, such as `web`, `mobile`, or a specific marketplace channel code.

This property is a direct projection of the nullable `channel` column in the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` table. When present, it narrows the rule’s effect to the specified channel only. When omitted or stored as `null` in the database, the rule is not channel‑specific and is interpreted as applying to all channels for the given product (and region, if any) during visibility evaluation.

is_visible.description:
Indicates whether the product should be visible under this rule in the evaluated context.

This field is a **computed projection** based primarily on the underlying `visibility` column in `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` (for example, values like `visible`, `hidden`, or `restricted`) and, in full catalog evaluation, may also consider product lifecycle and compliance state. The raw `visibility` string is not exposed in this summary; instead, `is_visible` provides the final show/hide decision that clients should use when rendering product lists or detail pages.
Consumers should treat this flag as the authoritative visibility outcome for the scope represented by this summary (product, optional region, and optional channel), rather than attempting to reconstruct visibility from lower‑level fields.

starts_at.description:
Optional start timestamp from which this visibility rule becomes effective.

When set, this value mirrors the `starts_at` column in the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` table and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time in UTC. The rule only influences product visibility at or after this point in time. When `null`, the rule is considered effective immediately (subject to other system constraints) from the time of its creation.

ends_at.description:
Optional end timestamp after which this visibility rule no longer applies.

When set, this value mirrors the `ends_at` column in the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` table and is expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time in UTC. The rule stops affecting product visibility after this moment. When `null`, there is no scheduled end date and the rule remains in effect until it is updated or deleted.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this product visibility rule was created.

This value reflects the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` table and is stored in ISO 8601 date‑time format in UTC.
It is primarily used for auditing, debugging, and chronological sorting in administrative tools and reporting views.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this product visibility rule was last updated.

This value reflects the `updated_at` column in the `shopping_mall_product_visibility_rules` table and is stored in ISO 8601 date‑time format in UTC.
Clients can use this field to detect recent configuration changes, drive cache invalidation, or support synchronization logic between internal services.

IShoppingMallProductComplianceFlag.ISumm.description:
Summary view of a product compliance flag within the shopping mall catalog.

This summary is directly mapped to the `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags` Prisma model and exposes only a subset of safe, business-relevant fields. It is intended for listing and embedding within other DTOs where operators, administrators, or trusted sellers need to understand high-level compliance constraints on a product.

Sensitive or operationally internal details such as free‑form notes or audit timestamps are intentionally omitted in this variant to keep the payload lean and to avoid leaking implementation details. For deeper investigation workflows, separate, more detailed DTOs can be used instead.

id.description:
Primary key for the product compliance flag record.

This value corresponds directly to `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.id` and uniquely identifies a single compliance or restriction flag attached to a product. It is used as the stable identifier when referencing this flag from other administrative tools or internal APIs.

flag_type.description:
Type of compliance flag as stored in `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.flag_type`.

Common examples include values such as `age_restriction`, `hazardous_material`, or `region_restricted`. Exact allowed values are governed by business configuration and policy tables, and backend logic uses this field to decide which compliance rules to evaluate for the associated product.

flag_value.description:
Optional detailed value for the compliance flag mapped from `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.flag_value`.

This can hold a specific regulation code, localized tag, or other textual descriptor that refines the meaning of `flag_type`. When no additional detail is required for a given flag, this value may be null, indicating that there is no extra payload beyond the flag type itself.

is_blocking_sale.description:
Boolean indicator reflecting `shopping_mall_product_compliance_flags.is_blocking_sale`.

When true, the presence of this flag can block the sale of the associated product under certain conditions defined by business and regulatory policy. When false, the flag may still influence catalog visibility, messaging, or additional checkout warnings but does not by itself block all purchases.

IShoppingMallCatalogSearchResult.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of a catalog search result for the shopping mall.

Represents a single item in search result lists returned from catalog search operations. Each record provides enough information to render a search card, including basic product details, pricing and primary classification context. Heavy detail such as full description, full media gallery, inventory breakdown, and audit information is intentionally omitted for performance.

This summary may be used as the `data` item type in paginated search responses.

product.description: Summary information about the matched product itself. Contains the core fields required to render product name, primary image/thumbnail, key merchandising badges, and base price range as defined by the product summary schema.

brand.description: Summary information for the product brand, if any. Used to display brand name or logo alongside the product in search results.

primaryCategory.description: Primary category under which this product is being surfaced in the current search context. This may depend on the tree or merchandising rules applied by the search engine.

matchedTextSnippet.description: Optional snippet of text extracted from product fields (such as title or description) that highlights matched search terms. Can be used to emphasize why the item appears in the result set.

relevanceScore.description: Numeric relevance score assigned by the search engine for this product within the current query context. Higher scores indicate better matches. The absolute scale is search-engine specific and should generally be treated as relative, not absolute.

badges.description: Array of lightweight merchandising or UX badges that should be displayed for this search result item (for example, `BEST_SELLER`, `NEW`, `LIMITED_STOCK`). Each badge is represented as a simple string code; client applications map these codes to localized labels and icons.

IShoppingMallGuestCartItem.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO representing a single line item in a guest user's shopping cart.

This summary is used in lightweight cart overviews, mini-cart widgets, and list responses where only essential item information is required.

It exposes key identification, quantity, pricing snapshot data, lifecycle timestamps, and contextual product and SKU information for a specific SKU selected by an unauthenticated guest user.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest cart item record.

This value maps to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table and is used to address the item in update, delete, or audit operations for the guest cart aggregate.

guest_cart_id.description:
Identifier of the guest cart that owns this item.

Represents the hierarchical parent guest cart aggregate and maps to `shopping_mall_guest_carts.id`. This remains an ID rather than a nested object to avoid introducing a circular reference back to the cart aggregate, which already owns the collection of items.

product_id.description:
Identifier of the underlying catalog product for this guest cart item.

This is a direct exposure of the `shopping_mall_product_id` foreign key from the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table and is primarily intended for advanced client logic, analytics, or integrations that need to group or filter cart items by product without resolving through the nested product summary.

sku_id.description:
Identifier of the specific SKU (stock keeping unit) variant that this cart item refers to.

This field corresponds to the `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` column in `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` and is useful for integrations and internal tooling that operate directly on SKU identifiers instead of or in addition to the denormalized `sku` summary object.

sku.description:
Summary information about the SKU variant that this cart item refers to.

This replaces the raw `sku_id` foreign key for most UI use cases and provides enough context—such as SKU code, variant labels, and basic status—for cart views without requiring additional lookups.

product.description:
Summary information about the underlying catalog product for this cart item.

This replaces the raw `product_id` foreign key for front-end scenarios and allows clients to group and display items by product using human‑readable metadata such as product name, brand, and primary media.

quantity.description:
Number of units of the SKU that the guest has placed into the cart.

This is a positive integer and is constrained by inventory and business rules enforced at the application layer, such as maximum units per order or per customer.

unit_price.description:
Unit price of the SKU at the moment it was added to the cart, before discounts and promotions.

This value is expressed in the platform's default currency (or the session currency, depending on configuration) and reflects a pricing snapshot used for cart display. The final order price may differ if prices change or additional discounts are applied during checkout.

line_subtotal.description:
Subtotal amount for this line item before any discounts are applied.

It is normally computed as `quantity * unit_price` and is used for display and intermediate pricing calculations in the cart UI, as well as for analytical summaries of cart value before promotions.

line_total.description:
Final payable amount for this cart line after line‑level discounts and promotions have been applied.

This value is used to render the effective price for the line item in cart views and may differ from `line_subtotal` when campaign discounts, coupons, or other price adjustments are present.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code representing the monetary currency for `unit_price`, `line_subtotal`, and `line_total`.

Typical examples include `"USD"`, `"EUR"`, or `"KRW"`. Clients should treat this as the canonical currency context for rendering monetary values related to this line item.

product_name.description:
Display name of the underlying product shown in cart views.

This value is denormalized from the product record so that clients can render cart item rows without performing additional joins or API calls, and it provides a stable label for order and cart history even if the product name changes later.

sku_name.description:
Display name or variant label of the SKU for this cart item.

Common examples include strings describing option combinations such as size and color (for example, `"Size M / Blue"`). The value is intended for human‑readable presentation in cart and checkout UIs.

thumbnail_url.description:
URL of a thumbnail image representing this cart item in UI list views.

The URL points to a pre-uploaded image served from a media service or CDN, allowing clients to render a small preview image in cart rows, mini‑cart components, and order summaries without handling any binary file content directly.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest cart item was first created in the system.

This value mirrors the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` table and is typically used for sorting cart lines by recency and for analytics around when shoppers add items to their carts.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest cart item was last updated.

The value corresponds to the `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_guest_cart_items` and is advanced whenever mutable attributes of the line, such as `quantity` or pricing snapshot fields, are changed.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this guest cart item, if it has been logically removed.

When null or omitted in this summary view, the item is considered active. When present, it indicates that the line has been removed from the visible cart but is retained for audit, analytics, or debugging purposes.

IShoppingMallCustomerCart.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO representing a customer's persistent shopping cart.

This type is optimized for list and header-cart displays where high-level cart state is required without expanding all nested item details.

It exposes identifiers, active/archival state, aggregate counts, monetary totals, and key lifecycle timestamps so that clients can quickly render cart badges, overviews, and administrative lists.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the customer cart record.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` table and is used as the stable identifier for all subsequent read, update, and delete operations on the cart aggregate.

customer_id.description:
Identifier of the authenticated customer that owns this cart.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_customer_id` in the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` table and allows clients and administrative tools to associate the cart summary with a particular customer account.

is_active.description:
Flag indicating whether this customer cart is currently considered the active cart for the customer.

When `true`, the cart participates in standard cart flows such as merging with guest carts and serving as the default target for add‑to‑cart actions. When `false`, the cart represents a historical or archived cart that is retained for audit or analytics but is not used as the primary active cart.

items_count.description:
Total number of distinct line items currently stored in the cart.

This count represents the number of unique SKUs present rather than the sum of quantities across items, and is useful for displaying compact cart badges (for example, the number of different products in the cart).

total_quantity.description:
Total quantity across all cart items.

This value is computed as the sum of the `quantity` field of each line item and is often used to display badges showing the total number of units in the cart.

subtotal_amount.description:
Aggregate subtotal amount of all items in the cart before applying cart-level discounts, promotions, shipping, or taxes.

This is typically the sum of individual line item subtotals and provides a baseline value for indicating cart size and computing discounts.

total_amount.description:
Final payable amount for the cart after applying applicable discounts and adjustments, but usually before taxes and shipping unless the platform defines cart totals differently.

This is the main monetary figure shown in header-cart summaries and quick overviews to communicate the shopper's current spend level.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code representing the monetary currency used for `subtotal_amount` and `total_amount`.

Examples include `"USD"`, `"EUR"`, or `"KRW"`. Clients should treat this field as the authoritative currency context for the amounts in this summary.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this persistent customer cart was initially created.

This value mirrors the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_customer_carts` and is useful for understanding the age of a cart, auditing cart lifecycle, or driving retention and remarketing analytics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this customer cart was last updated.

The timestamp corresponds to the `updated_at` column of the `shopping_mall_customer_carts` table and is advanced whenever the cart contents or relevant metadata change, such as adding or removing items or changing quantities.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this customer cart, if it has been logically removed or archived.

When null or omitted, the cart is considered logically active (subject also to `is_active`). When present, it indicates that the cart has been deactivated or archived but remains in storage for audit, analytics, or troubleshooting.

items.description:
Optional lightweight list of customer cart item summaries representing the current contents of the cart.

In summary views this list may be truncated or omitted entirely depending on API design or performance considerations. Each entry is a `IShoppingMallCustomerCartItem.ISummary` providing per-item quantity and pricing snapshots.

IShoppingMallCustomerCartItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single line item inside a customer's persistent shopping cart in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is a read-optimized projection over the `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items` Prisma model combined with related product and SKU data. It is designed for cart list displays, mini-cart widgets, and cart validation responses, where only key identifying and pricing information is required instead of the full underlying entities.

Most scalar fields map directly to columns on `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items` (such as `id`, the reference to the parent cart, and the quantity), while monetary values and availability-related flags may be derived from a combination of the cart item, `shopping_mall_product_skus`, inventory tables, and policy configuration. Client applications can rely on this structure to render consistent cart views and to understand whether each item is currently purchasable, without needing to call lower-level product or inventory endpoints.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the cart item record.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_customer_cart_items` row and is used to address the line item in subsequent update and delete operations. It remains stable for the lifetime of the cart item, even if quantity or pricing fields change.

cartId.description:
Identifier of the parent customer cart that owns this item.

This value links the cart item back to its owning record in `shopping_mall_customer_carts`. It allows servers and clients to group line items by cart and to enforce that operations on this item are always scoped to the correct cart context.

skuId.description:
Identifier of the SKU (sellable product variant) that this cart item represents.

This maps to the primary key of a record in `shopping_mall_product_skus` and determines which concrete variant (for example, a particular size and color combination) is being purchased. Downstream calculations such as inventory checks, fulfillment eligibility, and price lookups use this identifier as the join key.

product.description:
Summary information for the product to which this SKU belongs.

This is a lightweight embedding of `IShoppingMallProduct.ISummary` so that cart views can display basic product details (such as name, primary image, and brand) without needing to perform a separate product lookup per line item.

sku.description:
Summary information for the specific SKU variant added to the cart.

This embedded `IShoppingMallProductSku.ISummary` provides variant-level details such as the business SKU code, current price, and variant-specific status. It allows the cart UI to show attributes like color and size while ensuring pricing is consistent with the variant that will be fulfilled.

quantity.description:
Number of units of this SKU that the customer has added to the cart.

This value is stored on the cart item row and must be at least 1. It is used together with pricing and availability information to compute line totals, validate against stock and policy constraints, and drive any minimum or maximum purchase rules.

unitPrice.description:
Unit price of the SKU at the time it was added to the cart or last refreshed, before applying any per-line discounts.

This value typically mirrors a snapshot of the effective selling price from `shopping_mall_product_skus` or a promotion engine at the time the cart was calculated. It is expressed in the currency indicated by the `currency` field and is used as the base for computing `totalPrice`.

totalPrice.description:
Total price for this cart line item in the specified currency.

In most cases this is calculated as `unitPrice` multiplied by `quantity`, optionally adjusted by any line-level discounts or surcharges. It represents the amount that will be charged for this line if the order is placed, excluding order-level fees such as shipping or tax that may be modeled separately.

currency.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the monetary fields on this cart item.

The value is typically aligned with the customer's session or market configuration (for example, `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW`). Clients must treat all pricing fields (`unitPrice` and `totalPrice`) as being denominated in this currency.

isAvailable.description:
Indicates whether this SKU is currently purchasable for the requested quantity.

This flag is computed based on a combination of product status, SKU status, inventory levels, backorder/preorder rules, and policy-based restrictions such as regional visibility or compliance flags. If `false`, the cart UI should surface an appropriate message and prevent the item from proceeding successfully through checkout.

maxPurchasableQuantity.description:
Maximum quantity of this SKU that the customer is currently allowed to purchase in this cart.

This value incorporates stock availability, per-order or per-customer purchase limits, and any other applicable platform or seller policies. When the user attempts to increase `quantity`, clients should validate against this upper bound and communicate any violations to the user before submitting changes back to the server.

IShoppingMallWishlist.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a customer's wishlist in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is a read-focused projection over the `shopping_mall_wishlists` Prisma model that is optimized for list screens, navigation components, and cross-cutting references. It exposes the core identifiers, ownership information, and lightweight aggregate counts required to render wishlists without loading the full list of items each time.

While most fields map directly to columns on `shopping_mall_wishlists` (such as `id`, `name`, lifecycle flags, and timestamps), the `itemCount` field is typically derived from the related `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table or a materialized aggregate. As a result, clients can efficiently show how many entries a wishlist contains and whether it is the default wishlist for that customer, using this summary alone.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the wishlist.

This value corresponds to the primary key in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and is used to reference the wishlist in follow-up operations such as fetching details, updating metadata, or deleting the wishlist.

customer.description:
Summary representation of the customer who owns this wishlist.

This association replaces the raw customer foreign key and provides enough information to display ownership context in list and administrative views without additional API calls. It can be traced back to the `shopping_mall_customer_id` foreign key on the `shopping_mall_wishlists` row.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the wishlist as defined by the customer, such as "Favorites" or "Birthday Gifts".

Clients typically display this value as the primary label for the wishlist in list views and navigation components, and they may allow the customer to edit it as part of wishlist management features.

itemCount.description:
Total number of active items currently stored in this wishlist.

This value is usually derived from `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` via a count of non-deleted entries, or from a materialized aggregate maintained by the backend. It enables UIs to convey the size of a wishlist without issuing separate item-list queries for each wishlist row.

isDefault.description:
Indicates whether this wishlist is the customer's default wishlist that frontends may use implicitly.

The platform typically ensures that at most one wishlist per customer is marked as default in the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table. Client applications can surface this state with special styling and may choose the default wishlist automatically when adding items without explicit wishlist selection.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this wishlist was created.

This value mirrors the `created_at` column on the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and can be used for sorting, reporting, or displaying historical information about when the wishlist was first established.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this wishlist was last modified.

The value is taken from the `updated_at` column on the `shopping_mall_wishlists` table and is updated whenever relevant wishlist attributes or contained items change. Clients can use it to highlight recently active wishlists or to detect when a list has been updated since it was last viewed.

IShoppingMallWishlistItem.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a single wishlist item in the shopping mall platform.
