This summary is backed by the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` Prisma model and is used in list responses where customers inspect items they have saved for later purchase. It focuses on identifiers and display-ready catalog fields and intentionally omits lifecycle metadata such as `updated_at` and `deleted_at`, which are available on full wishlist item entities if needed for audit or back-office flows.

The summary embeds product and optional SKU summaries instead of exposing raw foreign keys. Internally, these are resolved from the `shopping_mall_product_id` and `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` columns on `shopping_mall_wishlist_items`, allowing storefront UIs to render titles, brand, pricing, and thumbnails without additional API calls for each line.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the wishlist item.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` of the `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` table and is used as the stable reference for updates and deletes of the wishlist entry.

wishlist_id.description:
Identifier of the wishlist that owns this item.

At the database layer this maps to the foreign key column `shopping_mall_wishlist_id` on `shopping_mall_wishlist_items`, which references `shopping_mall_wishlists.id`. Client applications can use this value to group or filter items by their parent wishlist without loading the full wishlist resource.

product.description:
Summary information of the referenced product so the client can render title, brand, pricing, and primary thumbnail without extra API calls.

Even when the wishlist entry targets a concrete SKU, this product summary is resolved from the associated `shopping_mall_products` record and remains available for consistent product-level presentation and navigation.

sku.description:
Summary of the selected SKU variant for this wishlist item, if the customer saved a specific variant rather than the generic product.

This summary is resolved from the `shopping_mall_product_skus` record referenced by `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` on `shopping_mall_wishlist_items`. When the platform operates in product-level wishlist mode, this field may be omitted and only the product summary is populated.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this wishlist item was added, in ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This is mapped from the non-nullable `created_at` column on `shopping_mall_wishlist_items` and represents the moment the entry was first created. It does not change when the wishlist item is subsequently updated; for full lifecycle tracking, the underlying entity also maintains `updated_at` and an optional `deleted_at` soft-delete marker, which are deliberately omitted from this summary view.

IShoppingMallOrderLineThumbnail.ISummary.description:
Compact thumbnail representation of an order line used inside order summaries.

This DTO is backed by the `shopping_mall_order_lines` Prisma model and is intended for use in list views and lightweight order overviews where only key product and pricing information is required. It exposes immutable snapshot fields such as `product_name_snapshot` and `line_total_amount` from the order line so that historical pricing and naming remain accurate even if catalog data changes after the order is placed.

For full operational workflows such as fulfillment, returns, or dispute handling, richer DTOs expose additional properties including unit price, discounts, taxes, status history, and timestamps. The thumbnail focuses on the fields typically needed to quickly show what was ordered and at what total line amount.

order_line_id.description:
Identifier of the underlying order line record that this thumbnail represents.

This value directly maps to the primary key `id` of the `shopping_mall_order_lines` table and is used to correlate the thumbnail with the full order line entity when more detailed data is required.

product.description:
Summary of the ordered product for quick visualisation of what was purchased.

The information is derived from the related `shopping_mall_products` record and is meant for catalog-level context such as brand, category, and primary imagery. Pricing and naming in the thumbnail are, however, taken from snapshot fields on the order line to preserve the state at the time of ordering.

sku.description:
Summary of the concrete SKU (variant) that was ordered, if applicable.

This summary is resolved from the `shopping_mall_product_skus` record referenced by `shopping_mall_product_sku_id` on `shopping_mall_order_lines`, allowing UIs to show variant-specific information such as color or size alongside the order line thumbnail.

product_name_snapshot.description:
Product name as displayed to the customer at the time of ordering, stored as an immutable snapshot.

This field maps directly to the `product_name_snapshot` column on `shopping_mall_order_lines` and is not updated when the catalog product name changes later. Order detail and history views should prefer this snapshot for rendering the line title to ensure historical accuracy.

line_total_amount.description:
Final total amount charged for this line after discounts and taxes, recorded at order creation.

This value is taken from the non-nullable `line_total_amount` column on `shopping_mall_order_lines` and already reflects the ordered quantity, any per-line discounts, and applicable taxes. It is the primary monetary figure shown in order summaries for each line item.

quantity.description:
Quantity of this SKU purchased on the order line represented by this thumbnail.

The value is sourced from the `quantity` column on `shopping_mall_order_lines` and represents the number of units the customer ordered. It does not directly represent shipped or returned quantities, which may be tracked separately at fulfillment or after-sales layers.

IShoppingMallOrderSellerSegment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a seller-specific segment of a customer order in the shoppingMall platform.

This DTO provides a lightweight projection of `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments` for list responses and embedded views, focusing on identifiers, lifecycle status, and key monetary snapshot fields for each seller segment.

It is optimized for read-only scenarios such as order detail pages and administrative overviews where the full set of internal fields is not required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller segment record.

Corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.id`.

order.description:
Summary information about the master customer order that this seller segment belongs to.

This is a transformed BELONGS-TO relation for `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.shopping_mall_order_id` referencing `shopping_mall_orders.id`, exposed as `IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary` to provide rich order context in summary views.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller responsible for fulfilling this segment of the order.

This is a transformed BELONGS-TO relation for `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.shopping_mall_seller_id` referencing `shopping_mall_seller.id`, exposed as `IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary` to provide seller context without additional API calls.

segment_code.description:
Human-readable code or short identifier representing this seller segment within the context of its master order.

This is mapped from `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.segment_code` and is commonly used in UIs for quick identification.

items_subtotal_amount.description:
Subtotal amount for items in this seller segment before discounts, taxes, and shipping.

Directly mapped from `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.items_subtotal_amount`.

discount_total_amount.description:
Total discount amount applied to this seller segment, including item-level and segment-level discounts.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.discount_total_amount`.

shipping_amount.description:
Total shipping cost charged for this seller segment.

This is `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.shipping_amount` and represents shipping allocated to this seller's items.

tax_amount.description:
Total tax amount applied to this seller segment.

This value comes from `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.tax_amount` and reflects the tax component of the segment.

grand_total_amount.description:
Final payable amount for this seller segment after applying discounts, shipping, and taxes.

This is a projection of `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.grand_total_amount`.

segment_status.description:
Current high-level status of this seller segment from an operational perspective.

Mapped from `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.segment_status` and typically reflects values such as `new`, `preparing`, `shipped`, `delivered`, or `cancelled`.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller segment was created.

This maps to `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.created_at` and is useful for sorting and timeline views.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller segment was last updated.

This is `shopping_mall_order_seller_segments.updated_at` and allows clients to see recent operational changes at a glance.

IShoppingMallOrderAddress.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an order address snapshot captured at checkout time.

Used to display basic shipping or billing address information related to an order without exposing the full detailed address structure. Suitable for embedding in order summary views and lists.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order address record.

Corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_addresses.id`.

order.description:
Summary information about the master customer order that this address snapshot is associated with.

This is a transformed BELONGS-TO relation for `shopping_mall_order_addresses.shopping_mall_order_id` referencing `shopping_mall_orders.id`, exposed as `IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary` to provide order context when needed in address summaries.

type.description:
Type classification of this address snapshot, such as `shipping` or `billing`.

This property is a direct projection of `shopping_mall_order_addresses.address_type` and indicates how the address is used during fulfillment or invoicing.

recipient_name.description:
Full name of the person who will receive the shipment or invoice at this address.

Derived from `shopping_mall_order_addresses.recipient_name` at the time of checkout so later changes to the customer profile do not affect historical orders.

recipient_phone.description:
Primary phone number used for delivery or billing contact at this address.

Mapped from the nullable `shopping_mall_order_addresses.phone_number` column and stored as part of the immutable address snapshot. This value may be absent when the customer did not provide a phone number during checkout.

country.description:
Country name or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for this address.

This value corresponds to `shopping_mall_order_addresses.country_code` and is preserved as entered at checkout.

postal_code.description:
Postal or ZIP code of the address snapshot.

Mapped from `shopping_mall_order_addresses.postal_code`.

region.description:
High-level region, state, or province component of the address.

Derived from `shopping_mall_order_addresses.region` at the time of order placement.

city.description:
City, district, or locality component of the address.

Derived from `shopping_mall_order_addresses.city` at the time of order placement.

address_line1.description:
Primary street address line, including building number and street name.

Maps directly to `shopping_mall_order_addresses.street_line1` in the underlying snapshot table.

address_line2.description:
Secondary address line such as apartment, suite, floor, or building details.

This corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_order_addresses.street_line2` column and may be empty when not provided by the customer.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a single status transition event for an order in the shopping mall platform.

Used for listing status history or embedding compact status change information into other responses without including the full event payload, while still exposing the parent order context as a lightweight summary object.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order status event.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_order_status_events` record and is used to uniquely reference a single historical status change entry.

order.description:
Summary representation of the order whose status changed.

Replaces the raw foreign key to the master order so that consumers can understand which order this event belongs to without issuing additional API calls.

order_line_id.description:
Identifier of the specific order line impacted by this status event when applicable.

When non-null, this points to a particular line in `shopping_mall_order_lines`. When null, the status event applies to the entire order rather than a specific line.

previous_status.description:
Previous business status value of the order or order line before this event was applied.

This is a business-level status string derived from the order workflow and does not have to match the raw database enum name exactly, but should remain stable enough for analytics and UI mapping.

new_status.description:
New business status value of the order or order line after this event was applied.

Together with `previous_status`, this describes the transition that occurred for this event in the order lifecycle.

reason_code.description:
Optional machine-readable reason code explaining why this status change occurred.

Common examples include cancellation reasons, payment gateway outcomes, or internal error categories. Clients can use this code for analytics or localized message mapping.

message.description:
Optional human-readable message describing this status change.

This may be shown in customer-facing order history views or internal support tools to provide additional context beyond `reason_code`.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that triggered this status change, such as `customer`, `seller`, `platform_admin`, or `system`.

The value is aligned with business actor classifications and can be used for audit and analytics segmentation.

actor_id.description:
Identifier of the actor that triggered this status change when applicable.

For customer or seller events this is the corresponding actor id; for system or automated events this may hold a system identifier or service name.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when this status change actually occurred from a business perspective.

This may differ slightly from `created_at` if the event was ingested or synchronized from an external system after the fact.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this status event record was created in the system.

Stored in ISO 8601 format in UTC and used primarily for operational auditing and ordering of events as they were persisted.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellationRequest.IS.description:
Summary view of an order cancellation request in the shopping mall platform.

Used primarily in list responses and embedded contexts to show high-level information about a cancellation, including the parent order summary, without full audit and processing details. Designed to be lightweight for efficient transmission while still providing enough context for UI listing and filtering.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order cancellation request.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_order_cancellation_requests` record and is used to reference a single cancellation request entity.

order.description:
Summary representation of the customer-facing master order this cancellation request refers to.

Provides immediate context about which order is being cancelled, including key fields such as order number and monetary totals, without requiring an additional API call.

status.description:
Current business status of the cancellation request.

Represents the high-level lifecycle state as visible to customers and sellers. Typical examples include `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, or `cancelled_by_customer`. Exact allowed values are enforced by business rules at the service layer.

reason_code.description:
Machine-readable code representing the primary reason for requesting cancellation.

Usually mapped from the underlying `request_reason_category` field (for example, `changed_mind`, `ordered_by_mistake`, `stock_issue`, `policy_violation`, or `other`) and primarily used for analytics, reporting, and policy enforcement.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation request was first created.

Stored in ISO 8601 format in UTC and used for ordering, SLA evaluation, and reporting around cancellation request volumes over time.

IShoppingMallOrderReturnRequest.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a customer's order return or refund request in the shopping mall platform.

Used in list endpoints and embedded contexts to show compact information about a return or refund without full line-level and audit details. Optimized for dashboards and overview screens displaying multiple return requests at once.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order return request.

This maps directly to the `id` primary key column of the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` Prisma model.

order.description:
Summary information of the customer-facing master order that this return or refund request is associated with.

Replaces the raw `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key by providing a lightweight `IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary` association, so list and embedded views can render key order attributes (such as order number, date, and status) without additional API calls.

actor_type.description:
Actor type that initiated the return or refund request, as stored in the `actor_type` column of the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` table.

Typical current values include `customer`, but this field is modeled generically so that additional actor types (such as seller or platform_admin) can be supported in future workflows and analytics without schema changes.

request_status.description:
Current status of the return request as stored in the `request_status` column of the `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` table.

Typical values include states such as `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `awaiting_item`, `refunded`, or `closed`, and are enforced by the service layer according to the configured return/refund workflow.

request_reason_category.description:
Categorized reason for the return as stored in the `request_reason_category` column.

Common examples include `defective_item`, `wrong_item`, `not_as_described`, `size_issue`, or `changed_mind`. This field is used for analytics, policy enforcement, and operational reporting about why returns are initiated.

requested_resolution.description:
Requested resolution type captured when the return request is created, mapped from the `requested_resolution` column.

Common values include `refund`, `replacement`, or `store_credit`, and this field is used by back-office processes and automated workflows to route the request through the correct operational path and to measure resolution preference trends over time.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this return request record was created in the database.

Maps directly to the non-null `created_at` column on `shopping_mall_order_return_requests` and is represented as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string in API responses.

IShoppingMallOrderDispute.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a shopping mall order dispute used in list responses and lightweight embeddings.

Provides essential information about a dispute without including full relational collections or the complete history log, while mapping directly to columns on the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` Prisma model.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the order dispute record.

This corresponds to the `id` primary key column on the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` table.

order.description:
Summary information of the customer order that this dispute is associated with.

Replaces the raw `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key with a lightweight `IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary` association so that dispute lists and dashboards can render order context (such as order number and status) without additional API calls.

actor_type.description:
Actor type that opened the dispute, as stored in the `actor_type` column of the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` table.

Typical values include `customer`, `seller`, or `platform_admin`, and are used for analytics and routing the dispute to the correct resolution workflow.

issue_category.description:
Categorized type of problem being disputed, as stored in the `issue_category` column.

Examples include `non_delivery`, `damaged_item`, `incorrect_item`, `payment_issue`, or `policy_violation`. This field is primarily used for reporting, analytics, and dispute policy enforcement.

issue_title.description:
Short summary title describing the dispute, mapped from the non-null `issue_title` column on the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` table.

This value is used as the primary heading in dispute lists, dashboards, and notifications so that operators and actors can quickly understand the nature of the dispute without reading the full description.

dispute_status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the dispute, mirroring the value stored in the `dispute_status` column of the `shopping_mall_order_disputes` table.

Typical values include `open`, `awaiting_seller`, `awaiting_customer`, `resolved_customer_favored`, `resolved_seller_favored`, or `closed_without_action`, depending on the configured dispute workflow.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the dispute was first created and stored in the database.

Maps directly to the non-null `created_at` column and is returned as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this dispute record.

This corresponds to the non-null `updated_at` column on `shopping_mall_order_disputes` and is typically updated whenever status, category, or resolution-related fields change.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a payment method available on the shopping mall platform. Used for listing supported methods in configuration endpoints and for referencing the method in other DTOs without exposing full configuration details or provider secrets.

Each summary item corresponds directly to a row in `shopping_mall_payment_methods` and exposes the core business identifier, display label, logical method type, activation flag, ordering priority, and optional availability window timestamps used by administrative list and search screens.

In addition, it surfaces key optional configuration hints such as descriptive text, currency restrictions, and amount thresholds so that back‑office tools can make informed decisions without loading a full detail DTO.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment method definition.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_payment_methods` row and is used internally and in path parameters when addressing a specific payment method configuration from administrative APIs.

code.description:
Stable business identifier for the payment method used in APIs and configuration, such as `card`, `bank_transfer`, or `convenience_store`.

This value maps to the `code` column of `shopping_mall_payment_methods` and is unique across the platform so that integrations and configuration references can safely rely on it as a human-readable key.

display_name.description:
Human-readable name of the payment method shown to customers in checkout flows and administrative configuration screens.

This value comes from the `display_name` column of `shopping_mall_payment_methods` and is typically localized or selected to be understandable for non-technical operators.

description.description:
Optional longer description of the payment method configuration as stored in `shopping_mall_payment_methods.description`.

Administrators can use this field to document eligibility rules, operational notes, or guidance for support teams. In list and summary views it is often displayed as secondary text or a tooltip rather than a primary label.

method_type.description:
Logical classification of the payment method, mapped from the `method_type` column of `shopping_mall_payment_methods`.

Typical values include `card`, `bank`, `wallet`, or `offline` depending on how the payment is processed. This field is used in business rules, reporting, and for filtering and grouping in admin UIs.

currency_restriction.description:
Optional currency restriction information for this payment method, mapped from `shopping_mall_payment_methods.currency_restriction`.

Implementations may encode this as a list of ISO currency codes or a pattern when the method is not globally available. List and search screens can use it to highlight methods that apply only to certain markets or checkout currencies.

min_amount.description:
Optional minimum order amount threshold for which this payment method is allowed, mapped from `shopping_mall_payment_methods.min_amount`.

When present, orders below this amount should not be offered this payment method. Summary views can show this threshold so that operators understand why a method is not available for small orders.

max_amount.description:
Optional maximum order amount threshold for which this payment method is allowed, mapped from `shopping_mall_payment_methods.max_amount`.

When present, orders above this amount should not be offered this payment method. Summary views can show this limit to explain why large orders may require alternative payment options.

priority.description:
Display priority for this payment method in checkout and administrative lists, mapped from the `priority` column of `shopping_mall_payment_methods`.

Lower values are shown earlier. Administrative grids often sort by this field so that operators can control the visual ordering of payment options.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this payment method is currently active and eligible to be presented to customers during checkout.

This flag comes from the `is_active` column of `shopping_mall_payment_methods` and is used by both admin UIs and backend logic to decide whether the method can be selected for new orders.

starts_at.description:
Optional datetime after which this payment method becomes eligible for use in checkout, mapped from the `starts_at` column of `shopping_mall_payment_methods`.

When present, admin UIs can show this as the beginning of an availability window. If null, the method is considered available immediately once active.

ends_at.description:
Optional datetime after which this payment method should no longer appear in checkout selections, mapped from the `ends_at` column of `shopping_mall_payment_methods`.

When present, this is treated as the end of the availability window for new checkouts, although historical orders may still reference the method after this time.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a payment transaction in the shopping mall platform, optimized for list views and embedding in other DTOs.

This DTO is designed for lightweight listing and cross-entity embedding scenarios where administrators or back-office tools need to quickly scan payment activity. It exposes key identifiers, monetary amounts, high-level status, and minimal contextual information without loading the full transaction graph.

In addition to primitive fields such as identifiers and amounts, it may include small `.ISummary` association objects that provide essential context, like the payment method or provider, while still avoiding heavy compositions or reverse relations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment transaction.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_payment_transactions.id` and is used as the primary reference key across APIs, logs, and back-office tooling.

order_id.description:
Identifier of the customer order associated with this payment transaction.

This corresponds to `shopping_mall_payment_transactions.shopping_mall_order_id` and can be used by clients to navigate to order-level views or to correlate lists of payments with master orders.

amount.description:
Primary business-level monetary amount to display for this payment transaction in list views.

Typically this corresponds to the captured amount for simple flows, but it may also follow platform-specific business rules (for example, the authorized amount or a net effective amount). It is a derived field, not a direct column in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`, and should be interpreted as the main figure operators expect to see for this transaction.

authorized_amount.description:
Total amount that has been successfully authorized by the payment provider for this transaction, mapped from `shopping_mall_payment_transactions.authorized_amount`.

This value may be null when the provider or flow does not support a distinct authorization step, or when authorization has not yet succeeded. When present, it allows operators to compare authorized and captured amounts to understand remaining capture potential.

captured_amount.description:
Total amount that has been successfully captured from the provider for this transaction, mapped from `shopping_mall_payment_transactions.captured_amount`.

This value may be null if no capture has occurred yet. In reporting and dashboards it is often compared against the primary `amount` field and `refunded_amount` to understand net settlement.

refunded_amount.description:
Total amount that has been refunded against this payment transaction, aggregated from all related refund transactions and stored in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions.refunded_amount`.

The value is never null at the database level; zero indicates that no refunds have been processed. In list views, this field helps operators quickly assess how much of the original payment has been returned to the customer.

provider_name.description:
Name or code of the payment provider handling this transaction, such as a gateway identifier, mapped from `shopping_mall_payment_transactions.provider_name`.

This field is essential for reconciliation, support workflows, and reporting, allowing operators to quickly see which external system processed the payment.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for the amounts in this transaction (for example, "USD" or "KRW").

This field maps to the `currency` column of `shopping_mall_payment_transactions` and allows clients to render localized currency information and to group or filter payments by currency in reporting views.

status.description:
High‑level business status of the payment transaction, mapped from the `payment_status` column of `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`.

Typical values align with platform payment lifecycle states such as `payment_pending`, `payment_in_progress`, `payment_authorized`, `payment_captured`, `payment_failed`, `payment_expired`, `partially_refunded`, or `refunded`. Clients should treat this field as the primary, normalized status indicator for list screens and dashboards.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment transaction record was initially created.

This is stored in `shopping_mall_payment_transactions.created_at` and is commonly used for sorting, filtering, and building time-based reports over payment activity.

payment_method.description:
Summary of the payment method that was used for this transaction.

This association is derived from the foreign key `shopping_mall_payment_transactions.shopping_mall_payment_method_id` and provides essential contextual information such as method code and display name without requiring consumers to perform an additional lookup. It follows the BELONGS-TO pattern using the `.ISummary` variant to avoid circular references and heavy compositions.

IShoppingMallPaymentAuthorization.ISumma.description:
Summary view of a payment authorization attempt for a payment transaction.

This DTO is used primarily in list views or as lightweight embedded information under a payment transaction, allowing operators to quickly understand authorization history without loading the full authorization details.

It exposes key identifiers, the authorized monetary amount and its currency projected from `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.amount` and `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.currency`, the current `authorization_status` from `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.authorization_status`, the creation timestamp from `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.created_at`, and a summary of the parent payment transaction for contextual understanding.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment authorization record.

This is the primary key of the authorization attempt in the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.id` column and is used to reference this authorization from other entities, audit logs, and reconciliation workflows.

amount.description:
Amount that was requested to be authorized for this attempt.

The value is stored in the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.amount` column and is expressed in the same currency as the parent payment transaction. It should match or be less than the intended charge amount for the related order, subject to gateway rules and platform business policies.

currency.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code associated with the authorization amount.

This value maps directly to the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.currency` column and must be consistent with the currency used on the parent payment transaction so that financial reporting, reconciliation, and analytics remain coherent across the payment domain.

authorization_status.description:
Business status for this authorization attempt, mapped from the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.authorization_status` column.

Typical values include states such as `authorized`, `authorization_failed`, or `authorization_voided`. Implementations should constrain this field to a well-defined enum in application code, even though it is represented as a free-form string in this OpenAPI schema, to ensure consistent status handling in back-office tools and services.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this authorization record was created.

This value comes from the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.created_at` column and represents the moment the platform recorded the authorization attempt. It is commonly used for ordering histories, building audit trails, and constructing time-based reports over authorization activity.

payment_transaction.description:
Summary of the parent payment transaction that this authorization belongs to.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_payment_authorizations.shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key and provides high-level context such as the overall payment status, the chosen payment method, and transaction-level identifiers so that consumers can understand where this authorization fits within the overall payment flow without performing additional lookups.

IShoppingMallPaymentCapture.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single payment capture attempt within the shopping mall payment system.

It represents a lightweight projection of a capture operation that finalizes all or part of a previously authorized payment transaction. This summary is optimized for list views, status timelines, and embedding inside other payment-related DTOs rather than for full detail inspection.

It exposes key identifiers; the captured monetary amount and currency taken from `shopping_mall_payment_captures.amount` and `shopping_mall_payment_captures.currency`; the current `capture_status` from `shopping_mall_payment_captures.capture_status`; the creation timestamp from `shopping_mall_payment_captures.created_at`; and a summary of the parent payment transaction needed to understand capture history without loading full capture details or related entities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment capture record.

This is the primary key of the capture entity stored in the `shopping_mall_payment_captures.id` column and is used to reference this capture from other entities, logs, and reconciliation processes.

amount.description:
Monetary amount that was requested to be captured in this operation.

The value is stored in the `shopping_mall_payment_captures.amount` column and is expressed in the transaction currency. When business rules and gateway constraints are enforced correctly, this amount must not exceed the remaining authorized amount on the parent payment transaction.

currency.description:
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the captured amount.

This value maps directly to the `shopping_mall_payment_captures.currency` column and must match the currency defined on the parent payment transaction to ensure consistent financial reporting, settlement, and reconciliation across payment records.

capture_status.description:
Business status for this capture attempt, mapped from the `shopping_mall_payment_captures.capture_status` column.

Common values include `capture_succeeded` or `capture_failed`. Concrete implementations should constrain this field to a well-defined enum in application code, even though it is represented as a string in this OpenAPI schema, so that operational dashboards and automated workflows can reason reliably about capture outcomes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this capture record was created.

The value comes from the `shopping_mall_payment_captures.created_at` column and is typically used to order capture attempts chronologically, to construct payment timelines, and to support audit and compliance reporting around the capture lifecycle.

payment_transaction.description:
Summary of the parent payment transaction that this capture belongs to.

This association is derived from the `shopping_mall_payment_captures.shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key and provides context such as the original authorization amount, overall payment status, and selected payment method so that clients can interpret the capture in the correct transactional context without issuing separate read calls for the full payment transaction entity.

IShoppingMallPaymentStatusEvent.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a payment status transition event for a shopping mall payment transaction.

Represents a compact record in the payment status history that tracks how a payment transaction moved between logical states over time. This summary is suitable for timelines, audit overviews, and embedding within payment or order detail responses where only high‑level event information is required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payment status event.

This is the primary key of the status event record in the database.

payment_transaction.description:
Payment transaction whose status changed in this event.

Replaces the raw `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key and provides contextual information (such as payment number, amount, and current status) needed to understand this status event in timelines without additional API calls.

previous_status.description:
Logical payment status value before this event occurred.

This field is null for the very first status event of a payment transaction when no prior status existed.

new_status.description:
Logical payment status value after this event was applied.

This value represents the current state of the payment transaction immediately following the event and uses the same business vocabulary as the `payment_status` column on `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when the status change was recorded by the platform.

This field corresponds to the `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_payment_status_events` Prisma model and is expressed in ISO 8601 date‑time format in UTC for ordering events in status timelines.

admin.description:
Platform administrator responsible for this status event when it represents a manual override or administrative adjustment.

This association is populated when `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` is set in the underlying Prisma model and allows audit views and timelines to render who triggered the change without introducing reverse collections or circular references, by relying on the lightweight platform admin summary representation.

IShoppingMallRefundTransaction.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a refund transaction in the shopping mall platform.

Provides lightweight information about a single refund transaction, suitable for list views and embedding into other entities. It omits heavy relational collections and internal audit fields while exposing identifiers, monetary amounts, actor context, lifecycle status, and high-level reason metadata needed to understand the refund at a glance.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund transaction.

This is the primary key of the refund record in the database and is used as the technical identifier in internal APIs and logs.

code.description:
Business-facing identifier or code for the refund transaction.

This corresponds conceptually to the `refund_number` column in the underlying Prisma model and is the value typically shown to customers, sellers, and support staff in user interfaces and communications when referencing a specific refund.

order.description:
Customer-facing master order that this refund is associated with.

Replaces the raw `shopping_mall_order_id` foreign key in the Prisma model and provides a lightweight summary of the order, allowing list and detail views of refunds to display key order context such as order number, buyer, and status without additional API calls.

payment_transaction.description:
Original payment transaction that this refund partially or fully reverses.

Replaces the raw `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id` foreign key and exposes a summarized payment transaction, enabling clients to understand which payment the refund applies to without performing separate lookups.

total_refund_amount.description:
Total monetary amount that has been refunded in this transaction.

This value typically corresponds to the `refunded_amount` column in `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` and the sum of all associated refund items. It is expressed in the transaction currency and is useful for list and dashboard summaries where only the aggregate refunded amount is needed.

requested_amount.description:
Amount that was originally requested to be refunded by the initiating actor, mapped from the non-nullable `requested_amount` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` Prisma model.

This value allows operators, policy engines, and analytical tooling to compare the initial refund request with the actual total refunded amount represented by `total_refund_amount`. Differences between these two values can indicate partial approvals, policy-driven adjustments, or exceptional handling that may warrant additional review or explanation in support workflows.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code for this refund transaction (for example, `USD` or `KRW`).

The value matches the currency of the associated payment transaction and ensures that clients can correctly display and format the refund amount in multi-currency environments.

status.description:
High-level lifecycle status of the refund transaction.

Typical values follow the business status vocabulary from the Prisma model, such as `refund_pending`, `refund_in_progress`, `refund_failed`, or `refund_completed`. Finance, support, and analytics views rely on this field to understand where in the refund process this transaction currently resides and to group refunds by their current processing state.

actor_type.description:
Categorical type of the actor that initiated or owns the refund request, mapped from the non-nullable `actor_type` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` Prisma model.

Typical values include `customer`, `seller`, or `admin`, indicating whether the refund was initiated by the buyer, the merchant, or a platform administrator. This field is essential for list views, dashboards, and analytics to group and filter refunds by their origin and to support operational workflows and policy enforcement. It also aligns with the presence of `initiator_customer`, `initiator_seller`, and `initiator_platform_admin` reference properties in this summary, which provide richer context about the specific initiating user when available.

reason_category.description:
Categorized business reason for the refund, mapped from the non-nullable `reason_category` column in the `shopping_mall_refund_transactions` Prisma model.

Typical values include categories such as `customer_cancellation`, `seller_cancellation`, `return`, or `admin_adjustment`. This field provides a high-level explanation of why the refund exists and is heavily used by support teams and analytical reports to identify patterns in cancellations, returns, and discretionary admin adjustments, as well as to measure policy usage and customer experience impact over time.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund transaction record was created in the platform.

This value is typically used for sorting and for rendering timelines in administrative and customer-facing views and is expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC.

initiator_customer.description:
Customer who initiated the refund request when the refund originates from the buyer side.

This association is present when `initiator_customer_id` is set in the underlying Prisma model and provides a compact view of the customer actor, aligned with the `actor_type` value `customer`.

initiator_seller.description:
Seller who initiated the refund when the request originates from the merchant side.

This association is present when `initiator_seller_id` is populated in the underlying Prisma model and allows refunds initiated by sellers to be clearly associated with the responsible merchant, aligned with the `actor_type` value `seller`.

initiator_platform_admin.description:
Platform administrator who initiated or approved the refund when it is an admin-driven adjustment.

This association is populated when `initiator_platformadmin_id` is set in the Prisma model and corresponds to refunds with `actor_type` value `admin`, enabling audit and reporting tools to see which administrator performed the action without introducing reverse collections on the admin entity.

IShoppingMallRefundItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single line item within a refund transaction.

Represents the per-line breakdown of a refund, typically linked to a specific order line or order seller segment. Intended for list views inside a refund detail page or for lightweight embedding when showing refund allocations. Does not include nested collections or audit history.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund item record.

This UUID key corresponds to a single row in the underlying refund items table and is used by APIs, logs, and UIs whenever a particular refund line needs to be addressed or inspected.

refundTransaction.description:
Summary of the parent refund transaction that this line item belongs to.

Provides high-level financial and status context for the refund that aggregates this item, so list views and embedded usages do not need to perform an additional lookup by `refund_transaction_id`. The summary typically includes the refund business code, overall refunded amount, currency, and lifecycle status.

order.description:
Summary of the customer-facing master order that this refund item is associated with.

Allows UIs and reporting tools to show which order the refund allocation belongs to without needing to dereference the raw `order_id`. This summary commonly exposes the order number, customer, currency, and high-level order status so that a refund line can be visually tied back to its original purchase context.

orderLine.description:
Optional summary of the specific order line that this refund item refers to, when the refund is tied to a concrete line item.

This association is populated when the refund line is line-specific (for example, a refund of a particular SKU or quantity from the order). It is omitted for purely order-level adjustments that are not tied to a single order line. Including this summary avoids additional lookups by `order_line_id` in common list and detail views.

refunded_quantity.description:
Quantity of discrete units being refunded for the associated order line.

This value represents an integer count of units (for example, number of items) and should align with the original `quantity` field on the corresponding order line. It is typically non-negative and only populated when the refund is line-specific; for purely monetary order-level adjustments this field may be absent.

refund_amount.description:
Monetary amount refunded for this specific line item, expressed in the same currency as the parent refund transaction.

This field represents the amount of money the platform or seller is returning for this line component. It may be a full or partial refund relative to the original line total and is used, together with the parent refund transaction, to compute financial summaries for orders, customers, and sellers.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code (for example, "USD" or "KRW") representing the currency of this refund item.

The code should match both the currency of the parent refund transaction and the associated order to avoid cross-currency inconsistencies. Clients can rely on this field to select appropriate currency formatting and to group refund lines in multi-currency analytical views.

IShoppingMallPaymentChargeback.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a payment chargeback in the shopping mall platform.

Used in list views, search results, and as a lightweight reference inside other entities. Contains identifying information, key financial amounts, and high-level status but omits heavy relational details and internal audit data.

id.description: Unique identifier of the payment chargeback record.

paymentTransaction.description:
Summary of the original payment transaction that this chargeback is associated with.

Provides enough information for dashboards and reports to understand which payment was impacted without exposing raw payment_transaction_id and forcing additional lookups.

order.description:
Summary of the customer-facing order impacted by this chargeback.

Allows business and risk tooling to display which order is affected by the chargeback without relying on separate order_id dereferencing calls.

amount.description:
Total monetary amount of the chargeback in the transaction currency.

Represents the gross amount that has been charged back by the payment network or financial institution.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency code (for example, USD, EUR, KRW) representing the currency of the chargeback amount.

Should match the currency of the underlying payment transaction to maintain consistency in reporting and settlement.

reason_code.description:
Provider-specific reason or category code that explains why the chargeback was initiated.

Typically comes from the card network or payment provider (for example, `fraud`, `merchandise_not_received`), and is used for risk analysis and dispute workflows.

status.description:
Current business status of the chargeback within the platform workflow.

Common examples include values such as `pending_review`, `accepted`, `disputed`, or `reversed`. Concrete enum values are defined in the underlying Prisma model or business logic layer.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when the chargeback was first reported or registered by the payment provider.

Used as the primary reference time for time-based analytics and for ordering chargeback events in UI lists.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent status change or update to this chargeback record.

Supports UI display of last activity time and aids in monitoring stale or unresolved chargebacks.

IShoppingMallSellerPayout.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a seller payout batch in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is a read-optimized projection of a single row in the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` Prisma model and is primarily used for payout history lists, finance dashboards, and links from related financial entities. It exposes the main identifiers, status, monetary totals, and key provider and failure diagnostics without expanding into line-level payout items.

The monetary amounts map 1:1 to the corresponding database columns: `gross_amount` represents the sum of all positive earnings in the batch, `fee_amount` aggregates platform commissions and fees, `adjustment_amount` captures manual or exceptional adjustments, and `net_amount` is the final amount actually paid out to the seller.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller payout batch.

This is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` record and is used by internal services and external API consumers to reference a specific payout across APIs, logs, and reports.

payout_number.description:
Business identifier of the payout batch, unique per seller for reconciliation and communication.

This value is typically more human-friendly than the UUID `id` and may be used on statements, exports, and emails as the primary reference when communicating about a payout with the seller and internal finance staff.

payout_status.description:
Current status of the payout, as stored in the `payout_status` column of `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`.

Common values include states such as `payout_pending`, `payout_in_progress`, `payout_failed`, or `payout_sent`. Integrators should treat this as the source of truth for whether a payout is still pending, has been successfully sent, or encountered errors that require manual intervention.

currency.description:
ISO currency code of the payout, as stored in the `currency` column of `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`.

This is an ISO 4217 code such as `USD`, `EUR`, or `KRW` and determines the unit in which all monetary fields of this summary (`gross_amount`, `fee_amount`, `adjustment_amount`, and `net_amount`) are expressed.

gross_amount.description:
Total gross amount of all positive earnings included in this payout before fees and adjustments.

The value maps directly to the `gross_amount` column of `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` and typically aggregates item revenue, shipping revenue, and other seller-credited components for the covered period and orders.

fee_amount.description:
Total amount of platform fees or commissions deducted from the seller as part of this payout.

This corresponds to the nullable `fee_amount` column in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. When present, it represents the sum of all platform fees and commissions that reduce the gross earnings before arriving at the net payout. When absent, either there were no fees or they were not broken out at this level.

adjustment_amount.description:
Net effect of manual adjustments included in this payout, mapped from the nullable `adjustment_amount` column.

Adjustments may include manual credits or debits applied by operations or finance teams, such as goodwill credits, corrections, or retroactive adjustments. A positive value increases the payout to the seller, whereas a negative value reduces it.

net_amount.description:
Net amount actually paid out to the seller after fees and adjustments.

This value is taken from the `net_amount` column of `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` and represents the final amount sent to the seller via the configured provider. In finance and reconciliation views, this is the figure that should match bank statements or provider settlement reports.

period_start.description:
Optional start of the earnings period covered by this payout.

This corresponds to the nullable `period_start` column and is typically used when payouts are batched over a specific time window (for example, a weekly or monthly period). When provided, it helps finance teams and sellers understand which transactions are expected to be included.

period_end.description:
Optional end of the earnings period covered by this payout.

It maps to the nullable `period_end` column in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. Together with `period_start`, it describes the time interval whose transactions were aggregated into this payout batch for reporting and reconciliation.

provider_name.description:
Name or code of the external payment provider or bank used to send this payout.

This maps to the nullable `provider_name` column and may contain values such as a payment processor name, internal clearing system, or bank identifier. It is primarily used by operations and finance teams when reconciling payouts with external settlement channels.

provider_payout_id.description:
Identifier for this payout at the external provider or bank.

The value maps to the nullable `provider_payout_id` column and is typically a reference or transaction ID returned by the payment provider. It enables precise tracing of payouts when investigating disputes, reconciliation mismatches, or provider-side issues.

failure_reason_code.description:
Optional machine-readable code describing why the payout failed.

This field corresponds to the nullable `failure_reason_code` column on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`. It is populated when `payout_status` indicates a failure and allows automated systems or dashboards to categorize and aggregate failure causes.

failure_reason_message.description:
Optional human-readable message with more detail about a payout failure.

The value is taken from the nullable `failure_reason_message` column and is designed to be shown in internal tools or logs to help operators quickly understand what went wrong when a payout could not be completed successfully.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this payout record was created.

This is the `created_at` column from `shopping_mall_seller_payouts` and is generally set when the payout batch is first generated by the settlement logic. It is useful for sorting payout history and for understanding when the batch entered the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this payout record was last updated.

This maps to the `updated_at` column and changes whenever the payout batch status, amounts, or associated metadata are modified. It allows operators to see when the latest state transition or correction was applied.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller that receives this payout batch.

The embedded `IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary` DTO provides concise seller identification and display information, so list and dashboard consumers can render meaningful seller context alongside payout rows without issuing additional seller lookups.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single payout item included in a seller payout batch.

This DTO is a projection of a single row in the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` Prisma model and represents a specific monetary component such as item revenue, shipping revenue, a refund deduction, or a manual adjustment. It is designed for list views in seller settlement history, payout statement details, and admin reconciliation tools.

Each payout item links a portion of the payout back to the originating order, seller segment, or order line where applicable, and breaks out the gross amount, platform fee allocation, and resulting net amount that contributes to the seller’s overall payout.

id.description:
Primary key of the seller payout item.

This is the unique identifier of the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` record and is used to reference the line when drilling into detailed payout views or when reconciling specific components of a payout.

sellerPayoutId.description:
Identifier of the parent seller payout batch that this item contributes to.

This value maps to the `shopping_mall_seller_payout_id` foreign key column and groups multiple payout items under a single aggregate payout batch row in `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`.

orderId.description:
Identifier of the order that this payout item is derived from when applicable.

This corresponds to the nullable `shopping_mall_order_id` column. For revenue and refund components tied to a specific order, this field enables navigation from payout statements back to the original customer order.

orderSellerSegmentId.description:
Identifier of the seller segment within the order that this payout item relates to, when allocation is tracked at segment level.

This field maps to the nullable `shopping_mall_order_seller_segment_id` column and allows finer-grained reconciliation when a multi-seller order is split into per-seller segments.

orderLineId.description:
Identifier of the order line that this payout item relates to when the payout is calculated at line level.

The value map to the nullable `shopping_mall_order_line_id` column in `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`. It is typically populated for item-level revenues and refunds to provide precise linkage to the purchased SKU.

component_type.description:
Type of component included in the payout, mapped from the `component_type` column.

Common examples include `item_revenue`, `shipping_revenue`, `refund_deduction`, or `manual_adjustment`. Downstream tools and reports can use this field to group and aggregate payout items by business meaning.

description.description:
Optional human-readable explanation for this payout component as shown in seller statements.

This is derived from the nullable `description` column on `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items` and can contain free-form details that help sellers and finance staff understand why this line appears in a payout.

grossAmount.description:
Gross amount for this payout component before deducting any platform fees.

This field maps to the non-nullable `gross_amount` column and typically represents the positive value of the underlying transaction component, such as the item price or shipping fee credited to the seller.

platformFeeAmount.description:
Amount of platform fees allocated to this component when available.

This value corresponds to the nullable `fee_amount` column on `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`. When present, it indicates how much of the platform’s commission or fees is associated with this specific payout line; when absent, either no fee was allocated or the fee is tracked elsewhere.

netAmount.description:
Net amount from this component that contributes to the seller’s payout after fees.

This field maps to the non-nullable `net_amount` column in `shopping_mall_seller_payout_items`. It is the signed amount that actually affects the seller’s payout, and it is used when summing all items to match the batch-level `net_amount` on `shopping_mall_seller_payouts`.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this payout item record was created.

This is taken from the non-nullable `created_at` column and is typically set when the payout calculation job generates the line. It is useful for troubleshooting, chronological analysis, and incremental data exports.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller that receives this payout item.

Even though the seller is implied by the parent payout, embedding `IShoppingMallSeller.ISummary` here allows consumers to render standalone payout item lists and reports that still show seller context without fetching additional data.

IShoppingMallPaymentSettlementReportRow.description:
Represents a single aggregated settlement row in a payment settlement report for the shopping mall platform.

Each row summarizes the financial settlement information for a grouping key such as seller, period, or payout batch. It is designed for reporting and reconciliation views, not for direct persistence. Values are expected to be derived from underlying payment, refund, chargeback, and payout records.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the settlement report row.

This is a technical identifier for the reporting system and may not correspond directly to a primary key in a transactional table.

seller.description:
Seller associated with this settlement row.

Provides high-level information about the seller whose transactions are summarized in this row.

period_start.description: Inclusive start datetime of the settlement period for this row in ISO 8601 format.

period_end.description: Exclusive end datetime of the settlement period for this row in ISO 8601 format.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code in which all monetary values of this row are expressed.

Examples: "USD", "KRW", "EUR".

gross_sales_amount.description:
Total gross sales amount for the period before any discounts, refunds, or fees.

This includes the sum of all captured payment amounts for completed orders associated with the seller in this period.

discount_amount.description:
Total discounts applied to orders within the period.

Includes promotional discounts, coupons, or other price reductions that affect the seller’s receivable amount.

refund_amount.description:
Total amount refunded to customers within the period.

This includes full and partial refunds that reduce the net amount payable to the seller.

chargeback_amount.description:
Total monetary impact of chargebacks recognized in this period.

Includes chargeback principal amounts and associated fees deducted due to disputes resolved against the seller.

platform_fee_amount.description:
Total platform service fees charged to the seller for this period.

Typically includes commission fees, transaction fees, and any other marketplace service fees.

tax_withheld_amount.description:
Total tax amount withheld by the platform on behalf of the seller for this settlement period.

Used for tax reporting and compliance purposes.

net_settlement_amount.description:
Net amount to be settled to the seller for this period.

Calculated as gross sales minus discounts, refunds, chargebacks, platform fees, and tax withholdings.

payout_status.description:
High-level status of the payout associated with this settlement row.

Typical values may include:
- "pending": Settlement calculated but not yet paid out
- "in_progress": Payout initiated and being processed
- "completed": Payout successfully transferred
- "failed": Payout attempt failed and requires attention

payout_reference_code.description:
Reference code of the payout batch or payout transaction that will settle or has settled this row.

Useful for cross-referencing with payout statements, bank transfers, or external settlement systems.

generated_at.description: Datetime when this settlement report row was generated in ISO 8601 format.

IShoppingMallSellerPayoutStatementRow.description:
Represents a single row within a seller payout statement on the shopping mall platform.

Each row corresponds to a concrete payout item included in a seller payout batch, typically linked to one or more orders, order lines, or settlement report rows. It is used to present detailed payout breakdowns to sellers and finance teams.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the payout statement row.

Used to uniquely reference a specific payout item within the system.

seller.description: Seller who receives the payout amount represented by this statement row.

payout_batch_id.description:
Identifier of the payout batch that groups this statement row.

All rows with the same payout_batch_id belong to the same settlement transfer, such as a bank transfer or remittance batch.

payout_sequence_number.description: Sequence number of this row within the payout batch, used for stable ordering in statements.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code of the payout amounts for this row.

Examples: "USD", "KRW", "EUR".

gross_payable_amount.description:
Total gross amount payable to the seller in this payout row before deductions.

Derived from the sum of positively contributing settlements such as completed order revenue.

platform_fee_amount.description:
Total platform fee amount deducted in this payout row.

Represents commissions and other platform service fees charged against the seller’s gross payable amount.

refund_and_chargeback_adjustment_amount.description:
Net adjustment amount due to refunds and chargebacks associated with the items covered by this payout row.

Usually a negative amount (deduction), but may be positive if prior over-deductions are being corrected.

tax_withheld_amount.description:
Tax amount withheld by the platform for this payout row.

Covers withholding tax or other tax obligations the platform is responsible to remit on behalf of the seller.

other_adjustment_amount.description:
Additional adjustments applied to this payout row that are not covered by platform fees, refunds, chargebacks, or tax.

Examples include manual corrections, promotional incentives, or penalties.

net_payout_amount.description:
Final net payout amount to be transferred to the seller for this statement row.

Calculated as gross_payable_amount minus all deductions and plus/minus any adjustments.

settlement_period_start.description: Inclusive start datetime of the settlement period covered by this payout row in ISO 8601 format.

settlement_period_end.description: Exclusive end datetime of the settlement period covered by this payout row in ISO 8601 format.

related_settlement_report_row_ids.description:
List of identifiers of settlement report rows that were aggregated to produce this payout statement row.

Provides traceability between detailed settlement calculations and final payout entries.

payout_method.description:
Payment method used to transfer the payout amount to the seller.

Examples: "bank_transfer", "virtual_account", "e_wallet".

payout_status.description:
Current status of the payout represented by this statement row.

Typical values may include:
- "pending": Payout scheduled but not yet initiated
- "processing": Payout in progress
- "completed": Payout successfully transferred
- "failed": Payout attempt failed
- "cancelled": Payout was cancelled or reversed.

payout_initiated_at.description:
Datetime when the payout transfer was initiated in ISO 8601 format.

May be null if payout has not yet been initiated.

payout_completed_at.description:
Datetime when the payout transfer was successfully completed in ISO 8601 format.

May be null if payout has not yet completed or has failed.

IShoppingMallInventoryItem.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an inventory item in the shopping mall platform.

Represents a lightweight snapshot of per-SKU inventory state that is optimized for list views, dashboards, and embedding inside other DTOs. The summary focuses on identifiers, stock levels, and a high-level stock status indicator rather than full configuration detail.

It is typically returned inside paginated list responses such as `IPageIShoppingMallInventoryItem.ISummary` for search and monitoring operations.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the inventory item record.

Maps directly to the primary key `id` of the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` table and can be used to retrieve the full detail record when needed.

product_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU whose inventory this summary represents.

This foreign key references `shopping_mall_product_skus.id` via the `product_sku_id` column. Summary views keep this as an ID to avoid expanding SKU graphs; detailed SKU information can be fetched via product/SKU APIs if required.

on_hand_quantity.description:
Number of units physically available in storage for this SKU, not yet sold or reserved.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `on_hand_quantity` column in the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` table and represents the system-of-record quantity used for all inventory calculations, before considering reservations or soft business constraints.

available_quantity.description:
Current available, sellable quantity of this SKU as computed by the inventory subsystem.

This value is typically derived from `on_hand_quantity` minus `reserved_quantity` and may incorporate additional business adjustments such as safety stock, backorder or preorder rules, and temporary holds. It is not a persisted database column but a computed figure exposed specifically for dashboards and list views so clients do not need to recompute it.

reserved_quantity.description:
Current quantity that is reserved for open orders or in-progress checkouts.

These units are not yet fulfilled but are temporarily unavailable for new allocations. Exposing this value in the summary helps operators quickly identify SKUs that are heavily committed and understand the gap between on-hand and available quantities.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Optional threshold at or below which this SKU should be considered low stock.

This value maps to the nullable `low_stock_threshold` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_items`. When present, dashboards and catalog components can use it to trigger low-stock indicators, notifications, or search filters. When null, the SKU either uses global defaults or is not subject to low-stock alerting rules.

stock_status.description:
High-level availability status flag for this inventory item.

This mirrors the `stock_status` value from the base DTO and Prisma model, with typical values such as `in_stock`, `low_stock`, `out_of_stock`, `backorder_allowed`, or `preorder_only`. It allows list views to color-code or group items by operational state without requiring consumers to interpret numeric stock levels directly.

backorder_enabled.description:
Indicates whether backorders are allowed for this SKU based on current configuration and policies.

This field reflects the non-nullable `backorder_enabled` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_items` and summarizes whether customers may continue to place orders even when on-hand stock is insufficient. Detailed configuration is stored in the related `shopping_mall_backorder_settings` model, but this flag gives dashboards and catalog components an immediate yes/no signal.

preorder_enabled.description:
Indicates whether this SKU is currently available for preorder only, before normal stock is available.

The value maps to the non-nullable `preorder_enabled` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_items`. When true, the item is typically surfaced with preorder messaging and may follow separate fulfillment timelines governed by `shopping_mall_preorder_settings`. When false, the SKU behaves according to normal stock and backorder rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory item record was created.

Stored in the non-nullable `created_at` column of `shopping_mall_inventory_items`, this value helps administrators and analytics tools understand how long an inventory record has existed, analyze onboarding or catalog growth patterns, and sort or filter inventory items by age.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent inventory state update.

Mapped from the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_items`, this timestamp is useful for monitoring the staleness of inventory data in list views, troubleshooting synchronization issues, and ensuring that dashboards reflect recent operational changes.

IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.ISumma.description:
Summary view of an inventory reservation in the shopping mall platform.

Represents a lightweight snapshot of a temporary inventory hold associated with a checkout or order flow. This summary focuses on identifiers, reserved quantity, and linkage to orders or order lines, making it suitable for list views and embedding in higher-level order/inventory monitoring responses.

Used in reservation monitoring tools, order diagnostics, and seller/admin dashboards where only basic reservation information is needed.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the inventory reservation record.

Maps directly to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` table and can be used to navigate to more detailed reservation views when required.

inventory_item_id.description:
Identifier of the inventory item that this reservation is holding quantity against.

Foreign key referencing `shopping_mall_inventory_items.id`. In summary views this is kept as an ID to preserve scoping to the parent inventory item identified in the path parameter or outer context without inflating the payload size.

reserved_quantity.description:
Number of units reserved from the related inventory item.

Represents the quantity that is temporarily held and not available for other customers until the reservation is released or converted to a fulfillment. Non-negative integer aligned with the `reserved_quantity` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations`.

reservation_state.description:
Current state of the reservation such as `pending`, `active`, `consumed`, `expired`, or `cancelled`.

This field directly maps to the non-nullable `reservation_state` column in the `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` table and describes where in its lifecycle the reservation currently sits. Monitoring tools and diagnostics use this value to distinguish reservations that are still holding stock from those that have been finalized or invalidated.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when this reservation expires if payment is not completed.

Mapped from the nullable `expires_at` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations`. After this timestamp the system may automatically release the reserved quantity back to available inventory if the checkout or order has not progressed, depending on business rules and background jobs.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this reservation record was created.

This non-nullable value comes from the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_reservations` and is critical for understanding how long the reservation has been in place, constructing timelines, and tuning reservation expiry and cleanup processes.

order.description:
Summary information about the order that this reservation is associated with, when applicable.

Provides key order context such as order number, status, and key timestamps for use in list views and dashboards without requiring additional order lookup calls. This is a convenience projection on top of the underlying `order_id` foreign key.

order_line.description:
Summary of the specific order line that consumes this reservation, when applicable.

Allows list views to display which SKU and quantity within the order are linked to the reservation while keeping the payload compact. It is derived from the `order_line_id` foreign key and the associated `shopping_mall_order_lines` record.

IShoppingMallInventoryMovement.ISummary.description:
Summary view of an inventory movement record in the shopping mall system.

Provides lightweight information about a single stock change event for a specific SKU and location, suitable for list views, history timelines, and auditing summaries. The parent inventory item is referenced by ID only to avoid circular references when embedding summaries under inventory item detail views.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the inventory movement record.

This is the primary key of the corresponding row in `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` and is used to retrieve full movement details or to correlate with other audit data.

inventory_item_id.description:
Identifier of the inventory item (SKU + location) whose quantity was affected by this movement.

This field is the foreign key to the `shopping_mall_inventory_items` table and allows list views to link movements back to the owning inventory record. When more context about the item is required, clients should call inventory item endpoints using this identifier.

movement_type.description:
