Type of inventory movement that occurred, such as `restock`, `sale`, `reservation_create`, `reservation_release`, `return_restock`, or `manual_adjustment`.

The concrete set of allowed values is controlled at the application level and persisted in the `movement_type` column of `shopping_mall_inventory_movements`. It is used by reporting and monitoring tools to group and filter movement history.

quantity_delta.description:
Signed quantity difference applied to the inventory item's on-hand stock for this movement.

Positive values increase on-hand stock (for example, supplier receipts or restocks), while negative values decrease on-hand stock (for example, shipments or stock adjustments). This value is persisted in the `quantity_delta` column of the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` table and is crucial for reconstructing how on-hand levels changed over time.

reserved_delta.description:
Signed change applied to the reserved quantity of the inventory item for this movement.

Positive values indicate that units have been reserved (for example, when a cart is converted into an order and reservation rows are created), while negative values indicate that reservations have been released or converted into actual stock consumption. This value maps directly to the non-nullable `reserved_delta` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` and is essential for understanding the lifecycle of reservations and their impact on available-to-sell inventory.

resulting_on_hand_quantity.description:
On-hand quantity of the inventory item immediately after this movement was applied.

This field corresponds to the `resulting_on_hand_quantity` column in the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` table and represents the post-movement stock level that is available physically in the warehouse. It allows clients to render movement history as a running balance without re-computing totals from scratch.

resulting_reserved_quantity.description:
Reserved quantity of the inventory item immediately after this movement was applied.

The value is taken from the `resulting_reserved_quantity` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` and shows how many units are currently held as reservations at the time of this movement. It is useful for debugging reservation flows and visualizing how reservation levels evolve over time.

resulting_available_to_sell_quantity.description:
Available-to-sell (ATS) quantity of the inventory item immediately after this movement was applied.

This field maps to the `resulting_available_to_sell_quantity` column in `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` and reflects the quantity that can still be promised to new orders after considering both on-hand stock and existing reservations. It is a key metric for availability dashboards and alerts.

reason.description:
Human-readable reason or category for this movement.

Often maps to business events such as `order_reservation`, `order_cancellation_release`, `manual_adjustment`, `supplier_receipt`, or `return_to_stock`. This value mirrors the optional `reason` column in the Prisma model and is intended for operational users reviewing movement history and investigating anomalies.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when the inventory movement logically occurred, expressed in ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This value is derived from the non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` table and is used for chronological sorting, timeline visualizations, and time-based analysis of stock changes.

IShoppingMallFulfillment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a fulfillment aggregate in the shopping mall system.

Represents the high-level physical processing state for one or more order lines grouped under a single fulfillment. This summary is optimized for list displays in seller dashboards, warehouse UIs, and tracking overviews and exposes both status and quantity progress without requiring the full fulfillment detail.

The structure is backed by the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` Prisma model, surfacing key columns such as `fulfillment_status`, `packed_quantity`, `shipped_quantity`, `delivered_quantity`, and lifecycle timestamps, while also embedding related order and seller summaries for quick navigation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the fulfillment aggregate.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the underlying `shopping_mall_fulfillments` row and is used when navigating to the fulfillment detail view or when correlating with shipments and fulfillment items.

order.description:
Summary of the customer-facing master order to which this fulfillment belongs.

This object corresponds to the `shopping_mall_orders` record referenced by the `order_id` foreign key. It provides key order-level context such as order number, overall order status, and customer information without requiring a separate API call.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller responsible for processing this fulfillment.

This object represents the merchant account that owns the items in this fulfillment and typically matches the responsible warehouse or store. It is the association counterpart to the seller identity referenced by order lines and inventory items.

status.description:
Current high-level status of the fulfillment lifecycle.

This field is a direct abstraction of the `fulfillment_status` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and uses the same controlled vocabulary, for example `pending`, `pending_fulfillment`, `packed`, `ready_to_ship`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, `returned`, or `lost`. Operational dashboards and workflow engines rely on this status to drive picking, packing, and shipping processes.

fulfillment_number.description:
Human-friendly reference for this fulfillment used in operational UIs and external communication.

Typically follows a structured format such as `FUL-YYYYMMDD-NNNNN`, but the exact pattern is implementation-specific. This maps to a business key or derived identifier used for searching and cross-channel referencing in warehouse tools and customer support systems.

line_count.description:
Number of order lines currently attached to this fulfillment.

This value is derived from associated fulfillment items and order lines and provides a quick sense of workload size without loading full line item details. It is commonly displayed in fulfillment and shipment list views to indicate complexity at a glance.

packed_quantity.description:
Total quantity of units across all lines in this fulfillment that have been packed.

This field mirrors the non-nullable `packed_quantity` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments`. It moves from zero upwards as warehouse staff pack items and is used in dashboards and SLAs to track how close the fulfillment is to being ready for shipment.

shipped_quantity.description:
Total quantity of units across all lines in this fulfillment that have been shipped.

The value corresponds to the non-nullable `shipped_quantity` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and increases as shipments are dispatched. It allows monitoring tools to distinguish packed-but-not-yet-shipped workloads from shipments already handed over to carriers.

delivered_quantity.description:
Total quantity of units across all lines in this fulfillment that have been confirmed as delivered.

This field corresponds to the non-nullable `delivered_quantity` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and represents the portion of the fulfillment that has fully completed the physical delivery process. It is used for final SLA checks, analytics, and customer experience reporting.

last_status_reason.description:
Optional human-readable explanation for the current fulfillment status.

This value mirrors the nullable `last_status_reason` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and may describe failure reasons (for example, `carrier_address_issue` or `customer_not_available`), manual notes from support or warehouse staff, or other contextual information used to explain exceptional states.

packed_at.description:
Timestamp when this fulfillment first reached a packed state, expressed in ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This value is taken from the nullable `packed_at` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and is used in warehouse KPIs and SLA calculations to measure the time between order creation and completion of packing.

first_shipped_at.description:
Timestamp when units in this fulfillment were first shipped, in ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This maps to the nullable `first_shipped_at` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and marks the moment when at least one shipment associated with the fulfillment was dispatched. It is a key milestone for customers and operational reporting.

last_delivered_at.description:
Timestamp when units in this fulfillment were last marked as delivered, in ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This value corresponds to the nullable `last_delivered_at` column in the `shopping_mall_fulfillments` table and is typically used in SLA and experience reporting to measure delivery performance and to determine when a fulfillment is fully complete.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this fulfillment record was created, in ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This value mirrors the non-nullable `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and is used for sorting, reporting, and understanding how long a fulfillment has been in progress.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this fulfillment record was last updated, in ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This value corresponds to the non-nullable `updated_at` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments` and changes whenever status, quantities, or other tracked fields are modified. It is frequently used as a cursor in incremental synchronization or monitoring processes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this fulfillment, in ISO 8601 `date-time` format.

This field reflects the nullable `deleted_at` column in `shopping_mall_fulfillments`. When null, the fulfillment is active and should appear in normal operational views; when non-null, the record has been logically removed and should generally be excluded from default listings while still remaining available for audit and historical analytics.

IShoppingMallFulfillmentItem.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO representing a single fulfillment item that links a fulfillment aggregate to a shipment with a concrete quantity.

This view is built on top of the `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` Prisma model and exposes both the raw database quantity and higher-level, computed progress metrics that are useful in UIs and dashboards.

Foreign keys such as `fulfillment_id` and `shipment_id` are intentionally not exposed in this summary; callers infer parent context from the resource path and related DTOs in the shopping mall domain.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the fulfillment item.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items.id` and uniquely distinguishes a single fulfillment item row across the logistics subsystem.

quantity.description:
Base quantity recorded on this fulfillment item row.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items.quantity` and represents how many units of the related order line are associated with this particular fulfillment–shipment link.

requested_quantity.description:
Original quantity requested on the order line for this SKU at the time the fulfillment workflow was created.

This is a derived, application-level value that is typically aligned with the quantity on the related order line snapshot. It is not stored as a separate column in `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items`, but is computed from the order and fulfillment context to provide progress comparison against `quantity` and `fulfilled_quantity`.

fulfilled_quantity.description:
Quantity that has already been successfully processed for this fulfillment item.

This value is computed by the application from operational events such as picking, packing, and shipment handover. It is not a direct column in `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` but is derived so that clients can easily present completion progress without aggregating low-level events.

remaining_quantity.description:
Quantity that still remains to be fulfilled for this fulfillment item.

This is an application-level metric calculated from `requested_quantity`, `fulfilled_quantity`, and any cancellations or adjustments. It is not stored in `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` but is always provided in this summary DTO so that dashboards and UIs can show outstanding work per line at a glance.

status.description:
Current operational lifecycle status of this fulfillment item.

This field is a derived, application-level state rather than a direct column in `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items`. Typical values include states such as `pending`, `picking`, `packed`, `shipped`, or `cancelled`, combining information from fulfillment, shipment, and inventory signals into a single, human-readable status string.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this fulfillment item record was created.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items.created_at` and provides an audit trail for when the fulfillment–shipment link for this order line was first established.

IShoppingMallShipment.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO representing a shipment in the shopping mall logistics domain.

This summary combines core shipment fields persisted in the `shopping_mall_shipments` Prisma model with a small set of denormalized aggregates and business-friendly identifiers. It is optimized for list views and as an embedded reference from order, fulfillment, and dashboard endpoints.

Foreign keys such as `order_id` and `order_seller_segment_id` are not exposed here; callers obtain that context from the API path and companion DTOs, while this type focuses on shipment status, carrier details, tracking information, and aggregate item quantities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the shipment.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_shipments.id` and uniquely identifies a physical or logical shipment unit in the logistics subsystem.

shipment_code.description:
Human-readable shipment code used in internal tools and customer communication.

This is a business-level identifier that may be derived from order information, seller segment, or carrier data. It is not a physical column in `shopping_mall_shipments`, but is generated and stored at the application layer so that operators and customers can reference shipments without using raw UUIDs.

shipment_status.description:
High-level shipment status representing the current lifecycle state of this shipment.

This field maps directly to the `shopping_mall_shipments.shipment_status` column. Typical values include `pending`, `ready_to_ship`, `shipped`, `in_transit`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, or `lost`, depending on business configuration. Clients use this status to drive UI state, filtering, and notifications.

carrier_name.description:
Name of the carrier or logistics provider handling this shipment.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_shipments.carrier_name` and may be null when a carrier has not yet been assigned or when the shipment is handled entirely in-house without a named external provider.

carrier_service_level.description:
Optional service level name from the carrier, such as `standard`, `express`, or `next_day`.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_shipments.carrier_service_level` and is populated only when the carrier exposes or requires a service level designation for the shipment.

tracking_number.description:
Tracking number assigned by the carrier for this shipment.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_shipments.tracking_number` and may be null or omitted while tracking is not available or has not yet been generated. When present, it can be used to build external tracking URLs or to look up detailed tracking events.

shipped_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment was handed over to the carrier or otherwise marked as shipped.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_shipments.shipped_at` and remains null until the shipment transitions from preparation into an in-transit state.

delivered_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment was confirmed delivered to the customer or final destination.

This field maps to `shopping_mall_shipments.delivered_at` and remains null until a delivery confirmation is received either from the carrier or through manual operational input.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment record was created.

This value maps directly to `shopping_mall_shipments.created_at` and provides an audit trail for when the shipment was first registered in the system.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this shipment record was last updated.

This value maps to `shopping_mall_shipments.updated_at` and changes whenever core shipment attributes such as status, carrier, or tracking information are modified.

total_item_count.description:
Total number of fulfillment items or logical order line fragments included in this shipment.

This is a denormalized, computed value derived from related `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items` rows and associated order line data. It is not a physical column in `shopping_mall_shipments`, but is provided in this summary DTO so that list views and dashboards can quickly show how many lines are grouped into each shipment without additional queries.

total_quantity.description:
Total physical quantity of items contained in this shipment across all included SKUs.

This aggregate metric is computed from related `shopping_mall_fulfillment_items.quantity` values and any associated splits or adjustments. It is not stored in `shopping_mall_shipments`, but is always included in the summary to enable quick comparison of shipment sizes and volumes across the logistics workload.

IShoppingMallShipmentTrackingEvent.ISumm.description:
Summary view of a single shipment tracking event in the shopping mall logistics domain.

This DTO is designed for lightweight timeline displays and detail panels where consumers need to understand how a shipment progressed over time without loading the full shipment and order graph. It exposes only the columns that exist on the `shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events` Prisma model so that backend developers can rely on a strict 1:1 mapping with the database row.

Because it mirrors the underlying table, this summary type is also suitable for internal tools such as customer support consoles, reconciliation dashboards, and monitoring jobs that need to inspect raw tracking history with minimal transformation overhead.

id.description:
Primary key for the shipment tracking event record.

This value is the exact `id` column from the `shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events` Prisma model and uniquely identifies a single tracking event row in the database. It is used when fetching, updating, or deleting a specific tracking event and can be safely logged or included in internal links for support tooling.

In client applications, this identifier can be used as a stable key when rendering lists or timelines of tracking events for a shipment.

shipment_id.description:
Identifier of the shipment whose tracking status is being updated by this event.

This field corresponds to `shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events.shipment_id` and references `shopping_mall_shipments.id`. Multiple events share the same `shipment_id`, allowing the system to reconstruct the full lifecycle of a single shipment.

Consumers typically use this value to group events in a UI timeline or to join tracking data back to shipment, fulfillment, or order entities when performing analytics and debugging.

carrier_status_code.description:
Optional status code as provided directly by the external carrier or logistics provider for this tracking event.

The value is often vendor‑specific and may not be meaningful to end users on its own, but it is invaluable for reconciliation, debugging integrations, and building mapping tables to normalized business statuses. When present, it should be treated as raw data and not assumed to follow a particular format beyond what the carrier’s documentation describes.

For many UIs, this field is either hidden or surfaced only in advanced or internal views; use the normalized `status` field for customer‑facing messaging instead.

status.description:
Normalized shipment tracking status for this event.

Typical business‑level statuses include values such as `shipped`, `in_transit`, `arrived_at_hub`, `out_for_delivery`, `delivered`, `delivery_failed`, or `exception`. The exact vocabulary is owned by the shopping mall domain and is derived from carrier‑specific data, internal state machines, or a combination of both.

Client applications rely on this field to render concise and localized messages about where the shipment is in its lifecycle, independent of the raw carrier terminology.

location_description.description:
Optional human‑readable description of the shipment location at the time of this event.

Examples include a city name ("Seoul"), a carrier facility name ("Incheon Hub"), or a composite label such as "Seoul Distribution Center". The shopping mall platform does not enforce a particular structure here; it simply conveys whatever top‑level location description the carrier or internal logistics system supplies.

This field is best suited for supporting maps, list views, or detail tooltips and may be omitted entirely when the upstream system does not provide location information for a given event.

carrier_raw_message.description:
Optional free‑form message from the carrier or logistics provider associated with this tracking event.

The raw message may include localized text, internal carrier codes, or human‑oriented explanations that complement the normalized `status` field. It is especially useful when dealing with exceptions, failed deliveries, or long‑running in‑transit states where additional context helps support teams or customers understand the situation.

Because the content is unstructured and may not be suitable for direct end‑user presentation in all locales, frontends often either localize or selectively display this value based on audience and channel.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when this tracking event occurred according to the carrier or internal logistics system.

This value is stored as an ISO 8601 date‑time string and represents the point in time when the underlying logistics event actually took place (for example, when a parcel was scanned at a hub or loaded onto a delivery vehicle). It is the primary field used to order events in a shipment timeline and to analyze transit durations between legs.

Developers should treat this as business time rather than system ingestion time; discrepancies between `occurred_at` and `created_at` are expected when carrier feeds are delayed or batched.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this tracking event record was created in the shopping mall backend.

This field reflects when the platform successfully persisted the event into the `shopping_mall_shipment_tracking_events` table. It is also expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time string and may lag behind `occurred_at` in cases where carrier systems submit updates in batches or when integration queues experience delays.

For operational analytics or incident investigations, comparing `created_at` and `occurred_at` helps quantify ingestion latency and can reveal issues in external integrations or internal event processing pipelines.

IShoppingMallInventoryMovementStatistics.description:
Aggregated statistics about inventory movements for a specific SKU in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO represents a pre‑computed summary over a time window, typically produced by reporting or analytics logic that scans `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` and related SKU and inventory configuration data. It is not a direct mapping of a single Prisma model row, but rather an aggregate view designed for dashboards, reconciliation tools, and operational reports.

By exposing inbound, outbound, net change quantities, and movement counts, it enables operators, sellers, and platform administrators to quickly understand how stock for a SKU changed over time without loading each individual movement record.

sku_id.description:
Identifier of the SKU whose inventory movement statistics are being reported.

This value typically corresponds to `shopping_mall_product_skus.id` and acts as the primary key for joining statistics back to catalog entities, pricing, and seller context. Each statistics record produced by the analytics layer targets exactly one SKU over a defined time range.

Frontends and reporting consumers can safely use this identifier to group or filter statistics when rendering per‑SKU dashboards, alerts, or exports.

from_at.description:
Start of the time range (inclusive) over which inventory movements are aggregated.

The value is expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time string and usually denotes the beginning of a reporting window such as the start of a day, week, or month in a given time zone. All eligible inventory movement records with timestamps on or after this boundary are considered in the aggregation.

To ensure consistent reporting, clients and backends should agree on how this boundary is derived (for example, normalized to UTC or to a specific business region’s local time).

to_at.description:
End of the time range over which inventory movements are aggregated.

The value is also an ISO 8601 date‑time string and is typically treated as an exclusive upper bound in analytics queries (i.e., movements strictly before `to_at` are included, while those at or after `to_at` fall into the next window). This convention simplifies back‑to‑back window calculations and prevents double‑counting.

Reporting consumers should document and preserve the inclusivity/exclusivity semantics used here so that charts, exports, and downstream pipelines interpret the time window consistently.

total_inbound_quantity.description:
Total quantity of inbound inventory movements within the given time range.

Inbound movements typically include restocks from suppliers, returns that are placed back into sellable inventory, positive manual adjustments, and other events that increase available stock for the SKU. The value is a non‑negative integer representing the sum of quantities from all such movements that fall inside the `[from_at, to_at)` window.

This metric is often used to understand supply flow and to compare planned restocking levels against actual inbound activity during the period.

total_outbound_quantity.description:
Total quantity of outbound inventory movements within the given time range.

Outbound movements usually correspond to order allocations, shipments, write‑offs, shrinkage, and negative manual adjustments that reduce available stock for the SKU. The value is a non‑negative integer representing the sum of quantities for all outbound events in the `[from_at, to_at)` window.

Operators and sellers frequently compare this metric with sales and order statistics to detect anomalies such as unexpected stock loss or mismatches between recorded shipments and inventory decrements.

net_change_quantity.description:
Net change in inventory quantity for the SKU over the specified time range.

This value is conceptually `total_inbound_quantity - total_outbound_quantity` and may be positive, negative, or zero depending on the balance of inbound and outbound activity during the window. A positive value indicates that on hand stock increased overall, while a negative value indicates a depletion of stock.

Net change is useful for high‑level trend analysis and capacity planning, allowing stakeholders to quickly see whether inventory levels for a SKU are trending upward or downward in a given period without inspecting individual movement records.

movement_count.description:
Total number of individual inventory movement records considered when computing these statistics.

Unlike the quantity fields, which sum units, this value counts the number of distinct movement entries in `shopping_mall_inventory_movements` (or equivalent sources) that fall inside the `[from_at, to_at)` window for the SKU. It helps distinguish between scenarios where the same net change arises from a few large movements versus many small ones.

Analysts and operators can use this metric to understand operational churn around a SKU, such as frequent small adjustments that may signal process issues, or low movement counts that might be expected for slow‑moving items.

IShoppingMallProductReview.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for product reviews in the shopping mall platform.

Represents a lightweight view of a single customer-authored product review suitable for list and overview screens, product detail review sections, and admin moderation queues.

Optimized to include key author, rating, and visibility information without loading full moderation history or related aggregates.

This variant is designed for general client consumption and intentionally omits direct internal customer identifiers to reduce privacy and correlation risks.

review_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product review.

This value is a stable UUID generated by the backend and is used to retrieve full review details or perform moderation actions. It must not be supplied or controlled by clients.

product_id.description:
Unique identifier of the product that this review refers to.

This identifier enables clients to correlate the review with catalog product entities and is safe to expose publicly for navigation and aggregation purposes.

product_name.description:
Display name of the reviewed product so that lists of reviews can show product context without an additional product fetch.

The value is typically a snapshot of the product's display name at review time and may not always reflect later product renames.

sku_id.description:
Optional identifier of the specific SKU variant that this review is associated with.

When non-null, the review targets a particular variant instead of the whole product; when null, the review is considered to apply to the product in general.

This identifier is safe to expose to clients because it refers only to catalog entities and not to private user identities.

customer_display_name.description:
Display name or masked nickname of the customer shown alongside the review content.

The backend is responsible for enforcing any masking, pseudonymization, or formatting rules so that personally identifiable information (PII) is not exposed beyond what business policies allow.

rating_value.description:
Star rating value that the customer assigned to the product.

Typically represented as an integer in a fixed range (for example 1–5) and used in aggregate rating calculations and sorting operations.

title.description:
Optional short title or headline for the review, used in condensed review displays.

When null, the review is shown without a separate headline and only the body or content preview is presented.

content_preview.description:
Short textual preview of the review content used in summaries and list views.

This may be generated by truncating the full review body or stored separately as a summary. It should not contain sensitive personal data beyond the review text itself.

has_media.description:
Indicates whether this review includes any media attachments such as photos or videos.

Clients can use this flag to decorate review items (for example, showing a media badge) and to decide whether to fetch richer detail views.

helpful_vote_count.description:
Number of times other customers have marked this review as helpful.

The count is maintained by the backend and is read-only from the client perspective. It may be used for ranking, sorting, and highlighting high-quality reviews.

reported_flag_count.description:
Number of reports or abuse flags that have been submitted against this review by customers or moderators.

This value is primarily used for moderation and quality evaluation workflows. It does not expose the identities of reporting users in this DTO.

created_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp of when this review was created.

This timestamp is generated by the backend and reflects the original submission time of the review in the system.

last_edited_at.description:
Nullable field representing when this review was last edited, either by the customer or through moderation tools.

When non-null, this is an ISO 8601 timestamp. When null, the review has not been edited since creation, or edit tracking is not available.

visibility_status.description:
Current visibility status of the review in the storefront and admin tools.

Typical values can include statuses such as "visible", "hidden", "pending_moderation", or "removed". The exact set of allowed values is controlled by business rules and not enforced as an enum here to remain extensible.

IShoppingMallProductReviewReport.ISummar.description:
Summary view of a product review report in the shopping mall platform.

Used primarily in list views and embedded contexts where a lightweight representation of review reports is needed. Contains identifying information, minimal context about the reported review, and high-level moderation status indicators without full text payloads or audit history.

This variant omits direct reporter identity details so that it can safely be reused in a wider range of clients without leaking customer identifiers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the product review report.

This identifier is generated by the backend when a new report is created and is used to retrieve or update the report in administrative tools.

reviewId.description:
Identifier of the product review that is being reported.

Clients and moderation tools can use this value to navigate to the underlying review entity and its context. This aligns with the `reviewId` field used in the detailed `IShoppingMallProductReviewReport` DTO and corresponds to the `review_id` foreign key in the `shopping_mall_product_review_reports` table.

reasonCode.description:
Machine-friendly reason code describing why the review was reported.

Typically references a predefined enumeration such as `spam`, `abuse`, `hate_speech`, `nudity`, `off_topic`, or other policy category labels. Client applications may map these codes to localized human-readable labels.

status.description:
Current processing status of the product review report.

Common states include values like `received`, `in_review`, `accepted`, `rejected`, or `dismissed`, depending on the platform's moderation workflow.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the review report was created.

The value is an ISO 8601 date-time string assigned by the backend at the time the report is first persisted.

IShoppingMallProductReviewModerationEven.description:
Summary representation of a moderation event applied to a product review.

Used in timelines, audit summaries, and moderation dashboards to display high-level information about review decisions without full event payloads. Captures who made the decision, what action was taken, and when it occurred.

id.description: Unique identifier of the product review moderation event.

productReviewId.description: Identifier of the product review that this moderation event applies to.

actorType.description:
Type of actor who performed the moderation action.

Typical values may include platform_admin, automated_rule, or seller, depending on who or what initiated the moderation action.

actorId.description:
Identifier of the actor who performed the moderation action.

For human actors, this is typically the platform administrator or seller identifier. For automated systems, this may reference a pseudo-actor or system identity.

action.description:
High-level moderation action taken on the product review.

Common examples include approve, reject, hide, unhide, escalate, or flag_for_manual_review.

reasonCode.description:
Optional machine-friendly code describing the reason for the moderation action.

May reference configured review policies or fraud/risk rules that triggered this action.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the moderation event occurred or was recorded.

IShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsByPr.description:
Aggregate review and rating statistics for a specific product across all reviews in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is typically used as a response body when querying product-level review analytics, such as on a product detail page or in an admin reporting view. It summarizes counts and averages derived from individual review records and associated rating aggregates for a given product.

product.description:
Summary information of the product whose reviews are being aggregated.

This association replaces the raw `product_id` foreign key from `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and provides immediate access to key display fields such as product code, name, and primary media without requiring additional lookups.

seller.description:
Summary of the seller that owns the product whose review statistics are being presented.

This association replaces the raw seller identifier that would otherwise need to be resolved separately, enabling analytics and dashboards to show seller-level context alongside product-level review metrics.

totalReviewCount.description:
Total number of published product reviews associated with this product.

This count typically excludes soft-deleted, hidden, or pending-moderation reviews, and aligns with the `review_count` column on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` when that materialized view is used.

averageRating.description:
Average star rating for this product computed from all eligible reviews.

The value is usually derived from `average_rating` on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and is conventionally represented on a 1.0 to 5.0 scale. When no reviews exist, it may be 0 or null depending on business rules, but the aggregate row will still be present when using the backing table.

ratingCount1.description:
Number of 1-star ratings given to this product.

This value corresponds to the `rating_1_count` column on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and is used to render histograms and rating distributions in analytics views.

ratingCount2.description:
Number of 2-star ratings given to this product.

This value corresponds to the `rating_2_count` column on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and participates in computing rating distributions and quality scores.

ratingCount3.description:
Number of 3-star ratings given to this product.

This value corresponds to the `rating_3_count` column on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and helps visualize mid-range review sentiment.

ratingCount4.description:
Number of 4-star ratings given to this product.

This value corresponds to the `rating_4_count` column on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and is typically used when rendering bar charts or histograms for positive reviews.

ratingCount5.description:
Number of 5-star ratings given to this product.

This value corresponds to the `rating_5_count` column on `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and usually dominates distributions for top-performing products.

oneOf.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent review that contributed to these statistics.

When present, the value aligns with the latest `created_at` among all eligible reviews for the given product and, if applicable, SKU-level aggregates.

Indicates that there is no review yet for this product, so no last review timestamp is available.

This state occurs when `review_count` is zero in `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` or when no aggregate row exists and is synthesized at query time.

lastReviewAt.description:
Timestamp of the latest review that is included in these statistics.

When null, it indicates that the product has not received any valid reviews yet, which is useful for distinguishing unrated products from those with very old review activity.

IShoppingMallProductReviewStatisticsBySe.description:
Aggregate review and rating statistics across all products owned by a specific seller on the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is computed by aggregating per-product and per-SKU rating aggregates stored in the `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` materialized view, grouped by the seller who owns the underlying products. It is **not** a 1:1 projection of a single `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` row, but rather a higher-level analytical summary built on top of that model.

Fields such as `sellerId` and `productCount` are derived aggregation dimensions and do not exist as physical columns in the Prisma model. Count buckets and average rating values summarize approved, customer-visible reviews across the seller's active catalog and are optimized for dashboards, ranking algorithms, and administrative monitoring tools.

sellerId.description:
Unique identifier of the seller whose review statistics are being aggregated.

This identifier matches the primary key of the seller entity in the shopping mall domain and is used to group and retrieve rating aggregates across all products owned by that seller.

totalReviewCount.description:
Total number of published product reviews across all products owned by this seller.

The count typically excludes soft-deleted, hidden, or pending-moderation reviews so that only customer-visible feedback contributes to the aggregate. This value is derived by summing review_count values from the underlying `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` rows that belong to the seller's products.

averageRating.description:
Overall average rating across all products owned by this seller.

This value is calculated from the underlying rating buckets or average_rating values in `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` and is usually expressed on a 1.0 to 5.0 scale. When the seller has no eligible reviews, this value may be 0 to indicate the absence of rating signal.

ratingCount1.description:
Total number of 1-star ratings across all products owned by this seller.

This bucket is computed by summing the `rating_1_count` values from all applicable `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` rows associated with the seller's catalog.

ratingCount2.description:
Total number of 2-star ratings across all products owned by this seller.

This bucket aggregates `rating_2_count` from the underlying `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` rows for all products the seller owns.

ratingCount3.description:
Total number of 3-star ratings across all products owned by this seller.

This bucket aggregates `rating_3_count` values from the underlying `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` rows across the seller's products and SKUs.

ratingCount4.description:
Total number of 4-star ratings across all products owned by this seller.

This bucket aggregates `rating_4_count` values from the underlying `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` rows for the seller's catalog.

ratingCount5.description:
Total number of 5-star ratings across all products owned by this seller.

This bucket aggregates `rating_5_count` values from the underlying `shopping_mall_product_rating_aggregates` rows. A high value here is usually a positive signal for seller quality and customer satisfaction.

oneOf.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent review that contributed to these seller-level statistics.

The timestamp corresponds to the latest created_at (or equivalent) value among all approved, customer-visible reviews belonging to products owned by this seller.

Indicates that there are no reviews yet for any product owned by this seller, so no last review timestamp is available.

In this case, all rating buckets and the total review count will reflect the absence of rating activity as appropriate for the aggregation logic.

lastReviewAt.description:
Timestamp of the latest review that is included in these aggregated seller statistics.

When this value is null, it indicates that none of the seller's products has received any valid review yet or that all reviews are currently excluded by moderation or visibility rules.

productCount.description:
Total number of active products currently owned by this seller that are considered in these statistics.

The exact definition of "active" is determined by business rules (for example, products that are not archived, soft-deleted, or fully hidden). This count helps put the review statistics into context by indicating the catalog size for the seller.

IShoppingMallAdminActionAudit.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of an administrative action audit record in the shopping mall platform. Used primarily in list views and embedded contexts to present what action was taken by which admin and when, without exposing full internal metadata or verbose payload diffs.

This summary focuses on identification, actor context, high-level action classification, and key timestamps so that administrators can quickly scan and filter audit history. Detailed field-level changes, full request context, and extended diagnostic data belong to the full entity DTO that maps all columns of the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` Prisma model.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin action audit record as stored in the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` table.

This value maps directly to the `id` primary key column in the Prisma model and is used to retrieve the full audit record when more detailed information is required.

platformadmin_id.description:
Identifier of the platform administrator who performed the action that generated this audit entry.

This property corresponds to the `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` foreign key column in the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` table and references the primary key of the `shopping_mall_platformadmin` entity. In higher-level response DTOs, this identifier may be expanded into a nested summary object such as `IShoppingMallPlatformadmin.ISummary`, but the summary audit DTO itself exposes the raw UUID for lightweight consumption and filtering.

action_type.description:
High-level classification of the administrative action, such as role assignment, configuration update, moderation decision, or operational command.

The concrete string values follow the domain definition in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` (for example, `CONFIG_UPDATE`, `ROLE_ASSIGNMENT`, `SELLER_MODERATION`, `ORDER_INTERVENTION`) and are used for filtering, grouping, and analytics in admin UIs.

action_subtype.description:
Optional more granular subtype or reason code for the action, used to distinguish specific flows within the broader `action_type`.

This property maps directly to the nullable `action_subtype` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` Prisma model. When present, it helps administrators and analytics tools understand which specific workflow variant or reason was applied for a given action (for example, `PASSWORD_RESET_FORCE`, `CONFIG_ROLLBACK`, or similar fine-grained codes).

target_type.description:
Business type of the primary target resource of this action (for example, `customer`, `seller`, `order`, `product`, `payment`, `review`, or `configuration`).

This value comes from the `target_type` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and is intended for quick grouping and filtering of audit rows by the class of object being manipulated, without needing to inspect the full change payload or snapshots.

target_id.description:
Opaque identifier string of the primary target resource affected by this action.

The exact semantics of this value depend on `target_type` (for example, it might represent a customer ID, seller ID, order ID, or configuration key). It maps directly from the `target_id` column of `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and allows administrators to trace all audit events related to a specific target entity.

summary_message.description:
Human-readable short message summarizing the action that occurred, suitable for display in audit tables or notification feeds.

This property is derived from the `action_summary` column in the `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` Prisma model and should be concise but descriptive enough to explain the intent of the action without requiring access to full before/after payload data.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin action audit entry was created.

This maps directly to the `created_at` column in `shopping_mall_admin_action_audits` and is stored in UTC using ISO 8601 date-time representation. It is used for chronological sorting, time-range filtering, and audit retention policy enforcement.

IShoppingMallAdminConfigurationChangeLog.description:
Summary representation of a configuration change log entry in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is optimized for list and overview screens where administrators need to see which configuration entry was changed, in which domain, by whom, and when, without loading the full configuration payload or diff.

It exposes identifiers, domain and key information, short change summary, and core contextual fields that come from the `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` Prisma model, while omitting heavy serialized payloads that belong to a detailed view DTO.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the configuration change log record as stored in the `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs` table.

This value is a UUID primary key generated by the database and is used to retrieve the full log entry when an administrator opens a detailed configuration history view.

platformAdmin.description:
Summary information about the platform administrator who executed the configuration change.

This replaces the raw foreign key column `shopping_mall_platformadmin_id` with a human-readable representation so that list and audit views can immediately show which operator performed the change without additional joins or lookups.

config_domain.description:
Logical domain of the configuration that was changed, mapped from the non-nullable `config_domain` column of `shopping_mall_admin_configuration_change_logs`.

Typical examples include values such as `cancellation_policy`, `refund_policy`, `review_policy`, `inventory_settings`, or `risk_settings`. This field allows administrators to filter and group change logs by high-level area of responsibility, making it easier to audit changes to sensitive policy modules.

config_scope.description:
Optional scope information for the configuration change, mapped from the nullable `config_scope` column.

The scope can represent finer-grained targeting such as a region code, category code, specific seller identifier, or other domain-specific keys used to differentiate multiple configuration instances within the same `config_domain`. When not applicable, this field remains empty, indicating that the change applied at a global or default scope.

config_key.description:
Canonical key of the configuration entry that was modified.

This typically corresponds to a key in `shopping_mall_configs` or related configuration tables and can be used to correlate multiple change events that affect the same configuration setting over time. Combined with `config_domain` and `config_scope`, this uniquely identifies the configuration surface that was edited.

change_type.description:
Type of configuration modification that occurred in this log entry.

Common values include conceptual actions such as `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE`, reflecting whether the administrator introduced a new configuration record, modified an existing one, or removed it. The exact allowed set is defined by business rules and may be implemented as an enum at the application layer for consistent filtering and analytics.

changed_keys_summary.description:
Short textual summary of which configuration keys or sections were modified during this change, mapped from the non-nullable `changed_keys_summary` column.

This string is designed for quick scanning in list views. It can contain a comma-separated list of keys, a short sentence, or a compact description such as `cancellation_window_minutes, grace_period_days` so that administrators can understand the scope of a change without opening the full diff.

summary_message.description:
Human-readable summary message describing the essence of the configuration change.

This field is intended for display in administrator activity logs or change history timelines. It should concisely explain the intent and effect of the change, for example: `Updated default refund policy thresholds for EU region` or `Enabled stricter review moderation rules for electronics category`.

before_value.description:
Serialized representation of the configuration values before the change, mapped from the nullable `before_value` column.

The value is typically stored as a JSON string or other structured text format that captures the prior state of the configuration entry. For summary views, this field is often not rendered directly, but its presence indicates that a detailed view can expose a before/after diff for deeper troubleshooting or compliance review.

after_value.description:
Serialized representation of the configuration values after the change, mapped from the nullable `after_value` column.

Like `before_value`, this field usually stores a JSON string or similar textual representation of the new configuration state. It exists primarily to support detailed inspection and historical reconstruction of configuration behavior at a given point in time.

reason.description:
Optional human-readable justification entered by the administrator when performing the configuration change, mapped from the nullable `reason` column.

This field is used to capture the business rationale behind the change—for example referencing an incident, a policy decision, or a regulatory requirement. It is especially valuable during later audits or reviews to understand why sensitive configuration values were altered.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration change was recorded in the system, mapped from the non-nullable `created_at` column.

The value is stored as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC and is used to order log entries chronologically, apply time-range filters, and reason about which configuration was active at a particular moment in the platform's history.

IShoppingMallSellerPerformanceSummary.IS.description:
Summary view of a seller's performance on the shopping mall platform.

This DTO provides key performance indicators and risk signals for a single seller over a defined reporting period, such as daily, weekly, or monthly snapshots. It combines raw metrics stored in the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries` Prisma model with derived values that are convenient for dashboards and analytics tools.

The summary is intended for use in admin consoles, risk monitoring screens, and seller analytics reports where a lightweight yet information-rich representation of seller performance is required, without loading the full historical event data for each underlying order, review, or dispute.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the seller performance summary record.

This corresponds to the primary key of the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries` table and uniquely identifies a specific snapshot for a seller and period. It can be used to retrieve the full record or to reference this snapshot from other analytics or audit tables.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller whose performance is being summarized.

This replaces the raw foreign key `shopping_mall_seller_id` with an aggregated seller identity view, so that admin and analytics screens can show store name, basic status, and other headline information alongside performance metrics without additional joins.

period_start.description:
Start timestamp of the aggregation period for this performance summary, mapped from the non-nullable `period_start` column.

The value represents the inclusive lower bound of the reporting window in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). All metrics in this summary are computed using events that occurred at or after this timestamp.

period_end.description:
End timestamp of the aggregation period for this performance summary, mapped from the non-nullable `period_end` column.

The value represents the exclusive (or inclusive, depending on reporting conventions) upper bound of the reporting window in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). Together with `period_start`, it defines the exact time slice covered by this snapshot.

orders_count.description:
Raw count of orders that contained this seller’s items during the aggregation period, mapped from the non-nullable `orders_count` column.

This metric represents the total number of orders that progressed far enough to be included in performance computations, prior to applying derived filters such as cancellation or refund rates. It forms the base denominator for several ratios like `cancellation_rate` and `return_rate`.

cancelled_orders_count.description:
Number of orders or order segments associated with this seller that were cancelled during the aggregation period, mapped from the non-nullable `cancelled_orders_count` column.

This raw count feeds into derived metrics such as `cancellation_rate`. Admins can use it directly to compare absolute cancellation volumes across sellers, while ratios help normalize differences in order volume.

refunded_orders_count.description:
Number of orders or order segments associated with this seller that had refunds processed during the aggregation period, mapped from the non-nullable `refunded_orders_count` column.

This value complements `return_rate` and helps identify sellers with high refund volumes, which may signal product quality issues, mismatched expectations, or fraud patterns.

dispute_opened_count.description:
Raw count of disputes that were opened against this seller’s orders during the aggregation period, mapped from the non-nullable `dispute_opened_count` column.

While `dispute_open_count` in this DTO focuses on the number of currently open disputes at the end of the period, this raw count captures how many disputes were initiated during the window, offering additional insights into the rate at which new disputes arise.

dispute_resolved_against_seller_count.description:
Number of disputes resolved against the seller, meaning the outcome favored the customer, during the aggregation period, mapped from the non-nullable `dispute_resolved_against_seller_count` column.

A high value or ratio of this metric relative to total disputes can indicate systemic issues in fulfillment quality, customer service, or policy compliance and may feed into risk scoring and operational reviews.

average_rating_raw.description:
Raw average product review rating computed for this seller’s products during the aggregation period, mapped from the nullable `average_rating` column in `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries`.

This value is a direct snapshot of the aggregation layer’s computed rating and may differ slightly from UI-level averages that apply additional filters or rounding. When no reviews exist for the period, this value may be treated as absent or mapped to a neutral default by consumers of the DTO.

low_rating_review_count.description:
Count of low-rated reviews—typically those with 1 or 2 stars—for this seller’s products during the aggregation period, mapped from the non-nullable `low_rating_review_count` column.

This metric helps identify concentration of negative feedback and, when compared with total review volume and `product_review_rating_average`, can highlight sellers that require deeper quality or service investigations.

risk_level.description:
Categorical risk level assigned to this seller for the aggregation period, mapped from the non-nullable `risk_level` column.

Common values include tiers such as `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`, but the exact vocabulary is defined by the platform’s risk engine. This field is suitable for use in filters, dashboards, and alerting workflows that need to quickly segment sellers by overall risk posture.

risk_reason_summary.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of why the seller was assigned the given `risk_level` for this period, mapped from the nullable `risk_reason_summary` column.

This text may summarize key drivers such as high cancellation and refund rates, abnormal dispute patterns, or fraud rule violations. It is primarily intended for operational and risk analysts to quickly understand the context behind a flagged risk level without manually correlating multiple metrics.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this performance summary snapshot was generated and stored in the `shopping_mall_seller_performance_summaries` table.

This non-nullable value uses the ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC and represents when the aggregation job or batch completed. It allows operators to verify the freshness of metrics and trace how risk levels and performance indicators have evolved over time.

total_orders.description:
Derived total number of customer orders that were confirmed for this seller during the aggregation period.

In many implementations this mirrors `orders_count`, but it may apply additional business filters such as excluding certain ephemeral or test orders. It is intended for use in UI components and analytics where the term "total orders" is more intuitive than raw column names.

total_gmv.description:
Gross merchandise value (GMV) associated with the seller's orders in the aggregation period.

This represents the sum of item-level prices before platform fees, discounts, and refunds. It is typically expressed in the platform’s base currency and is a core metric for analyzing seller revenue contributions and sales trends.

average_order_value.description:
Average order value (AOV) for the seller during the aggregation period.

Usually computed as `total_gmv / total_orders` when `total_orders` is greater than zero, this metric approximates the typical basket size for the seller. It can be used in conjunction with order counts and refund statistics to classify seller profiles and merchandising strategies.

cancellation_rate.description:
Derived rate of cancellations for this seller during the aggregation period.

Expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1, it is typically calculated as `cancelled_orders_count / orders_count` or a closely related variant. A higher cancellation rate may point to inventory issues, mispriced items, or operational problems affecting order completion.

return_rate.description:
Derived rate at which delivered orders were returned or refunded for this seller during the aggregation period.

Also expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1, this metric reflects the proportion of fulfilled orders that resulted in returns or refunds. Persistent elevation of this rate relative to peers may signal product quality, fit, or description accuracy problems.

average_fulfillment_latency_hours.description:
Average time in hours from order confirmation to shipment creation for this seller during the aggregation period.

Lower values indicate faster fulfillment performance, while higher values may indicate capacity constraints, process inefficiencies, or operational issues. Negative values are not permitted, and the value is generally computed from timestamp differences associated with order and fulfillment events.

on_time_shipment_rate.description:
Proportion of shipments created on or before the expected handling deadline for this seller during the aggregation period.

This rate, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1, is often used in service-level agreements (SLAs) and contributes directly to risk assessments and seller scorecards. A low on-time shipment rate may trigger warnings, coaching, or enforcement actions.

product_review_rating_average.description:
Average product review rating for this seller’s items, considering reviews within or up to the aggregation period.

This metric is typically normalized to a 0–5 or 1–5 star scale and may apply additional business rules such as excluding unverified reviews or weighting recent reviews more heavily. It is closely related to `average_rating_raw` but may reflect a more user-centric aggregation suitable for display in dashboards.

product_review_count.description:
Total number of published product reviews associated with this seller’s items considered in the aggregation.

This count generally includes only reviews that are in a visible state after moderation and excludes soft-deleted or hidden reviews. It helps contextualize the average rating metrics and low-rating counts by exposing the underlying sample size.

dispute_open_count.description:
Number of disputes that remained open for this seller at the end of the aggregation period.

This metric is distinct from `dispute_opened_count`, which captures how many disputes were initiated during the period. The open count is used by operational teams to gauge current workload and unresolved customer issues for the seller.

dispute_resolution_sla_breach_rate.description:
Proportion of disputes associated with this seller that breached configured dispute handling SLAs for first response or final resolution during the aggregation period.

Expressed as a value between 0 and 1, a higher breach rate indicates that the seller is frequently missing response or resolution deadlines, which can negatively impact customer satisfaction and overall risk scoring.

fraud_rule_violation_count.description:
Number of fraud or risk rule violations linked to this seller during the aggregation period.

This metric is derived from `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` or related sources and counts how many times rule conditions were triggered. It is an important signal in the risk engine and often contributes directly to `risk_level` and `risk_score` calculations.

risk_score.description:
Composite numerical risk score computed for this seller based on cancellations, returns, disputes, fraud signals, and other performance indicators.

The exact computation model is business-specific. Higher values typically represent higher risk and may be mapped into discrete `risk_level` tiers. This field is primarily used by automated risk engines, dashboards, and decision-support workflows that require a single scalar risk indicator.

IShoppingMallDisputeResolutionLog.ISumma.description:
Summary view of a single dispute resolution log entry in the shopping mall platform.

This DTO is backed by the `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs` Prisma model and exposes the key fields needed to understand when and how a dispute was resolved and by which actor type. It is optimized for list views, administrative dashboards, and seller consoles where a compact representation is sufficient and full historical context can be fetched via dedicated detail endpoints.

The summary focuses on the non-nullable core fields such as `actor_type`, `resolution_outcome`, and `created_at`, and selectively exposes optional narrative fields like `resolution_rationale` and `notes_internal` that help explain why a particular outcome was chosen without requiring additional joins or queries.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the dispute resolution log entry.

This value corresponds to the primary key `id` column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs` table and is used to retrieve the full resolution log record when needed.

dispute.description:
Summary representation of the order dispute associated with this resolution log entry.

This association replaces the raw `shopping_mall_order_dispute_id` foreign key from the `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs` table and provides immediate access to high-level dispute information such as status and issue category in list and dashboard views.

order.description:
Optional summary of the customer-facing order related to this dispute resolution event.

Although the underlying `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs` table does not store an order foreign key directly, many consumer experiences benefit from showing order context next to the dispute resolution. Implementations may populate this field by traversing from the dispute to its order.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor that performed the resolution action recorded in this log entry.

This field maps directly to the non-nullable `actor_type` column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs` table. Typical values include labels such as `seller`, `platform_admin`, or `automated_rule`, and they determine which concrete actor foreign key is expected to be set on the underlying record.

resolution_outcome.description:
Outcome code of the resolution step represented by this log entry.

This corresponds to the non-nullable `resolution_outcome` column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs` table and may contain values such as `refund_approved_full`, `refund_approved_partial`, `refund_rejected`, `replacement_issued`, or `goodwill_credit`, depending on the platform’s configured dispute resolution vocabulary.

resolution_rationale.description:
Detailed human-readable explanation of why this specific resolution outcome was chosen.

This field is backed by the nullable `resolution_rationale` column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs` table and typically contains information such as evidence evaluation, policy references, or reasoning about goodwill gestures that justify the outcome.

notes_internal.description:
Optional internal notes associated with this resolution event that are intended for platform staff only.

This value mirrors the nullable `notes_internal` column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs` table and can contain operational comments, escalation notes, or quality review annotations that should not be exposed to customers or sellers.

resolved_at.description:
Timestamp at which this resolution event was recorded in the dispute handling workflow.

Even if client applications use the domain term "resolved" for the moment this log entry is created, the underlying persistence is tracked through the `created_at` column. This field exposes that moment as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string and is used to build dispute resolution timelines and measure handling durations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this dispute resolution log record was created in the database.

This non-nullable `created_at` column in the `shopping_mall_dispute_resolution_logs` table provides a precise persistence time for audit and reporting purposes and is returned as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string.

IShoppingMallFraudRuleViolation.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a fraud rule violation detected by the shopping mall risk engine.

Each instance represents a single hit of a configured fraud or risk rule against a target such as an order, payment transaction, account, or session, and is backed directly by the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` Prisma model. It is designed for use in admin and risk-operations dashboards, as well as in compact overviews attached to related entities like orders or payment transactions.

The summary surfaces non-nullable identifiers and timestamps together with the string-based severity classification and optional narrative and context fields so that analysts can quickly understand what happened and decide whether further investigation is required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the fraud rule violation event.

This value maps directly to the primary key `id` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and is used to retrieve the full violation record when more detail is required.

rule_definition.description:
Summary of the fraud rule definition that was violated by this event.

This BELONGS-TO association corresponds to the non-nullable `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_definition_id` foreign key on the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and provides quick access to rule metadata such as code, name, and configured severity.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor or entity the violation is associated with, such as `customer`, `seller`, `platform_admin`, `session`, or `payment_method`.

This field mirrors the non-nullable `actor_type` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and indicates the logical category of the entity that triggered the rule evaluation.

actor_id.description:
Opaque identifier string of the actor or entity to which this violation pertains.

The value is stored in the non-nullable `actor_id` column of the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and may contain an order ID, payment transaction ID, account ID, session identifier, or another stable identifier depending on the `actor_type`.

severity.description:
Severity classification of this particular violation instance.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable `violation_severity` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and typically uses values such as `info`, `warning`, `high`, or `critical`, which may mirror or refine the configured severity of the associated rule definition.

violation_reason.description:
Optional human-readable explanation of why this fraud rule fired for the given actor and context.

This field corresponds to the nullable `violation_reason` column and often includes details such as threshold comparisons, anomalous behaviour descriptions, or policy references that support manual review and rule tuning.

evaluation_context.description:
Optional serialized evaluation payload or context captured when the rule was evaluated.

This maps to the nullable `evaluation_context` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and typically stores structured data (for example, JSON or a domain-specific language) describing the inputs and intermediate metrics used during evaluation so that investigators can replay or understand the decision.

occurred_at.description:
Timestamp when the rule evaluation that produced this violation occurred.

This field is backed by the non-nullable `occurred_at` column in the `shopping_mall_fraud_rule_violations` table and is commonly used as the primary sort key when exploring violations over time.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this fraud rule violation record was stored in the database.

This value reflects the non-nullable `created_at` column and may differ slightly from `occurred_at` when there is persistence latency or asynchronous ingestion of evaluation results. It is returned as an ISO 8601 UTC date-time string for consistent auditing and analytics.

IShoppingMallAccessLog.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shopping mall access log entry for list displays and high-level monitoring.

Represents a lightweight projection of a single web or API request handled by the shopping mall platform, containing only the most relevant fields for overviews, dashboards, and quick inspection. This summary omits heavy or verbose technical details that are present in the full access log entity.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the access log entry.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_access_logs` record and is used to fetch the full log entry when deeper inspection is required.

actor_type.description:
High-level classification of the actor associated with this request, if any.

Examples include values such as `guestUser`, `customer`, `seller`, or `platformAdmin`. When no authenticated identity is associated, this field may be null to indicate a fully anonymous or unauthenticated access.

actor_id.description:
Opaque identifier of the actor that performed the request when known.

This value typically corresponds to a customer, seller, or administrator record in the core domain, but no foreign key constraint is enforced from the logging table. In the summary view it enables quick correlation between traffic patterns and specific actors without loading the full log entity.

http_method.description:
HTTP method of the request such as `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE`.

This value is captured directly from the incoming request and is used for high-level traffic and routing analysis, including method-level error rates and performance metrics.

path.description:
Normalized request path or route template that was accessed.

The path usually omits the domain and query string, and may be normalized to a canonical route pattern. It is used for grouping and analyzing traffic per API endpoint or page family.

status_code.description:
HTTP status code returned for this request.

This value is used to monitor error rates, identify failure patterns, and track general health of the platform. Typical values include `200`, `201`, `400`, `401`, `403`, `404`, `429`, `500`, and `503`.

success.description:
Boolean indicator describing whether the platform considers this request to have completed successfully.

This flag is usually `true` for 2xx responses and `false` for 4xx and 5xx responses, although business logic can refine this classification in edge cases. In summary views it provides a quick visual cue for distinguishing healthy traffic from failures without needing to interpret status codes manually.

latency_ms.description:
Total processing time for the request on the backend, measured in milliseconds.

This value excludes client-side network latency and focuses on server-side handling time. It is useful in list views and dashboards for quickly spotting slow endpoints, performance regressions, or capacity issues without loading the full log payload.

ip.description:
Client IP address from which the request originated, as observed by the platform.

Depending on proxy and load balancer configuration this may represent the end-user IP address or the last trusted proxy in the chain. Operations and security teams can use this field in summaries to identify hotspots, suspicious access patterns, or regional behavior differences.

user_agent.description:
User agent string of the client making the request.

This value typically describes browser, device, or API client characteristics and is used for analytics and troubleshooting. In summaries it allows quick identification of problematic client versions or automation tools, even if the underlying storage truncates extremely long user agent strings.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this access log entry was recorded by the backend.

The value is stored as a `DateTime` column in the `shopping_mall_access_logs` table and normally corresponds to the time when the response was sent to the client. In summary grids and analytics views it is essential for sorting, time‑window filtering, and correlating access logs with other telemetry such as error and integration event logs.

IShoppingMallErrorLog.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a shopping mall application error log entry for list displays and high-level diagnostics.

Represents a lightweight projection of an error or exception recorded by the shopping mall backend. This summary focuses on when the error occurred, where it originated, and its high-level classification, without including full stack traces or large payloads.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the error log entry.

This value is the primary key of the `shopping_mall_error_logs` record and is used to retrieve the full error details when deeper investigation is required.

error_code.description:
Application-specific error code or symbolic identifier for this error condition.

Typical examples include domain-oriented codes such as `ORDER_VALIDATION_FAILED`, `PAYMENT_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT`, or `INVENTORY_OUT_OF_SYNC`. In summary tables this field enables quick grouping of similar incidents and supports dashboards that show the most frequent error categories.

severity.description:
